about: Findings about hoi3_tfh.exe from BiceLib's headers, hooks and reversing notes. rva is module relative. Checked against the executable by buildFindings.py. A global may carry a type, which the script gives the data there ("string" for a C string).

addresses.name: std::string::operator=
addresses.comment: Four instructions: `assign(source, 0, npos)`. **The source arrives in eax** - the compiler gave this thunk a convention of its own - and the destination in ecx as usual. Eight call sites. What CCountry::SetOobFile is made of.

addresses.name: std::string::clear
addresses.comment: Gives the buffer back where the string had one - `if (capacity >= 0x10) free(data)` - and leaves it empty: capacity 0xF, length 0, first byte 0. The destructor's body as well as `clear()`, which is why it turns up at the end of every function that built a string.

addresses.name: C3dVisibleObject::IsVisible
addresses.comment: Slot 15 (`+0x3C`). `mov al, byte ptr [ecx+0x29]; ret` - reads the byte Show and Hide (slots 13 and 14) write.

addresses.name: C3dVisibleObject::SetScene
addresses.comment: Slot 16 (`+0x40`): `[ecx+0xE8] = arg; ret 4`. Paired with the getter at slot 17 (rva 0x10C0), whose result CCombat's destructor path hands to CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject (rva 0x66FBC0) - so +0xE8 is whatever owns and draws the object. `likely` because the owner's class was not identified; `scene` is the name the use suggests, not one read anywhere.

addresses.name: C3dVisibleObject::GetScene
addresses.comment: Slot 17 (`+0x44`): `mov eax,[ecx+0xE8]; ret`. Read at 0x56E045 in CCombat's destructor path, where the result is passed to the graphics object's own teardown - which is the evidence that +0xE8 is the owner. `likely` on the name, as for the setter at rva 0x10B0.

addresses.name: C3dVisibleObject::C3dVisibleObject
addresses.comment: Writes vftable 0x15B4B54 (94 slots), `[+0xF4] = 1.0f`, `[+0x2C] = 0`, **`[+0xF8] = the type`** and two `std::string`s at +0xFC and +0x118. `this` is a stack argument. **23 classes derive from it**, each identified by the vftable its own constructor writes right after this call - CCounterObject 0x15E0F6C, CMasked3dFlag 0x15E1BAC, CProjectionObject 0x15E1DCC, CUnitArrow 0x15E3C14, CBillboardObject 0x16010D0, and so on; scratchpad/gui/ctors.py lists them with the allocation size of each.

addresses.name: std::string::assignString
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall assignString(Hoi3CString* this, Hoi3CString* text, unsigned int from, unsigned int count) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Replaces** this string with part of another - the same three arguments and the same bounds check as `appendString` (`0x33E30`), and the pair are easy to mistake for each other. **5489 call sites.** The requirement renderer uses this one to hand its finished text back through the out parameter.

addresses.name: floorf
addresses.comment: **The `float` overload of `floor` from <math.h>**, emitted out of line: `return (float)floor((double)x)`. It widens the stack float to a double, calls `floor` (rva 0x8084B0) and narrows the result back, answering in st(0). Not a game function and nothing to do with clamping by itself - see `_ftol2_sse` for what it is paired with.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::clear
addresses.signature: void __thiscall std::ios_base::clear(std::ios_base* this, int state, bool reraise)
addresses.comment:
**`std::ios_base::clear(iostate, bool)`**, the bottom of every stream error path. `_Mystate` (`+0xC`) = `state & 0x17` (MSVC's `_Statmask`); if nothing in the new state is in `_Except` (`+0x10`) it returns; if `reraise` it rethrows with `_CxxThrowException(0, 0)`; otherwise it throws `std::ios_base::failure` carrying `ios_base::badbit set` (0x15B4E4C), `ios_base::failbit set` (0x15B4E64) or `ios_base::eofbit set` (0x15B4E7C), in that priority order, through `_CxxThrowException` with the `_ThrowInfo` at 0x164B158.

`this` is the `basic_ios` (== the `ios_base` subobject), so callers reach it as `[[os]+4] + os`. The `basic_ios::clear` wrapper is inlined at every call site as the two instructions `cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x38], 0 / or eax, 4` - the 'no rdbuf means badbit' rule - which is why the callee never looks at the buffer itself.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment:
Confirms the handover in full. MSVC's `??_G` for `ios_base`, and **the virtual-table slot that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) sits behind**:

    mov  [esi], 0x15A7B8C        ; the ios_base vftable
    push esi; call 0x794BAE; add esp,4
    if (flags & 1) free(esi);
    return esi;

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. **It has no direct callers at all** - every use is a virtual dispatch, which is what one expects of a slot-0 destructor and is the complement of `_Ios_base_dtor`'s 700 direct calls.

**It is slot 0 of two tables**: `std::ios_base`'s own (`0x15A7B8C`, RTTI `.?AVios_base@std@@`) and `std::basic_ios<char>`'s (`0x15A7B9C`, RTTI `.?AV?$basic_ios@DU?$char_traits@D@std@@@std@@`, which project.json spells `std::anon::anon::std::D::DU__char_traits::__basic_ios`). Both tables have exactly one slot. The body belongs to `ios_base` - it writes `ios_base`'s own vftable, not `basic_ios`'s - and `basic_ios` derives from `ios_base` in project.json's class record, so the derived table holds the inherited body. Both slots are recorded under `vftable_slots`.

The neighbouring vftable `0x15A7B94` is `std::basic_ostream<char>`'s at object offset 8 and its slot 0 is a different body (`0x50E270`), so it is not part of this and is left on the frontier.

addresses.name: std::endl
addresses.comment:
**`std::endl`** - MSVC's `basic_ostream<char>::put(widen('\n')); flush(); return os`, out of line. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`, answers the stream in eax so it chains.

The body is two halves. The `put('\n')` half is the call to `0x9B50`, which is `__stdcall` and cleans the argument itself - which is why there is no `add esp,4` after it at any call site. The `flush()` half is inlined here and is instruction for instruction the body of `std::ostream::flush` at `0x65BB20`: `if (!(rdstate() & (failbit|badbit)) && rdbuf()->pubsync() == -1) state = badbit;` then `if (state) clear(rdstate() | state | (rdbuf() ? 0 : badbit), false)` through `std::ios_base::clear` at `0x20B0`.

**681 direct call sites, and they are the game's log.** The idiom is `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl` - `0x2410` builds the record, `0xA64A00`/`0xA64A30` are its own inserters, `0x21D30` writes the C strings and this ends the line. `*::LoadKey` dominates the caller list because that is where the engine complains about a key it did not understand. MSVC inlined the same pair at about 120 further sites (`0x16E92` is one: `push esi; call 0x409B50` followed by a private copy of the flush body), so the real number of `<< endl` in this executable is higher than the call count.

The stream is reached through a virtual base: `[[os]+4] + os` is the `basic_ios`, whose fields this touches are `+0xC` `_Mystate` and `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`.

addresses.name: LogRecord::Make
addresses.signature: LogRecord* __cdecl LogRecord::Make(LogRecord* this@ECX, Hoi3CString* file, int line, int channel)
addresses.comment:
**Builds one log record**, and first makes sure there is a sink: if `g_log_sink` (`0x17162A4`) is still null it allocates the four byte do-nothing sink whose vftable is `0x11FCEA0` and installs that, so a message logged before `InstallLogSink` is discarded rather than queued. Then calls the register-convention forwarder `LogRecord::Construct` (`0x6649D0`) with the file, the sink, the line and the channel. There is **no channel test here or anywhere after it** - every record built is flushed to the sink. `this` arrives in ECX and is returned in EAX; the three stack arguments are cleaned by the caller (bare `ret`, `add esp, 0xC` at the call site), so the convention is `__cdecl` with a register `this`, not `__thiscall`.

**`file` is an `Hoi3CString*`, not a `const char*`.** The constructor hands it to `std::string::assignString` (`0x1BD0`), which takes a string, and every call site builds one first: `mov edx, 'battleplan.cpp'; lea esi,[ebp-0x74]; call std::string::fromCString` and then pushes that temporary (0x404743..0x404768).

addresses.name: LogRecord::Flush
addresses.comment: **The complete destructor of the record, and where a log line is decided.** Every message in the game arrives here in a record holding its file, line and channel, and this is what does or does not write it - `[persistent.cpp:39]`, `[countryhistory.cpp:450]` and the 597KB of setup.log all pass through it. Takes the record in eax, pushes `record+0x78` (the `std::basic_ios` virtual base) into `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct`, then puts the `ios_base` vftable `0x15A7B8C` at `record+0x78` and runs `~ios_base` (`0x794BAE`). Nothing is returned: eax at the `ret` is whatever `~ios_base` left there and no caller reads it. **The one place worth hooking to see everything the engine complains about**, including the channels that produce no file.

addresses.name: CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase
addresses.comment: Constructor: takes the freshly allocated 0x57C bytes as its one stack argument and answers them.

addresses.name: CCountryTag::GetCountry
addresses.comment: **The tag -> country lookup the whole image goes through: 1295 direct call sites.** Five instructions, no branch, no call: `g_CCountryDataBase->countries_first[this->id]`. `mov eax,[ecx]` reads the four tag characters and `mov [esp],eax` stores them in a stack slot nothing reads again - the dead half of a by-value CCountryTag copy the optimiser flattened - so only `this->id` at +4 is used. It does not range-check the id and it does not check that g_CCountryDataBase is non-null.

addresses.name: std::putNewline
addresses.comment:
**The `put(widen('\n'))` half of `std::endl`, kept out of line**: construct the sentry (`rdbuf()->_Lock()`, flush `_Tiestr`, ok = `_Mystate == 0`), write 0x0A through the buffer's put pointer or, when there is no room, through `overflow`; `badbit` if either the sentry was not ok or `overflow` answered -1; `setstate`; destroy the sentry; answer the stream.

**`__stdcall`** - it cleans its own argument, `ret 4`, which is why no call site has an `add esp,4` after it. 120 direct call sites: 0x2240 (`std::endl` itself) and about 119 places where the compiler inlined `endl`'s flush half but left this call standing, 0x16E92 among them.

The name is descriptive, not a symbol the library exports. It is not `basic_ostream::put`: the character is the constant 0xA, baked in at both 0x9BF2 and 0x9BFF, and there is no character parameter.

addresses.name: std::string::assign
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall assign(Hoi3CString* this, char* text, uint length) @EAX
addresses.comment: `assign(const char*, size_t)`: thiscall, both arguments pushed, `ret 8`. Up to fifteen characters it writes them into the object and past that it allocates. What BiceLib calls to hand the game a string of its own - see GameClasses/GameString.cpp.

addresses.name: std::ostream::_Osfx
addresses.comment: MSVC's `basic_ostream<char>::_Osfx()`, the end-of-operation hook the `sentry` destructor runs: `if (flags() & unitbuf) flush();`, wrapped in a catch-all (the SEH funclet at 0x40A2AC swallows anything the flush throws). `unitbuf` is `_Fmtfl & 2` at basic_ios `+0x14`; the flush is 0xA5BB20 with `this` handed over in esi. `this` in ecx as usual, no stack arguments, bare `ret`.

addresses.name: GetCurrentGameState
addresses.comment: Two instructions, 0x40C370..0x40C375: `mov eax, [0x1A89790]; ret`. The game's own non-inlined `CCurrentGameState::current()` - exactly what BiceLib's CCurrentGameState::current() reimplements. 38 direct callers, each of which then tests the result for null and constructs a game state if it is; it is the out-of-line half of the get-or-create accessor the compiler inlined at 2772 other places. Class-free on purpose: it is a free accessor over a global, not a method.

addresses.name: GuiTooltipText::Destroy
addresses.comment: Destructor of the GUI's shared 0x5C-byte tooltip-result record: frees and empties the Hoi3CStrings at +0x38, +0x1C and +0 in that order, each guarded by `capacity >= 0x10`. Receiver in **ESI**, nothing on the stack, bare `ret`. **114 callers**, which is what shows the type is the interface's standard tooltip return rather than one panel's local struct. A builder constructs the record itself, so the caller supplies raw stack space and calls this afterwards - that is the discipline BiceLib has to follow or it leaks or double-frees. The name is BiceLib's; the game's own name for the type is not established (no vftable, no Lua registration). See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.name: GuiTooltipText::CopyConstruct
addresses.comment: Copy constructor of the 0x5C tooltip record, and the cleanest evidence for its layout because it names every field exactly once: three std::string::assignString calls on +0, +0x1C and +0x38, then `[this+0x54] = [src+0x54]` and `[this+0x58] = [src+0x58]`. `this` on the stack, the source in **EDI**, `ret 4`, answers `this`. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.name: GuiTooltipText::Assign
addresses.comment: `operator=` for the 0x5C tooltip record - the same five fields as the copy constructor, no prologue at all, bare `ret`, answers ESI. 27 callers. CAlignment::BuildDriftTooltip's caller uses it at 0x78540E to move the finished record into its own out parameter before destroying the local. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetCapitalLocation
addresses.comment:
The capital's province: the game state's province vector (+0xB8C) indexed by CCountry +0xE20. Byte for byte the same function as GetActingCapitalLocation (0x2F100) but for the offset it reads, which is what settles which field is which.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetStrategy
addresses.comment: Two instructions, `lea eax,[ecx+0x48C]; ret`. The game's own name for CCountry +0x48C, out of the luabind table (ghidra/luabind.json: {"name":"Strategy","offset":1164,"type":"CAIStrategy"}). **This names the object FINDINGS-aiunit.md called the anonymous theatre manager**: it is a third CAIStrategy held by value, the merged working copy of ai_hard_strategy (+0x1DC) and ai_event_strategy (+0x334). Confirmed independently: CCountry's constructor builds all three with CAIStrategy::CAIStrategy at 0x4C8CD6/0x4C8CE6/0x4C8CF6, the last with `lea edx,[ebx+0x48C]`, and the destructor destroys the same three in reverse at 0x4CB1D6/0x4CB1F7/0x4CB206.

addresses.name: GetCustomGameSettings
addresses.comment: The lazily built **custom game modifier settings** singleton, 0xD8 bytes, held at 0x1A85C1C and constructed by 0x41C570. A bare `ret`; the struct has no vftable, so RTTI does not name it. +0x70 is theory_decay_months, +0x74 practice_decay_months, +0xA0 a CCGMUnitCostMult, +0xB8 a CCGExtraPracticeDecay whose map is +0xC0..+0xC4, +0xD0 officers_ratio. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: ApplyCustomGameSettings
addresses.comment: **Where the whole technology recalculation hangs off.** Extent 0x41D560..0x41E33C, `ret 8` - verified by linear sweep, there is no earlier `ret`, and nothing but a `call` reaches it so findRefs --address finds no reference at all. Per country it calls CTechnologyStatus::ReapplyAllTechnologies (rva 0x132840), then RecalculateTheoryAbilities (rva 0x1FE10), and later RecalculatePracticalAbilities (rva 0x1FFF0). Its two callers are CCgmSetStageCommand slot 6 (0x428AA0) and CInGameIdler slot 3 (0x65A2B0), so it runs at game start and when the custom game stage changes - **not on any tick**. What the second argument means was not read. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: LoadCustomGameSettings
addresses.comment: The save loader for the custom game settings singleton: a token switch writing theory_decay_months (0x835) to +0x70, practice_decay_months (0x836) to +0x74, unit_cost_mult (0x837) to the sub-loader at +0xA0, extra_practice_decay (0x83A) to the one at +0xB8, and officers_ratio (0x543) to +0xD0. The two months go through the plain integer helper 0xB969F1. **The constructor leaves both months zero**, so a save without them decays nothing whatever BASE_TECH_DECAY says. `ret 8`. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: RecalculateTheoryAbilities
addresses.comment: **Rebuilds every theory ability from the technology levels, then decays them.** Zeroes each category with CTechnologyCategory +0x60 set through CCountry::SetTechAbility, then for every technology whose `on_completion` (CTechnology +0x28C, a CTechnologyCategory*) is a theory and whose researched level is above zero adds `(level + [0x160A460]) x [0x160A300]` into it through 0x4E02F0, and finishes by calling ApplyTechCategoryDecay (rva 0x204A0) with theory = 1. One caller, rva 0x1D560. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: RecalculatePracticalAbilities
addresses.comment: The practical half of rva 0x1FE10: the same rebuild over the categories whose CTechnologyCategory +0x60 is clear, finishing with ApplyTechCategoryDecay (rva 0x204A0) with theory = 0 at 0x42047C. One caller, rva 0x1D560. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: ApplyTechCategoryDecay
addresses.comment:
**Practical and theory decay as applied when the custom game settings are applied** - at game start or a custom-game stage change, not on any tick. It reads BASE_TECH_DECAY (CDefines `country +0x40`) at 0x420661. It is **not** the image's only reader of that define, as this comment used to say: CCountry::UpdateMonthly (rva 0xDC840) reads it again at 0x4DCACA and is the one that runs during play. The scan that found "one reader" missed it because GetDefines is inlined there. For every CTechnologyCategory in the database (`[0x1A87B78] + 0x1C`) whose +0x60 matches the bool argument:

    step  = BASE_TECH_DECAY x (1.000 + CCountry +0x1174[category->index])
            x extra x months x (1.000 - slack)          clamped to -1.000 .. 0
    level = max(own_ability, the sharer's)
    CCountry::SetTechAbility(country, category, level x (1.000 + step))

`months` is the custom game settings' theory_decay_months (+0x70) or practice_decay_months (+0x74); `extra` is 1.000 for a theory and the extra_practice_decay map's entry (settings +0xC0, default 1.000) for a practical; `slack` is `[+8] x [+0x10]` summed over the **Reinforcement and Upgrade production sliders** (CCountry +0x5F4 elements 4 and 5), so IC spent there slows the decay.

**It is not a tick.** Called twice, from 0x41FFCA (theory = 1) and **0x42047C** (theory = 0), both in wrappers whose only caller is rva 0x1D560 - reached from CCgmSetStageCommand slot 6 and CInGameIdler slot 3. CTechnologyCategory +0x60 == 0 is a practical, because that is the pass consulting extra_practice_decay. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.signature: void __fastcall ApplyTechCategoryDecay(CCountryTag* tag@ECX, void* customGameSettings@stack:4, bool theory@stack:8)

addresses.name: CountryTagVector_Contains
addresses.comment: Nine instructions, bare `ret`, 40 direct callers, both arguments in registers and nothing on the stack. Walks an 8-byte-stride vector {begin at +0, end at +4} and compares the **id half** at entry +4 against the tag's id half at +4, answering `setne` on 'the scan stopped before the end'. Used on CWar +0x2C (attackers) and CWar +0x3C (defenders) by AreaMayWidenFrontSearch (0x495140) at 0x4954BC and 0x4954E6, with the country's own tag at CCountry +0xCA4. Class-free on purpose: it is a tag-in-vector test, not a method of either side.

addresses.name: std::operator<<Chars
addresses.signature: std::ostream* __cdecl std::operator<<Chars(std::ostream* os, const char* text)
addresses.comment:
**`std::operator<<(std::ostream&, const char*)`** - the free inserter for a C string, out of line. `__cdecl`, `os` at `[ebp+8]`, the string at `[ebp+0xC]`, bare `ret`, answers `os` in eax. The `Chars` suffix distinguishes it from the other `operator<<` overloads, the way `std::string::appendChars` is distinguished from `appendString` in these findings.

It is the standard algorithm, in order: `strlen` inline (0x421D61, and the same inline `strlen` opens `std::string::assign`'s caller at 0x4022A0); `pad = width() > len ? width() - len : 0`, computed as a full 64-bit compare and subtract because `streamsize` is `__int64` here, against `_Wide` at basic_ios `+0x20`/`+0x24`; then the sentry - `rdbuf()->_Lock()`, and if `_Mystate == 0` and `_Tiestr` (`+0x3C`) is set, `_Tiestr->flush()` through 0xA5BB20; if the sentry is not ok, `badbit`. When it is ok, `(_Fmtfl & 0x1C0) == 0x40` - `adjustfield == left` - decides whether the padding goes after the text (0x421F44) or before it (0x421E22); the fill character is `_Fillch` at `+0x40` and each one goes out through the sputc fast path or `overflow`. The text itself goes through `sputn` (0x22170) and a short write is `badbit`. Then `width(0)` - `_Wide` zeroed at 0x421EA4 - `setstate(state)` through `std::ios_base::clear`, and the sentry's destructor: `uncaught_exception()` (0x794AE9), `_Osfx` (0xA260), `rdbuf()->_Unlock()`.

**845 direct call sites**, for the same reason as `std::endl`: this is what writes every literal in the game's log lines, and `*::LoadKey` is over-represented because that is where parse complaints are written.

basic_ios is a virtual base, reached as `[[os]+4] + os`; the fields used are `+0xC` `_Mystate`, `+0x14` `_Fmtfl`, `+0x20` `_Wide` (64 bit), `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`, `+0x3C` `_Tiestr`, `+0x40` `_Fillch`.

addresses.name: std::locale::Destruct
addresses.comment:
Confirms the handover's reading of the body, with one correction to the name's spelling. This is `std::locale::~locale()` with `facet::_Decref()` inlined into it:

    if (_Ptr) {                       // the _Locimp* at locale +0
        _Lockit lock(_LOCK_LOCALE);   // 0x79504A with the literal 0
        if (0 < _Ptr->_Myrefs && _Ptr->_Myrefs != (size_t)-1) --_Ptr->_Myrefs;
        dead = _Ptr->_Myrefs == 0 ? _Ptr : 0;   // the neg/sbb/not/and at 0x42EE69
        ~_Lockit();                   // 0x795072
        if (dead) dead->vftable[0](1);          // scalar deleting destructor
    }

So a `locale` is one pointer wide, which is why `ios_base::_Init` allocates exactly four bytes into `_Ploc`; the refcount is at `_Locimp +4`; and `-1` is the sentinel that keeps the classic locale alive forever.

`__thiscall`, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Four callers: `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`), which destroys `_Ploc` at `+0x30` and then frees it, and three in `0x50E742`/`0x50ED2E`/`0x50ED54`.

**The name is spelled `Destruct`, not `~locale`.** project.json holds exactly one `~` name (`CSubUnitDataBase::~CSubUnitDataBase`) and the convention the log family already established for this is a word - `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct`, `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor`. Whoever prefers the tilde should rename it once, everywhere.

The bombing half of the same decision, with the same three arguments and the same return - the kind it created, 4 ground bombing, 5 land bombing, 6 naval bombing, or 0 for none.

**4** when the province's terrain byte (+0xD4, +0x22) is set, the bomber's +0xB0 object passes slot 0x68, and 0x42F1B0 says the province's controller (+0x334/+0x338) is hostile to the bomber's owner (+0x124) - that is, a raid on the province itself, with no enemy unit needed. Otherwise it walks the province's units for a target and takes **5 or 6** from the target's slot 16: `setne cl; add ecx,5` at 0x43045D, so a target that answers true is 6 and one that answers false is 5. Either way it gives up if province->+0x2FC already holds a bombing.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::StartCombat
addresses.signature: int __stdcall CCombatManager::StartCombat(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, CUnit* unit) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Decides whether `unit` starts an ordinary combat in `province` and, if so, which kind, then calls CCombatManager::CreateCombat. Returns the kind it created - 1 land, 2 naval, 3 air - or 0 for none; the kind lives in one stack slot that is zeroed at 0x4307C4 and is also the return value on every early exit.

It walks the province's units (+0x2B8) for an enemy, then: the enemy unit's slot 17 true gives **3**; otherwise the province's terrain record (+0xD4) with a nonzero byte at +0x22 gives **1**; otherwise **2**, but only when the attacker's own slot 11 result passes 0x431840 and its +0x40 is at least 1. Before creating, 0x4A6010 refuses a second combat of the same kind in the province.

addresses.comment: **Where every combat in the game starts.** ~34 callers, all of them 'this unit's situation changed' - CUnit::EnterProvince, ApplyAttrition, SetUnitPath, CUnit/CNavy slot 31, CAir slot 37, CAddDivisionEffect::Execute, the split/transfer commands. Two exits: CCombatManager::StartCombat (0x30760) for the ordinary case, and CCombatManager::StartBombing (0x302A0) at VA 0x00431354 for the bombing case, which is reached only when `unit->slot17()` (CUnit::IsAir) **and** `unit->order->slot17(province)` are both true. `ret 8`, so `this` is in ecx and both other arguments on the stack.

addresses.name: CCombatManager::CreateCombat
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCombatManager::CreateCombat(CCombatManager* manager, CMapProvince* province, int kind, CUnit* attacker, CUnit* defender)
addresses.comment:
The live combat factory - where a combat starts in a running game, as opposed to CCombatManager::LoadKey's path out of a save. `ret 0x14`, five stack arguments, nothing in ecx.

A jump table at 0x431604 on `kind - 1` covers 1..6 and every arm is the same three instructions: `operator new(0x44)`, the kind's own constructor, `edi = the new combat`, `jmp 0x43141F`. 1 CLandCombat (0x17B480), 2 CNavalCombat (0x17B720), 3 CAirCombat (0x17BB50), 4 CGroundBombing (0x2FE20), 5 CLandBombing (0x2FE70), 6 CNavalBombing (0x2FEC0). A failed allocation sets edi = 0 and joins the same tail.

The common tail, with edi the combat and esi the manager:

    CCombatManager::AddCombat(manager, combat)      0x2FFC0
    combat->slot 6 ()                               CreateCombatants
    combat->SetProvince(province)                   slot 16
    if (kind == 4)                                  ground bombing only
        push the province's controller tag+id (province +0x334/+0x338, 8 bytes)
        into combat->defender->countries (+0x54/+0x58/+0x5C)
    combat->attacker->slot 12 (attacker);  0x5BFE80;  if (!combat->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(attacker, 1)
    if (defender)
        combat->defender->slot 12 (defender); 0x5BFE80; if (!combat->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(defender, 0)
    for each unit in province->units (+0x2B8)
        skip it if it is the attacker or the defender, and, for a bombing,
        only offer it when slot 8 and the unit's own tests agree
        combat->AddUnit(unit)                       slot 18
    if the attacker's +0xB0 object passes slot 0x6C, walk province +0x354's list
        the same way and offer those units too
    if (combat->slot 8 ())   province->+0x2FC = combat, if it was null
    else                     CMapProvince::AddCombat(province, combat)   into province +0x2EC

Slot 8 is `xor al,al; ret` on CCombat and `mov al,1; ret` on all three bombings, so the last two lines read: a bombing goes in the province's single +0x2FC slot, an ordinary combat onto the province's +0x2EC list. Both bodies are linker-folded, so neither is named here.

**The default arm is dead code, and the reading `(manager, province, kind, attacker, defender)` stands.** The arms all jump to 0x43141F; 0x43141C is three bytes of its own - `mov edi,[ebp+0xC]` - reached only by the `ja` at 0x43137F, that is only when `kind` is outside 1..6. Both callers are exhaustive: CCombatManager::StartCombat sets its kind slot to 1, 2 or 3 on every path that reaches the call, and CCombatManager::StartBombing to 4, 5 or 6, checked off cfg.py's edge lists into 0x430883/0x43093F and 0x430467/0x430474. And the arm is not a second calling convention: arg2 is the province by three independent reads - SetProvince stores it in CCombat +0x18 and its terrain in +0x24, the kind-4 block reads its controller tag at +0x334, and both callers read +0xD4, +0x2B8 and +0x2FC off the same value - so running that arm would call CCombat virtuals on a CMapProvince. It is what MSVC emitted for a `combat` variable left undefined when the switch matched nothing.

addresses.name: ShouldStartNavalCombat
addresses.comment:
**Corrected: it returns a bool, not a code.** The function has exactly two exits, `mov al, 1` at 0x431A85 and `xor al, al` at 0x4320B0, both `ret 8`. The `cmp al, 1` at the StartCombat call site that this entry read as a tri-state is how MSVC compares a bool against true; the other three call sites use a plain `test al, al`. It also has **four** callers, not one: 0x430415, 0x430861 (CCombatManager::StartCombat), 0x59A85E and 0x59D12C - the last two in the naval order block, so naval orders ask the question themselves as well. Both manager call sites guard it with CProvinceTemplate.is_land (+0x22), so it only ever runs for a sea zone.

The naval spotting roll, 0x880 bytes, VA 0x00431840..0x004320BD. **Returns a bool, not a code** - exactly two exits, `mov al,1` at 0x431A85 and `xor al,al` at 0x4320B0; the `cmp al,1` at 0x430866 is how MSVC compares a bool, and the other three call sites use `test al,al`. **Argument order**: edi=[ebp+8]=ours, ebx=[ebp+0xC]=theirs, and StartCombat pushes `edi` (theirs) then `eax` (ours). Four callers: 0x430415, 0x430861 (CCombatManager::StartCombat), 0x59A85E, 0x59D12C.

Six gates return false: theirs->regiments.count<1 (0x431862); ours->IsNaval() && ours->AsNavy()->+0x2F8>0, the fleet cooldown (0x431889); ours->order is convoy_raid 0x6E9 (0x4318A3); our owner is AI (gameState->played_countries_array[owner_id]==0) and our order is rebase/invasion/transport/none (0x43194B); both naval and ours.submarines>0 and theirs.screens>ours.submarines/3 (0x431A11); both naval, order==patrol 0x42E, COrder::GetStance()!=0, and 5*(ours.carriers+capitals) < 3*(theirs.carriers+capitals) (0x431A58). The two fleet censuses come from CountShipsByRole (0x1CF640).

Six short-circuits return true: province intel byte >= 9 (0x431A6E); theirs->combats.count>0; theirs->current_combat!=0; g_FogOfWar (0x130AD30) == 0; any unit in theirs->AsNavy()->carrying is moving or fighting (0x431AE0).

Then four scale factors - A = mission efficiency (1000, or 1000 + GetMissionEfficiency(ours->order) - GetMissionEfficiency(theirs->order) when convoy_escort-or-patrol meets convoy_raid); B = 1000, or NAVAL_INTERCEPTION_AFTER_ATTACK_FACTOR (military +0x270) when theirs' province was convoy-raided within one day; C = 1000 + GetTraitEffect(ours, spotting_chance=0xE); D = ours->IsAir() ? 1000 : 10000 - and a double loop over theirs->regiments x ours->regiments:

  V = our->IsAir() ? our.def.surface_detection : (their.def.is_sub ? our.def.sub_detection/2 : our.def.surface_detection)
  S = max(1000, their.def.visibility)
  v = V*S/1000 * C/1000 * A/1000 * B/1000
  v = v*1000 / (theirs->movement_remaining>0 ? 3000 : 2000)
  if (theirs->+0x95) v *= 2
  intel>=2: v = v*1250/1000;  intel>=6,7,8: v *= 2 each
  v = v * (1000 - rain*SPOTTINGRAINMODIFIER/1000 - cloud*SPOTTINGCLOUDMODIFIER/1000) / 1000
  v = max(v, 1000)
  if (rand() % D < v/1000) return true

Everything in thousandths. A moving fleet is HARDER to see (3000 vs 2000). The 1250 is not a define, it is (int)floor(1250.5f) folded at startup into 0x1A88170's family of literals.

addresses.name: LoadDefines
addresses.comment: Fills `CDefines` from the parsed `common/defines.lua`. One unrolled run of 396 loads, each of them `mov <reg>, [defines + <block>]`, `push "<KEY>"`, `call` the reader, `mov [<reg> + <offset>], eax` - so **every define is looked up by name and stored at an offset compiled into this function**. A mod cannot move a define by reordering the file; a key the file does not define goes unreported and stores 0, because the reader's type check fails; a key the file defines that this function never pushes is never read at all, which is what BlackICE's PRIDE_SUNK_DISSENT_IMPACT, WHITESEA, WHITESEA_BLOCKER and GFX_RAINIMPACT_LIMIT are. addresses.name: Date_DayOfMonth
addresses.comment: From a tick: day of the month, 0 based.

addresses.name: Date_SetFromString
addresses.signature: void __stdcall Date_SetFromString(int* date@ESI, const char* text)
addresses.comment:
Sets a date tick from the text `year.month.day.hour`, in place, joining `Date_Year`, `Date_DayOfYear`, `Date_DayOfMonth` and `Date_DayOfWeek` as the writing half of that family. **782 direct call sites**, the most-called unnamed function in the image after the parse helpers, and the text handed to it is `parse + 0x22C` (`CParseContext::value.text`) at every site inspected.

It is `sscanf(text, "%d.%d.%d.%d", &year, &month, &day, &hour)`, then month and day are decremented to 0 based, then the tick is rebuilt on the epoch `CLASSES.md` records: `tick = 24 * sign(year) * (365*|year| + dayOfYear(old tick)) + 43800000 + hourOfDay(old tick)`, where 0x29C55C0 = 43800000 and 0x538AB8*8 is the same number. The month is then added by 0x4C420 and the day of the month by 0x4C360 - both walk the month length table at rva 0x1313294 - and finally the hour of day is replaced by the parsed one. Callers hand it a date holding exactly the epoch (`mov [esp+0x64],0x29C55C0; lea esi,[esp+0x64]` at 0x4CE4A2), so the old day-of-year and hour-of-day it preserves are both zero and the result is exactly the date in the string.

**The sscanf return is never tested.** A string that is not a date leaves year 0 and, because the decrements are unconditional, month -1 and day -1, so the tick walks backwards off the epoch and nothing is reported - the same silence `FINDINGS-...` records for unknown keys.

addresses.name: IntegerSqrt
addresses.comment: An integer square root by Newton's method, taking its only argument in **edi** and returning it in eax: `x = (v - sign)/2` then iterate `x = (v/x + x)/2` until it stops decreasing, with `v <= 1` short-circuited. Eleven callers and no vftable, so it is a shared utility rather than anyone's method - which is why the name carries no class (trap 11: a register argument is spelled value@EDI and costs no stack). addresses.name: CTraitGainTracker::Update

addresses.name: OwnerAreaPathFind

addresses.name: CConstruction::AddProgress
addresses.comment: **Advances one queue item by `amount` thousandths of a day's work.** `this` is in ESI and is not passed on the stack; the one argument is cleaned by the callee (`ret 4`). It works out `amount * 1000 / duration` - or -1 when duration is zero - and hands that to virtual slot 20 (`[vftable+0x50]`), adds `amount` to progress (+0x38), and then writes **status** (+0x3C): 1000 when `amount >= 1000`, `amount` when it is positive and cost (+0x30) is positive, 0 otherwise. So status is the share of a full day the item last received, and this is the only place it is ever written apart from the loader, the save and the constructors' default of 1000. Three callers: the daily production pass at 0x119D10, once with a literal 1000 and once with a computed partial amount, and the two build commands at 0x145BA0 and 0x146E40. The name is BiceLib's. See reversing/FINDINGS-oob.md.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::AddStartExperience
addresses.comment: **Slot 20 - what CConstruction::AddProgress hands the day's funding fraction to.** It takes the owning country's MODIFIER_UNIT_START_EXPERIENCE (modifier 52, at [CCountry +0xDA8] + 0x1A0 - the modifier values array is **eight bytes an entry**, which 77 x 8 = +0x268 for RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE in GetBuildCostIC settles), scales it by reserves_factor (+0x9C) over 1000 where is_reserve (+0x8C) is set, multiplies by the fraction over 1000 and adds that to accumulated_experience (+0xA4), then adds the raw fraction to accumulated_progress (+0xA8). Both fields are already named from the save, which is what makes the reading safe. `this` in ecx, one stack argument, `ret 4`. The name is ours.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::RecalculateCost

It finds the country as gamestate[+0x16C][this+0x4C] and calls CCountry::GetBuildCostIC (0x4E18F0, at 0x485494 and 0x4854EF) and CCountry::GetBuildTime (0x4E19A0, at 0x4855B6 and 0x4855CF), passing byte [this+0x8C] (is_reserve) as the reserves flag. Two arms: where brigades_count (+0x84) is positive and the first element of the vector at +0x7C has a non-null +0x38 the item is an upgrade, so it takes the difference between the new cost and the old (floored at zero at 0x4854F8) and applies the `military` defines UNIT_UPGRADE_COST (+0x234), UNIT_UPGRADE_TIME (+0x238) and UNIT_UPGRADE_PRACTICAL_MOD (+0x23C); otherwise it walks the brigade list for a fresh build. **It runs at exactly two moments** - when the item is queued (0x546166) and on every queued item whenever one completes (0x51A253) - so a queued item's cost lags the country's current technology and practical until something in the queue finishes. addresses.name: CMap::CMap
addresses.comment: CMap constructor (object 0x2A94 bytes), and the only place the whole layout is visible at once - it has exactly one caller, 0x488243. `this` arrives on the stack, not in ecx (`mov edi,[ebp+8]`, `ret 4`), and comes back in eax. It writes CMap's primary vftable (rva 0x11BE3EC) at +0 and CMap's secondary vftable (rva 0x11BE408) at **+8**, with the CPersistent meta word 0x18D at +4; the +8 sub-object is built first with a base vftable at VA 0x15FDB48 and holds an Hoi3CString at +0xC set to `default.map`. It then constructs 512 CLists at +0x50 (through the CRT vector-constructor iterator, element ctor 0x9CE0, dtor 0x4A30D0), empties the twelve file-name strings from +0x2054 to +0x219C, zeroes the province and terrain vectors, memsets +0x2220 (0x400 bytes, to 0) and +0x2620 (0x400 bytes, to 0xFF), builds the engine string hash table at +0x2A50 with 0x1FF buckets, defaults +0x2A80 to 400 and the player tag at +0x2A88 to `---`/0, and finally reserves **14500** entries in the province vector at +0x2200. It also fills six global Hoi3CStrings with the map paths it will read: `default.map`, `cache/time`, `cache/navaldist.bin`, `cache/climate.bin`, `cache/provincecache.bin`, `cache/bboxcache.bin` at VA 0x170C750, 0x170C76C, 0x170C788, 0x170C7A4, 0x170C7C0, 0x170C7DC.

addresses.name: MapPath
addresses.comment: Turns a bare name into a map-relative path: reads the path registry at *[0x1685558] + 0x2CC (the override slot for 'map') and concatenates. The results, read live, are 'map/default.map', 'map/cache/time', 'map/cache/navaldist.bin', 'map/cache/climate.bin', 'map/cache/provincecache.bin' and 'map/cache/bboxcache.bin'. Called from CMap::CMap for those six and from ReadAdjacencyCache/WriteAdjacencyCache for cache/adjacencies.bin. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CMap::LoadMapFiles
addresses.comment: Everything time.log attributes to map.cpp lines 288-636, in one body (0x489BA0..0x48B7CB, 1846 instructions, one ret). Its first act is to compute the cache stamp into CMap +0x2C (call 0x492100 at 0x489C35) and the stale flag into CMap +0x28 (call 0x4921E0 at 0x489C3E). Then: if not stale, ReadAdjacencyCache (0x48A6AC) and skip the rebuild; otherwise build the graph from the province raster (0x4911B0 at 0x48A6B6) and layer adjacencies.csv (0x48E520 at 0x48A6BC). Then 0x48F260, 0x48FAC0, the geometry pass 0x4917A0 and the positions.txt loader 0x48FBB0 - the last two unconditional, so positions.txt is reparsed every launch. Then, only when stale, the CALC_PATHS block (0x48A777) which is map.cpp:597 'calculate paths' and :605 'fix naval distances', and finally WriteAdjacencyCache (0x48AEB8), also only when stale. The single caller is InitMapLogic (rva 0x88200).

addresses.name: LoadProvinceClimate
addresses.comment: Builds every province's base temperature out of map/climate.bmp. One caller, 0x8AE32, in the map build. Samples one byte of the climate image (CMap +0x2108) per province at the province's own pixel position (CProvinceTemplate +0x64 x, +0x68 y) at 0x8BF82, caches the resulting array to and from map/cache/climate.bin, and at 0x8C0DD writes CProvinceTemplate +0x8 = (byte - 100) x 150 + terrain->temperature (CTerrain +0x58), in thousandths of a degree. The 150 is an inline (int)floor(150.5f) from the float at rva 0x120A83C, hoisted out of the loop at 0x8C078; no define reaches it.

addresses.name: ClimateBitmapSample
addresses.comment: movzx edx, byte ptr [edi + eax] - one byte of map/climate.bmp per province, addressed as image->pitch (+0x18) x template->+0x68 plus image->bytes_per_pixel (+0xC) x template->+0x64 into image->pixels (+0x20). One sample point per province, at its own stored position; nothing is averaged over the province's area. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: ProvinceBaseTemperatureStore
addresses.comment: mov dword ptr [ebx + 8], eax - the only write to CProvinceTemplate +0x8 in the image, and therefore the whole origin of a province's base temperature: (climate.bmp byte - 100) x 150 thousandths plus the terrain's own temperature. 0.150 C per index step, so the index is not degrees. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: ReadMapCache
addresses.comment: Deserialises the province graph out of the binary map cache (map/cache/map.bin): per province an int count followed by count raw 20-byte ProvinceEdge records, pushed onto CProvinceTemplate +0x90 at 0x8E16C. One caller, 0x8A6AC. This is where a non-zero ProvinceEdge +0x10 (bearing) and +0xC (distance) actually come from - the two in-code edge builders (0x917A0 and the adjacencies loader 0x8E520) both leave those two fields zero.

addresses.name: WriteMapCache
addresses.comment: The counterpart of ReadMapCache: per province it writes the edge count (0x8E423) and then each 20-byte ProvinceEdge verbatim (0x8E461, push 0x14). Because the record is dumped and restored byte for byte, whatever computes ProvinceEdge +0x10 must run before this and must be somewhere in the image; I did not find it.

addresses.name: CMap::LoadPositionsFile
addresses.comment: Parses map/positions.txt (Tokenizer over CMap +0x2070 at 0x48FC64) and switches on the save token in [ctx+0x20]. Token 0x256 'unit' reads an int pair through 0x4909C0 and writes CProvinceTemplate +0x68/+0x64 unconditionally (0x49009D/0x4900A0); token 0x3D2 'text_position' writes a float pair to +0x3C/+0x40 and ALSO +0x68/+0x64 as truncated ints, but only when is_land (+0x22) is clear (0x48FEA5 jne skips the land case); token 0x2A2 'city' writes floats to +0x4C/+0x50. Each of the two int writes is followed by setting the hemisphere byte +0xA2 from +0x68 against half of CMap +0x2A78, and by a check that the raster at CMap +0x20E0 says the pixel belongs to this province - 'Unit position outside province for #' (land) or '... for seazone #' (sea), on the error channel 0x10004. Called unconditionally at 0x48A73F, so it runs whether or not the cache was used.

addresses.name: ProvinceSouthernHemisphereFlag
addresses.comment: `mov eax,[map+0x2A78]; cdq; sub eax,edx; sar eax,1; cmp [ebx+0x68],eax; setge al; mov [ebx+0xa2],al` in the map loader: CProvinceTemplate+0xA2 is set where the province's y coordinate (+0x68, written two instructions earlier beside x at +0x64) is at or past half the map height. ComputeProvinceClimate uses it to rotate its six-season table by three - half a year - and CWeatherManager::CreateFront uses it to flip a new front's rotation, which is why weather fronts curve the other way in the other hemisphere.

addresses.name: CProvince_StorePort
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry, so it has no calling convention of its own
addresses.comment: mov [ecx+0x354], eax - the only place a CProvince's CPort is set. ecx is the land province looked up out of the map's province array, eax a new 0x1C-byte CPort whose +0x18 holds the adjacent sea province id. Runs at map load, once per land-to-sea adjacency.

addresses.name: ParseIntPair
addresses.comment: Zeroes out[0] and out[1] and fills them from the context's x and y. Used by positions.txt's 'unit' handler at 0x49008B; out[0] becomes CProvinceTemplate +0x64 and out[1] becomes +0x68. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CMap::BuildAdjacencyFromRaster
addresses.comment: Walks the province raster and creates both directions of every edge it finds, as {kind 0, other, 0, 0, 0} - the 20-byte stack record at [ebp-0x54], whose +0x4C/+0x48/+0x44 (crossed_province, distance, bearing) are all zeroed - push_backed at 0x4913D9 and 0x491442. Called at 0x48A6B6, only when the cache could not be used. THIS is the builder FINDINGS-temperature.md attributes to 0x917A0; 0x917A0 is the geometry pass and does not touch edges.

addresses.name: CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces
addresses.comment: `ret 4`, 77 callers. Indexes `CMap +0x2A60` by each province id, takes the per-entry coordinates at +0x2C and +0x30, wraps the x difference against half of `CMap +0x2A74` (the map width), and answers the integer square root of `16 * (dx*dx + dy*dy)` by Newton's method - so **four times the straight-line map distance**, not a path length. Every proximity decision in CAIUnit slot 76 is made with this.
addresses.signature: int __stdcall CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces(int provinceIdA@EAX, int provinceIdB@EDX, CMap* map)

addresses.name: CMap::ComputeCacheStamp
addresses.comment: The number map/cache/time holds. Collects seven paths through 0x492390, calls ChecksumFile (0xAB3D00) on each and returns the plain 32-bit sum. Confirmed three ways: recomputing the seven checksums over the mod's map folder gives 0x856CAC69, CMap +0x2C reads 0x856CAC69 live, and the mod's own map/cache/time contains 0x856CAC69. The same program over the base tfh/map gives 0x93E125C4 and tfh/map/cache/time contains 0x93E125C4, which is the positive control for the file list.

addresses.name: CMap::IsCacheStale
addresses.comment: True means rebuild. Returns 1 when the cache/time path is empty or the file does not exist (FileExists 0xB84A20), otherwise reads four bytes and returns (stored != this->+0x2C) via setne at 0x492290. The arm at 0x4922AB returns 0 when the stream fails to open, which is the opposite polarity, but FileExists has already passed on the line above so it looks unreachable - recorded as written, inferred to be dead. One caller, 0x489C3E; its result goes to CMap +0x28.

addresses.name: CMap::WriteCacheStamp
addresses.comment: Opens map/cache/time with the write flag (0xA6C1B0 with 1) and writes the four bytes of this->+0x2C (0xA6D080 at 0x49233B). One caller, 0x45531B, which is outside the map module - consistent with the file dates in the per-mod user cache folder, where map.bin is written hours before time is.

addresses.name: CMap::CollectCacheStampFiles
addresses.comment: Pushes the seven paths the cache stamp covers, in order: the global map/default.map (VA 0x170C750), then CMap +0x2070 positions.txt, +0x2128 terrain.txt, +0x208C provinces.bmp, +0x20A8 terrain.bmp, +0x210C definition.csv and +0x2054 adjacencies.csv. Takes the map in ESI and never writes esi - trap 11, it is __fastcall with a register receiver, not a __thiscall. Note what is NOT covered: climate.bmp (+0x20EC), rivers.bmp (+0x20C4), continent.txt (+0x2144), region.txt (+0x2160), coastlines.txt (+0x217C) and trees.txt (+0x219C). Since every map cache is gated on the one flag, editing climate.bmp leaves cache/climate.bin stale with no log line.

addresses.name: COrder::GetStance
addresses.comment:
`return this->stance (+0x20)`, two instructions. COrder slot 19, and **no order class overrides it** - COrder's vftable (0x15C589C) and CPatrolOrder's (0x15C6F14) both hold 0x4944C0. ShouldStartNavalCombat's patrol gate tests it against 0; since FINDINGS-airnaval.md records stance as 1 on every order in a running game, that gate is always active in practice.

**buildFindings warns that this body is "folded into 37 classes" - that is a false positive here.** 36 of the 37 slots are slot **19** and every holder is a COrder subclass, so this is one base-class method inherited by its own family, which is what a correctly named base method looks like. The 37th is some unrelated class's slot 0 whose body happens to be the same two instructions. The warning cannot tell a family from a coincidence, so read its list of holders before acting on it - unlike 0xA80690 or 0xABF890, this one really is COrder's.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::IsCarrier
addresses.comment:
`cmp [ecx+0x190], 0; setg al; ret` - three instructions. A carrier is a ship whose `carrier_size` (+0x190) is **above** zero, not a flag byte like the other kind tests, so a definition with a zero or negative carrier_size is not one.

Nothing calls it directly. Its one reference in the image is at 0x8EDDF8, where its address is pushed next to the literal `IsCarrier` in a run of (name, address) pairs alongside `IsValid`, `IsSecondRank` and `GetCompletionSize` - a luabind class registration. So the name is the game's own, the receiver really is the definition in ecx, and the function exists for script rather than for engine code.

addresses.name: CProvince::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Province save writer, slot 2 of CProvince and of CMapProvince. Slot 2 of CPersistent, which the rest of the family calls SaveContents; BiceLib had it as WriteSave, kept as a label. **It is the province's field list in save order**: flags (+0xC4), owner (+0x32C, only when the tag id at +0x330 is set), controller (+0x334, gated on +0x338), underground_owner (+0x38C, gated on +0x390), underground_action (+0x394, skipped when it is 2), one `core` per node of the list at +0x344 (the node *is* the tag, next at node+0xC), capital (+0x2B0, only when true), manpower (+0x320) and leadership (+0x324) when positive, revolt_risk (+0x328) when positive, strategic_resource (the object at +0x18, its name string at +0x30), every building at +0x310, history (+0xD8) when +0xEC is positive, points (+0x34), nationalism (+0x24) when non-null, then the seven goods pools - pool (+0x15C), throughput ([+0x1F8]), last_throughput ([+0x1F4]), drawn ([+0x1A8]), last_drawn ([+0x1A4]), current_producing (+0x268), max_producing (+0x28C) - each skipped when all seven of its goods equal the global at VA 0x1A87818, then weather (+0x68), last_convoy_attack (+0x1C) when the date is more than a year old, out_of_supply_days (+0x20) when positive, and one `modifier` per node of the list at +0x13C. It does *not* write +0x180 (last_pool) or the drawn/throughput buffers directly, only through the two pointers each.

A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CProvince_LoadKey_InfrastructureGate
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [ecx + 0x24], 0xC` where `ecx = building->effect (CBuilding +0xC)`, loaded one instruction earlier at 0x496125, inside CProvince::LoadKey's default (building-name) arm. **This is a MODIFIER id, not a building index.** The identical shape is already recorded in project.json at CBuildingDataBase_RoleByModifierId (rva 0xB78AB), which reads `building->+0xC` and then compares `[eax+0x24]` against 0x2E, 0x2D, 0x4B, 0x0F and 0x66 - MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY, NAVAL_CAPACITY, LOCAL_AA, IC and LOCAL_UNDERGROUND - and the same comparison appears again in SetProvinceBuildingLevel at 0x4A3AED. Modifier 12 is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE (reversing/modifierIds.py), i.e. the building `infra`, so the write two instructions later makes `CMapProvince +0x5C` the province's infrastructure. This closes the blocker FINDINGS-power.md recorded as "which building type index 12 is was not established": `+0x24` was never a building index, so the mod's reordering of buildings.txt is irrelevant to it.

addresses.name: ComputeProvinceLatitude
addresses.comment: void ComputeProvinceLatitude(CMapProvince* province@EDI), bare ret, 0x963F0 to 0x96478. Writes CProvince +0x388: dy = template->centre_y (+0x60) minus CMap height (+0x2A78) / 2; if dy is negative it is set to 0; +0x388 = dy x 1000 / (height/2). Province y grows northward (province 1, Porsangerhalvoya at 71 N, has y 2106 of 2160), so the field is the normalised distance north of the equator in thousandths. One caller: CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25AFAD, in a loop over every province, immediately before ComputeProvinceClimate - so it is recomputed on every entry into a game and never afterwards.

addresses.name: LatitudeSouthernHemisphereClamp
addresses.comment: xor eax, eax on the negative branch of sub eax, ecx (centre_y minus height/2), so every province south of the equator gets CProvince +0x388 = 0. Zero is at or below the 250 cut in ComputeProvinceClimate, which therefore takes its early exit and leaves climate at its default 3 - which BaseTemperature reads as +5.000. So the southern hemisphere has no season, no latitude penalty, and, through IsNight's latitude-scaled month table, no seasonal day length either. The dead abs() at 0x9646D shows abs(centre_y - height/2) was intended. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: LatitudeDeadAbs
addresses.comment: neg eax under test eax,eax; jns - an absolute value taken on CProvince +0x388 that can never fire, because the clamp at 0x96412 has already made the input non-negative. It is the evidence that the clamp is a bug rather than the intent. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: SupplyCapacity
addresses.comment: How much a province can pass on in a day, in thousandths, written through out; unlimited where the province byte +0x2B0 is set. Only reads.

addresses.name: SupplyLoss
addresses.comment: Fills the supplies lost crossing one province, which the daily supply pass adds to the demand it carries to a neighbour and subtracts again on delivery. Starts from defines->supply(+0xAC)(+0x34), **halves it where the province's owner id (+0x330) equals its controller id (+0x338)**, adds a partisan term built from defines->supply(+0x38) and the province's +0x84 when +0x88 is zero, scales the whole thing by the controller's +0xDF8(+0xC), and floors the result at zero. Against the mod's own common/defines.lua the two defines are SUPPLY_TAX and PARTISAN_EFFECT_ON_SUPPLY_TAX.

addresses.name: SupplyLossMuddynessTerm
addresses.comment: In SupplyLoss (0x9DE80, which abuts SupplyCapacity 0x9DD00 and is the function the muddyness term is really in): where the province is not frozen, muddyness x MUDDYNESSSUPPLYTAXMODIFIER/1000 is added into the multiplier applied to SUPPLY_TAX. Mud raises supply losses.

addresses.name: SupplyNeed
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SupplyNeed(CMapProvince* province, int* suppliesOut, int* fuelOut@EDI)
addresses.comment: Fills the per-province supply and fuel need the daily supply pass writes into CMapProvince::need. **Two out parameters and only one of them is on the stack**: the supplies total goes through the stack pointer at [ebp+0xC] and the fuel total through EDI, which the callers keep as a moving pointer into the fuel array. Both are zeroed on entry. It sums CUnit::SupplyConsumption (0x1BB560) and CUnit::FuelConsumption (0x1BB7A0) over the province's `units` (+0x2B8) and over two further unit lists at CMapProvince +0x54 and +0x58 whose meaning is not established. A unit is skipped where the province's controller id is a country at war with the unit's owner, and where either tag is REB; a virtual call on the unit's slot at +0x3C also has to return true.

addresses.name: RunDailyProvincePass
addresses.comment: **The daily pass over one province.** Called once per province from a plain serial loop inside RunDailyPass at 0x682E4B - **not** RunHourlyPass, which it abuts and which image.functionStart wrongly reports for that call site. No TBB task, so it is on the game thread. In order: infrastructure and the resource pools from provinceValues at +0x60/+0x68/+0x70 scaled by the controller's +0xDF8(+0xC4); the acting-capital flag +0x2B0; suppression into +0x28 via 0x49F360; the modifier rebuild 0x49F3E0 behind a local flag; **revolt_risk (+0x328) at 0x49EE0F..0x49EED6**; and an out-of-supply draw when +0x20 is exactly 1. ret 4. The byte at [ebp+0xB] is a local packed into the argument slot's spare bytes, not a second argument. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: DailyClimateRecompute
addresses.comment: call ComputeProvinceClimate at the head of RunDailyProvincePass (0x9EAB0), with no CProvince +0x30 guard - the only gate above it is CProvinceTemplate +0x13D at 0x9EAD5. RunDailyPass runs it once a game day for every province (0x282E4B), so a province's climate band is recomputed daily and is NOT frozen for a session: FINDINGS-weatherfront.md's claim that all six callers are guarded on +0x30 is wrong, this one and the one in CInGameIdler::Enter (0x25AFB3) are not. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: SuppressionInProvince
addresses.comment: The suppression the units standing in one province deliver. Province in eax, out int* the one stack argument, ret 4. Over the Units list (+0x2B8), keeping units whose owner passes 0x4EF7C0 against the province's controller tag, it adds (sum of the unit's regiments' +0x5C) * 1000 / GetMaxStrength() * definition->suppression / 1000, definition being CUnit +0xC8 and suppression CSubUnitDefinition +0x130. **Suppression comes from the unit's own definition, not summed over its brigades** - only strength is. The total is then divided by 10, so a brigade with suppression 2.0 at full strength lands as 200.
addresses.signature: int* SuppressionInProvince(/*eax*/ CMapProvince* province, int* out)

addresses.name: SuppressionNearProvince
addresses.comment: SuppressionInProvince for the province itself plus every province in its adjacency vector (+0x14C..+0x150) that is land (path_node +0x22) and under the same controller (+0x338), so **one garrison suppresses a cluster**. Province in edi, out int* the one stack argument, ret 4. Its only caller is the daily province pass, which stores the result in CProvince +0x28.
addresses.signature: int* SuppressionNearProvince(/*edi*/ CMapProvince* province, int* out)

addresses.name: RebuildProvinceModifierValues
addresses.comment: Rebuilds the province's CProvinceModifier at +0xFC, whose values array is what +0x114 points at. ret 4, ends at 0x4A0673. It folds in the terrain, the buildings (+0x310..+0x314), the province's own modifier list (+0x12C) and the global at 0x1A86208. **At 0x49FBE2 it folds in the occupation policy**: when owner_id (+0x330) differs from controller_id (+0x338) and the controller's tag is not REB, it takes countryDb->byId[controller_id]->statuses(+0xE28)[owner_id]->+0x10 - the COccupationPolicy, which RTTI says derives from CModifier - and adds its whole values array (+0x18) into the province's, one modifier id at a time over ([0x1A86198]-[0x1A86194])/4 entries. **That is the entire occupation penalty**: local_ic, local_resources, local_manpower_modifier, local_leadership_modifier, local_partisan_support and local_revolt_risk from common/occupation_policies.txt reach the game as ordinary province modifiers, and a REB-held province gets none of them. Called from the daily province pass at 0x49EE0A and from the full-revolt path at 0x65BF7A. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: read_static_modifier_manpower
addresses.comment: `mov esi, [edx+0x40]` in RebuildProvinceModifierValues, guarded by `province->manpower > 0` at 0x4A0019 and scaled by that manpower at 0x4A00A1. That is what identifies static modifier database +0x40 as static_modifiers.txt's `manpower` block. Recorded because it is the second of the three slots in that database whose meaning is pinned by what the engine scales it with, rather than guessed from the file's order - which does not match the field order.

addresses.name: read_static_modifier_revolt_risk
addresses.comment: `mov ecx, [esp+0x14]; mov eax, [ecx+0x48]` in RebuildProvinceModifierValues - the static_modifiers.txt `revolt_risk` block, taken off the database at [0x1A86208]. The block reached from here (0x4A0543..0x4A0689) copies it into a fresh CStaticModifier (0x48 bytes, vftable 0x15BC568), scales every value by the province's effective revolt risk floored at MINIMUM_REVOLT_RISK (0x45A080 at 0x4A05DB - a shared CModifier helper that does `values[id] = values[id] * factor / 1000` over every modifier id, and 0x45A020 beside it is the value-copy), adds the result into the province's modifier values and records the copy in the province's contributor list. Only runs when that risk is strictly positive (0x4A053D). So **static_modifiers.txt's revolt_risk is multiplied by the revolt risk in percentage points** - in BlackICE, -2 % local IC, manpower and resources per point.

addresses.name: GetProvinceAttrition
addresses.comment:
**The only reader of the `attrition` modifier off a province's own modifier** (`[province + 0xFC + 0x18]`, entry 7, read at `0xA09CD`). `ApplyAttrition` calls it once per subunit at `0x1C75AE` and scales the result by a global and by the subunit's maximum strength.

Three callers in all: `0xA19BF`, `0x1C75AE` and `0x3593E3`.

**No signature recorded** - what it takes beyond the province, and how, was not read.

addresses.name: ProvinceAttritionWeatherTerm
addresses.comment: `call CWeather::AttritionEffect` in GetProvinceAttrition, on province+0x68 with the unit's owner tag. Where the province's temperature is negative the leader/HQ effect of type 6 (CUnit 0x1D1120) is added to it, and the sum is floored at 0 before going into the province's attrition.

addresses.name: BuildAttritionTooltip
addresses.comment: **Attrition broken into its causes**: TERRAIN_ATTRITION, ATTR_INFRA, ATTR_WEATHER, ATTR_TECH, plus IN_FRIENDLY_FOR_ATT, IN_HOSTILE_FOR_ATT and IN_FRONT_PROV_ONLY_10. Extent 0x4A0BA0..0x4A1CCB, `ret 0xC`, one caller 0x75AEF7 inside CUnitStatusEntry slot 13 (0x35AE20). [ebp+0x10] is a polymorphic object asked its slot 9 at 0x4A0BEE; **false empties the out string and returns at once**, so the whole tooltip is gated on it. [ebp+0xC] is the out Hoi3CString and the function constructs it (0x4A0BF8). The first argument was not identified. The several `mov byte [reg+0x58],1` inside are locals - sub-tooltips - not the out. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall BuildAttritionTooltip(void* unknown, Hoi3CString* out, void* unit)

addresses.name: SetProvinceBuildingLevel
addresses.comment: 0x4A39B0-0x4A3B59, `ret 0xC`, receiver in **ESI**, three stack arguments. Trap 3: its first `ret 0xC` is at 0x4A3AD2 and the main path is the block after it, reached by the `jne 0x4A3AD5` at 0x4A39E1. It sets `province->buildings[definition->index]->level_max (+0x20)` and `level_current (+0x24)` to `level`, and then - **when the definition's modifier is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE, `definition->effect(+0xC)->id(+0x24) == 12`** - recomputes `province->+0x5C = level * definition->effect_size(+0x8) / 1000`. With `notify` set it raises a message through 0x47F540 when the old value was under g_FixedPoint0_200 and the new one over g_FixedPoint0_100, and finally rebuilds the province's modifiers through 0x49F3E0. Eight callers. **One of five writers of `CMapProvince +0x5C`**, which FINDINGS-power.md recorded as having exactly one - the others are CProvince::CProvince (0x494767, zero), the province building reset 0x496480 (0x496680, zero), CProvince::LoadKey (0x496152) and CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged (0x4B8024). Its opening also special-cases MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY (0x2D) on a province whose template +0xA4 is zero, reporting through 'province.cpp'. The name is from the body.
addresses.signature: void __fastcall SetProvinceBuildingLevel(CProvince* province@ESI, CBuilding* definition, int level, bool notify)

addresses.name: GetProvinceEffectiveRevoltRisk
addresses.comment: **The effective revolt risk**, thousandths of a percentage point: the accumulated +0x328, but only when the controller IsEnemy (0x42F1B0) of the owner; plus countryValues[MODIFIER_GLOBAL_REVOLT_RISK] ([[c+0xDA8]+0x10]), taken from the province's **owner** when the controller is REB and from the controller otherwise, and skipped when controller_id is 0; plus provinceValues[MODIFIER_LOCAL_REVOLT_RISK] ([[p+0x114]+0x8]); minus the province's suppression (+0x28). Its address is taken nowhere, so it has a register convention: province in edi, out int* in esi, one dword pushed and left for the caller, plain ret. **It does not apply the MINIMUM_REVOLT_RISK floor** - that is the whole difference between CRevoltRiskTrigger and CPureRevoltRiskTrigger.
addresses.signature: int* GetProvinceEffectiveRevoltRisk(/*edi*/ CMapProvince* province, /*esi*/ int* out)

addresses.name: GetProvinceRawRevoltRisk
addresses.comment: Three instructions: writes the province's raw accumulated revolt_risk (+0x328) through the out pointer. One call site, 0x5FE390, and in no vftable. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: SetProvinceRevoltRisk
addresses.comment: 0x4A40F0, ret 0xC: __stdcall(CProvince* province, int value, bool announce). Writes max(value, 0) into province->revolt_risk (+0x328) at 0x4A411A/0x4A4120 and, when announce is set, allocates 0x18 bytes and builds a change report through 0x5FE2D0. The companion to GetProvinceRawRevoltRisk (0x4A40E0). Four call sites: 0x4C1301 inside CreateRebelBrigadesInProvince, which calls it as (province, 0, false) - **creating rebel brigades in a province resets that province's revolt risk to zero** - plus 0x5FE3EB, 0x5FE410 and 0x9A55E3.

addresses.name: CProvince::HasHostileLandNeighbour
addresses.comment: Body 0x4A56B0-0x4A57C9, ret 4, read end to end. False at once when the province is unowned (+0x330 == 0) or has no edges. Then over the CProvinceTemplate edge vector (+0x90/+0x94, 0x14-byte ProvinceEdge): skip kind 3 (the impassable kind CPathFind::MayStep also refuses), skip a neighbour whose template is not is_land, skip one whose area fails the area's slot 0, skip one with our own controller id, skip one whose controller is not an enemy by CCountry::IsEnemy (0x42F210, receiver in ESI, &this->controller in EDX). The first survivor answers true - unless the bool argument is set, in which case the neighbour must also hold at least one land unit by CountLandUnitsInList(&neighbour->units) (0x5D5C60). **This replaces the 'isolated / no land link' guess**: the predicate is 'this province is in land contact with an enemy', i.e. it is on a front. All three recorded uses read correctly that way - the 10x penalty in CAIInvasion::PickEmbarkationPort is against loading an invasion in a frontline port, the four hardcoded theatre seats in CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres require !this, and CAIInvasion::UnitCanReachObjectiveOverland needs it true before a unit can be thought to march to the objective. 14 direct callers.

addresses.name: CMapProvince::AddCombat
addresses.comment: Appends the combat to the province's combat list - first at +0x2EC, last at +0x2F0, count at +0x2F4, 0x10-byte nodes { combat, previous, next, byte } - unless a node already holds it. A failed `operator new(0x10)` stores a null and still bumps the count. Two callers: CCombatManager::CreateCombat's tail and 0x16E360, both under the same `if (!combat->slot 8 ())`.

addresses.name: CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind
addresses.comment: Walks province->combats (+0x2EC) and returns true as soon as one combat's slot 11 equals `kind`. Eleven instructions, bare `ret`, both arguments in registers. CCombatManager::StartCombat calls it to refuse a second land, naval or air combat of the same kind in one province.

addresses.name: MessagePopupCallback
addresses.no_signature: `this` in ecx is the popup and the one stack argument is the message, but neither class is named yet, so the types would be two voids.
addresses.comment:
**Passed to PostMessage as its fourth argument at every raise site**, loaded as a bare immediate (`mov esi, 0x4A6040` at 0x100DBE, `mov eax, 0x4A6040` at 0x173A31), and handed on to whichever popup the post builds. Effectively a constant rather than a choice a caller makes.

Takes the message as its one argument, reads the type's name out of it at `+0x20` and dispatches on that name - AIRATTACKTHEM, AIRATTACKUS and the rest.

**Not where a popup's text comes from**, which is what it first looked like. A probe standing on it printed nothing at all for a message that renders correctly, so it is never called while the popup is up - a button's callback rather than a builder. See BuildMessagePopupText for the function that does fill one in.

addresses.name: SpawnFullRevoltInProvince
addresses.comment: **A whole province goes into revolt.** One caller, 0x65BF81, on the in-game screen path, which calls RebuildProvinceModifierValues immediately before and tests the province's controller for REB immediately after - consistent with CSpawnFullRevoltCommand::Execute, though the vftable slot was not checked. It sets revolt_risk (+0x328) to provinceValues[MODIFIER_LOCAL_PARTISAN_SUPPORT] when it is zero, bails when CProvince +0x60 (the CRebelType*) is null, works out +0x64 * max(1, manpower(+0x320)/1000) brigades, finds the faction with 0x686CF0 and calls 0x4BAA20 with the null tag, or 0x686D80 when there is no faction yet.

addresses.name: CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot
addresses.comment: Assigns this province's supply_depot_id - the supply network's label - and marks the network dirty. Does nothing unless the owner's country id (+0x330) is non-zero and the area at +0x2B4 answers true to its virtual slot 0 (CNullOwnerArea does not). The area gets first refusal: where area+0x70 is non-null and either (area+0x70)+8 is above 1 or area+0x69 is 1, a non-zero (area+0x70)+0x10 becomes the label. Otherwise the label comes from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot (0xF2B00) called on the controller's country. Afterwards out_of_supply_days (+0x20) is incremented when the label came out 0 and zeroed when it did not, and g_CCurrentGameState +0x50 is set to 1 so the next tick rebuilds the distances. Called per province from CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25C557 for every province still carrying label 0, from 0x282D3B on the farthest province when its distance exceeded 500, and from 0x9EF5B, 0xA3546 and 0xB8279.

addresses.name: IsNight
addresses.comment: Whether it is night in a province: `(CMapProvince* p@EDI, int hour@[ebp+8], int month@[ebp+0xC])`. Turns CProvinceTemplate+0x64 (the province's x position) into a longitude with CMap+0x2A74 (the map width), adds the hour and 12 and reduces mod 24, picks a month from the second argument where CProvinceTemplate+0xA2 is clear, and scales CProvince+0x388 by a per-month table at 0x130C8B0. Its answer is what UpdateProvinceWeatherRange stores in CProvince+0x2C. The name is inferred from the use and from the daylight arithmetic.

addresses.name: NavalBaseCapacity
addresses.comment: How much a province's naval base can move in a day, in thousandths, written through an out pointer in ESI and also returned. Computes `naval_base->level_current * defines->supply(+0xAC)(+0x274) / 1000`, caching that define in the global at 0x1BEBAB8 behind the flag at 0x1BEBABC, then scales it by `(1000 + controller->modifier.NAVAL_BASE_EFFICIENCY + controller->+0xDF8(+0x7C)) / 1000`. The daily supply pass uses it in phase 3 as the ceiling on what a depot can ship home by convoy. Twenty callers in all, so the name describes what it computes rather than any one use.

addresses.name: ProvinceNavalBaseCheck_OwnerIdTest
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x330], 0` - the same test as the sea-hop gate's, on the same field: +0x330 is the `id` half of CProvince +0x32C `owner`, so it asks whether the province is owned at all. The function it opens (0xA7EE0, reached from 0x81AC1 and 0x81AD0) writes `province->naval_base->level_current` (+0x24) through the out pointer in edi unconditionally, and then **zeroes it again** at 0xA7F6C only where every gate passes: owner.id non-zero, the port at +0x354 non-null, `naval_base->level_max` (+0x20) > 0, a match on the adjacent sea province through the path node at +0xD4, and a true from the call at 0xA7F61. Any gate that fails leaves the level standing.

addresses.name: ComputeProvinceClimate
addresses.comment: Works out and stores CProvince+0x30, a climate zone in 1..5, from CProvinceTemplate+0xA2 and the province's position; called from CWeather::BaseTemperature (0xB22FE) whenever that field is still 0, so it runs once per province. Name inferred from the field it fills and from `climate` being one of default.map's keys.

addresses.name: CountryIdListContains
addresses.comment: 0x4A8630, bare ret: walks the list whose head is [eax] (node id at +0x4, next at +0xC) and returns in al whether any node's id equals [ecx+4]. **39 call sites in 17 functions** across combat, diplomacy, the AI and the revolt roll, so it is a general helper and must not be named after a domain. The 'country id' reading comes from the revolt roll's call at 0x4C0881, where ecx is &country->tag (+0xCA4, so [ecx+4] is the tag's id) and eax is gameState->scenario (+0xD0C) + 0x78; other callers may pass a different id list.

addresses.name: MapProvinceIsLandlockedWater
addresses.comment: Body 0x4A9B70-0x4A9BDE, bare ret, the template in EAX and nothing on the stack. False unless is_land (+0x22) is clear; true at once when +0x14 is set; otherwise true only when every neighbour reached through the edge vector (+0x90/+0x94, each entry's +0x4 indexed into CMap +0x2A60) is itself land - i.e. a water province with no water neighbour. A lake, in other words. CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince uses it at 0x8940FA to insist that a candidate landing province touch real sea rather than a lake. 5 direct callers. Note that image.functionStart answers 0x4A9B33 for this address because the entry's first byte is 0x80 (`cmp byte ptr [eax+0x22], 0`), which is not in the walker's prologue set; the four int3 before 0x4A9B70 say it is a real entry.

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::IsIsolatedLand
addresses.comment: False for a sea zone; otherwise true only when **every** one of the province's edges leads to a water province - a land province with no land neighbour. `this` in EAX, no stack arguments; it walks +0x90..+0x94 and returns false at the first land neighbour. Its use in CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x16AB82) is to exempt such a province from BM_ENVELOPMENT_PENALTY. The name is ours, off the body.

addresses.name: ProvinceEdgeVector::push_back
addresses.comment: The only way an edge is ever added to CProvinceTemplate +0x90, and it has exactly four callers in the image: 0x48E16C (ReadAdjacencyCache, twenty bytes verbatim from the file), 0x4913D9 and 0x491442 (BuildAdjacencyFromRaster, {0,to,0,0,0}) and 0x4A9CD5 (CProvinceTemplate::AddEdge, which adjacencies.csv's loader 0x48E520 reaches). Since none of the four supplies a non-zero bearing, ProvinceEdge +0x10 must be filled in place by a later pass - which was not found. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CTerrain::CTerrain
addresses.comment: `this` in ESI, the terrain id in ECX (stored at +0x8), the name as a 28-byte Hoi3CString by value on the stack, `ret 0x1C`. Writes CTerrain's vftable 0x15C0764 (the RTTI export agrees, 8 slots) at 0xAD80A, 0x18D at +0x4 and +0x10, a second vftable 0x15B6914 at +0xC, 1.0f at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1C/+0x20 and 1 at +0x24, then zeroes +0x48..+0x6C. **Its last act is the one that matters: it compares the terrain's name against five hardcoded strings and sets a byte for each** - `plains` -> +0x68 (0xAD8E9), `mountain` -> +0x69 (0xAD92B), `urban` -> +0x6A (0xAD96A), `desert` -> +0x6B (0xAD981), `arctic` -> +0x6C (0xAD998). So those five flags are not keys in map/terrain.txt at all; they are the engine recognising five terrain names by spelling.
addresses.signature: CTerrain* __fastcall CTerrain::CTerrain(CTerrain* this@ESI, int id@ECX, Hoi3CString name)

addresses.name: CTheatre::CTheatre
addresses.signature: CTheatre* __fastcall CTheatre::CTheatre(CTheatre* this@EAX, int tagChars@stack:4, int tagId@stack:8)
addresses.comment: `this` in EAX (the caller's allocation), the CCountryTag's two halves on the stack. Writes vftable 0x15C0788 at 0x4AEFE7. **CTheatre is 0xA8 bytes** - all seven allocation sites `push 0xA8`. Nine callers, and they are the whole census of who makes a theatre: CCreateHigherCommand::Execute (0x5DFCFB), CAIStrategy::LoadKey's `area_theatre` case (0x8A4699), the six sites inside CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres (0x8AA0DE, 0x8AA419, 0x8AA605, 0x8AA7E6, 0x8AA9C3, 0x8AAB02) and 0x8ACBAA. A second, argument-less constructor 0x4AEEB0 serves CAddTheatreCommand's prototype and clone. **Nothing in the scenario or OOB loader makes one** - the OOB's `theatre =` key makes a CArmy - which closes FINDINGS-oob.md's open question in the negative. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CTheatre::AddFront
addresses.comment: 0x4AF580, ret 0xC, returns immediately when the bool argument is false. Begins by std::vector_assign-ing the front's province vector (front->+0x8) into a local and comparing counts, then loops with a 0x64 seed. Called by the front-driven theatre site in BuildTheatres (0x8AA198) and twice more in the later province-assignment passes (0x8AB357, 0x8AB748). **Only the first ~60 instructions were read** - the name is from the argument types and the call sites, not from the body, and whether it also appends the front to CTheatre +0x50 was not established.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CTheatre::AddFront(CTheatre* theatre, CAreaBorder* front, bool flag)

addresses.name: CTheatre::AddProvince
addresses.comment: Receiver in EAX, ret 4. Appends the province to the saved provinces list at +0x30/+0x34/+0x38 and again to a second list at +0x60/+0x64/+0x68, then stamps the theatre's own id pair onto the province: province->+0x380 = theatre->+0x8 and province->+0x384 = theatre->+0xC, which project.json already carries as CMapProvince::theatre_id_type / theatre_id. Called by four of the six theatre sites in CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres.

addresses.name: CTheatre::AddKeyProvince
addresses.comment: Receiver in ESI, ret 4. Appends the province to +0x40/+0x44/+0x48, which CLASSES.md already identifies as the list the save token `key` fills and names this address (rva 0xAFCE0) as its adder. Its callers in CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres are the four hardcoded-province theatre sites and nothing else, which is why a live game shows exactly three theatres with one key province each (Paris, San Fransisco, Washington D.C.).
