A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::DistanceToTheatreFronts
addresses.comment: 4 callers, all in CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives. Walks the theatre's fronts (CTheatre +0x50) and each front's province array, and answers the smallest CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces from the given province to any of them, seeded at 1000000. It is what makes the AI hand a candidate objective to the theatre whose front line is nearest it.

addresses.name: CWeather::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CWeather::LoadKey(CWeather* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: Eight keys, the whole of a province's weather: `temperature`, `precipitation`, `cloud_coverage`, `humidity`, `muddyness`, `frozen`, `pressure` and `windspeed`.

addresses.name: CWeather::Clamp
addresses.comment: Clamps every field of a CWeather to its range, `this` in EAX: windspeed to [0, 200.000], temperature to [-50.000, 50.000], humidity to [MINHUMIDITY, MAXHUMIDITY], muddyness and frozen to [0, 1.000], and the rest below. Called at the end of CWeather::Update.

addresses.name: CWeather::BaseTemperature
addresses.comment:
int* BaseTemperature(int* out@ESI, CWeather* w@[ebp+8]), ret 4, answers out in EAX; 0xB22E0 to the ret at 0xB2580 with int3 padding up to CWeather::Update at 0xB2590, so no trap-3 funclet. The temperature CWeather::Update chases. out starts at province->path_node_ptr->base_temperature (CProvinceTemplate +0x8 = climate.bmp + terrain.temperature); then, on CProvince +0x30: climate 3 adds 5.000, 4 adds 1.000, 2 adds 1.000, 1 subtracts 1.000 plus a further 1.000 for each of the latitude thresholds 0.950 and 0.650 that CProvince +0x388 exceeds, and 5 subtracts 4.000 plus 4.000 above 0.650 plus 2.000 above 0.950 and - climate 5 only, and only while the running total is below -3.000 and frozen is at 1.000 - a wind chill of windspeed x 0.125 plus a flat 5.000. Night (CProvince +0x2C) costs 2.000 in climates 1-4 and 5.000 in climate 5. Two terms are common to every climate: cloud_coverage x CLOUDCOVERAGETEMPERATUREDROP is subtracted when the total is above 10.000 OR the province is not land (0xB2532-0xB254C), and a further 4.000 when the total is below 3.000 and precipitation is above zero. NOTE: project.json already carries this name at this rva with confidence inferred; this is the same function read in full, so the new content is the comment and the confidence.

*(Upgraded from `inferred` to `confirmed` on 2026-10-01: the function was read instruction by instruction, and the model it implies was checked end to end against a savegame - the coldest 30 provinces all sit at the -50.000 clamp that this arithmetic predicts for an arctic terrain on the bitmap's coldest index at night in band F. See reversing/FINDINGS-temperature.md.)*

addresses.name: WinterWindChillTerm
addresses.comment: imul dword ptr [CWeather+0x10] against the inline (int)floor(125.5f) from the float at rva 0x120A9E4, divided by 1000 at 0xB2512 - windspeed x 0.125 degrees of wind chill, followed by a flat 5.000 at 0xB2519. Reached only in the climate 5 branch, and only when the accumulated base temperature is below -3.000 (0xB24DA) and frozen is at 1.000 (0xB24E2). The only place in the image where windspeed affects temperature. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: CloudTemperatureDropTerm
addresses.comment: imul dword ptr [0x130CAC4] (the cached CLOUDCOVERAGETEMPERATUREDROP) against CWeather +0x24, divided by 1000, subtracted from the base temperature. The branch above it (0xB2532 cmp against 10000, 0xB2543 the land flag) means it applies at sea unconditionally and on land only where the base temperature is already above 10.000 C. (The line in `source` is provisional - the findings file could not be written from here, so it must be re-checked against the file once it exists.)

addresses.name: CWeather::Update
addresses.comment: One province's weather, one hour. `this` in EDI, no stack arguments. In order: takes the province from CWeather+0x2C, is_land from its CProvinceTemplate+0x22, and the CWeatherFront over it from CProvince+0x14 (caching it in CWeather+0x28; where there is none the windspeed decays by a compiled-in 0.980). It reads the terrain's own `humidity` (CTerrain+0x60, at 0xB25F4) and uses `50.000 - terrain.precipitation` (CTerrain+0x64, at 0xB2708) as a target, and writes humidity, precipitation and cloud_coverage - the exact interpolation was not read line by line. Then muddyness and frozen: muddyness RISES (0xB28F7) while it rains or while frozen ground sits above -5C, and otherwise DRIES by max(infrastructure effect, 2) per hour, where the infrastructure effect is the province modifiers MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE x (1000 + LOCAL_ + GLOBAL_INFRASTRUCTURE)/1000 capped at 1000; it is zeroed outright below -5C. frozen rises by HOURLYFROZENINCREASE below -5C with precipitation over 0.250, by fractions of it in the drier cold branches, and falls by HOURLYTHAW above 0C. Calls CWeather::BaseTemperature (0xB22E0) and CWeather::Clamp (0xB2210).

addresses.name: WindspeedDecayNoFront
addresses.comment: `imul dword ptr [0x1686F3C]` in CWeather::Update, bytes f7 2d 3c 6f a8 01, then /1000: windspeed = windspeed * 750/1000 an hour wherever no front is over the province. [0x1686F3C] is floor(750.5) = 750. CORRECTION: project.json's CWeather+0x10 comment and the weather survey both say 0.980 here; 0.980 is [0x168703C], a different global, which is the humidity and pressure transfer factor in CWeatherFront::SpreadWeather. The hourly windspeed decay is 0.750.

addresses.name: PrecipitationFromCloud
addresses.comment: `movss xmm0,[0x120A5F4]` (2000.5) feeding floor+__ftol2 and then `imul esi` on (cloud_coverage - threshold): precipitation = 2.000 x (cloud_coverage - threshold), clamped to [0, 1.000] by CWeather::Clamp, where threshold is 0.500 at sea, 0.250 on land under a front and 0 on land with no front. The 2.000 is an inline floor of a float literal, not a define and not even a cached static, so nothing in defines.lua moves it. Verified against autosave.hoi3 on 2092 of 2092 provinces.

addresses.name: RainConsumesHumidity
addresses.comment: `sub dword ptr [edi+8], eax` in CWeather::Update, with eax = precipitation * floor(10000.5)/1000 = 10 x precipitation. Together with the cloud burn-off four instructions earlier it runs ONLY where the province has no weather front (guarded at 0xB27B8), which is why a front means persistent rain: under a front neither the cloud nor the humidity that feed the rain are consumed.

addresses.name: TemperatureClimateMultiplierSignGate
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [ebp-8], 0; jle` in CWeather::Update, where [ebp-8] holds TEMPERATURECHANGESPEED. It gates the climate-3 x10 multiplier on the define being POSITIVE, and the twin test at 0xB2A56 gates a climate-5 x2 multiplier on it being NEGATIVE. Since TEMPERATURECHANGESPEED is 0.075 in BlackICE and positive in vanilla, the climate-5 branch is unreachable dead code. The direction of the temperature step is decided separately at 0xB2A92, so the sign is not doing double duty.

addresses.name: CWeather::AttritionEffect
addresses.comment: How much of the weather attrition a unit takes, in thousandths: `this` in ECX, `int* out` in ESI, a CCountryTag on the stack (`ret 8`; only the id half at [ebp+0xC] is used). 1.000 when temperature >= HIGHTEMPERATUREATTRITIONTHRESHOLD, scaled by (1000 - the owner's MODIFIER_JUNGLE_EFFECTS)/1000 where the province's terrain has a POSITIVE `humidity` (CTerrain+0x60 > 0); 1.000 scaled by (1000 - MODIFIER_WINTER_EFFECTS)/1000 when temperature <= LOWTEMPERATUREATTRITIONTHRESHOLD; a flat 1.000 when windspeed >= WINDATTRITIONTHRESHOLD; otherwise 0. Called only from GetProvinceAttrition (0xA0990).

addresses.name: CWeather::LandCombatEffect
addresses.comment: The land combat weather penalty, in thousandths: `(CWeather* w@[ebp+8], int* out@[ebp+0xC], CCountryTag tag@[ebp+0x10])`, `ret 0x10`. rain = min(precipitation x (windspeed + 5000)/1000 x LANDRAINIMPACTMODIFIER/1000, LANDRAINIMPACTCAP). Below LANDLOWTEMPERATURETHRESHOLD it adds (-(threshold + temperature))/20 x LANDLOWTEMPERATUREIMPACT/1000 x (1000 - the country's MODIFIER_WINTER_EFFECTS)/1000. Above LANDHIGHTEMPERATURETHRESHOLD it adds LANDHIGHTEMPERATUREIMPACT, scaled by (1000 - MODIFIER_JUNGLE_EFFECTS)/1000 where the terrain's `humidity` is positive. The answer is a POSITIVE penalty; the caller negates it.

addresses.name: CWeather::AirCombatEffect
addresses.comment: The air combat weather penalty, in thousandths: `this` in EDI, `int* out` in ESI, `ret 8` (the eight bytes the callers push are a CCountryTag the body never reads - so no country modifier touches air weather). windspeed x AIRWINDSPEEDMODIFIER/1000, plus AIRLOWTEMPERATUREIMPACT at or below AIRLOWTEMPERATURETHRESHOLD, plus AIRHIGHTEMPERATUREIMPACT at or above AIRHIGHTEMPERATURETHRESHOLD, plus cloud_coverage x AIRCLOUDMODIFIER/1000, plus precipitation x AIRRAINMODIFIER/1000.

addresses.name: CWeather::BombCombatEffect
addresses.comment: The same computation as CWeather::AirCombatEffect (0xB4130) against the BOMB* defines, for a bombing raid's bomber side. `this` in EDI, `int* out` in ESI, `ret 8`, the pushed CCountryTag unread.

addresses.name: CWeather::MovementEffect
addresses.comment: The weather term in a land unit's movement speed, in thousandths and NEGATIVE: `this` in EDI, `int* out` in ESI, a CCountryTag by value on the stack (`ret 8`). out = (frozen == 0 ? muddyness x MUDDYNESSMOVEMENTMODIFIER/1000 : 0), plus COLDMOVEMENTMODIFIER x (1000 - the country's MODIFIER_WINTER_EFFECTS)/1000 when temperature < LANDLOWTEMPERATURETHRESHOLD, then floored at the compiled-in -989 (g_WeatherMovementFloor, 0x1687030). So frozen ground pays no mud penalty, and with BlackICE's MUDDYNESSMOVEMENTMODIFIER -0.75 and COLDMOVEMENTMODIFIER -0.5 the two together (-1250) already hit that floor.

addresses.name: CWeatherFront::SpreadWeather
addresses.comment: How a weather front writes numbers onto the provinces it has just reached: `void SpreadWeather(CWeather* from@[ebp+8], CList<CWeather*>* to@[ebp+0xC])`, ret 8. Called once per province CWeatherFront::Tick is leaving, with the neighbours that province just recruited. rain = from->humidity * 980/1000 ([0x168703C]); from->humidity -= rain/5; then per target: humidity += rain (the whole of it, so a front CREATES humidity), windDelta = (from.wind - to.wind) * 970/1000 ([0x1686FCC]), and where to.pressure > from.pressure also to.pressure -= (to.p - from.p) * 980/1000 and windDelta = max((to.p - from.p) * 250/1000 ([0x1686F98]), windDelta); to.windspeed += windDelta; to.temperature += clamp((from.t - to.t) * 950/1000 ([0x1687068]), -10000, +10000). It writes humidity, pressure, windspeed and temperature and NOTHING else - precipitation, cloud coverage, muddyness and frozen are all manufactured later in CWeather::Update. No Clamp call, so all four may be out of range until the province's own Update runs.

addresses.name: CWeather::GraphicName
addresses.comment: Picks the weather's display/graphic string, `this` in EAX, bare `ret`, answering one of seven std::strings at 0x130CAF0..0x130CB98. Snow and snowstorm when precipitation is over GFX_SNOW_LIMIT and temperature under -5.000, rain and storm over GFX_RAIN_LIMIT with GFX_STORM_LIMIT on the windspeed, otherwise cloud / partial cloud / clear on cloud_coverage against GFX_CLOUD_LIMIT and GFX_PARTIAL_CLOUD_LIMIT. This is the only reader of all six GFX_* defines and it is cosmetic - nothing in the simulation asks it anything.

addresses.name: IsAngleWithinArc
addresses.comment: `bool IsAngleWithinArc(int value@[ebp+8], int centre@[ebp+0xC], int half@[ebp+0x10])`, bare ret. A circle of 1000 units: hi = (centre+half)%1000, lo = (centre-half)%1000, and the answer is lo <= value <= hi, or value >= lo || value <= hi where the window wrapped. Its only caller is CWeatherFront::Tick (0xB48CE), which asks whether a neighbour's bearing (ProvinceEdge+0x10) lies within the front's spread arc of the front's heading (CWeatherFront+0x08). The C `%` keeps the sign, so a window straddling 0 produces a negative lower bound rather than wrapping.

addresses.name: CWeatherFront::CWeatherFront
addresses.comment: `CWeatherFront* ctor(this@[ebp+8], CMapProvince* home@[ebp+0xC], int direction@[ebp+0x10], int rotation@[ebp+0x14])`, ret 0x10. Writes the save token `none` at +0x04 and the vftable 0x15C08B8, zeroes the CList at +0x0C..+0x18, pushes `home` onto it so the front starts one province wide, then +0x20 = rotation, +0x24 = 0 (so the first Tick moves it immediately), +0x08 = direction, +0x1C = home. Finally it DROPS THE HOME PROVINCE'S PRESSURE by `LOWPRESSUREBASE + 1000 * (Random() % (LOWPRESSUREOFFSET/1000))` and calls CWeather::Clamp - that is the low pressure zone. The `idiv` at 0xB4595 has no zero check, so LOWPRESSUREOFFSET below 1.0 in defines.lua is a division by zero on the first front created. Called only from CWeatherManager::CreateFront (0xB5F2C), which allocates 0x28 bytes.

addresses.name: NewFrontPressureDropDivide
addresses.comment: `idiv edi` in CWeatherFront::CWeatherFront with edi = LOWPRESSUREOFFSET/1000, taking `Random() % (LOWPRESSUREOFFSET/1000)`. There is no zero check anywhere on the path, so a defines.lua `LOWPRESSUREOFFSET` below 1.0 divides by zero the first time a weather front is created - inside the first game hour. The flagged limit for the mod.

addresses.name: CWeatherFront::~CWeatherFront
addresses.comment: The destructor body, `this` in EDI, bare ret: writes its own vftable, clears CProvince+0x14 on every province the front covered, frees the list nodes and zeroes the CList. Reached through the scalar deleting destructor at vftable slot 0 (0xB1FC0), which calls it with ecx moved to edi and then frees the object when its flag argument is set.

addresses.name: CWeatherFront::Tick
addresses.comment: One weather front, one hour: `(CWeatherFront* f@[ebp+8])` -> bool, `ret 4`. Decrements f+0x24 (the loader's `speed`, used as a countdown); while it is still positive the front only re-stamps itself onto CProvince+0x14 for every province on its list at f+0xC and answers true. At zero it resets f+0x24 to WEATHERMOVEMENTDELAY/1000 and moves the front on across the map, answering false when the front has run out - which is what makes CWeatherManager::Tick free it.

addresses.name: FrontPressureThresholdTest
addresses.comment: `sub eax,[g_PRESSURETHRESHOLD]; cmp eax,edx` in CWeatherFront::Tick - the ONLY reader of PRESSURETHRESHOLD in the whole image. It refuses to spread into a neighbour whose pressure exceeds the current province's by more than the define. CWeather::Clamp holds every pressure inside [PRESSUREMIN, PRESSUREMAX], a span of 220 at BlackICE's 870/1090, so at PRESSURETHRESHOLD = 300 the test can never fire and the define is effectively dead; it would start to bite below 220.

addresses.name: CWeatherFront::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Vftable slot 2, so a weather front IS written to a savegame. Five keys, which is what names the whole class: `direction` (token 76) from +0x08, `rotation` (382) from +0x20, `speed` (109) from +0x24, `home` (596) as the home province's id out of [+0x1C + 0xD0], and `provinces` (476) as a block of one id per node of the CList at +0x0C. direction and rotation go through the thousandths formatter 0x6694C0 (so 739 prints as `0.739`) and are read back by the thousandths parser 0x669550 - the round trip is intact. `speed` uses sprintf "%d" and plain atoi, so it is a whole number of hours. The "%d" push at 0xB4A51 is only the compact-writer branch, taken when writer+0xC is set.

addresses.name: CWeatherFront::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CWeatherFront::LoadKey(CWeatherFront* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: A weather system: where it is, which way it is going, how fast. **The keys its switch names**, 5 of them, one case each: `direction`, `home`, `provinces`, `rotation`, `speed`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CWeatherManager::InitialiseWeatherState
addresses.comment:
**The one-time weather setup, and the reason a `GetDefines` scan finds no reader of the weather block at all.** It does two things, which is why two surveys named it differently in the same wave. It copies 49 of the 56 `weather` defines (`CDefines +0xEC`) into individual globals, one `mov ecx,[eax+0xEC]; mov edx,[ecx+N]; mov [global],edx` per define - so every consumer afterwards reads a bare absolute address and the block is never touched again. It also fills `CWeatherManager +0x18`'s per-zone countdown vector, which is why `CWeatherManager::Tick` (rva 0xB5A20) calls it when that vector is empty.

Extent: one function from 0x4B54F0 with `int3` padding at 0x4B59BC, and **no `ret` anywhere between 0x4B54F0 and the cache write at 0x4B58A7** - so the cache is inside it. 0x4B5670, proposed elsewhere as the cache's own entry point, is not a function start; it decodes as garbage.

This is a **third** way a define hides from a `call GetDefines (0x445D90)` scan, after inlining: the block is read once at startup and never again. scratchpad/naval/definecache.py recovers 49 such globals. See reversing/FINDINGS-navaldetection.md and reversing/FINDINGS-weather.md.

addresses.name: CWeatherManager::ResetZoneState
addresses.comment: `void ResetZoneState(CWeatherManager* this@EAX)`, bare ret, one caller (0x28256B). Sets every entry of the per-zone heading cache at +0x28 to [0x168701C] - a global nothing in the image writes, so zero, meaning "pick a fresh random heading" - and every per-zone cooldown at +0x18 to 0, so every low pressure zone may spawn again at once.

addresses.name: CWeatherManager::Tick
addresses.comment: The global half of the weather, once an hour. `this` in EDI (g_CCurrentGameState+0xAEC); called only from RunHourlyPass at 0x2826F3 and from the new-game setup loop at 0x3DC89. In order: (1) fills the per-zone cooldown vector at +0x18/+0x1C if it is empty (0xB54F0) and decrements every entry; (2) for each province id on CMap+0x21C8 - default.map's `high_pressure_zones` - calls PropagateHighPressure (0xB6050); (3) while the number of live fronts (+0x10) is below (the number of `low_pressure_zones` on CMap+0x21D8) x MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE/1000 - which is 19 x 8 = 152 with BlackICE's default.map - makes another front with 0xB5D80 and links it; (4) clears CProvince+0x14 on every province in the game state's vector at +0xB8C; (5) ticks each front (0xB4620), unlinking and freeing the ones that answer false.

addresses.name: WeatherFrontMarkInsteadOfUnlink
addresses.comment: `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` in CWeatherManager::Tick: while that byte is set, a spent front's list node is marked (node+0xC = 1) instead of being unlinked, although the front object is deleted either way. The manager is embedded at CGameState+0xAEC, so the byte is CGameState+0xB00; of the eight instructions in the image that touch [reg+0xB00] the only write to a CGameState is `mov byte ptr [ebx+0xb00], 0` at 0x27D1D9 inside CGameState::CGameState. NOTHING EVER SETS IT, so this path is dead - and would be a use-after-free if it ran, because the walker at 0xB5CA4 dereferences node->data without testing node+0xC.

addresses.name: CWeatherManager::CreateFront
addresses.comment: Makes one CWeatherFront: picks a low pressure zone whose cooldown at CWeatherManager+0x18 has run out, reads MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE at 0xB5E47, and returns the front (or null). Called only from CWeatherManager::Tick at 0xB5AD4 and 0xB5B49. The name is inferred from its one caller and its return being linked onto the front list.

addresses.name: LowPressureZoneClimateMask
addresses.comment: `mov eax,1; shl eax,cl; test ebx,eax` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront, with cl = CProvince+0x30 (the climate zone, 1..5) and ebx the second dword of the CMap+0x21D8 record - i.e. the number after the `=` in default.map's `low_pressure_zones`. So that number is a BITMASK OVER CLIMATE ZONES, and because the zones are numbered from 1 its bit 0 is wasted while bit 5 (value 32) is needed for climate 5: the ubiquitous `31` covers climates 1-4 only, and 62 or 63 would cover all five. Vanilla uses the same values, so this is an engine/vanilla trait rather than a BlackICE mistake. Note this branch skips the zone WITHOUT advancing the index into the manager's per-zone cooldown and heading vectors.

addresses.name: FrontHeadingStep
addresses.comment: `add edi, eax` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront, with eax = 1000000 / MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE and edi the zone's cached heading, then wrapped by `if (edi > 1000) edi -= 1000`. So MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE does two jobs: /1000 it caps the fronts one zone may have alive, and here it sets the angle between successive fronts from that zone - at BlackICE's 8 that is a step of 125, one eighth of the compass. Confirmed in autosave.hoi3: zone 13833's eight live fronts read 0.060, 0.185, 0.310, 0.435, 0.560 and the same 0.125 lattice appears in every multi-front zone.

addresses.name: LowPressureZoneCooldown
addresses.comment: `call Random; idiv 0x30; add edx,0x18; mov [esi+ebx],edx` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront: after a zone spawns a front its cooldown is set to 24 + Random() % 48 hours. Hardcoded - no define touches it - so one low pressure zone produces a front every 24 to 71 hours at best.

addresses.name: FrontRotationHemisphereFlip
addresses.comment: `cmp byte ptr [eax+0xa2], 0 ... neg ebx` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront: a new front's rotation is +[0x1686FC8] (= 10) in one hemisphere and -10 in the other, chosen by CProvinceTemplate+0xA2. Confirmed in autosave.hoi3, where the surviving non-zero rotations include -0.003 and -0.008 alongside +0.001..+0.008.

addresses.name: CWeatherManager::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CWeatherManager::LoadKey(CWeatherManager* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: One key, `front`, which is where each CWeatherFront in a save comes from.

addresses.name: CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure
addresses.comment: Pushes pressure outward from one high-pressure-zone province, `this` (the seed CMapProvince) in ECX. Sets CProvince+0x10 to 99999 on every province, the seed's pressure to PRESSUREMAX and its +0x10 to 0, then breadth-first over the province graph (CProvinceTemplate+0x90/+0x94 edges, the neighbour id at edge+4 through CMap+0x2200, the step cost at CProvinceTemplate+0x24): for a neighbour reached at distance d, target = seedPressure - d x PRESSUREREDUCTION/1000, and where that beats the neighbour's own pressure the neighbour's pressure rises by PRESSUREPROPAGATION and the walk continues through it while target stays positive. So a high pressure zone raises pressure by one PRESSUREPROPAGATION step per hour out to wherever the reduction exhausts it.

addresses.name: HighPressureScratchReset
addresses.comment: `mov edi, 0x1869f` and the loop that follows: PropagateHighPressure begins by writing 99999 into CProvince+0x10 on EVERY province. It runs once per high_pressure_zones entry per hour, so BlackICE's nineteen highs cost about 95,000 stores an hour before any pressure is propagated - the one place in this subsystem where a long list in default.map has a measurable cost.

addresses.name: HighPressureTargetReduction
addresses.comment: `imul eax,eax,0x3e8; imul dword ptr [g_PRESSUREREDUCTION]; ... /1000` in CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure. The x1000 and the /1000 cancel, so the target pressure for a province at accumulated cost d is PRESSUREMAX - d * PRESSUREREDUCTION with both already in thousandths - NOT `- d * PRESSUREREDUCTION/1000` as the earlier outline had it. At BlackICE's PRESSUREREDUCTION = 2 the target reaches zero, and the walk stops, at an accumulated cost of 545. The cost is the sum of CProvinceTemplate+0x24 along the path, the same per-province traversal cost CSupply::SpreadFromDepot uses, not a hop count.

addresses.name: CListOfOwned_ClearByPointer
addresses.comment: 63 bytes, bare `ret`, read end to end, 79 callers. Identical to CListOfOwned_Clear (0x81C80) except that the list arrives on the stack rather than in a register: per node it calls the payload's vftable slot 0 with argument 1 (the scalar-deleting destructor), `free`s the node, then zeroes head, tail and count. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits uses it at 0x4D7CC6 to destroy the CProvinceFloat records it allocated.

addresses.name: CBuilding::CBuilding
addresses.signature: CBuilding* __stdcall CBuilding::CBuilding(CBuilding* this, Hoi3CString name, int index)
addresses.comment:
Builds one building definition. Writes CBuilding's own vftable 0x11C09F8 at +0, takes its name as an Hoi3CString by value - 0x1C bytes at [ebp+0xC], which is why the ret is 36 and not 12 - and stores the last argument into index at +0x54.

Recorded mainly so the building-database loader types itself: without a return type the buildings come back as int* and the role ladder's five modifier comparisons stay bare numbers however well CModifier and CBuilding are typed. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CBuilding::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBuilding::LoadKey(CBuilding* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 16 of them, one case each: `capital`, `completion_size`, `confirm`, `cost`, `damage_factor`, `max_level`, `not_if_x_exists`, `on_completion`, `onmap`, `orientation`, `port`, `prerequisites`, `repair`, `show_for_province`, `time`, `visibility`. Inherited by 2 classes in all. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: GetBuildingDataBase
addresses.comment: The buildings singleton, called at 0x637060 before buildings.txt is read and again at 0x639994 near the end of the stage. Extent 0x4B7580..0x4B75DF, bare `ret`. **It abuts its own loader**: 0x4B75E0 begins at the very next byte with no padding, so functionStart(0x4B75E0) answers this function - a new trap 2 pair.

addresses.name: LoadBuildings
addresses.comment: Reads `common/buildings.txt`, resolved-path slot [ebp-0x6d0], called once at 0x637067. Extent 0x4B75E0..0x4B7DB0, `ret 8`. Logs `BuildingDatabase Initialized`, eu3application.cpp:990. Abuts GetBuildingDataBase above it with no padding.

addresses.name: CBuildingDataBase_RoleByModifierId
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry, so it has no calling convention of its own
addresses.comment: The building-role ladder in the building-database loader. eax = building->+0xC, the CModifier the building's one modifier key mapped to, then five compares of the modifier id at CModifier +0x24: 0x2E MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY -> db +0x1C, 0x2D MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY -> db +0x20, 0x4B MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA -> db +0x24, 0x0F MODIFIER_IC -> db +0x2C, 0x66 MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNDERGROUND -> db +0x28. In vanilla and in BlackICE that is air_base, naval_base, anti_air, industry and underground. It is an if/else ladder with no break, so where two buildings carry the same modifier the last one parsed takes the slot. The defaults are set at rva 0xB769B, which points all five slots at the built-in 'nobuilding'.

addresses.name: CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged
addresses.comment: 0x4B7FA0-0x4B8296, `ret 4`, `this` on the stack. Runs after a province building's level has moved, and it is the **live** maintainer of the province's infrastructure field. Gated at 0x4B7FC4 on `this->definition_ptr(+0x18)->effect(+0xC)->id(+0x24) == 12`, MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE, it reads the old value out of `this->province(+0x1C)->+0x5C` into edi and writes the new one as `this->level_max(+0x20) / 10` - the 0.1 of `infrastructure = 0.1` is **hardcoded here as a divide by 10000 after a multiply by 1000**, where CProvince::LoadKey and SetProvinceBuildingLevel both read it out of `CBuilding +0x8 effect_size`. A mod that changed that value on `infra` would therefore make the three writers disagree. It then compares old and new against g_InfraThreshold0_200 (200) and g_InfraThreshold0_100 (100) and, on a crossing in either direction, raises a message through 0x47F540 with the province's controller and invalidates four path or supply caches (0x47FFF0, 0x47FEB0, 0x4807F0, 0x480690) - which is the mechanism behind the `impassable_infra` province flag a savegame carries, and a third independent reason to read `+0x5C` as infrastructure: the two thresholds are infra levels 1 and 2. Four callers: 0x42CC39, 0x485D41, 0x50BF03, 0x57E6E2. The name is from the body.

addresses.name: AddMonths
addresses.comment: Advances a tick-valued date in place by a whole number of months; the date pointer arrives in eax and the count on the stack. Named from its two readers here - CCountry::CanBreakNap, which walks the NAP month windows with it, and the election phase of the country's daily pass, which uses it on last_election. Not read beyond its calling convention.

addresses.name: AreaIsConnectedTo
addresses.comment: Whether two areas are joined overland: it walks the list at COwnerArea +0x34 looking for the other one. CCountry::NeedConvoyToTradeWith is the caller - two acting capitals on different continents need convoys unless this says yes. Both arguments arrive in registers.

addresses.name: CRebelFaction::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRebelFaction::LoadKey(CRebelFaction* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 10 of them, one case each: `army`, `country`, `government`, `id`, `independence`, `name`, `province`, `provinces`, `target`, `type`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: RunDailyRebelFactionPass
addresses.comment: **One rebel faction's daily work.** ret 4. RunDailyPass walks CCurrentGameState +0xC7C (rebel_factions) at 0x682E64 and calls this on each, then unlinks and frees any faction whose +0x90 byte this set - unless CCurrentGameState +0xC88 is set, in which case the node is only marked at +0xC. Two death tests open it: the faction asks to die when the country it belongs to (+0x38) has CCountry +0xCF8 at zero and its type's area (+0x180) is 0, and **also when it has an independence country (+0x44/+0x48) whose +0xCF8 is above zero** - an independence faction ends the moment the country it wanted released exists. It then walks the faction's provinces (+0x94), keeps those controlled by REB with a non-null owner, asks 0x4B98D0(faction, ownerTag, ownerId) about each and builds a list of 0x10-byte nodes from the ones that pass; what that list is for is not established. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CreateRebelsForFaction

The only place that reads a country's countryValues[MODIFIER_PARTISAN_EFFICENCY] ([[c+0xDA8]+0x278] at 0x4BAD3F; 0x628060 is the only other reader and is UI). It **clamps its count argument to 1..4** at 0x4BAACD..0x4BAADD, records the province's pre-revolt owner/controller pair when the province is occupied and the actor is not a government in exile (+0x95), and raises the player message from REBELS / REBELDESC / PROV / REVOLT under MESSAGE_HEAD_MARS. Its body past the clamping was not read. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: rebeltype_is_triggered_only_case
addresses.comment: CRebelType::LoadKey's handler for `is_triggered_only` (token 0x61D). The loader's jump table is at 0x4BFD9C with a byte index table at 0x4BFDD8 and a base of `eax - 0x61D` (0x4BFB72), so token 0x61D is index 0 and lands here: `add edi, 0x19C; push edi; call 0xA7B410`. This is what places the key fieldmap.py could not see.

addresses.name: GetRebelTypeDatabase
addresses.comment: 0x4BFE70 to the bare ret at 0x4BFECF - **no arguments at all**, which is what makes the three pushes before its call sites belong to the next call. The lazy getter for the global at 0x1A871D8: on first use it allocates 0x1C bytes, runs the shared container constructor 0x45BD30 (a 0x1FF-bucket hash at +0x0/+0x4/+0x8 and an empty vector at +0xC/+0x10/+0x14) and installs it through 0x4C06B0. **0x4BFED0 is a different function abutting it with no int3 between**, so image.functionStart is wrong for anything inside 0x4BFED0. Seven callers, including CRebelFaction::LoadKey (0x4B9579), 0x4C1139, CEffect::LoadKey (0x99B3E0) and CCreateRevoltEffect::Execute (0x9A4F19).

addresses.name: LoadRebelTypes
addresses.comment: Reads `common/rebel_types.txt`, resolved-path slot [ebp-0x580], called once at 0x638FFE on GetRebelTypeDatabase' singleton (0x4BFE70, already in the record). Extent 0x4BFED0..0x4C040E, `ret 8`. Logs `Rebel Types Initialized`, eu3application.cpp:1210. TRAPS.md already lists 0x4BFE70/0x4BFED0 as an abutting pair; this is what the two halves of it are for.

addresses.name: ChooseRebelTypeForProvince
addresses.comment: 0x4C0430 to the two ret 0x10 at 0x4C050D and 0x4C06A1. __stdcall(CRebelTypeDatabase* db, CMapProvince* province, bool allowTriggeredOnly, CCountryTag* tag) returning CRebelType*. When the province's controller tag is 'REB' (0x4C0456) it short-circuits to 0x686C60(province)->type (+0x30). Otherwise it builds a CEventScope on the stack (vftable 0x15B8AEC, persistent id 0x18D) whose country is *tag when allowTriggeredOnly and the province's owner (+0x32C/+0x330) otherwise, then walks db->+0xC..+0x10 (a vector<CRebelType*>) and, skipping a type whose is_triggered_only (+0x19C) is set unless allowTriggeredOnly (0x4C063B) and a type whose independence (+0x190) resolves to no area through 0x4BF6F0, evaluates CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays(&type->spawn_chance /* +0x28 */, &scope) at 0x4C0676 and keeps the type with the strictly largest value (0x4C0681). **This is the only reader of CRebelType::spawn_chance**, so that key is not dead: it selects the rebel type, exactly as the mod's own comment in rebel_types.txt says. Five callers: 0x4A43ED, 0x4C113F, SpawnPartisansFromUnderground at 0x50B920 (the only one passing allowTriggeredOnly = true), 0x686DDB and CCreateRevoltEffect::Execute at 0x9A4F1F.

addresses.name: read_rebeltype_spawn_chance
addresses.comment: `lea eax, [esi + 0x28]` immediately before `call CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays` at 0x4C0676, with esi a CRebelType*. **The only reader of CRebelType::spawn_chance in the image**, and the evidence that the key is not dead: the type with the largest value is the one chosen for the province.

addresses.name: RunDailyRevoltRoll
addresses.comment: 0x4C07C0 to the ret 4 at 0x4C0B41. f(CCountry*) on the stack. **This is the revolt roll**, and it has exactly one caller: 0x4DBBC2, inside CCountry's daily pass (0x4DA530, see FINDINGS-politics.md). Returns at once when country->NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) <= 0, when the game state's in_game (+0xDA4) is clear, or when gameState->scenario (+0xD0C) is set and the country's id is not in the list at scenario+0x78 (0x4A8630 at 0x4C0881). Then, for each node of country->province_ids (+0xD00, payload at +0x0, next at +0x8): skip a province whose area (+0x2B4) slot0() is false; set denom = 10000, or 20000 when gameState->+0xBCC[country id] is zero (0x4C0A7D) - so an AI country gets half a human's revolt chance; call GetProvinceEffectiveRevoltRisk (edi = province, esi = &temp) at 0x4C0A87 and floor the result at max(provinceValues[MINIMUM_REVOLT_RISK], 0); compute threshold = round(floorf(20000.5) * risk / 1000 / 1000.0) = round(risk/50) at 0x4C0AA8..0x4C0AF3; then two gates, Random() % denom < threshold at 0x4C0AF6 and Random() % 365 == 0 at 0x4C0B03; and only if both pass, 0x4C1110(province@ESI, "---"@EDI, 3). The 1-in-365 gate makes the whole thing rare: over a year the two gates come to threshold/denom, i.e. effective revolt risk in percentage points / 500 for a human and / 1000 for the AI. See reversing/FINDINGS-revolt.md.

addresses.name: revolt_roll_ai_halves_the_chance
addresses.comment: `mov dword [ebp-0x1c], 0x4E20` - reached when gameState->+0xBCC[country id] is zero, i.e. when nobody is playing the country. It doubles the revolt roll's denominator from 10000 to 20000, so **an AI country gets exactly half a human player's revolt chance**, on top of whatever the difficulty static modifiers do.

addresses.name: revolt_roll_risk_gate
addresses.comment: `call Random; cdq; idiv [ebp-0x1c]; cmp edx, edi; jge` - the first of RunDailyRevoltRoll's two gates. edi is round(effective_revolt_risk / 50) and [ebp-0x1c] is 10000 for a human-played country or 20000 for an AI one. Bytes: e8 85 24 5e 00 99 f7 7d e4 3b d7 7d 25.

addresses.name: revolt_roll_annual_gate
addresses.comment: `call Random; cdq; mov ecx, 0x16D; idiv ecx; test edx, edx; jne` - RunDailyRevoltRoll's **second** gate, a flat 1-in-365 every day on top of the risk gate, and the reason revolts are almost never seen: the two together give threshold/denom per year rather than per day. Bytes: e8 78 24 5e 00 99 b9 6d 01 00 00 f7 f9 85 d2 75 14. Hooking here, or patching the `jne` to a `nop`, is the cheapest way for a mod to make revolt risk matter.

addresses.name: SpawnRebelsOfChosenTypeInProvince
addresses.comment: 0x4C1110 to the ret 4 at 0x4C1156. **Register convention**: CMapProvince* in esi, CCountryTag* in edi, brigade count on the stack. Returns without doing anything when province->area (+0x2B4) slot0() is false or province->path_node->+0x13D (+0xD4) is clear. Otherwise it calls GetRebelTypeDatabase (0x4BFE70, which consumes no arguments, so the three pushes before it survive), ChooseRebelTypeForProvince(db, province, false, tag) at 0x4C113F, and CreateRebelBrigadesInProvince(this=province, type, count, false, tag) at 0x4C114E. Two callers: RunDailyRevoltRoll at 0x4C0B23 with count 3, and the unreferenced console handler 0x43DDE0 at 0x43E03F.

addresses.name: CreateRebelBrigadesInProvince
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CreateRebelBrigadesInProvince(CMapProvince* province@ECX, void* rebelType@stack:4, int count@stack:8, bool arg3@stack:0xC, CCountryTag* actor@stack:0x10)
addresses.comment: **The shared entry for putting rebel or partisan brigades in a province**, five call sites including the underground mobilisation (0x50B92B) and the wrapper 0x4C1110. ret 0x10. It refuses a province in no real area (+0x2B4 slot 0) or whose path node's +0x13D flag is clear, clamps count up to at least 1, finds the faction with 0x686CF0(province, rebelType) and goes to 0x686D80 when there is none. When the province's controller tag is not REB it first calls 0x4B9150(controller tag, controller id), then hands off to 0x4BAA20. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CAlignment::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAlignment::LoadKey(CAlignment* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **One key, `position`**, an `{ x = .. y = .. }` block read by ParsePoint into `this + 8`. That is a country's place on the political compass; everything else is unknown.

addresses.name: CAlignment::ComputeDrift
addresses.comment: Sums the seven alignment terms into CAlignment+0x18[i] for every ideology group i whose slot 6 returns true, then returns SUM of (unit vector toward group i) * values[i] / 1000. Relation (0x4C3950), Ideology (0x4C3B10), Proximity (0x4C3C00) and AlignTowards (0x4C3790) are added; Revanchism (0x4C3E40), Threat (0x4C4120) and Repulsion (0x4C4380) are subtracted and only when the group is within distance 200 (`cmp eax, 0x9C40` on the squared distance, at 0x4C3361). Two callers: CAlignment::UpdateDaily and 0x4FA123.
addresses.signature: Point* __stdcall CAlignment::ComputeDrift(CAlignment* this, Point* out, CCountry* country)

addresses.name: CAlignment::UpdateDaily
addresses.comment: The alignment drift step. Both arguments are registers - the compiler gave it no stack frame arguments and it ends in a plain `ret`. A country in a real faction (slot 7 on CCountry+0xD8) does not drift: unless it is the faction leader its position is **snapped** to the leader's (leader+0xE4/+0xE8). Otherwise it calls 0x4C3200 for the drift vector, 0x4C4B00 to clamp it inside the ideology groups' bounding box, and adds it to +0x8/+0xC. Its one caller is the country's daily pass at 0x4DB87E, gated on today > CCountry+0x124.

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetAlignTowardsTerm
addresses.comment: `ret 8` and the group arrives in **edi**. The seventh alignment term and the only one that reads no `alignment` define: it reads the faction's own ALIGN_TOWARDS modifier (values entry 47, [modifier+0x18]+0x178, through 0x523560) - the thing CFaction's `influence` string `align_towards_axis` names. (1 - leaderEffectiveNeutrality/100) x ALIGN_TOWARDS x ((1 - countryEffectiveNeutrality/100) + [0x1A8732C]). Zero for a country already in a faction, or a faction with no members.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetAlignTowardsTerm(int* out, CCountry* country, CIdeologyGroup* group@EDI)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetRelationTerm
addresses.comment: Zero unless the country is in no faction (CCountry+0xD8 == the null-faction singleton at 0x1A855A8) and the group's faction has members. Otherwise: mean of CDiplomacyStatus+0x38 over every member, x RELATION_WEIGHT (alignment +0x4), x (1 + SUSEPTIBILITY), x (1 + suseptibility_<factiontag>), the latter modifier index taken from CFaction+0xB4.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetRelationTerm(int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetIdeologyTerm
addresses.comment: `ret 8` - the out pointer arrives in **edi**, which the body never sets. A flat term: IDEOLOGY_WEIGHT (alignment +0x8) x (1 + DRIFT_SPEED) when the country is unaligned and its ruling ideology (CCountry+0x1140) passes its slot 17 and belongs to this group (CIdeology+0x50 == group); zero otherwise. Abuts 0xC3C00 with no padding - the `ret 8` at 0x4C3BFD is followed straight by a fresh prologue with its own SEH handler.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetIdeologyTerm(CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country, int* out@EDI)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetProximityTerm
addresses.comment: Zero unless the country is unaligned and the group's faction has members. Takes the **maximum** over members of (10 - capitalDistance/500, floored at [0x1A87334]) x floor(member.maxIC / country.maxIC), then x PROXIMITY_WEIGHT (alignment +0xC) x (1 + SUSEPTIBILITY) x (1 + suseptibility_<factiontag>). The IC ratio is an **integer** divide of CCountry+0x60C before scaling, so a member smaller than the country contributes exactly nothing. Distance is 0x492030 between the two acting-capital provinces.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetProximityTerm(int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetRevanchismTerm
addresses.comment: Subtracted by the aggregator. Zero when the faction holds at least half the world's victory points: s = faction.progress / total victory points (0x522CC0), and the 0.5 comes from floor(500.50003f), the float at 0x160A5E8. Otherwise (number of the country's claims, CCountry+0xD10, whose current owner is in this faction) x (0.5 - s) x 5 x REVANCHISM_WEIGHT (alignment +0x10) x (1 + SUSEPTIBILITY) x (1 + suseptibility_<factiontag>).
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetRevanchismTerm(int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetThreatTerm
addresses.comment: Subtracted by the aggregator. max of CDiplomacyStatus+0x5C over the faction's members, x THREAT_WEIGHT (alignment +0x14) x (1 + SUSEPTIBILITY) x (1 + suseptibility_<factiontag>) x min(base IC / LARGE_COUNTRY_IC, 1) - the last clamp is exactly what defines.lua's own comment on LARGE_COUNTRY_IC (alignment +0x2C) describes. **It also has a dead branch**: the loop tracks whether any member's status has the hostile flag +0x20 and calls GetDefines at 0x4C41EE on the first hit, then discards both; nothing reads either, and WAR_THREAT (alignment +0x28) has no reader anywhere in the image.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetThreatTerm(int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetRepulsionTerm
addresses.comment: Subtracted by the aggregator, and the only term that needs the CAlignment itself (in ecx). base = REPULSION_WEIGHT (alignment +0x18) x (200 - distance to the group), the distance by an inlined integer Newton square root at 0x4C4480. Where the country's ruling ideology is *not* in this group, base is multiplied by (country.maxIC x REPULSION_IC_FACTOR, alignment +0x30) / (leader.maxIC + (members' maxIC - leader.maxIC)/4) when that ratio exceeds 1 - which is defines.lua's own comment on REPULSION_IC_FACTOR, term for term.
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CAlignment::GetRepulsionTerm(CAlignment* this, int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group, CCountry* country)

addresses.name: CAlignment::DistanceSquaredTo
addresses.comment: `ret 8`. Writes ((this->x - other->+0x58)^2 + (this->y - other->+0x5C)^2), each squaring divided by 1000, through `out` and returns it - so the result is a squared distance in thousandths and nothing takes a square root. `other` is a CIdeologyGroup, whose position is at +0x58/+0x5C. Seven callers, three of them the FACTION_*_DIST functions.
addresses.signature: int* __fastcall CAlignment::DistanceSquaredTo(CAlignment* this@ECX, int* out, void* other)

addresses.name: CAlignment::ClampMove
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, with `this` arriving in **eax**. Copies `delta` into `out`, calls 0x4C46C0 to rebuild the bounding box of all ideology-group positions into this+0x28..+0x44, and shortens the move so the resulting position stays inside it. Called by the constructor (to place a new alignment at 0,0) and by CAlignment::UpdateDaily.
addresses.signature: Point* __fastcall CAlignment::ClampMove(CAlignment* this@EAX, Point* out, Point* delta)

addresses.name: CAlignment::IsWithinFactionJoinDistance
addresses.comment: **The gate on faction invitations.** Reads FACTION_JOIN_DIST (alignment +0x1C) through GetDefines, squares it (x itself, /1000) and compares it against CAlignment::DistanceSquaredTo(alignment, faction->+0x8): true when the distance is *less* than the define. The game names it itself - at 0xA3386A the false branch pushes the localisation key 'FACTION_DISTANCE' (0x15FACF4). Five callers: 0x6047C3 and four inside the faction-action validity functions 0xA32FD0 and 0xA33CD0.

addresses.name: CAlignment::IsWithinFactionStratBonusDistance
addresses.comment: Byte-for-byte the same function as 0xC4CD0 with FACTION_STRAT_BONUS_DIST (alignment +0x20) in place of FACTION_JOIN_DIST. Two callers: 0x4FAC8C, inside the function that recomputes all seven alignment terms, and 0x68BFBC.

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetFactionThreatDistanceFactor
addresses.comment: Not a predicate, unlike its two neighbours. *out = distanceSquared * 1000 / FACTION_THREAT_DIST^2 (alignment +0x24), in thousandths, or -1 when the define is zero; returns `out`. The second argument slot is reused as scratch by the inner DistanceSquaredTo call, so the value is read back out of the caller's own frame. Two callers, 0x4F54B9 and 0x4FBE00.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CAlignment::GetFactionThreatDistanceFactor(CAlignment* alignment, int* out, CIdeologyGroup* group)

addresses.name: CAlignment::GetValueForGroup
addresses.comment: Three instructions: *out = this->+0x18[group->+0x50]. Wrong `this` convention to be a plain thiscall - ecx holds the CAlignment but the function is `ret 8` with both arguments on the stack. This is how CIdeologyGroup+0x50 is established as the group's index into the per-group weight vector.

addresses.name: CConvoy::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Convoy save writer; the source of the convoy's saved field names. Slot 2 of CPersistent, which the rest of the family calls SaveContents; BiceLib had it as WriteSave, kept as a label.

addresses.name: CConvoy::LoseShips
addresses.comment:
**What a sunk convoy costs.** `ret 0x18`, six stack arguments, 0xFF0 bytes of which most is message text. One caller, ResolveConvoyRaid at 0x1D26CC.

    transportsLost = min(transportsLost, convoy->transports (+0x98))
    escortsLost    = min(escortsLost,    convoy->escorts (+0x9C))
    if (convoy->is_lend_lease (+0xA1) && transportsLost > 0 && transports > 0)
        f = transportsLost * 1000 / transports                        ; the share sunk, thousandths
        convoy->ll_efficiency (+0xAC) -= LL_CONVOY_EFF_IMPACT (economy +0x4C) * f / 1000
        convoy->ll_efficiency = max(convoy->ll_efficiency, 0)
    convoy->escorts    -= escortsLost
    convoy->transports -= transportsLost
    threat = THREAT_FROM_CONVOYS_MODIFIER (economy +0x30) * (transportsLost + escortsLost)
    0x4F4E80(countries[attackerCountryId], &threat, ...)              ; the threat the raider earns
    ... CONVOY_ATTACK_ON_US / WE_ATTACK_CONVOY messages, keyed convoys_1 and convoys_2 ...
    convoy->last_attack (+0xCC) = gameState->tick (+0xBDC)            ; at 0x4C6903

**There is no direct IC, resource or supply penalty.** The whole cost is the transports and escorts themselves - fewer transports means a lower CConvoy::GetEfficiency, which scales every good the route carries that day, and the ships have to be rebuilt at CONVOY_BUILD_COST / ESCORT_BUILD_COST. The only extra levers are LL_CONVOY_EFF_IMPACT on a lend-lease route and THREAT_FROM_CONVOYS_MODIFIER on the raider's threat.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CConvoy::LoseShips(CConvoy* convoy, int transportsLost, int escortsLost, CMapProvince* where, int attackerTagLetters, int attackerCountryId)

addresses.name: CConvoy::ClearPath
addresses.comment: `this` in EDI. Walks the path list at +0xB0, and for each province whose area (+0x2B4) answers true to its slot 0 calls 0x481760 and 0x4816E0 with that area and 0x4A7550 with the province - deregistering the convoy from the provinces and areas it ran through - then frees every node and zeroes +0xB0/+0xB4/+0xB8. Four callers: RunDelivery's date tail (0xC72FB, the day after an attack), RunCountryDailyPass at 0xDAB94, 0xE7165 (which repaths every one of a country's convoys and then touches is_at_war), and 0xFD3BD. Whether the rebuild happens inside it or in its caller was not read, so the name covers only what was read.

addresses.name: CConvoy::GetEfficiency
addresses.comment: The fraction of a convoy route that is actually running, in thousandths, written through out and also returned. Defaults to 1000, then becomes `transports (+0x98) * 1000 * 1000 / (transports wanted * 1000)` where a helper at 0xC7320 supplies the wanted figure, and is multiplied by +0xAC / 1000 - an unnamed field, most likely the lend-lease efficiency the defines call LL_CONVOY_EFF_IMPACT - when is_lend_lease (+0xA1) is set. The daily supply pass multiplies a depot's NavalBaseCapacity by it once per convoy that ends at the depot.

addresses.name: CConvoy::RunDelivery
addresses.comment:
**The whole convoy economy, in one function.** `ret 4`, convoy at [ebp+8]. It first zeroes the convoy's `daily` pool (the seven dwords at +0x40..+0x58, each from the CFixedPoint zero at 0x1687818) and bails on three gates: path_count (+0xB8) < 2, transports (+0x98) == 0, or CConvoy::IsRouteUsable (0xC7A10) false. **A lend-lease convoy (+0xA1) bails immediately too** - the `jne` at 0x4C6CBB jumps past every transfer to the date tail, so nothing in this function moves a lend-lease load.

Then, with S = provinces[start_province_id], E = provinces[end_province_id] and C = GetCountry(S.controller):

1. **Source pool.** If S.area == GetActingCapitalLocation(C).area, the source is CCountry::GetPool(C) - the national stockpile (C->+0x9F8 when IsGovernmentInExile, else the acting capital province's `pool`). Otherwise it is **S's own `pool` (+0x15C)**, which is why a cut-off port's production piles up there.
2. **Puppet reserve.** If C->overlord_id (+0xF3C) == convoy->owner.id, every good has 1000.000 subtracted, then CGoodsPool::ClampEach(99999.000) (0x123830) floors it at 0.
3. **Efficiency.** All seven goods are multiplied by CConvoy::GetEfficiency (0xC6B80) / 1000.
4. **Naval-base cap.** If S.area == C's acting capital's area, CGoodsPool::ClampEach(NavalBaseCapacity(E)) (0xA75D0) caps **every good** at the destination port's capacity.
5. **Control gate.** If S.controller.id != convoy->owner.id and S.controller is not our puppet, it returns with nothing moved.
6. **Mask.** Every good whose entry in the `ship` vector (+0x5C) is zero is set to zero.
7. **Area headroom.** supplies and fuel are additionally capped (negatives clamped to 0) by the two out-params of AreaSupplyAndFuelHeadroom (0xDD4D0) - 35 days of the destination area's draw less what the area already holds.
8. **Transfers.** The source pool pays; `ConvoyedOut` (+0x7B8) is credited on S.controller and `ConvoyedIn` (+0x794) on E.controller, each only when S.area != E.area; the load lands in **E's `pool`**, or, when S is outside its controller's capital area, in E.controller's national stockpile instead; E's `throughput` buffer (+0x1F8) is credited; and convoy->`daily` (+0x38) records the run.
9. **Repath.** Finally, if GetDays(now) - GetDays(convoy->last_attack) == 1 it calls 0xC6930 to drop the path.

Two callers, both with the same guard set in front: RunCountryDailyPass (0xDA530) at 0x4DAB78, and the supply driver 0x278AB0 at 0x678FC0.

addresses.name: CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports
addresses.comment:
How many transports the route wants, and the only reader of two economy defines. `ret 4`.

    p = (int)floor(path_count + 0.0005) * 1000          ; path_count in thousandths
    p = p * CONVOY_PATH_LENGTH_MULT (economy +0x3C) / 1000
    b = provinces[end_province_id]->naval_base (+0x300)->level_max (+0x20) * 1000 / 10000
    if (convoy->is_trade (+0xA0)) p = p * CONVOY_TRADE_WEIGHT_MULT (economy +0x40) / 1000
    return (b * p / 1000 + 1000) / 1000

So it scales with the **number of provinces on the path** and with the destination naval base's **maximum** level divided by ten - not its current level, which is what NavalBaseCapacity uses. The +1000 before the final divide makes the answer at least 1. The float round trip is `floor` (0x4A75D0's neighbour 0x8084B0 via the wrapper 0x1FD0) then ftol (0x808870) and is an identity on an integer count. The cached copy of the answer is CConvoy +0x90, which the game's own Lua names GetDesiredTransports.

Seventeen callers; the interesting ones are CConvoy::GetEfficiency (0xC6B80, twice) and CConvoy::ComputeDesiredEscorts (0xC7450).

addresses.name: CConvoy::ComputeDesiredEscorts
addresses.comment:
Fills CConvoy +0x94 (the game's own GetDesiredEscorts). `ret 4`. It **adds to** +0x94 rather than assigning, after zeroing it at the top.

    convoy->escorts_wanted = 0
    if (!GetCountry(convoy->owner)->is_at_war (+0xACC)) return        ; adds 0
    want = transports (+0x98) / 2 + 1                                 ; truncating divide
    if (transports <  GetDesiredTransports(convoy)) want += 3
    if (transports > 10)                             want += 4
    d = GetDays(now) - GetDays(convoy->last_attack (+0xCC))
    convoy->escorts_wanted = want + (d < 3 ? 5 : d < 7 ? 3 : d < 15 ? 1 : 0)

**No define anywhere in it** - every number is a literal, so a mod cannot move the escort demand curve. A convoy wants no escorts at all while its owner is at peace. A convoy never attacked has last_attack 0, whose GetDays is -1825000, so the recency bonus is 0.

addresses.name: CConvoy::IsRouteUsable
addresses.comment: `this` in ESI. The gate every delivery site checks before CConvoy::RunDelivery. It returns false at once when either endpoint is unowned - provinces[start_province_id]->owner.id (+0x338) == 0 or the same on the end province - and then, for a convoy that is neither lend-lease nor trade and carries neither supplies nor fuel (ship[0] and ship[1] both zero), takes a different branch from the one a supply convoy takes. Only the entry conditions were read; the body past 0x4C7A8B was not.

addresses.name: CConvoy::GetDefence
addresses.comment:
The number a raider's attack is compared against. `this` in EAX, out in ESI, bare ret.

    d = convoy->escorts (+0x9C) * 5000                     ; 5.0 per escort, hardcoded
    if (convoy->path_count (+0xB8) != 0) d = d * 1000 / (path_count * 1000)
    d = d * (1000 + GetCountry(convoy->owner)->technology_status (+0xDF8)->+0x78) / 1000
    *out = d

So **escort cover is diluted by route length**: five escorts on a four-province route defend as 6.25, the same five on a twenty-province route as 1.25. The 5.0 per escort is a literal, not a define. +0xDF8+0x78 is the escort-efficiency technology effect (the mod's `escort_efficiency` tech key). Two callers, both in ResolveConvoyRaid (0x1D1250): the per-convoy target scan at 0x1D14C0 and the final attack-versus-defence test at 0x1D15BD.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Init
addresses.comment:
`ios_base::_Init()`: zeroes `+8`, `_Except` (`+0x10`), sets `_Fmtfl = 0x201` (`skipws|dec`) at `+0x14`, `_Prec = 6` at `+0x18`/`+0x1C` (a `streamsize` is `__int64` here), `_Wide = 0` at `+0x20`/`+0x24`, `_Arr = _Calls = 0` at `+0x28`/`+0x2C`, calls `std::ios_base::clear(0, false)` for `_Mystate` at `+0xC`, and finally allocates a four-byte `locale` into `_Ploc` at `+0x30`. `ecx` is the receiver, nothing is on the stack, bare `ret`.

**`+0x30` is the highest field it writes**, which together with `_Mystrbuf` at `+0x38` is what bounds `sizeof(ios_base)` at 0x34..0x38.

addresses.name: CDistributionSetting::GetBasePercentage
addresses.comment: Nine instructions: copies the eight bytes at this+8 to *out and returns. **This is the function project.json's CDistributionSetting +0x8 = base_percentage was named from, and it is what makes that name certain.** Registered to Lua as `GetPercentage` at 0x8EC702 - the registration pairs each name with the function pushed after it, which is confirmed in the same call by 'GetNeeded' pairing with 0x414F70, a bare `jmp [vftable+0xC]` thunk on slot 3, the slot the record already gives GetNeeded. No vftable holds it and nothing calls it directly, so Lua is its only consumer. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CCountry::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCountry::LoadKey(CCountry* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: Slot 4 of CPersistent for a country: one key from a save, dispatched on its token id through a tree of comparisons. The value is the CToken at parse +0x228, so a number is read straight out of parse +0x22C. The mirror of CCountry::SaveContents, and the other place a field's save key can be read off.

addresses.name: CCountry::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CPersistent for a country: the whole of what a country writes into a save, key by key. Reading it is how a field can be named from the key the game saves it under - the goods pools were told apart this way. Nothing else in the class writes a key.

addresses.name: CCountry::AfterLoad
addresses.comment: Slot 5 of CPersistent for a country: run once the country's block has been read, to fill in what the save did not carry - a country with nothing at +0xF20 is given the Generic one.

addresses.name: CCountry::BuildMessageVariables
addresses.comment:
**The variables every message starts with**, as a `{first, last, count}` list of CMessageVariable with `$COUNTRY$` first and fourteen in all.

**It does not allocate the list.** The first thing it does is `[country + 0x24]` into edi and clear it (0x33F60), then refill it - so the list is the **country's own member**, and every caller gets the same one. It is returned for convenience, not because it is fresh.

Which makes the lifetime a trap. CMessage::CMessage copies the entries into the message and **releases the source**, so two messages cannot be in flight for one country: raising one from inside CCountry::ShatterUnit, which was holding this list in edi, freed the nodes under the game's own message and it died walking them at `$MONARCHTITLE$` (a virtual call through a stale vftable at 0x67ACE7). Anything raising a message has to do it where no other raise is part-built.

addresses.name: CountryHasModifier
addresses.comment: 0x4D8040 to the two bare `ret`s at 0x4D8060/0x4D8063, twelve instructions, **both arguments in registers** (country in EAX, modifier in EDX), so class-free per trap 11. It walks the country's active_modifiers list at +0x648 - nodes {item, prev, next} with `next` at +8 - and returns true when some `item->+8` equals the modifier. Eight callers. The same loop is inlined at 0x89B7E7 inside CEU3AI::IsInfluencing, which is how that function was read. `image.functionStart` is safe here: 0x4D8040 is the target of a `call rel32` at 0x4C382C.

addresses.name: RunCountryHourlyPass
addresses.comment:
**The per-country hourly pass, and the only place `CUnit` slot 31 is ever dispatched.** One caller in the whole image: `RunHourlyPass` at `0x682833`, in a serial loop over the country vector `CCurrentGameState +0xBBC` gated on `CCountry +0x44`. So everything here runs on the **tick thread**, once per game hour, before any TBB fan-out.

Per node of `country->units` (`+0xBAC`; a node is `{unit, ?, next}`):

    unit->slot31()                                CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat, at 0x4D8F7D
    if (unit->+0x40 == 0 && unit->slot15())
        CGameState::RemoveUnit(state)(unit, 0, 1)  0x4D8FB5 - synchronous, this thread
    else if (no provinces, no government in exile, owner is not "REB")
        CGameState::RemoveUnit(state)(unit, 0, 1)  0x4D8FFD
    else
        push unit onto *survivors                  0x4D9004-0x4D904F

`RunHourlyPass` then hands that same vector to `SpawnProcessUnitParallelFor` at `0x682887`, and `ProcessUnitFunctor`'s serial body calls `CUnit::UpdateHourly` per element at `0x68ECC9`. **So slot 31 runs on the tick thread over every unit, and `UpdateHourly` runs on workers over the survivors.**

After the unit loop: `0x508C30(country)`; then an hour gate, `hour == country->id % 24`, feeding `0x8AC400(country + 0x48C, matched)` - or `0x8A9B10(country + 0x48C, 0)` when `CCountry +0x580` is set; then `0x4E0B80(country)` when the owned-province count is positive; then `country->+0x11CC = 0`. `ret 4`, `this` in ECX, ends at `0x4D9165`.

addresses.name: RunCountryHourlyPass_TheatrePass
addresses.comment: `cmp byte [edi+0x580], 0` inside RunCountryHourlyPass - the fork that decides which theatre pass a country gets this hour, and **the proof that the whole theatre-building layer is tick-thread code**: `retsBefore(0x4D8EB0, 0x4D9093)` is empty and 0x4D8EB0 is a fresh prologue with its own SEH push after a single int3 at 0x4D8EAF, so this is inside the confirmed tick-thread hourly pass. Set: `BuildTheatres(&country->Strategy, 0)` at 0x4D9093, the full rebuild. Clear: `MaintainTheatres(&country->Strategy, hour == country->id % 24)` at 0x4D90C6 - the same per-country stagger the ministers use.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: RunCountryDailyPass
addresses.comment: **Everything a country does once a day**, not just politics: 0x4DA530 to the `ret 4` at 0x4DC239 (0x4DC242 onward is SEH unwind, not body). One caller, RunDailyPass at 0x682E1A, looping the country vector; the address is in no vftable. Phases: three unread helpers, then Neutrality clamped to [0,100000] and EffectiveNeutrality derived; convoys and lend-lease; CCountry::ChangeNeutrality by the NEUTRALITY_CHANGE modifier; the IC block; the daily influence upkeep and then dissent forced to 0 for REB; the underground; elections; surrender; the AI. Alignment drift at 0x4DB87E, every ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL days. See FINDINGS-politics.md for the full ordered table.

addresses.name: DailyPass_ActivateLeaders
addresses.comment: The only place RunCountryDailyPass (0xDA530) touches CCountry's leaders list (+0xE10). The block runs to 0xDAB2A and does leader activation only - no experience, no skill: for each leader it finds the date of the first history entry whose save token is 0x10A (rank), falling back to the global at rva 0x130C2B8, and when that date equals CCurrentGameState->tick and the leader is not yet in active_leaders (+0xE00), sets rank (+0x6C) to 1 and appends him.

addresses.name: CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade
CCountry::UpdateMonthly
addresses.comment:
**The country's monthly pass, and where practical and theory decay is really applied.** Extent 0x4DC840..0x4DCD69, `ret` with no immediate, SEH handler 0xC5D647, `this` in ECX, clean int3 padding and a fresh prologue at 0x4DCD70. One caller, 0x683BE9 inside RunMonthlyPass (rva 0x283B50), over the country vector state+0xBBC starting at index 1; no data reference and no vftable slot.

In order: resets spiescaught (+0x11D4) at 0x4DC8D3; computes the decay slack from ProductionDistribution elements 5 and 4 (Upgrade and Reinforcement, [[this+0x5F4]+0x14] and +0x10) as int64 [+8] x [+0x10] >> 15 each, summed and scaled by 0x1F40000 >> 30 into thousandths (0x4DC8D9..0x4DC943); then, **only when CCurrentGameState +0xDA4 in_game is set** (0x4DC9C0), for every technology category index i in 0..(([0x1A87B78]+0x20 - +0x1C)>>2)-1:

    step = BASE_TECH_DECAY x (1000 + tech_decay_modifier[i]) / 1000
                            x (1000 - slack) / 1000        clamped to <= 0 only
    category_levels[i] = category_levels[i] x (1000 + step) / 1000

and writes category_levels (+0x698) **directly** at 0x4DCB20, not through CCountry::SetTechAbility, so there is no floor at 0 and no MAX_TECH_ABILITY cap. Unlike ApplyTechCategoryDecay (rva 0x204A0) it covers theories and practicals alike, never reads the custom game settings singleton, so theory_decay_months, practice_decay_months and extra_practice_decay do not affect ongoing decay, and it decays the country's own level rather than max(own, the sharer's).

The rest of the function is the country's other monthly work: 0x4F0270, +0x90 += [+0xDF8]->[+0xBC], 0x4DDD80, 0x4FBC10, 0x4E1C00, 0x4E1FC0, the war_exhaustion clamp at +0xAD0 against [+0xDA8]->[+0x48], a relations loop calling 0x4E78D0 per country, then 0x4F6D00 and 0x528770 twice. See reversing/FINDINGS-techdecay.md. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: MonthlyTechDecay_ReadBaseTechDecay
addresses.comment: `mov eax, [ecx+0x40]` - the image's **second** reader of the BASE_TECH_DECAY define, inside CCountry::UpdateMonthly. ecx is the CDefines `country` block, [0x1A86040]->[+0xCC]. FINDINGS-research.md and project.json call 0x420661 the only reader; it is not, and the survey missed this one because GetDefines is **inlined** here (0x4DCA62..0x4DCABD duplicates 0x445D90's body and calls the CDefines constructor 0x4452E0 directly), so no `call 0x445D90` exists to anchor a scan on.

addresses.name: MonthlyTechDecay_WriteCategoryLevel
addresses.comment: `mov [edi+ebx], eax` - the only instruction in the image that reduces a technology category level over time. edi is CCountry +0x698 (category_levels), ebx is the category index x 4, eax is level x (1000 + step) / 1000 in thousandths. A census of all 90 sites in .text carrying displacement 0x698 finds only four writers into the array: this one, 0x4CF32F (CCountry::LoadKey), 0x4D45EB (the reset in 0x4D2B60) and 0x4E0431 (CCountry::SetTechAbility).

addresses.name: Patch_WarExhaustionNeutralityReset_3
addresses.comment: Replaced with mov dword ptr [esi+0xAD0], 0 by disableWarExhaustionNeutralityReset.

addresses.name: Patch_WarExhaustionNeutralityReset_1
addresses.comment: One byte patched to 0x01 by disableWarExhaustionNeutralityReset.

addresses.name: Patch_WarExhaustionNeutralityReset_2
addresses.comment: Six bytes nopped by disableWarExhaustionNeutralityReset.

addresses.name: AreaSupplyAndFuelHeadroom
addresses.signature: void __stdcall AreaSupplyAndFuelHeadroom(CCountry* country, CMapProvince* destination, int* outSupplies, int* outFuel)
addresses.comment:
**The cap on how much supply and fuel a convoy may land.** Four stack arguments, two of them out-params. It takes the destination's area (CMapProvince +0x2B4), bails with both out-params zero when the area's slot 0 answers false, and otherwise walks the area's province lists (area->+0x70, each node's +0x48) summing four figures: each province's `drawn` buffer (+0x1A8) supplies and fuel, and each province's `pool` supplies (+0x164) and fuel (+0x168). Then

    *outSupplies = drawnSupplies * SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS (military +0x3C) - poolSupplies
    *outFuel     = drawnFuel     * SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS                 - poolFuel

So **an overseas theatre stops importing once its area holds SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS (35 in both vanilla and BlackICE) days of its own draw**, and that define is the one lever on how much stock a convoy route will build up at the far end. CConvoy::RunDelivery clamps negatives to 0 and applies each cap only when the matching bit of the `ship` mask is set. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers
addresses.comment: **Only its espionage arm was read**, so the name is inference from that arm's shape. At 0x4DEE44..0x4DEE9B it walks every country with provinces, takes `other->espionage[this->tagId]` - THEIR spies in ME - and where the level is positive calls 0x530340 to fold the spy_lower_national_unity / spy_raise_national_unity modifiers into an accumulator; it then goes on to the modifier-definition registry at 0x1A86208 and more the same shape. That is why CDistributeEspionage::Distribute calls it after every single spy it places (0x51F11D) and why the production queue calls it on a completion. FINDINGS-production.md lists it as 'not read'; the rest of the body still is.

addresses.name: Patch_MinisterTechDecay
addresses.comment: One byte patched to 0x01 by fixMinisterTechDecay.

addresses.name: GetDifficultyCombatModifier
addresses.comment:
**The whole of BM_DIFFICULTY (0x02), and the same function for land, naval, air, bomber and target.** The country arrives in EDI, never loaded from the frame; the out pointer is the single stack argument and comes back in EAX.

    settings = [rva 0x1689790]          ; a lazy singleton of 0xDA8 bytes, vftable rva 0x11CF674
    if settings->+0xBCC[country->+0xCA8] == 0:  *out = 0        ; not a human-played country
    else:
        bonus = one of { 0, +2000, +1000, -1000, -2000 } chosen by settings->+0xC98
        *out = bonus * COMBAT_DIFFICULTY_IMPACT / 1000

So the difficulty modifier applies **only to the player's own countries**, with the sign set by the difficulty setting. The jump table is at rva 0xDFADC and the arms are 0x7D0, 0x3E8, -0x3E8, -0x7D0 plus a fall-through zero; **which setting index maps to which arm was not read**, so the magnitudes are settled and the mapping is not.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetBuildCost(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, CBuilding* building)
addresses.comment:
What this country pays for a building: the building's own cost (CBuilding +0x58) scaled by the discount its technology category earns, cost x (1000 - discount) / 1000. The slot 2 call on the category that guards it is the folded `mov al,1; ret` at 0xA92590, true for a real category and for the nocategory object alike, so the discount is always applied. That matters for a building whose category is nocategory - its index is 0, where every country's ability is 0, and an ability below 5.000 raises the cost: A building whose category is nocategory therefore costs about half as much again.

**Signature**: out is the hidden first stack argument and comes back in eax; `this` is in ecx, which is why the `ret` is 8 and not 12.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetAllowedResearchSlots
addresses.comment:
round(base_percentage x factor x TotalLeadership) - the research slider (LeadershipDistribution->Research, the fourth of the four) times the country's total leadership. Reads the two as fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>, so the shifts by 15 and 30 and the 0x1F40000 are only the fixed point arithmetic.

**Signature**: no arguments at all - `this` in ecx and a bare `ret` - and it answers a plain rounded int, not a CFixedPoint through a hidden pointer.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetAbility
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetAbility(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, CTechnologyCategory* category)
addresses.comment:
The country's effective level in a technology category: its own (+0x698), or the level of the country sharing that category with it (+0x6A8) where that is higher.

**Signature**: out is the hidden first stack argument, returned in eax; the category is the second.

addresses.name: CCountry::SetTechAbility
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CCountry::SetTechAbility(CCountry* country, CTechnologyCategory* category, int level)
addresses.comment: **Writes one of a country's theory or practical levels**, thousandths: floors the level at 0, caps it at MAX_TECH_ABILITY - the `country` define block at CDefines +0xCC, offset +0x44, read once and cached in the static at 0x17EBAB0 behind the flag at 0x17EBAB4 - and stores it in own_ability (+0x698) at the category's own index (+0x5C). Called by CPracticalEffect::Execute. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetLeadershipDistributionAt
addresses.comment:
[this+0x5E4][i] - the leadership slider at that index: 0 officers, 1 diplomacy, 2 espionage, 3 research, the order of the game's LeadershipCategory enum.

**Signature**: `this` in ecx, the index the one stack argument (`ret 4`). No direct caller exists in the image, so the convention is read off the body's own `ret`.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildCostIC
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CCountry::GetBuildCostIC(CCountry* this, CFixedPoint* out, CSubUnitDefinition* definition, int technologyBonus, bool reserves)
addresses.comment:
What a unit type costs this country. base is the definition's BuildCostIC (+0xF8); the multiplier is 1000, plus CTechnologyStatus +0x24C for the type, plus the third argument times 10 (so 1% a point), less the discount the definition's technology category (+0x3C) earns - the same 0xE1AC0 buildings use. Then, where the fourth argument is set, times (1000 + the country's RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE modifier, 77) over 1000. The third argument is the caller's: the game works it out at 0x63D40 by adding up CTechnologyStatus +0x218 over the definition's own technology list (+0x44..+0x48). Only Lua calls this entry point; the game's own path is GetTotalBuildCost (0x63D40), which works the same cost out inline without the reserves step and multiplies it by GetBuildTime.

**Signature**: four stack arguments (`ret 0x10`) with out hidden first and returned in eax; the flag at [ebp+0x14] is tested as a byte, so it is a bool.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetBuildTime
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CCountry::GetBuildTime(CCountry* this, CSubUnitDefinition* definition, int technologyBonus)
addresses.comment:
How long a unit type takes this country to build. The definition's BuildTime (+0x100) times two factors over a million. The first is 1000, plus CTechnologyStatus +0x26C for the type, plus the second argument times 10, plus the country's UNIT_RECRUITMENT_TIME modifier (51), less the discount the definition's technology category earns (0xE1AC0, the same one the costs use); it is floored at 50. The second is 1000 plus one build speed modifier, chosen by the definition's kind flags in this order: is_rocket (+0x33) ROCKET_BUILD_SPEED, is_tank (+0x34) TANK_BUILD_SPEED, is_air (+0x2C) AIR_BUILD_SPEED, is_ship (+0x2E) NAVAL_BUILD_SPEED, else LAND_BUILD_SPEED.

**Signature**: unlike the costs this one answers a plain int in eax - divided by 1000 at 0x4E1AA5, and the callers multiply it back up - so there is no hidden out pointer and the `ret` is 8, not 12.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount(int* out@ESI, CCountry* country@stack:4, CTechnologyCategory* category@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
The discount a technology category earns, in thousandths, which the build cost is scaled by as (1000 - this). Takes the country's ability in that category - its own level at +0x698, or the sharer's if a tag at +0x6A8 names one with a higher level, the same lookup GetAbility makes - floors it at 0 and measures it against 5.000: below that the result is negative and the cost goes up, at 100 per point; above it 50 per point with everything past 1.000 halved first. Then adds the country's INDUSTRIAL_EFFICIENCY modifier (74) and CTechnologyStatus +0x94, and caps the whole at 990, so at most 99% off. The name is BiceLib's.

**The out pointer travels in ESI, not on the stack** - that is the whole of why the recorded signature wanted ret 12 and the function does ret 8. Only two things are pushed, the country and the category; ESI is never written in the body, only read (every store is `mov [esi], ...`), and the return is `mov eax, esi` at 0x4E1BCA.

addresses.name: CCountry::RebuildNeighbours
addresses.comment:
Fills a country's two neighbour sets and the two CCountryList they stand for. It clears both, walks OwnedProvinces marking the owner of every adjacent province that nobody is occupying, then walks ControlledProvinces marking the controller of every adjacent province owned by somebody else. It is what says which set means what.

**Signature**: __stdcall, not __thiscall - the country is [ebp+8], ecx is never read, and the single `ret 4` is the callee cleaning it.

addresses.name: CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies
addresses.comment: 0x4E6A70-0x4E6ED3, `ret 8`, `this` in ecx. **The only writer of `CCountry +0xACC` (at_war) and of the enemies list at `+0x1008`.** It clears `+0xACC`, frees `+0x1008`/`+0x100C`/`+0x1010`, then walks the whole country database (`[0x1A855A4] +0x168` count, `+0x16C` array) and for every other country whose `CDiplomacyStatus +0x20` (war) is non-null: sets `+0xACC = 1`, appends a 0x14-byte `{tagChars, tagId, prev, next, byte}` node to `+0x1008`, and stamps the pair's `CDiplomacyStatus +0x54` with the current tick (`state->+0xBDC`). It then runs the mobilisation side: with `+0x94` clear and `+0xACC` set it adds the static modifier `initial_mobilization` and sets `+0x94 = 1`; the reverse transitions remove it, and the one at 0x4E6E44 also clears `+0x94` - but only for a country the played-countries array `state->+0xBCC` says is not played. Nine call sites: 0x65B398 (inside CInGameIdler's hourly body) and eight in the diplomacy action code at 0x4A503D6..0x4A51BF5, which always call it on **both** sides of the action. The name is from the body.
