Four callers, each calling it twice, once per side, immediately after writing diplomacy[other]->+0x24: CUndeclaredWar::AddAttacker (0x76040 at 0x760BD/0x760D1), 0x760F0 (0x7618B/0x7619F), CUndeclaredWar::AddDefender (0x761C0 at 0x7623D/0x76251) and 0x76270 (0x7630B/0x7631F). `this` arrives in ESI: every caller does `mov esi, db->+0x16C[id]` immediately before the call.

addresses.name: CCountry::CollectCountriesWeCanOperateIn
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, **one caller in the image** - CAIUnit slot 76 at 0x4DB0F6. Clears `out`, then walks every country in the game state (index 0 to the game state's slot 6, array at +0xBBC) and appends a 0x14-byte node holding the country's own tag (CCountry +0xCA4) for every one that passes CCountry::CanOperateIn's test, inlined: skip id 0 and `REB`, accept IsSameSide, otherwise require the diplomacy status's +0x58 and not-enemy. **The country's own tag passes**, so its own theatres are in the result. Slot 76 unions all those countries' theatre lists (CCountry +0x570) and takes its candidate fronts from them. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CCountry::IsFriendly
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, 75 callers. True when the tag is this country, when either side's +0xF3C names the other, when both share a +0xF3C, when `this->+0xD8` answers its slot 7 and equals the other country's +0xD8, when the other country's diplomacy status for us has +0x14 set, or when it has +0x58 set and we are not its enemy. With `includeRequested` it also accepts our own status's +0x4C. CAIUnit slot 76 uses it with true to **skip any plan objective in friendly-controlled territory**.

addresses.name: CCountry::IsSameSide
addresses.comment: `bare ret`, 37 callers. False for tag id 0 and for `REB`. True when the tag is this country, when the other country's +0xF3C is this country's id, when this country's +0xF3C is the tag's id, or - only if this country's +0xF3C is non-zero - when both carry the same +0xF3C. So **CCountry +0xF38/+0xF3C is a CCountryTag naming the faction leader or overlord, and +0xF34 the byte saying there is one.**

addresses.name: CCountry::CanOperateIn
addresses.comment: `bare ret`, 31 callers. False for tag id 0 and `REB`; true if CCountry::IsSameSide (0xEF940); otherwise true only when this country's diplomacy status for that tag has the byte at +0x58 set **and** CCountry::IsEnemy (0x2F210's tag-only sibling 0x2F1B0) says no. Slot 76 uses it to decide where its drawn path stops being its own ground, and CCountry::CollectCountriesWeCanOperateIn (0xEE110) is the same filter over every country. The three independent consumers all read +0x58 as the thing that makes another country's territory usable, which is why **CDiplomacyStatus +0x58 is inferred to be military access** - nothing names it.

After that, **three successive windows of NAP_FORCE_BALANCE_RULE_MONTHS (+0xE8)**, each requiring the border force balance (NAP+0x24, inverted when this country is the NAP's `second` party) to reach NAP_BREAK_FORCE_BALANCE_1 / _2 / _3 (+0xEC / +0xF0 / +0xF4); once all three have elapsed it is always breakable. addresses.comment: The daily IC calculation. `ret 8`, nothing in ecx, `country` parked in ebx at once. Extent 0xF0CC0..0xF15BD (0x8FE bytes), `ret` at 0xF15BB with int3 padding after. Zeroes +0x604/+0x608/+0x60C/+0x610 and the three CGoodsPools +0x8B4, +0x8D8, +0x968; seeds the sum with the MODIFIER_IC of a global CModifier reached as [[[0x1A86208]+0x64]+0x18]+0x78; walks the province list at CCountry +0xD00 adding provinceValues[MODIFIER_IC] * (1000 + provinceValues[MODIFIER_LOCAL_IC]) / 1000 each; divides by 1000 into +0x60C and +0x604, then scales +0x604 by (1000 + countryValues[GLOBAL_IC] + technologyStatus[+0x90]) / 1000, floor 1. Fills +0x968 with metal/energy/rares in 1:2:0.5 of the total. `applyDailyEffects` additionally runs the energy-to-crude-oil conversion (into +0x8D8/+0x8B4), the metal/energy resource cap (+0x614) and the lend-lease add (+0x608). addresses.signature: int __thiscall CCountry::FindSupplyDepot(CCountry* this, CProvince* province, void* visited, CCountry* origin)
addresses.comment: Answers the province id that a province should draw supply from, or 0. Returns the origin country's acting_capital_province_id (CCountry +0xE24) once the province's area matches that of the origin's own acting capital, and otherwise recurses into the countries reached through the area's list at +0x34 and through +0xF34/+0xF38 on the country, carrying the same origin and a visited list so the walk terminates. `origin` defaults to `this` when it is passed null. This is what makes two provinces share a supply_depot_id: they resolve to the same acting capital.

addresses.name: BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip
addresses.comment:
**One goods category's whole daily ledger as text, and the only place all fifteen of CCountry's per-goods arrays are named at once.** Extent 0x4F3000..0x4F4B5E, `ret 0xC`, returns its `out` (`mov esi,[ebp+0xc]` at 0x4F4AFB). The argument order is read off the call sites, not guessed: `push goods; push &out; push country; call` at 0x6CCCD9..0x6CCCE1. Fourteen call sites - seven in CTopBar slot 5 (0x6CCB80), one per category, the rest around 0x801AA9.

Every localisation key in it is immediately preceded by the load of the value it labels, so the mapping is read: RES_PROD = country + goods*4 + 0x778 (home_produced), RES_CONVOYED_IN +0x79C (convoyed_in, suppressed for goods 0 and 1 - supplies and fuel), RES_CONVOYED_OUT +0x7C0, RES_TRADED_AWAY +0x7E4, RES_REPAID_AWAY +0x82C, RES_INC_DEBT +0x850, RES_TRADED_FOR +0x874, RES_CONVERTED +0x8BC (conversion_made) and +0x8E0 (conversion_used, shown negated), RES_FROM_PUPPETS +0x904 (tribute_received), RES_SENT_TO_MASTER +0x928 (tribute_sent, shown when negative - which confirms it is held negative), RES_USED +0x994 (usage), RES_INTO_NET +0x9B8 (sent_to), RES_SHIPPED_BACK +0x9DC (sent_back). The index is the CGoodsPool index: 0 supplies, 1 fuel, 2 money, 3 crude oil, 4 metal, 5 energy, 6 rare materials.

**So five pools the record carried as unknown or unused have names**: +0x7B8 is convoyed_out (which the convoy-economy comment already called ConvoyedOut - a convergence, trap 14's good case), +0x7DC traded_away, +0x824 repaid_away, +0x848 income_from_debt, +0x86C traded_for. **BiceLib should read those fields rather than call this.** See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip(CCountry* country, Hoi3CString* out, int goods)

addresses.name: GoodsLedger_Aggregates
addresses.comment: Where BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip forms the two sums the RES_CHANGE line is built from, before any text exists. Expenses into [ebp-0x14]: +0x9B8 - +0x82C - +0x928 + +0x994 + +0x8E0 + +0x7C0 + +0x7E4. Income into eax at 0xF30C1: +0xA6C + +0x9DC + +0x850 + +0x8BC + +0x874. Production in esi: +0x778, plus +0x79C when the goods index is 2 or more. All offsets are `country + goods*4 + N`, thousandths. The instruction sequence is `confirmed`; reading the two sums as expense and income is `likely`. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetSpareICIn
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall GetSpareICIn(CCountry* country, int* out, ProductionCategory category)
addresses.comment: How much of what a production slider allocates is not needed by it, in thousandths of IC and never negative. Allocated is the setting's percentage times its factor times TotalIC (+0x604); what is taken off depends on the category (a jump table at 0x0F4D54): CONSUMER nothing if there is any dissent, otherwise the setting's own GetNeeded scaled by a define; PRODUCTION the production queue, GetUsedIC; REINFORCEMENT the country's +0xA98; UPGRADE its +0xAA4; SUPPLY and LENDLEASE fall through to zero. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetAvailableIC
addresses.comment:
Spare industrial capacity: GetSpareICIn summed over the five ProductionCategory values from _PRODUCTION_CONSUMER_ to _PRODUCTION_UPGRADE_ - lend lease, category 0, is left out - and divided by 1000. So it is IC a slider has been given but does not need, not IC that is unallocated.

**Signature**: no arguments, `this` in ecx, a bare `ret`, and a plain int in eax.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetPool
addresses.comment:
Answers the capital province's pool, or the country's own pool at +0x9F8 when the country is a government in exile (+0x95).

**Signature**: `this` in ecx, no stack arguments, a bare `ret` on both arms - the out-of-line body needs no register notation.

addresses.name: CCountry::EnqueueConstruction
addresses.comment: **Puts a finished CConstruction on the country's build queue.** It zeroes the construction's location (+0x44) - which is why that field reads null on every military and convoy item and holds a province only on building ones - calls virtual slot 8, copies the country's tag from CCountry +0xCA4/+0xCA8 into +0x48/+0x4C, and appends a new 0x10-byte node (item, prev, next, byte) at the tail of the list at CCountry +0xF40/+0xF44. **Both arguments arrive in registers**, the construction in eax and the country in edi, and there is no stack argument, so the convention is read off its own `ret` and its two call sites, 0x545D2B in CConstructUnitCommand::Execute and 0x5471E7 in CConstructSingleUnitCommand::Execute. It is the path taken when the command's instant-build flag is clear. The name is ours.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetConsumerGoodsNeeded
addresses.comment: **The share of industrial capacity the country wants on consumer goods**, in thousandths. It takes MODIFIER_WAR_CONSUMER_GOODS_DEMAND (modifier 40) or MODIFIER_PEACE_CONSUMER_GOODS_DEMAND (modifier 41) from the country's modifier values - [CCountry +0xDA8] + 0x140 + 8 x (byte [CCountry +0xACC] == 0), the array being eight bytes an entry - adds a term from 0x4F9F10, and clamps the result between floorf(10.5f) and floorf(990.5f), so **between 0.010 and 0.990**. **`this` arrives in eax and out in esi**, and there are no stack arguments. It is the first term of both CDistributeConsumerGoods::GetNeeded (0x119030) and the daily dissent change (0x118F80). The name is ours.

addresses.name: CAlignment::BuildDriftTooltip
addresses.comment: The game's own alignment-drift tooltip, 0x4FA0B0..0x4FBBD8, `ret 8`, returning its `out` argument. One caller, at 0x7853FE. It is the **second independent derivation of the whole alignment formula** and it agrees with FINDINGS-politics.md term for term: it calls ComputeDrift(country+0xDC, &point, country) once at 0x4FA123, then recomputes each of the seven terms into its own stack slot (Relation 0x4C3950, Ideology 0x4C3B10, Proximity 0x4C3C00, Revanchism 0x4C3E40, Threat 0x4C4120, Repulsion 0x4C4380 with ecx = country+0xDC, AlignTowards 0x4C3790 with the group in edi), takes an integer square root of the group distance (IntegerSqrt, 0x46C2E0), zeroes Threat, Revanchism and Repulsion when that distance is >= 200, and sums them at 0x4FA9EA..0x4FAA1B as relation + ideology + proximity - revanchism - threat - repulsion + aligntowards. **It also names all seven, with the game's own localisation keys**: FACTION_DRIFT_RELATIONS, _PROXIMITY, _IDEOLOGY, _REVANCH_NEW, _THREAT, _REPULSION and - for the term the record had to call AlignTowards - _INFLUENCE, each loaded from the slot that term's own function wrote. The total is labelled FACTION_DRIFT_INSTANT. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetInfluencedCountryCount
addresses.comment: No stack arguments, plain `ret`, the country in ecx. Walks every country o and counts those whose o->+0xE28[this->+0xCA8] has +0x2C set - the same flag the daily influence upkeep charges for. Abuts CCountry::ChangeNeutrality, which starts at 0x4FBF80 after eight int3. (First recorded at rva 0xFBF00, which is inside this function rather than its start - 0xFBF80 is CCountry::ChangeNeutrality, so 0xFBF00 could not begin anything. The start is 0xFBEA0, preceded by int3 padding, `push ebp; mov ebp, esp; and esp, -8`. buildFindings.py dropped the entry until this was corrected.)

addresses.name: CCountry::ChangeNeutrality
addresses.comment: `ret 8` with the country in **esi**. +0xA8C += delta floored at zero, then EffectiveNeutrality (+0xA90) recomputed as clamp(Neutrality - this->+0xE28[this->+0x11DC]->+0x5C, 0, 100000). With logHistory it allocates a 0x18-byte entry (constructor 0x5F11F0), stamps it with the current tick and appends it to the country's `history` (+0xCCC). The country's daily pass calls it at 0x4DAE9B with delta = the NEUTRALITY_CHANGE modifier (values entry 78) and logHistory false, which is the whole of the daily neutrality drift. 0x4FC0E0 beside it is the plain setter.

addresses.name: CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes
CCountry::DailyEspionagePass
addresses.comment: 0x4FFD10 to the `ret 4` at 0x4FFEBD, clean int3 padding after. **One caller, 0x4DB93E, inside RunCountryDailyPass** (0x4DA530..0x4DC239), which RunDailyPass runs in its serial country loop at 0x682E1A - so espionage resolves once per country per game day **on the tick thread, not a TBB worker**. Body: for every country i with owned provinces (+0xCF8 > 0) whose presence `espionage + i*0xF8` has level > 0, call CSpyPresence::RunDailyMissions (0x5300A0) with the two tags by value; then, if the country's OWN record's missions[0] is non-zero, call CSpyPresence::CatchSpies (0x52E3A0) directly with its own tag twice. Counter-espionage therefore lives on a country's record about itself.

addresses.name: CCountry::LoadOobFile
addresses.comment:
**Reads the order of battle named at `CCountry::oob_file`** and puts it in the country. It builds `<base>/units/<path>` - the base chosen by `[0x1685558 + 0x50]`, which has three values - and tries it with FileExists; then allocates a CParseContext (0x360 bytes) and a Tokenizer (0x114) over the file and calls **the country's own slot 3, `CPersistent::Load`**, with that context, before deleting it.

So **an order of battle is read as a piece of a country's save block**: Load pulls keys and hands each to `CCountry::LoadKey` (`0xCCDA0`), the same one a savegame goes through, and every keyword in the file is a SaveToken - `theatre` 1125, `armygroup` 1126, `corps` 1127, `division` 1128, `navy` 593, `air` 1088, `regiment` 594, `location` 544, `leader` 616, `military_construction` 637. **This is where the units are made.** The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CCountry::RecountUnitTotals
addresses.comment: The serial body of `ProcessCountryFunctor`, so it runs on a **TBB worker** once a game hour (called at `0x68EDC1`, inside that functor's `start_for::execute`). `this` in **EDI**, one stack argument. It zeroes `CCountry +0xC8`, `+0xCC`, `+0xD0` and `+0x108C`, then walks `country->units` (`+0xBAC`), skips a unit whose `+0x290` is non-zero, adds `unit->+0x40 * 1000` to `+0xC8`, and walks the unit's subunit list at `+0x38` dispatching unit slot 15 per subunit. **It writes `CCountry` fields from a worker thread**, which is worth knowing before reading any of those four offsets from a hook. Five other callers, none inside a functor: `0x41C44E`, `0x41E0E5`, `0x41EBAD`, `0x4E3989` and `CInGameIdler` slot 3 at `0x65B4F7`. The name is inference from the shape; nothing was watched running.

addresses.name: CCountry::ShatterUnit
addresses.comment:
**Takes a shattered unit off the map and gives it somewhere to come back to.**

The new home is the country's acting capital, or - where the unit's current province has a supply depot whose controller is not an enemy - that depot's province. It then walks `oob_level` up the order of battle, which is what puts the unit back under its theatre command rather than leaving it where it fell.

addresses.name: ShatterUnit_PlayerCheck
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry
addresses.comment:
**Where the game decides a message is worth showing.** CCountry::ShatterUnit compares the country's `+0xCA8` against the game state's player id at `+0xC34` and, when they differ, jumps past the whole message block.

So the engine never raises a message for an AI country. Anything BiceLib raises has to make the same test, or every division lost anywhere on the map pops a window at the player.

addresses.name: ShatterUnit_MessageName
addresses.no_signature: two instructions inside a larger function, not a function entry
addresses.comment:
**Where CCountry::ShatterUnit names the message it raises**: `push 9` then `push "SHATTERED"`, seven bytes, immediately before the std::string is built from them.

Patching these two instructions raises a type of your own through machinery that is otherwise untouched - the cheapest way to prove a mod-declared type can be raised at all, and to tell a broken raise apart from a broken type. BiceLib did this for a while; Game::Message replaced it.

**The pointer is relocated**, so the site cannot be checked by matching its bytes - only `6A 09 68` is fixed, and the immediate has to be resolved against the module base.

**The head string this raise passes is empty**, not a localisation key: 0x100DB5 builds it from a zero length. Anything reproducing the raise passes an empty string there.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetInfluenceUpkeep
addresses.comment: *out = INFLUENCE_UPKEEP (diplomacy +0xD0) times the number of countries whose diplomacy status toward `country` has +0x2C set. The read-only counterpart of 0x103E90, presumably for the tooltip.

addresses.name: CCountry::PayDailyInfluenceUpkeep
addresses.comment: No stack arguments, plain `ret`, the country in **esi**. For every country whose diplomacy status toward this one has +0x2C set, subtracts INFLUENCE_UPKEEP (diplomacy +0xD0) from diplo_influence (+0xA88); if that would go negative it is clamped to zero and 0x503F90 is called to cancel the influence. **This is where diplo_influence is spent per day.** Called from the country's daily pass at 0x4DB671, immediately before dissent is forced to zero for REB.

addresses.name: RunDailyUndergroundPass
addresses.comment: 0x50A110 to 0x50AE40, f(CCountry*) on the stack, called unconditionally from CCountry's daily pass at 0x4DBB64. Walks the list at CCountry +0xD60 and per province: (1) grows the underground - province->underground (+0x30C) ->level_current (+0x24) += UNDERGROUND_STRENGTH_GAIN (defines military +0x258) * (1 + provinceValues[MODIFIER_LOCAL_PARTISAN_SUPPORT]/100), capped at +0x20 with the dirty byte at +0x28; (2) rolls for detection - Random() % 1000 < round(province->suppression (+0x28) * UNDERGROUND_DETECT_CHANCE (military +0x25C) / 1e6), and a detected province goes on a stack list that the tail of the function turns into the OURUNDERGROUNDREMOVED / UNDERGROUNDREMOVED messages; a province whose controller is back to its owner (+0x338 == +0x330, 0x50ABFE) joins the same list; (3) otherwise switches on province->underground_action (+0x394) at 0x50AC4E - 0 means mobilise partisans (0x50B450 then SpawnPartisansFromUnderground at 0x50AD08), 1 means spread the underground (0x50BB20 then 0x50BD00), 2 or more means do nothing. **This is where partisans actually come from, and step 3 has no roll in it at all.**

addresses.name: underground_action_switch
addresses.comment: `mov esi, [esi+0x394]; sub esi, ebx; je <mobilise>; dec esi; jne <idle>` in RunDailyUndergroundPass. The switch that gives CProvince::underground_action its values: **0 = mobilise partisans** (0x50AC74, CanMobilizePartisans then SpawnPartisansFromUnderground), **1 = spread the underground** (0x50AC5B, CanSpawnUnderground then 0x50BD00), **2 or anything else = do nothing** - which agrees with the record's note that 2 is the default and is not saved.

addresses.name: underground_partisan_spawn_call
addresses.comment: `call SpawnPartisansFromUnderground` inside RunDailyUndergroundPass, at the end of the province loop, once for each province collected on the underground_action == 0 branch. **There is no roll on this path**: an underground on action 0 whose level is at or above SPAWN_PARTISAN_LIMIT spawns partisans every single day, each spawn burning SPAWN_PARTISAN_LIMIT levels off it. This, not the revolt roll, is where a game's partisans come from.

addresses.name: GetMobilizeUndergroundsAvailability
addresses.comment: The availability text for mobilising undergrounds, ret 4. When CCountry +0x95 is clear it answers WE_NOT_GOVERNMENT_IN_EXILE, which is what identifies that byte as the government-in-exile flag. Otherwise it counts, over the provinces the country **owns** (+0xD60, +0x330 against +0xCA8), how many have underground_building->level_current above SPAWN_PARTISAN_LIMIT; none gives UNDERGROUNDS_NOT_PREPARED with TOTAL. 0x50B1E0 is a whole-country variant; 0x50B4A0 (MOBILIZE_PARTISANS) and 0x50BB60 (MOBILIZE_UNDERGROUND, SPAWN_UNDERGROUND_LIMIT) are the per-action siblings. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CanMobilizePartisans
addresses.comment: 0x50B450, bare ret, register convention: CCountry* in eax, CMapProvince* in esi, returns bool in al. Walks country->+0xD60 for the province's id (+0xD0) and, having found it, answers true at once when the byte at 0x1A85599 is set, otherwise province->underground (+0x30C) ->level_current (+0x24) >= SPAWN_PARTISAN_LIMIT (defines military +0x248, read at 0x50B485). One caller, 0x50AC7A in RunDailyUndergroundPass. 0x50BB20 is the identical twin for SPAWN_UNDERGROUND_LIMIT.

addresses.name: SpawnPartisansFromUnderground
addresses.comment: **Mobilises a province's underground into partisan brigades.** ret 8. It picks a *neighbour* to put them in: a random edge of the source's path node (+0xD4, edges +0x90..+0x94, stride 0x14) whose province is in a real area (+0x2B4 slot 0) and has the **same owner id** (+0x330); failing that the first qualifying edge in order; failing that the source province itself, and if even that is in no real area it logs `Failed to spawn partisant from underground at location` (country.cpp) and does nothing. Then 0x4C0430 picks the rebel faction and 0x4C1160 creates UNDERGROUND_SPAWN_STRENGTH/1000 brigades. Finally it **charges SPAWN_PARTISAN_LIMIT levels to the source province's underground building** (+0x30C, level_current +0x24), floored at 0, setting that building's dirty byte +0x28 when the level moved.

addresses.name: CanSpawnUnderground
addresses.comment: 0x50BB20, bare ret, CCountry* in eax and CMapProvince* in esi, returns bool. Identical to CanMobilizePartisans but reads SPAWN_UNDERGROUND_LIMIT (defines military +0x24C, at 0x50BB49) and has no bypass flag. One caller, 0x50AC61 in RunDailyUndergroundPass, on the underground_action == 1 branch.

addresses.name: SpawnUndergroundFromProvince
addresses.comment: 0x50BD00, reached only on the underground_action == 1 branch of RunDailyUndergroundPass (0x50AC6D) and from 0x55C39A. Draws a random number at 0x50BD8D. Its body was not read; the name comes from its position in the switch and from its sibling SpawnPartisansFromUnderground, not from the code.

addresses.name: CList_FreeAndClear
addresses.comment: 47 bytes, bare `ret`, read end to end, 177 callers - a template instantiation the linker emitted once, not a semantic fold. `free`s every node of the CList at EDI through node->+8 and then zeroes head, tail and count. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits calls it at 0x4D63AF, 0x4D63BB, 0x4D63DE, 0x4D63EA and 0x4D706E.

addresses.name: PostMessage
addresses.no_signature: The third of five arguments is a 0x78 byte object passed by value. Naming it would need a type for the message, which is only known field by field; the frame is in the comment, which is what a caller needs.
addresses.comment:
**Shows a message**: logs it, puts it on the map, pops it up, according to what `interface/messagetypes.txt` says for its type.

`ret 0x88` is the whole of its argument shape, and it is **five** arguments, not three:

    +0x08  the handler
    +0x0C  the province
    +0x10  the message, 0x78 bytes **by value**
    +0x88  the popup builder at 0xA6040
    +0x8C  zero

8 + 0x78 + 8 = 0x88. The two above the message are pushed before it is reserved, so at a raise site they read as stray pushes a long way from the call.

This tests the builder at 0x1112DA and skips a branch when it is null, and passes it to every popup it builds - DefaultPopup, CombatStartPopup, ElectionResultPopup. What it is for is MessagePopupCallback's business; a popup's text is not built here or by it, but by BuildMessagePopupText from the popup's own update.

Reading the pair as coming *before* the message shifts every field by two words and crashes at 0x110B8C, where the type is read out of the message at +0x20.

addresses.name: CCountryDataBase::AddCountry
addresses.comment: 0x515CC0 onward; manipulates the countries vector at +0x16C/+0x170 at its head and then runs a 45-arm string-compare chain over the hardcoded tag names at .rdata 0x15C1DE4 ('GER','ENG','SOV','USA','JAP','FRA','ITA',...,'NZL', immediately followed by the string 'countrydatabase.cpp'). Each arm that matches caches the tag into its own 8-byte slot at the front of the database: GER into +0x0/+0x4 (store at 0x51622F), ENG into +0x8/+0xC (0x516336), SOV into +0x10/+0x14 (0x51643B), USA into +0x18/+0x1C (0x516546), JAP into +0x20/+0x24, FRA into +0x28/+0x2C, and so on in .rdata order to +0x160/+0x164. The constructor 0x4024D0 zeroes exactly those 45 id halves.

Runs immediately after countries.txt (whose reader is CCountryDataBase::AddCountry, 0x515CC0, already in the record and with exactly one caller, 0x63832C); one `CountryDatabase Initialized` line at eu3application.cpp:1130 covers both. Both blocks create the singleton inline - `if ([0x16855A4] == 0) [0x16855A4] = new(0x57C)` then CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase - which agrees with that entry's recorded 0x57C.

It reads no defines, calls 0x508620 and 0x508900, and is the only IC distributor that does **not** read CCountry +0x608 - so everything it spends is charged in resources, through CCountry::GetResourceLimitedIC at 0x5188E7 and CCountry::ConsumeICResources at 0x5188FE. addresses.name: CDistributeConsumerGoods::Distribute
addresses.comment: **Slot 0 - money, the resource bill, and dissent.** Three things. First, where the `available` argument is non-zero it calls 0x118F00 with a fraction of 1000 and MaxIC (+0x60C) x 1000 and adds the money that comes back to HomeProduced's money (CCountry +0x780) and to the national stockpile's money (pool +0x10) - the fraction is a literal and the IC is MaxIC, so **the money income carries no term from the consumer goods share**. Second, it charges resources for percentage x factor x available less percentage x factor x CCountry +0x608, through CCountry::ConsumeICResources at 0x518DE3; consumer goods spends its whole allocation daily, so it pays for all of it that is not resource-free in one go. Third, unless the flag argument is set, or gamestate +0xD0C is non-zero, it moves dissent: 0x118F80 gives GetConsumerGoodsNeeded minus percentage x factor plus MODIFIER_DISSENT, and that goes onto CCountry +0x10B4 floored at zero, or the field is zeroed outright for a country with no tag id (+0xCA8). So the dissent rate is **one for one and linear** - a share one point over what the country needs takes one point of dissent off a day - with no percentage and no half-life. Returns zero.

Four callers, of which 0x518E95 is CDistributeConsumerGoods::Distribute. The name is ours.

addresses.comment: **Slot 3.** CCountry::GetConsumerGoodsNeeded (0xFA020) shifted into fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15> plus the country's MODIFIER_DISSENT - the same two terms as the dissent change, which is why a country that already has dissent needs a bigger consumer goods share to stop it growing. `this` in ecx, one stack argument.

addresses.name: CDistributeProduction::Distribute
addresses.comment: **Slot 0 of vftable 0x15C21D4 - the daily production pass.** It works out two budgets from the same share: pool = percentage(+0x8) x factor(+0x10) x the `available` argument, and freePool = the same share of CCountry +0x608, which is the part of the day's IC that costs no resources. Then it walks the queue at CCountry +0xF40 head to tail (back edge 0x51A230 -> 0x519DC0) and gives each item, **strictly in queue order and with no proportional split or priority**, up to one full day of its own cost (+0x30, thousandths). Per item: slot 12 with &country->tag decides whether the item still exists (false unlinks and destructs it); if pool is spent, AddProgress(0) unless the flag argument is set (0x51A213); a zero-cost item gets AddProgress(1000) (0x519ED9); otherwise base = min(1, freePool/need), and any shortfall is topped up from pool only if CCountry::GetResourceLimitedIC allows it, paid for with CCountry::ConsumeICResources, with the total rounded up to a full 1000 once it reaches floorf(999.5f). AddProgress with the computed amount is 0x51A1B6. Then progress (+0x38) >= duration (+0x34) - or the global byte at 0x1A8559A - calls slot 9, and an answer of exactly 1 completes and destroys the item. After the walk, if anything completed, 0x4DDD80 runs and **slot 14 is called on every remaining item**, which is the only time a queued item's cost is recomputed apart from insertion. Finally 0x51A290 rebuilds +0x20. It always returns zero. Three of the image's five AddProgress call sites are in here. See reversing/FINDINGS-production.md.

addresses.name: CDistributeProduction::UpdateNeeded
addresses.comment: Zeroes this->+0x20/+0x24 and adds every construction's cost (+0x30) divided by 1000 into it, walking the country's queue at CCountry +0xF40. So +0x20 is the queue's total daily IC appetite as an fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>, and slot 3 GetNeeded (0x11A2E0) returns exactly that. Called once, from the end of CDistributeProduction::Distribute (0x51A265). **`this` arrives in esi**, not ecx, and the body is a bare `ret` - the convention is read off its own epilogue, since the one call site sets esi and pushes nothing. The name is ours.

addresses.name: CDistributeProduction::GetNeedTooltip
addresses.comment:
**Slot 1.** Builds a localised string from the key SLIDER_NEED (the literal at 0x15C1F14). The slot-1 and slot-5 bodies of the leadership distributors are, with their own slot 0, the only readers of LEADERSHIP_TO_OFFICERS, LEADERSHIP_TO_DIPLOMACY and LEADERSHIP_TO_SPIES, which is what says these slots are the text that tells the player what a slider buys. The name is ours; only the prologue and the key were read.

**Signature corrected 2026-10-02** (reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md): the body is `ret 0xc`, not the `ret 4` the old one-argument signature predicted. Three stack arguments, of which this body reads only the first (`mov esi, [ebp+8]` at 0x51A369); the receiver is in ECX (0x51A328). The last two are named `unused2`/`unused3` because they are passed and ignored here, not because their purpose is known.

Only read as far as the multiply; the name is ours and the argument count is taken from the two dwords it reads at [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10].

addresses.comment:
**Slot 0 of its virtual table, and where the manpower tooltip's two numbers come from.** The class derives from `CDistributionSetting`, so this is the reinforcement slider spending what it has been allocated; every sibling distributor - supply, upgrade, production, research, consumer goods, lend lease, NCO, diplomacy, espionage - has its own body at the same slot.

It zeroes `CCountry +0xA98`, `+0xA9C` and `+0xAA0`, then walks the country's units and every subunit under each, and rebuilds all three from nothing. `this + 0x18` is the country throughout.

**The stack arguments are three, not one**, which is why the recorded signature wanted ret 4 and the function does ret 16: a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8] for the eight-byte fixed point it answers, the amount it has been given as a 64-bit `fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>` split across [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10], and a byte flag at [ebp+0x14]. This body ignores the flag; the consumer-goods (0x118C50) and production (0x119D10) bodies read it and skip their last step when it is set. `__int64` is written for the middle argument only so the arithmetic sizes - it is the same fixed point type as the return.

addresses.name: ReinforcementCountersCleared
addresses.comment:
The last of the three counters the pass clears before it walks anything, with `edi` zero and `esi` the country.

**BiceLib stands here to start its own day**: the split it keeps has to begin and end with the game's, or the parts would not add up to the total printed beside them. It is also the only thing in the game that happens once a day per country and that BiceLib stands on, so a day of troop rotation is closed here too.

addresses.name: ReinforcementManpowerUsedAdded

addresses.name: ReinforcementManpowerNeededAdded
addresses.comment:
`country->reinforcement_manpower_needed += need`, which the tooltip prints as `$NEED$`. `eax` is the country and `ecx` is what this one subunit's missing strength is worth.

**Which subunit that is, is still at `[esp + 0x44]`** - written at `0x11BF98` and read back as late as `0x11C43D`, with the stack unmoved, and the very next instruction reads `[esp + 0x48]` for the loop's own next node. That is what lets one hook here split the total into land, air and naval by the subunit's class.

addresses.name: CSpyPresence::IsHostileMission
addresses.comment: `this` in **EAX**, bare `ret`, `push ecx`/`pop ecx` for its one stack slot. Answers 1 when any of missions 1 (military), 2 (tech), 4 (boost our party), 5 (lower national unity), 6 (increase threat) or 8 (covert ops) is set - so counter_espionage, boost_ruling_party and raise_national_unity are the benign three. For mission 0 alone it also resolves the record's target tag (+0xE4) to a country and asks 0x4EF7C0 whether it is allied with the owner (+0xEC), answering benign only when it is. Used once, by CSpyPresence::CatchSpies at 0x52E6A7.

addresses.name: CSpyPresence::CatchSpies
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSpyPresence::CatchSpies(CSpyPresence* presence, CCountryTag* actor, CCountryTag* target)
addresses.comment: Mission 0, counter-espionage: 0x52E3A0 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x52EBDD. **0x52EBE0 abuts it with no int3** (fresh prologue, own SEH handler 0xC8B2B4), so a padding scan runs 4.4 KB past the end - a new instance of the abutting-function trap. Chance, in thousandths: `SPY_DETECTION_CHANCE` (country +0x20, at 0x52E473) plus, when actor==target, the actor's MODIFIER_COUNTER_ESPIONAGE (modifier 55, +0x1B8); times the presence's level; times mission_share[0]; and in the home arm times `1 - 800*(1000-share[0])/1000` where 800 is floorf(800.5f) off the float 0x160AADC. Then per foreign country with at least one whole spy in the target: ally handling through 0x4EF7C0 and IsHostileMission (+1000000 on the chance, or skip), times `1000 - target->MODIFIER_ESPIONAGE_BONUS` (modifier 42, +0x150 - read off the TARGET, so it LOWERS the chance), times NO_MISSION_SPY_DETECTION_MULTIPLIER (+0x3C) when none of that country's nine missions is set. Roll: `(MT19937 % 1000) < chance` through 0xAA2FD0, then a flat second gate `(MT19937 % 100) < 10` through 0xAA2F80. On success the caught country loses exactly 1000 of level (one spy), the actor's spiescaught rises when target==actor, and a message goes up when the actor is the player. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: SpiesCaught_Increment
addresses.comment: `mov eax, [ecx + 0x11D4]` / `inc eax` / `mov [ecx + 0x11D4], eax` at 0x52E779..0x52E780 - **the only writer of CCountry::spiescaught that is not a reset**, and it fires only when the presence's target is the actor itself (the home counter-espionage arm). The nine sites on that field are: the constructor's zero 0x4C9B6D, CCountry::LoadKey 0x4CE5F1, CCountry::SaveContents 0x4D08A4, 0x4D2BA7, the monthly reset 0x4DC8D3, this pair, and two reads in the espionage view (0x6202DF, 0x62849E). **So spiescaught has no gameplay consequence**: nothing but the save writer and the UI reads it.

Only the chance was read: `percent = level * TECH_ESPIONAGE_BASE_CHANCE (country +0x94, at 0x52EC11) / 1000 * mission_share[2] (+0x34) / 1000 / 1000`, then `if (MT19937() % 100 > percent) return` at 0x52EC4B..0x52EC5A - a `>` comparison on whole percent, so a computed 0% still succeeds one day in a hundred. It then reads both countries' CTechnologyStatus (+0xDF8) and goes into 0x540D60; TECH_ESPIONAGE_TECH_PICK_FACTOR is read at 0x52EEED. What is actually stolen was not read. addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus::ApplyTechnologyEffects
addresses.comment:
**How a technology's effects reach the country.** Over every unit type in the definition database (0x1A886F0) it adds `technology->+0x2D0[i] x scale / 1000` into `status->+0x24C[i]`, +0x2E0[i] into +0x25C[i] and +0x2F0[i] into +0x26C[i] - the build cost, manpower and time arrays. Then it sets `status->+0x27C[definition->index]` for every entry of the `activate_unit` vector (CTechnology +0x300..+0x304), sets `status->+0x28C[building->+0x54]` when `activate_building` answers slot 8 true, and hands the country-wide effects to 0x5374F0.

**The technology arrives in EDI** - it is never loaded in the body and both callers set it (0x53292D, 0x532FD5). `ret 8`.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CTechnologyStatus::ApplyTechnologyEffects(CTechnology* technology@EDI, CTechnologyStatus* status@stack:4, int scale@stack:8)

addresses.name: GetDaysToResearch
addresses.comment: `(1.0 - progress) / GetResearchGain(...) + 1`, or -1 when the gain is not positive. `fromScratch` takes the progress as zero rather than reading CTechnologyStatus +0x228[i]. `ret 0xC`, with **the technology in EAX and the status in EDI** - both set by every caller. Five callers: 0x41A2C0, 0x41A2F7, 0x815CED, 0x81F13C, 0x8235D3. That this is a count of *days* is what says one call of GetResearchGain is one day. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.signature: int GetDaysToResearch(CTechnology* technology@EAX, CTechnologyStatus* status@EDI, int level@stack:4, int leadership@stack:8, bool fromScratch@stack:0xC) @EAX

addresses.name: GetResearchGain
addresses.comment:
**The research speed formula.** One call's progress on one level of one technology, answered through `out` as a 64-bit fixed point where **1.0 = 0x8000, i.e. one level**:

    levels per call = leadership x research_efficiency / year_penalty / cost

`cost` is CTechnologyStatus::GetResearchCost (rva 0x1333F0) in thousandths and the code **divides** by it (`__alldiv` at 0x532E89). `research_efficiency` is `1000 + MODIFIER_RESEARCH_EFFICIENCY (id 73) + CTechnologyStatus +0xA8`, floored at 100 by the compiled-in global 0x1A87BE8. `year_penalty` is `1000 + max(dueYear - currentYear, 0) x TECHNOLOGY_YEAR_IMPACT`, where dueYear is `start_year` for level <= 1 and `first_offset + max(level-2,0) x additional_offset` above that, and currentYear is `(CCurrentGameState +0xBDC - 43800000)/24/365.0` truncated - **the calendar year**. So `start_year`, `first_offset` and `additional_offset` are years and they are difficulty, not gates.

**No standard convention fits**: `ret 0xC`, with the level in ecx (-1 meaning `level_by_technology[i] + 1`) and the technology in edx; a leadership of -1000 means read it from CTechnologyStatus +0x238[i]. See reversing/FINDINGS-research.md.
addresses.signature: int64* GetResearchGain(int level@ECX, CTechnology* technology@EDX, CTechnologyStatus* status@stack:4, int64* out@stack:8, int leadership@stack:0xC) @EAX

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus::ClearResearchLeadership
addresses.comment: Zeroes the whole +0x238..+0x23C vector, the leadership assigned to each technology. A bare `ret`, no arguments, **the object in EAX**. One caller, 0x51F6BA in CDistributeResearch slot 0, so the research tick clears the assignments and then writes them back one technology at a time through AdvanceResearch. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus::AdvanceResearch
addresses.comment:
**One tick of research on one technology**, answering whether a level was gained. Records the leadership at +0x238[i], adds GetResearchGain's answer into +0x228[i] as an **8-byte fixed point where 1.0 = 0x8000** (add/adc at 0x532F5B), and returns false unless that reaches 1.0 or the `instantresearch` byte at 0x1A8559B is set. Otherwise it subtracts 1.0, floors at zero, increments +0x218[i], calls ApplyTechnologyEffects (rva 0x132970) with scale 1000, and **zeroes the leftover progress when CTechnology +0x2C0 (additional_offset) is 0** - a single-level technology keeps nothing.

**`this` arrives in EAX, not ecx**, and the technology is the first stack argument; `ret 8`. Both game callers (0x51F73F, 0x51F9DB) are in CDistributeResearch slot 0, plus one at 0x9A2747.
addresses.signature: bool CTechnologyStatus::AdvanceResearch(CTechnologyStatus* this@EAX, CTechnology* technology@stack:4, int leadership@stack:8) @AL

addresses.name: GetCategoryResearchAbility
addresses.comment:
**What one practical or theory contributes to research speed.** Takes the higher of the country's own level (CCountry +0x698[index]) and the level of the country sharing that category with it (CCountry +0x6A8), clamps it to 0..20.000, subtracts 5.000, takes the fixed-point square root (rva 0x69CEC0) of anything above 1.000, and multiplies by 0.100. Below 5.000 the term is negative - the `js` at 0x533339 skips the square root - so an untrained category makes the technology cost more.

**The 20.000 cap is an immediate at 0x533319, not MAX_TECH_ABILITY**, so raising that define past 20 does not raise this. **The out pointer travels in ESI**, never on the stack, which is why the `ret` is 8 and not 12 - the same shape as CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall GetCategoryResearchAbility(int* out@ESI, CTechnologyStatus* status@stack:4, CTechnologyCategory* category@stack:8) @EAX

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus::GetResearchCost
addresses.comment:
**What a level of a technology costs, and where the practical bonus is applied.** Thousandths, answered through the hidden first stack argument and returned in eax (`ret 8`):

    cost = (difficulty x 0.100 + 1.000) x 125 x (1.000 - bonus)

`difficulty` is CTechnology +0x2C8, read by the loader with the same integer helper `start_year` uses, so it is not scaled by 1000; the 0.100 is the compiled-in global 0x1A87BB4 (100) and the x125 is the immediate 0x1E848 over 1000. `bonus` is the sum over the `research_bonus_from` list at CTechnology +0x2A4 (node: [0] category, [4] weight, [0xC] next) of the category's ability term (rva 0x1332B0) times the weight, plus MODIFIER_NUKE_RESEARCH (id 96) when `is_nuclear`, **capped at 900 by the compiled-in global 0x1A87B70** - at most 90% off. Four callers: 0x4D6101, 0x4D6192, 0x532C7B and 0x820C92. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CTechnologyStatus::GetResearchCost(CTechnologyStatus* this, int* out, CTechnology* technology)

addresses.name: CTechnology::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTechnology::LoadKey(CTechnology* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The grammar of the technology files.** A dozen keys of its own - the ones in CTechnology.hpp - and **anything it does not know is taken as a unit type's name**: that is how `infantry_brigade = { soft_attack = 0.1 }` becomes an effect, resolved through the same by-name lookup the unit files use. `research_bonus_from` reads a list, and `folder` and `activate_*` resolve against their own databases.

addresses.name: CTechnology::CheckResearchAllowed
addresses.comment: **Where max_level and additional_offset really are gates.** A level of -1 means the country's next one. It fails when `additional_offset` (+0x2C0) is 0 and the level is above 1 - **so additional_offset = 0 declares a single-level technology** - fails when the level exceeds `max_level` (+0x2C4), checks a per-technology ceiling out of the custom game settings (0x41F500, its +0x28), and ends by evaluating the technology's own `allow` block, [this+0x248] slot 6, with `cmp al, 1; sete al`. **The polarity is unresolved**: both use sites (0x51F728, 0x5335CA) branch *past* the research when it answers true, which reads the opposite way round from that ending. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CTechStatistics::BuildEffectsTooltip
addresses.comment: 0x538D60..0x540598, `ret 0x14`, answers its `out` in EAX. **The Effects block of a technology's tooltip, and a complete field map of CTechStatistics** - 50 localisation keys, 46 of them within five instructions of the load of the field they label, which is the BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip shape and the only other function in the localisation-key sweep that has it. Every arm is `cmp [edi+N], 0 / je skip / cmp [edi+N], 0 (sign picks green 0x15B5C50 or red 0x15B5C58) / mov edx, KEY / mov eax, [edi+N]`. The receiver is a CTechStatistics, which is what CCountry +0xDF8 (a CTechnologyStatus) derives from, so the offsets apply to a country's accumulated totals as well as to one technology's. Three scales: 43 of the 44 scalars are the data file's fraction times 1000 and are shown times 100 with two decimals; `attack_delay` (+0x18) is HOURS times 1000, shown with 0 decimals beside AD_HOURS ("hours"); the combat-tactic vector at +0x24 is the file's whole PERCENTAGE times 1000 with no times-100 step. One caller, 0x5359A0.

addresses.comment: The lazy singleton both technology phases go through: `if ([0x1687B78] == 0) [0x1687B78] = new(0x58)`, so the database object is 0x58 bytes. Extent 0x540D00..0x540D5C, bare `ret`, no arguments, result in eax. Called at 0x6369AA (phase 1), 0x63824F (the after-load pass) and 0x637BA3 (phase 2). The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CTechnologyDataBase::AfterLoadAll
addresses.comment: A third technology call, at 0x638255, after `CombatTactics Initialized` and before countries.txt. Extent 0x540E60..0x540E8C, `ret 4`. Its entire body walks the database's first vector ([db+0]..[db+4], 4-byte elements) and calls **virtual slot 6** on every element - a post-load fix-up over all technologies. `AfterLoadAll` is the guess; what slot 6 is was not read.

addresses.name: CTechnologyDataBase::LoadTechnologies
addresses.comment: **Technology phase 2, and it reads a different input from phase 1.** Extent 0x540E90..0x541BBB, `ret 4`, called once at 0x637BA9 as `push eax` with **no CParseContext** - it does its own file discovery: two search directories off [0x1685558 + 0x358] and [+0x1B4] with the count at [+0x70], two ListFilesWithExtension('.txt') calls (0x540FD8, 0x541027), merge at 0x541091, then a Tokenizer per file at 0x541568. That directory is `technologies/`, confirmed against the mod on disk, which has common/technology.txt and a technologies/ folder of ~30 .txt files. This phase builds the technologies themselves - CNullTechnology at 0x54140C, 'notech' at 0x5413FA, `TECHNOLOGIES loaded ` logged through technology.cpp - and it runs **after the map logic and after CSubUnitDataBase**, logging `TechnologyDatabase Phase #2 Initialized` at eu3application.cpp:1080. **So laws, traits, gainable_traits, combat_tactics, countries, occupation_policies, strategic_resources, triggered_modifiers, on_actions, cb_types, rebel_types and covert_ops are all parsed AFTER the technologies**, and a technology effect naming one of them resolves against a database that is still empty - which the engine answers with index 0, the null object, silently.

addresses.name: CTechnologyDataBase::LoadTechnologyFile
addresses.comment: **Technology phase 1**: reads `common/technology.txt` and builds the **folder and category** skeleton - the body mentions CNullTechnologyFolder (0x541E36) and CNullTechnologyCategory (0x542214) and no technology class at all. Extent 0x541BC0..0x542519, `ret 4`. Called once, at 0x6369B2, as `mov ecx,eax; push context` - the only loader in the whole database stage that is __thiscall rather than (database, context); logs `TechnologyDatabase Phase #1 Initialized` (eu3application.cpp:943). The file arrives as the resolved-path slot [ebp-0x778] of CEU3Application::LoadDatabases.

addresses.name: StringHashInsert
addresses.comment: **The insert half of `StringHashFind` (rva 0x5C7D60) for the instantiation whose key is at `value+8`** - not the `0x5C87C0` one, which keys at `value+4`. The table arrives in **EDI** and the value on the stack. Same hash as the find, `h = (h + c) * 0x3D` over the key's length (`imul eax,eax,0x3D` at 0x542DA8), reduced by `div [edi+4]`; it then `new`s an 8-byte node `{value, next}`, pushes it on the bucket's head and increments `[edi]`. The key is read as an `Hoi3CString` at `value+8` (SSO test `cmp [value+0x1C],0x10`, length at `value+0x18`), which is why a `CObjectType` or a `CGuiType` - both of which put `name` at +8 - can be stored without copying anything. Its one caller is CEU3Graphics::LoadKey's `objectTypes` case at 0xA70FB2.

addresses.name: VcallThunk_Slot11
addresses.comment:
MSVC's vcall thunk for a pointer-to-virtual-member at **slot 11** - two instructions, `mov eax,[ecx]; jmp dword ptr [eax+0x2C]`, so it forwards the caller's stack frame unchanged and the effective calling convention is the callee's. It ends in a `jmp`, not a `ret`, so checkSignatures.py has no ret immediate to test against; the signature above records only the register receiver. **Named class-free on purpose (trap 4): a vcall thunk belongs to a slot index, not a class**, and this one is in no vftable and has zero direct callers.

It matters because it is the one way slot 11 can be reached without a `call [reg+0x2C]` anywhere. Its address appears six times in .text, every time as `push <subject>; push 0x549E00; xor eax,eax; call 0x8A2D70` - BroadcastToListeners, which calls the handler once per registered listener with `ecx` set to that listener's target. The six sites are rva 0x147EE0 (CCreateUnitCommand slot 6), 0x17DF60 (CUnitDeployment slot 9), 0x1DFF9E (CCreateHigherCommand slot 6), 0x1E11C5 (CCreateNewHQCommand slot 6), 0x1EBCD1 and 0x23DFEA. None can be reaching CCombatant slot 11: that body's first act is `mov dword ptr [arg], 0` and the argument at all six is an object pointer, so it would zero the subject's vftable pointer. **But the listener table at rva 0x1714DC0 is filled at runtime, so the general route cannot be closed statically** - it is the stated bound on 'nothing else calls CCombatant slot 11'.

First statement, 0x54EF85-0x54EFB0: `GetCountryById(this->+0x40)->laws(+0x628)[ this->position(+0x48)->index(+0x50) ] = this->law(+0x44)`. **The index field is +0x50, not the +0x4C that CChangeMinisterCommand uses**, because `position` here resolves in a different database: CChangeLawCommand::LoadKey's `position` arm (0x54FC57) sscanf's an integer and indexes `GetLawDataBase()->+0x28`, the law-group vector, while its `law` arm (0x54FC9E) indexes `->+0x18`, the law vector. addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::CBomberCombatant
addresses.comment:
`ret 4` - `this` on the stack, the combat in ecx untouched so that CCombatant::CCombatant can store it at +0x3C. It runs the base with the attacker flag hardwired to 1, writes its own vftable 0x11C45DC, and then builds three vectors of its own:

    +0x10B4  one int per **building definition**, from g_CBuildingDataBase
    +0x10C4  seven ints
    +0x10D4  seven ints
    +0x10E4  int, 0

The first loop is the same lazy-singleton-and-fill the base constructor does for the subunit database, but on a different global: it creates g_CBuildingDataBase inline if it is null (0x30 bytes, 0x1FF buckets) and then pushes one zero per entry of that database's definition vector, count `([db+0x10] - [db+0x0C]) / 4`. So a bomber combatant carries a tally indexed by building type - which is what a strategic raid needs and what nothing else in the combatant family has. The second loop pushes seven zeros into each of +0x10C4 and +0x10D4 and is a plain `for (i = 0; i < 7; ++i)`, not a database count.

The object is 0x10E8 bytes and, like CAirCombatant and CNavalCombatant, leaves +0xB0..+0x10B3 untouched - see CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets for what that region is.

addresses.name: CombatModifierKey
addresses.comment:
**Turns a combat modifier id into its localisation key**, and is the only place that enum is written down. `reversing/combatModifiers.py` reads all 30 names off the jump table at 0x16429C and buildFindings makes them the `CombatModifier` enum, so the arms do not have to be transcribed - which is how this entry was twice wrong before, once putting BM_NIGHT_MODIFIER at 0x1C when it is 0x1B, and once putting BM_SURPRISE_BONUS at 0x1E, one past the end.

**The bound is the function's own**: `cmp eax, 0x1d; ja <default>` at 0x164067, so the ids are 0..0x1D and anything else gets the fallback. The id arrives in **EAX** and the string to build into in **ECX** (`mov esi, ecx` at 0x164065); `ret 0`, so nothing is passed on the stack at all - an earlier reading here said the string was a stack argument, and checkSignatures caught it against the ret.

addresses.name: CCombatant::CCombatant
addresses.signature: CCombatant* __stdcall CCombatant::CCombatant(CCombatant* this@stack:4, bool attacker@stack:8, CCombat* combat@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment: The base constructor every combatant kind runs. `this` and the attacker flag come on the stack and it cleans them (`ret 8`); the combat comes in ecx and is stored at this+0x3C, which is the back-pointer to the combat. Writes, in order: +0x04 = 0x18D, +0x00 = the CCombatant vftable 0x11C4CA4, four CLists at +0x28, +0x40, +0x54, +0x64 (three words and a byte each), three empty vectors at +0x74, +0x88 and +0x98, +0x84 = 0 (losses), +0xAC = 0 (tactic), +0x50 = 0 (dice), +0x38 = the flag, +0x3C = ecx, byte +0xA8 = 0 (unnamed), and finally +0x08..+0x25 zeroed with three movq, a dword and a word (all unnamed). It then pushes one zero into each of +0x74, +0x88 and +0x98 per entry in g_CSubUnitDataBase's definition vector (count = ([db+0x20]-[db+0x1C])/4), so those three are indexed by subunit type by construction - and it creates g_CSubUnitDataBase inline, with a 511-bucket table, if it is null. Returns this in eax.

So duration counts distinct game hours and the routine is safe to call more often than hourly. addresses.name: ResetSubUnitCombatProducts
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 0x3E8` at 0x16563B then `mov [esi+0x50], eax` here and `mov [esi+0x54], eax` at 0x165643 - the per-tick reset of a sub-unit's two combat-modifier products to 1000, inside CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (rva 0x165590, the base slot 19 that all five kinds run first), immediately after the CList at +0x40/+0x44/+0x48 is freed and zeroed. Recorded because it is the **positive control** for the scan that establishes CSubUnit +0x54 has one reader: a scan for [R+0x54] paired with [R+0x50] on the same register finds 435 sites image-wide, of which this is a known write pair on a CSubUnit in the same module and 0x16645E/0x166461 is the only multiply. A negative needs a positive control, and this is it.

addresses.name: CUnit::RetreatFromCombat
addresses.comment:
**Falls a unit back when a combat ends, or removes it from the game when it cannot.**

    call FindRetreatProvince(unit)     ; 0x1C5D50
    ...                                ; or the unit's own province, where the
                                       ; combat is not in it
    cmp  [esp+0x10], 0                 ; is there a destination at all?
    je   <message, then RemoveUnit>

With a destination it records it and sets `disengage` and `retreat`. **Without one the unit is removed from the game** through CGameState::RemoveUnit. Its two calls to that are the same ending reached two ways, differing only in the message shown.

**Do not read this one from the decompiler.** Ghidra invents a `CProvince *unaff_ESI` and tests it against null, which reads like the destination check and is not: at the call site `mov ecx, esi` makes ESI the unit. The destination lives in `[esp+0x10]`.

**Nor should its end be found by looking for padding.** CCombatant::RetreatAllUnits follows it with no `int3` between, so a scan for the next padding run reports that function's bare `ret` as this one's and makes the stack argument look caller-cleaned. It is an ordinary __thiscall: `ret 4`, on five paths.

addresses.name: CCombatant::RetreatAllUnits
addresses.comment:
Walks this side's units (`CCombatant +0x40`) and calls CUnit::RetreatFromCombat on each, so a lost combat falls the whole side back in one pass - and destroys whichever of them have nowhere to go.

The loop pushes the side and does not clean up after the call, which is the clearest evidence that RetreatFromCombat cleans its own argument: anything else would walk the stack up by four bytes per unit.

addresses.name: CCombatant::DetachAllUnits
addresses.comment: Runs CTraitGainTracker::Update for every leader on the side (0x165CFC), then for each unit clears +0x110 and removes this combat from its combats list at +0x114, and finally empties the side's own unit list (+0x40/+0x44/+0x48). Called twice - once per side - from the CCombat method at 0x17AB00 that ends a combat. Name inferred from the body.

addresses.name: CCombatant::GetHighestRankedLeader
addresses.comment: Walks this->units (+0x40), takes each unit's leader_ptr (+0x12C), calls the leader's slot 8 and keeps the one with the largest rank (+0x6C) among those that answer true. Falls back to g_NullLeader (the lazily built 0xD0-byte singleton at 0x16855E0), which is what makes the slot-8 test in UpdatePositioning a real-leader test. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CCombatant::ApplyLosses
addresses.comment:
**Applies a tick's damage to this side's subunits and totals what it cost.** 790 bytes; the receiver is in EDI and the single stack argument is an out parameter that receives the strength lost by this call (`mov [eax], ecx` at 0x1661CE).

The accounting, at 0x16625F, is the part worth hooking. ESI is the **CSubUnit** taking the hit and EDI its combatant:

    edx = subunit->strength (+0x5C) - damage
    type = subunit->definition(+0x58)->index(+0x24)
    if (edx < 0)   combatant->destroyed[type] += 1000; combatant->losses += 1000
    else           combatant->damaged[type]  += the damage

So losses are kept **per side** (+0x84) and **per subunit type** (+0x88 destroyed, +0x98 damaged) and **never per unit** - though the subunit is in hand at that instruction, and CRegiment +0xB0 leads to its CUnit, which is what makes per-unit tracking possible from here.

Two earlier names for this function were wrong, both from partial readings: it is not `ApplyUnitStrengths` and not `ApplyOwnCombatModifiers`. Ghidra had it as a one byte body - reversing/ghidra/RepairFunctionBody.java fixes that - so every reading before the repair saw a fraction of it.

**Extent, settled 2026-10-01 after one wrong attempt.** This function ends with its own `ret 4` at 0x5662ED, so it runs 0x565FD0-0x5662ED. An earlier note here said it continued to 0x566477 and owned a cold block at 0x566455; that was wrong. **0x5662F0 is a separate function** - CCombatant slot 11, held at slot 11 by all seven vftables in the family - abutting this one's `ret` with no int3 padding (trap 2). The `ret 4` at 0x566452 and the block that reads CSubUnit +0x54 are slot 11's. `image.functionStart` answers 0x565FD0 for an address in either; `image.retsBefore(0x565FD0, 0x56645E)` returns three `ret`s, which is the signal.

addresses.name: CCombatant_LossAccounting
addresses.comment: Loss accounting: a destroyed subunit adds 1000 to combatant +0x88[type] and +0x84, damage goes to +0x98[type].

addresses.name: CCombatant::SumSubUnitStrength
addresses.comment: **CCombatant slot 11**, and a function in its own right - it abuts CCombatant::ApplyLosses (0x165FD0), whose `ret 4` is at 0x1662ED with no int3 between them (trap 2). Held at slot 11 by CCombatant and six subclasses (CAirCombatant, CBomberCombatant, CGroundTargetCombatant, CLandTargetCombatant, CNavalCombatant, CNavalTargetCombatant), one direct caller at 0x168EE8 from the pass-through 0x168EE0. It sums, over every CUnit on `units` (+0x40) and every sub-unit on that unit's `regiments` (+0x38): (organisation x strength / 1000) x a modifier, and returns the running total through the `out` pointer (which it also returns in eax, the by-value CFixedPoint convention). The modifier is where slot 9 of the sub-unit branches, at 0x166361. **This function, not ApplyLosses, owns the two instructions project.json already records at 0x166361 and 0x16645E**; TRAPS.md's trap 3 table and FINDINGS-combatmods.md attribute them to ApplyLosses, which is wrong by one function. The name is descriptive of the arithmetic, not recovered.

addresses.name: CombatLosses_SelectProductSource
addresses.comment: `je 0x566455` - the branch that chooses which pair of combat-modifier products a sub-unit's loss factor is built from. Taken when the sub-unit's **slot 9** answers false, in which case the cold block at 0x566455 uses the sub-unit's own CSubUnit +0x54 x +0x50; not taken, the fall-through uses the division's CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0 with +0xF4/+0xF8 and the definition's +0x134/+0x138. Since the CUnit-level products are the land model, slot 9 true is land and false is a ship or wing - **inferred** from the field set, not read out of the slot bodies. **Owning function corrected 2026-10-01**: this is in CCombatant slot 11 (0x5662F0), not CCombatant::ApplyLosses (0x565FD0), which ends at 0x5662ED. The two abut with no padding.

addresses.name: CombatLosses_DiscardedIsNavalCall
addresses.comment: `call edx` on `[vftable+0x28]`, i.e. **CSubUnit slot 10**, the first instruction of the cold block the slot-9 branch at 0x166361 jumps to. Its result is discarded: the next instruction (0x16645E) overwrites eax with `[esi+0x54]`. Slot 10 is the folded ReturnFalse (0x192360) on CSubUnit, CRegiment and CWing and the folded ReturnTrue (0x692590) on CShip, so neither body has a side effect and the call does nothing at all.

addresses.name: CombatLosses_ReadSubUnitDefenceProduct
addresses.comment: `mov eax,[esi+0x54]` followed by `imul [esi+0x50]` and a /1000 - **the only read of CSubUnit +0x54 in the image**, and the proof that defence-side naval, air and bombing combat modifiers are not inert. `esi` is a CSubUnit, established by the same loop reading +0x58, +0x5C, +0x60 and +0xA8. Sits past CCombatant slot 11's `ret 4`: trap 3. **Owning function corrected 2026-10-01**: this is in CCombatant slot 11 (0x5662F0), not CCombatant::ApplyLosses (0x565FD0), which ends at 0x5662ED. The two abut with no padding.
