addresses.comment: pos = 400 (the literal at 0x1A88170); leader = CCombatant::GetHighestRankedLeader(this); if (leader->slot8()) pos += leader->skill (+0x70) * 100 (the literal at 0x1A882E8); NavalStackingPositionPenalty(&this->units (+0x40), &penalty); this->positioning (+0x10B4) = this->+0x10B8 + pos - penalty, clamped at 0. `this` in EDI, bare ret, in no vftable. Called from CNavalCombat slot 13 (0x17B910) at combat start and from CNavalCombatant slot 12 (0x166F20) when a unit joins the side.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::AddUnit
addresses.comment: CCombatant slot 12 for a naval fight (base 0x165190, land 0x1693A0, air 0x16D3E0). It calls CNavalCombatant::UpdatePositioning at 0x166F34, which is why positioning is recomputed whenever a unit joins. The name follows FINDINGS-combat.md's reading of the factory at 0x31370, which calls slot 12 on combat+0x10 with the attacking unit and on combat+0x14 with the defending one; the body itself was not read beyond that call.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets(CNavalCombatant* this, CNavalCombatant* out, CSubUnit* attacker)
addresses.comment:
**This is what the ~0x1000 unwritten bytes are.** The function clears `out->+0x10B0` to 0, walks `this->units` (+0x40) and each unit's subunits (CUnit +0x38), and for every subunit that passes its filters does

    out->[0xB0 + count * 4] = subunit;  ++out->+0x10B0

So a naval, air or bomber combatant carries a fixed array of **1024 `CSubUnit*` at +0xB0 with its count at +0x10B0**: 0xB0 + 1024 * 4 = 0x10B0, and the count dword ends at 0x10B4, which is exactly where all three classes' own fields start. It is scratch - the count is reset on every call, nothing initialises it at construction and no LoadKey or SaveContents touches it - which is why the constructors leave the region alone. 0x1675D0 then picks one entry with `random % count` (`idiv [ebx+0x10B0]` at 0x5678CC) as the target of one attack.

CLandCombatant does not have it: that class is 0xE4 bytes and uses +0xB0 for its `front` list. There is no bounds check on the append.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::PickTarget
addresses.comment:
**Where naval positioning is actually spent: it buys a better choice of target, not more damage.** Called once per firing ship from CNavalCombatant::Attack (0x167ACA); the ship is in ECX, the side and the enemy on the stack.

    country = resolve(attacker->unit(+0xB0)->+0x290 ? +0x28C : +0x124)
    p = attacker->+0x58->positioning (+0x184) + side->positioning (+0x10B4)
    p = p * 100000 / 1000                                     ; x100
    p = p * (1000 + country->CTechnologyStatus(+0xDF8)->+0x70) / 1000
    p = p / 1000
    if the combat's province is at night: p = p / 2

and p then gates a search over the enemy's lists with five draws from Random (0x6A2F80). So the CSubUnitDefinition field `positioning`, the combatant's accumulated +0x10B4, a naval technology figure at CTechnologyStatus +0x70 and a halving at night all feed one number, and that number is a target-selection quality. **+0x10B4 is read nowhere in the damage path** - CNavalCombatant::Attack's only two touches of it are the creep that raises it. The selection rule past the gate was not read, and attacker->+0xB8/+0xBC, which the search walks, is unidentified. **Qualified `CSubUnit::`, not `CNavalCombatant::`, and deliberately**: the receiver really is in ECX and really is a `CSubUnit` - the entry does `mov edi, ecx; mov eax, [edi+0xb0]`, and `+0xB0` is `CSubUnit::unit_ptr`. The old `CNavalCombatant::` qualifier typed `this` as the wrong class and mis-decompiled every field access through it, and because the `ret` arithmetic is identical either way `checkSignatures.py` could never see it (trap 11). Not a virtual - `vtable.py --holding` puts it in no table - and one caller, `CNavalCombatant::Attack` at 0x167ACA, which is why it reads a combatant's `+0x10B4` as an ordinary argument rather than through `this`.
addresses.signature: CSubUnit* __thiscall CSubUnit::PickTarget(CSubUnit* attacker, CNavalCombatant* side, CCombatant* other)

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::Attack
addresses.comment: CCombatant slot 15 for a naval fight, the sibling of CLandCombatant::Attack (0x16B340). **Only its tail, 0x167980..0x167A28, was read**: it recomputes the positioning cap without the die - cap = 400 + (leader ? leader->skill * 100 : 0) - NavalStackingPositionPenalty(units), floored at 100 - and if this->positioning is below it, adds 20 (the literal at 0x1A88174). The body above 0x167980, where the damage is decided and where positioning is presumably multiplied in, is unread.

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombatant::LoadKey(CNavalCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 1 of them, one case each: `positioning`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::CLandCombatant
addresses.signature: CLandCombatant* __cdecl CLandCombatant::CLandCombatant(CLandCombatant* this@ESI, bool attacker@AL, CCombat* combat@ECX) @EAX
addresses.comment: The only combatant kind with a constructor the compiler did not inline. Everything travels in registers: `push eax; push esi; call CCombatant::CCombatant` forwards the flag and the object, ecx falls through untouched to the base. It then writes `[esi] = 0x11C4DFC` and zeroes three CLists - +0xB0/+0xB4/+0xB8/byte +0xBC, +0xC0.., +0xD0.. - and byte +0xE0, and returns this in eax. CLandCombatant::LoadKey (0x169040) names all three: +0xB0 is `front` (key 0x396), +0xC0 `reserves` (0x398) and +0xD0 `retreat` (0x1A6); it also sets byte +0xE0 to 1 on every call. The destructor at 0x168E40 walks and frees the nodes of all three through their +8 next pointers. The object is 0xE4 bytes.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::SumSubUnitStrength
addresses.comment: **CLandCombatant's slot 11, and it adds nothing**: it pushes its own `out` argument, calls CCombatant::SumSubUnitStrength (0x1662F0) *non-virtually*, returns the out pointer in eax and `ret 4`. ECX is never touched, so `this` passes straight through. It is the eighth member of the slot-11 family - project.json's note on 0x1662F0 lists the seven vftables that hold the base and this is the one that does not. The body appears exactly once in the whole image, at 0x11C4E28 = CLandCombatant's vftable + 0x2C, so the only route into it is a virtual call through slot 11. An override that only forwards to the base is what is left when a derived implementation is emptied, and nothing else distinguishes it.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::LoadKey(CLandCombatant* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 2 of them, one case each: `front`, `reserves`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CCombatant::PickTarget
addresses.comment:
**Draws one of a side's front line units at random**, uniformly: `r % side->front_line.count` nodes along the CList at +0xB0, or 0 when the count is below 1. The side is in EDI, the random state in EDX and the result comes back in EAX - which has to be said, because a signature that places any parameter switches Ghidra to custom storage and then the **return** needs a place as well or it decompiles as an undefined4 at every call site. ECX is live at the call but the body never reads it, so it is not an argument.

The generator is the MSVC one, `x = x * 0x343FD + 0x269EC3` twice per draw with the top bits multiplied together, and its state is threaded through the whole tick from CLandCombatant::Attack - so one stream decides every target and every fractional shot in a round.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::AddAssaultModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::AddAssaultModifiers(CLandCombatant* this, CUnit* unit, int unknown)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 27, land only, and called for the attacker only** (from 0x16A347, inside `if (is_attacker)`). Decides four modifiers. First it classifies the assault: if the unit's own province is water then amphibious, unless the owner tag is literally 'REB'; otherwise it finds the ProvinceEdge from the unit's province to the combat's province and reads its `kind` - **2 is a river crossing, 1 is a sea crossing**.

BM_RIVER_PENALTY (0x0E) at 0x169864: `v = RIVER_CROSSING_PENALTY + unit->+0xC8->river.attack(+0x9C) + GetTraitEffect(unit, 7 river_attack)`; added only when negative, and sets +0x16.

BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY (0x0D) at 0x1698A5: when unit->+0x97 is set, `v = PARADROP_PENALTY + GetTraitEffect(unit, 27 paradrop_mission)`, negative only, sets +0x15, and clears the amphibious flag.

BM_AMPH_PENALTY (0x0B) at 0x169A63: `v = AMPHIBIOUS_LANDING_PENALTY + unit->+0xC8->amphibious.attack(+0xB4) + GetTraitEffect(unit, 25 amph_attack)`. When that is negative and 0x1C2E80(unit, 0) and the province has a naval base (+0x300), the penalty is cut by the landing-craft technology: `s = 1000 + sum over the division's regiments of lookup(base->+0xC8->+0x218.., regiment->def->type_index)->+0x10`, `r = min(s * base->+0xC8->+0x18C / 1000, AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_LANDING_PENALTY_DECREASE)`, `v = v * (1010 - r * 1000 / cap) / 1000`, then `v = max(v, -990)`. 1010 and -990 are inline floorf of the literals 1010.5 (0x120A7C8) and -989.5 (0x120A7C4), not defines. Sets +0x13.

BM_FORT_MODIFIER (0x0C) at 0x169B3D: `level = prov->modifiers(+0x114)[amphibious ? 11 COASTAL_FORT_LEVEL : 10 FORT_LEVEL] / 1000 * 1000` (truncated to whole levels); for the attacker `v = level * BASE_FORT_PENALTY / 1000 + GetTraitEffect(unit, 8 fort_attack) + unit->+0xC8->fort.attack(+0x84)`, zeroed if positive; **for the defender v is GetTraitEffect(unit, 24 fort_defence) and nothing else** - the fort itself reaches land combat only as the attacker's penalty. Sets +0x14. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CLandCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment: **Slot 19 for a land fight**, and the readable example of the family. Walks `units` (+0x40), and for a unit that is invading over water interpolates between AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_ATTACK_LOW and _HIGH into CUnit +0xF4 and between the defend pair into +0xF8. Calls the base at 0x165590 first.

addresses.name: LandSurprise_Gate
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [eax+0x1C], 0x18` - the surviving gate of land combat's removed surprise mechanic: this side must be the attacker (`cmp byte [ebx+0x38],0` at 0x16A29F), a byte local at [esp+0xE] must be clear, and the combat's `day` (CCombat +0x1C) must be **under 24 ticks**. All three guards are intact and all they guard is an inlined GetDefines() whose result is never read - the fast path at 0x16A2C8 jumps past the whole singleton block straight to the `push 1` at 0x16A327 - and the discarded trait read at 0x16A330.

addresses.name: LandSurprise_DiscardedTraitRead
addresses.comment: `call CUnit::GetTraitEffect (0x1D1120)` with kind **1 = surprise_chance** - **the only read of that trait kind in the whole image, and its answer is thrown away.** The out buffer is the stack slot the `lea ecx,[esp+0x44]` at 0x16A329 takes (frame+0x40 after the `push 1`), and no instruction in CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers reads `[esp+0x40]`; eax is clobbered at 0x16A33B by `mov eax,[ebp+8]` without being read, and cfg.py shows the only edges into 0x16A335 are the two skip branches. The control: the other eleven GetTraitEffect sites in this function all dereference the returned pointer on the very next instruction (`mov eax,[eax]` / `add edi,[eax]`), each with its own buffer at esp+0x4C, 0x50, 0x54, 0x58, 0x60, 0x68, 0x70, 0x74, and the function has no `[ebp - N]` locals at all. So the engine's only way to read a trait effect is through eax, and this site does not.

addresses.name: LandCombatWeatherCall
addresses.comment: `call 0xB4000` in CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers: &combat->province->weather (combat+0x18, then +0x68) and the unit's owner tag (CUnit+0x124/+0x128).

addresses.name: LandCombatWeatherModifier
addresses.comment: `push 0x1A; call CUnit::AddCombatModifier` - BM_WEATHER on a land unit, attack and defence both set to the negated CWeather::LandCombatEffect. Skipped entirely when the effect comes out 0.

addresses.name: ArmorAdvantage_CompareArmourToPiercing
addresses.comment: `cmp edx, dword ptr [ecx+0x13C]` then `jg 0x16AD8D`: edx is the **maximum** of `unit->+0xC8->armor (+0x12C)` over this side's front line (the cmovl loop at 0x16AD50..0x16AD68) and [ecx+0x13C] is one enemy front-line unit's `piercing_attack`. The loop at 0x16AD74 stops at the **first** enemy unit whose piercing is below our best armour, so the test is existential, not universal - recorded as what the bytes do. Both lists are `front_line` (CCombatant +0xB0), not `units` (+0x40).

addresses.name: ArmorAdvantage_SetFlag
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [ebx+0x1B], 1` - sets BM_ARMOR_ADVANTAGE's bit of CCombatant::modifier_used (+0x08 + 0x13), the last thing CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers does. Gated on `other->slot 6()` at 0x16AD33, which is true only for a CLandCombatant, so the flag is land-versus-land only. **Its only reader in the image is CCombatModifierTrigger::Evaluate (0x607E80)**, by computed index - so the flag reaches script and the modifier tooltip and nothing in the simulation. The armour mechanic itself is implemented separately in CLandCombatant::FireUnit at 0x16B05A.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::FireUnit
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CLandCombatant::FireUnit(CLandCombatant* side@stack:4, uint* random@stack:8, CUnit* attacker@ESI, CCombatant* enemy@ECX)
addresses.comment:
**One attacking unit's shots for a tick.** The attacker is in **ESI** and the side being shot at in **ECX**, neither loaded from the frame; the two stack arguments are this side and the tick's random state. Read off the call site in CLandCombatant::Attack (0x16B3B0..0x16B3BE), not off the decompiler - which showed the enemy as EDI, the register FireUnit copies ECX into at 0x16ADE3 for CCombatant::PickTarget's benefit.

It draws **one** target for the whole tick - CCombatant::PickTarget, a uniform random pick from the enemy's front line - and then works out how many shots to fire:

    hard = attacker.definition.hard_attack * (1000 + owner.HARD_ATTACK) / 1000
    soft = attacker.definition.soft_attack * (1000 + owner.SOFT_ATTACK) / 1000
    s    = target.definition.softness
    hard = hard * (1000 - s) / 1000      soft = soft * s / 1000
    shots = (attacker.+0xEC * attacker.+0xF4 / 1000) * (soft + hard) / 1000 / 1000
    and the remainder is a chance at one more shot

**So the split between soft and hard attack is the target's softness**, and the combat modifier the tooltip prints multiplies the shot *count* rather than the damage per shot.

Each shot then runs while the target is not already finished (CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight): the defence is the target's toughness when this side is defending and its defensiveness when attacking, times the target's own defend product; CUnit::RollToHit decides; and on a hit the damage is scaled by the combat's doctrine figure plus CUnit::StrengthDamageFactor, halved through LAND_COMBAT_STR/ORG_ARMOR_DEFLECTION_FACTOR when the attacker's piercing_attack is below the target's armor, scaled again by LAND_COMBAT_STR/ORG_DAMAGE_MODIFIER, and handed to CUnit::TakeDamage.

addresses.name: FireUnit_ArmorOnSoftTest
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [edx+0x12C], eax` then `jle 0x16B08E` - **the live armour-advantage mechanic**, in CLandCombatant::FireUnit. eax is the drawn target's `+0xC8->piercing_attack (+0x13C)` (loaded at 0x16B04E off the target CUnit at [esp+8]) and [edx+0x12C] is the attacker's `+0xC8->armor`. When the attacker's armour exceeds the target's piercing, both land dice sizes are replaced: EDI takes LAND_COMBAT_STR_ARMOR_ON_SOFT_DICE_SIZE instead of LAND_COMBAT_STR_DICE_SIZE and EBX takes LAND_COMBAT_ORG_ARMOR_ON_SOFT_DICE_SIZE instead of LAND_COMBAT_ORG_DICE_SIZE. This is the counterpart of the deflection halving the record already notes on this function, which runs the other way round (attacker piercing below target armor). Note it is the **summed** definition on both sides, so a division's armour is the sum of its brigades'.

addresses.name: FireUnit_ArmorOnSoftStrDice
addresses.comment: `imul dword ptr [ecx+0x158]` with eax = 0x10624DD3 and a `sar edx,6` after it - the divide-by-1000 of **LAND_COMBAT_STR_ARMOR_ON_SOFT_DICE_SIZE** (military block, CDefines +0xAC, entry +0x158), and the only reader of that define in the image. ECX is the military block, loaded at 0x16B014 from the inlined GetDefines. It overwrites the LAND_COMBAT_STR_DICE_SIZE value taken at 0x16B034.

addresses.name: FireUnit_ArmorOnSoftOrgDice
addresses.comment: `mov ecx, dword ptr [ecx+0x15C]` - **LAND_COMBAT_ORG_ARMOR_ON_SOFT_DICE_SIZE** (military +0x15C), divided by 1000 two instructions later, and the only reader of that define. It overwrites the LAND_COMBAT_ORG_DICE_SIZE value taken at 0x16B01F. Both of these were a false zero for fieldchain.py --holder because its default window is 0x40 bytes and the block pointer is loaded 0x53 bytes earlier.

addresses.name: CLandCombatant::Attack
addresses.comment: **One side's shooting for a tick**, CCombatant slot 15, which CCombat is pure virtual for. Walks this side's front line - the CList at CCombatant +0xB0 - and calls CLandCombatant::FireUnit once per unit on it. Everything before that is set-up: it refreshes the doctrine figures out of LAND_DOCTRINE_INCREASE and seeds the tick's random stream.

addresses.name: CCombat::AttachAndRegister
addresses.comment:
**CCombat virtual slot 5**, and the same implementation in all seven kinds - none of CLandCombat, CNavalCombat, CAirCombat or the three bombings overrides it.

What it does, in order:

1. sets the word at `+0x29` to 1
2. walks the attacker's units (`combat+0x10`, then the combatant's list at `+0x40`, nodes `{ data, ?, next }`) and calls 0x1BFE80 for each
3. the same for the defender at `combat+0x14`
4. asks its own slot 8, and on false appends the combat to its province's combat list through 0xA5F90; on true stores itself at `province+0x2FC` if that is empty
5. goes on to slot 11 (GetKind)

So it is the step that puts a built combat into play: both sides' units attached, and the combat findable from its province. 0xA5F90's other caller is CCombatManager::CreateCombat's tail, which does the same registration - so this is that work reached virtually.

**A known crash site.** It faults at `0x16E391`, reading `defender->units`, when `combat+0x14` holds something that is not a combatant. Seen in a user's dump with `+0x14 == 1`, the attacker a valid combatant and its unit list empty, at **3.62 GB private in a 32-bit address space**.

The obvious reading is CreateCombatants stopping half way: its second `operator new(0xE4)` throws `bad allocation`, so `+0x14` is never written and keeps the combat's own recycled block content, while `+0x10` keeps the attacker it already stored. The unit list is empty because units are added after slot 6, not by it. And the combat is already on the manager's list - CCombatManager::AddCombat runs before slot 6 in both the loader (0x2FCBE) and the live factory (0x31424) - so it stays there for whatever walks that list next to call this and read `0x41`.

**That reading needs a catch above and there is none** - no try block in eight levels of direct callers above CCombatManager::CreateCombat, none in CInGameIdler::Update or DailyUpdate, and one __try in the whole image, in the CRT. An uncaught `bad allocation` ends the process, so it cannot leave a half-built combat for later. The proximate cause is certain and the 3.62 GB is real; the route between them is open. See reversing/FINDINGS-combat.md.

addresses.name: CCombat::AddUnit
addresses.comment:
Slot 18. Offers a unit to a combat that already exists and lets the combat pick the side:

    a = this->attacker->slot 17 (unit)
    d = this->defender->slot 17 (unit)
    if (d && !a)   attacker->slot 12 (unit); 0x5BFE80; if (!this->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(unit, 1); return true
    if (a && !d)   defender->slot 12 (unit); 0x5BFE80; if (!this->slot 8 ()) 0x5C7970(unit, 0); return true
    return false

so a unit joins the side the *other* side is hostile to, and a unit both sides or neither side object to is refused. The defender branch has two extra gates for bombings - the unit's own slot 17 and the global test at 0x5CDC30. CCombatManager::CreateCombat calls this for every bystander in the province; the same body is slot 18 in all six combat classes.

addresses.name: CCombat::Tick
addresses.comment:
**The land per-tick combat resolution**, CCombat slot 15 - and CLandCombat's, which shares this body. **Not naval or air**: both override the slot, with 0x17BA00 and 0x17BC50, and neither reaches slot 19 at all. Increments `duration` (+0x20), swaps tactics when TACTIC_SWAP_FREQUENCEY divides it or either side has none, then calls CCombatant slot 19 on `attacker` (+0x10) and `defender` (+0x14) and CCombatant slot 15 on each, and finally ApplyOwnCombatModifiers on each. The one stack argument is **never read** - `[ebp+8]` appears nowhere in the function - so it is named for the space it takes.

**The refresh is gated on the PLAYER being a belligerent, established 2026-10-02.** In CCombat::Tick the call at 0x16F34C is reached only when CountryIdListContains (0x4A8630) answers true for the **defender's** CCombatant::countries (+0x54) at 0x16F330 or the **attacker's** at 0x16F343, and the id it looks for is the player's: 0x16F2E9/0x16F2EF load `[gameState+0xC30]` and `[gameState+0xC34]` - player tag and player id - into the local the gate is handed. 

**So this runs only for combats the human player is in.** An AI-vs-AI battle never calls it, and therefore never computes CCombatant slot 11 or reads CSubUnit +0x54 at all. That is a stronger statement than 'the defence-side naval/air/bombing modifiers only feed a display': they are **player-only**, so they cannot be part of a symmetric simulation even in principle. It also means a live probe on slot 11 sees nothing unless the player is a belligerent - an observer country gives zero calls, which must not be mistaken for a negative result.

This is the call that gives CCombatManager::CreateCombat's second argument its type, and it is what puts the province the CCombatHistoryEntry constructor later reads +0xD0 off.

addresses.name: CCombat::GetAttackerStrengthShare
addresses.comment: **CCombat slot 17, and the one consumer of CCombatant slot 11.** Held at slot 17 by all seven combat vftables (CCombat, CLandCombat, CAirCombat, CNavalCombat, CGroundBombing, CLandBombing and one more), overridden by none. It calls slot 11 on `attacker` (+0x10) at 0x17B083 and on `defender` (+0x14) at 0x17B091, each with its own stack out-slot, floors both at `(int)floor(1.5f) = 1` (the float 1.5 at rva 0x13179AC, truncated inline through floorf 0x1FD0 and 0x808870), and returns `attacker * 1000 / (attacker + defender)` - the attacker's share of the two sides' summed strength, in thousandths. The `total == 0` arm at 0x17B0AA writes -1 and is unreachable, because both terms are already floored to 1. The division is done three ways depending on magnitude: a plain `imul`/`idiv` when `a + 0x189373 <= 0x39580D`, otherwise through __allmul and __alldiv. Its only call site found is 0x17C15C, in CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow.

addresses.name: CombatShare_AttackerSum
addresses.comment: `call eax` on `[attacker_vftable + 0x2C]` - **the attacking side's CCombatant slot 11**, with `ecx = this->attacker (+0x10)` and the out slot [ebp-4]. With 0x17B091 (the defender, out slot [ebp-8]) these are the only two invocations of slot 11 found anywhere in the image, and they are what makes every combat modifier on every unit and sub-unit reach a number.

addresses.name: CombatShare_DefenderSum
addresses.comment: `call edx` on `[defender_vftable + 0x2C]` - the defending side's CCombatant slot 11, `ecx = this->defender (+0x14)`, out slot [ebp-8]. The pair at 0x17B083/0x17B091 is read, then each is floored at 1 by `cmovl` against the inline `(int)floor(1.5f)`.

addresses.name: CLandCombat::CLandCombat
addresses.comment: The CCombat base constructor inlined plus CLandCombat's two vftables - there is no separate CCombat::CCombat body. Sets +0x04 = 0x18D, +0x08 = 0x11C0694 (the CSelectable base table) then 0x11C4F34 (CLandCombat's own), byte +0x0C = 0, +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 = 0 (attacker, defender, province all null at this point), +0x1C = -1 (day), +0x20..+0x40 = 0, +0x00 = 0x11C4EE4. Both callers allocate 0x44 bytes for it, which is CCombat's size.

addresses.name: CLandCombat::CreateCombatants
addresses.comment:
CCombat slot 6, land. Two `operator new(0xE4)` calls, each followed by CLandCombatant::CLandCombatant (0x168DB0) with the attacker flag in al (1 then 0) and this in ecx; the results go to this+0x10 (attacker) and this+0x14 (defender). A failed allocation stores null and skips the constructor - the only branching in it. It reads nothing at all off the combat: the object is still blank at this point, because both call sites run slot 6 immediately after the constructor and before anything else is set. The SEH frame (state -1/0/1) exists only to destroy the first combatant if the second allocation throws.

**How it goes wrong, from a user's dump.** `combat+0x14` is written only after the second `operator new(0xE4)` returns, and that `operator new` (0x79602F) **throws** rather than answering null. So a failure there leaves `+0x14` holding whatever the combat's own recycled `operator new(0x44)` block held - a 1, in the dump - while `+0x10` keeps a valid attacker, because the unwind state is -1 across that allocation and frees nothing. The combat is already on the manager's list by then (CCombatManager::AddCombat runs before this slot), so it stays there half-built for CCombat::AttachAndRegister to find.

**That reading needs a catch above and there is none** - no try block in eight levels of direct callers above CCombatManager::CreateCombat, none in CInGameIdler::Update or DailyUpdate, and one __try in the whole image, in the CRT. An uncaught `bad allocation` ends the process, so it cannot leave a half-built combat for later. The proximate cause is certain and the 3.62 GB is real; the route between them is open. See reversing/FINDINGS-combat.md.

addresses.name: CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow
addresses.comment:
**The combat_status window's per-tick refresh**, and the end of the chain that consumes every combat modifier. 0x609 bytes, bare `ret` at 0x17C379, the receiver in **ESI** and never loaded from the frame (trap: it takes no stack argument at all). One caller, 0x16F34C at the very end of CCombat::Tick, guarded by the combat not being kind 2 or 3 and by the player's own country tag appearing in `defender->countries` (+0x54) or `attacker->countries` - so it runs only for a combat the player is in. On its first call it looks up the GUI windows named 'combat_status' (0x11C4C78) and 'combat_status_close' (0x11C4C88) and caches them in CCombat +0x2C and +0x30; thereafter it jumps straight to 0x17BF92. It then calls CCombat::GetAttackerStrengthShare (slot 17) at 0x17C15C, picks one of three icon states from the share against 660 and 330 thousandths - the order inverted when the player is the defender - pushes the state into [combat+0x2C]'s slot 24, and formats share x 100000 / 1000 into a string through 0x65ACA0. Marked likely because the two GUI objects' classes were not identified; the arithmetic and the call chain are read.

**'Window' in this name is a misnomer, established 2026-10-02** (reversing/FINDINGS-gui.md). What it updates is a pair of **billboards** - textured quads drawn on the map - not GUI windows: `combat_status` and `combat_status_close` are `billboardType` entries in `interface/mapitems.gfx`, and the lookup runs against the object-type registry at `CGraphics +0x6BCF0`, which is not the GUI registry and does not resemble it. The name is kept only because FINDINGS-gui.md and FINDINGS-combat3.md both cite it throughout; read it as UpdateCombatStatusBillboards.

**The refresh is gated on the PLAYER being a belligerent, established 2026-10-02.** In CCombat::Tick the call at 0x16F34C is reached only when CountryIdListContains (0x4A8630) answers true for the **defender's** CCombatant::countries (+0x54) at 0x16F330 or the **attacker's** at 0x16F343, and the id it looks for is the player's: 0x16F2E9/0x16F2EF load `[gameState+0xC30]` and `[gameState+0xC34]` - player tag and player id - into the local the gate is handed. 

**So this runs only for combats the human player is in.** An AI-vs-AI battle never calls it, and therefore never computes CCombatant slot 11 or reads CSubUnit +0x54 at all. That is a stronger statement than 'the defence-side naval/air/bombing modifiers only feed a display': they are **player-only**, so they cannot be part of a symmetric simulation even in principle. It also means a live probe on slot 11 sees nothing unless the player is a belligerent - an observer country gives zero calls, which must not be mistaken for a negative result.

addresses.comment: `call StringHashFind` with `eax = CInGameIdler->slot17() + 0x6BCF0` - the **object-type** registry on CEU3Graphics, not a GUI registry - and the name `combat_status` (string at 0x15C4C78). The result's slot 18 at 0x57BE5F is CBillboardType::CreateInstance, and the live billboard is cached in `CCombat +0x2C` at 0x57BE7F. `combat_status` is a `billboardType` in `interface/mapitems.gfx` with `noOfFrames = 3`.

Beware the two other `[reg+0x44]` calls in the same function, at 0x17BE4B and 0x17BECE: their receiver is the GUI manager, not a CCombat, which is trap 12 on a slot number.

addresses.signature: void __stdcall AddExperience(CLeader* leader@ESI, int factor@stack:4, int amount@stack:8)

addresses.comment:
Puts a leader back to the state he was defined with. The leader arrives in **eax** and costs no stack - a bare `ret` - and nothing comes back.

`rank` (+0x6C) to 0; `skill` (+0x70) to `starting_skill` (+0xC8) but only where that is not negative, so a leader defined with -1 keeps the skill he has; `current_experience` (+0x78, 64 bit) to `starting_experience` (+0xCC) scaled by 32768/1000, computed as `__alldiv(exp << 30, 0x1F40000)` - 2^30 over 1000*32768, which is the same ratio without losing the low bits.

Then a step the earlier note missed: the new experience is **clamped down** to `table[0x170AEE0][skill] << 15`, the experience ceiling for the skill just written, so resetting can lower the experience as well as raise it. Finally, where +0xC4 is non-null it is passed in edi to 0x74140, which walks a list off its +0xC.

One caller: a loop at 0x4D2DE3 over the list at `[ebx+0xE10]`, taking each node's +0 into eax and stepping by +8.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModel::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CHistoricalModel::LoadKey(CHistoricalModel* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **No keys of its own.** Every key is taken as a **technology's name**: it is looked up in the technology database, that technology's effects are walked for the one whose CSubUnitDefinition index matches this model's unit type, and it is applied (`0x111D90`). A name that is not a technology, or one with nothing for this type, is logged against `model.cpp` with both names. So a model is the list of technologies a unit was built with.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModelSet::MakeSubUnit
addresses.comment: **Builds a throwaway regiment to compare models against.** From the set's definition it news a CRegiment, a ship or an air unit by the two flags at `CSubUnitDefinition +0x2C` and `+0x2E`, calls CSubUnit::SetType, then walks the definition's `technologies` vector (`+0x44..+0x48`) and writes each one's researched level - `CTechnologyStatus::level_by_technology[technology->index]` of the country the set's tag names - into the matching node of the new regiment's `technologies` list, and finishes with CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies. Its only caller destroys it immediately. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModelSet::PickCurrentModel
addresses.comment: **The model a country would build right now**: MakeSubUnit for a regiment carrying the country's current research, PickBestModel against it, then the regiment's deleting destructor. Takes its one argument in eax and answers in eax, an LTCG convention. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel
addresses.comment: **Which of a unit type's models a country would build today.** `ret 4`, so it takes **one** stack argument, not two: ecx is the CHistoricalModelSet whose first three words are the model vector, and the stack argument is a CSubUnit whose `technologies` list at `+0x84` says what the country has researched. It scores every model as the sum, over the model's own CSubUnitTechnology entries, of `|the regiment's level - the level the model wants| * 1000`, **counting only technologies whose `CTechnology::change` is set** (789 of 1175 in this mod), and answers the model with the smallest total - starting from 999,999,000, and null for an empty set. **The absolute value is what `Patches::historicalModelLogicFix` replaces**, so that a model asking for more than is researched is penalised rather than treated as equally close. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: InitMissionEfficiencyModifiers
addresses.comment:
**This is what fills the table at 0x174DA00**, which FINDINGS-navaldetection left open. One loop, i = 0..0x20 (33 missions):

    if (i == 0) { table[0] = 0; continue; }                       ; 0x583A8A
    token = MissionIndexToOrderToken(i)                           ; 0x184640
    name  = <token's save key> + "_eff"                           ; the literal '_eff' at 0x15C5310
    id    = (modifierDefs.end (0x1686198) - modifierDefs.begin (0x1686194)) / 4
    def   = new CModifierDefinition(0x2C bytes, vftable 0x15BC4E4)
    def->name (+0x4) = name;  def->+0x20 = token;  def->id (+0x24) = id;  def->+0x28 = 0x0101
    modifierDefs.push_back(def)                                   ; 0x5C5D0
    table[i] = id                                                 ; 0x5839F0

So the 32 mission-efficiency modifiers are **created by the engine at startup, not read out of any file**, and their ids are consecutive from whatever the modifier count already was. Their keys are the order's own save token plus `_eff`, so the two that matter here are **`convoy_escort_eff` and `convoy_raid_eff`** (indices 9 and 10). BlackICE defines neither - nothing in `common/` uses any `*_eff` key - so the GetMissionEfficiency difference in ShouldStartNavalCombat currently rests on the technology term alone.

addresses.name: CreateOrder
addresses.comment: The order factory: one binary-search switch on the `GetTypeId` token with a case per concrete order class, each allocating and constructing. `ret 0` with `add esp, 8` at all 21 call sites. `arg` is 0 in both sites read - `CUnit::SetOrder` (0x1CD9E0) and `CUnit` slot 31 (0x1BA2F0), both of which build a `CNullOrder` with `CreateOrder(0x18D, 0)`. Some branches also read `edi`, so a caller that relies on a non-zero `arg` may be passing more than the two stack words.

The name is ours; the mapping itself was not tabulated.

addresses.name: CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit_Thunk
addresses.comment:
CStrategicRedeploymentOrder vftable **slot 13** - the virtual that dispatches to the re-route. Five instructions and nothing else: `push edi; mov edi,ecx; call CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit; pop edi; ret`. It exists because the compiler gave the body a register calling convention (the order in edi) and the table needs an ordinary `__thiscall` entry. The bool comes straight back in al.

Slot 13 is `_purecall` on COrder itself, so every concrete order supplies its own: CMoveOrder 0x187B00, CAirOrder 0x18A790, CSupportAttackOrder 0x187FB0. Those are not named here - only this one is known to route.

addresses.name: CStrategicRedeploymentOrder::RouteUnit
addresses.comment:
The body of the order-side re-route. **Not a virtual and not CMoveCommand::RouteUnit's slot-mate**: it is a private helper reached in three places, one of them the `push edi; mov edi,ecx; call` thunk at 0x188440 that occupies CStrategicRedeploymentOrder vftable **slot 13**, where CMoveCommand::RouteUnit is slot 6 of the CCommand hierarchy (and slot 6 is CCommand::Execute). Two different hierarchies, two different slots; what they share is the work, not the dispatch.

The order arrives in edi and costs no stack - a bare `ret` at both exits - and the answer is a bool in al. What it does, in order:

1. Touches `g_CCurrentGameState`, creating it (0xDA8 bytes, CGameState::CGameState then the CCurrentGameState vftable) if it is still null - the singleton accessor inlined.
2. **Gives up early, answering true, when the unit is not due yet**: `if (gamestate[0xBDC] < order->unit->[0xCC]) return true`.
3. **Gives up early, answering true, when the unit is already heading the right way**: where the unit has a path (count at +0x140 > 0), its first province (`g_CMap->[0x2200][ path[0] ]`) is compared against the order's target province at +0xC, and an equal one means there is nothing to redo.
4. Otherwise builds a **CVerySafePathFind** in the frame (vftable 0x15C5B6C written at 0x1887FE) - always that finder, never the plain or merely-safe one CMoveCommand picks between - and calls CPathFind::Find with the unit, the unit's +0x130 and the order's target province.
5. On success calls SetUnitPath(unit, path, 1) and answers true; on failure it destroys the finder and answers **false**, which is the only way this returns false.

So "routing" here is: decide whether the unit still needs a new path, work one out with the most cautious finder, and hand it to the unit.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAirOrder::LoadKey(CAirOrder* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
CAirOrder vftable slot 4, and the image's ordinary LoadKey shape: `this` in ecx, `CParseContext*` at [ebp+8], the four byte SaveToken at [ebp+0xC], every exit `ret 8`.

Three keys of its own. `provinces` (0x1DC) reads the value with `sscanf(parse+0x22C, "%i", &n)`, turns `n` into a CMapProvince* through `g_CCurrentGameState->[0xB8C][n]`, and appends a 16 byte node {province, prev, next, flag} to the list at +0x44/+0x48/+0x4C - so `provinces = N` may be repeated and accumulates. `return_to_base` (0x6DF) is ParseBool into the **base's** +0x18, and `priority` (0x8A) is `sscanf "%i"` into the base's +0x1C; unlike CNavalOrder it does not give those two fields of its own.

Every other key is taken as **a unit type name**: the raw key text at `parse+0x24` is copied into a std::string and looked up with StringHashFind in the database returned by 0x1ADE80, and where that hits, the value is read as `%i` and stored into the int array at +0x34 at that type's index (`type+0x24`). Only a key that is not a unit type either reaches COrder::LoadKey. A failed sscanf calls ReportParseError, so a bad value is reported but the key is not.

The body is slot 4 of CAirOrder and of its thirteen subclasses, which all inherit it.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::IsFitToFly
addresses.comment: COrder slot 25 (+0x64); the base and every naval order return false, and **this one body is shared by all 19 CAirOrder subclasses**. Returns false before `this->+0x28` (`start_date`). addresses.name: CPathFind::Find
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CPathFind::Find(CPathFind* finder, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, CList* path)
addresses.comment:
The A* search itself, and **not a member call**: the finder is the first stack argument, not a receiver. The call site at rva 0x1D8F08 pushes five and adds nothing back (the body does `ret 0x14`), and ECX there holds the unit's own province from CUnit +0x130 - so nothing puts the finder in a register.

What it does: refuses unless unit, from and to are all non-null, then asks the finder's slot 1 (MayUse) whether it may run at all. It allocates three arrays the size of the game state's province vector - a visited byte per province, a 16-byte open-list record per province and a came-from index per province - and loops: take the cheapest open province, ask slot 3 (IsGoal), and for each edge of its template (CProvince +0xD4) ask slot 2 (MayStep) and then slot 0 (StepCost). The heuristic added on top is the straight-line distance between the two templates' +0x2C/+0x30 coordinates, wrapped at the map width in CMap +0x2A74 and scaled by [0x1688618]. On success rva 0x1A11F0 fills `path` with 16-byte nodes holding province **ids** (the CList head is first/last/count/flag, the nodes are data/prev/next/flag).

addresses.name: CCountryTag::FindProvinceRoute
addresses.comment: `this` is a CCountryTag: it starts with CCountryTag::GetCountry(this), gates on 0xEFA50(country, 0), and sizes its work off the province vector (`gamestate +0xB90`). Three callers: 0x4A032F, 0x4BC5C5 (inside 0x4BBB50) and 0x4C3585 (CAIUnit::UpdatePlanAxis). The name is inference from the consumer: UpdatePlanAxis hands it a start province, a target province and an empty CList, and the list it comes back with is posted as the plan's `path` through CSetPlanAxisCommand. The search itself was not read.

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayUse
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayUse(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 1: whether this finder may be used for this unit at all. CPathFind::Find asks it once, before allocating anything, and answers false when it does. `this` is not read - see CPathFind::StepCost for why the convention is still __thiscall - and `ret 0xC` covers the three stack arguments.

False unless the unit's own slot 34 (vftable +0x88) accepts `to`. If the unit's slot 16 (+0x40) then says nothing, true; if it does, the test at rva 0xA7D70 - `to` in ECX, `from` in EAX, `&unit->owner` pushed - has to agree as well.

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayStep(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 2: whether `unit` may step from `from` to `to` along `edge`, with `goal` the search's destination (which the base ignores and both safe finders use). `this` is not read; `ret 0x14` covers the five stack arguments.

Refuses when the edge's kind is 3, when `from` is `to`, when `goal`'s template flag +0x13D is clear, and when the helper at rva 0x1A2600 says a kind-1 edge is blocked - that one reads the province the edge crosses (edge +8) and refuses if its controller is hostile or a foreign unit that is not retreating stands in it. Then the two provinces' templates have to agree: the byte at template **+0x22, unnamed**, may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's **+0xA4, unnamed**, must be the other province's id. What follows is the supply gate: with the destination's controller hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) it refuses a unit whose supply_received_percentage is zero and whose CUnit::SupplyConsumption is positive, and likewise fuel_received_percentage against CUnit::FuelConsumption; and last, the unit owner's relation record for `from`'s controller (country +0xE28 indexed by tag id, byte **+0x4C unnamed**) together with **+0x20** on the record for `to`'s controller refuses the step.

addresses.name: CPathFind::IsGoal
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::IsGoal(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* at)
addresses.comment: CPathFind slot 3, which no class in the family overrides: `sete` on `goal == at`, three stack arguments, `ret 0xC`, and neither `this` nor `unit` read. CPathFind::Find asks it for every province it takes off the open list and builds the path the moment it answers 1 (0x5A13B3-0x5A13B7), which is what the name says. Slot 3 was previously recorded only as "unknown" on the CPathFind vftable entry.

addresses.name: CPathFind::StepCost
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CPathFind::StepCost(CPathFind* this, CFixedPoint* out, CProvinceTemplate* from, int edge, CMap* map, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment:
CPathFind slot 0: the cost of stepping out of `from` along its edge number `edge`. **The name is right and the receiver is in ECX.** The body belongs to CPathFind - vtable.py --holding puts it at slot 0 of CPathFind, CSafePathFind, CVerySafePathFind and CPlannedPathFind, which inherit it, while CSafeNavalPathFind overrides it at 0x1A2E00 - and CPathFind::Find loads ECX with the finder at every one of its four dispatch sites (0x1A12E5, 0x1A1390, 0x1A143A, 0x1A145C). The body never reads ECX because these finders are four-byte objects holding nothing but a vftable pointer; that is a `this` that is not needed, not a missing argument. `ret 0x14` accounts for the five stack arguments exactly.

The cost is `from->edges_begin[edge].distance`, in thousandths. Then, if the country controlling `map->provinces[from->edges_begin[edge].to_province]` is hostile to the unit's owner - the tag test at rva 0x2F1B0 - it is scaled by 1100/1000, or by 2000/1000 when that province's intel byte for the owner (CProvince +0x370, bounds-checked against +0x374) is 2 or more **and** units are standing in it (+0x2C0). The two constants are the floats at 0x160A5F0 (1100.5) and 0x160A5F4 (2000.5), truncated to int. Returns `out` in EAX, MSVC's struct return.

addresses.name: CSafePathFind::MayStep
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CSafePathFind::MayStep(CSafePathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CSafePathFind slot 2. Forwards all five arguments unchanged to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2AFB-0x5A2B00, no ECX set, callee cleans) and refuses on top of it. Allows the step outright when `to` is the goal - the last step into the destination is exempt. Otherwise it weighs the destination: when the unit's slot 16 or 17 answers true it takes rva 0x1D6900 over `to`'s unit list with the unit's owner tag and multiplies by 1000; when neither does it walks that list itself and adds rva 0x1C3120's value for each unit there whose owner is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0), skipping a `REB` owner when the province's owner tag id (CProvince +0x330) is the unit's own. Either way it refuses when that total is greater than the sum of +0x5C over the unit's own list at CUnit +0xB8.

addresses.comment: CVerySafePathFind slot 2, the same shape as CSafePathFind's: forwards all five arguments to CPathFind::MayStep (0x5A2C5B-0x5A2C60), exempts the last step into the goal, and refuses otherwise. It differs in what it does when the unit's slot 16 and slot 17 both say nothing - where the safe one still weighs the units in the destination, this one refuses as soon as the destination's controller is hostile (rva 0x2F1B0) or rva 0xA6010 objects to the province. When either slot does answer it compares rva 0x1D6900 over the destination's unit list (x1000) against the sum of +0x5C over CUnit +0xB8, exactly as the safe one does.

addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPlannedPathFind::MayUse(CPlannedPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* from, CProvince* to)

addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPlannedPathFind::MayStep(CPlannedPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)

It keeps the base's first tests and drops everything after them: refuses a kind-3 edge and `from == to`, applies the same template rule (the byte at template +0x22 may not be set on both, and where it is set on one, that template's +0xA4 must be the other province's id), and asks the unit's slot 16 (+0x40), slot 15 (+0x3C) and slot 34 (+0x88, with `to`). addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::Assign
addresses.comment: Copies a whole definition, the name and the adjusters included. CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies uses it twice: to put the type's template back on the sub unit's own copy before it starts, and to take a copy of each effect it is about to scale.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::Scale
addresses.comment: Multiplies every number on a definition by `factor / 1000`: the 42 stat fields from +0xE8 to +0x190 inline, and each CUnitAdjuster - the four inline ones and both vectors - through CUnitAdjuster::Scale. This is how a technology's effect is scaled by the level a regiment holds, the factor being the level x1000.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::Add
addresses.comment: Adds one definition into another, field by field, the adjusters included. What applies a scaled technology effect to a sub unit's own definition.

addresses.name: AddToughnessTwice
addresses.comment: `mov eax,[ecx+0x120]; add [esi+0x120],eax` - the **second** add of `toughness` in one call of `CSubUnitDefinition::Add`; the first is at 0x1A8044. Verified against the bytes, `8b 81 20 01 00 00 01 86 20 01 00 00` at both. So every brigade contributes twice its `toughness` to its division, and every technology level applies twice to a sub unit's. `+0x104 repair_cost_multiplier` is the one field of the 0xE8..0x194 block the function never touches, which is consistent with the duplicate having displaced it.

addresses.name: AddPrioritySpriteCopyIsDead
addresses.comment: `if (source->priority > destination->priority) { destination->priority = source->priority; destination->sprite = source->sprite; }` - but `priority` (+0x194) was already **added** into the destination 0x142 bytes earlier, at 0x1A8230, so for non-negative priorities the test can never pass. The `std::string::assign` (0x1BD0) it guards is therefore dead, and a synthesised definition keeps the empty `sprite` the null definition gave it. This is also the evidence that **+0x198 is a Hoi3CString, not an int**: it is assigned as a string, and +0x1B4 (`unit_group`) is exactly 0x1C further on.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::Divide
addresses.comment: `v = v * 1000 / divisor` over a **selective** set: only `+0xF0 default_organisation`, `+0xF4 default_morale` and `+0x124 softness` inline, then `CUnitAdjuster::Divide` (0x1D4EB0) over `night` (+0x64), `fort` (+0x7C), `river` (+0x94), `amphibious` (+0xAC) and every element of both adjuster vectors (+0x54/+0x58 and +0xC4/+0xC8). `ret 4`, rva 0x1A83B0..0x1A8531. Exactly the inverse of `CSubUnitDefinition::Scale` (0x1A78B0) but over three scalars rather than forty-two - which is the point: these are the only numbers a division must average rather than sum. Its one caller is CUnit::RebuildDefinition at 0x1B61F4, which passes `regiments.count * 1000`, so the divide is a divide by the number of brigades.

addresses.name: GetSubUnitDefinitionCombatValue
addresses.comment: **What one brigade type is worth to the AI**, out of the definition's own stats, so a mod moves it from `units/*.txt`. Three arms, chosen by two bytes on the definition: `+0x2D` (land) gives `(soft_attack + hard_attack + piercing_attack + (defensiveness + toughness)/10 + armor) * (2000 - softness) / 1000`; `is_air` (+0x2C) gives `air_attack + air_defence + 500`; otherwise (ship) `(500 + sea_attack + sea_defence) * hull / 1000`. The 500 is the global at rva 0x16886AC, a compiled-in `(int)floorf(500.5f)`. The `(2000 - softness)` factor is the one with teeth: an infantry brigade at softness 1.0 scores x1, an armour brigade at 0.2 scores x1.8. Bare `ret`, both arguments in registers, so it is `__fastcall` and not a `__thiscall` (trap 11).

addresses.name: CSubUnitDefinition::ClampMinimums
addresses.comment: Raises `+0xF8 build_cost_ic` and `+0xFC build_cost_manpower` to `g_MinimumBuildCost` (0x1688698, 100 = 0.100) and `+0x100 build_time` to 1000 (1.000 day), and does nothing else - the two loops ahead of it over the adjuster vectors have empty bodies. Bare `ret` at 0x1A883F. **The last thing `CSubUnitDefinition::Add` does**, so it runs once per brigade during a division rebuild and once per technology level during a sub unit rebuild; it is what stops a technology discounting a unit below those floors.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::GetMaxStrength
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CSubUnit::GetMaxStrength(CSubUnit* this, int* out, bool penaltyWhenOwnerAcc, bool penaltyAlways) @EAX
addresses.comment:
Virtual slot 12, `ret 0xC`: `this` in ecx, a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8] and two bool flags at [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10]. The answer is written through the pointer and the pointer comes back in eax, the same shape as CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation next door.

`*out` starts as the definition's `max_strength` (`this->sub_unit_definition_ptr(+0x58)->+0xEC`). Where the subunit's `is_reserve` byte (+0xA4) is clear that value stands. Where it is set, the owner is fetched (0x1ABCF0, subunit -> unit_ptr +0xB0 -> country) and the RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE modifier is applied as `*out = max_strength * (1000 + owner->global_modifier.values->RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE) / 1000` - but only past a gate: `penaltyAlways` ([ebp+0x10]) applies it unconditionally, otherwise owner+0x94 set skips it, otherwise owner+0xACC clear applies it, otherwise `penaltyWhenOwnerAcc` ([ebp+0xC]) decides. Both flags are 0 at the call sites looked at (0x5AC1CD pushes 0 and 0), so the everyday answer is: reserves take the penalty unless the owner's +0x94 says otherwise.

**Which modifier it is, is settled.** `owner->[0xDA8]` is CCountry +0xD90 `global_modifier` plus CModifier +0x18 `values`, so `[edx+0x268]` is entry 0x268/8 = 77 of the values array, and entry 77 is RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE by two independent routes that agree: the live walk of a country's array that named all 143 entries off each entry's CModifierDefinition key, and the global initialiser at rvas 0x56E10..0x59320, whose 77th CModifier is built from the literal MODIFIER_RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE with 77 in edx (reversing/modifierIds.py). What the code does with it agrees with the name: it scales a **reserve** subunit's max strength by (1000 + value)/1000, and nothing else in the function reads it.

Finally `*out` is **floored** at the global at 0x1A8869C - a minimum strength, not a maximum.

**The name is BiceLib's and may sit one class too low**: the body is slot 12 of CSubUnit's own table as well as CRegiment's, CShip's and CWing's, so it is CSubUnit that declares and implements it and the other three inherit. Left as recorded rather than moved, because moving it is a rename and this wave is not one.

addresses.name: CSubUnit_GetMaxStrength_ReservesPenaltyValue
addresses.comment: `mov ecx,[edx+0x268]` - the reserve penalty itself: entry 77 of the owner's global modifier values, RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE, in thousandths. edx came from `mov edx,[eax+0xda8]` one instruction earlier, which is CCountry +0xD90 global_modifier plus CModifier +0x18 values. The next instruction adds 1000 to it, so -500 here halves a reserve subunit's max strength.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall GetMaxOrganisation(int* out@EAX, CSubUnit* subunit@stack:4, int zero@stack:8, int alsoZero@stack:12)
addresses.comment: Answers through a hidden return pointer, ret 0xC, the same shape as slot 12's maximum strength. Walks the HQ chain above the unit - +0x1F4 being the oob level, 4 for a theatre, 3 for an army group, 2 for an army. The name is BiceLib's, from what CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies clamps with it.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::SettleDamage
addresses.comment:
**Spends a subunit's pending damage and clears it.** The receiver is in ESI and the one stack argument is not read. Four callers: CCombatant::ApplyLosses (0x166298) and three in the 0x1C38xx-0x1C3Exx range.

    ebx = min(pending organisation, organisation)   ; 0x1ABAE1, a cmovg
    strength     -= pending strength                ; 0x1ABAE4, unclamped
    organisation -= ebx                             ; 0x1ABAE7, clamped
    pending strength = pending organisation = 0     ; 0x1ABAF7, 0x1ABAFD

**The clamp is the thing worth knowing.** A tick's organisation damage is capped at what the subunit still has, so the total CUnit::TakeDamage accumulated is damage *attempted* and this is damage *dealt* - they differ by a lot in a one-sided fight. A tooltip built on the raw total showed a division with about sixty organisation taking several hundred, which is what sent the watch here.

Found by a hardware write watch on a fighting subunit's +0xAC: 488 writes adding from CUnit::TakeDamage and 49 clearing from here. Nothing static had reached it - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::SetType
addresses.comment: Gives a sub unit its CSubUnitDefinition and builds the `technologies` list from it, one node per entry of the definition's `technologies` vector (+0x44 to +0x48), each at level zero. A regiment therefore keeps the tech state it was raised with while its country's moves on.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies
addresses.comment: **Rebuilds the sub unit's own definition**: puts the type's template back on it, then for every node of `technologies` takes the technology's effect for this unit type, scales a copy of it by the node's level and adds it in. Then totals the levels into `extra_consumption`, and unless `keepStrength` is set clamps `strength` and `organisation` to the maxima that come out of the new definition; either way it raises `strength_ceiling` to the strength. **Read live**: the whole formula holds to the point on all 1068 engineer_brigade regiments in a 1942 game, on the stat fields and the adjusters alike, and what is left over each time is the template.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier
addresses.comment: **The second combat-modifier adder, and the one FINDINGS-combat's scan missed.** `(int id@[ebp+8], int attack@[ebp+0xC], int defence@[ebp+0x10])`, `this` (a CSubUnit) in ESI, `ret 0xC`. Exactly the shape of CUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1C3040) but against the sub unit: it appends a 12-byte {id, attack, defence} record to the CList at CSubUnit+0x40/+0x44/+0x48 and then multiplies max(1000+attack, g_CombatModifierFloor) and max(1000+defence, the same) into two running products on the sub unit. Air, naval and bombing combat add all of their BM_* modifiers through this; only land uses the CUnit one. Nine BM_* ids were recorded as having no call site at all - BM_RADIO, BM_ARMOR_ADVANTAGE, BM_BASE_PROXIMITY, BM_POOR_SCREEN_PENALTY, BM_RADAR_STATION, BM_INTERCEPT, BM_AIRCOMBAT, BM_SURPRISE_PENALTY, BM_SURPRISE_BONUS - and seven of the nine push their id here.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::FiringRange
addresses.comment: `(CSubUnit* su@EAX, int* out@ESI)`, bare `ret`. The sub unit definition's range (definition+0x14C), then, where the sub unit has a parent CUnit (+0xB0), scaled by (1000 + the unit's province's precipitation x FIRINGRANGEMODIFIER/1000)/1000. So rain shortens firing range - -50% at full precipitation with BlackICE's FIRINGRANGEMODIFIER of -0.5. The same maths is inlined in the naval combat code at 0x1672C0.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance
addresses.comment:
The CSubUnitDataBase singleton accessor. Returns the global at 0x1A886F0 when it is non-null; otherwise `operator new(0xC0)` at 0x5ADEA2, then CSubUnitDataBase::CSubUnitDataBase (0x1ADEE0) and CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance (0x1B1BE0), both of which the record already had `confirmed` against that same global. Every offset its callers read is an already-named CSubUnitDataBase field: +0x1C/+0x20 the definition array, +0x2C armor_brigade, +0x34 infantry_brigade, +0xA8 destroyer, and so on through all 33 cached type pointers.

**Renamed 2026-10-01 from `GetConvoyShipDefinitions`**, which was `likely` and came from the one call site anyone had read: ResolveConvoyRaid calls it twice and takes +0xA8 and +0x88. Those are not a convoy-specific pair - they are two of the cached type pointers, which settles that entry's own open question: **+0x88 is `transport_ship`** (the convoy) and **+0xA8 is `destroyer`** (the escort). The correction is load bearing rather than cosmetic: with the right name, the 5.5 KB force-needs half of 0x4B60F0 stops being a wall of `[eax+0xNN]` and reads as a list of unit types by name, which is what made it readable at all. See reversing/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::CSubUnitDataBase
addresses.comment: Zeroes the container at +0x00, sets the hash map at +0x10 to 0x1FF empty buckets (allocating and memset-ing 0x1FF*4 bytes into +0x18), zeroes the CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> at +0x1C and the container at +0xB0, and returns the object. It does NOT touch +0x28..+0xAC, the cached role definitions, which the loader fills later. Writes no vftable, so the class is not polymorphic.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::~CSubUnitDataBase
addresses.comment: Walks the CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> at +0x1C ((+0x20 - +0x1C)/4 entries) and tears the database down. Called by CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance before it frees the old database, and by the array-owning helper at rva 0x1B1C30.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::LoadDefinitions
addresses.comment: **One call takes two files.** Called once, at 0x637A7B, as `call CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance; mov edx,[ebp-0x1c]; push edx; push esi; push eax` - eax the database, esi the `common/unit_upgrades.txt` context (slot [ebp-0x510], tokenizer at 0x637A32), edx the `common/combined_arms.txt` context (slot [ebp-0x644], tokenizer at 0x6379A5). Extent 0x5AE1C0..0x5B0699, `ret 0xC`, the only three-argument loader in the stage. Builds CNullSubUnitDefinition (0x5AF016) and logs `CSubUnitDataBase  Initialized` (two spaces, as the engine spells it) at eu3application.cpp:1069 - which is the moment technology phase 2 becomes possible.

addresses.name: NullSubUnitDefinitionConstruction
addresses.comment: `push 0x15B4E98` (the string `---`, rva 0x11B4E98) ahead of the `CSubUnitDefinition` constructor call at 0x1AEFFD, after which 0x1AF016 overwrites the vftable with `CNullSubUnitDefinition`'s (rva 0x11C7A44, which RTTI names). **This is the object `CUnit::RebuildDefinition`'s reset copies**: the database's index-0 null, keyed `---`, every number zero.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase_RoleByKey
addresses.no_signature: a single instruction inside a larger function, not a function entry, so it has no calling convention of its own

Each step compares the definition's key against one hardcoded literal - the contiguous block 0x15C7750..0x15C794C, infantry_brigade through carrier - and on a match stores the definition pointer into one fixed slot of CSubUnitDataBase between +0x2C and +0xAC. addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase::BuildHistoricalModels
addresses.comment: Called once, at 0x6385C8, on CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance' result, right after the `country database <` timer and before `Historical Models Initialized` (eu3application.cpp:1144). Extent 0x5B0870..0x5B1B95, `ret 4`. **This is where the 255 MB of historical models comes from** - census.py measured 5,323,320 objects at 48 bytes, being 108 country tags x 1,643 unit types x HISTORICAL_MODEL_MAX (30). It needs both the sub-unit definitions and the country database, which is why it sits after both.

addresses.name: CTrait::AddEffect

addresses.name: CTrait::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrait::LoadKey(CTrait* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole grammar of `common/traits.txt`**, and the only thing that reads it: `allowed_leader = { land sea air }` sets the three flags at `+0x2B0` (all three when the key is absent), and 31 effect keys each add one entry through AddEffect. The three terrain ones read `type` then `value`, in that order, which the loader insists on. Anything else is logged against `traits.cpp` with the key's own text.

**Checked against the mod**: all 33 distinct keys across the 341 traits in BlackICE's `traits.txt` are ones this knows. `gainable_traits.txt` is a different class - CGainableTrait, whose keys (`trait`, `combat`, `trigger`, `hours_required`) none of this would take.
