addresses.name: LoadTraits
addresses.comment: Reads `common/traits.txt`, resolved-path slot [ebp-0x5d4], called once at 0x637F43 on CTrait::database (0x5B4640, already in the record). Extent 0x5B46B0..0x5B4EA5 with earlier exits at 0x5B4DFD (`ret 8`) and 0x5B4E9A (`ret 4`) - trap 3 territory. One `Traits Modifiers Initialized` line at eu3application.cpp:1105 covers this and gainable_traits.txt together.

addresses.name: ReturnThis
addresses.comment: `mov eax, ecx; ret`. **A compiler fold in 20 vftable slots across unrelated families** - CArmy slot 9, CNavy slot 12, CAir slots 13 and 14, CAddAttackerChange/CAddDefenderChange/CAddWarGoalChange/CAllianceChange slot 9 and more - so by trap 4 it is recorded class-free. 7 direct callers. It is what every `unit->slot9()` in the AI bodies resolves to for a CArmy, so those expressions are simply the unit itself; the same goes for CollectUnitsMovingIntoProvince pushing `unit->slot9()`.

addresses.name: CUnit::ConstructPlanInPlace
addresses.comment: `lea eax, [edi + 0x1FC]; call CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan` inside CUnit's constructor (`0x1B5010`). **This is what settles that `CUnit +0x1FC` is a CUnitPlan held by value and not a pointer**: nothing is allocated, the plan is built in place at that offset, and the very next store is `expeditionary_owner` at `+0x28C`. The matching destruction is at `0x1B5799`.

addresses.name: CUnitCtorAllocatesDefinition
addresses.comment: `push 0x228` ahead of `operator new` in `CUnit::CUnit` (0x1B5010): **this is where the definition a unit owns comes from**, 0x228 bytes, constructed at 0x1B5396 with the key string `---` (rva 0x11B4E98) and type index 0, and stored into `+0xC8` at 0x1B539F. Nothing else in the image writes `CUnit +0xC8`. The `---` key is what makes the reset in `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` find the `CNullSubUnitDefinition` the database keeps at index 0.

addresses.name: CUnit::~CUnit
addresses.no_signature: A destructor's own shape - it writes the vftable at +0 and +8 and takes no argument beyond its receiver - but which of the three unit classes Ghidra should attach it to has not been checked, and a wrong `this` type reads every field at the wrong offset.
addresses.comment: **CUnit's destructor**: writes CUnit::vftable into +0 and +8, releases the orders and plans, calls CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers to free the combat modifier list, then walks the regiments. Reached while looking for what *builds* that list, which it is not.

addresses.name: CUnit::RebuildDefinition
addresses.comment: **Rebuilds the definition a unit owns at +0xC8 out of its brigades**, 0x36C bytes, rva 0x1B5ED0..0x1B623C, `ret 8`. Order: (1) make `g_CSubUnitDataBase` (0x16886F0) if it is missing - the `operator new(0xC0)` at 0x1B5F02 is that database, not the definition; (2) zero `CUnit +0x1D0`'s presence vector; (3) **reset** - look the unit definition's own key up in the database's by-name hash (`StringHashFind`, 0x5C7D60) and `CSubUnitDefinition::Assign` the hit over it. CUnit's constructor gives that key the string `---`, which the database holds as the `CNullSubUnitDefinition` at index 0, so the reset is a copy of an all-zero definition; (4) per brigade: `CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies(brigade, keepStrength)` to rebuild *its* definition first, then either `CSubUnitDefinition::Add` (0x1A7FC0) of all 59 fields or, on the reduced path, `+0x124 softness` alone; then overwrite `+0x108 maximum_speed` and `+0x148 range` with the running **minimum** and `+0x12C armor_value` and `+0x13C ap_attack` with the running **maximum**; accumulate `+0x188`; mark the brigade's `unit_group`; (5) after the loop set `CUnit +0x1CC base_ca_bonus`, set `+0x188 amphibious_invasion_speed` to the **average** over the brigades that declare a non-zero one, and `CSubUnitDefinition::Divide` the whole definition by the brigade count (`CUnit +0x40`), which averages `default_organisation`, `default_morale`, `softness` and every adjuster. The second argument is forwarded to ApplyTechnologies and used nowhere else. Eight callers: 0x102BC0, `CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute` (0x11CE60), `CUnit::AfterLoad` (0x1B80D0, the only one that passes true), `CUnit::UpdateHourly` (0x1B9C50), `AddRegimentToUnit` (0x1BE640), `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (0x1BE9A0), 0x1CDC90 and 0x362780.

addresses.name: RebuildDefinitionReset
addresses.comment: `call CSubUnitDefinition::Assign` with the unit's definition in esi and the hash hit in eax - **the only thing that clears the unit's definition before the brigades are summed into it again**, and it is conditional on `StringHashFind(g_CSubUnitDataBase + 0x10, definition->key)` answering non-null at 0x1B5F49. The key is always `---`, which the database holds, so it fires; if the database were ever present without its null entry the sums would compound on every rebuild.

addresses.name: RebuildDefinitionIsLandCall
addresses.comment: `call eax` on `[CUnit vftable + 0x3C]`, **slot 15 = IsLand**: rva 0x192360 (`xor al,al`) on CUnit, CNavy and CAir, rva 0x692590 (`mov al,1`) on CArmy alone - and slots 16 and 17 are the matching IsNaval and IsAir. It opens the reduced path, so **only a land division can have a brigade that stops contributing**; a ship or an air wing always contributes all 59 fields.

addresses.name: RebuildDefinitionReducedPath
addresses.comment: `softness += brigade->definition->softness` and nothing else - the whole of what a brigade contributes when it is on the reduced path. Reached when the unit is land, the brigade's own `combat_width` (+0xE8) is `<= 0`, and either its `strength` is below `g_IneffectiveStrength` (0.100) or its `organisation` is below `g_IneffectiveOrganisation` (1.000). Because `softness` is divided by the brigade count afterwards, a knocked-out support brigade is still in the denominator of `default_organisation`, `default_morale`, `softness` and every adjuster while contributing nothing to the first two - so it drags them down by (N-1)/N.

addresses.name: RebuildDefinitionDivideByBrigades
addresses.comment: `call CSubUnitDefinition::Divide` with the unit's definition in edi and `regiments.count * 1000` (CUnit +0x40) in a stack slot - **what turns the summed organisation, morale, softness and adjusters into averages**. Skipped where the count is zero.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetCombinedArmsBonus
addresses.comment:
**The whole of BM_COMBINED_ARMS (0x12)**, called from CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers at 0x16A574 and only when this->+0x1CC is above zero.

    base   = this->base_ca_bonus (+0x1CC)
    ts     = resolve(this->+0x290 ? +0x28C : +0x124)->CTechnologyStatus (+0xDF8)
    groups = sum of ts->+0x5C[g] for every group index g set in this->+0x1D0..+0x1D4
    *out   = GetTraitEffect(this, 9 combined_arms_bonus) + groups + base

+0x1CC and the group bitmap at +0x1D0 are both built by the definition rebuild at 0x1B5ED0: for every group present with its CCombinedArmsGroup's +0x24 byte set, +0x1CC accumulates that group's +0x28.
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CUnit::GetCombinedArmsBonus(CUnit* this, int* out, int unused)

addresses.name: CUnit::CommandReachFrom
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CommandReachFrom(CUnit* unit, int* out, CUnit* hq)
addresses.comment: How much of one HQ's command reaches a unit, in thousandths: 1000 at the HQ's own province, falling with the square of the distance to it (province +0x2C and +0x30, wrapped by CMap + 0x2A74) against a radius from the HQ's first regiment's definition +0x180 scaled by the RADIO_*_LEADER_DISTANCE define for the HQ's oob_level, and 0 out of range or where either unit is off the map. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CUnit::CommandReach
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CommandReach(CUnit* unit@EAX, int* out@stack:4, int hqLevel@stack:8)
addresses.comment: The same compounded over every HQ from the unit up to the given oob_level: 1000 when the unit is itself at that level, and each step multiplies by that HQ's reach. Unit in eax, ret 8. What the consumption functions scale the army group leader's skill by. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CUnit::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::LoadKey(CUnit* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of what an order of battle block accepts** - a `division`, `corps`, `army`, `navy`, `air` or `theatre` - 40 keys in one switch of 4658 bytes. Seven open a child unit (`theatre`, `armygroup`, `army`, `corps`, `division`, `navy`, `air`), three say what the unit is made of (`regiment`, `ship`, `wing`, all reaching CSubUnit::LoadKey), four are identity (`id`, `name`, `location`, `leader`) and the rest is state a save carries: `path`, `track`, `previous`, `movement_progress`, `retreat`, `possible_retreat`, `disengage`, `arrow_state`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `was_paradropped`, `supplies`, `fuel`, `dig_in`, `attack_delay`, `combat_hours`, `can_upgrade`, `can_reinforce`, `is_reserve`, `is_prioritized`, `plan`, `expeditionary_owner`, `expeditionary_date`, `aggression_enabled`, `aggression_setting`, `country_intel`. The loader cannot tell an OOB file from a save - it is the same switch - so every one of them is legal in `history/units`.

**The keyword does not pick the class, the parent does**: CNavy::LoadKey and CAir::LoadKey take the five child-unit keywords back and send all five to one handler that still builds a CArmy. Reached from RTTI, not from the first vftable: CArmy keeps CPersistent at object offset 8, so slot 4 of its primary table is a per-unit update and not this.

addresses.name: CUnit::AfterLoad
addresses.comment: **CPersistent slot 5, and where a unit's id comes from.** If the block carried an id (either half of the pair at +8 non-zero) it keeps it and then pushes the global generator at 0x170AF78 past it, so a later runtime id cannot collide with it. If it carried none, it takes `counter++` and stamps id type **0x29 (41)**. That is why an OOB file need not carry ids at all, and why units from one that does not - the mod's flying_dutchman files - come out as type 41. It goes on to fix up the rest of what the block lacked. See reversing/FINDINGS-oob.md.

addresses.name: UnitAttachmentLimit_EarlyExit
addresses.comment: Early exit of the attachment limit function taken when no attached unit was counted.

addresses.name: Hook_UnitAttachmentLimit
addresses.comment: The compare against the attachment limit when a unit is attached to a higher unit (cmp [ebp+0x8], edi); ebx is the unit to attach, ecx the last counted attached unit. Hooked.

addresses.name: CUnit::UpdateHourly
addresses.comment: **The per-unit leaf of `ProcessUnitFunctor`**: its `operator()` (`0x0068EBF0`) ends in `ecx = units[i]; call 0x005B9C50`, and one direct caller only. Since FINDINGS-tick.md establishes that functor is fanned out to TBB worker threads every hour, **this runs off the main thread** and nothing hooked here may touch Lua or the ImGui frame. Does movement, per-regiment organisation regain, an owner test against the literal "REB", and the retreat flag; it does **not** read `CUnit + 0xB0` and never dispatches CUnit slot 31 or slot 32.

addresses.name: UpdateHourlyEffectivenessTest
addresses.comment: In `CUnit::UpdateHourly`, for a land unit only (slot 15 at 0x1BA27C): for every brigade whose definition's `combat_width` is zero, recompute `strength >= g_IneffectiveStrength && organisation >= g_IneffectiveOrganisation`, cache it in `CSubUnit +0xD4`, and **if any brigade's answer changed, call `CUnit::RebuildDefinition(unit, false)`** at 0x1BA2D6. This is the only clock on the rebuild: nothing refreshes a division's stats hourly as a matter of course, only when a support brigade crosses one of those two thresholds. Note it tests `combat_width != 0` where RebuildDefinition tests `<= 0`, so the two disagree on a negative combat_width.

addresses.name: CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat
addresses.comment: CUnit slot 31, shared by CUnit/CArmy/CAir (CNavy overrides with rva 0x1CFDD0). **The only simulation driver of `COrder` slot 14 found**: at VA `0x005BA356` it calls `order->slot14()` and, when that returns false, replaces the order with a fresh `CNullOrder` through `CUnit::SetOrder`. Then, for an air unit whose order's slot 24 is false, it talks to the unit's base at `+0x98`. Also calls `CCombatManager::CheckForCombat` twice (VA `0x005BA82B`, `0x005BAC1B`). **How often it runs is not established** - it is not called by `CUnit::UpdateHourly` nor by `CUnit::UpdateDaily`, so whether it is on a worker thread is unknown.

addresses.name: CUnit::UpdateDaily
addresses.comment:
**`CUnit`'s virtual slot 32, the per-unit update.** `CArmy` and `CNavy` share it; `CAir` overrides it with `0x1D0B60`, and nothing else derives from `CUnit`.

It ages the timed entries at `this + 0x2A8`, asks the order two questions, digs in and rotates troops (land only), and then tidies three vectors.

**The name claims a period, and that part is inference.** What the code shows is the work: troop rotation here divides a thousandth-scaled annual rate by 365000 and applies it once a call, and dig-in advances by exactly one level a call. Both only make sense once a day. The caller would settle it and was not found - the slot is reached through a virtual table, and `+0x80` is 150 call sites in 119 functions, none of the three that also walk units being this one. So `Update` rather than `Daily` is the part to rely on.

addresses.name: UpdateDailyLandOnly
addresses.comment: `if (!this->IsLand()) ...` - slot 15, and **the whole of the gate on troop rotation**. All three unit classes arrive here: a navy shares this function, and `CAir::UpdateDaily` ends by calling it. So rotation is an army's alone, and so is the manpower it costs.

addresses.name: DigInRequiresWar
addresses.comment:
`if (!owner->isAtWar) goto 0x1BB146` - and `0x1BB146` is **the rotation code**, not the end of it.

**This test belongs to digging in, not to rotation**, which is the trap in this function: the name `peacetime_manpower_rotation` invites the opposite reading. The flow graph settles it - `0x1BB146` has seven incoming edges, six of them branches taken to skip the dig-in block - and the decompiler agrees, putting the whole of that block in one nested `if` whose body is `dig_in_level += 1000`.

addresses.name: PeacetimeManpowerRotationRead
addresses.comment:
**The only read of `peacetime_manpower_rotation` in the executable.** Checked by pairing all 153 fetches of a country's modifier array with a read of entry 50 within the next 0x200 bytes.

It is scaled up at `0x1BB184` where the unit is under-supplied, by `PEACETIME_MANPOWER_ROTATION_LOW_SUPPLY_FACTOR`, and then divided by 365000 per subunit - a thousandth-scaled annual rate applied daily.

addresses.name: RotationStrengthStored
addresses.comment:
Where rotation writes the reduced strength back. **The drain worked out above is clamped to nothing below zero and to the maximum above it**, so what actually went is `[edi + 0x5C]` before this instruction less `ebx` after it - which is where BiceLib stands, rather than on the figure the arithmetic produced.

`edi` is the subunit and `esi` is still the unit. The `jns` two instructions above lands on the first byte of this, so a jump written here is still what that branch arrives at.

addresses.name: DailyTickEndGate
addresses.comment: `cmp byte ptr [gamestate + 0xDA4], 0` - the gate on the last block of `CUnit::UpdateDaily`, which is attrition and, for a fleet, the transport overload check.\n\n**What the byte means is not known, and it matters.** It is zeroed when the game state is constructed, and `ApplyAttrition` has **exactly one caller** - the call this gates. So if nothing ever sets this byte, that attrition function never runs at all. Nothing that sets it was found, but the search is not conclusive: `+0xDA4` is a common displacement and the global is loaded in thousands of places, so the scan cannot be made clean. **It is settled in a game rather than here** - watch whether BiceLib's `$ATTRITION$` ever leaves zero. Sizing `CCurrentGameState` to its real `0xDA8` is what makes it read as `+0xDA4` at all - the structure used to end at `0xD9E`, so this came out as an index past the end of it.

addresses.name: CUnit::SupplyConsumption
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall SupplyConsumption(CUnit* unit, int* out, bool withoutLeaders)
addresses.comment: Unit supply consumption in thousandths, written through out and returned in eax; ret 0xC.

addresses.name: CUnit::FuelConsumption
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall FuelConsumption(CUnit* unit@EAX, int* out@stack:4, bool withoutLeaders@stack:8)
addresses.comment: Unit fuel consumption in thousandths, written through out and answered in eax; unit in eax, ret 8. A land unit on a strategic redeployment (order slot 16 answering 0x5A4) gives 0. Otherwise a potency of 1000 plus the country's SUPPLY_CONSUMPTION modifier, less the army group leader's skill x 50 scaled by how far that HQ's command reaches, plus the chain of command's own effect of type 2; then per regiment (potency + regiment[+0xCC] x 10) x the definition's fuel_consumption / 1000. Unlike supply it does not scale by the regiments' strength.

addresses.name: CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel
addresses.comment: The daily supply and fuel draw for one unit. Asks CUnit::SupplyConsumption (0x1BB560) and CUnit::FuelConsumption (0x1BB7A0) what the unit wants, takes what it can get, and writes CUnit::supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and CUnit::fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) as taken*1000/wanted (1000 when fully supplied, -1 when nothing was wanted, 0 when nothing was available). The country it bills is the expeditionary_owner (+0x28C) where CUnit +0x290 is set, the owner (+0x124) otherwise, through CCountryTag::GetCountry (0x2610). Two paths, chosen on g_CCurrentGameState +0xC9C: >0 draws straight out of CCountry::GetPool(country) (0xF4DE0 - pool_in_exile at +0x9F8 when use_own_pool, the capital province's pool at +0x15C otherwise), the inline copy of that function appearing four times; <=0 walks the supply network - the unit's supply source province, its supply_depot_id (+0x48) into g_CMap +0x2200, and draws that province's pool.supplies (+0x164) and pool.fuel (+0x168) pro rata against the province's need.supplies (+0x24C) and need.fuel (+0x250). Where the depot is controlled by another country a lend-lease conversion runs: the amount is scaled by a rate built from CDefines +0xCC and the receiving country's CGoodsPool at +0x7DC is credited, the supplier's at +0x86C, and both countries' pools are moved. Fuel is only taken when the unit is moving (movement_order_remaining_provinces_count > 0) or is naval and 0x1CDC30 says no; a land or air unit standing still burns none. The last act, for the player's own units only, is to set the byte at +0x1BC on both objects hanging off CUnit +0x164 (+0x13C and +0x140) when either received percentage has fallen below Define50 - the out-of-supply marker on the counter.

addresses.name: CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall UpdatePlanForceNeeds(CUnit* unit, void* difference, void* groupDifference, void* needed, void* wanted)
addresses.comment: Recomputes, per subunit type, what this unit's order of battle is short of against its plan. The three vector<int> arguments are always &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C and &unit->+0x7C at both call sites; all three are indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index and sized to the subunit definition database's count ((db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4), grown and zero-filled on the first call and, on later calls, with the second and third zeroed at 0x1BD40C while the first is overwritten wholesale. It then walks up higher_oob_unit_ptr to the top of the OOB and, unless that top unit has plan+0x8 (CUnit +0x204) set with oob_level 0, calls ComputePlanWantedSubUnits (0x4E1D00) to build the wanted composition out of the unit's plan (CUnit +0x1FC) and the owner's available subunit types; with the fifth argument null it fills the plan's own buffers at plan+0x18/+0x70/+0x80/+0x84, with it non-null it fills locals instead. The wanted list is the local one where 0x4E1D00 produced one and unit->+0x26C (which is plan+0x70) otherwise. CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType (0x1BD7E0) then counts what the unit actually has, and: difference[i] = wanted[i] - have[i]; groupDifference[GenericType(i)] += difference[i] for every non-zero entry, where GenericType is 0x1ADF70 folding a subunit type onto a representative one; then, over a copy of groupDifference, needed[i] = min(difference[i], groupNet) for each positive deficit, drawing that group's remaining net down as it goes - so a surplus of one type inside a group cancels a deficit of another. Returns true if any entry of needed was set. Runs once a day from CUnit::UpdateDaily for units at oob_level 0 and for HQs at level 1..3 whose +0x198 is set; the level 1..3 units with +0x198 clear have the three vectors cleared instead, and level >=4 is skipped entirely.

addresses.name: UpdatePlanForceNeeds_SkipWhenTopPlanActive
addresses.comment: `if (top->plan_active (CUnit +0x204) && top->oob_level (+0x1F4) == 0) skip to 0x1BD4CB` - the gate that decides whether ComputePlanWantedSubUnits runs at all. **This is what lets the two AI force planners' output survive.** CSetPlanForcesCommand::Execute calls CUnitPlan::SetMinForces and then CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds, which re-enters UpdatePlanForceNeeds; without this gate the recompute at 0x1BD498 would immediately overwrite the vector the command just installed.

addresses.name: UpdatePlanForceNeeds_FillPlanBuffers
addresses.comment: The `wanted == 0` arm: it calls ComputePlanWantedSubUnits with the plan's own buffers, pushing &plan+0x84, &plan+0x80 and &plan+0x70 and zeroing the first two first. plan+0x70 is CUnit +0x26C (plan_subunit_wanted) and plan+0x80/+0x84 are CUnit +0x27C/+0x280 (our_power/their_power). **So ComputePlanWantedSubUnits is a third writer of our_power and their_power**, which corrects FINDINGS-power.md's claim that CSetPlanAttributesCommand's two real call sites are the complete set outside the savegame loader.

addresses.name: CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds
addresses.comment: The out-of-line copy of the gate CUnit::UpdateDaily inlines at 0x1BB273. On a unit with oob_level >= 4 it does nothing; with oob_level 0, or with +0x198 set, it calls CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds(unit, &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C, &unit->+0x7C, 0); otherwise it clears all three vectors. Called from CSetPlanForcesCommand slot 6 (twice) and CSetPlanAttributesCommand slot 6.

addresses.name: CUnit_CountSubUnitsByTypeIndex
addresses.comment: 0x1BD740-0x1BD7D7 (`ret 4`), 52 instructions, read end to end, 12 callers. Lazily builds the CSubUnitDataBase singleton (0x1A886F0), memsets (definitions_end - definitions_begin) ints at the ESI array, then walks unit->+0x38 doing `counts[subunit->+0x58->type_index]++`. Both AI bodies _alloca the array first (0x4CDA79, 0x4CE698) and then index it with the cached role type_indices, which is how a wing's or a fleet's composition is tested.

addresses.name: CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType(CUnit* this, void* counts, int reserved)
addresses.comment: Counts this unit's subunits by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index into a vector<int>, recursing through the OOB. Where the vector is empty it is first grown to the subunit definition database's count and zero-filled; then counts[regiment->sub_unit_definition_ptr->type_index]++ over CUnit::regiments (+0x38), then the same call on every entry of CUnit::children (+0x1E4). The second argument is pushed as 0 at both call sites and never read.

addresses.name: CUnit::CollectSubtree
addresses.comment: 0x1BDA90 to the `ret 4` at 0x1BDAF4 - 101 bytes, read end to end. Appends `this` to the CList it is handed (a fresh 0x10-byte node: payload, prev at +4, next at +8, byte at +0xC; head/tail/count written at list +0/+4/+8) and then recurses into every child on CUnit +0x1E4, so the list comes back holding the unit and every unit below it in the OOB. Called by CUnit::MeanDistanceToProvince (0x4C1FC0).

addresses.name: CUnit::CountDivisions
addresses.comment: `ret 0x10`, 5 callers, recursive. Counts this unit and everything under it whose `oob_level` (CUnit +0x1F4) is **>= 4** - i.e. divisions and below - skipping a non-land unit when the first argument is set. Every call site in the image passes (1, 0, 0, 1) and the recursion passes the first argument down unchanged; the other three are never read. This is the strength figure CAIUnit slot 76 divides a front's length by.
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CUnit::CountDivisions(CUnit* this, bool landOnly, int unused1, int unused2, int unused3)

addresses.name: CUnit::GetRegimentList
addresses.comment: Six instructions: `return unit ? &unit->regiments (+0x38) : nullptr`. Bare ret, no stack arguments, `this` in EAX. Used by ShouldStartNavalCombat to get the inner loop's list.

addresses.name: AddRegimentToUnit
addresses.comment: The counterpart of `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (0x1BE9A0), which abuts its `ret 4` at 0x1BE995: it pushes the regiment onto the unit's `regiments` list (+0x38), writes the regiment's `unit_ptr` (+0xB0) at 0x1BE6CD, renames the unit after its first brigade's type key where `[unit+0x1F8] >= 3` and there is a brigade, and ends by calling `CUnit::RebuildDefinition(unit, false)` at 0x1BE937. The unit arrives in **edi** and is never loaded from the frame.

addresses.name: RemoveRegimentFromUnit
addresses.comment: **Takes a regiment out of its unit.** It walks the unit's `regiments` for the node holding this one and unlinks it, then sets the regiment's `unit_ptr` (`+0xB0`) to zero - which is what says so rather than any guess. The caller deletes the regiment afterwards.\n\n**No signature recorded**: the compiler passed the unit in `edi` and the regiment on the stack.

addresses.name: CUnit::EnterProvince
addresses.comment: Puts a unit into a province: it writes `current_province_ptr` (`+0x130`) at `0x1BF4D3`.\n\n**Only that much was read.** The function is over 2.5KB and does a great deal besides - it reads the province's path node in half a dozen places - so the name is what it is *for* at the one call site traced here, not a full account of it. The convention is read off that call site: `ecx` is the unit and the province is pushed.

addresses.name: CUnit::CanEngage
addresses.comment: **`this` is in EDI**, `ret 0xC`. The filter `CCombatManager::StartCombat` applies to each unit standing in the province before it will build a combat. At VA `0x005C0341`/`0x005C0357` and `0x005C0377`/`0x005C038B` it calls `order->slot34()` and then `order->slot25()` on **each side in turn**, so an air-to-air combat needs both orders to be `air_intercept`/`air_superiority` (or carrier protection) and both wings to pass `CAirOrder::IsFitToFly`.
addresses.signature: char __stdcall CUnit::CanEngage(CUnit* this@EDI, CUnit* other, int flag, CMapProvince* province)

addresses.name: CUnit::CanMoveTo
addresses.comment:
**Whether this unit may enter that province**, virtual slot 35.

Among its tests: a land unit whose strength fraction is below CUnit::ShatterThreshold **may not enter an enemy controlled province at all**. CPathFind::MayStep applies the same test, and the interface shows it as `UTM_MAY_SHATTER` and `UTM_NOT_LEGAL_RETREAT`.

So the shatter threshold does two jobs: below it a unit shatters when hurt, and below it a unit cannot push into enemy ground.

addresses.name: CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers
addresses.comment:
**Empties a unit's combat modifiers and puts the four multipliers back to neutral.** Frees every node of the CList at +0xDC, zeroes its three fields, and writes 1000 into +0xEC, +0xF0, +0xF4 and +0xF8 - which is what settles that all four are multipliers rather than two values and two multipliers.

Two callers: CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590), which clears before it rebuilds, and CUnit::~CUnit (0x1B5560). Found with a hardware write watchpoint on a live unit - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp - after a byte search for stores to +0xDC had turned it up and a range filter had thrown it away for sitting in CUnit's code rather than the combatant's.

addresses.name: CUnit::AddCombatModifier
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit::AddCombatModifier(CUnit* unit@ESI, CombatModifier id@stack:4, int attack@stack:8, int defend@stack:12)
addresses.comment:
**Adds one modifier to a unit's list and folds it into the running product.** `ret 0xC` for the three stack arguments; the unit arrives in **ESI** and is never loaded from the frame, which is why a byte search for stores to +0xDC through a named pointer never found this.

It allocates twice: a 12 byte record holding the id at +0, the attack delta at +4 and the defend delta at +8 - which is what the battle tooltip reads and prints as `x%/y%` when the two differ - and a 16 byte CListNode for it. Then `last = node`, `++count`, and `first = node` only when the count was zero, which is why watching +0xDC caught resets and no additions: the head is written on the empty-list branch alone.

**Then it multiplies.** `unit->+0xEC = unit->+0xEC * max(attack + 1000, floor) / 1000` and the same for the defend side into +0xF0, with `floor` read from the global at 0x1A8873C (zero in the image, so presumably set at load). So a modifier's value is a **delta** - +22.5% is 225 - turned into a factor by the `add eax, 0x3e8`, and the two fields hold the running product of everything on the list. That is what the tooltip prints as its Attack and Defend Modifier, and why CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds both with 1000.

Found with a hardware write watchpoint on a live unit's +0xE4, the list's count - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp. Nothing static had reached it.

addresses.name: CUnit::ShatterThreshold
addresses.comment:
**How weak a unit has to get before it shatters**, in per mille of full strength:

    t  = min(1000 - 500 * national / 1000, 500)     // national = CCountry +0xD4
    t -= leader->skill * 10                          // CLeader +0x70
    t -= unitStat * 3 / 1000                         // CUnit virtual slot 22

With no national modifier the base is 50%, and each point of leader skill takes a percentage point off it.

**The 500, 3 and 10 are baked into the executable**, not defines.lua - see g_ShatterBase, g_ShatterStatWeight and g_ShatterSkillWeight, each filled by a static initialiser of the shape `_ftol2_sse(floorf(500.5))`. The only levers a mod has are the leader's skill and the national value, and that value has not been identified.

Both arguments arrive in registers and the result is the pointer it was handed back in eax; the body ends in a bare `ret`.

**It dereferences `leader_ptr` (+0x12C) with no null check.**

addresses.name: CUnit::SettleCombatDamage
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::SettleCombatDamage(CUnit* this, int* strengthLost, int arg)
addresses.comment:
**Where a combat tick's damage lands on a unit, and where shattering is decided.**

Walks the regiments through CSubUnit::SettleDamage, totalling the strength lost into the out parameter, then adds the casualty trickleback and charges the owner's officer pool. After that:

    strength = sum(regiment->strength)
    fraction = strength * 1000 / GetTotalStrengthCeiling()
    if (fraction < CUnit::ShatterThreshold(unit))
        CCountry::ShatterUnit(owner, unit)

**Nothing here looks at where the unit is** - not the province, not its controller, not whether anything has it surrounded. Shattering is a strength check and only that, which is why a surrounded unit is not reliably destroyed: it shatters here, before ever reaching the retreat that would have removed it.

The third argument is untouched on the paths read.

addresses.name: AddCasualtyTrickleback
addresses.comment:
**What comes back to the manpower pool from casualties.** The only reader of the `casualty_trickleback` modifier in the executable, at `0x1C3FB6`.

    manpower = casualties x build_cost_manpower / max_strength
             x (trickleback + a technology bonus) / 100000

The first half is the same pricing the reinforcement pass uses, so a casualty is valued at what replacing it costs, and the modifier decides how much of that returns. It credits the **expeditionary owner** where there is one (`+0x28C`) and the owner otherwise.

**No signature recorded**: the compiler gave it a register convention, taking the unit in `eax` and the casualties on the stack, so it cannot be written as an ordinary function - the same reason `CCountry::IsEnemy`'s second overload has none.

addresses.name: TricklebackCredited
addresses.comment: `country->Manpower += trickled back`, floored at zero by the two instructions after it, and the one write in the whole function. `esi` is the country and `eax` the manpower, **already in the units the tooltip prints** - nothing to price here, unlike attrition and rotation.\n\n**BiceLib stands here** to total what comes back per country.

addresses.name: GrantCombatExperience
addresses.comment: The only source of leader experience in the build. Builds one value from the enemy side's size (0x1D6710/0x1D6670), scales it by the double 328.18 at 0x120A7B8 (0.01 in 48.15), clamps it to 6, divides by 3 and adds a 1..6 die, then multiplies by EXP_GAIN_LAND/NAVAL/AIR (vslot 15/16/17 pick), by 1 + the leader's xp_gain trait effect, by EXP_GAIN_CONVOY_MODIFIER when convoyRaid, and by 0.01 a second time. Then EXP_GAIN_DIV x 1000 goes to every regiment (+0x3C, capped at 100000) and EXP_GAIN_LEADER goes to the unit's leader and to every HQ leader above it, divided at each level by that HQ's child count clamped to 2..5. Called from 0x1BA555 (in combat) and 0x1D243C (convoy, flag 1).

addresses.name: CUnit::FindRetreatProvince
addresses.comment:
**Where a unit falls back to**, or null when there is nowhere - which is what has CUnit::RetreatFromCombat remove it from the game instead.

Walks the provinces adjacent to the unit's own, over the path node's edge array (stride 0x14), and keeps the **best scoring** one. A candidate has to be passable and to pass the unit's virtual slot 13; its score is then built from *its* own neighbours:

- one under the unit owner's control, or passing the test at `0x0EFA00`, adds **1000**;
- one under nobody's enemy control adds **500** (g_RetreatNeutralNeighbourScore);
- **an enemy controlled neighbour halves the total** rather than adding to it.

The province is only taken if it scores above a floor, and the highest score wins. **Nothing qualifying means null**, and the unit is destroyed.

Rebels come first and separately: an owner tag of `REB` takes a path of its own which returns null outright unless `0x286C10` finds them somewhere with a flag at `+0x30`'s `+0x198` set.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetTotalStrengthCeiling
addresses.comment: Virtual slot 24: adds up the regiments' +0x30 ceilings, without dividing. The name is BiceLib's, and what the game shows this as has not been established.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetAverageOrganisation
addresses.comment: Virtual slot 20, shared by CUnit, CArmy, CNavy and CAir: adds up the regiments' organisation (CRegiment +0x60) and divides by the regiment count. Answers a CFixedPoint through a hidden return pointer. The name is BiceLib's - the game does not register this one to Lua.

addresses.name: CUnit::GetAverageStrength
addresses.comment: Virtual slot 21, the same shape as slot 20 over the regiments' strength (CRegiment +0x5C). Answers a CFixedPoint through a hidden return pointer. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: GetUnitAverageStrengthAndOrganisation
addresses.comment: For each regiment, `strength / GetMaxStrength` and `organisation / CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation`, each as a 0..1 fraction summed into the out parameter and then divided by `CUnit::regiments_count` - so both outputs are averages over the brigades. Adds nothing when a maximum is zero (it contributes -1). Eight callers; the two that matter here are CAIUnit slot 78 at 0x4B27DA and 0x4B2B97, where the strength average is compared against the commitment factor the power ratio chooses.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall GetUnitAverageStrengthAndOrganisation(CUnit* unit, float* strengthOut, float* organisationOut)

addresses.name: CUnit::GetPower
addresses.comment: **Slot 27 of CUnit, CArmy, CNavy and CAir - the one body in all four, which is inheritance and not folding (trap 4).** `*out = 0`, then for each CSubUnit on `this->+0x38`: `*out += (strength/100) * typeValue / 1000 * (organisation/100) / 1000`, where `typeValue` is 0x1A8690 of the regiment's **technology-applied** definition (CSubUnit +0x58). Nothing else enters: no terrain, no leader, no supply, no air or naval support, and no modifier array. A unit above the division level contributes nothing, because only a division holds regiments, so summing over a whole OOB subtree does not double count.

addresses.name: ApplyAttrition
addresses.comment:
**What attrition takes off a unit, once a day.** `CUnit::UpdateDaily` calls it.

Per subunit: the province's own `attrition` modifier, scaled by a global and by the subunit's maximum strength, over 30000 - a monthly rate applied daily. The strength lost is totalled into the second argument, which is also what it answers.

Two gates, both at the top and both the same ones rotation has: `combats.count` must be below 1, and the unit must answer `IsLand`. So attrition here is an army standing still out of combat, and neither fleets nor air commands take it.

addresses.name: AttritionStrengthStored
addresses.comment:
Where attrition writes the reduced strength back - **the same shape as rotation's store at `0x1BB25D`**, down to the clamp above it and the ceiling raised after, because both are a subunit losing strength.

`esi` is the subunit and `edi` what its strength is about to become, so what actually went is `[esi + 0x5C]` before this instruction less `edi` after. **The unit is not in a register**: `edi` held it at the top of the function and has been reused, so it comes off the frame at `[ebp + 8]`.

**BiceLib stands here** to price the loss in manpower and total it per country.

addresses.name: CMapProvince::CanUnitReach
addresses.comment:
0x1C7710 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x1C7961, three exits (0x1C78D7, 0x1C793E `xor al,al`, 0x1C7961 `mov al,1`). 18 direct callers, thirteen of them in CAIUnit's code. **The receiver is the province and the unit is the first stack argument** - 0x1C7733 reads `[arg1+0x130]`, which is CUnit::current_province_ptr, and compares it with ECX.

Head and tail read; the middle is not. It answers **true immediately when the unit is already in the province**, false when the unit is retreating (CUnit +0x158), when CUnit +0x40 (brigade count) is below 1, when the unit's slot 35 refuses the province, and in several other arms; and it ends by constructing a CPathFind in its own argument slot - one of two vftables, 0x15C884C or 0x15BE414, chosen by `arg2` - and calling CPathFind::Find(finder, unit, unit->current_province, this, &path), answering true when a route exists. So: 'can this unit actually get to this province'. The name is inference from that shape; the two bool arguments are not understood.
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CMapProvince::CanUnitReach(CMapProvince* this, CUnit* unit, bool altPathCostModel, bool arg3)

addresses.name: BuildSpeedModifierTooltip
addresses.comment: **A unit's movement speed broken into its nine causes**, one line each: SPEED_MODIFIER (the total), _COMBAT, _FUEL, _TERRAIN, _TRAIT, _ADJACIENCY (the game's spelling), _WEATHER, _LOCAL_MOD, _MOTORIZED_BONUS, _RETREATING, every one with $PERC$. Extent 0x5C82A0..0x5C8CEB, `ret 8`, one caller 0x75CE5E. It calls 0x5C8D10 once at 0x5C82D4 - its immediate neighbour - passing both the value of [ebp+8] and **its address**, then re-reads [ebp+8] afterwards, so that argument is written through. **Which of the two stack arguments is the out record and which the unit is not established**; one of them is a GuiTooltipText (+0x58 written at 0x5C85B5). Nothing the simulation stores, so for BiceLib this is read-rather-than-recompute. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.name: CUnit::MovementSpeedModifier
addresses.comment:
Builds a unit's movement speed multiplier in thousandths through an out pointer: `(CUnit* u@[ebp+8], int* out@[ebp+0xC])`. Starts at 1000 and multiplies in, in order: a combat term where the unit is in a battle it is attacking; the owner's MODIFIER_COMBAT_MOVEMENT_SPEED (entry 63) with the leader/HQ effect of type 5, capped at 1000 and floored at Define10; a fuel term; the terrain's `movement` adjuster for the next province out of the definition's terrain vector (+0x54); the unit's own type/order term (0x1D0F80 with effect 0x1C); and, where the unit is land (slot 15), **(1000 + CWeather::MovementEffect(next province's weather, owner) + the province's MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED)/1000** at 0x1C900A-0x1C9028; then a river/strait term. Named for what it produces; the non-weather terms were read once each and are summarised rather than confirmed.

**Its one caller, added 2026-10-02** (reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md): `BuildSpeedModifierTooltip` (rva 0x1C82A0) calls it at 0x5C82D4 as the first thing it does, passing both the value of its own first argument **and the address of it**, then re-reading that slot - so this writes through. A proposed rename to `ComputeSpeedModifierTerms` was declined: that name was a guess from the call position by an agent that had not read the body, and this entry's own account of the formula is the better-founded one.

addresses.name: MovementWeatherTerm
addresses.comment: `call CWeather::MovementEffect` in CUnit::MovementSpeedModifier, guarded on the unit being land (slot 15). Its answer is added to 1000 and to the province's MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED and the whole thing multiplies the speed; then a tail term built from how many of the unit's regiments have the byte at definition+0x35 set.

addresses.name: WantsToDisengage
addresses.comment: `limit = 5 * (1000 + *CUnit::GetTraitEffect(unit, &tmp, 0xC)) / 1000; return unit->disengage (+0xA8) >= limit`. Trait effect 0xC is `disengage_timer` (CTrait::Effect entry 12), so with no trait the limit is 5. `this` in ESI, bare ret, no stack arguments. Called from CNavalCombat::Tick's disengage loop; a true answer ends the whole combat.

addresses.name: SetUnitPath
addresses.comment: Gives a found route to a unit: (unit, path, 1). Gives a route to a unit (same function as RVA 0x1C9AC0).

addresses.name: CUnit::StrengthDamageFactor
addresses.comment: **How hard a unit hits for the men it still has.** Totals its subunits' strength, divides by GetMaxStrength (slot 23), and returns roughly that percentage over a hundred - floored at 1, so even a shattered division still throws something - times the global at rva 0x1A8874C. Added to the combat's doctrine figure by CLandCombatant::FireUnit to scale a landed shot.

addresses.name: CUnit::RollToHit
addresses.comment:
**Whether one shot lands, and it spends the target's defence.** `defence` is thousandths; its whole part is how many shots the target can still defend against this tick and the remainder is a chance at one more.

    if (slots <= target->defences_used)  avoid = CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF
    else { avoid = BASE_CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT
           if (target->IsLand()) avoid += the owner's TechnologyStatus +0x8
           ++target->defences_used }
    avoid = min(avoid, 99000)
    return avoid / 1000 <= rand() % 100

**So a unit does not dodge by chance alone - it runs out.** Once `defences_used` reaches what its defence value bought, every further shot that tick is judged by the much worse no-defence figure, which is what makes being outnumbered compound.

addresses.name: CUnit::TakeDamage
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit::TakeDamage(CUnit* unit@EAX, int strength@stack:4, int organisation@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
**Spreads one landed shot over every subunit of the unit hit.** The unit is in EAX. Strength damage is shared in proportion to each subunit's own maximum - `share = subunit.GetMaxStrength * 1000 / unit.GetMaxStrength` - while organisation damage is split evenly, one part per subunit.

Nothing is subtracted here. It accumulates into CSubUnit +0xA8, which CCombatant::ApplyLosses spends against `strength` at the end of the tick, and into +0xAC, **whose consumer has not been found** - see that field. That is what lets CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight tell a unit already killed this tick from one still worth shooting at, before any of it has been applied.

addresses.name: CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight
addresses.comment: **True when every subunit is already dead on this tick's arithmetic**, which is what stops a unit being shot at twice over. For each subunit it takes `strength - pending_strength_damage` - or `strength - global(0x1A8868C) * pending / 1000` where the subunit answers either of slots 9 or 11 - and returns 0 the moment one of them is still above zero. The unit is in EAX.

addresses.name: CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand
addresses.comment: **The gate on BM_LEADER_BONUS**, called at 0x16AA22 and inlined in the naval, air and target slot 19s. `this` in EAX, no stack arguments, a jump table on `this->oob_level (+0x1F4)` over 0..7 that compares the leader's **rank** - CLeader +0x6C, not skill at +0x70 - against a per-level threshold: 3 at the top two levels, 2 at the next, 1 below that, with one arm deferring to 0x1CD920. A leader of insufficient rank for the unit's place in the order of battle contributes **no** BM_LEADER_BONUS at all, in any kind of combat. The name is ours and reads the thresholds rather than any string.

addresses.name: CUnit::SetOrder
addresses.comment: **`this` is in EAX**, the new order on the stack, `ret 4`, 14 call sites. Parks a fresh `CreateOrder(0x18D, 0)` in `this->+0xB0`, deletes the old order through its slot 0 with the delete flag, deletes that temporary `CNullOrder` too, then installs the real order. So `CUnit + 0xB0` is briefly a throwaway `CNullOrder` in the middle of this function - a hook that reads the order here can see it.

addresses.name: CUnit_IsAtOwnBase
addresses.comment: 0x1CDC30-0x1CDC88, bare `ret`, 28 instructions, read end to end, 58 callers. False when unit->+0x98 (the home-base object) is null or when its slot 0 - the province - is not unit->current_province_ptr (+0x130). Then, only when the base's slot 1 answers true, false again if the object at base->+0x18 -> +0xB0 has +0x11C > 0 or +0x110 non-zero. The name rests on the first two clauses; the third clause's object is not identified. Both AI bodies use it as the 'this unit is sitting at home doing nothing' test before giving it a mission, and in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits it is also the reason a tired wing is left alone (0x4CE016).

addresses.name: COrder::IsTargetInRange
addresses.comment: **`this` is in EAX**, `ret 8`, 12 call sites. Short-circuits to true for the three rebase orders - GetTypeId `0x574` `rebase_air`, `0x573` `rebase_to_carrier`, `0x6DE` `rebase` - and for any unit with no base at `+0x98`; otherwise takes the range from `unit->+0xC8->+0x148` (the CSubUnitDefinition) and the origin from the base province, and compares. `CAirInterceptOrder` slot 14 calls it with the unit's *current* province and, on failure, orders a return to base and clears `CAirOrder + 0x68`.
addresses.signature: char __stdcall COrder::IsTargetInRange(COrder* this@EAX, CUnit* unit, int provinceId)

addresses.name: CArmy::ClassifyRole
addresses.comment: 0x5CE8A0-0x5CEC31, bare `ret`, `this` in ecx. **CArmy virtual slot 41, and the writer of `CArmy +0x2FC`.** CUnit's slot 41 is `_purecall` (0xB961D5) and CAir's and CNavy's are the folded empty stub 0xABF890, so only an army has a role. It writes **ten** distinct values; the full enum is 0..9 and the order of the tests is the order below. First it sets 9, then returns at once with 9 if `this->+0x40` (brigade count) is zero. Otherwise it walks the brigade list at `+0x38` (the `PAVCSubUnit::__CList` base RTTI puts at offset 56) and for each brigade reads its `CSubUnitDefinition` at `CSubUnit +0x58`, taking the definition's `type_index (+0x24)` and comparing it against the cached definitions on g_CSubUnitDataBase: `+0x78 hq_brigade` sets role **0** and returns immediately; `+0x4C police_brigade`, `+0x50 garrison_brigade`, `+0x54 militia_brigade` count towards role **5**; `+0x40 bergsjaeger_brigade` towards **6**; `+0x44 marine_brigade` towards **7**; `+0x48 paratrooper_brigade` towards **8**. It also accumulates `softness (+0x124)`, `max_speed (+0x108)` and the number of brigades whose `combat_width (+0xE8)` is under 1000. After the loop: average softness below g_FixedPoint0_500 gives role **3** and wins over 5/6/7/8; then 5, 6, 7, 8 in that order; then, only if nothing matched, average max_speed at or above 6000 gives **4**, at least half the brigades having combat_width under 1.000 gives **1**, and the fall-through is **2**. Reading the stock `units/` folder, combat_width 0 is exactly the support brigades, 1 the infantry family and 2 the armour family, so role 1 is a mostly-support formation and role 3, by softness, is armour. Dispatched virtually only; `AddRegimentToUnit` (0x5BE96A) and `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (0x5BED3F) both call slot 41 on the unit, so the role is recomputed whenever the order of battle changes. The name is from the body.

addresses.name: CArmy::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CArmy::LoadKey(CArmy* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 3 of them, one case each: `parent`, `staging_province`, `target`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CNavy::CNavy
addresses.comment: Calls the CUnit base constructor (0x1B5010), writes CNavy's two vftables (0x15C869C at +0, 0x15C8750 at +8), then initialises **CNavy's own fields**: +0x2E4/+0x2E8/+0x2EC a CList (the `carrying` list), byte +0x2F0 (`at_sea`), float +0x2F4, int +0x2F8 (the combat cooldown), and oob_level (+0x1F4) = 5. So CNavy is 0x2FC bytes and everything from +0x2E4 up belongs to CNavy, not CUnit - project.json currently records `carrying` on CUnit. Returns this in eax. It is the only writer of CNavy's vftable in the image.

addresses.name: ProvinceSeaHopCheck_OwnerIdTest
addresses.comment: `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x330], 0` - **not a field of its own**: +0x330 is the `id` half of the CCountryTag at CProvince +0x32C, so this is `province->owner.id != 0`, the province is owned by somebody. CCountryDataBase::GetTag hands back `---` with id 0 where there is none. It is the second of four tests in this gate: the path node's +0x22 byte at 0x1CEE9A, this one, `+0x354` (the CPort*) at 0x1CEEAD and `naval_base->level_max(+0x20) > 0` at 0x1CEEBC.

addresses.name: RemoveFromTransport
addresses.comment: Takes a unit off whatever is carrying it: it writes `CUnit::carrying` (`+0x2E4`) at `0x1CF19F`, which is the fleet's list of passengers.\n\nCalled by `CheckTransportOverload` together with `CUnit::EnterProvince`, which is the pair that puts a unit ashore. Only the one write was read; the rest of the function was not.

addresses.name: CountShipsByRole
addresses.comment: Zeroes five ints at `out` and walks unit->regiments (+0x38), classifying each ship by its CSubUnitDefinition (CSubUnit +0x58) in this exclusive order: def->is_capital (+0x2F) -> out[4] (+0x10); def->is_transport (+0x30) -> out[1] (+0x04); def->is_sub (+0x31) -> out[0] (+0x00); def->carrier_size (+0x190) > 0 -> out[3] (+0x0C); otherwise -> out[2] (+0x08), the screens. Bare ret, 0x60 bytes. Its only caller is ShouldStartNavalCombat, which uses out[0] against out[2] for the submarine gate and out[3]+out[4] for the patrol gate. The name is ours; nothing in the image names it.

addresses.name: CNavy::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavy::LoadKey(CNavy* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: What a `navy` block adds over CUnit::LoadKey: `at_sea` and `base`. It also takes `army`, `theatre`, `armygroup`, `corps` and `division` back off the base and sends all five to one handler of its own, which still builds a CArmy (new 0x308, ctor 0x4828C0) and then sets it up differently - embarked land units is a guess, not traced. The four land keywords reach one body through a range test - `cmp eax, 0x465 / jl default / cmp eax, 0x468 / jg default` and fall through - which switchmap.py did not read until 2026-09-28, so this was recorded with four keys and not eight. See reversing/FINDINGS-oob.md.

addresses.name: CheckTransportOverload
addresses.comment:
**Whether a fleet is carrying more than it can.** The last thing `CUnit::UpdateDaily` does, for naval units only - it downcasts through slot 11 and calls this.\n\n    carried = sum of transport_weight over fleet->carrying\n    if (carried > fleet->definition->transport_capacity / 1000) ...\n\nBoth halves are read off `CSubUnitDefinition`: `weight` at `+0x10C`, which the unit files call `transport_weight`, and `transport_capacity` at `+0x144`.\n\n**It throws cargo overboard until the load fits**, re-measuring each time round:

    do
        for each unit in fleet->carrying
            if (its province's info byte +0x22 is set)
                RemoveFromTransport(...); unit->EnterProvince(province)
            else
                RemoveRegimentFromUnit(its first regiment); delete it
                if that was its last, post {unit->type, unit->id} to the game
                    state's message ring at +0xBF8
    while (carried weight > capacity)

So a unit that **can** be put ashore is put ashore, and one that cannot is taken apart a regiment at a time. Which is which turns on a byte of the province's info object at `+0x22` - 246 places in the image read it, so it is something fundamental, but nothing here says which way round it means land.

addresses.name: CNavy::CheckOrderAndCombat
addresses.comment:
`CNavy`'s slot 31 override: 0x34 bytes, and no `ret` of its own. It decrements the countdown at `CNavy +0x2F8` when positive, calls `0x5C7C70(this)` when the fleet has combats (`+0x11C > 0`) or `+0x110` is set, and then **tail-jumps to `CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat`** (`jmp 0x5BA2F0` at `0x5CFDFF`). That tail jump is why the navy path needs no separate call site.

Slot 31 holds `CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat` in `CUnit`, `CArmy` and `CAir` (vftables `0x15C85CC`, `0x15BDE0C`, `0x15C8774`) and this override in `CNavy` (`0x15C869C`), and nowhere else in any of the image's 2707 vftables - read out of the image at each vftable address, since the RTTI export records only slot counts.

addresses.name: CAir::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAir::LoadKey(CAir* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: What an `air` block adds over CUnit::LoadKey: `base`. Like CNavy::LoadKey it takes the five child-unit keywords back off the base and sends them to one handler of its own, which builds a CArmy. The four land keywords reach one body through a range test - `cmp eax, 0x465 / jl default / cmp eax, 0x468 / jg default` and fall through - which switchmap.py did not read until 2026-09-28, so this was recorded with four keys and not eight. See reversing/FINDINGS-oob.md.

addresses.name: CAir::UpdateDaily
addresses.comment:
`CAir`'s own slot 32. **It does not replace `CUnit::UpdateDaily` - it ends by calling it**, on every path, after its own air-specific work.

So an air unit does reach the troop rotation code, and what stops it there is the `IsLand` test at the top, the same thing that stops a navy. That test is the single gate; no class avoids rotation by not running the function.

The period in the name is inferred, the same way and on the same evidence as `CUnit::UpdateDaily`.

addresses.name: CAir::CanMoveTo
addresses.comment: **The one place weather gates air.** CAir's override of CUnit::CanMoveTo (vftable slot 35, CAir's vftable VA 0x15C8774 slot at 0x15C8800): `bool CanMoveTo(CProvince* p)`, `this` in ECX untouched, `ret 4`. It answers false outright when the province's cloud_coverage (p+0x8C) is at or above ALLOWEDTOFLYTHRESHOLD, and otherwise tail-calls CUnit::CanMoveTo (0x1C2BA0). CArmy and CNavy inherit the base and have no weather test. This is why CAirOrder::IsFitToFly reads no weather: the gate is on the move, not on the wing.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit
addresses.comment: Copies a whole plan onto a unit's own plan at CUnit +0x1FC. In order: CUnitPlan::SetActive(dest, source->active), `unit->plan_stance(+0x208) = source->stance`, then CopyOpsArea, CopyObjectives, CopyPath, CopyPath2 and SetMinForces from the source's +0x18, +0x38, +0x48, +0x5C and +0x70, then our_power and their_power into CUnit +0x27C/+0x280. **What it does not copy is as informative as what it does**: the fallback line (+0x28), embark and debark (+0x88/+0x8C) and the three unnamed fields (+0x58, +0x6C, +0x7C) are all left as the reset left them. Both call sites are CUnitPlanCommand's slot 6, which is how a plan drawn in the interface reaches the unit.

addresses.name: CUnit::CommandEffect
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CommandEffect(CUnit* this, int* out, int effectType)
addresses.comment:
Adds up one kind of effect reaching a unit from its chain of command: recurses up higher_oob_unit_ptr (+0x1E0), scales each superior's contribution by CommandReachFrom (the radio proximity factor, 0x1B67B0) and halves it, and adds the values of the unit's own leader's traits whose type matches effectType - walking the traits at +0x30, matching effect_kinds at +0xA8 and reading effect_values at +0x68, with the count at +0x2A8. Everything is in thousandths, and it returns `out` in eax.

**This is how a trait reaches a combat or a unit, and it does not go through the CModifier base's value array** - so a trait effect will not be found by looking at modifier ids. Type 2 is what the supply and fuel functions ask for; kind 0 is xp_gain, asked for at 0x1C457E. **63 call sites.**

Also read, independently, as CUnit::GetTraitEffect (kept as an alias): both readings agreed on the body, and differ only in whether the name should say where the numbers come from or how far they travel. The name is BiceLib's either way. See reversing/FINDINGS-leaders.md.

addresses.name: CUnit_AllSubUnitsAreCag
addresses.comment: 0x1D1220-0x1D1243, 15 instructions, read end to end, 10 callers. Returns false if any subunit's definition (CSubUnit +0x58) has +0x32 clear, otherwise `unit->regiments_count (+0x40) > 0`. The name is inferred from its use as the gate on issuing the carrier_protection order in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CDF89) plus the position of +0x32 in CSubUnitDefinition's bool run, and it stands or falls with the CSubUnitDefinition +0x32 = is_cag entry. If +0x32 turns out to be something else this name is wrong; the honest fallback is a name that says only 'every subunit has definition flag +0x32'.

addresses.name: ResolveConvoyRaid
addresses.comment:
**The convoy raid, end to end.** One body from 0x5D1250 with an early `ret 4` at 0x5D201C and the success path continuing at 0x5D201F in the same frame (trap 3). Three callers, all in the order code: 0x1998EF (CAirConvoyRaid), 0x19C66B and 0x1A02CD (CConvoyRaid).

**1. The raider's attack.** Over the raider's regiments (+0x38), with def = CSubUnit->+0x58:

    a = raider->IsNaval() ? def->convoy_attack (+0x164) : def->sea_attack (+0x168)
    attack += a * strength(+0x5C)/1000 * 0.01 * organisation(+0x60)/1000 * 0.01
    detect  = max over the regiments of def->surface_detection (+0x150)

The two 0.01 factors are `x * 1000 / 100000`, so the term is really attack x (strength/100) x (org/100). **A naval raider uses `convoy_attack`; an air raider uses `sea_attack`** - the air mission reads the surface-combat stat, not the convoy one.

**2. Target selection**, over every convoy in the raider's own sea zone (raider->current_province (+0x130)->convoys (+0x38..+0x3C)): skip our own; if CDiplomacyStatus->war (+0x20) is null the pair must involve "REB" or pass 0x763A0 on the status's +0x24; skip a convoy with no transports; then `if (Random() % 50 < detect/1000)` consider it, preferring one whose CConvoy::GetDefence is at or below our attack and otherwise keeping the first seen. So **the raider's `surface_detection` is the per-convoy find chance, out of 50**.

**3. The test.** An **air** raid multiplies the attack by 5.0 (the literal 0x1388) before comparing. If GetDefence(target) > attack the raid fails with CONVOY_TOO_STRONG and the victim's statistics series at CCountry +0x1184 takes -(STRAT_CONVOY_DAMAGE / victim->convoys_count (+0xA8)) / 10.

**4. The sinking.** It builds a throwaway CNavy (CNavy::CNavy 0x1CEE20, byte +0x48 set) filled with CShip regiments of the `convoy` and `escort` subunit definitions from the singleton at 0x1ADE80 (+0x88 and +0xA8), in counts scaled by `max(path_count * 0.2, 1.0)` so a long route exposes fewer ships per raid, fights it, rounds the two loss counts and calls CConvoy::LoseShips (0xC5940).

**5.** It writes `raider->current_province->last_convoy_attack (+0x1C) = gameState->tick` at 0x1D286D.

It never touches CNavy::carrying (+0x2E4): a convoy is a record with two integer ship counts, not cargo on a real fleet.

addresses.name: WriteLastConvoyAttack
addresses.comment:
`mov dword ptr [eax + 0x1c], ecx` with eax = raider->current_province (+0x130) loaded at 0x1D2861 and ecx = gameState->tick (+0xBDC) loaded at 0x1D2867 - **the writer of CMapProvince +0x1C `last_convoy_attack`**, which nothing had found. It sits on the success path of ResolveConvoyRaid, after the ships are sunk, so the field marks a sea zone where a raid actually landed, not one where a raid was attempted. Its only reader is ShouldStartNavalCombat, which scales the spotting value by NAVAL_INTERCEPTION_AFTER_ATTACK_FACTOR while the attack is one day old or less.

Searched the whole of .text for `mov [reg+0x1c], reg32` (1290 sites) and kept the ones with a `+0xBDC` read in the preceding 24 bytes: 13 sites, of which this is the only one in the simulation; the rest are in diplomacy and interface code writing their own objects' +0x1C. Stores through other encodings (an immediate, or a date held in a register for longer) were not excluded.

addresses.name: CArmy::GetAttackValue
addresses.comment: **CUnit slot 39 for a land unit.** Returns -1 where `[this+0x1F8] < 7`; otherwise `(hard_attack + soft_attack)` out of the unit's own definition (+0xC8 then +0x138 and +0x134), x1000 and divided. Both fields are plain sums over the brigades, so the figure scales with division size. CNavy's override (0x1D2BA0) uses `sea_attack` (+0x168) and CAir's (0x1D2CE0) `air_attack` (+0x140); CUnit's own slot is the pure-virtual stub at rva 0x7961D5. What `[this+0x1F8]` holds is **not** established.

addresses.name: CArmy::GetDefenceValue
addresses.comment: **CUnit slot 40 for a land unit**, the same shape as slot 39: -1 below the `[this+0x1F8] >= 7` gate, otherwise `(toughness + defensiveness)` off the unit's own definition (+0x120 and +0x11C), both plain sums - and `toughness` is the field `CSubUnitDefinition::Add` counts twice. CNavy's override (0x1D2C40) uses `sea_defence` (+0x160) and CAir's (0x1D2D80) `air_defence` (+0x128).

addresses.name: CList_RemoveNode
addresses.comment: `ret 4`, 86 bytes, read end to end, 215 callers. Returns false for a null node. When the list's byte at +0xC is set it only marks the node (node->+0xC = 1) and returns, which is how an iteration-safe erase is done here; otherwise it unlinks through +4/+8, fixes head (+0) and tail (+4) and decrements the count. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits calls it at 0x4D7914 and 0x4D7943 to take a unit back out of the attacker list when adding it did not improve the odds.

addresses.name: CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey(CUnitAdjuster* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
CUnitAdjuster vftable slot 4, the ordinary LoadKey shape: `this` in ecx (kept in esi), `CParseContext*` at [ebp+8], SaveToken at [ebp+0xC], every exit `ret 8`.

Four keys, and **all four go through TokenToFixedPoint on `parse+0x228`**, so every number on an adjuster is the engine's thousandths fixed point - `0.5` in a mod file is stored as 500, not truncated to 0: `attack` (0x174) into +0x8, `defence` (0x45E) into +0xC, `movement` (0x45F) into +0x10, `attrition` (0x2DC) into +0x14.

There is no base call. An unrecognised key is reported inline, with the log record built from the literals `unitadjuster.cpp`, `unknown key '` and `' in file `, so a misspelt terrain adjuster key is a log line and nothing else. Its SaveContents is an empty `ret 4`, so an adjuster is read out of the mod's files and never written back.

addresses.name: CUnitAdjuster::Scale
addresses.comment: Multiplies an adjuster's attack, defence, movement and attrition by `factor / 1000`. Four muldivs and nothing else, which is what confirms those four are all a CUnitAdjuster holds.

addresses.name: CUnitAdjuster::Divide
addresses.comment: Four muldivs, `v = v * 1000 / divisor`, over the adjuster's attack (+0x8), defence (+0xC), movement (+0x10) and attrition (+0x14). `ret 4` at 0x1D4F3A. Byte for byte `CUnitAdjuster::Scale` (0x1D4E20) with the multiplier and the divisor swapped, and it abuts it with no padding. Only `CSubUnitDefinition::Divide` calls it.

addresses.name: NavalStackingPositionPenalty
addresses.comment: hull = sum over the list of unit->CSubUnitDefinitionPtr (+0xC8)->hull (+0x178); p = max(0, hull - NAVAL_STACK_POS_HULL_LIMIT (military +0x1DC)); p = p * NAVAL_STACK_POS_PENALTY_HULL_MULT (military +0x1E0) / 1000; p = min(p, NAVAL_STACK_POS_PENALTY_MAX (military +0x268)). `ret 4`, `out` in ESI, returns out in eax. Note it sums one `hull` per UNIT in the combatant's list, not per ship - worth a live check. These three are the only mod-facing defines in the whole naval positioning calculation.

addresses.name: CountLandUnitsInList
addresses.comment: Body 0x5D5C60-0x5D5C89, bare ret, receiver in ECX. Walks the CList from *list, next at +8, calls each member's [vft+0x3C] - CUnit slot 15, which project.json's vftable_slots records as IsLand - and counts the trues. One direct caller, CProvince::HasHostileLandNeighbour (0x4A5793), which hands it &neighbour->units (CProvince +0x2B8). 0x5D5C90 is a separate function with the same shape.

addresses.name: SumTransportWeight
addresses.comment: Adds up `CSubUnitDefinition::weight / 1000` over a `CList<CUnit*>`, which is what a fleet's load is measured in.\n\n**No signature recorded**: the compiler passed the list in `eax` - the caller does `add eax, 0x2E4` on the fleet and calls straight in - so it cannot be written as an ordinary function.

addresses.name: EnemyLandStrengthIn
addresses.comment: How much enemy land strength stands in a province: over the province's Units list (CProvince +0x2B8), skipping naval and air units (slots 16 and 17), keeping those whose owner CCountry::IsEnemy answers for, and adding up each regiment's strength (CRegiment +0x5C); the total comes back over a thousand. Takes the list in eax and the asking country's tag on the stack, and cleans it itself. CUnit's vtable slot 19 uses it.

addresses.name: CountEnemyLandUnitsInList
addresses.comment: Body from 0x5D6880, ret 8, the list in EAX and the tag's two halves on the stack; answers 0 for an empty list. Per member it skips a unit whose [vft+0x40] (slot 16, IsNaval) or [vft+0x44] (slot 17, IsAir) answers true, then counts it when CCountry::IsEnemy(GetCountry(&unit->owner)@ESI, &tag@EDX, unit->current_province@EDI) holds - so the count is of **enemy land units**, taken from the tag's point of view. 8 direct callers; CEU3AI::PickNearestInvadableNeighbourProvince multiplies the answer by 34.0 and CAIInvasion stage 2 only tests it for zero. Distinct from SumTransportWeight, which project.json has at rva 0x1D6690.

addresses.name: EnemyAirStrengthIn
addresses.comment: The same count over the air units in a province instead (slot 17 kept rather than skipped). CAir's vtable slot 19 uses it.

addresses.name: CPromoteLeaderCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6. Resolves the leader from the id pair at +0x40/+0x44 into +0x3c, then rank (+0x6C) += or -= the delta at +0x68 depending on the direction byte at +0x64 (0 adds). That write at 0x1D7CDC is BiceLib's Hook_LeaderRankChange site. addresses.name: CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand_default
addresses.comment: CMoveCommand constructor that leaves every field zero. **The object arrives on the stack, not in ecx**: `mov esi,[ebp+8]` at 0x1D870D is the only thing it takes, ecx is never read, and it gives the object back in eax and does `ret 4`. Writes CCommand's table (0x15B4F74) first and CMoveCommand's own (0x15C8C1C) at 0x1D8770, sets the type id 0x18D at +4 and 0x255 at +0x2C/+0x30, empties the strings at +8 and +0x48, and zeroes +0x64..+0x6A.

addresses.comment: CMoveCommand constructor, `ret 0x14`. The object is the **first stack argument** (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`), returned in eax; the four values go to +0x64 (target province), +0x68 (mode68), +0x69 (safe) and +0x6A (very safe). **The unit arrives in edi**, unset anywhere in the body: it is pushed with `lea edx,[esi+0x3C]` into 0x42DD70, which builds the command's object reference from it, and then `[edi+0x130]`'s +0xD0 - the unit's current province - is stored at +0x6C.

addresses.name: CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand_copy
addresses.comment: CMoveCommand copy body, `ret 4`. **The receiver is the source, not the destination**: ecx is the command being copied (`mov edi,ecx`, then every read is [edi+...]) and the new object is the stack argument (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`, every write is [esi+...], and it is returned in eax). addresses.name: CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand
addresses.signature: CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand* __stdcall CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand(CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand* self, void* unit, void* provinces)
addresses.comment:
**Not slot 6, and in no virtual table**: this is `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand`'s constructor, and the reason it looked like the third `RefreshPlanForceNeeds` caller is that `image.functionStart` attributes `0x1E629D` to it - there is no `int3` padding between its `ret 0xC` at `0x1E617D` and the real owner, `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::Execute`, at `0x1E6180`.

It inlines the `CCommand` base constructor rather than calling it - `CCommand`'s vftable at `0x15B4F74` goes in first and is overwritten with its own at `0x15C931C` - then fills `+0x2C`/`+0x30` with 0x70A, the tickstamp word at `+0x34` with 0xFFFF, the identity at `+0x38` with 0, builds the `unit` reference at `+0x3C` out of its second argument and copies the province list into `+0x64`. `this` arrives on the stack rather than in ecx and the object comes back in eax; the five callers all `operator new(0x78)` first, which is the class's size.

addresses.name: CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand::Execute
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`), and the third and last body in the image that reaches `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds`.

One province list at `+0x64` and one flag at `+0x74` decide which of the plan's two province lists it replaces:

    if (this->fallback_line)   CUnitPlan::SetFallbackLine(plan, &this->provinces)   // plan +0x28, returns here
    else                       CUnitPlan::SetOpsArea(plan, &this->provinces)        // plan +0x18
                               CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds(unit)
                               if (unit->owner == the local player's country
                                   && this->unit_ref matches the local session)
                                       gamestate->+0xBE8 slot 32(...)               // 0x1E649F

So a fallback line costs nothing - it is a line, not an area to hold - while an operations area changes what the plan needs and refreshes it. The tail is the only part of the three plan commands that touches the GUI, and it is gated on the unit belonging to the player at this client.

addresses.name: CSetPlanAttributesCommand::CSetPlanAttributesCommand
addresses.signature: CSetPlanAttributesCommand* __stdcall CSetPlanAttributesCommand::CSetPlanAttributesCommand(CSetPlanAttributesCommand* this, CUnit* unit, int stance, int airStance, int navalStance, int ourPower, int theirPower)
addresses.comment:
`ret 0x1C`, returns `this` in EAX, 7 call sites. Writes the save token 0x707 (`set_plan_attributes_command`) into +0x2C and +0x30, 0xFFFF into +0x34, takes the unit reference through 0x2DD70 into +0x3C, sets the byte +0x64 to 1 (`active`), and stores the five remaining arguments into +0x68, +0x6C, +0x70, +0x74 and +0x78 in order. Its Execute's sentinels are already recorded: stance 5, air and naval 3, and negative for the two powers.

What the seven call sites pass: 0x351C8E and 0x35244E are the interface's naval and air stance pickers (5, 3, v / 5, v, 3); 0x4916AD sets air and naval to 2; 0x4B7E87 sets only the two powers (5, 3, 3, v, v); 0x4C375E is CAIUnit::SetPlanStance, which sets only the ground stance; and 0x4DAD74 is CAIUnit slot 76's theatre-adoption path, which passes the constant (1, 0, 0, -1000, -1000). Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanAttributesCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`). It resolves the command's `unit` reference and writes the six battle-plan attributes it carries onto that unit's embedded `CUnitPlan` (`CUnit +0x1FC`), each with a sentinel meaning "not set by this command":

| command field | key | sentinel | lands on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x64` byte | `active` | none | `CUnitPlan::SetActive` (`0x4DEB10`) |
| `+0x68` | `stance` | `== 5` skips | plan `+0xC` = `CUnit +0x208` |
| `+0x6C` | `air_stance` | `== 3` skips | plan `+0x10` = `CUnit +0x20C` |
| `+0x70` | `naval_stance` | `== 3` skips | plan `+0x14` = `CUnit +0x210` |
| `+0x74` | `our_power` | `< 0` skips | plan `+0x80` = `CUnit +0x27C` |
| `+0x78` | `their_power` | `< 0` skips | plan `+0x84` = `CUnit +0x280` |

Only the `stance` branch calls `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds` (at `0x1E78B4`) - changing the ground stance is what changes what the plan needs; the air and naval stances and the two power estimates do not.

**It re-resolves the unit for every field it writes** - six separate `FindPersistentById` lookups off `this->+0x40`/`+0x44` - rather than resolving once, which is why the body is four times longer than what it does. Each lookup has a failure arm that falls through to `xor eax, eax` and then stores through the null pointer anyway (`0x1E79EB` writes `[0 + 0x280]`); the game survives only because a command whose target has gone is rejected by `IsValid` before slot 6 is reached.

addresses.name: CSetPlanForcesCommand::Execute
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetPlanForcesCommand` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`). It resolves its `unit` reference, hands the `min` vector it carries at `+0x64` to `CUnitPlan::SetMinForces` (`0x4DF0F0`), which replaces plan `+0x70` - `CUnit +0x26C`, already named `plan_subunit_wanted` - and then calls `CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds` so the shortfall per subunit type is recomputed against the new target.

The two calls to `RefreshPlanForceNeeds` (`0x1E8928` and `0x1E8934`) are the two arms of the second lookup, not two refreshes: the second passes `eax = 0`, the null arm of a resolve the compiler inlined twice. So it refreshes once, and would dereference null if the unit had gone - which `IsValid` prevents.

addresses.name: ParseObjectReference
addresses.comment: **Reads the `{ type = N id = N }` block a save writes for an object reference into the 0x28-byte reference a command keeps.** It calls `ParseObjectId` (0x67B250) for the pair and then fills the reference: `+0` the cached object pointer, set to 0 because the block names no object yet; `+4` type; `+8` id; `+0xC` an `Hoi3CString` assigned from the parse context's own name at `+0x32C`. It takes no stack argument - the parse context arrives in ECX and the reference in ESI (`mov ecx,[ebp+8]` and `lea esi,[this+0x3C]` at the call site, a bare `ret` here), the same register-argument style as the rest of the loader primitives. 61 call sites, every one of them a command's `LoadKey` case for a key whose value is an object: `unit` is token 0x256 and `parent` 0x84, and a command keeps one such reference per key at `+0x3C`, `+0x64` and so on, 0x28 apart. **It stores nothing when the parse context's error handler at `+0x35C` has latched** - handler non-null and both its bytes at `+4` and `+5` set jumps straight to the epilogue and leaves the reference as it was, although `ParseObjectId` has already consumed the tokens. The mirror image is the command's `SaveContents`, e.g. `CMoveCommand`'s at 0x1D9160: `SaveWriteKey(0x256)` then the pair out of `+0x40` and `+0x44` - the string at `+0x4C` is never written to the save. The same reference is built from a live object by 0x2DD70 (unnamed): type from `CUnit +0x10`, id from `+0x14`, the string from the object's `+0x1C`, and the object pointer cached at `+0`.
