addresses.name: CEU3Application::CEU3Application
addresses.comment: The constructor of the object at CInGameIdler +0x1790, CFrontEnd +0x210 and CBackEndIdler +0xB8. At 0x22F134 it writes **[this] = 0x15CD1A8** and at 0x22F13A **[this+8] = 0x15CD1D0**; the RTTI export names those two tables `CEU3Application` (9 slots at offset 0, 4 at +8). retsBefore(0x62F080, 0x62F140) is empty, so both writes are inside this function, and 0x62F070 holds `14 c3` then 14 int3, so 0x62F080 is a real entry. One caller, 0xA59C43, at startup. Body otherwise as recorded: builds 'HoI3 v4.02' and 'HoI3', calls the base constructor 0x6909A0, builds the startup session with mode 2 at 0x22F30F and stores it at [this+0x12C]; `ret 0xC`, returns this in eax. The `SessionManager` reading came from that one field - the application *holds* a session, it is not a session manager - and `MakeBackEndIdler` is a real symbol, so the concept exists in the source without being this class's name. The signature gains an explicit __stdcall and a typed `this`, which is what lets scripts/checkSignatures.py check it: under the old name it was skipped twice, for 'no virtual table recorded for SessionManager' and 'no calling convention in the signature'. Simulated against a patched copy of project.json, the renamed entry is **checked and passes both tests** - `ret 0xC` against three stack arguments, and the constructor-against-vftable test, which can only run once the class name matches an RTTI table.

addresses.name: CEU3ApplicationVftableWrite
addresses.comment:
`mov dword ptr [esi], 0x15CD1A8` - the CEU3Application vftable (RTTI: 9 slots at object offset 0, plus a 4-slot secondary at +8), written inside the function project.json names `SessionManager::SessionManager` (rva 0x22F080). retsBefore(0x62F080, 0x62F140) is empty, the padding before 0x62F080 is 14 bytes, the function builds the strings 'HoI3 v4.02'/'HoI3' and calls the base CApplication constructor 0x6909A0 first, and findRefs reports exactly one caller (0xA59C43, at startup).

**So 0x22F080 is CEU3Application::CEU3Application, its comment's "No RTTI" is wrong, and CInGameIdler +0x1790 / CFrontEnd +0x210 / CBackEndIdler +0xB8 are the CEU3Application** - which is what makes the inlined `[+0x88]=1; [+0xE0]=screen` idiom in ProcessSessionEndRequests legible as CEU3Application::SetNextScreen (0x290F40). project.json already says as much in its entry for 0x234570. A correction for a human; the merge tool will not overwrite the name. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 8.

addresses.name: CEU3Application::LoadEverything
addresses.comment: **The game's startup**, named from its own log strings, which cite `eu3application.cpp`. In order: graphicalculturetype.txt and bookmarks.txt, `Initialise Defines`, `App Init`, the cursors, sound and music, graphics, the .gfx files, the .gui files, the databases (LoadCommonFiles below), LOAD_EVENTS, the sound effects, the flags, `history execute`, and last the idler. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CEU3Application::CreateChecksum
addresses.comment: **The last thing startup does**, not the seventh - called once, at 0x632AB4, after `Idler Initialised <`. Extent 0x632DA0..0x634568, `ret 4`, one stack argument (the application). Shows the `CREATING_CHKSUM` progress text and logs `Creating checksum for all files took ` (eu3application.cpp:759), `Checksum is ` (760) and `Testversion 4(settings)` (761). Its file list is the .rdata run from 0x15CC9A0: common/countries, units/models, units/country, history/{countries,diplomacy,provinces,wars,leaders,units}, map/default.map, map/cache/time, map/cache/adjacencies.bin, /cgm, /battleplans. It does **not** cover common/*.txt as files, the graphics or the localisation. That the purpose is multiplayer desync detection is **inferred** from the list, not read. In a real startup it costs 10.3 of the 33.8 seconds of app init.

addresses.name: CEU3Application::InitialiseGraphicalMap
addresses.comment: **Not part of LoadEverything.** Exactly one caller, 0x6EF51A, inside CFrontEnd slot 3 (0x6EEF00) - `mov ecx,[esi+0x210]; call 0x634570`, so `this` is the application reached off CFrontEnd +0x210 and there are no stack arguments (bare `ret` at 0x6348E2). Logs `initialise map` (eu3application.cpp:768), news and builds the graphical map through 0x640600/0x640950, logs `Initialising Graphical Map <` (775), then cleans up through 0x4924E0 and logs `Cleaning up after Graphical Map <` (779). Every provincemanager.cpp and bordermanager.cpp timing - CEU3MapCache, beach manager, borders, texts, rivers, terrain textures, meshes, waves - happens under it. So the graphical map is built **after** the whole of application init including the checksum, which is why its strings sitting beside the database strings in .rdata is trap 12 and not a sequence.

addresses.name: LoadCommonFiles
addresses.comment: **Works out which `common/*.txt` to read and reads them**, one argument, the application. Per file it builds `<directory> + "/name.txt"`, calls FileExists on it and keeps the path only where the file is there, which is how a mod's copy wins over vanilla's; the names are consecutive strings from 0x11CCB94, starting technology, static_modifiers, event_modifiers, buildings, governments, countries. Then it makes a tokenizer and a CParseContext over each. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: ResetGameStateToStartDate
addresses.comment:
0x63A460..0x63A83C, 0x3DD bytes, 283 instructions, `ret 4`. **Extent settled: trap 2, not trap 3.** retsBefore(0x63A460, 0x63AA10) returns two rets; the second (`ret 0xC` at 0x63AA01) belongs to 0x63A840, a separate function separated by only THREE int3 - so a padding scan looking for a run of five walks past the boundary, the same shape as 0x685F40/0x685FB0. cfg.py finds no edge from the body at or past 0x63A83A and functionStart(0x63A840) answers itself.

It clears three global registries (0x47FFF0, 0x4807F0, 0x47D160 - the last walks the country database at [0x1A855A4]), get-or-creates the game state, calls **CGameState::ResetSession (0x27BAF0)** at 0x23A505, calls CGameState::ClearPlayers (0x285F40) at 0x23A582 only when the argument is set, calls 0x23A330 (which the savegame loader also calls, at 0x27CEAD), repeats the three clears, clears loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) at 0x23A60E, then reads GetDefines()+8 and **writes it into state->tick (+0xBDC)** at 0x23A710 - i.e. it puts the clock back to the start date - and re-registers the clock with the global at [0x1A88BC0].

**It does NOT clear in_game.** It contains five `mov byte [reg+0xDA4], 0` instructions - 0x23A4C8, 0x23A54F, 0x23A5DB, 0x23A6D8, 0x23A7A2 - and every one is dead: each sits in the `operator new` succeeded arm of a copy of the inlined get-or-create accessor, guarded on [0x1A89790] == 0, which is never true after startup. Five of the 2,772 accessor copies FINDINGS-session.md section 1 accounted for. Looking for the live clear here finds only those; it is in the caller, 0x49 bytes after this function returns to 0x2542B0.

**It creates nothing, so it is not "start a game"**, which FINDINGS-session.md section 5 guessed and deliberately did not record. Five callers: 0x20BB2A (in 0x20BAF0), 0x25472C (ProcessSessionEndRequests), 0x30D2FD (in 0x30D010), 0x3147A7 (CGameSetup slot 11, which forwards its own argument) and 0x31D98E (CTutorialScreen::OnTutorialButtonPressed). Four pass 1; the tutorial screen passes 0, and it is the one caller about to set a game up rather than abandon one - which is the evidence for the argument's name. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: UpdateMapCamera
addresses.no_signature: Four stack arguments - it ends `ret 0x10` - **and** two objects in registers: the camera arrives in ESI and the mouse in EDI, both read before the prologue has finished. Under custom storage every parameter has to be placed or none does, and two of the four stack arguments have not been identified, so placing the rest would be a guess dressed as a fact.
addresses.comment:
**Moves the map camera, once a frame.** ESI is the camera (a MapCamera, which lives at CInGameIdler +0x1938), EDI the object the mouse position is asked of, and the first stack argument the one key states are asked of.

In order: dragging with the middle button, which works through the map projection rather than the screen; the arrow keys, tested as VK_LEFT, VK_UP, VK_RIGHT and VK_DOWN through the key object's +0x24; **the four screen edge tests at 0x23CE97** (see MapEdgeScrollTests); then clamping the result to the camera's limits.

Read for the parts named; the zoom and rotation arithmetic around them has not been followed.

addresses.name: MapEdgeScrollTests
addresses.comment:
**Where the map starts scrolling because the mouse is against the edge of the screen**, and where BiceLib stops it.

Four tests in a row, one per edge, each the same shape: ask EDI for the mouse position, compare one coordinate against one of the camera's edges give or take six pixels, and move the camera if it is past it.

    mov  edx, [edi]              ; the mouse object's vftable
    mov  edx, [edx + 0x4C]       ; its "where is the mouse"
    lea  eax, [esp + 0x24]
    push eax
    mov  ecx, edi
    call edx
    mov  ecx, [esi + 0x328]      ; edge_top, then bottom, left, right
    add  ecx, 6
    cmp  [eax + 4], ecx
    jge  <past it>

They run from here to **0x23CFB5**, where the camera is clamped, with nothing else in between - so a five byte jump from the first to the last removes all four and leaves the keyboard and the drag alone. The two instructions it replaces are exactly five bytes.

**Every branch that enters the range lands on this first byte** - five of them, with the only others being each test skipping itself - which is what makes jumping over the whole run safe. Checked with `reversing/cfg.py --lands-in 0x63ce97 0x63cfb5`.

Virtual slot 73 (vftable 0x15CEB54 + 0x124 = 0x15CEC78), read off the table directly. Four instructions: `push ecx; mov byte [ecx+0x1CD8], 1; call 0x277130; ret`. image.findValue over .rdata finds the address at exactly one vftable entry, so it is not a fold (trap 4). Properly padded, with its own int3 run before 0x24C010.

addresses.comment:
**Puts the camera on a province**, virtual slot 48. What the unit panel's `unit_location_button` ends up calling, and so what its `w` shortcut does.

addresses.name: UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows
addresses.comment:
0x64FC70..0x64FF77, bare `ret` at 0x64FF76, retsBefore empty. Receiver in **ESI**, no stack argument, so __fastcall with an explicit @ESI rather than a __thiscall (trap 11). One caller: 0x255AF4, inside CInGameIdler::Update, in a block reached unconditionally - so it runs every frame. It sits immediately before CInGameIdler::AutosaveWrite (0x24FF80) in .text.

Per-frame housekeeping for the in-game screen's auxiliary windows and, load-bearingly, **for the tutorial**: it shows or hides `chat_window` through [this+0x134C], pokes [this+0x1D2C] and [this+0x1CD0], and then runs the tutorial block. With state->tutorial_active (+0xD9D) set and no runner yet (slot 91), it creates one through slot 90 with state->tutorial_id (+0xDA0) as the value, at 0x24FEAA. When a runner exists and its +0x3C says it is finished, it destroys it through slot 90 with (0,0) and **sets exit_to_menu_requested (+0x1CDA) = 1 at 0x24FF10 - the only writer of a one to that byte in the image.** It finishes with [this+0x1D38] through 0x219E80 with the frame delta, and [this+0x1D4C]/[this+0x1D48] through 0x2D1CB0/0x2D2990.

The name covers the two halves that were read; 0x219E80, 0x2D1CB0 and 0x2D2990 were not. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: TutorialFinishedRequestsMenu
addresses.comment:
`mov byte ptr [esi+0x1CDA], 1` - the **only** instruction in the image that writes a one to exit_to_menu_requested. fieldchain's writer census for this field returns exactly three sites: the constructor's zero at 0x248473, this, and the read in ProcessSessionEndRequests. Positive control for that negative: the same scan finds the immediate stores to +0x1CD8 and +0x1CD9 through two different base registers, so it sees this class's writes in both encodings.

It fires when the tutorial runner at CInGameIdler +0x1D54 has its +0x3C byte set, immediately after slot 90 destroys the runner. So the whole route from Update to the game-state reset is the tutorial's automatic return to the main menu. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: ProcessSessionEndRequests
addresses.comment:
0x6542B0..0x65492C, 0x67C bytes, 471 instructions, TWO `ret 4` exits at 0x6547CF and 0x654929 - one function, not two: 0x65457A `je 0x6547d2` jumps past the first ret and both exits restore the same SEH slot [esp+0x74] (trap 3, and NOT trap 2 - a fresh prologue would have said the opposite). The idler arrives as a STACK argument, not in ecx, so this is not a __thiscall and carries no `::` (trap 11).

**The deferred end-of-session handler, called unconditionally once per frame** from CInGameIdler::Update at 0x25676A - its only caller. Every edge from the first half of Update into the second lands on 0x65644F, and from there to the call is a run of diamonds, so there is no gate above it; the gates are the three one-shot request bytes inside it, read in order:

- it first runs the **elimination detector**: with +5 clear, it looks the played tag (slot 23) up in the country database at [0x1A855A4]+0x16C and, if that CCountry's NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) is below 1 and the tag is not "REB", sets game_over_requested (+0x1CD9) at 0x25432E.
- `if (+0x1CD9)` -> new(0x600) + SessionManager::MakeBackEndIdler (0x254518), installed as the pending screen. **No reset, and in_game is not written** - but MakeBackEndIdler calls CGameState::SetInGameScreen, so in_game_screen is a CBackEndIdler while in_game is still 1.
- `if (+0x1CDA)` -> ResetGameStateToStartDate(1) at 0x25472C, then new(0x8B0) and, if that succeeded (0x254760), CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd at 0x254775, which clears in_game at 0x2ED9AF. Returns at 0x6547CF.
- `if (+0x1CD8)` -> PostQuitMessage(0) through the IAT at 0xD2B2BC.

Each branch also replaces the CSession with a placeholder built by 0xA887A0 from the literals "NoAdress" (0x15CC4C0) and "InitialSession" (0x15CC4CC), but only when multiplayer (+0x68) is set - an independent third reader that fits that field's name. Those two strings and the shared empty string 0x15B4945 are the ONLY .rdata references in the whole body; `messagelog_window` and `messagecat_*`, which FINDINGS-session.md section 4 attributed here, are not referenced.

The name is ours, read from the body; no string names it. Not in any vftable. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: PlayerEliminatedSetsGameOver
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [ebx+0x1CD9], 1` - the elimination detector at the head of ProcessSessionEndRequests, so it is evaluated every frame. Reached only when the played tag's CCountry has NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) below 1 (tested at 0x254306) and the tag is not "REB" (0x25431D..0x25432C), and only when CInGameIdler +5 is clear. The flag is acted on 7 bytes later, in the same call. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: ExitToMenuRequestGate
addresses.comment: `cmp byte ptr [ebx+0x1CDA], 0` followed by `je 0x2547D2` - the predicate FINDINGS-session.md section 4 said "was not read". It is the gate on the only reachable path from CInGameIdler::Update to CGameState::ResetSession. Its one writer of a one is 0x24FF10, inside UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows, under `if (state->tutorial_active)`. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: SessionExitCallsReset
addresses.comment:
`push 1; call 0x23A460` inside ProcessSessionEndRequests - **the only path from CInGameIdler::Update to the full game-state reset.** It is reached only when exit_to_menu_requested (+0x1CDA) is set, which in this build happens only when a tutorial's lesson runner reports itself finished.

**It does not leave a frame in which in_game is 1 over a wiped state.** 0x49 bytes later in THIS function - not inside 0x23A460, which has only dead clears - CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd is called at 0x254775 and clears in_game at 0x2ED9AF. The only branch in between is the `operator new` failure arm at 0x254760, and even on that arm CInGameIdler::Leave clears the byte at 0x262337: the run loop's swap calls the OUTGOING screen's slot 4 at 0x2913BC, four instructions after Update's slot-1 call returns and before it ever reads the incoming pointer. The only other call in the window is an indirect one at 0x254743 that resolves to 0x20CD50, a bare `ret 4`. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md sections 3 and 4.

addresses.name: InertSuspendCallInResetWindow
addresses.comment:
`call eax` reached through `[[idler+0x1790]+0xE4]` with `[vft+0x10]` - slot 4, index 4 - sitting **between** the game-state reset at 0x25472C and the in_game clear inside CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd. It is the one call in that window that could have touched the wiped state, and **it does nothing**: CEU3Application +0xE4 is a 0xC0-byte object installed once by the base CApplication constructor at 0x690B1C, its primary vftable is 0x15FDDC0 for the object's whole life (findValue finds that constant written only by the constructor, by its own slot 0 at 0x6802C8 and by one other method of the same class - the standard MSVC pattern), and slot 4 of that table is **0x20CD50, a bare `ret 4`** - TRAPS.md trap 4's 1420-holder shared stub. So it reads nothing, raises nothing and cannot reach a DLL; the hazard does not exist inside the frame either.

The same stub call appears with argument 1 at 0x254726, just before the reset, and again in CInGameIdler::AutosaveWrite at 0x25000C before the `save games/` path is built, so the idiom is a suspend/resume bracket that is inert in this build. Beware the off-by-one: reading `[vft+0x10]` as index 3 gives 0x680BA0, a plausible-looking global getter, and the wrong answer. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 3(a).

addresses.name: ExitToMenuAllocationFailureArm
addresses.comment:
`cmp eax, esi; je 0x25477E` - **the only branch between the game-state reset and the in_game clear**, and it is taken only when `new(0x8B0)` at 0x25474A returns null. On that arm CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd never runs, so in_game is NOT cleared inside ProcessSessionEndRequests; the function instead installs a **null** pending screen (app->+0x88 = 1 at 0x254797, app->+0xE0 = 0 at 0x2547B8) and returns.

It is discounted twice over. First, in_game is still cleared: the run loop's swap calls the OUTGOING screen's slot 4 - CInGameIdler::Leave, clearing the byte at 0x262337 - at 0x2913BC, *before* it reads app->+0xE0 at 0x2913BE. Second, the arm is self-terminating: with app->+0x84 set to 0 at 0x2913E4, the swap dereferences it with no null test at 0x291404 (`mov edx,[ecx]`) and faults 0x48 bytes later. Same class of arm as the dead "release the old one" branch in FINDINGS-session.md section 5 - reachable only if operator new returns 0. Recorded because it is the one branch in the window and the block should not be described as straight-line. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 3(b).

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Update
addresses.comment: Per-frame update of the in game idler, virtual slot 1; calls the autosave writer (0x24FF80, `push ebx` with ebx = this, at 0x255E28). `ret 4`, but **no implementation of slot 1 reads its stack argument** - not this one, not CEU3Idler's at 0x244750, not CFrontEnd's at 0x2EDD60 (which only forwards it to the base), not CBackEndIdler's 0x208AF0 or CNudgeIdler's 0x29BE90 - so the argument is real but its meaning is not recoverable from the bodies. Frame timing is taken from the clock at +0x192C instead, into +0xA88/+0xA8C.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Enter
addresses.comment:
Slot 3 of `CInGameIdler`'s virtual table, and the whole of entering a running game: it looks up the `unitlist_start` / `unitlist_offset` gui types (`Missing unitlist_start or unitlist_offset gui type.`), runs `LOAD_GFX`, `LOAD_EVENTS` and `ADAPTING_HISTORY`, logs the six `eu3idler.cpp` setup stages, **sets `gamestate->in_game` at `0x25D126`**, then builds the in-game interface.

`CFrontEnd` overrides the same slot at `0x2EEF00`, where it logs `entering frontend...` and **clears** the same byte at `0x2EFE58` - which is what makes slot 3 the screen's enter hook rather than anything more specific.

Spans `0x25A2B0`..`0x261BB8`, about 0x7900 bytes, which is why `image.functionStart`'s default 0x2500 limit reports `?` for the write inside it.

addresses.name: EnterGame_SetInGame
addresses.comment:
**The only instruction in the executable that writes `CCurrentGameState +0xDA4` a nonzero value**: `mov byte ptr [ecx + 0xDA4], 1`, with `ecx` loaded from `g_CCurrentGameState` two instructions earlier.

It sits near the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter` (`0x25A2B0`), after the session has been built - the log lines above it are `Countries initialized<`, `provinces initialised<`, `information caches setup<`, `supply logic defined<`, ` processed weather <`, ` processed intel setup <` - and before the in-game GUI is built (`menubar`, `chat_list`, `mapmode_1`..`mapmode_10`).

Unconditional on its path: the block at `0x25D120` is the join of the inlined get-or-create of the game state, entered from `0x25D082(taken)`, `0x25D114(taken)` and `0x25D11E(flow)`, and the block above it at `0x25D075` is reached from all three arms of the camera setup. **So the attrition gate opens in every game**, which is what the live tooltip measurement already showed.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::DailyUpdate
addresses.comment: CInGameIdler virtual slot 53: repaints the map in modes 4/18/19, then always runs the autosave check. Takes nothing on the stack (bare `ret` on all three paths) and returns true - every path sets `al, 1` before the epilogue. The mode is the dword at +0xD34; mode 4 calls MapMode_Supply_Colour (0x266EE0), 0x12 and 0x13 go through 0x46A1E0/0x46AD60 and 0x46A6F0 on the map object's +0x1DC4; every path ends with `push esi; call 0x261D20`, the autosave check.

addresses.name: DailyUpdate_CallAutosaveCheck
addresses.comment: Fallthrough in DailyUpdate that calls the autosave check whatever the map mode.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::AutosaveCheck
addresses.comment: Decides whether to autosave: clears idler +0xAB0, then sets it when the date matches the frequency; ret 4.

addresses.name: AutoSave_ClearRequest
addresses.comment: mov byte ptr [eax+0xAB0], bl - clears the autosave request flag at the top of the autosave decision; eax is the idler, esi the tick. Hooked. The autosave flag clear hooked by BiceLib (same site as RVA 0x261DBA).

addresses.comment: Slot 4 of `CInGameIdler`'s virtual table, the counterpart to slot 3: it frees the idler's lists and then **clears `gamestate->in_game` at `0x262337`**. `CFrontEnd` overrides the same slot at `0x2F0140`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetTutorialRunner
addresses.comment:
Virtual slot 90 (vftable 0x15CEB54 + 0x168), `ret 8`. Releases this->tutorial_runner (+0x1D54) through its own slot 1 with 1 and nulls it; then, if `create`, allocates 0x40 bytes, constructs through 0x8E7370, stores the result at +0x1D54 and calls 0x8E7950(it, max(tutorialId,1) - 1).

Its only two call sites in this class are inside UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows (0x24FEAA with (1, state->tutorial_id) and 0x24FF0E with (0,0)); slotcalls.py's other 34 hits at this displacement are unrelated classes. The 0x40-byte object's class, and what 0x8E7370/0x8E7950 do, were not established, so the argument name is read from the one caller. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::SetTutorialRunner(CInGameIdler* this, bool create, int tutorialId)

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::HasTutorialRunner
addresses.comment: Virtual slot 91 (vftable 0x15CEB54 + 0x16C). Four instructions, read in full: `xor eax,eax; cmp [ecx+0x1D54], eax; setne al; ret`. It answers whether the tutorial runner exists, which is how UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows avoids creating a second one and how it decides whether to examine the existing one. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetAutosaveRequested
addresses.comment: Virtual setter (slot 92) for the autosave request pair; clears +0xAB1 whenever +0xAB0 is set to 0. Nine instructions: `mov al,[ebp+8]; mov [ecx+0xAB0],al; test al,al; jne; mov [ecx+0xAB1],al`, then `ret 4`. The byte it leaves in al is the argument, not a return value.

addresses.name: RunSupplyAndConvoyIterations
addresses.comment:
The outer driver FINDINGS-supply knew only as 'the entry reached from CInGameIdler::Enter'. It is a loop, and the loop count is the answer to that file's open question about CCurrentGameState +0x58:

    iterations = (gs->tutorial_active (+0xD9D) || gs->arcade_mode (+0xC9C) > 0) ? 1 : gs->max_supply_depot_distance (+0x58) + 2

Each iteration snapshots every country's stockpile into a per-country CGoodsPool vector (indexed by CCountry +0xCA8), runs CSupply::DailySupplyPass (0x2872D0, skipped in Arcade) with four alloca'd per-province arrays, and then walks every country's convoys and calls CConvoy::RunDelivery. **A convoy whose `ship` mask includes supplies or fuel runs on every iteration; a lend-lease, trade, or pure-resource convoy runs only on iteration 0** (the test at 0x678F72..0x678F99 against the loop index). That is what lets supply cross several sea legs inside one day while resources cross one. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CEU3Minimap::CEU3Minimap
addresses.comment: Calls CIcon::CIcon (rva 0x6A1C00) at 0x67A47D, then `mov [esi], 0x15cf15c`. The one live instance is the iconType named minimap_pic, which is why a CEU3Minimap turns up in CGui+0x5C alongside twelve RTTI-less widget classes. `ret 0x10`; argument boundaries not read.

addresses.name: CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending
addresses.comment: The qsort comparator for provinces_by_supply_order. Returns +1 when b's supply_depot_distance is the larger, 0 when equal, -1 otherwise - a descending sort on +0x4C, so element 0 is the province farthest from its depot. This is the derivation of the 'farthest first' in CCurrentGameState::provinces_by_supply_order's name, which CSupply::DailySupplyPass's single forward sweep depends on.

addresses.name: CCurrentGameState::CCurrentGameState
addresses.comment:
0x67B130..0x67B155, 38 bytes, bare `ret`, clean int3 padding, `this` in ESI and returned in EAX, no stack arguments. Calls CGameState::CGameState (0x27D070), zeroes +0xD9C as a word (so tutorial_active +0xD9D with it), zeroes +0xDA0, zeroes in_game +0xDA4 at 0x27B146, then writes CCurrentGameState's own vftable 0x11CF674 and returns this.

**This corrects project.json's comment on 0x27D070**, which says CCurrentGameState has no standalone constructor to name. It has one; the compiler emitted both an out-of-line copy here, with 282 direct callers, and 2772 inlined copies. Found by scanning .text for the displacement 0xDA4 and keeping the writes that are not preceded by the vftable constant 0x15CF674 - this one writes the vftable *after* the zeroing, which is why it stood out. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 1.

addresses.name: CCurrentGameStateCtor_ZeroInGame
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [esi + 0xDA4], al` with al zeroed two instructions earlier - in_game cleared by the out-of-line CCurrentGameState constructor (0x27B130). One of only six instructions in the image that write CCurrentGameState +0xDA4; the other construction-time clear is the 2772-times-inlined copy of the same accessor. Independently re-derived 2026-10-02 by a second method before the record was changed on its strength.

addresses.name: ProcessAITradeFunctor::operator()
addresses.comment: The per-country body the hourly AI trade functor runs; its only caller is 0x28EEA3 inside ProcessAITradeFunctor_start_for::execute (0x28EDE0), which is a TBB task vtable slot and so has no direct caller. It calls CCountry::RunHourlyAITrade (0xDC410) at 0x27B1A2. The name follows FINDINGS-tick's naming of 0x28E190; the body itself was read only as far as that call. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: UpdateProvinceWeatherRange
addresses.comment: The leaf of the hourly weather pass over provinces: `(CMapProvince** range@EAX, provinces@[ebp+8])`, `ret 4`. For each province in the range whose CProvinceTemplate+0x13D is set it writes CProvince+0x2C from IsNight (0xA7390), runs CWeather::Update (0xB2590) on province+0x68, and where CWeather::GraphicName (0xB4400) now answers a different string than CProvince+0x98 holds it stores the new one and sets the CProvince+0x9C redraw flag. Reached only through ProcessProvinceFunctor_start_for::execute (0x28EEB0), whose root task ProcessProvinceFunctor (0x28E270) has exactly one caller: RunHourlyPass at 0x282A3B. So this - and nothing else - is what advances province weather, once an hour.

addresses.name: CGameState_StartupResetAndLoadGameplaySettings
addresses.comment:
0x67B240..0x67BAE8 inclusive - the `ret 4` at 0x67BAE6 is three bytes - so 0x8A9 = 2217 bytes, 586 instructions, one `ret 4`, one stack argument. Extent clean of traps 2 and 3: retsBefore(0x67B240, 0x67BB00) returns exactly one ret, and seven int3 separate it from CGameState::ResetSession at 0x67BAF0. **Exactly one caller**, 0x23286D, inside CEU3Application::LoadEverything (0x62FAC0..0x632CE6 by the int3 scan), at the `history execute <` stage; so it runs once per process, at startup, on the global game state, before the first screen exists - the first CFrontEnd is constructed later in the same function, at 0x2329DE.

What it does, in order: (1) 0x27B29E state->+0xF0 = <the 4-byte factory at [0x174DA90], vftable 0x15FDF60>->slot1(), which allocates a 4-byte object with vftable 0x15FDCFC, and then calls slot 1 on that, which is the 1691-holder empty stub 0xABF890. (2) get-or-creates g_CCurrentGameState (dead - it exists from the database stage). (3) 0x27B33B..0x27B3C1 collects every country's tag (CCountry +0xCA4) out of state->countries_begin (+0xBBC) into a local std::vector<Hoi3CString>, hands it to 0x148B0, and passes the 0x10-byte result **by value** to 0x1F3640(state->income_statistics (+0xC6C), keys) - 0x1F3640 ends `ret 0x14`, which is what identifies the second argument as the 0x10-byte temp rather than a discarded local. So the statistics series are re-keyed by country tag. (4) only when state->+0xCEC == 0 (jne at 0x27B406 skips it): rebuilds the singly linked list at state->+0xCE8 with count +0xCEC and tail +0xCE4, one 0x10-byte node {value, next, 0, 0} per element of the vector at +0x1C of the global at [0x1A878BC] whose virtual slot 6 returns true, the value being that element's +0x54 or, when that is null, the CNullFaction singleton at [0x1A855A8] (lazily built with 0x1224B0 and given vftable 0x15C248C). (5) 0x27B58D..0x27B59F clears in_game_screen (+0xBE8), loaded_from_save (+0xD9C), **in_game (+0xDA4)** and tutorial_id (+0xDA0). (6) CGameState_SetProvincesAndSizePerCountryVectors(state, [0x1A8557C]+0x2200). (7) get-or-creates the 0x57C-byte CCountryDataBase at [0x1A855A4] with CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase (0x2024D0), then 0x27E550(state, &db->+0x16C), which clears and resizes both state->countries (+0xBBC/+0xBC0) and state->played_countries (+0xBCC) to the database's country count and copies every CCountry* across, zeroing the played entry for each. (8) **CGameState::ResetSession (0x27BAF0)** at 0x27B5F3. (9) 0x28A6E0([0x1A8557C]), which parses `<...>/colors.txt`. (10) 0x27B604..0x27BA69: assigns the string 'gameplaysettings.txt' (the image's only reference to it, 0x15CF29C), and when the mod-name string the settings singleton at [0x1A863F8] yields through 0x40C600 is non-empty, replaces it with 'mod/' + <mod> + '/' + 'gameplaysettings.txt'; then FileExists (0x784A20) on it, and when it exists builds a 0x114-byte tokenizer over the file - an inlined copy of **Tokenizer::Tokenizer (rva 0x669990, VA 0xA69990)**, which project.json already records as 0x114 bytes with vftable 0x11FD1FC (rva) = 0x15FD1FC (VA), the same table written here at 0x27B9AD, with 0xA6C1B0 and 0xA69AD0 as its internals - and an inlined CParseContext (0x360 bytes, vftable 0x15FD93C, name 'UNNAMED_SESSION', tokenizer at +0x1C - the same object CParseContext::CParseContext 0x67A460 builds) and calls **virtual slot 3 of the game state - [0x15CF674+0xC] = 0xA7C050, CPersistent::Load** - on it, then releases it through slot 0 with 1. (11) frees the tag vector.

**So the mod's own `mod/<mod>/gameplaysettings.txt`, if present, is parsed into the game state at startup through CGameState::LoadKey, and when a mod is active the game-root copy is not read at all.** Neither file exists in this install, so the parse is skipped here.

For the DLL: this is the only writer of in_game that is neither a construction nor a screen transition, it runs once, at startup, before any screen exists, and its clear writes 0 over a byte that is already 0. It changes nothing about Gui::Lua::sessionActive() or GameClock::movedInPlay().

addresses.name: StartupReset_ClearInGame
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [esi + 0xDA4], bl` with ebx the zero register - in_game cleared inside 0x27B240, the reset LoadEverything's `history execute` stage runs over the global game state. Written beside `[esi+0xBE8] = 0` and `[esi+0xD9C] = 0`. Not previously in the record's writer list for the field.

addresses.name: CGameState::ResetSession
addresses.comment:
0x67BAF0..0x67CAA7, `ret 4`, 4026 bytes, one stack argument. The game state's own teardown-and-clear: at its head it zeroes supply_network_dirty (+0x50), +0xD9C (0x27BB26), +0xC8C, frame_time_accumulator (+0xBE4) and game_speed (+0xBEC), and at 0x27C99A it calls MarkSimulatedProvinces(state, 0), which is what **nulls scenario (+0xD0C)**. **It does not touch in_game (+0xDA4).** Three callers: the startup reset 0x27B240 (0x27B5F3), the savegame loader 0x27CE30 (its very first call, 0x27CE58), and 0x23A460 (0x23A505), which is itself reached from CGameSetup slot 11, CTutorialScreen::OnTutorialButtonPressed and a CInGameIdler method. Only the head of the function was read; the name is inference from what it clears and who calls it. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md sections 4 and 5.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation.

addresses.name: ResetSession_ClearLoadedFromSave
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [ebx + 0xD9C], 0` at the head of CGameState::ResetSession (0x27BAF0), beside the clears of +0x50, +0xC8C, +0xBE4 and +0xBEC. The savegame loader calls this reset first and then sets the same byte to 1 at 0x27CEB9, so the pair is clear-then-set and the flag survives the load.

addresses.name: LoadSaveFile
addresses.comment: 0x67CAE0..0x67CE2F, `ret 8` at 0x67CD74 with an exception funclet past it ending `ret` at 0x67CE2D (trap 3). Builds a stream and a CParseContext over its second argument - `UNNAMED_SESSION`, 0xA6C1B0, CParseContext::CParseContext 0xA7A460 - and calls CGameState::LoadFromSave (0x27CE30) at 0x27CCF8 and again at 0x27CE09 on the alternate arm. **Three callers and no others**: 0x30B08B and 0x30B73C inside 0x30A5C6, which is gamesetup.cpp (`save_games_list`, `SAVE_LOADED`, `SAVE_TRANSFER_DONE`, `play_button`), and 0x31D933 inside CTutorialScreen::OnTutorialButtonPressed. The three call sites were independently re-confirmed 2026-10-02 by decoding every `call rel32` in the image that targets this address. **So a savegame can only be loaded from the pre-game lobby or the tutorial screen, neither of which has in_game set** - which is why in_game is 0 for the whole of a load and not 1. The second argument's type was not read. **TRAP 2**: 0x67CAD0 is a separate 16-byte tail-call thunk ending `ret` at 0x67CADF and this function begins at the very next byte with no padding, so image.functionStart answers 0x67CAD0 for anything inside it. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 4.

addresses.name: CGameState::LoadFromSave
addresses.comment:
0x67CE30..0x67CFB2, `ret 8`, with the catch arm past it out to 0x67D060 logging gamestate.cpp:570 `Failed to load save file ` (trap 3). **The whole of loading a savegame into the game state**, in order: CGameState::ResetSession(state) at 0x27CE58; in_game_screen (+0xBE8) virtual slot 64; 0x23A330; **`state->+0xD9C = 1`** at 0x27CEB9, the loaded-from-save flag; CGameState::SetInGameScreen (0x280F30) to put the screen back after the reset; 0x28BB90; **virtual slot 3 on the state, CPersistent::Load, which parses the save**; 0x45E690 over `&state->scenario_name (+0xD10)` to resolve the scenario the save named; MarkSimulatedProvinces(state, that scenario) at 0x27CF90, which is what sets scenario (+0xD0C); then 0x28BB90 again and 0x28C190.

**It never writes in_game (+0xDA4)** - re-confirmed 2026-10-02 by checking that none of the field's six writers falls inside 0x67CAE0..0x67CFB2. Two callers, both in LoadSaveFile (0x27CAE0). See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 4.

addresses.name: LoadFromSave_SetLoadedFromSave
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [ebx + 0xD9C], 1` inside CGameState::LoadFromSave (0x27CE30), after the session reset has cleared it and immediately before CPersistent::Load parses the save. **The only instruction in the image that writes CCurrentGameState +0xD9C a nonzero value**, which is what makes that byte the new-game/load switch: CInGameIdler::Enter branches on it thirteen times, and CCountry::LoadKey, CUnit::LoadKey and ProcessAI read it too.

addresses.name: CGameState::CGameState
addresses.comment:
Base constructor: it writes CGameState's own vftable (rva 0x11CF624) at +0. Called from the inlined CCurrentGameState constructor at all 2773 sites, each of which then writes CCurrentGameState's vftable (rva 0x11CF674) and zeroes the derived fields +0xD9C, +0xDA0 and in_game at +0xDA4 - so CCurrentGameState has no standalone constructor to name. This entry read CCurrentGameState::CCurrentGameState until the wave of 2026-09-23; it was marked confirmed on the strength of CLASSES.md rather than the image.

**Correction 2026-10-02** (reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 1): this comment said CCurrentGameState has no standalone constructor to name. It has one - 0x27B130, 38 bytes, `this` in ESI, with 282 direct callers - alongside 2,772 inlined copies of the same get-or-create accessor. The 2,773 'direct callers' figure counted accessor copies, not constructions: at most one of them ever constructs anything, because every one is guarded on the global being null.

addresses.name: CGameState_Ctor_ClearFreezeFronts
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [ebx+0xB00], 0` in CGameState::CGameState, sixteen bytes after it writes the CWeatherManager vftable at +0xAEC - the embedded manager's `freeze_fronts` (+0x14) being seeded to zero. **It is the only write to that byte in the image**: the manager exists exactly once (one vftable reference, at 0x27D1C3), every instruction in .text encoding `[reg+0xB00]` is accounted for, and every function that ever holds the manager as `this` touches `this+0x14` only at the read 0xB5CD7. So the marking path at 0xB5CD7 never runs.

addresses.name: InitialiseGui
addresses.comment: The one call between `Used RAM after GUI loaded [` (eu3application.cpp:510) and `Loading GUI <` (515) in LoadEverything, at 0x632264. Extent 0x67D740..0x67D8E8, `ret 4`. **Position only** - the GUI framework is covered elsewhere and this entry deliberately says nothing about its interior. Stage order: the .gui files are enumerated and parsed under the `LOADING_GUI_DEF` progress text (one `Loaded GUI Definition File: ` per file, line 507), then this runs, then the databases.

addresses.name: CGameState_SetProvincesAndSizePerCountryVectors
addresses.comment: 0x67E320-0x67E542, `ret 8`. Copies the given vector of CProvince* into `state->+0xB8C` (calling slot 6 on each), then resizes **both** per-country vectors `+0xB9C` and `+0xBAC` to the country count `(state->+0xBC0 - state->+0xBBC) / 4`, through the 0x10-byte-element helpers 0x68D760/0x68D7D0/0x68F3C0. That resize is what establishes the element size (`sar eax, 4` at 0x67E428) and the index (a country id). The name is from what the body does; the game's own name is not recovered.

addresses.name: CGameState::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGameState::LoadKey(CGameState* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 31 of them, one case each: `active_war`, `ai_seed`, `allied_objectives`, `automate_sliders`, `automate_tech_sliders`, `automate_trade`, `battle_plan`, `combat`, `controller`, `date`, `diplomacy`, `faction`, `fired_events`, `flags`, `gameplaysettings`, `id`, `income_statistics`, `inflation_statistics`, `leader`, `nation_size_statistics`, `player`, `previous_war`, `rebel`, `rebel_faction`, `scenario`, `selectionGroups`, `start_date`, `undeclared_war`, `unit`, `victory_conditions`, `weather`. Inherited by 2 classes in all. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CGameState::SetInGameScreen
addresses.comment:
0x680F30..0x680FD3, `ret 4`: the state on the stack, **the screen in EDI**, stored into state->in_game_screen (+0xBE8) at 0x280F37, after which it reads +0xBC0. One of only three instructions in the image that write that field (the others are the startup reset's zero at 0x27B58D and 0x4C9545, which is a different class). Five callers: SessionManager::MakeBackEndIdler, a site at 0x24901C **inside CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler** (retsBefore(0x6474A0, 0x648728) is empty, so the constructor really does run that far), CGameState::LoadFromSave, 0x29D793, and **CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd at 0x2EDB47**.

That last one is the point: **at the main menu, state->in_game_screen is a CFrontEnd, not a CInGameIdler.** Anything reading CInGameIdler fields through +0xBE8 has to gate on in_game first. Corroborated live 2026-10-02: in a running game it resolves to CInGameIdler by its own RTTI. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 6.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation.

addresses.name: CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock
addresses.comment: **The frame's end of the clock**, 0x281130 to 0x2813E3, a bare `ret` - so nothing is passed on the stack: **the frame's elapsed time arrives in xmm0**, which is not how MSVC passes a stack float, so do not read a stack slot for it. One caller, 0x256006, inside CInGameIdler::Update. It adds the delta to +0xBE4, and returns at once if +0xBF0 says a tick is already in flight (the `cmp` is at 0x28114F, the `jne` at 0x281179 - the float work between them does not touch the flags). Otherwise it indexes five float thresholds - 0x160A2EC, 0x1718064, 0x171DBAC, 0x15AB304, 0x160A740 - by the speed at +0xBEC and compares; below the threshold it does nothing. When an hour is due it zeroes the accumulator, news 0x4C bytes, calls CHourlyTickCommand's constructor with a pointer to +0xC58, and posts it: in_game_screen (+0xBE8) slot 18 returns an object whose +0x38 gets slot 6 called with the command. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: RunHourlyTick
addresses.comment: **One hour of game time, and the map of everything periodic.** 0x2813F0 to 0x282438, `ret 8`. Sets the interlock (`mov byte [edi+0xBF0], 1` at 0x281425) that stops AdvanceClock queueing another hour while this one runs, and holds the image's **only** advance of the clock, `inc dword [edi+0xBDC]` at 0x28155F. It takes the date apart first - `[state+0xBDC] - 0x29C55C0`, then /24 by the 0x2AAAAAAB magic, MonthLengthTable and the 365.0 at 0x160A550 - and compares afterwards, so each period runs when its number changed. In order: SnapshotRandomState (0x28207A, hourly); RunHourlyPass (0x282080, hourly); RunDailyPass (0x28213A) and in_game_screen slot 53 (0x28213F) when the day changed, gated by `cmp [esp+0x28], eax; je` at 0x282133; RunMonthlyPass (0x2821C1) and slot 54 when the month changed, gated at 0x2821BA; RunYearlyPass (0x282211) and slot 55 when the year changed, gated at 0x28220A; then 0x28DB20 every hour, last, which defers unit deletion through CGameState::RemoveUnit. **Slots 54 and 55 are both the do-nothing stub 0x692590**, so nothing in this build hangs off the monthly or yearly screen hook. A second counter at 0x1A8560C is incremented once per tick and is not identified. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: SnapshotRandomState
addresses.comment: Run **every hour** from RunHourlyTick at 0x28207A, on the game state's +0xC58, and ends 0x28250A with a bare `ret`. Clears the vector, then pushes two dwords into it through 0x221F0: g_random_draws (0x174DA8C) and the contents of **0x174DA94, which is not identified** - it is not the seed, since that is the state array at 0x1310F80. Along the way it lazily allocates a 4-byte object with vftable 0x15FDF60 into 0x174DA90. The same +0xC58 is handed to CHourlyTickCommand::Construct. Named for what it does; no class. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: RebuildEventCandidatesAndDailyCaches
addresses.comment: 0x682510 to the bare `ret` at 0x682628. **Takes the game state in EAX** - not ecx, not the stack - and cleans nothing. It is a separate function from the hourly generator snapshot at 0x682440, which ends at 0x68250A with its own bare `ret` and int3 padding between them. It creates the global event list if null (through SetEventList at 0x682550), then calls RebuildCountryEventCandidates on it at 0x68255B, then 0x68BB90(state), 0x68C190(), 0x4B59C0(state+0xAEC @EAX), a per-entry 0x5082C0 loop over the state+0xBBC array, and finally copies seven dwords +0x164..+0x17C to +0x188..+0x1A0 on each entry of the state+0x54 array. **This is the only path other than RunMonthlyPass that builds the per-country candidate lists**, and its own two callers are CInGameIdler vftable slot 67 (0x64C170, vftable 0x15CEB54, the only class that overrides the 0xABF890 stub that CEU3Idler/CBackEndIdler/CNudgeIdler leave there) and CReopenLobby::Execute (0x6D8430, CCommand slot 6). Inside 0x64C170 the call is gated on [[this+0x1790]+0x12C]+0x236 being non-zero (0x64C20C). The name covers only the event part; the other five calls were not read. See reversing/FINDINGS-events.md.

addresses.name: RunHourlyPass
addresses.comment: The simulation work that happens **every hour**. 0x282630 to 0x282C1D, `ret 4`. **It abuts RunDailyPass with no int3 between them**, which is how the two were once read as one function and the daily supply work recorded as hourly - a scan for the next padding runs straight past 0x282C1D into 0x282C20. The only thing named in it so far is CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork at 0x2826E8, guarded on the dirty flag at +0x50, so a depot label changed during the hour is repaired within the hour. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: HourlyWeatherManagerTick
addresses.comment: `lea edi,[ebx+0xAEC]; call 0xB5A20` inside RunHourlyPass - CWeatherManager::Tick, once an hour, with the manager embedded in the game state.

addresses.name: HourlyWeatherProvincePass
addresses.comment: `call 0x28E270` inside RunHourlyPass: the only caller of the TBB root task whose leaf is UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B1C0). This is the hourly per-province weather update, and 0x28E270's existing name ProcessProvinceFunctor says what it is shaped like rather than what it does.

addresses.name: RunDailyPass
addresses.comment: **Everything the game does once a day.** 0x282C20 to 0x283077, `ret 4`. One caller: the tick body at 0x2813F0 calls it at 0x28213A, and only when the day number it recomputed differs from the stored one - the `cmp [esp+0x28], eax; je 0x282157` just above skips both this and CInGameIdler's slot 53 when the day has not turned. **It is not 0x282630**, the hourly pass that ends at 0x282C1D with its own `ret 4`; the two abut with no padding between them, which is how they came to be read as one function. What this one calls, in order: 0x28C190, 0x63030, CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x282CEF, guarded on the dirty flag), CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder, a qsort with the comparator at 0x27B100 pushed at 0x282D0C, CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot in a loop, 0x4F28B0, RunDailySupplyPass at 0x282D7E, then 0x28A0A0, 0x28E350, 0x4E39C0, 0x4DA530, 0x49EAB0, 0x4B9D60, 0x5BF720, 0x5C0A40, 0x288D40 and 0x143AB0. So the supply order is sorted and the daily supply pass run **once a day**, not once an hour. Named for what it does; no class, like RunDailySupplyPass beside it.

addresses.name: SupplyOrder_CallQsort
addresses.comment: qsort(state->provinces_by_supply_order, provinceCount, 4, CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending) - the one place the supply order array is sorted. The instructions after it read back element 0's supply_depot_distance into CCurrentGameState +0x58, clamp it to 500, and where it exceeded 500 re-run CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province.

addresses.name: CGameState::RunAIPass
addresses.comment: **The gate that makes the AI hourly.** `ret 4`, one caller: CInGameIdler::Update at 0x656278, so it is offered every frame. Returns at once when `state[+0xC68]` is set; otherwise sets the global byte 0x1A857BF, launches the ProcessAI parallel_for (0x28E430) over `state[+0x114..+0x118]` with grain `max(1, count / ([0x170ABB0] == 1 ? 1 : 16))`, restores the global and sets `state[+0xC68] = 1`. **RunHourlyPass clears +0xC68 at its end (0x682B1D)**, and a byte-exact sweep finds no other clear, so the AI runs exactly once per game hour. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CGameState::StartAI
addresses.comment: `ret 4`. Logs `Starting AI` (0x15CF31C) from `gamestate.cpp` line 0x795, then walks every country in `state[+0xBBC]`, news 0x12C bytes, constructs a CEU3AI with `(country[+0xCA4], country[+0xCA8])`, stores it in `country+0x1D8` at 0x6832FD and pushes it onto the vector at **state +0x114/+0x118/+0x11C**. That vector is what the hourly parallel AI pass iterates. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: RunMonthlyPass
addresses.comment: 0x283B50 to 0x283D0F, `ret 4`, then clean int3 padding. Called from RunHourlyTick at 0x2821C1 only when the month number changed, immediately before in_game_screen slot 54 - which is the do-nothing stub 0x692590, so this function is the whole of what the game does on a month change. Its contents have not been read. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: RunMonthlyPass_DecayProvinceNationalism
addresses.comment: `add dword [esi+0x24], -0x53` - the unidentified monthly -83 noted in FINDINGS-tick.md, floored at 0 by 0x683BAB. esi is an entry of state+0xB8C, which project.json already records as provinces_begin, and CMapProvince +0x24 as nationalism. So this is **province nationalism running down 83 thousandths a month**, i.e. one unit a year, and it has nothing to do with technology categories. That YEARS_OF_NATIONALISM (CDefines country +0x8) is what seeds the field is inference.

addresses.name: RunYearlyPass
addresses.comment: Called from RunHourlyTick at 0x282211 when the year number changed, then in_game_screen slot 55 - the same do-nothing stub as the monthly hook. The caller pushes one argument and does not clean up, and the `ret 4` at 0x283E7D matches that, so the function is 0x283D20 to 0x283E7D. **The block from 0x283E80 to the bare `ret` at 0x283ED1 is a separate function**, not out-of-line code as this comment used to say: it takes the game state in EDI with no stack arguments, which is why it looked like it was using edi unset, and it has 12 callers of its own (RefreshAllCountries, rva 0x283E80). Still do not read the two as one body. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: RefreshAllCountries
addresses.comment: **Not out-of-line code, which is what the RunYearlyPass comment currently says.** 0x283E80 to the bare `ret` at 0x283ED1, then ten int3; frame-less (`push ecx` reserves the slot, `pop ecx` restores it), the game state in EDI, no stack arguments - which is why it appears to use edi without setting it. A rel32 scan of .text finds twelve calls to it (0x2D629C, 0x2EDA27, 0x2F4474, 0x2F4AC4, 0x2F50C4, 0x2F5724, 0x307F16, 0x30B333, 0x30B798, 0x30BA89, 0x3148D2, 0x31DAB5) and **none on the tick**; two of the containing functions are CSetHistoryDate slot 6 (0x2D60C0) and CGameSetup slot 11 (0x314100), so the callers are the lobby and scenario setup. Body: for each country in state[+0xBBC] with `[c+0x44] != 0` call 0xE3EB0 (country in ESI; CCountry::RebuildNeighbours then 0xE39C0), then 0x288D40(state) - the same pair of jobs RunDailyPass does. The name is **inference** from that shape and those callers. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval
addresses.comment:
**How a TBB worker gets a unit deleted without deleting it.** Thirty instructions: copy the object's id pair (`+0x10`, `+0x14`) to the stack, `lock xadd` the tail counter of the `tbb::concurrent_queue` at `CCurrentGameState +0xBF4`, and push the pair into the micro-queue that ticket selects. The object arrives in **EAX**, the state is the one stack argument, `ret 4` at `0x684CDA`.

Eight callers, and the first two are the ones that matter for hooking: `0x5B9F0C` and `0x5B9FE7` are inside **`CUnit::UpdateHourly`**, which runs on a TBB worker. `0x5BA4C8` and `0x5BA714` are inside `CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat` (tick thread), `0x5D0D8F` is in `CAir::UpdateDaily`, `0x5D0443`, `0x5CA7CB` and `0x8ABBE8` are the rest. Nothing on this path frees anything: the queue is drained on the tick thread at the end of `RunHourlyTick`.

addresses.name: CGameState::RemoveUnit
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGameState::RemoveUnit(CGameState* this, CUnit* unit, bool arg2, bool arg3)
addresses.comment:
**A unit ceases to exist**, and this is where it is destroyed.

It unlinks the unit from everything holding it - its country's units, its province, its parent's Children in the order of battle, plans and orders, the interface's selection - takes its regiments off it through RemoveRegimentFromUnit, and then calls **the unit's own scalar deleting destructor**, `unit->vftable->vf_0(1)`. So the object is freed, not handed on.

Its callers are every place a unit is gone for good: a country capitulating or being annexed with units it cannot transfer, CDisbandCommand::Execute, and CUnit::RetreatFromCombat finding nowhere to retreat to.

`ret 0xC`, so three stack arguments past the receiver; what the two flags mean has not been established.

addresses.name: CGameState::GetLocalPlayer
addresses.comment: `ret 4`. Walks the player list at `state+0x60`, chained on `+0x54`, matching each entry's `+0x1C` against `in_game_screen (+0xBE8)` slot 18's `+0x6C`, and falls back to `state+0x70` when nothing matches. **Its `+0x38` is the array of five AI-delegation flags** the two minister-creation functions index, and `+0x30` is the four-way setting that seeds the tech minister's two bytes. Two callers, both in the AI. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CGameState::ClearPlayers
addresses.comment:
0x685F40..0x685FAC, bare `ret`, `this` in ESI and no arguments. Calls 0x2799B0 on `&this->+0x60` (the player list), writes 0 over every entry of the played-countries vector (+0xBCC..+0xBD0), and sets player (+0xC30) to the null tag `---` with its id (+0xC34) to 0. The name is inference from exactly those three effects. **TRAP 2**: only three int3 separate its `ret` from MarkSimulatedProvinces at 0x285FB0, so a padding scan that wants five or more bytes runs the two functions together.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation.

addresses.name: MarkSimulatedProvinces
addresses.comment: void MarkSimulatedProvinces(CCurrentGameState* state@[ebp+8], CScenario* scenario@[ebp+0xC]). Sets CProvinceTemplate +0x13D on every province in state+0xB8C to (scenario == 0) at 0x28600F, and then, when a scenario was given, back to 1 for each province id in its provinces vector (+0x98/+0x9C, the key CScenario::LoadKey 0x5E990 fills for save token 0x1DC) at 0x286062. Nine callers, all beside an install of g_CCurrentGameState. So +0x13D is the per-province simulation switch: on everywhere in an ordinary campaign, restricted to the scenario's own province list in a scenario.

addresses.name: MarkSimulatedProvinces_StoreScenario
addresses.comment: `mov dword ptr [eax + 0xD0C], ecx` at the tail of MarkSimulatedProvinces (0x285FB0) - `eax` the game state from [ebp+8], `ecx` the scenario from [ebp+0xC]. **The only instruction in the image that writes CCurrentGameState +0xD0C scenario** (the other two hits on that displacement are CGameState::CGameState zeroing it at 0x27D535 and 0x4C964D, which is another class). So the field is a pure function of who calls MarkSimulatedProvinces and with what: the session reset passes 0, CGameState::LoadKey passes 0, the savegame loader passes whatever 0x45E690 resolved from the save's `scenario` name, and of the six lobby callers five pass 0 and only 0x30FBDE passes a value. This extends the existing comment on 0x285FB0, which describes only its effect on CProvinceTemplate +0x13D. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 8.

addresses.name: CGameState::AssignHumanControllers
addresses.comment: 0x6868F0..0x686B2F, `ret 4`, one stack argument. Walks the country vector (+0xBBC), and for each country whose tag id (+0xCA8) is non-zero matches it against the player list at state+0x60 (entries chained on +0x54, the tag at +0x20 and its id at +0x24); on a match it writes the country's slot in the played-countries vector (+0xBCC) and logs gamestate.cpp:2929 `Human controller set for `. Called from CFrontEnd::LaunchGame, so it is part of session setup rather than of the game state's own lifecycle. The name is inference from the log line and the writes.

addresses.name: FindRebelFactionByObjectId
addresses.comment: The other rebel-faction lookup: over the factions at CCurrentGameState +0xC7C and, inside each, the list at +0x80 (next at +0xC), matching the node's object id pair at +0x0/+0x4 against the argument's +0x10/+0x14. This is the function the CUnit::RetreatFromCombat comment already refers to as 0x286C10. Game state in eax, ret 4. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: FindRebelFactionForProvince
addresses.signature: void* __fastcall FindRebelFactionForProvince(CCurrentGameState* state@EAX, CMapProvince* province@stack:4, void* rebelType@stack:8)
addresses.comment: Walks the rebel factions at CCurrentGameState +0xC7C and answers the one whose type (+0x30) is the wanted CRebelType*; when that type's independence (+0x190) is non-zero it also requires the area 0x4BF6F0 computes from the faction's +0x44/+0x48 to match the province. So **one faction per (rebel type, area)**, and a nation-wide type shares a single faction. Game state in eax, ret 8. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: RunDailySupplyPass
addresses.comment: Builds the four per-province arrays CSupply::DailySupplyPass takes and calls it. Returns at once when CCurrentGameState::arcade_mode (+0xC9C) is above zero. Allocates four count*4 arrays on the stack (count = (provinces_end - provinces_begin)/4), memsets them to zero, and for every province whose CProvinceTemplate +0x13D is set fills capacity from SupplyCapacity, supplies and fuel need from SupplyNeed and the per-step loss from SupplyLoss. The loop keeps a moving pointer into the fuel-need array in edi - which is also SupplyNeed's second out parameter - and reaches the other three arrays through precomputed deltas off it. One caller, 0x282D7E inside RunDailyPass (0x282C20), which takes the game state as its own argument. Not 0x282630, which an earlier reading of this said: that is the tick's hourly pass and it ends at 0x282C1D with `ret 4`, so the two are separate functions and this one runs only on a day change. Named for what it does; no class, like SupplyCapacity, SupplyNeed and SupplyLoss beside it.

addresses.name: CSupply::DailySupplyPass
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::DailySupplyPass(CCurrentGameState* state, int* capacity, int* fuelNeed, int* supplyNeed, int* stepLoss)
addresses.comment:
The daily supply distribution, for Normal (non-arcade) games only: both callers skip it when CCurrentGameState::arcade_mode (+0xC9C) is above zero, the same switch CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel takes its arcade branch on. Five stack arguments, `ret 0x14`, no `this`; the four arrays are one entry per province id, _alloca'd and zeroed by the caller and filled only for provinces whose CProvinceTemplate +0x13D is set - `capacity` from SupplyCapacity (0x9DD00), `supplyNeed` and `fuelNeed` from SupplyNeed (0x9E020), `stepLoss` from SupplyLoss (0x9DE80).

It sweeps CCurrentGameState::provinces_by_supply_order (+0x54) forward to pull supply inwards and backward to push surplus home. Two provinces are on the same network exactly when supply_depot_id (+0x48) matches; the pass only ever compares that field for equality, so it is the network label, and supply_depot_distance (+0x4C) is the hop count, 0 at the depot. A neighbour only counts when it carries the same depot id and is strictly closer.

**Phase 1** (0x2872F0): for every flagged province, swap drawn_ptr with last_drawn_ptr and throughput_ptr with last_throughput_ptr, zero today's drawn and throughput and zero `need`. So last_drawn/last_throughput are yesterday's, which phase 2 reads.

**Phase 2** (0x2874D2), forward: SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS is read once through the inlined GetDefines() as defines->supply(+0x3C)/1000, floored at 1 - 35. A province that is its controller's acting capital (CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation) is skipped but for copying pool into last_pool: the national stockpile is the end of the chain, not a link in it. For every other province: need.supplies = supplyNeed[id] and need.fuel = fuelNeed[id], each raised to 1000 when it is between 0 and 1000 and the matching pool good is under 5000; want = need*35 - pool; local = min(need, current_producing) is added to the unnamed CGoodsPool at CCountry +0xA1C (+0xA24/+0xA28) and subtracted from want; want is floored at 0, capped at need*2 and added to `drawn`. `drawn` then holds this province's own shortfall plus all the demand provinces farther out already pushed on to it. One step's stepLoss[id] is added to the demand carried to the neighbours and taken off again on delivery.

Then three sweeps over the template's ProvinceEdge vector (+0x90..+0x94, stride 20, neighbour id at +4), each considering only same-network, strictly-closer neighbours. (1) Take goods: available = min(neighbour->last_pool, capacity[nid]), scaled by this province's share of yesterday's demand where the neighbour's last_drawn exceeded its last_throughput (congestion rationing, capped at 1), then capped by the neighbour's current pool; the take is added to the neighbour's drawn and throughput, taken off its pool, and `max(take - stepLoss[id], 0)` added to this province's pool - and where the neighbour is a capital, to CCountry::usage. (2) Split what is still wanted evenly over the qualifying neighbours, each share capped by that neighbour's capacity minus its drawn, into its `drawn`. (3) Dump anything still unmet into each closer neighbour's drawn, capped at capacity[nid]. Sweeps 2 and 3 move demand, not goods, which is what the farthest-first sort order is for. Then last_pool = pool, all seven goods.

**Phase 3** (0x287CD3), backward: the controller's acting capital is skipped where its distance is 0, and a province short of what was drawn from it in both supplies and fuel keeps everything. Otherwise surplus = pool - (need*35 + drawn). At a depot (distance 0) the surplus is shipped to the controller's acting capital province, limited by the sum over the province's convoys (CMapProvince +0x38..+0x3C, counting only those that end here and start in the capital's `area`) of NavalBaseCapacity(province) * CConvoy::GetEfficiency / 1000, capped by NavalBaseCapacity itself, and recorded in CCountry::sent_back. Anywhere else the whole surplus goes to the first neighbour found on the same network and closer to the depot, with no capacity limit.

So `drawn` is what was asked of a province today and `throughput` is what actually moved through it, and phase 2 rations next day's takers by exactly that ratio. **No supply is produced here**: current_producing only reduces what has to be fetched, and every increase to a pool is a transfer out of another pool.

addresses.name: ClearIntelFunctor_SerialBody
addresses.comment: The per-element body ClearIntelFunctor's start_for::execute calls at 0x68F241, with the range in **EAX** and the functor pushed. It iterates the **province** vector, not countries: `prov = functor->provinces[i]`, then `memset(prov->+0x370, [0x170AD30] ? 0 : 9, prov->+0x374)` through 0xB99220 - and +0x370/+0x374 is the per-country intel array and its length that FINDINGS-mapmode.md names, with 9 the level a country has on its own provinces. It then zeroes `prov->+0xD4->+0x278`, sets `+0x13C` to 1, and writes a flag into the 12-byte-per-province scratch array the launcher alloca'd (functor +0x4). What prov+0xD4 is was not established. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: UpdateIntelFunctor_SerialBody
addresses.comment: The per-element body UpdateIntelFunctor's start_for::execute calls, range in **ECX**. Also iterates the **province** vector: gates on `prov->+0xD4->+0x13D`, reads the province's owner (+0x334) and controller (+0x338), compares the controller id against the functor's +0x10 and resolves tags through 0x402610. **Read only to 0x688480**; what it writes back into a province's intel array at +0x370 is not established, so 'it recomputes what ClearIntel wiped' is inference from the pairing and the names. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: RunIntelRefresh
addresses.comment:
**Both intel fan-outs are launched from this one function**, which settles the period `FINDINGS-tick.md` and `FINDINGS-aisched.md` left open. It runs `0x688D40` to `ret 4` at `0x689303` - one body, no `ret` in between, so `image.functionStart(0x689278)` answering `0x689201` is a mis-walk - and inside it:

    0x688DD8  SpawnClearIntelParallelForOuter   -> ClearIntelFunctor
    0x689278  SpawnUpdateIntelParallelForOuter  -> UpdateIntelFunctor

Six callers. Two are on the tick and neither is inside a TBB functor: `0x683056`, the second-to-last call in `RunDailyPass`, **unconditional, once a game day**; and `0x6822C3` in `RunHourlyTick` through the wrapper `RunIntelRefreshIfRequested`, at the end of **any hour in which a refresh has been requested**. The other four are one-offs: `ApplyCustomGameSettings` (`0x41D8EA`), `0x66042A`, `RefreshAllCountries` (`0x683EC9`) and `CNudgeIdler` slot 3 (`0x69DDB3`).

So the launch point is always the **tick thread**, and the per-element intel work (`0x688170` and `0x6883B0`) is always on **TBB workers**. Between the two launches it also walks the province vector `state+0xB8C` and the country vector `state+0xBBC`, and sets the byte at `0x1A857BF` around them the way the other fan-out sites do.

addresses.name: RunIntelRefreshIfRequested
addresses.comment: Ten instructions, one caller: `RunHourlyTick` at `0x6822C3`, with `eax = state + 0xCF8` and the state pushed. It calls `RunIntelRefresh` only when that list holds at least one entry (`cmp dword [eax+8], 1; jl` at `0x689319`) **and** the head node's value is `-1`. Neither it nor `RunIntelRefresh` consumes the list, so once a `-1` is queued the hourly refresh keeps happening. The one writer found is `CSetCountryControllerCommand` slot 6, which allocates a 0x10-byte node holding `-1` at `0x6D3887`; what a value other than `-1` would mean is not established.

addresses.name: CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder
addresses.comment: Refills provinces_by_supply_order (+0x54) from the province vector (+0xB8C..+0xB90), one pointer per province in province-id order. The whole body is a single copy loop. Called at 0x282CF8 immediately before the qsort at 0x282D18 that puts the array in farthest-from-depot order, and at 0x27E537 right after +0x54's storage is allocated at 0x27E52A as count*4 bytes.

addresses.name: CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork
addresses.comment: Recomputes every province's supply_depot_distance. Clears the dirty flag at CCurrentGameState +0x50, then sweeps the province vector: supply_depot_hops (+0x50) is zeroed, and supply_depot_distance (+0x4C) is set to 100000 where the province already carries a depot label and its template's +0x13D is set, and to 0 otherwise. A second sweep calls CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0) for every province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id - that is what makes a province a depot. It never writes supply_depot_id; that is CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). Reached from CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25C611, after the loop there has given every unlabelled province a depot, and from both passes of the tick, each guarded on CCurrentGameState +0x50: the hourly pass (0x282630) at 0x2826E8 and RunDailyPass (0x282C20) at 0x282CEF. Those are two functions, not one - 0x282630 ends at 0x282C1D with `ret 4` - so the network is rebuilt on the hour when it is dirty, while everything else the daily pass does to it happens only on a day change.

addresses.name: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::SpreadFromDepot(CCurrentGameState* state@stack:4, int depot@stack:8, int depotIndex@EDX)
addresses.comment: The distance relaxation, one depot at a time. Sets the depot's own supply_depot_distance to 0, then works a FIFO queue of 0x10-byte nodes over the template's ProvinceEdge vector (+0x90..+0x94, stride 0x14, neighbour id at edge+4). A neighbour is considered only if its template's +0x13D is set and its supply_depot_id already equals `depot` - the label partitions the map and this only fills in distances inside one partition. The step cost is infrastructure-weighted, not a hop: infra = provinceModifier[MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE] * (1000 + [MODIFIER_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE] + [MODIFIER_GLOBAL_INFRASTRUCTURE]) / 1000, clamped below by a lazily computed constant at rva 0x17EA400 (from the float 10.5 at rva 0x120A680) and above by 1000; then step = max(4000 - 4*infra, 1000) / 1000, an integer 1, 2 or 3 - the lower clamp keeps 4000 - 4*infra at or under 3960, so 4 is out of reach - multiplied by the neighbour's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. Since a province that improves is pushed back on the queue (the node at 0x689DAA, right after the write at 0x689DA4), this is Bellman-Ford by queue and the distances it leaves are true minima. The neighbour is relaxed only when its current distance is strictly greater, and it then also gets supply_depot_hops = parent's hops + 1. The queue is a CList by value on the stack - three dwords and a byte cleared together at 0x689C0F - and its nodes are CListNode<CMapProvince*>; the `locals` on this record are what make the body read in terms of the province rather than `*(iVar3 + 0x4c)`.

locals.name: frontier
locals.comment: head of the queue of provinces still to relax

locals.name: frontierTail
locals.comment: last node, so a push can link onto it

locals.name: frontierCount
locals.comment: how many are queued; the loop runs until it reaches zero

addresses.name: CGameState_AddAlliedObjective
addresses.comment: 0x68AD20-0x68B26D, `ret 0x10`. Records "country `countryId` is asked by `requesterId` to take province `province`" in **both** halves of the allied-objective index: it find-or-creates a 0x14-byte record keyed on the province in `state->+0xB9C[countryId]` and appends `requesterId` to that record's int vector (begin +4, end +8), then does the mirror image in `state->+0xBAC[requesterId]`, appending `countryId`. Appending is idempotent - a requester already in the list is skipped (the flag at [ebp-0xD]). Two callers: `CSetAlliedObjectiveCommand::Execute` (0x553CD0) when the command's `active` byte is set, and `CGameState::LoadKey`'s `allied_objectives` arm (0x6809BF), which walks the saved int list three at a time. The argument order is the loader's: it passes (v[i], v[i+2], v[i+1]) against a writer that pushed province, requester, country.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CGameState_AddAlliedObjective(CGameState* state, int province, int countryId, int requesterId)

addresses.name: CGameState_RemoveAlliedObjective
addresses.comment: 0x68B270-0x68B4BD, `ret 0x10`. The exact inverse of CGameState_AddAlliedObjective: finds the record for `province` in `state->+0xB9C[countryId]` and drops `requesterId` from its int vector, then the same in the mirror `state->+0xBAC[requesterId]` for `countryId`. One caller: `CSetAlliedObjectiveCommand::Execute` at 0x553D64, the branch taken when the command's `active` byte at +0x50 is clear. Abuts CGameState_AddAlliedObjective with no padding - trap 2.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CGameState_RemoveAlliedObjective(CGameState* state, int province, int countryId, int requesterId)

addresses.name: CGameState_ClearAlliedObjectivesForCountry
addresses.comment: 0x68B4C0-0x68B7BF, `ret 8`. Empties both `state->+0xB9C[countryId]` and `state->+0xBAC[countryId]`, then walks every other country's `+0xB9C` entry and removes `countryId` from each record's requester vector. One caller: `CFaction::RemoveMember` at 0x5227C3 - leaving a faction cancels every allied objective in either direction. It is also the clearest proof that the index of the outer vector is a country id and that the inner int vectors hold country ids.

addresses.name: ConcurrentQueue_MicroQueuePush
addresses.comment: `tbb::strict_ppl::internal::micro_queue::push(item, ticket, base)` - the four-argument push that every enqueue path shares. Four callers, all pushing a `{id_type, id}` pair onto `CCurrentGameState +0xBF4`: `0x501099`, `CheckTransportOverload` at `0x5CFD72`, `CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval` at `0x684CD1`, and `CRemoveBrigadeEffect` slot 11 at `0x9BC11D`. Named for the container rather than the domain because it is a template body.

addresses.name: ConcurrentQueue_TryPop
addresses.comment:
**Not "deferred unit deletion" - it is `tbb::strict_ppl::concurrent_queue::internal_try_pop`.** `lock cmpxchg` to claim a ticket off the head counter at `queue->rep[0]`, then `0x68EA80` on the micro-queue at `rep + 0x180 + ((ticket * 3) & 7) * 0x50`; returns false when the head has reached the tail. `ret 8`.

`FINDINGS-tick.md` lists `0x28DB20` as the tick's ninth stage, "deferred unit deletion, through CGameState::RemoveUnit". The *stage* is that; this *function* is only the pop. The stage is the loop `0x682230`-`0x6822B7` in `RunHourlyTick`: while the queue at `CCurrentGameState +0xBF4` is non-empty, pop an id pair, look the object up in the database at `0x1A857F0` or `0x1A857F4` (chosen by `id_type <= 0x1268`) through `0xA9DA00`, `add eax, -8` to get from the `CReferenceObject` sub-object to the `CUnit`, and call `CGameState::RemoveUnit(state)(unit, 0, 1)`.

The name is deliberately not a domain name: this is a template body, and its other caller `0x68EBD7` is the queue's own clear helper (`0x68EBA0`). Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: SpawnProcessUnitParallelFor

Writes the start_for vftable 0x15CF6EC at 0x28E04E - the RTTI export names it `start_for<blocked_range<I>, ProcessUnitFunctor, auto_partitioner>` - copies the range in from EDI and the functor from the stack, and spawns the root task. One caller, RunHourlyPass at 0x282887, so it runs every game hour. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

One caller, RunHourlyPass at 0x2829DC - and RunHourlyPass sets the ai_pass_done latch immediately afterwards, at 0x2829E4. So AI *trade* is hourly and is a separate fan-out from the AI proper. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: SpawnProcessProvinceParallelFor
