addresses.name: SpawnProcessCountriesPreDailyUpdateParallelFor
addresses.comment: **This, not the AI, is what RunDailyPass fans out.** 0x28E350 to the bare `ret` at 0x28E429, then int3. Instruction-for-instruction identical to SpawnProcessAIParallelFor (0x28E430) except for the vftable it writes: `mov dword [esi], 0x15CF72C` at 0x28E3CE, and the RTTI export names 0x15CF72C `start_for<blocked_range<I>, ProcessCountriesPreDailyUpdate, auto_partitioner>`. That is how FINDINGS-tick.md came to credit this call with running the AI once a day; it does not. One caller, RunDailyPass at 0x282DDD, which pops the one stack argument itself (`add esp, 4`), so the range arrives in EDI and the functor on the stack. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: SpawnProcessAIParallelFor
addresses.comment: Builds the TBB root task for the AI: `task_group_context::init`, `allocate_root_with_context_proxy::allocate(0x18)`, writes the start_for vftable 0x15CF73C, copies the range and the functor in, asks `get_initial_auto_partitioner_divisor` for +0x14, and spawns it. Bare `ret`; the range arrives in EDI and the functor on the stack. One caller, CGameState::RunAIPass. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md. **__cdecl, not __stdcall**: the `ret` is bare and the caller cleans up with `add esp, 4` at 0x683113.

addresses.name: SpawnClearIntelParallelForOuter
addresses.comment: Wraps the ClearIntelFunctor fan-out: calls SpawnClearIntelParallelFor (0x28E800) at 0x28E598. Bare `ret`, so the caller pops - and its one call site, 0x288DD8, does `lea ecx, [ebp-0x6C]` over a three-dword range {end, 0, grain} and `push eax` with the functor, which is where the convention comes from. **0x28E510 ends with a bare `ret` at 0x28E5DF and 0x28E5E0 begins a fresh function with no int3 padding at all** - own prologue `push ebp; mov ebp, esp; and esp, -8` and own SEH push 0xC1183D - and 0x28E6B0 abuts that one in turn; a scan to the next int3 swallows all three. 0x288DD8 is inside 0x288D40, and RunDailyPass calls 0x288D40 last (0x283056), so intel is cleared at least once a day on worker threads. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: SpawnUpdateIntelParallelForOuter
addresses.comment: The twin of 0x28E510 for UpdateIntelFunctor: it calls SpawnUpdateIntelParallelFor (0x28E870) at 0x28E668. 0x28E5E0 to the bare `ret` at 0x28E6AF, with **no padding on either side** - 0x28E510 abuts it above and 0x28E6B0 (a `ret 0x10` function) below. One caller, 0x289278, which sets up the range in ECX the same way and cleans up with `add esp, 4` at 0x28927D. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: SpawnClearIntelParallelFor

Writes the start_for vftable 0x15CF74C at 0x28E82A - the RTTI export names it `start_for<blocked_range<I>, ClearIntelFunctor, auto_partitioner>`. Unlike the six tick fan-outs this one ends `ret 8`, so it takes two stack arguments; which is which is not established. One caller, 0x28E598. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

Its serial body calls 0x1B9C50 per element. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.comment: Slot 1 of vftable 0x15CF72C, named verbatim in the RTTI export. 0x28EF80 to the `ret` at 0x28F077, then int3. Splits its range and allocates a child start_for of its own type - the `mov dword [eax], 0x15CF72C` at 0x28EFFF, which is the *second* reference to that vftable and not a second launch site. The serial body at 0x28F04D is `for (i = begin; i < end; ++i) { c = vec[i]; if (c[+0x44]) { 0x1033B0(c); CCountry::RebuildNeighbours(c); } }` over the country vector at CCurrentGameState +0xBBC. So each country's neighbour sets are rebuilt once a day, on TBB worker threads. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: ProcessAIFunctor_start_for::execute
addresses.comment: **The AI runs on TBB worker threads, and this is the proof.** The RTTI export names the class verbatim: `tbb::internal::start_for<blocked_range<...>, ProcessAIFunctor, auto_partitioner>`, vftable 0x15CF73C. It halves its range and allocates a continuation plus a child task while the range exceeds the grain at `+0xC`, and otherwise runs the serial body at 0x68F14D: `for (i = begin; i < end; ++i) ProcessAI(functor->vec[i])`. So ProcessAI is re-entered concurrently for different countries - any hook on it or on a minister tick must be thread-safe. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: UpdateIntelFunctor_start_for::execute
addresses.comment: Slot 1 of vftable 0x15CF75C. 0x28F250 to the `ret` at 0x28F2FC, then int3. Its serial body calls 0x2883B0 per element. **Unlike the other seven, its child-task allocation is not inside this function**: the second write of 0x15CF75C is at 0x28F684, inside 0x28F510, and why the split exists is not established. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

addresses.name: RunLoopCallsScreenUpdateSlot
addresses.comment:
`call eax` with eax = `[[app->+0x84]] + 4` - **slot 1 of the current screen**, loaded at 0x291397/0x291399. While the in-game screen is current this is CInGameIdler::Update (0x2559D0).

This is the only way Update is reached: image.findValue(0x6559D0) returns ZERO hits in .text - it has no direct callers anywhere in the image - and exactly one in .rdata, at 0x15CEB58, which is CInGameIdler's vftable 0x15CEB54 + 4. One holder, so trap 4 is discharged too. Slot 1 differs per class (CFrontEnd 0x2EDD60, CBackEndIdler 0x208AF0), so the slot identifies which Update runs. project.json's comment on CEU3Application::Run gives 0x29138D, which is where the screen pointer is loaded; the call is here. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 4.

addresses.name: RunLoopCallsOutgoingScreenLeave
addresses.comment:
`call eax` with eax = `[[app->+0x84]] + 0x10` - **slot 4 of the OUTGOING screen**, and the first thing the pending-screen swap at 0x2913A0 does. For the in-game screen that is CInGameIdler::Leave (slot 4 = 0x262060; padding ends at 0x26205F and retsBefore(0x662060, 0x662340) is empty, so its in_game clear at 0x262337 is inside it); for the frontend it is 0x2F0140.

**This is the control that settles whether a reset game state can ever be seen with in_game set.** Between Update's slot-1 call returning at 0x2913A0 and this call there are four instructions and no call at all, so no frame can be presented in between - whatever the screen's Update did to the game state, and whichever arm of 0x254760 it took. It also runs *before* the swap reads app->+0xE0 at 0x2913BE, which is why a null pending screen still gets the byte cleared. CEU3Application::Run's existing comment lists the swap's calls to the INCOMING screen's slots 2, 3 and 5 but not this one. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 4.

addresses.name: GetMessageHandler
addresses.comment:
**The one message handler**, made on first use and kept at `0x1689A8C`. Takes nothing and ends in a bare `ret`.

Worth knowing because CCountry::ShatterUnit calls it in the **middle of pushing another call's arguments**, which reads like an eight argument call and is not. Mistaking it for one is what made the message system look far harder than it is.

addresses.name: LoadMessageTypes
addresses.comment: Reads `interface/messagetypes.txt` (call at 0x637376) and then `messagetypes_custom.txt` (0x637484), both on GetMessageHandler's object (0x698E80, already in the record - the independent confirmation). Extent 0x698EE0..0x6991E6, `ret 8`, two exits. These two run after governments.txt and before the phase-1 `Loading Databases <` timer, so the message types are the last thing in phase 1 and neither file is in the common/ list.

addresses.name: CMessageHandler::FindType
addresses.comment:
**A message type by name.** Forwards to the lookup at 0x299AC0 - the handler into eax, the name as a stack argument - and calls it a second time on the way out, which is what its result comes from.

**A name the registry does not hold is not a crash**: it logs `Failed to find message type: <name>` from messagehandler.cpp and returns null. That is the whole cost of a misspelt or undeclared type, and it is what makes raising a mod-declared type safe to try.

addresses.name: CMessageHandler::LookupType
addresses.comment: The search itself, under CMessageHandler::FindType. **The handler arrives in eax** and the name is the one stack argument; `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CMessage::CMessage
addresses.no_signature: Twelve arguments of which several are only passed on, and two are a reserved eight bytes rather than pushes. Writing it out would type four things as ints that have not been identified; the order is in the comment, which is what a caller needs.
addresses.comment:
**Builds a message**, into the 0x80 buffer its first argument points at. Twelve arguments, `ret 0x30`, in the order CCountry::ShatterUnit pushes them:

    1  the buffer to build into
    2  the type, from CMessageHandler::FindType   -> +0x20
    3  the variable list, which it walks and releases
    4  the province                                -> +0x44
    5  a head string, which CCountry::ShatterUnit passes **empty**
    6  zero                                        -> +0x70
    7,8   the game state's player tag and id       -> +0x34, +0x38
    9,10  the country's +0xCA4 and +0xCA8          -> +0x3C, +0x40
    11,12 two zeroes                               -> +0x68, +0x6C

Arguments 11 and 12 are not pushed: they are eight bytes reserved below the ten that are. The body is a plain field setter.

addresses.name: CTopBar::BuildTooltip

addresses.name: CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute
addresses.comment:
Slot 6 of `CSetGamePlayOptions` - the command's own **Execute** (see `CCommand::Execute`), and **the only thing in the image that writes either gameplay option**:

    gamestate->difficulty   = this->options[0]          // +0xC98
    if (this->options.size() >= 2)
        gamestate->arcade_mode = this->options[1]        // +0xC9C

The vector it carries is at `+0x3C`/`+0x40` and is what `CSetGamePlayOptions::LoadKey` (`0x2D5EC0`) fills from the save's `setgameplayoptions` key; the save writes it back under token `0x60D` at `0x2D5E90`. It ends by touching the globals at `0x171042C`/`0x1710430` and `0x1A857F0`/`0x1A857F4`, which was not followed up.

addresses.name: CHourlyTickCommand::Construct
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, so both the object and its second argument come off the stack rather than ecx - called from CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock at 0x281214 with the freshly allocated 0x4C bytes and **a pointer to the game state's +0xC58**, the vector SnapshotRandomState refills every hour. addresses.name: CHourlyTickCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: **Slot 6, and the whole tick hangs off it.** Ends 0x2DA41D with a bare `ret`. It first makes sure the CCurrentGameState singleton at 0x1A89790 exists - newing a 0xDA8-byte one with vftable 0x15CF674 and destroying any previous - then calls RunHourlyTick (0x2813F0) with that state and this command's payload at `this+0x3C`. So **the game clock runs through the command queue** like any other order. See reversing/FINDINGS-tick.md.

addresses.name: PopulateCountryInfoPanel
addresses.comment: Recorded for its **boundary**, which is what made FINDINGS-survivors.md's last open item hard. Extent 0x784E30..0x78524F, bare `ret`, no stack arguments, receiver in ECX (`mov edi,ecx`). The `ret` at 0x784EE1 is an early exit returning false (`xor al,al`) with the body continuing past it - trap 3 - and the jump at 0x784EC9 to 0x784EE2 is inside this function, not across a boundary. It pushes 'country_info' (0x15CBA90) and 'country_flag' (0x15BC960) and makes two virtual calls off a member at +0xA8. Three callers: 0x78314B, 0x784B4F, 0x78DDAB. **`functionStart` answers this address for anything up to 0x785432**, because the next function abuts it; use retsBefore. The name is BiceLib's and is a guess from the two string literals. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.name: BuildFactionIntentionTooltip
addresses.comment:
**The one caller of CAlignment::BuildDriftTooltip, and the answer to FINDINGS-survivors.md's open item about it.** `functionStart(0x7853FE)` answers 0x784E30; it is wrong. 0x784E30 is a separate `bool __thiscall(this)` running 0x784E30..0x78524F, and this function begins at 0x785250 with a fresh `push ebp` **immediately after** that bare `ret`, with no padding - trap 2, second failure mode. Three independent signals: the two bodies push different SEH scope tables (0xC2CA2C against 0xC77C0C), they have different `ret` immediates (bare against `ret 4`), which one MSVC function cannot, and they return different widths (al against eax).

Shape: receiver in ECX and used as a CCountryTag (`mov ecx,edi; call CCountryTag::GetCountry` at 0x7853F3), the 0x5C GuiTooltipText out at [ebp+8], `ret 4`, answers out. It initialises the out record itself at 0x785278..0x7852A4.

Its one caller is 0x7801F0, inside **CDiplomacyView slot 10** (0x37F490) - the faction column. It chooses between two texts: `0x78F900` true gives LEAVE_FACTION_INTENTION, false asks `0x78F790` for the country's faction and **a null answer is what produces the alignment-drift tooltip**. So the drift tooltip is what a country with no faction shows. The receiver's exact class is `inferred`. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

addresses.comment: 0x7C3510..0x7C5C0C, `ret 4`, receiver in ECX. 66 localisation keys - the most of any game function in the image - and **not one number**. Every arm is `mov edx,[esi]; mov eax,[edx+0x44]; call eax` (slot 17, the window's current sort column name), a string compare against a `ledger_sort_*` literal, and on a match the matching BUILD_*_IRO or _DRO key. addresses.name: DoNothing_4Args

addresses.comment: `ret 0x10` and nothing else, so the linker folded it: this one address fills a virtual slot in 38 unrelated classes and belongs to none of them. It was recorded as LogSink::WriteNothing, which is one of the 38 - the fallback sink's slot 1 does point here, but so does everything else that needed a four argument no-op. Slot 1 of the **fallback** sink's vftable (rva `0x11FCEA0`, VA `0x015FCEA0`), and it is `ret 0x10` and nothing else. That sink is the one `0x2410` makes if the global is still null, so a message logged before the real sink is installed is discarded outright rather than queued. **The body is not the fallback sink's own** - the linker folded it with every other four-argument do-nothing virtual in the program, and it sits in 38 RTTI classes' tables.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CreateMinisters
addresses.comment: **Creates or destroys the five ministers, and the whole AI-delegation rule is here.** Bare `ret`, one caller: the tail of CEU3AI::CEU3AI at 0x888566. For each ministry: return outright when `gamestate[+0xD0C] != 0`; create unconditionally when this is not the played country (`this[+0x24] != gamestate[+0xC34]`); and when it is, create only when `GetLocalPlayer()[+0x38][n] == 1`, else destroy. So **an AI country always has all five, and the human's country has only the ones delegated**. Order: flags[0] foreign +0x60, [1] production +0x64, [2] tech +0x6C, [3] politics +0x70, [4] espionage +0x68. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::ApplyPlayerDelegation

Same create/destroy body as CreateMinisters but without the is-this-the-player test: it always consults `GetLocalPlayer()[+0x38]`. It also writes the tech minister's two bytes +0x5C/+0x5D from a four-way switch on `GetLocalPlayer()[+0x30]`. Four callers, all UI: 0x2EBF00 is slot 13 of CCountryView, CDiplomacyView, CEspionageView, CPoliticsView, CProductionView and CTheatreView; 0x422290 and 0x422600 are CTechnologyView slots 12 and 13. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: ProcessAI
addresses.comment: **One country's whole AI pass, and the one hook for the entire AI.** `ret 4` at 0x889BB5, then int3. Bails on `ai[+0x128]` and on `country[+0x580]`; calls 0x89A800 and 0x889E10; bails through 0x899A10 when the country-database record at `g_CCountryDataBase[+0x16C][ai->id]` has `+0xCF8 <= 0` and `+0x95 == 0`; then walks the agent list at `ai+0x74` on `+8` and calls slot 9 on every agent whose `+0x3C` byte is set; then 0x89E010 on the foreign minister. Four callers, and **the recurring one is a tbb::parallel_for** - see reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md for which thread.

addresses.name: ProcessAI_TheatreReadinessGate
addresses.comment: `cmp byte [edi+0xa6], al` with al == 0 - the top of a block in ProcessAI (0x8897E8-0x889852) that runs only while CEU3AI +0xA6 is set. It walks `GetCountry(ai->tag)->+0x570` (read at 0x8897F7), resolves each theatre's `unit` id pair (CTheatre +0x74/+0x78) through 0xA9D390, and **bails back to the agent loops the moment one does not resolve**, leaving +0xA6 set to retry next hour. When every theatre has a live HQ unit it calls AnnounceLoadedUnitsToScreen(ai, ai->id == gamestate->+0xC34) at 0x88984D and clears +0xA6 at 0x889852. Worker thread - which means AnnounceLoadedUnitsToScreen reaches CCurrentGameState::in_game_screen off the tick thread.

addresses.name: ProcessAI_UpdateUnitAgents
addresses.comment: `mov edi, [edx+0x40]` inside ProcessAI (0x4894E0): the head of the CEU3AI's **unit-agent** list, walked through node `+8` calling each agent's slot 9 (`[vftable+0x24]`, CAIAgent::Update) at 0x489881. **This is the only recurring path that ticks a CAIUnit**, and it runs where ProcessAI runs - on a TBB worker thread, once per game hour. Unlike the minister loop at 0x4896C8 it does not test the agent's `+0x3C` byte itself; slot 9 does that through slot 8.

addresses.comment: `mov edi, [eax+0x50]` inside ProcessAI, immediately after the unit-agent loop: the head of the CEU3AI's **CAIInvasion** list, walked the same way through node `+8` calling slot 9 at 0x48989B. So ProcessAI ticks three agent families per country per hour: the ministers (+0x74), the unit agents (+0x40) and the invasion agents (+0x50).

addresses.name: CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea
addresses.comment: Three stack arguments. Walks the CEU3AI's unit-agent list at +0x40 looking for an agent whose GetArea (0x4BBAE0) already answers this area; where `flag` is clear it will also re-point an agent's `+0x68`/`+0x6C` at the area after a check through 0x46C310. If nothing covers the area and `this[+0x2C]` is set, it allocates 0x374, constructs a CAIUnit, writes the area's id pair into `+0x68`/`+0x6C`, **sets the dirty byte `+0x87 = 1`** so the next Tick re-anchors it, AddRefs, calls slot 52 (Enable) and push_backs onto +0x40/+0x44/+0x48. Four callers, all at 0x4ABAEF, 0x4ABC38, 0x4ABE8F and 0x4ABFAE.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForTheatres
addresses.comment: One stack argument. For each entry of the country's theatre list at **CCountry +0x570**, it walks the CEU3AI's own unit-agent list at +0x40, climbs each agent's `+0x40` parent chain to the root, asks the root's slot 65, resolves its `+0x68`/`+0x6C` id, and compares the resolved object against the theatre. If no agent's root is this theatre it allocates 0x374 bytes, constructs a CAIUnit, AddRefs it, push_backs it onto +0x40/+0x44/+0x48, copies the theatre's id pair `+0x8`/`+0xC` into the agent's `+0x68`/`+0x6C`, calls slot 52 (Enable) and then resolves the theatre's `unit` id pair (`+0x74`/`+0x78`) through 0xA9D390. Called once, from ProcessAI at 0x489A61 - so **on a TBB worker thread**.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits
addresses.comment: One stack argument. Walks the country's `units` list (CCountry +0xBAC) and for each unit **skips it unless its battle plan is switched on (CUnit +0x204) and it has no agent yet (CUnit +0x198 == 0)**. It then climbs `higher_oob_unit_ptr` (+0x1E0) while each ancestor's plan is also active, to find the topmost planned unit; allocates 0x374, constructs a CAIUnit, AddRefs it, and - only if the iterated unit's `oob_level` is 0 - fills `+0x68`/`+0x6C` from FindTheatreForUnit; then slot 52 (Enable), push_back onto the CEU3AI's +0x40 list, slot 63 (SetUnit) with the **topmost** planned unit, and slot 76. Called once, from ProcessAI at 0x4897D5, and gated there on the country being the **player's** (`ai->id == gamestate[+0xC34]`), on the AI having no unit agents yet (`ai[+0x48] == 0`) and on `gamestate[+0xD9C]` being set. So this is how a human player's delegated AI acquires agents from the plans he has drawn.

addresses.name: AnnounceLoadedUnitsToScreen
addresses.comment: **Tells the interface about a country's units**, which is the last thing CLoadOOBEffect::Execute does - and only when a scenario is running and the country is the **player's own**, so it is presentation rather than game state. It takes the thing at `CCountry + 0x1D8`, whose CCountryTag at `+0x20` gives it the country, walks that country's `units`, and for each one that passes a virtual test builds a 0x64 byte object and hands it to a virtual on `CCurrentGameState::in_game_screen`. **What `CCountry + 0x1D8` is has not been established**, nor which alert this raises. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances
addresses.comment:
**Where the AI actually picks a battle-plan stance.** 0x4912D0 to the two `ret 8` exits at 0x491BCA and 0x492182; one caller, **ProcessAI at 0x489B8F**, so it is worker-thread code. Returns at once when `force` is false and `ai->+0xA9` is clear (0x4912F3-0x491301).

It computes a value, clamps it to [0, 4] (0x491B46-0x491B52, with a 0.9 comparison at 0x491B3A feeding the decrement), and calls CAIUnit slot 77 - CAIUnit::SetPlanStance - through [vftable+0x134] at 0x491B89 **only when the value differs from the unit's current CUnit +0x208**. Since slot 77 recurses into the whole agent subtree, one call restances a whole theatre.

It also builds CSetPlanAttributesCommand directly at 0x4916AD with (unit, 5, 2, 2, -1000, -1000) - stance left alone, air and naval stance both set to 2.

The arithmetic that produces the 0-4 value was not read; the entry point, the clamp, the gate and the dispatch were.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion
addresses.comment: `ret 0xC`, 0x892190-0x893C70. **What makes the AI mount an invasion.** Two ProcessAI call sites: 0x889A39, once per unit agent in ai->+0x40 on the branch taken when the country *is* the player's and ai->+0x2C is clear and behind an `id & 1` parity test, and 0x889AB5 with agentOrNull = 0 on the ordinary AI-country branch. The decision: **at 0x892B9E it skips any candidate area that `AreaIsConnectedTo` (0x4B8DC0) says is joined overland to ours** - that is the amphibious test - requires CCountry::IsEnemy (0x42F210, two sites), scores areas by CountEnemyUnitsInArea (0x8A8EF0) and NavalBaseCapacity (0x4A75D0, three sites), sizes the force with CUnit::SupplyConsumption (four sites), SumTransportWeight (four sites) and CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation, and finally at 0x893AD7-0x893B5D: `if (transports.count >= 1 && SumTransportWeight(transports) >= required)` it allocates 0x94, constructs the CAIInvasion, push_backs onto ai->+0x50/+0x54/+0x58, calls slot 63 (AddUnit, [vft+0xFC]) over three gathered lists, then slot 7 (AddRef) and slot 52 (Enable, [vft+0xD0]). **Worker thread.**
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion(CEU3AI* ai, void* outList, CAIUnit* agentOrNull)

addresses.name: PlanAmphibiousInvasion_AddTransportNeed
addresses.comment: `agent->+0x36C += tonnageShort / (transport_ship->transport_capacity / 1000) + 1` - the writer of CAIUnit +0x36C, which the force planner adds straight onto its transport-ship want. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion clears both +0x36C and +0x370 at 0x492483/0x492489 when it is given an agent, so the pair is a per-planning-pass accumulator and not a running total.

addresses.name: PlanAmphibiousInvasion_AddBrigadeNeed
addresses.comment: `agent->+0x370 += (brigades wanted - brigades available)` - the writer of CAIUnit +0x370, which is the additive term in both force planners' brigade demand (`+0x370 + round(need * shortage * 3)` at 0x4B626D, `+0x370 + need * 3` at 0x4B528B).

addresses.name: CreateInvasionAgent
addresses.comment: `call 0x49F920` (CAIInvasion's constructor, which writes vftable 0x15EBAE4 at 0x49F936) followed by a push_back onto the CEU3AI's list at `+0x50`/`+0x54`/`+0x58`. **This is what settles CEU3AI +0x50..+0x58 as the invasion-agent list**, as against +0x40..+0x48 for the unit agents and +0x74..+0x7C for the ministers.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::EstimateProvinceDefence
addresses.comment: Body 0x893C80-0x893E6D, ret 8, answer in xmm0; 0x893E70 abuts it with no padding (trap 2, and image.functionStart(0x894184) answers 0x893C80 for exactly that reason). Sums over the province's units (+0x2B8), keeping only those whose CUnit slot 15 (IsLand) answers true and whose owner (+0x124) passes CCountry::IsEnemy(us@ESI, &owner@EDX, province@EDI): for each regiment in CUnit +0x38 it adds strength (CSubUnit +0x5C) divided by the max from slot 12, in thousandths, then /1000.0 - and divides that term by 3.0 when the regiment's definition's type_index equals g_CSubUnitDataBase->hq_brigade (+0x78) ->+0x24, so an HQ brigade counts for a third. The whole sum is then multiplied by (province->modifiers[11]/1000/5.0 + 1.0); CProvince +0x114 is the CModifierValues array at id*8 and id 11 is COASTAL_FORT_LEVEL per FINDINGS-combatmods.md, so each coastal fort level adds 20%. Both callers are in CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince (0x894184 against a neighbour, 0x894390 against the candidate) and nothing else calls it. Low is attractive. The name is from the body; the two scale constants 3.0 (0x160A4E8) and 5.0 (0x160A508) are .rdata literals, not defines.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince
addresses.comment: Two callers, both decisive. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion calls it at 0x8930C6 with invasionOrNull = 0 and uses the answer as the province it hands to the CAIInvasion constructor, reading the result's naval_base capacity (+0x300 then +0x20) immediately after. CAIInvasion stage 3 calls it at 0x8A1154 with the objective's own area, stores the answer back into +0x84 and issues the 0x3A5 `invasion` order on it. This - not 0x49FBC0 - is the function that chooses where the troops come ashore. Its body was not read. **Trap 2**: it abuts the function at 0x893C80, which ends `ret 8` at 0x893E6D with no int3 between, so image.functionStart(0x893E70) answers 0x893C80. 0x893E70 has its own prologue and SEH push, so it is a real entry; add 0x893C80/0x893E70 to TRAPS.md's known-pairs list.
addresses.signature: CProvince* __stdcall CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince(CEU3AI* ai, COwnerArea* area, CAIInvasion* invasionOrNull)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::PickNearestInvadableNeighbourProvince
addresses.comment: Body 0x894A70-0x894C29 (ret 8) with a second exit at 0x894C34 returning null, int3 run at 0x894C37. Walks `from`->area->neighbour_areas (COwnerArea +0x34); for each area it takes the controller tag off the area's first province, skips the area when that is us, and requires the pair to be at war, or REB on either side, or UndeclaredWarCoversProvince (0x4763A0) - the same cascade CCountry::IsEnemy uses. Inside a surviving area it scores every province whose CProvinceTemplate +0xA4 (sea_province_id) is at least 1 by `0x4A5570(province, from->id)/1000 + 34.0 * CountEnemyLandUnitsInList(&province->units, ourTag)` and keeps the minimum, initialising the running best to the 1000000.0f at 0x160A598. Its two callers are CAIInvasion stage 3 (0x8A09B0), which only tests the answer for null before deciding between an `invasion` and a `transport` order, and 0x8A11B0. The 34.0 is the same .rdata literal (0x160A968) PickInvasionLandingProvince uses.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::AbandonInvasionArea
addresses.comment: Called from exactly one place in this work: CAIInvasion stage 3 at 0x8A116A, when PickInvasionLandingProvince returns null for the objective's area, immediately before `+0x3E = 1` kills the agent. The receiver is in ESI and the area is the one stack argument. The name is from that use alone; the body was not read.

addresses.name: AreaMayWidenFrontSearch
addresses.signature: bool __cdecl AreaMayWidenFrontSearch(CCountry* us, COwnerArea* area, bool* outIsOwnFocusArea, bool acceptAnyUnplayed)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces
addresses.comment: One direct caller: ProcessAI at 0x489A93, immediately before its call to CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives at 0x489AA8. Its first act (0x497703-0x497731) is to free every node of the list at `ai->+0x118` and zero head, tail and count, and it appends 0x10-byte `{provinceId, prev, next, byte}` nodes back onto it at 0x4979D5/0x4979F9 - so **`CEU3AI +0x118` is per-hour scratch, rebuilt from nothing every AI pass**, which is what makes the flat +100 it contributes to an objective's priority recomputed rather than persistent. It reaches the owner's country through `CCountryTag::GetCountry(&ai->+0x20)` and walks that country's faction (CCountry +0xD8) member list at CFaction +0x28, keeping members whose country id is not `ai->+0x24` and whose `CCountry +0xACC` byte is set; the province ids themselves come out of a per-index vector on CGameState +0xBAC and **where they come from was not established**. The name is from what it does to +0x118 and is not recovered. Note the body also contains the inlined lazy `GetCurrentGameState()` (new 0xDA8, CGameState::CGameState, vftable 0x11CF674, swap into g_CCurrentGameState) - that is the singleton accessor, not a game state being built by the AI.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives
addresses.comment:
**The only place in the image that computes a CObjective's `priority`** (the other non-copying writer, CTogglePlanObjectiveCommand::Execute, uses a constant). `ret 4`, one caller: **ProcessAI at 0x489AA8**, so it runs on a TBB worker thread once per game hour with the rest of the AI pass.

For each unit agent on ai->+0x40 whose slot 74 answers a unit and whose CAIUnit::GetArea resolves, and whose theatre is `hot` (CTheatre +0x70), it walks that theatre's fronts and their provinces' adjacencies. For each candidate province:

    priority  = province->victory_points (CMapProvince +0x34) * 20          0x49844C
    priority += the matching entry's +0xC from CCountry +0x4A8, if listed    0x4984A0
    priority += 100 if the province id is in CEU3AI +0x118                  0x4984A5
    drop the province if priority < 1                                       0x4984AC
    drop it if any other unit agent's theatre is nearer to it, by
      CAIUnit::DistanceToTheatreFronts (0xB08C0)                            0x4985F3

The survivors become CObjectives (vftable written at 0x498648) with `hold = 0` and `invasion` from a local, and the list is handed to CSetPlanObjectivesCommand (0x1E68B0) at 0x498767.

**So priority is a raw integer of about 0-1000, not thousandths**: 20 per victory point plus two additive terms. The interface writes 400 for a hand-placed objective. Nothing divides it by 1000 anywhere.

addresses.name: AIObjectives_ComparePriority
addresses.comment: `mov ecx, [ecx+0xC]` followed by `cmp ecx, [esi+0xC]` at 0x49871D and `je` at 0x498720 - **the only instruction in the image that branches on CObjective::priority**. Inside CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives, it walks the agent's existing plan objectives (`CUnit +0x234`) and counts those whose province (+0x8) *and* priority (+0xC) both match a freshly computed one. Nothing weights or orders anything by priority; this is a change detector, and its only effect is at 0x49872D.

addresses.name: AIObjectives_SuppressUnchangedCommand
addresses.comment: `cmp ebx, [esp+0x50]; je 0x498808` - if every freshly computed objective matched an existing one on province and priority, CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives posts no CSetPlanObjectivesCommand at all. This is the whole consequence of the priority comparison at 0x49871A: a priority a mod or the interface writes that differs from the AI's own `victory_points x 20 + bonuses` makes this test fail, so the AI reposts its own list - with its own priorities - that hour.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CreateUnitAgent
addresses.comment: `this` in **EDI**, `ret 4`. Allocates 0x374 bytes, constructs a CAIUnit with (this, this->tag at +0x20, this->id at +0x24), and **only when the unit's `oob_level` (CUnit +0x1F4) is 0** resolves the unit's theatre through FindTheatreForUnit (0x4ACD00, with `&country[+0x48C]` off `g_CCountryDataBase[+0x16C][unit->owner_id]`) and copies its id pair into the agent's `+0x68`/`+0x6C`. Then AddRef (slot 7), push_back onto the CEU3AI's unit-agent list at `+0x40`/`+0x44`/`+0x48`, slot 52 (Enable) and slot 63 (SetUnit) with the unit. **Its only caller is 0x34FB7B, inside CObjectivesEntry slot 22 (0x34F910)** - so this path runs on the interface thread, from the battle-plan objectives panel, not on a TBB worker.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::MoveUnit
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3AI::MoveUnit(CEU3AI* this@ECX, CUnit* unit, int provinceId, int recordOnly, bool safe, bool verySafe, CAIAgent* agent)
addresses.comment:
**Renamed from `CMoveCommand::IssueFromInterface`, which was wrong about the class and about the caller.** The luabind registration table - the same table the whole Lua API was recovered from - carries this pointer (9021504 = 0x89A840) as `class CAI`, `cpp CEU3AI::MoveUnit`, `void MoveUnit(CEU3AI&, CUnit*, int, int, bool, bool, CAIAgent*)`. So it is **the AI's own move entry point, exposed to the mod's Lua as `CAI.MoveUnit`**, and `CAIUnit` slot 32 (0x8B0E60) calls it. The old name survived despite its own comment noting that the receiver in ECX is not a CMoveCommand; the seventh argument, recorded as an unread `int unused`, is the CAIAgent*, which accounts for both observations. Kept as an alias.

The body, unchanged from the earlier reading: What the GUI calls to issue a move; hardcodes mode68 = 1 and forwards its fourth and fifth arguments as safe and very safe; `ret 0x18`. The unit is the first stack argument (+0x158 gate, virtual +0x8C asked whether the province is reachable); `provinceId` indexes the game state's province vector at +0xB8C; when `recordOnly` is greater than zero it only writes the province to the unit's +0x2CC and returns; the sixth stack dword is never read on any path. **The receiver in ecx is not a CMoveCommand** - it is only ever handed on, as the first argument of 0x49ABD0 (issue a command of type id, 0x18D here or 0x5A4 for the sibling path) and of 0x499E50, which does `add ecx,0x20; call 0x402610`, so the object carries a CCountryTag at +0x20: the per-player interface the order is issued through. Its class was not identified.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder
addresses.comment: ret 0xC with a fourth argument in EDI, which is consistent at all five call sites in CAIInvasion stage 3 (0x8A0A2D, 0x8A0B22, 0x8A102F, 0x8A118B and the 0x8A1122 arm): EDI is loaded with a province id in the instruction before the pushes. It builds a one-element province list and tail-calls 0x89AD00 at 0x89ACD0. The order types seen through it are the save tokens 0x18D `none`, 0x3A8 `transport` and 0x3A5 `invasion`.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder(CEU3AI* ai, SaveToken orderType, CUnit* unit, int provinceId@EDI)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder
addresses.comment: The real order factory behind 0x89ABD0. When orderType is 0x3A5 (`invasion`) it first walks ai->+0x40 (the unit agents) setting each agent's +0x86 = 1, then allocates a 0xA0 byte COrder subclass and refuses outright when unit->+0x158 is non-zero. CAIInvasion stage 2 calls it directly at 0x8A0977 with the eight arguments, passing the now/sunrise pair as `from`/`to`.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder(CEU3AI* ai, SaveToken orderType, CUnit* unit, int provinceId, void* provinceIds, int* from, int* to, void* x)

addresses.name: CUnit::GetMovementDestinationProvince
addresses.comment: Answers the province the unit is heading for, or null. Asks its order (CUnit +0xB0) slot 16 and bails on the save token 0x4E5 (`support_attack`), then resolves CUnit +0x2CC as a province id through the game state's province array. Bare `ret`, 52 callers. CAIUnit slot 76 uses it, falling back to current_province, when deciding how many units are already standing on a front.

addresses.name: CUnit_GetPendingDestinationProvince
addresses.comment: 0x49B010 to the bare `ret` at 0x49B104, 244 bytes, read end to end, 8 callers (5 of them in CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits). Returns provinces[this->movement_destination_province_id (+0x2CC)] when that is non-zero; otherwise this->order (+0xB0)->+0xC when the order's slot 24 answers true; otherwise null. **Not the same as CUnit::GetMovementDestinationProvince (0x49AF00)**, which CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits also calls twice - this one additionally reports the target of a blocking order, which is what makes it the AI's 'where is this unit going' test.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CanDeclareWar
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the baked-in registration at 0x8F64D0 whose RTTI type is `bool CEU3AI::CanDeclareWar(CCountryTag, CCountryTag) const` - the two tags **by value**, so four stack dwords. Body not read; recorded because the name and signature are the compiler's own and the function sits in the same CEU3AI Lua cluster as the five trade predicates.
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CEU3AI::CanDeclareWar(CEU3AI* this, CCountryTag actor, CCountryTag target)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::GetAmountTradedFrom
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the baked-in registration at 0x8F6540 whose RTTI type is `CFixedPoint CEU3AI::GetAmountTradedFrom(GoodsCategory, const CCountryTag&, const CCountryTag&) const`. The return slot is [ebp+8], the category [ebp+0xC], the two tags [ebp+0x10] and [ebp+0x14]. It zeroes the result, takes the pair's CDiplomacyStatus as countries[arg4->id]->+0xE28[arg3->id] and walks its trade routes at +0x60. `likely` rather than `confirmed` because only the first fifteen instructions were read; the signature is the compiler's, not an inference.
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CEU3AI::GetAmountTradedFrom(CEU3AI* this, CFixedPoint* result, GoodsCategory category, const CCountryTag* from, const CCountryTag* to)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingResourceOtherWay
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the registration at 0x8EFCAD. `ret 4`, a CTradeRoute by reference. Compares the route's from_id (+0x28) against the AI's own country id (CEU3AI +0x24) and then walks the seven goods categories - **skipping index 2** - looking for a category the route moves one way and the country's own trade tables at CCountry +0x808 / +0x898 already move the other. True on the first hit. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the registration at 0x8EFCA3, and the fourth gate inside CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance (called at 0xA38B64 on the **recipient's** CEU3AI, with the action's embedded route) - a true answer makes the trade's AI acceptance zero. It fetches the pair's CDiplomacyStatus (country[route->from_id]->+0xE28[route->to_id]), walks the existing trade routes at CDiplomacyStatus +0x60, and only examines a route whose byte at +0x54 is set (`cmp byte [edx+0x54], 0; je next` at 0x89B425) - hence "disabled". For each such route it compares both goods blocks against the candidate's, category by category, against the global threshold at [0x1B148A0]. This is one of the two `bool CEU3AI::(const CTradeRoute&)` registrations FINDINGS-convoys.md found mangled names for; it is a **gate before** the Lua call, not the untraced route to it. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::IsTradeingAwayNeededResource
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name - the misspelling is the game's - from the registration at 0x8EFC99. `ret 4`. Works out which side of the route the AI is on and then checks every good that side gives away against the country's own balance for that good (CCountry method 0x4F18A0), returning true when the balance is below -[0x1B148A0]. **It also settles which of CTradeRoute's two goods blocks is which**: on the branch where the AI is the `from` side (route +0x28 == CEU3AI +0x24) the goods it gives away are read from the block at route +0x44, and on the branch where it is the `to` side (+0x30) they are read from +0x34 - the opposite of the inferred placement project.json currently records. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::GetSpamPenalty
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the baked-in registration at 0x8F6691 whose RTTI type is `float CEU3AI::GetSpamPenalty(const CCountryTag&)` - non-const. It loads g_CCurrentGameState [0x1A89790] and indexes **played_countries_array (+0xBCC) by the argument tag's id**; where that entry is zero it returns 0.0f immediately (`fldz` at 0x89B55A). So the penalty is only ever non-zero for a country somebody is playing: the AI applies no spam penalty to another AI's proposals. The rest of the body (from 0x89B565, which starts `add ecx, 0x20` - the AI's own CCountryTag) was not read, hence `likely`.
addresses.signature: float __thiscall CEU3AI::GetSpamPenalty(CEU3AI* this, const CCountryTag* tag)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::HasTradeGoneStale
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the baked-in registration at 0x8F6711 whose RTTI type is `bool (CEU3AI::*)(const CTradeRoute&) const`. 0x89B640 to the `ret 4` at 0x89B71F; `this` is never read. Body: false unless the route's `inactive` byte (+0x54) is set; false if its `last_inactive` (+0x84) is still the null date 0x29C55C0 at [0x170C2B8]; otherwise true when `last_inactive + 0x150 < gameState->tick` (+0xBDC). The tick is hours, so **0x150 = 336 hours = 14 days**: a route counts as stale once it has been inactive for a fortnight. Not a define - 0x150 is an immediate. This is the predicate the mod's cancel logic wants beside CEU3AI::EvaluateCancelTrades.
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CEU3AI::HasTradeGoneStale(CEU3AI* this, const CTradeRoute* route)

addresses.name: CEU3AI::CanTradeFreeResources
addresses.comment: The Lua name from the registration at 0x8EFC94/0x8EFC8F. The pairing convention in that registration call - argument order is (name, function), (name, function) - was confirmed twice independently: 'GetNeeded' pairs with 0x414F70, which is nothing but `jmp [vftable+0xC]`, slot 3, which the record already says GetNeeded is; and the three bodies at 0x89B310/0x89B3E0/0x89B480 each match the name the convention gives them. **The body of this one was not read**, which is why it is `likely` rather than `confirmed`. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::IsInfluencing
addresses.comment: The Lua name from the registration at 0x8EFC7B/0x8EFC76, on the same pairing convention as CanTradeFreeResources. Body not read. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: CEU3AI::EvaluateCancelTrades
addresses.comment: The game's own Lua name, from the baked-in registration at 0x8F68D1 whose RTTI type is `float CEU3AI::EvaluateCancelTrades(float, GoodsCategory)`. It bails to 0x89BC67 when `0.0f >= amount` (`comiss`/`jae` at 0x89B831), then reads its own tag at +0x20. Only the prologue was read. Its Lua name is the companion of the mod's `EvalutateExistingTrades` driver in script/ai_trade.lua.

addresses.name: CList::AppendAllNodes
addresses.comment: A template instantiation, 14 callers, **not in any vftable and not to be named after a domain**: CAIUnit slot 76 uses the same body for a list of CTheatre* (0x4DB139) and for a list of province ids (0x4DBC6A). It walks the source list through +0x8 and, for each node, allocates a fresh 0x10-byte node {payload, prev, next=0, flag=0} and links it onto the destination's {first +0x0, last +0x4, count +0x8, byte +0xC}. It does not touch the source.

addresses.name: CList_InsertByDescendingFloatAtC
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, 211 bytes, read end to end, 3 callers (0x497535, 0x497692, 0x4C6724). Walks back from list->+4 (the tail) through node->+4 while (*item)->+0xC exceeds node->data->+0xC, then links after that node, or push_front through 0x5F5E0 when it reaches the head - so the list comes out in DESCENDING order of the payload's +0xC float, highest at the head. The +0xC-keyed sibling of CList_InsertByDescendingScore (0x4DD4B0), which keys on +8. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits uses it to order CProvinceFloat records.

addresses.name: CAIAgent::SetParent
addresses.comment: **Slot 48 of CAIAgent.** Writes `this[+0x40] = parent` and then mints an object id for the agent: type `0x1268 + word[0x1A857EC]` and serial `++dword[0x1A857F8]`. That is what settles **CAIAgent +0x40 as the parent pointer** (and so +0x44/+0x48/+0x4C as the children CList that CAIAgent::Update walks). 0x4BBAE0 walks +0x40 to the root of an agent tree, and 0x48AA80 does the same.

addresses.name: CAIAgent::IsEnabled
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 8, shared by all seven CAIAgent subclasses.** Four instructions: `xor eax,eax; cmp byte [ecx+0x3C], al; setne al; ret`. CAIAgent::Update calls it first and does nothing at all when it returns false, and the driver ProcessAI tests the same byte before calling Update. The constructor leaves +0x3C at 0, and what sets it is not established. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIAgent::GetTypeName
addresses.comment: **Slot 55 of CAIAgent: `mov eax, 0x15EB668; ret`, and 0x15EB668 is the string "Agent".** Neither CAIUnit nor CAIInvasion overrides it, so a CAIUnit still calls itself "Agent".

addresses.name: CAIAgent::CAIAgent
addresses.comment: **Takes `this` in EAX** - the first instruction is `mov dword [eax], 0x15C3AE4` with nothing having written eax - and `ret 8` for the two stack arguments, returning `this` in eax unchanged. Sets +0x04 = 0x18D, +0x28 = 0x0F, +0x24 = 0, +0x30 = 0, +0x34 = tag, **+0x38 = the country's id**, +0x3C..+0x3E = 0, +0x40..+0x4C = 0, +0x50 = 0, and the CAIAgent vftable 0x15EB674 last. All ten call sites push `[owner+0x20]` and `[owner+0x24]` off the CEU3AI, which is why +0x38 is the country id and not an arbitrary stagger. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CAIAgent::DisableAndDisband
addresses.comment: **Slot 49 of CAIAgent.** Clears the enable byte `+0x3C` and then empties the children list at `+0x44`: for each first node, if the child is enabled it calls the child's slot 54 (`[vftable+0xD8]`), otherwise it calls `this`'s own slot 58 (`[vftable+0xE8]`) with the node - and loops until +0x44 is null. CAIUnit overrides it at 0x4B05B0, which additionally frees the list at CAIUnit +0x1EC/+0x1F0/+0x1F4 and then tail-jumps here.

addresses.name: CAIAgent::Enable
addresses.comment: **Slot 52 of CAIAgent, one instruction: `mov byte [ecx+0x3C], 1; ret`.** This is what sets the enable flag that CAIAgent::IsEnabled (slot 8, 0x49C6F0) tests, that CAIAgent::Update (slot 9) gates on, and that ProcessAI's minister loop gates on - the hole FINDINGS-ai.md calls 'the single biggest'. A minister or unit agent becomes live when somebody calls slot 52 on it; CAIUnit overrides it at 0x4B0360 and its four creation paths all call it immediately after construction.

addresses.name: CAIAgent::Update
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 9, the same body in all seven subclasses, 0 direct callers.** 21 instructions: if slot 8 (`[vftable+0x20]`) returns true, `dec [this+0x30]` and on zero call **slot 10** (`[vftable+0x28]`) - the "do your job" slot; then walk the child-agent list at `+0x44`, chained on `+8`, calling slot 9 (`[vftable+0x24]`) on each. Every minister's slot 10 re-arms `+0x30` to 1, so the countdown is not the throttle - the hour-of-day test inside each body is. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIEspionageMinister::CAIEspionageMinister
addresses.comment: Bare `ret`, `this` in EAX and the owner in ESI. Pushes `[owner+0x24]` and `[owner+0x20]` into CAIAgent::CAIAgent, then vftable 0x15EB7BC, `+0x54 = owner`, `+0x58 = -1`. The object is 0x5C bytes and lands at CEU3AI+0x68. One caller, CEU3AI::CreateMinisters at 0x888B8D - CEU3AI::ApplyPlayerDelegation has the same body inlined. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIEspionageMinister::DoWork
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 10 - the espionage minister's daily tick, and the shortest of the five.** Sets `+0x30 = 1`, then acts only when `(this->countryId (+0x38) + 1) % 24 == (gamestate->tick - 0x29C55C0) % 24`, and the whole body is a call to the mod's Lua `IntelligenceMinister_Tick` (0x49D0D0) - note the name is Intelligence, not Espionage. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: Lua_IntelligenceMinister_Tick
addresses.comment: Pushes the name `IntelligenceMinister_Tick` and fetches it from the Lua globals table, the same shape as Lua_ForeignMinister_Tick. Called from CAIEspionageMinister::DoWork at 0x89CF2F - note the engine class is Espionage but the Lua entry point is Intelligence, which is the name script/ai_intelligence_minister.lua defines. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIForeignMinister::CAIForeignMinister
addresses.comment: Bare `ret`; both operands are registers - `this` in EAX (handed straight to CAIAgent::CAIAgent, which also takes EAX) and the owner in ESI. Pushes `[owner+0x24]` and `[owner+0x20]`, writes vftable 0x15EB97C, `+0x54 = owner`, `+0x58 = 0`, `+0x5C = 0.0f`, `+0x60 = -1`, `+0x64 = 0x2D2D2D`. The object is 0x74 bytes and lands at CEU3AI+0x60. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIForeignMinister::DoWork
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 10 - the foreign minister's daily tick.** Sets `+0x30 = 1`, honours a skip-once byte at `+0x70`, then acts only when `(this->countryId (+0x38) + 0x0D) % 24 == (gamestate->tick - 0x29C55C0) % 24` - the **hour of the day**, not the day. It calls 0x89E010 and then the mod's Lua `ForeignMinister_Tick`; executes the pending action cached at `+0x58` when its score `+0x5C` exceeds 50.0 (0x160A4C8) by handing it to 0x89A750 with the OwnerAI; and then filters the list at `country+0x5D4` by `country->neighbours (+0xF58)`. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIForeignMinister::OnWar
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 41, one of only two CAISubscriber slots any minister implements** (the rest are the 0x60CD50 / 0xA806D0 stubs). `ret 8`. It takes `b->id (+0xCA8)`, indexes `a[+0xE28]` with it, reads that record's `+0x20`, and hands that plus both countries' tags at `+0xCA4` to the mod's Lua `ForeignMinister_OnWar` (0x49E860). The slot's own name is inferred from the Lua function it calls, not from the caller. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.comment: `lua_pushstring(L, "ForeignMinister_Tick")` (0x15EB8F0) then `lua_gettable(L, 0xFFFFD8EE)` - LUA_GLOBALSINDEX, -10002 - so it fetches the mod's global of that name. Then fills the frame at ESI with `{L, 1, 0xB7E9D0, args, 0}` and returns it in eax. Bare `ret` with one stack argument, so cdecl, and both other operands are registers. Called from CAIForeignMinister::DoWork at 0x89D69F. **This is where script/ai_foreign_minister.lua is entered.** See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::GetUnits
addresses.comment: Slot 62, two instructions: `lea eax,[ecx+0x74]; ret`. The getter for the list of every unit committed to the invasion, which is the list slot 63 appends to. CAIAgent has the shared null stub 0xA80690 in this slot.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::CAIInvasion
addresses.comment: `ret 8`; the tag arrives in ECX and its two halves are forwarded to CAIAgent::CAIAgent (0x89C720, `this` in EAX, which returns the object). Writes vftable 0x15EBAE4 at 0x89F934, zeroes three CLists (+0x54/+0x58/+0x5C, +0x64/+0x68/+0x6C, +0x74/+0x78/+0x7C, each with a trailing byte), then stores `staging` into +0x84 and `owner` into +0x8C and zeroes +0x88 and +0x90. **CAIInvasion is 0x94 bytes** (`push 0x94` at 0x893AFB, its one allocation site).

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::Enable
addresses.comment: Slot 52, four instructions: `+0x3C = 1; +0x30 = 1`. The CAIAgent::Enable counterpart (0x89C8E0) sets only +0x3C; this one also asks to be ticked at once. Called through [vftable+0xD0] at 0x893C11, immediately after construction, which is the only place an invasion agent becomes live.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::Tick
addresses.comment: Slot 10, eleven instructions: `if (+0x3E) return; +0x3E = IsInvasionOver(this); if (+0x3E) return; this->slot73(); +0x30 = 1`. Slot 73 is reached through `[vftable+0x124]`. Reached from ProcessAI's +0x50 loop through CAIAgent::Update (slot 9, not overridden), hourly, **worker thread**.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::DoTick
addresses.comment: Slot 73, forty instructions, the whole of the agent's behaviour: `country = GetCountry(&this->tag); if (!this->+0x88 || !0x4EF7C0(country, &this->+0x88->controller, 1)) PickLandingSite(this); if (!this->+0x88 || !0x4EF7C0(country, &this->+0x88->controller, 1)) { this->+0x3E = 1; return } 0x8A01F0(this); 0x8A0610(this); 0x8A09B0(this)`. So it re-picks its landing province whenever the one it holds stops qualifying, and kills itself when nothing does. 0x4EF7C0 takes a CCountryTag* and the fact that `this->+0x88 + 0x334` is passed to it is one of the three readings that make +0x88 a CProvince* (CProvince +0x334 is `controller`). The three stage functions were not read; 0x8A09B0 is the likely home of the CNavalInvasionOrder.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::PickLandingSite
addresses.comment: `ret 4`, 0x89FBC0-0x8A01E6. **Where the AI decides to land.** A minimising search: the running best starts at 0xF4240 (1,000,000) at 0x89FD45 and a candidate wins on `jl`. (1) Measures its own force over +0x54, then `canTakeMore = (+0x5C <= 5) && SumTransportWeight(&+0x64) >= SumTransportWeight(&+0x54)`. (2) A distance limit of **1000 or 2000** from `0x47FD90(GetActingCapitalLocation(country)->area)` (the movzx/neg/sbb/and 0xFFFFFC18/add 0x7D0 idiom at 0x89FD2D). (3) Outer loop over `country->+0xF98`, inner over each of those countries' `+0xD30` COwnerArea list, skipping the staging province's own area. (4) A per-area weight: 1.0, or 2.0 when 0x47FD90(area) holds, or 4.0 when the area is not the owner's acting-capital area (constants 0x171DBAC=1.0, 0x1718064=2.0, 0x171DF34=4.0). (5) Per province in the area: `0x4D52A0(country, province, +0x84, 1)` must pass; `dist = 0x4A5570(province, +0x84->id)` floored at 1000 and rejected above the limit; `w = 1.0` or **10.0** when `0x4A56B0(province, 0)` holds; `score = (1.5 - (province->naval_base->+0x20 / 1000) / 10.0) * w` (0x160A6B8=1.5, 0x160A340=10.0); `score *= 0.3` (0x160A3E8) when the area's controller id equals our own (CAIAgent +0x38). The winner is written to +0x88 and +0x90 at 0x8A0176/0x8A0186. **The naval base is the only term that can lower the score, so a port is what makes a province a landing site.**
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::MarchLandForceToPort
addresses.comment: Stage 1 of slot 73. Body 0x8A01F0-0x8A0602 (ret 4), int3 run at 0x8A0605. Walks the land force at +0x54; skips a unit whose slot9 unit has +0x300 set or whose province's map data +0xD4 +0x22 byte is clear; drops a unit (slot 64) when CAIInvasion::UnitCanReachObjectiveOverland (0x8A11B0) says yes or when unit->+0x128 is not our country id; otherwise orders it to +0x88 (the port of embarkation) through CEU3AI::MoveUnit when 0x5A1A90 finds a route, else to the nearest reachable port in the unit's own area (COwnerArea +0x48) or in a friendly neighbouring area (COwnerArea +0x34, gated on CCountry::IsFriendly), writing that waypoint's id into +0x90.

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::LoadTransportsAtNight
addresses.comment: Stage 2 of slot 73. Body 0x8A0610-0x8A09A8 (ret 4). Returns at once unless +0x6C == 1, the single naval unit's COrder (CUnit +0xB0) reports type id 0x3A5 (save token `invasion`) from slot 16, and CCountry::IsEnemy holds for (+0x84)->controller. Then it works only at night: hour = (gamestate->+0xBDC - 0x29C55C0) % 24 must be <= 0x4A7450(province) or >= 0x4A74D0(province), and at least 3 hours of darkness must remain. Picks up to three land units standing in the fleet's own province, scored by the two floats 0x5C7250 returns against the 0.5 at 0x15AB304 and the 0.33 at 0x160A958, and issues each a 0x6FB (`ground_attack`) order on (+0x84)->id through 0x89AD00, valid from now until sunrise.

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::SailAndIssueInvasionOrder
addresses.comment: Stage 3 of slot 73 and the home of the CNavalInvasionOrder. Body 0x8A09B0-0x8A11A8 (ret 4). First pass over +0x64 clears or re-issues fleet orders (0x18D `none`, 0x3A8 `transport`) through 0x89ABD0. Then, when +0x90 is not yet (+0x88)->id, it issues 0x3A8 `transport` to the port of embarkation and stores that id in +0x90 (0x8A101F-0x8A1040). Once the fleet is at the port it tests CCountry::IsEnemy on (+0x84)->controller: if the objective is still enemy held it calls 0x893E70(ai, (+0x84)->area, invasion) to choose the actual beach, overwrites +0x84 with the answer and issues 0x3A5 `invasion` on it (0x8A1145-0x8A118B); when 0x893E70 returns null it calls 0x894C40 and sets +0x3E (finished). If the objective is no longer enemy held it falls back to a 0x3A8 `transport` order unless the small-area/friendly-unit-count test at 0x8A106E-0x8A110E passes.

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::UnitCanReachObjectiveOverland
addresses.comment: Body 0x8A11B0-0x8A12E9, bare ret, both arguments in registers (this in ECX, the unit in EAX). True when the unit's current province is +0x84 itself, when its area is +0x84's area, when 0x4A6B00(province@EAX, objectiveArea) holds, or when one of the unit's area's neighbour areas (COwnerArea +0x34) is enemy controlled and AreaIsConnectedTo(unitArea, objectiveArea) holds. False early when 0x4A56B0(province, 0) is false, when the unit's area is +0x88's area, or when it is our acting capital's area. Its one caller is stage 1 (0x8A028A), which drops the unit from the invasion when it answers true - the mirror of the planner's 'only invade what you cannot march to'.

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::IsInvasionOver
addresses.comment: `ret 4`. Answers true - the agent is finished forever - when `+0x6C < 1` (no transports left) or `+0x5C < 1` (no land units left). Where `+0x6C == 1` it also asks the single transport's COrder* (CUnit +0xB0) for its type id through slot 16 and compares it with **0x3A5, the save token `invasion`** (CNavalInvasionOrder), then requires that order's +0x2EC to be positive. So an invasion ends when its force is gone, not when it succeeds.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::AddUnit
addresses.comment: Slot 63, `ret 4`, answers true on success. Refuses duplicates by walking +0x74, then **steals the unit's agent pointer**: `if (unit->+0x198 && unit->+0x198 != this) unit->+0x198->slot64(unit)` (through [vft+0x100]) and `if (!this->+0x3D && !this->+0x3E) unit->+0x198 = this` at 0x8A16D7, then push_backs onto +0x74/+0x78/+0x7C. **So CUnit +0x198 can hold a CAIInvasion* as well as a CAIUnit*** - see the fields note. Called three times from the invasion planner at 0x893B84, 0x893BB6, 0x893BE8, once per gathered list.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::ReleaseUnitOutsidePortArea
addresses.comment: Vftable slot 70, one holder. Twelve instructions, ret 8: if +0x88 is set and province->+0x2B4 equals (+0x88)->+0x2B4 it returns, otherwise it forwards (this->+0x8C, a, province) to 0x897B40. So a unit in the embarkation port's own area is the invasion's business and anything else is handed back to the owning CEU3AI. The name is a description of the body; what the slot means to CAIAgent's interface was not established, and neither was 0x897B40.

The block caches `(float)*0x4EE560(country) / 1000.0` in +0x5C and calls the mod's Lua `ProductionMinister_Tick`. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: BroadcastToListeners
addresses.comment:
A signal/slot broadcast. Bare `ret` at 0x4A2DF1 and both callers do `add esp, 8`, so the two stack dwords are the caller's to clean; the channel arrives in **eax** and costs no stack. [ebp+8] is the handler (pushed last) and [ebp+0xC] the subject.

    ecx = subject->+0x198;  if (ecx) handler(subject)
    node = *(0x1714DC0 + channel*16)
    for (; node; node = node->+8)
        ecx = node->+0                       ; the listener's target
        if (ecx) handler(subject)
        ... unlinks nodes whose +0xC byte is set ...

So `handler` is called with the subject as its single stack argument and **ecx set to the listener's target**, which is why the handlers passed to it are vcall thunks such as VcallThunk_Slot11 (rva 0x149E00). The table at rva 0x1714DC0 is 16 bytes per channel and is written by the add/remove side at 0x4A2E9D/0x4A2EA4; nothing static says which classes register. Named for what it does; no symbol was recovered.
addresses.signature: void __cdecl BroadcastToListeners(void* handler, void* subject, int channel@EAX)

addresses.name: CList::FreeNodes
addresses.comment: 97 callers, **a shared template body, so not to be named after any one class**. Walks the singly linked chain at [list+0] through +0x8 freeing every node, then zeroes +0x0, +0x4 and +0x8. The same loop is inlined at dozens of places in the AI code rather than called.

addresses.name: VirtualThunkSlot17
addresses.comment: `mov eax,[ecx]; jmp dword ptr [eax+0x44]` - two instructions, a pointer-to-virtual-member thunk for **vftable offset 0x44, i.e. slot 17**. MSVC emits one of these whenever a virtual member function's address is taken, so a luabind registration that names a virtual method points here, and 0x44/4 names the slot. Recorded class-free per trap 4: it has 8 references and two of them are registrations for *different* classes - 0x8FDBD8 for `int CDiplomaticAction::GetAIAcceptance()` and 0x8FAB08 for `bool CGovernment::(...)const`. **It is what finally makes CDiplomaticAction slot 17 = GetAIAcceptance confirmed rather than inferred** (FINDINGS-diplomacy.md recorded the registration as resolving to _purecall, which it does not).

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::CAIStrategy
addresses.comment: `this` on the stack, returned in EAX, `ret 4`. Writes `+0x4 = 0x18D` (a constant type id) at 0x4A33CD, vftable 0x15EBF24 at 0x4A33D4, and `+0x8 = 0x2D2D2D` ("---", the no-country tag) at 0x4A33DA - which is what proves **CAIStrategy +0x8 is a CCountryTag**. Then zero-fills, including the theatre list at +0xE4/+0xE8/+0xEC (0x4A35F5). Four callers: three in CCountry's constructor (0x4C8CD6, 0x4C8CE6, 0x4C8CF6 - the country's +0x1DC, +0x334 and +0x48C) and 0x99BDC2.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::~CAIStrategy
addresses.comment: Rewrites vftable 0x15EBF24 at 0x4A38A1 and frees the eighteen lists, including the theatre list at +0xE4/+0xE8 (0x4A39AF). Five callers: the three embedded strategies in CCountry's destructor (0x4CB1F2, 0x4CB201, 0x4CB210), 0x4A3856 and 0x99C677.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: MergeAIStrategy
addresses.comment:
Folds one CAIStrategy into an accumulator. Three call sites and they are the whole story of how AI strategy reaches the AI: ApplyCountryAIStrategies passes `CCountry+0x1DC` (`ai_hard_strategy`) and `CCountry+0x334` (`ai_event_strategy`), and CAddAIStrategyEffect::Execute (0x5B0E00) passes the effect's own embedded CAIStrategy. What it does with the 18 fields was not read. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

*(2026-10-01: both arguments retyped. The first was `AIStrategyCache*`, which is not a declared struct. The second was `CAIStrategy**`; it is one level of indirection too many, and the bytes say so - `mov eax, [ebp+0xc]` at `0x8A3BA1` is followed directly by `mov edi, [eax+0x1c]` at `0x8A3BB4`, a field read with no load in between, and `+0x1c` is then walked as a list head (`[edi]` to the node's data, `[edi+8]` to the next node). A `CAIStrategy**` would have had to be dereferenced first. Checked here because the survey and the record disagreed.)*

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAIStrategy::LoadKey(CAIStrategy* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 21 of them, one case each: `air_perc`, `antagonize`, `area_theatre`, `armor_bias`, `befriend`, `building_prov`, `conquer_prov`, `consolidate`, `defend_prov`, `initialized`, `land_perc`, `max_subunits`, `military_access`, `naval_perc`, `personality`, `protect`, `rival`, `static`, `threat`, `vassal`, `war_with`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2. Among the eighteen keys it writes, it reads the theatre list at `+0xE4` (0x4A4D43) and writes it under key id **0x6EF, `area_theatre`** (0x4A4D56). With CAIStrategy::LoadKey's matching case this settles that +0xE4 is the `area_theatre` list and that it is the half of the theatre layer a savegame round-trips.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::Rebuild
addresses.comment:
Rebuilds a country's merged AI strategy. Bails when `+0xC` is null or the tag at `+8` is `REB`; stamps `+0x10 = gamestate->tick` and `+0x14 = 1`; calls 0x8A5DD0, 0x8ACE20, 0x8AD430, ApplyCountryAIStrategies (0x4A62A0) and 0x8AD6E0. **11 direct callers** across 0x4DB7C4, 0x4E055D, 0x4E3E5E, 0x4E6CCB, 0x4EF2A2, 0x4EF781, 0x4F640E, 0x4F645B, 0x65C282, 0x9B0E78 and 0xA4018C, so the strategy is consumed lazily and widely rather than by one minister. Which class owns the object is not established. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

**Renamed 2026-10-01 from `AIStrategyCache::Rebuild`.** `AIStrategyCache` was a good *description* - the object caches the country's two loaded strategies merged together, and the `+0x10 = tick` / `+0x14 = 1` stamp this writes is exactly a cache validity stamp - but it is not a class, and the receiver has a name already: every caller passes `&country[+0x48C]`, which the record declares as `CAIStrategy`. See `FINDINGS-aitheatre.md`.

addresses.name: ApplyCountryAIStrategies
addresses.comment:
**The answer to who consumes CAIStrategy.** A sweep of all 1295 CCountryTag::GetCountry call sites for a `+0x1DC` access within 0x30 bytes returns exactly one hit, 0x8A62C4, and it is here: `country = GetCountry(&acc[+8])`, then `0x8A3B90(acc, &country[+0x1DC])` (`ai_hard_strategy`) and `0x8A3B90(acc, &country[+0x334])` (`ai_event_strategy`). 0x8A3B90 is the same merge routine CAddAIStrategyEffect::Execute uses, so the two loaded strategies and the `add_ai_strategy` effect all feed one accumulator. One caller, the cache rebuild at 0x4A5C90. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

*(2026-10-01: the argument type was `AIStrategyCache*`, which is not a declared struct. It is a `CAIStrategy*` - `CCountry +0x48C`.)*

addresses.name: CountEnemyUnitsInArea
addresses.comment: `ret 0xC`; answers 0 for a null area. Walks the area's provinces (COwnerArea +0x24, nodes {province, ?, next@+8}), then each province's `units` (CProvince +0x2B8), and for each unit passing slot 15 compares the unit's country id (CUnit +0x128) against GetCountry(&strategy->+8)->+0xCA8, counting the ones whose CDiplomacyStatus +0x20 (`war`) is set, excluding REB on either side. It touches the strategy only to read its CCountryTag at +0x8. The invasion planner clamps the result to >= 1 and multiplies it into its score (0x892C0B-0x892C22), so a weakly held area scores better. Name is BiceLib's.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion
addresses.signature: int __stdcall CountEnemyUnitsInArea(CAIStrategy* strategy, COwnerArea* area, bool flag)

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::IsFrontWorthyEnemy
addresses.comment: Body 0x8A9390-0x8A9A29, ret 8, with four interior ret 8 early exits (0x8A94DC, 0x8A9676, 0x8A96D1, 0x8A977A) that share the one `sub esp, 0x20` frame and are jumped to from inside - trap 3, not trap 2. The predicate CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres and CollectAreaFrontsForCountry both apply to a CAreaBorder's local_enemy. In order: false if the tag is our own; recurses on the other country's faction leader (+0xF38) when it has one; true if 0x8A9A30 says so; false if CCountry::IsFriendly; false if our own faction leader's CDiplomacyStatus toward them has +0x14 set; true if 0x8ADE10 says so; false if CCurrentGameState +0xD0C (scenario) is non-null; then two faction tests on CCountry +0xD8 and finally a **compiled-in table of country pairs** read off CCountryDataBase's 45 tag slots - for example SOV against LIT/ROM/POL/SPA/SPR/ETH/SWE/HUN/BUL/TUR/YUG/SLO/CZE/AUS/MAN/JAP, GER against HOL/BEL/LUX/POL/LAT, FRA against ITA/BEL/LUX, JAP against CHC/CHI/CGX/CSX/KOR/MAN/MEN/SIK/CXB/CYN. The tail past 0x8A98D0 adds an ideology (GetIdeologies, 0x527280) and threat computation that was not read. 18 direct callers. Read statically, game not running.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::IsWarCandidate
addresses.comment: Receiver in **EDI**, two stack arguments, `ret 8`; every call site reaches it as `edi = country + 0x48C` - the embedded CAIStrategy. It resolves `this->+0x8` (the strategy's own tag) to a CCountry, answers true at once if CCountry::IsEnemyTag says the argument is an enemy, false at once if CCountry::IsFriendly says it is a friend, and otherwise asks the argument country's faction (`+0xD8`, never null) a slot-7 question and consults `ourCountry->+0x1008`. Four readers in the unit AI: CAIUnit::SetArea twice (0x4BAE63 and 0x4BAD4D's sibling 0x4A9390), ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier at 0x4BE13E, and 0x4BD619. The name is inference from the two early answers plus the CCountryWarTargetValue class sitting beside CAIStrategy in .rdata; the body past 0x4A9AC9 was not read. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres
addresses.comment: **The AI's theatre builder, and the home of two of EnsureAgentForArea's four callers.** One body, VA 0x8A9B10-0x8ABC83 (rva 0x4A9B10-0x4ABC83), `ret 8`; the one interior `ret` at 0x8A9C2A is a real early exit sharing the `sub esp,0x150` frame, not an abutting function. Bails for the REB tag (0x8A9B43-0x8A9B56) and for a zero tag id. When `in_game` (gamestate +0xDA4) is set and the strategy already has theatres (+0xEC > 0) it delegates to the refresh 0x8ABC90(strategy,1) and returns. Otherwise it builds from scratch: six separate `new CTheatre` sites (0x8AA0DE, 0x8AA419, 0x8AA605, 0x8AA7E6, 0x8AA9C3, 0x8AAB02), each `push 0xA8` then 0x4AEFB0(tagChars, tagId), each stamping its id from g_theatre_id (0x170AEBC) with id type 0x2D; appends them to strategy->+0xE4/+0xE8/+0xEC at 0x8AB8E0/0x8AB8F5 and 0x8AB9AA; and for each one, when GetCountry(&strategy->tag)->+0x1D8 is non-null, calls CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea(ai, theatre, 1) and sets ai->+0xA6 = 1. **Six callers, and the two that matter are tick thread**: RunCountryHourlyPass at 0x4D9093 (gated on CCountry +0x580), 0x4E6CD3, 0x4F6416, 0x4F6477, 0x7FC925, 0xA401B1. What distinguishes the six creation paths was not read.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::RefreshTheatreProvinces
addresses.comment: 0x8ABC90-0x8ABFF6, `ret 8`, a genuine function - int3 padding at 0x8ABC86-0x8ABC8F, so not the abutting-function trap. **The other two CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea callers live here (0x8ABE8F, 0x8ABFAE)**, and it sets CEU3AI +0xA6 at 0x8ABF22. Its only caller is 0x8A9C15, the early-exit arm of CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres taken when the strategy already has theatres. It walks GetCountry(&strategy->tag)->+0xD00 (province_ids) and re-sorts those provinces over the existing theatres. Tick thread, through BuildTheatres.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::MaintainTheatres
addresses.comment: The third member of the theatre family, and the one that runs on the ordinary hour. RunCountryHourlyPass calls it at 0x4D90C6 with `hour == country->id % 24` as the flag, on the arm where CCountry +0x580 is clear; BuildTheatres also calls it at 0x8ABC44. It appends to the strategy's theatre list at +0xE8 (0x8ACCA1). Tick thread. What it does beyond that was not read.
addresses.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

addresses.name: FindTheatreForUnit
addresses.comment:
`ret 4`, unit in **EAX**, one stack argument which every caller supplies as `&country[+0x48C]`. It walks the unit's `higher_oob_unit_ptr` chain (CUnit +0x1E0) up to the topmost unit, then walks the list at `manager[+0xE4]` comparing each entry's `+0x74`/`+0x78` against that top unit's id pair (`CUnit +0x10`/`+0x14`); `+0x74`/`+0x78` on a CTheatre is its `unit` key, so the entries are CTheatres and the answer is **the theatre whose HQ unit is the root of this unit's order of battle**. Answers null when nothing matches. Its result's `+0x8`/`+0xC` (the theatre's own id pair) is what the three unit-agent creation paths store in CAIUnit +0x68/+0x6C.

*(2026-10-01: the second argument was `void *countryTheatreManager`. It is a `CAIStrategy*`: the `manager[+0xE4]` this walks is the `area_theatre` list, filled by `CAIStrategy::LoadKey`'s token `0x6EF` case at `0x8A4685` and written back by its `SaveContents` at `0x8A4D43`.)* Extent: `0x8ACD00`-`0x8ACD4A` with `int3` padding after, so `0x8ACD50` is a **separate** function and any address of the form `FindTheatreForUnit+0x50` is nearest-entry noise.

addresses.name: CAITechMinister::CAITechMinister
addresses.comment: Bare `ret`, `this` in EAX and the owner in ESI. Pushes `[owner+0x24]` and `[owner+0x20]` into CAIAgent::CAIAgent, then writes vftable 0x15EBF5C, `+0x54 = owner`, `+0x58 = -1`, **`word +0x5C = 0x0101`** (the two booleans CEU3AI::ApplyPlayerDelegation later overwrites from the player's +0x30), and zeroes +0x60..+0x78. The object is 0x80 bytes and lands at CEU3AI+0x6C. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: CAITechMinister::OnCountryEvent
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 47, the only other CAISubscriber slot a minister implements.** `ret 8`. Its first act is `if (country[+0xCA8] != this[+0x38]) return;` - **independent confirmation that CAIAgent+0x38 is the country's id** - and then it news 0x48 bytes and builds a command-shaped object with `0x557E00(obj, this->tag, this->id, arg)` before touching the game state. Which notification this is, and what `arg` means, is not established; the name is a placeholder. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAITechMinister::OnCountryEvent(CAITechMinister* this, CCountry* country, int arg)

addresses.name: CAITechMinister::DoWork
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 10 - the tech minister's tick, and the only one with a monthly re-plan.** Sets `+0x30 = 1`, computes the day of the month (365.0 at 0x160A550, month lengths at 0x1713294), and calls 0x8AECA0(this) then 0x8AEF40(this) whenever either of its vectors (+0x60..+0x64, +0x70..+0x74) is empty or `+0x58 > dayOfMonth` - which is only true on the day a month turns - then stores dayOfMonth in +0x58. Separately, when `(this->countryId (+0x38) + 3) % 24 == hours % 24`, it calls the mod's Lua `TechMinister_Tick` with the two bytes at +0x5C/+0x5D. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: Lua_TechMinister_Tick
addresses.comment: Pushes the name `TechMinister_Tick` and fetches it from the Lua globals table. Called from CAITechMinister::DoWork at 0x8AEC60, with the minister's two bytes +0x5C/+0x5D as the arguments. The mod defines it in script/ai_tech_minister.lua. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl Lua_TechMinister_Tick(void* args, lua_State* L@EDI, LuaCallFrame* out@ESI) @EAX

addresses.name: ReturnDwordAt0x64
addresses.comment: `mov eax, [ecx+0x64]; ret` - three bytes. It is **CAIUnit slot 74** (where it answers the agent's CUnit, and 0x48A880 calls it through `[vftable+0x128]`), and it is also in the vftable at 0x15CF20C, which RTTI does not name. Two vftables in all, so the name is deliberately neutral (trap 4).

addresses.name: UnitHasBlockingOrder
addresses.comment: `this` in **ESI**, bare `ret`, no stack arguments; 0x4AF4E0 to 0x4AF529, with six int3 before CAIUnit::CAIUnit at 0x4AF530. Answers true if `this[+0x2CC] > 0`; otherwise it asks the order at `this[+0xB0]` for its kind through slot 16 (`[vftable+0x40]`) and answers false when that is **0x4E5** or **0x56C** (two save tokens, the same way CStrategicRedeploymentOrder is recognised by 0x5A4 elsewhere), and otherwise the order's slot 24 (`[vftable+0x60]`). So **CAIUnit +0xB0 holds a COrder\***. Called from slots 78, 79 and 85. The name is from the shape.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::CAIUnit
addresses.comment: `ret 0x10` - `this` is on the stack, not in a register, and the function returns it in EAX. It calls CAIAgent::CAIAgent (0x49C720, `this` in EAX) with (tag, countryId), writes CAIUnit's vftable 0x15EC0B4 at 0x4AF568, and then zero-fills the derived part field by field out to +0x370, with these non-zero seeds: `+0x5C = 1`, `+0x60 = owner`, `+0x80 = 0x100` (so byte +0x81 = 1), `+0x84 = 0x10101` (bytes +0x84/+0x85/+0x86 = 1, +0x87 = 0), `+0x88 = 1`, `+0x366 = 1`. It also builds three 0x3C-byte containers in place at +0x294, +0x2D0 and +0x30C (comparator byte, sentinel node at +4, size at +8, a float at +0x28 from 0x171DBAC) and a 0x1FF-entry table out of the lazily-built singleton at 0x1A886F0. **Note it zeroes +0x54**, which is where CAIAgent keeps the owner AI for the five ministers and what the luabind getter `GetOwnerAI` (0x4E90A0, `mov eax,[ecx+0x54]`) reads - CAIUnit keeps its owner at +0x60 instead. Four call sites, all allocating 0x374 bytes: 0x48A994, 0x48AB9F, 0x48BF9F and 0x49A1F8.
addresses.signature: CAIUnit * __stdcall CAIUnit::CAIUnit(CAIUnit *this, CEU3AI *owner, CCountryTag tag, int countryId)

addresses.name: CAIUnit::~CAIUnit
addresses.comment: The destructor proper: writes CAIUnit's vftable 0x15EC0B4 back at 0x4AFC51 and unhooks the agent from the eight global CAISubscriber channels CAIUnit::Enable put it on (it reads 0x1B14E50 at 0x4AFC6E, and the others beside it). Slot 0 (0x4AFBF0) is the scalar deleting destructor: it calls this and then `free`.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Enable
addresses.comment: **Slot 52, CAIUnit's override of CAIAgent::Enable (0x49C8E0).** It sets the enable byte `+0x3C = 1` - which is what CAIAgent::IsEnabled (slot 8) tests and therefore what makes the agent tick at all - and then subscribes the agent to **eight process-wide CAISubscriber channels**, each a `{first, last, count}` triple of 0x10-byte nodes, by push_back in this order: 0x1B14E50, 0x1B14E70, 0x1B14E60, 0x1B14E30, 0x1B14E20, 0x1B14E40, 0x1B14F30, 0x1B14E90. That subscription is why CAIUnit is the only CAIAgent subclass that overrides any of the observer slots (17-25, 69-72). It is called right after construction at all four creation sites.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::DoUpdate
addresses.comment: **CAIUnit's slot 10** - the 'do your job' slot CAIAgent::Update (slot 9) calls when the countdown at +0x30 reaches zero. Six instructions: it calls its own **slot 73** (`[vftable+0x124]`, 0x4B0730) and then sets `+0x30 = 1`, so the agent asks to be ticked again on the very next AI pass. Unlike the five ministers there is no hour gate here; the gating is inside slot 73.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Tick
addresses.comment: **Slot 73, and the whole of what a unit agent does.** 0x4B0730 to the bare `ret` at 0x4B0D17.
