It takes the tick from CCurrentGameState +0xBDC (constructing the singleton if 0x1A89790 is null), divides `tick - 0x29C55C0` by 24 into days and the hour of the day, and then computes **four** staggers off the country id at CAIAgent +0x38: `id % 24`, `(id+3) % 24`, `(id+6) % 24` and `(id+9) % 24`. What runs when: (a) if byte `+0x87` is set, **or** the hour is 1 and `dayOfYear % 7 == 0`, `0x4BBAE0` (GetArea) then `0x4BA5A0` (SetArea) - the weekly re-anchor to the theatre; (b) if the hour is `id % 24` or byte `+0x80` is clear, `0x4C3330`; (c) for a land unit (CArmy slot 9 answers `this`), the unit's plan objectives at CUnit +0x234 are copied into CArmy +0x2EC by 0x4DD350; (d) **slot 82 runs every hour**, with a bool that is true only at hour `id % 24` on every ninth day of the year; (e) at hour `(id+3) % 24`, slot 85; (f) at hour `(id+9) % 24`, 0x4B0D20; (g) 0x4DCAE0 answers a float into `+0x368`, and slot 78 runs unless byte +0x86 is clear and the hour matches `(id+9) % 24`. Since the AI pass itself is hourly, each of the four staggers fires once a game day.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::RebuildFocusOwnerAreas
addresses.comment: 0x4B0D20 to the bare `ret` at 0x4B0E52, read end to end. Two callers: CAIUnit::Tick (slot 73) at 0x4B09CD and CAIUnit::SetArea at 0x4BA679, where it is the **first** thing SetArea does after its guards. FINDINGS-aiunit.md lists this address among slot 73's callees known only as an address. It frees the CList at `this->+0x338` node by node and zeroes its first/last/count, asks CAIUnit::GetArea for the agent's theatre and returns if there is none, then walks the theatre's list at `+0x84`, takes each entry's `COwnerArea*` at its `+0x6C`, deduplicates into a local list, and - where 0x803F0(ownerArea@EAX) answers more than 1 - calls 0x4B0F20(theatre, ownerArea, &this->+0x338), which is what actually appends to the list. So `+0x338` is rebuilt from the agent's theatre every time, and SetArea then reads it to widen its front search. What 0x803F0 counts was not established.

addresses.name: CollectUnitsMovingIntoProvince
addresses.comment: 0x4B1480-0x4B16EB (`ret 0x14`), read end to end, four callers (0x4CB0C3, 0x4CDC38, 0x4CE37D, 0x4D6FA8). Walks province->path_node_ptr (+0xD4)'s edge vector (+0x90/+0x94, stride 0x14); skips a neighbour whose template is not is_land (+0x13D) or whose +0x2B8 unit list is empty; per unit requires slot 15, then with enemiesOnly non-zero the inlined at-war test against `tag` (owner id +0x128 against country->+0xCA8, diplomacy +0xE28, the at-war flag +0x20, the two REB tests and UndeclaredWarCoversProvince) or with it zero CCountry::IsFriendly; then requires the unit's movement destination - provinces[unit->+0x13C[0]] when +0x140 > 0, else null - to equal `province`; then pushes unit->slot9() onto `out`. With enemiesOnly = 1, which is what both air call sites pass, it answers 'which enemy land units are marching into this province right now', and in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits that is the airfield-evacuation trigger.
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CollectUnitsMovingIntoProvince(CMapProvince* province, CUnitList* out, bool enemiesOnly, CCountryTag tag)

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Slot78_ManageSubordinates
addresses.comment: **Slot 78**, 0x4B1D10 to the bare `ret` at 0x4B32AC, with an EH funclet after it that shares the frame (so the body runs to 0x4B32DF and slot 79 starts at 0x4B32E0 - trap 3, not trap 2). About 5.5 KB. It reads more of CUnit than anything else in the class (movement, supply, organisation, leader, order, oob_level) and builds **CDetachUnitCommand** (0x5DE1D0), **CSendExpeditionCommand** (0x5E95B0) and **CSetAIParamCommand** (0x5E90B0), as well as calling GetArea (0x4BBAE0) and the order-kind test 0x4AF4E0. CAIUnit::Tick reaches it through `[vftable+0x138]`. Not read.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::ManageExpeditions
addresses.comment: **Slot 79, 0x4B32E0-0x4B3A4F, bare `ret` at 0x4B3A46.** Gated on `owner_ai->+0x2C`; called from slot 73 at 0x4B0A36 under the same daily-stagger flag that gates slot 78. Walks the land-unit vector CAIUnit +0x11C and splits on `CUnit::expeditionary_owner` (+0x28C/+0x290): a unit that **has** one, whose owner is not a government in exile and not a played country, has every child detached (`CDetachUnitCommand`, 0x4B34D1, one site, inside the children loop) and is then **given back** with `CSendExpeditionCommand(unit, its expeditionary_owner)` at 0x4B35C5. A unit with **no** expeditionary owner that is standing in a faction partner's province it has no business in - not our territory, not at war with the controller, same faction, a leaf unit with `oob_level != 0` - is **lent away** with `CSendExpeditionCommand(unit, that province's controller)` at 0x4B3973, after being erased from six of the agent's own vectors (+0x11C, +0x12C, +0x13C, +0x14C, +0x15C, +0x16C).

addresses.name: Patch_InterAiExpeditionaries_1
addresses.comment: Conditional jump turned into nop + jmp by disableInterAiExpeditionaries.

addresses.name: Patch_InterAiExpeditionaries_2
addresses.comment: Conditional jump turned into nop + jmp by disableInterAiExpeditionaries.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower
addresses.comment: **The general writer of CUnitPlan our_power / their_power.** 81 bytes of logic: `this->+0x35C = 0; this->+0x358 = SumOurPower(this, &this->+0x35C); this->+0x360 = 0; this->+0x354 = EstimateTheatreNeed(this, &this->+0x360)`, then, if either figure differs from the plan's by more than a thousandth (both sides are divided by 1000 before the comparison at 0x4B50E0 and 0x4B5112), posts `CSetPlanAttributesCommand(unit, 5, 3, 3, +0x35C, +0x360)` - stance 5 and air/naval 3 are the command's own "leave it alone" sentinels, so this call sets **only** the two power fields. Two callers: 0x4BA02E, inside CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63), and 0x48E553 in CEU3AI. Unlike 0x4B60F0 it runs for every country.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ComputePlanForces
addresses.comment: 3804 bytes, 0x4B5210-0x4B60EC (`ret 4`), immediately followed by one int3 and then 0x4B60F0. The sibling arm of 0x4B60F0, taken from 0x4B0B76 when `played_countries_array[countryId]` is zero - i.e. for a country no human is playing. It posts `CSetPlanForcesCommand` (0x4B6028) and **not** `CSetPlanAttributesCommand`, so it never writes our_power/their_power; those stay whatever CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower last set. Read as a call list and an extent only.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ComputePlanForcesAndPower
addresses.comment: 7818 bytes, 0x4B60F0-0x4B7F79, one exit (`ret 4` at 0x4B7F77) and no cold path past it. One caller, 0x4B0B7D in slot 73, taken when `gamestate->played_countries_array[agent->countryId]` is **non-zero**; the zero arm calls 0x4B5210 instead. It does two things: builds a per-subunit-type want vector and posts `CSetPlanForcesCommand` (0x4B7D9B) when it differs from `CUnitPlan::min`; and posts `CSetPlanAttributesCommand(unit, 5, 3, 3, ourPower, theirPower)` at 0x4B7E87, the sentinels meaning that only the two power fields are set. **our_power here is NOT what CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower computes**: it is the plain sum of `CUnit::GetPower` over every entry of CAIUnit +0x11C, with no `oob_level == 4` filter and no fort bonus. their_power comes from `CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed`, whose return value (a division count) is multiplied by a shortage factor from CCountry +0x590 and by 3 to seed the brigade demand. Abuts 0x4B5210 with a single int3 between - new for trap 2's list.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_FuelIncome
addresses.comment: `CCountry::GetDailyIncome(FUEL)` inlined. The seven loads at 0x4B64D2..0x4B64FA are CCountry +0x854, +0x77C, +0x908, +0x878, +0x8C0, +0xA70 and +0x9E0, all added and divided by 1000 into a float. They are exactly GetDailyIncome's (0xF1830) pool bases +0x850, +0x778, +0x904, +0x874, +0x8BC, +0xA6C and +0x9DC taken at goods category index 1, so every one of them is a pool's `fuel` member at pool+0xC. The `convoyed_in` pool (base +0x79C) is absent, which is the same skip GetDailyIncome makes for categories 0 and 1.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_FuelExpense
addresses.comment: `CCountry::GetDailyExpense(FUEL)` inlined, and the matching half of 0x4B64D2: CCountry +0x9BC - +0x830 - +0x92C + +0x998 + +0x8E4 + +0x7C4 + +0x7E8, divided by 1000. The two subtractions reproduce GetDailyExpense's (0xF1950) own two, at pool bases +0x82C and +0x928. The result is subtracted from the fuel income at 0x4B6592.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_FuelShortageHalvesArmour
addresses.comment: The only consumer of the fuel balance in the force planner: **when the day's fuel balance is negative and the country is at war (CCountry +0xACC), the armour want and the mechanised want are both halved** (`fp+0x40 = fp+0x44 = fp+0x2C / 2` at 0x4B65B4..0x4B65C1). Nothing else in 0x4B60F0 reads either fuel figure.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_LandTypeFallbackChain
addresses.comment: 0x4B65DD..0x4B683E, the substitution ladder: eight `unit_available[type] && SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy(tag, type)` tests, each falling back to a cheaper type when it fails. battleship -> heavy_cruiser -> light_cruiser; heavy_cruiser -> light_cruiser; mechanized -> motorized -> infantry; armor -> light_armor -> whatever the mechanised chain settled on; bergsjaeger -> infantry; garrison -> infantry. This is where a mod's `usable_by` blocks and its technology tree decide what the AI asks for instead of its first choice.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_LandWants
addresses.comment: The five stores that put the whole land order of battle into the want vector, 0x4B684D..0x4B6879: want[bergsjaeger-or-infantry] += the mountain share, want[armour chain] += the armour share, want[mech chain] += the same share again, want[garrison-or-infantry] += min(round(theatre->areas_count * shortage * 3), brigadeDemand), want[infantry] += whatever is left of brigadeDemand after the other four, floored at zero (0x4B65D9). The mountain share is brigadeDemand * (mountain provinces / all provinces) * 0.5; the armour share is brigadeDemand * (plains provinces / all provinces) * CCountry +0x594 / 1000, which is zero unless something writes +0x594.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_AirborneAndMarineWant
addresses.comment: w = max(invasion weight, base_ic / 40); then want[paratrooper] += ceil(w/2) and want[marine] = max(floor(w/2), theatre->areas_count), each only when the type passes the availability gate - paratroopers additionally need transport_plane to pass. The invasion weight is counted at 0x4B69A0..0x4B6AFB: one per plan objective province that an enemy holds and whose area is not adjacent to our capital's area, plus one more if that area has over 5 provinces and one more over 10. The whole block is skipped unless the country's base_ic (+0x604) is at least 50 and the agent's theatre is the capital's theatre.

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_EscortRatios
addresses.comment: **The escort fleet, sized off convoy tonnage.** T = sum of CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports over CCountry +0xA0 (the convoy list). The five libdivide sequences at 0x4B7B11..0x4B7B6A are T/20, T/35, T/50, T/100 and T/200, applied as **floors** (a max, not a sum) on want[destroyer], want[light_cruiser], want[heavy_cruiser], want[capital ship] and want[carrier] respectively. Only reached when the agent's theatre is the capital's theatre (0x4B7ACC).

addresses.name: ComputePlanForces_PostIfChanged
addresses.comment: The gate on the two commands. It compares the want vector element by element against `CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted` (+0x26C/+0x270) and posts `CSetPlanForcesCommand` only when the sizes differ or any entry does; `CSetPlanAttributesCommand` is then posted unconditionally at 0x4B7E87. The stack at that call is (this, unit, 5, 3, 3, our_power = fp+0x4C, their_power = fp+0x18) - `ret 0x1C` over seven dwords, which settles the argument order FINDINGS-power.md gives.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed
addresses.comment: 4507 bytes, recursive into neighbouring regions, and **the only place their_power is computed**. Two early exits: if the region's first province is controlled by an enemy it answers `CountEnemyUnitsInArea(&country->strategy, region, 0)` and touches nothing; and it answers 0 when a country-database comparison matches. Otherwise it walks the agent's front-province vector at CAIUnit +0xC0 and, for each province adjacent to this region across a usable edge, accumulates `enemyStrength * weight / 1000` into `*theirPowerOut`. `enemyStrength` is the sum of `CUnit::GetPower` over the hostile units standing in the province; `weight` is 1000, 2000 when at war and this is not an agreement border, 500 when it is neither, halved again when a relation test passes. Reads `defines.lua`'s `diplomacy.NAP_UNBREAKABLE_MONTHS` at 0x4B8985 and refuses to treat a border as a front while the NAP is younger than `NAP_UNBREAKABLE_MONTHS * 2 / 3` months. Four callers: 0x4B9155 (itself), 0x4B966C, 0x4BF9F3, 0x4C453C.
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed(CAIUnit* this, COwnerArea* region, int* theirPowerOut, CList* visited, bool relaxed)

addresses.name: CAIUnit_SumOurPower
addresses.comment: **our_power, in full.** Walks the agent's land-unit vector at CAIUnit +0x11C (rebuilt by slot 78 earlier in the same tick) and for each unit whose `oob_level` is exactly 4 - a division - takes `CUnit::GetPower` (slot 27, 0x1C73F0). A division that is **not** moving (`+0x2CC == 0`), whose order is neither kind 0x4E5 nor 0x56C or whose order answers false to slot 24, and whose plan stance is **below 3**, is credited a fort bonus: `power = power * (1000 + fortLevel * 80) / 1000`, where `fortLevel` is `province->modifiers[FORT_LEVEL] / 1000` and the 80 is an inlined `(int)floorf(80.5f)`. So the AI values a dug-in division at +8% per fort level and nothing else about terrain. Returns how many divisions it counted; the power goes to `*powerOut`. Named as a free function on purpose: `this` arrives on the stack, not in ecx, and `ret 8` agrees (trap 11). One caller, 0x4B508E.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed
addresses.comment: **their_power is a by-product of "how many divisions do I need here".** Takes the agent's area through CAIUnit::GetArea (a CTheatre), walks the CList of COwnerArea at CTheatre +0x84, and sums `CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed(region, theirPowerOut, &visited, 1)` (0x4B82F0) over them. The return value is a division count; `*theirPowerOut` is the enemy strength the same walk accumulated. Two callers: 0x4B50A8 (CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower) and 0x4B622B (0x4B60F0).

addresses.name: CAIUnit::SetUnit
addresses.comment: **Slot 63**, 0x4B9EB0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4BA05C (slot 64 abuts it at 0x4BA060). Returns at once if `this[+0x64]` is already set. Otherwise: if `unit[+0x198]` holds a *different* agent, that agent's slot 64 is called with the unit (detach); if both `this[+0x3D]` and `this[+0x3E]` are clear, `unit[+0x198] = this`; then `this[+0x64] = unit`. Finally it resolves the object id pair at `+0x68`/`+0x6C` through the game's id registry (0x1A857F0 for id types above 0x1268, 0x1A857F4 otherwise, via 0xA9DA00) and hands the result to 0x4BA5A0 (SetArea). **This is what settles CAIUnit +0x64 = CUnit\* and CUnit +0x198 = CAIUnit\*.**

addresses.name: CAIUnit::ClearUnit
addresses.comment: **Slot 64**, 0x4BA060 to the `ret 4` at 0x4BA291. The counterpart of slot 63, called on the *old* agent when a unit is handed to a new one (0x4B9EF8) and from CAIAgent's slot-68 path. It shares most of slot 63's body - the same calls to 0x486A70, CActivateUnitPlanCommand (0x5E5350) and CSetAIParamCommand (0x5E90B0) - but the detach half was not read line by line.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::GetWantedCommandLevel
addresses.comment: `this` in EAX. Named from its single use: CAIUnit slot 82 (0x4C0600) calls it at 0x4C0653, compares the answer against `unit->oob_level` (CUnit `+0x1F4`) and, when the unit sits higher than the answer, posts `CSetCommandLevel(unit, answer)` (0x1E1870) - so the answer is the oob level the agent thinks its unit should be commanded at. The body was not read. FINDINGS-aiunit.md lists this address among slot 73's callees known only as an address.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::SetArea
addresses.comment: Both arguments on the stack. It clears the dirty byte `agent[+0x87]` unconditionally, and then **does nothing at all unless the agent has a unit (`+0x64`), the area is non-null, and that unit's `oob_level` (CUnit +0x1F4) is 0** - that is, unless the unit is a theatre-level HQ. So an area only ever belongs to a theatre agent; the agents below it reach it through GetArea's walk to the root. Called from CAIUnit::Tick, from CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63) and from slot 76. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: CAIUnit::GetArea
addresses.comment: `this` in **EAX**, bare `ret`, no stack arguments. Walks `+0x40` (the parent chain) up to the **root agent** of the tree, calls the root's slot 65 (`[vftable+0x104]`), and if that answers true resolves the root's object id pair `+0x68`/`+0x6C` through the id registry (0x1A857F0 / 0x1A857F4, via 0xA9DA00). The object it returns is a CTheatre in every path that fills +0x68/+0x6C. Answers null when the predicate is false or the registry is empty. Called from CAIUnit::Tick (the weekly re-anchor), from 0x48A880 and from slots 78, 79, 80 and 85.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches
addresses.comment:
**RENAMES the inferred `CAIUnit_RebuildFrontFromOpsArea`**, which was true of the first 190 of 3339 bytes and silent about the rest. 0x4BBB50 to the `ret 8` at 0x4BC858, read end to end; **five int3 then a fresh prologue at 0x4BC860** (the old comment said no int3), one `ret`, no branch target past it, its one "list<T> too long" throw inside the body at 0x4BC1EF. Three callers: CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BB980), CAIUnit::SetOpsAreaAndReplan (0x4C05BD), CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree (0x4DCA7D). The second argument is read only in step 1; [ebp+0xC] is reused as a scratch slot afterwards.

Step 1 (0x4BBB50-0x4BBD43) clears the vector at +0xC0/+0xC4 and refills it with the provinces adjacent to the handed ops area that pass the three usual adjacency gates (edge kind != 3, template +0x22 and +0x13D), whose controller CAIStrategy::IsFrontWorthyEnemy accepts, and whose `ai_front_value` (CMapProvince +0x5C) is at least g_AiFrontProvinceThreshold (200). **So +0xC0 is the enemy-held front worth fighting over**, which that field's entry left unestablished.

Step 2 (0x4BBD49-0x4BC1E8) needs a unit. It clears the ordered map at +0x294, the vector at +0x2A4, and writes the constants 7 and 8 to +0x2B4/+0x2B8. Then per front province it averages CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces to each of the unit's plan objectives (CUnit +0x234) that lies in the same owner area, stores the mean in the map, and - when the means differ at all - rescales every value in place to `(max - v) * 100 / (max - min)`. So the map ends holding 0..100 with 100 on the front province nearest the objectives. Its subscript 0x4DCE40 has only two callers in the image, so 0x4D57F0 is the only possible consumer.

Step 3 (0x4BBFF9-0x4BC82F) clears the CLists at +0x1BC and +0x1CC, collects the distinct owner areas of the ops-area provinces we control (filtered by 0x7FD90), and then for each COwnerArea on `ourCountry->areas_first (+0xD30)` with its byte +0x68 set, not our acting capital's area and passing 0x7FD90: accepts it when OwnerAreaPathFind reaches it from one of our areas under OwnerAreaCost_Accessible in at most two hops **and not** under OwnerAreaCost_NoEnemy. For an accepted area it appends every one of its provinces to +0x1CC; picks the three ops-area provinces in our area nearest to it; runs CCountryTag::FindProvinceRoute from each; and appends to +0x1BC every province on those routes that we do not control and that is either at war with us, rebel, ours-as-rebels, or covered by the pair's undeclared war (an inlined UndeclaredWarCoversProvince, 0x763A0).

CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces reads +0xC0 at 0x4BD74B and +0x1BC at 0x4BD9C8, which is what ties the two together.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::RebuildAreaNeighbourProvinces
addresses.comment: 0x4BC860 to the `ret 8` at 0x4BCD59 - 1276 bytes; the second of the five calls CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree (0x4DCA70), CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BA5A0, at 0x4BB987) and CAIUnit::SetOpsAreaAndReplan (0x4C0550) all make, in the same order. It clears **two** vectors on the agent, `+0xA0`/`+0xA4` and `+0xB0`/`+0xB4`, with the usual zero-length memmove + `end = begin` idiom (0x4BC88D-0x4BC8DD), then walks every province of the ops-area vector it is handed and every 20-byte adjacency record of each (skipping edge kind 3, requiring template `+0x22` and `+0x13D`). The accept test at the tail (0x4BCC5B-0x4BCCA8) is `CCountry::IsSameSide(nbTag) || (diploStatus->+0x58 && !CCountry::IsEnemyTag(nbTag))` - i.e. a neighbour we may enter - and the survivor is pushed onto `agent->+0xA0` after three dedup walks (not already in the ops area, not in a local vector, not already in `+0xA0`). The middle, 0x4BC9DD-0x4BCC50, was not read, so which of the two vectors gets the other half is inference; the extent, the signature and the two cleared vectors are read.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::RebuildOpsAreaProvinceRecords
addresses.comment: 0x4BCD60 to the `ret 4` at 0x4BCDE5 and a second exit past the `_CxxThrowException` at 0x4BD268 - 1293 bytes. The third of the five replan calls, and the only one of the five that is **conditional**: every caller guards it with `unit->+0x208 == 0`, which is `CUnitPlan::stance == 0`, not `plan.active`. It resets the 0x3C-byte container at `this->+0x30C` through 0x4DCFC0 and the one at `+0x2FC` through 0x81C80, then for each ops-area province whose `+0x48` equals its own id (`+0xD0`) looks the province up in the map at `+0x30C` (0x4DCF30 is that map's operator[]) and, where the slot is still zero, allocates a 0x1C-byte record for it. Everything past 0x4BCE57 was not read; the name describes the two containers it rebuilds and nothing more.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces
addresses.comment:
**RENAMES the inferred `CAIUnit::ApportionOpsArea`** - it apportions nothing; 0x4C8EE0 does that from what this leaves behind. 0x4BD270 to the `ret 4` at 0x4BDCB5, 2632 bytes, read end to end; 8 int3 then a fresh SEH prologue at 0x4BDCC0, one `ret` in the body, no branch target past it, so trap 3 does not apply. Four callers: CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BB9A7), CAIUnit::SetOpsAreaAndReplan (0x4C05E8), **CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (0x4C3844)** and CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree (0x4DCAA8) - SetPlanStance calls only this of the five, because the score depends on CUnit +0x208.

It computes one float priority per province of the agent's ops area (+0x90), writes it into a fresh 0x1C record {province, 0.0f, score, 0, 0, 0, 0}, inserts the record score-descending into the CList at +0x2C0 (0x4DD4B0), indexes it by province in the ordered map at +0x2D0 (0x4DCF30), and sums every score into +0x34C. 0x4C8EE0 then divides a count among the provinces in proportion to `record->+8 / agent->+0x34C` by largest remainder, capped at `record->+0x18` - that is the apportionment, and it is not here.

The score, per province p: base 10.0. With `agent->+0x364` (frontier at war) clear it is `10*fortLevel + 10`, +10 when some neighbour belongs to a front-worthy enemy, and +20 for exactly `m mod n` of the n provinces by a carried-fraction spread (m = the +0x12C vector's count). With +0x364 set and plan stance < 3 it is `10*passableNeighbours - 10` when the owner area holds more than 5 provinces, plus `2*fortLevel + 20` unless the province has at most one passable neighbour and at least three front neighbours, plus 100 when the province is its own supply depot (+0x48 == +0xD0). With stance >= 3 it is 15.0 for a depot and doubles once per member of `agent->+0x1BC` the province is adjacent to. Then, for a theatre-level agent only, x3 when the province's CAreaBorder front is shorter than a fifth of the ops area; + `defend_prov` priority / 2 (peace) or / 8 (war) for an AI-run country; +100 per region (CProvince +0x358) whose byte +0x6D is set; x the thousandths multiplier from the CCountry +0xCC ratio; and 0 outright when the frontier is at war but this province has no war-candidate or objective-area neighbour.

fortLevel is `p->modifiers (+0x114)[0x50] / 1000`, modifier id 10 FORT_LEVEL. The CCountry +0xCC ratio averages that field over the distinct controller tags of this province's war-candidate / objective-area / front-worthy-enemy neighbours (an _alloca array, 8-byte stride, count at [ebp-0x14]) and compares mean*1000/ours against 150, scaling the score by max(r*1000/150, 50)/1000 when it is at or below - so 0.150 and 0.050 of a ratio, and +0xCC is the country's total brigade combat value.

Note `xor ebx,ebx` at 0x4BD50B destroys the agent pointer; it is reloaded from [ebp+8] at 0x4BD73F, 0x4BD8BF and 0x4BDA41.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier
addresses.comment: 0x4BDF30 to the `ret 4` at 0x4BE1B9 - 652 bytes, read end to end. The fourth of the five replan calls. It zeroes the three flag bytes `agent->+0x364`, `+0x365`, `+0x366` and then walks the ops area at `+0x90`: `+0x366` is set to 1 unless (gamestate `+0xD0C` is zero AND the province's controller is not us AND the owner AI's `+0x2C` is set); and for each adjacency neighbour that passes the template gates it sets **`+0x364` and `+0x365` together (written as the word 0x101 at 0x4BE11D) when we are at war with the neighbour's controller**, or `+0x365` alone when CAIStrategy::IsWarCandidate (0x4A9A30) answers yes for it. It returns the byte `+0x364`. So the function is the agent's answer to "does my operations area touch a shooting war, a prospective one, or neither".

addresses.name: Unit_GetAnchorProvince
PostCreateUnitCommand
addresses.comment: 0x4BEAD0-0x4BEC6B (`ret 0x10`), three callers and all three are the unit-split sites of the two AI bodies: 0x4CE8D3 (air, unitKind 2), 0x4D12EA and 0x4D1BA4 (naval, unitKind 1). Allocates 0x5C bytes, calls 0x147870 with nine dwords (object, the agent's tag halves from ESI +0x34/+0x38, the id pair, provinceId, unitKind, baseProvinceId, 0) and posts the command through the inlined CCurrentGameState singleton. The caller composes the new unit's id as `word[0x1A857EC] + 0x1268` with the serial from `[0x1A857F8]++`. unitKind 1 = navy, 2 = air at all three sites; 0 is presumably an army and was not seen.
addresses.signature: void __fastcall PostCreateUnitCommand(CAIUnit* agent@ESI, int* idPair, int provinceId, int unitKind, int baseProvinceId)

addresses.name: LandAttackOddsThresholdForStance
addresses.comment: 37 bytes, bare `ret`, **one caller in the whole image** (CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D7440), so the name is safe. `sub eax,2; je` / `sub eax,2; je`: stance 2 -> 5.0f [0x160A2EC], stance 4 -> 3.0f [0x171DC88], anything else -> 4.0f [0x171DF34]. The value is the odds estimate above which a candidate unit that is itself covering more than one enemy province is left in place. Note it returns in **XMM0**, not ST0 - it is a compiler-generated branch table for an inlined ternary rather than an ABI function, which is why the signature is spelled with a register argument.

addresses.name: LandUnitStrengthThresholdForStance
addresses.comment: 37 bytes, bare `ret`, one caller (CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D761B), result in XMM0. Stance 2 -> 0.7f [0x160A2E8], stance 4 -> 0.5f [0x15AB304], otherwise 0.6f [0x170AC00]. Compared against GetUnitAverageStrengthAndOrganisation's strength output: a land unit below the bar is not sent to attack. The same two literals the air body uses for wing fitness.

addresses.name: LandUnitOrganisationThresholdForStance
addresses.comment: 37 bytes, bare `ret`, one caller (CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D763B), result in XMM0. Stance 2 -> 0.75f [0x17179A8], stance 4 -> 0.5f [0x15AB304], otherwise 0.6f [0x170AC00]. Compared against GetUnitAverageStrengthAndOrganisation's organisation output.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::SetOpsAreaAndReplan
addresses.comment: 0x4C0550 to the `ret 8` at 0x4C05F2 - 165 bytes, read end to end, one caller: CAIUnit::DistributeOpsAreaToSubordinates (slot 83) at 0x4C156C. It clears the agent's ops-area vector at `+0x90` and assigns the argument into it (0x4DD860, std::vector::assign - the `test eax, 0xfffffffc` at 0x4C0597 is always zero because the clear just happened, so the 0x82190 arm is dead), then runs exactly the first five calls CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree makes - 0x4BBB50, 0x4BC860, 0x4BCD60 (only when `unit->+0x208 == 0`), 0x4BDF30, 0x4BD270 - and stops. No slot 82, no recursion into children, no 0x4C3330. **This is the one function in the image that writes another agent's operations area**, which makes it the whole of the top-down distribution path.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::MaybeSetCommandLevel
addresses.comment: **Slot 82**, 0x4C0600 to the `ret 4` at 0x4C078A, and the one CAIUnit slot that runs *every* game hour. It answers false at once unless the agent has a unit, the unit is **land** (CUnit slot 15, the `isLand` predicate), and the unit has children (CUnit +0x1EC, the count of the CUnitList at +0x1E4). It then asks 0x4BA550 for a target level, and if the agent has no parent (`+0x40 == 0`), the unit's `oob_level` (+0x1F4) is deeper than that target, and the owner's `CEU3AI +0x2C` byte is set, it allocates 0x68 bytes and builds a **CSetCommandLevel** command (0x5E1870) for (unit, target). So this is the AI promoting its own headquarters up the order of battle.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::DistributeOpsAreaToSubordinates
addresses.comment: CAIUnit slot 83, 0x4C0790 to the **bare** `ret` at 0x4C177A (it answers the byte `[esp+0x1F]`) with an early exit at 0x4C07F9 - and this is a fresh instance of trap 3: two `_CxxThrowException` arms for "list<T> too long" and "vector<T> too long" sit *after* that `ret`, running to 0x4C178E, and slot 84 begins at 0x4C1790. The entry test is the mirror image of slot 76: it answers false unless the agent's unit is **below** theatre level (`oob_level != 0`) or the agent records no area id pair, and unless its own ops-area vector at `+0x90` is non-empty. It builds a std::map<COwnerArea*,int> of the ops area keyed by owner area (0x4DD000 constructs it, 0x4DCF30 is its operator[]) and a list of the ops-area provinces with exactly one usable neighbour outside the area, then per child unit of its own unit builds a **CIDValue** (vftable 0x11EC094, 20 bytes: `+4 = 0x18D`, `+8`/`+0xC` the child's object id pair, `+0x10 = divisions * 1000` from CUnit::CountDivisions) to weight the child. Per subordinate it then (1) counts how many of the slice it computed are already in the subordinate's plan ops area (CUnit `+0x214` list) and skips when that count equals the plan's count at `+0x21C`, (2) posts `CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand(subUnit, &provinceIds)` at 0x4C1491, and (3) where the subordinate has an agent (`CUnit +0x198`) whose slot 65 answers true, calls CAIUnit::SetOpsAreaAndReplan (0x4C0550) on it with the slice. **So this is how an operations area reaches a subordinate agent.** The scoring middle, 0x4C0D60-0x4C13A0, was not read, so how the slice is apportioned is not established. `slotcalls.py 83` finds no dispatch of this slot anywhere in CAIUnit's code, with slot 82 as a positive control, so how it is entered is an open question.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::DistributeOpsAreaToSubordinates_Apportion
addresses.comment:
The largest-remainder apportionment inside CAIUnit slot 83, 0x4C0D47-0x4C0DE8. Per subordinate, with `weight` = the CIDValue's +0x10 divided by 1000 (its division count), `total` = the summed division count and `n` = the number of the parent's ops-area provinces lying in that subordinate's own owner area:

    exact = n * (weight / total)
    quota = (int)exact
    carry += exact - quota
    if (carry >= 1.0f) { carry -= 1.0; quota++; }
    cidValue->+0x10 = quota * 1000

`carry` lives in [esp+0x60], is zeroed once before the loop at 0x4C0BEA and is carried across subordinates, so the fractions are not lost - the classic Hare/largest-remainder split. The 1.0f is the float at 0x171DBAC and the 1.0 the double at 0x160A248. Note that the CIDValue's value field is **reused**: it holds divisions*1000 going in and quota*1000 coming out.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::DistributeObjectives
CUnit::MeanDistanceToProvince
addresses.comment: 0x4C1FC0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4C20B8 - 249 bytes, read end to end; slot 85 begins at 0x4C20C0. Collects the unit and its whole subtree with CUnit::CollectSubtree (0x1BDA90), sums CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces(member->current_province->id, provinceId) over every **land** member (vf[15]) that has a current province, divides by the list length, frees the list and returns the mean. **The float comes back in XMM0, not ST0** - a non-standard return the one caller reads with `movss`. Its only caller is CAIUnit slot 83 at 0x4C1022, where it is the score that decides which province of the parent's operations area goes to which subordinate.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Slot85
addresses.comment: **Slot 85**, 0x4C20C0 to the `ret 0` at 0x4C276E, and what CAIUnit::Tick runs at hour `(country_id + 3) mod 24`. It contains two copies of the **command-range calculation**: `radius = unit->regiments.first->definition[+0x180] * RADIO_<x>_LEADER_DISTANCE / 1000`, where `<x>` is picked from the unit's `oob_level` (CUnit +0x1F4) through a four-way jump table - 0 theatre, 1 army group, 2 army, 3 corps - and the define comes from `GetDefines()[+0xAC]` at `+0x21C`, `+0x218`, `+0x214`, `+0x210`. That is the same arithmetic 0x1B6980 uses for supply reach. It also calls GetArea (0x4BBAE0) and builds **CAttachUnitCommand** (0x5DE890). So the four `RADIO_*_LEADER_DISTANCE` entries in the mod's `defines.lua` bound where the AI is willing to put a unit, not only its supply.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ReadsRadioLeaderDistance
addresses.comment: `call GetDefines` at 0x4C288D, followed by `mov eax,[eax+0xAC]; mov eax,[eax+0x21C]` - RADIO_THEATHRE_LEADER_DISTANCE. The three sibling arms are at 0x4C28A0 (+0x218), 0x4C28B3 (+0x214) and 0x4C28C6 (+0x210), and the whole block is repeated at 0x4C2A4A/0x4C2A5D/0x4C2A70/0x4C2A83. **These eight, plus 0x4D454E, are the only reads of any `defines.lua` value anywhere in CAIUnit's code.**

addresses.name: CAIUnit_Slot85_OobLevelToRadioDistance_1
addresses.comment: Four entries, indexed by CUnit::oob_level (0-3), reached by `jmp [eax*4 + 0x8C2CB0]` at 0x4C2886. Each arm loads one of RADIO_THEATHRE / RADIO_ARMYGROUP / RADIO_ARMY / RADIO_CORPS _LEADER_DISTANCE from GetDefines()[+0xAC].

addresses.name: CAIUnit_Slot85_OobLevelToRadioDistance_2
addresses.comment: The second copy of the same four-way switch inside slot 85, reached by `jmp [eax*4 + 0x8C2CC0]` at 0x4C2A43.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::UpdatePlanAxis
addresses.comment: 0x4C3330 to the bare `ret` at 0x4C36EB - 956 bytes, read end to end. **This is where CSetPlanAxisCommand is issued** (the construction is at 0x4C35F4), and it is the tail call of CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree (0x4DCA70 at 0x4DCAD2), of CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (slot 77, at 0x4C382A) and of CAIUnit::Tick (slot 73, at 0x4B08D8). It returns without doing anything unless the agent has a unit, unless a theatre-level agent is the root of its tree, and unless `owner->+0x2C` is set - so **the AI never redraws a human-played country's attack arrows**. It then sets `+0x80 = 1` and, only when `CUnitPlan::stance` (CUnit `+0x208`) is **3 or 4**, scores every (ops-area province, plan objective) pair: 0x1CE350 must accept the pair and then the smallest CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces wins. The winner is handed to 0x1A1A90, which fills a local CList with a province route. The second list (the plan's `path2`) is left empty, because the `owner->+0x2C` test that chooses between the two destinations at 0x4C3578 can only answer one way after the early return. Finally it compares the new lists against the plan's `path` count (CUnit `+0x24C`) and `path2` count (`+0x260`) and their contents, and posts the command only if either differs.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::SetPlanStance
addresses.comment: **Slot 77.** 0x4C36F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4C38BD. Sets `this->+0x80 = 1` (which is also one of slot 73's gates, so +0x80 means 'a stance has been set'), and if it commands a unit posts `CSetPlanAttributesCommand(unit, stance, 3, 3, -1000, -1000)` - the 3s and the negatives are that command's 'leave alone' sentinels, so it sets the ground stance only. It then **recurses into every child agent (CAIAgent +0x44) with the same value** through [vftable+0x134] at 0x4C3818, and finishes with 0x4C3330(this). Its AI caller is CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4912D0) at 0x491B89, which calls it only when the new value differs from CUnit +0x208.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits
addresses.comment:
**Renamed from CAIUnit_ReorganiseAirUnits, and the extent corrected.** Body is 0x4CD890-0x4D051D, 11406 bytes - trap 3: the `ret 8` at 0x4CEE68 is a shared epilogue laid out mid-function, jumped *over* by three `jne`s at 0x4CEE1A/0x4CEE26/0x4CEE2F and jumped back to from 0x4CF9DE, 0x4CF9F6, 0x4D04CE and 0x4D04E6. The recorded 0x4CD890-0x4CEE68 was short by 5813 bytes, which is also where the record's '19 KB between the two bodies' came from (the true figure is 25264). functionStart is useless inside it - 28 isolated 0xCC bytes make it answer 0x4CDED6 for 0x4CEE6B and 0x4CF05D for 0x4D04EB, both inside the body.
AIR is now **confirmed from instructions**, three ways: it caches the type_index of all eight of CSubUnitDataBase's air role definitions and no others (+0x58 tactical_bomber, +0x5C cas, +0x60 cag, +0x64 strategic_bomber, +0x68 naval_bomber, +0x6C interceptor, +0x70 multi_role, +0x74 transport_plane, at 0x4CD945-0x4CD9AC); it reads CUnit::plan_air_stance (+0x20C) at 0x4CD9B5/0x4CEE6E/0x4CF908 and never +0x210; and a whole-.text `push imm32` scan makes it the only producer of air_intercept (0x4CF8B9), logistical_strike (0x4CFD54) and join_air (0x4CECE4), with strategic_bomb/nuke_mission at 0x4CFF98/0x4CFF9F and naval_strike/port_strike at 0x4D025D/0x4D030C loaded into a register instead of pushed.
REORGANISE is wrong: regrouping is phase 3 of four (0x4CE64F-0x4CED97, 1.8 KB of 11.4), and the mission blocks alone are 5.7 KB. Four phases: (1) 0x4CDA90 triage the +0xFC air-unit list, cancel a dead join_air, and flag a base with enemy land units marching in; (2) 0x4CE1E9 rebase, scoring candidate provinces from one of agent->+0x1FC/+0x20C/+0x21C/+0x22C by role on distance and airfield crowding; (3) 0x4CE64F split an over-mixed air group (CCreateUnitCommand at 0x4CE8D3 with kind 2, CTransferSubUnitCommand at 0x4CE90E) and join_air small ones; (4) 0x4CEE76 assign ground_attack, air_intercept, logistical_strike, strategic_bomb/nuke_mission and naval_strike/port_strike. Phase 4 needs force-or-at-war and plan_air_stance != 0, and is skipped entirely when a regroup is still pending (returns 1 at 0x4CEE12).
Gates: `if (agent->air_units_count (+0x104) < 1) return false` at 0x4CD8BA. Four wing fitness thresholds chosen by plan_air_stance (==2: 0.5f/0.75f, else 0.7f/0.85f) and halved for a CAG or interceptor group. One caller, slot 73 at 0x4B0C6E, under the topmost-agent test; the bool it returns ('I changed the air order of battle', [ebp-0xd]) is **not read**. The second argument is declared int because the body reads byte 3 of it at 0x4CE14E, which the caller's `push dword [esp+0xc]` leaves uninitialised; the value is never read back and has no effect.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits
addresses.comment:
**Renamed from CAIUnit_ReorganiseNavalUnits.** Extent 0x4D0880-0x4D3EA1 (13858 bytes) confirmed as recorded, including trap 3 twice over - the first `ret 8` at 0x4D08E5 is the entry bail and the bad_alloc throw tail sits past the real `ret 8` at 0x4D3E67.
NAVAL is now **confirmed from instructions**: CountShipsByRole seven times with branches on CSubUnitDefinition is_capital/is_transport/is_sub; CUnit::plan_naval_stance (+0x210) at 0x4D24DB and 0x4D3243 and never plan_air_stance; and it is the only producer in .text of convoy_raid (0x4D2C9F), patrol (0x4D3776) and intercept (0x4D3CCF), plus two of three join_fleet sites and all three rebase sites.
REORGANISE is wrong: fleet splitting is one of nine phases (0x4D19F6-0x4D2025). The nine: 0x4D08CF entry and area; 0x4D099D **withdraw from a losing sea battle** (per combat in CUnit::combats +0x114, the slot-17 ratio against 0.5f, then FindRetreatProvince and MoveUnit); 0x4D0B30 send an idle fleet home; 0x4D0D70 choose a home port, rebase, and split off the ships that cannot use it (CCreateUnitCommand kind 1 at 0x4D12EA, a CTransferSubUnitCommand per ship at 0x4D1341); 0x4D14F0 classify each fleet's existing order against support_attack/carrier_protection/join_fleet/convoy_raid/convoy_escort/patrol/intercept; 0x4D19F6 split fleets by role and join_fleet small ones; 0x4D2120 enemy-fleet survey; 0x4D2418 the 3.6 KB convoy/rebase block with the only MT19937Next (0x4D2BBF); 0x4D33C0 patrol; 0x4D3800 intercept and join_fleet.
Fleet composition rules at 0x4D1AD0: at most 4 capitals, 4 transports (and no carrier or capital with them, unless agent->unit->+0x284 is set), 3 subs and nothing but subs, 4 screens. Gates: `if (!force && !country->at_war && !country->+0xACD) return false` at 0x4D08A1, then `if (count(agent->naval_units) < 1) return false` at 0x4D08FE; force also clears agent->+0x85. One caller, slot 73 at 0x4B0CB3, with force = dailyStagger || agent->+0x85. The returned bool is set at only 0x4D1D32 and 0x4D1FFC, both in the fleet-split phase, so it means 'I split or merged a fleet' and nothing else - and slot 73 does not read it.

addresses.name: AIUnit_EstimateMoveTime
addresses.comment: Called from CAIUnit slot 69 (0x4D5510) and from 0x4C745B. At 0x4D454E it calls GetDefines and reads `[+0xAC][+0x1E4]` - **military.STRAT_REDEP_BASE_SPEED** - divided by 1000.0, but only on the branch where a virtual it has just called answers the save token **0x5A4**, the id CStrategicRedeploymentOrder carries. So it is estimating how long a move will take, with the strategic-redeployment speed used when the unit would redeploy rather than march. The name is from that shape; the body was not read in full.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Slot17_18_19
addresses.comment: **One body in three slots - 17, 18 and 19 all hold 0x4D5320** (CAIAgent leaves all three as the shared empty 0x60CD50). 0x4D5320 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D549B; slot 70 follows at 0x4D54A0 after two int3. It reads the unit through `+0x64`, builds a **CAttachUnitCommand** (0x5DE890) and calls 0x4D42D0 and 0x4D4070. Which of the three notifications it answers was not established.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Slot69
addresses.comment: **Slot 69**, and it is tiny: 0x4D5510 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D552D - ten instructions. It zeroes the word at `this[+0x2C8]` and tail-calls 0x4D42D0 with `this[+0x300]`. **Slot 71 (0x4D5530) abuts it with no int3 padding** - a fresh `push ebp; mov ebp,esp; push -1; push 0xC3CEB3` follows the `ret 4` immediately - so a padding-based walk reads the two as one function (trap 2).

addresses.name: CAIUnit_MoveAgentUnitToCommandProvince
addresses.comment: 0x4D5720 to the bare `ret` at 0x4D57E5, 70 instructions, read end to end; int3 x10 then CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D57F0. One caller, CAIUnit slot 73 at 0x4B0CB8, between the naval body and the land body. It MoveUnits the agent's own unit to the province in agent->+0x54, with safe and verySafe both 1, after requiring: the same topmost-agent test as the land body; CArmy::army_role (+0x2FC) == 0; agent->+0x54 non-null; !slot86(unit); !unit->retreat; unit->combats_count == 0; the unit not already there; and CMapProvince::CanUnitReach(agent->+0x54, unit, 1, 1). **Its two uses of agent->+0x54 are as a CMapProvince*** - as CanUnitReach's `this`, and dereferenced at +0xD0 for the province id - which contradicts the recorded `command_level_state int`; see the findings file.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits
addresses.comment:
**The land half of CAIUnit slot 73**, the third body it calls after CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890) and CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits (0x4D0880). Extent 0x4D57F0-0x4D7F7E, 10126 bytes, 2768 instructions, read end to end by walking every branch; two `ret 4` at 0x4D7F5B and 0x4D7F7B, both in the epilogue, so trap 3 does not apply. int3 x16 before it, int3 x2 and a fresh SEH prologue at 0x4D7F80 after. Trap 2: functionStart is wrong inside it twice (functionStart(0x4D6B45)=0x4D653C, functionStart(0x4D7D00)=0x4D78FB), both isolated 0xCC bytes. One dead 5-byte `jmp`+nop at 0x4D613B. One caller, slot 73 at 0x4B0D01: unconditional when the daily-stagger flag is set, otherwise one pass in three and only when at_war, in_undeclared_war or CCountry +0xF50 > 0. Return value set at exactly one place (0x4D7AB3) and never read.

ENTRY GATE: the topmost-agent test, then the +0x12C vector must hold at least one element, then **agent->+0x364 (frontier at a shooting war) and +0x366 must both be set** - so the whole function is dead for an agent whose operations area does not border an active war.

PHASE 1 (0x4D5944-0x4D678D) scores every enemy-controlled province of agent->front_provinces (+0xC0) into a fresh CProvinceFloat {vftable 0x15EB644, 0x18D, province id, float} inserted score-descending through 0x49C330. Base weight is a 0..500 ramp on map distance from the ops area's supply depot (flat 100.0 in arcade mode), x2 in an owner area of under 3 provinces, + half each enemy neighbour's plan-objective priority, + (operable land neighbours - 1) x 50 (x20 at stance 3, x10 at stance 4), +1000 for being on agent->+0x1BC and +500 for touching it, + 5*navalBase.level_max+100. At plan stance 3 or 4 only it also adds the province's own objective priority, 90 per plan-path province it is and 45 per one it touches (for both CUnit +0x244 and +0x258), 1000 when every operable neighbour is in agent->+0x1CC, **and agent->front_province_scores (+0x294)[province] through AIOrderedMap_SubscriptFloat at 0x4D5F6B - the single instruction that consumes CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches's output, and its only reader in the image**; plus 125/250 for a thin enemy salient and 200/400 for a split approach, and x0.25/x0.5 for a redundant pocket approach (dropped outright below stance 3).

PHASE 2 (0x4D6795-0x4D7CB9) walks the targets best first. A score of 500 or more promotes the local stance to 4. Candidate units are the agent's own leaf land units (slot 15) standing in the target's friendly neighbours, filtered on fuel, ai_held_back, slot 86, combat state and pending destination; each is scored enemyNeighbours*10 - slot89(target,unit)*10 (+100 when slot88 > 95, /10 when it belongs to another agent, /5 when it has a blocking order) into **CUnit +0x2B8**, with the number of garrisoned unattacked enemy neighbours in **CUnit +0x2BC**. Units are added best first while 0x4D93B0's odds figure does not fall; the attack goes ahead when the figure reaches 3.0 (1.1 at stance 4, 5.0 at stance 2 for admitting more units) and at least one attacker is movable, and is called off below 0.8 - both bars collapsing to 0.2/0.01 when the target borders two or more region groups or when an attacker is unsupplied and the target has a port. **A unit that cannot be spared from its own province gets `support_attack` (0x4D7AD6); every other one gets CEU3AI::MoveUnit (0x4D7AAE).**

PHASE 3 (0x4D7CBF-0x4D7F2C) sweeps agent->+0x11C's CUnit vector and stands down units whose attack is going badly - the combat's slot-17 ratio over 0.5 when defending, or a `support_attack` whose whole attacking side is pinned - but never one whose destination is on agent->+0x1BC.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds
addresses.signature: float __thiscall CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds(CAIUnit* this, CUnitList* ourUnits, void* theirCache, CMapProvince* target, CMapProvince* excludeProvince, int followCombats)
addresses.comment:
**Body read end to end 2026-10-02** (this entry previously said it was unread). 0x4D93B0-0x4D9E2A, 2682 bytes, 705 instructions, `ret 0x14`, answer in ST0. Two `ret 0x14`: the cold block at 0x4D9E0F past the one at 0x4D9E0C is the `their damage <= 0 -> return 50.0f` arm, reached by the `jbe` at 0x4D9D7E and reusing the same frame - trap 3 in form, and the recorded extent was already right.

**It returns our side's estimated damage output divided by theirs** - a damage ratio, which is what the name means and why it is compared against the 3.0/1.5/1.1 attack bars and 0.8 abort bar. Three constant exits: ourUnits->count < 1 -> 0.0f; theirCache->list->count < 1 -> 100.0f [0x1717BFC]; their damage <= 0 -> 50.0f [0x15C0548].

Per unit u of a side, the weight is `GetAverageStrength(u)/100000 * GetAverageOrganisation(u)/100000 * (engagement + helper(u))` - CUnit virtual slots 21 and 20, each answering the plain mean of the regiments' +0x5C/+0x60 (slot 21 sums +0x5C and divides by regiments_count, slot 20 the same over +0x60; the `* 1000` and `/ 1000` inside them cancel). The caller turns that into a 0..1 fraction in two steps - an overflow-guarded integer `v * 1000 / 100000` and then a further `/ 1000.0` in floats - so strength and organisation are held as percent-in-thousandths, 100000 being 100%. Our side does the integer step with the `imul`/magic-multiply fast path and __allmul/__alldiv for the out-of-range case (0x4D95DB-0x4D9615, 0x4D9662-0x4D969C); the defending side does the same division entirely in doubles, `/1000.0` then `/100.0` (0x4D9A74/0x4D9A84, 0x4D9AD6/0x4D9B08). Same value, different rounding. The four sums are then

    A = sum (1 + owner->modifiers[MODIFIER_SOFT_ATTACK]/1000) * def->soft_attack/1000  * weight
    B = sum (1 + owner->modifiers[MODIFIER_HARD_ATTACK]/1000) * def->hard_attack/1000  * weight
    C = mean over the units of  def->softness/1000
    D = mean over the units of (def->toughness/1000 * u->combat_defend_modifier_b * u->combat_defend_product / 1e6)

with `def = u->CSubUnitDefinitionPtr (+0xC8)` and `owner->modifiers = CCountry +0xDA8`, 8 bytes an entry (trap 5), ids 94/95. A and B are plain sums over the side's units; C and D are divided by the side's unit count (0x4D98D3-0x4D98E6 for ours, 0x4D9CE2-0x4D9CE6 for theirs). The defending side computes the same four with **defensiveness (+0x11C)** in place of toughness - which is the game's own meaning of the two keys, the attacker using toughness and the defender defensiveness. Then

    theirDamage = (1 - D_ours/100)  * (A_theirs * C_ours  + B_theirs * (1 - C_ours))
    ourDamage   = (1 - D_theirs/100)* (A_ours   * C_theirs + B_ours   * (1 - C_theirs))
    return ourDamage / theirDamage

so soft attack is weighted by the enemy's softness and hard attack by one minus it, and the enemy's defensiveness (or our toughness) is a straight percentage off the other side's output.

**`engagement` is where the two sides differ, and it is the interesting half.** For one of ours it starts at 1.0 and, for every combat in u->combats (+0x114) in which u is in `combat->defender->units`, is multiplied by `(1 - CCombat::GetAttackerStrengthShare()/1000)`, squared again when that factor is below 0.5 - a unit pinned defending contributes almost nothing. For one of theirs it starts at 1.0 and is **replaced** by `min(odds, 4.0) * 0.25` (0 becomes 0.01) for the **first** combat in which that unit is in `combat->attacker->units`, where `odds` is this function called recursively on that combat - so an enemy defender committed to an attack elsewhere is discounted by how badly that attack is going.

**The recursion is one level deep and cannot be more.** The self-call at 0x4D99CE passes `followCombats = 0`, and the combat walks that are the only route to it are inside `if (followCombats)`. It swaps the roles - arg1 becomes `&combat->attacker->units` and the cache's list `&combat->defender->units` - so the sub-question is "how is that unit's own attack going". `excludeProvince` is passed the current target there and is **dead in this build**: its only test (0x4D999A) sits inside the `followCombats` block, the top-level callers pass 0, and the province has already been tested non-null, so the comparison is always true at depth 0 and never reached at depth 1.

**arg2 is not a unit list, it is a 0x20-byte cache** the caller keeps on its frame at [ebp-0x110] (both call sites) and does not reset between the trials of one target: +0x00 `CUnitList*` of the defenders, +0x04 B (their hard-attack sum), +0x08 A (their soft), +0x0C C (their mean softness), +0x10 D (their mean defensiveness term), +0x14 their total brigade count, +0x18 the number of **distinct** provinces our units stand in, +0x1C the valid byte. Only +0x00 and +0x1C are initialised by the caller. The whole defending side is recomputed only when +0x18 changes, which is exactly right: the defenders' figures depend on our side only through `theirBrigades - 3 * ourProvinceCount` (the second argument of 0x4D8590) and through nothing else.

**The receiver is never dereferenced** - ecx is stored at 0x4D93CC and read back once, at 0x4D99C2, only to be forwarded to the recursive call - so `CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds` would be the more honest spelling but the body would read the same either way.

Two terms are **not** established: the helpers 0x4D8C50 (ours; `this` in ECX, args target province, our brigade total, our distinct-province count) and 0x4D8590 (theirs; `this` in **EAX**, args `theirBrigades - 3*ourProvinces`, clamped to at most 100 at 0x4D8A93, our distinct-province count). Both are large, both go through GetDefines()+0xAC, CUnit::CommandEffect, GetDifficultyCombatModifier, CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand, CProvinceTemplate::IsIsolatedLand and the encirclement helper 0xA6850, and both cache into CUnit (+0x2DC/+0x2E0 and +0x2D4/+0x2D8). Reading them is the next thing in this area.

**Correction to the caller's write-up**: the figure is *not* monotone in our committed strength. Adding a unit raises A and B but also moves C and D, which are means, and changing the number of distinct attacker provinces lowers `theirBrigades - 3*ourProvinces`. Monotonicity is enforced by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits, which backs the unit out when the new figure is lower (0x4D78F2), not by this function.

**Confidence.** Every arithmetic statement above is decoded instruction by instruction and a machine could check it; `inferred` is for three things only - that the two helper terms at 0x4D8C50/0x4D8590 are what they are called here, that the ratio is fairly described as "odds", and the order of magnitude the helpers contribute, which decides whether the four sums above dominate the answer or garnish it. `likely` would be the word for that and the merge takes only two.

addresses.name: AILandAttackOdds_ReadDefendProduct
addresses.no_signature: an instruction entry, not a function - it names one site inside rva 0x4D93B0
addresses.comment:
`mov eax,[esi+0xF8]` at 0x4D981F then `imul dword ptr [esi+0xF0]` here, then __alldiv by 1000 - the **CUnit defend-product pair** on one of *our* candidate attackers, inside CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds (rva 0x4D93B0). The product is divided by 1000 again in floats and multiplied by `def->toughness/1000` into the mean D, which ends up as the factor `(1 - D/100)` on the **enemy's** estimated damage output. Repeated at 0x4D9C3A on one of *their* defenders, where it multiplies `def->defensiveness (+0x11C)` instead.

**Promoted from `likely` to `confirmed` 2026-10-02 when the body was read.** `esi` is a CUnit by a chain, not by trap 12's neighbour fallback: scripts/fieldchain.py --holder 0xC8 --field 0x134 (window 0x200) puts both of this function's soft_attack reads behind a `[esi + 0xC8]` load, which is CUnit::CSubUnitDefinitionPtr; the same holder reaches +0x11C, +0x120, +0x124 and +0x138; `esi` is the receiver of `[[esi]+0x50]` and `[[esi]+0x54]`, which vtable.py --holding shows are CUnit/CArmy/CNavy/CAir slots 20 and 21, CUnit::GetAverageOrganisation and CUnit::GetAverageStrength; and esi is written only at 0x4D94CC and 0x4D994D in the whole function, each time from a unit-list node's payload, so the register that reads +0xF0 is the register that reaches all of those.

**The products are not always neutral, and not always 1000 either.** CUnit::CUnit (rva 0x1B5010) zeroes +0xDC..+0xF8 at 0x1B513C-0x1B514E, and the only writers of +0xF0 in the image are CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers (rva 0x1C3029, the 1000) and CUnit::AddCombatModifier (rva 0x1C3108, the multiply) - both reached only from CCombatant slot 19, i.e. only for a unit in a combat. So a unit that has never fought reads +0xF0 == 0 here and gets **no** toughness or defensiveness term at all; a unit fighting now reads its real land defend product; a unit that has stopped fighting keeps the last combat tick's value, because nothing clears it on exit.

addresses.name: AILandAttackOdds_ReadDefendProduct2
addresses.no_signature: an instruction entry, not a function - it names one site inside rva 0x4D93B0
addresses.comment: The second `imul dword ptr [esi+0xF0]`, preceded by `mov eax,[esi+0xF8]` at 0x4D9C34 - the same CUnit defend-product pair as rva 0x4D9825, but in the **defending** side's loop, where it multiplies `def->defensiveness (+0x11C)` rather than `toughness (+0x120)` and ends up as the factor `(1 - D/100)` on **our** estimated damage output. See 0x4D9825 for the chain that makes `esi` a CUnit and for the writer census; same confidence and the same reason for it.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan
addresses.comment: **Slot 76**, and the largest body in the class: 0x4DABD0 to the bare `ret` at 0x4DCA6A, about 7.8 KB, with early exits at 0x4DAC17, 0x4DAD9F and 0x4DAE63. It is the plan builder. It constructs **CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand** (0x5E60B0) and **CSetPlanAttributesCommand** (0x5E7710), copies objective lists through 0x4DD350, and calls CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BA5A0) and the object-id resolver 0xA9D390. Called through `[vftable+0x130]` at 0x48C064 (inside CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits) and at 0x34FB8C (inside CObjectivesEntry slot 22). Not read line by line - **this is where the next reader should start.**

addresses.name: FallbackOpsArea_FirstPostFallsThrough
addresses.comment: The join of CAIUnit slot 76's fallback epilogue, and the instruction that settles whether the fallback's two CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand posts are on one path. cfg.py gives it exactly two predecessors - 0x4DBCF5 (taken, the 'nothing to post' arm) and **0x4DBE39 (fall-through, straight out of CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree after the first post)** - so after the first command is posted control reaches here, not a return. Read off the edge list, not off one jump (trap 13).

addresses.name: FallbackOpsArea_EmptyListBeforeSecondPost
addresses.comment: `xor esi, esi` then three stores zeroing head, tail and count of the province CList at [esp+0x7C] (0x4DBE74/0x4DBE78/0x4DBE7F) and its trailing byte at 0x4DBE86, after the free loops at 0x4DBE3E-0x4DBE56 and 0x4DBE58-0x4DBE70. Between here and the second CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand construction at 0x4DBEE8 nothing writes those three slots, so the second command's payload is necessarily **empty**.

addresses.name: FallbackOpsArea_SecondCommandWithEmptyList
addresses.comment: `call 0x1E60B0` - CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand's constructor, taking `lea edx, [esp+0x7C]` from 0x4DBEE1: the same stack CList the fallback filled and 0x4DBE72 has just emptied. Guarded at 0x4DBEB4 by `unit->plan.ops_area_count (+0x21C) > 0` alone, which is a strict subset of the first post's guard at 0x4DBCE2/0x4DBCF5 (`count > 0 || the agent's own ops-area vector is non-empty`), so **this post never happens without the first and can only undo it**. Posted through the same channel in the shared epilogue at 0x4DC96F, so it executes second. Net behaviour of the fallback path: a unit the AI could not find a front for ends the hour with an empty ops area, whichever way the author's intent is read.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree
addresses.comment:
What slot 76 calls after posting its ops area, and what spends the province vector at CAIUnit +0x90. 0x4DCA70 to the bare `ret` at 0x4DCADA; 4 callers. In order:

    0x4BBB50(this, &this->opsArea)      ; refills the vector at CAIUnit +0xC0 from it
    0x4BC860(this, &this->opsArea)
    if (this->unit && unit->plan_active (+0x204) == 0) 0x4BCD60(this, &this->opsArea)
    0x4BDF30(this)
    0x4BD270(this)
    this->vf[82](true)                  ; the CSetCommandLevel slot
    for (child in this->children (+0x44)) ReplanSubtree(child)
    0x4C3330(this)

So this is the function the earlier record meant by 'slot 76's subtree': CSetPlanAxisCommand and CSetPlanForcesCommand are issued below it, not by slot 76 itself. Note it passes `&this->+0x90` to three callees, which is the independent confirmation that +0x90 is a container and not three loose fields.

addresses.name: AIOrderedMap_SubscriptFloat
addresses.comment: The `operator[]` of the AI's circular-sentinel ordered map for the instantiation whose value is a float: receiver in EDI, the key's address in EAX, returns a pointer to the value. Calls AIOrderedMap_Find (0x4DD130) and, on a miss, AIOrderedMap_NewNode (0x4DE4D0). **Exactly two callers in the image**: CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BBF98, which fills the front-province score map at CAIUnit +0x294, and 0x4D57F0 - which makes 0x4D57F0 the only possible consumer of that map.

addresses.name: AIOrderedMap_Subscript
addresses.comment: The `operator[]` of the AI's ordered map for the pointer-valued instantiation: receiver in EDI, key address in EAX, returns a pointer to the value, which the caller then assigns. 50 callers across the unit AI. Already described in the record's prose for CAIUnit slot 83 and 0x4BCD60 but never named; CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces uses it at 0x4BDC6A to put each 0x1C scored-province record into the map at CAIUnit +0x2D0.

addresses.name: AIOrderedMap_Clear
addresses.comment: Empties one of the AI's circular-sentinel ordered maps: receiver in EAX. Four callers - CAIUnit::~CAIUnit twice, CAIUnit::RebuildOpsAreaProvinceRecords on +0x30C, and CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces on +0x2D0 at 0x4BD305. Already cited by address in two existing comments; this names it.

addresses.name: AIOrderedMap_Find
addresses.comment: `find` over the AI's circular-sentinel ordered map: map in EAX, an out-iterator address and the key's address on the stack; the iterator comes back equal to the map's sentinel (`[map+4]`) on a miss. 13 callers. Already described in FINDINGS-subdivide.md's account of slot 83 as `0x8DD130 find(map@EAX, &outIterator, &key)` but never named. CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches calls it at 0x4BC166 while rescaling its own map, where the miss arm is therefore dead.

addresses.name: CopyObjectiveList
addresses.comment: Deep-copies a list of CObjective. For each source node it allocates **0x24 bytes**, writes CObjective's vftable 0x15C8BE0 at +0, copies `+0x4`, `+0x8`, `+0xC`, `+0x10` and the byte `+0x14` across, and links the new node in with `prev` at `+0x18`, `next` at `+0x1C` and a byte at `+0x20`. So a CObjective *is* the list node, and its whole layout is those five fields. Called from CAIUnit::Tick (copying CUnit +0x234, the plan's objectives, into CArmy +0x2EC) and from slots 76 and 83.

addresses.name: CList_InsertByDescendingScore
addresses.comment: `ret 8`, 8 callers, read end to end. Walks the CList backwards from its tail (`[list+4]`, prev at node +4) while the new item's float at `item->+8` is greater than the current node's, and inserts after the first node that is at least as large - so the list is kept in DESCENDING order of `payload->+8`. Appends at the tail when nothing beats it (bumping the count at `[list+8]`), and falls through to 0x5F5E0 to push at the head when everything is smaller. **This is what makes CAIUnit +0x2C0 a best-first list of scored provinces**, and it is the independent evidence that the 0x1C record's +0x8 is the score: it is the only field the comparator touches.

addresses.name: std::vector_assign
addresses.comment: `ret 4`. Copies a source vector's [begin, end) over a destination vector, reusing the buffer when it is large enough and reallocating through 0x142A60 / 0x93670 when it is not. CAIUnit slot 76 uses it at 0x4DBC43 to seed its +0x90 ops-area vector from a CAreaBorder's province array when the vector is still empty, and 0x82190 to insert into it when it is not.

addresses.name: AIOrderedMap_NewNode
addresses.comment: Allocates and links a node for the float-valued instantiation of the AI's ordered map. Two callers: AIOrderedMap_SubscriptFloat (0x4DCE78) and the inlined copy of the same subscript inside CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BC18D. The node layout is the family's {next, prev, key, value}; the caller bumps the size at `[map+8]` and then rebalances through 0x4DD980.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan
addresses.comment:
The battle plan's constructor, and **the whole of its layout in one place**. A leaf: the object arrives in EAX, nothing is pushed, and it ends in a bare `ret`.

It writes the vftable `0x15C8BFC` at `+0x0`, the save-token id `0x18D` at `+0x4` (CPersistent's own field), zeroes the word at `+0x8` (`active` and `allow_hq_reorg`), sets `stance` (`+0xC`) to 2 and `air_stance`/`naval_stance` (`+0x10`/`+0x14`) to 1, zeroes five CList heads at `+0x18`, `+0x28`, `+0x38`, `+0x48` and `+0x5C` (each first/last/count and a flag byte, 0x10 bytes), the loose dwords at `+0x58` and `+0x6C`, the `vector<int>` at `+0x70`/`+0x74`/`+0x78`, and the four dwords `+0x80`..`+0x8C`. `+0x7C` is the one dword it does not touch.

The last field written is `+0x8C`, so **CUnitPlan is 0x90 bytes**, which is exactly the room CUnit leaves between `+0x1FC` and `expeditionary_owner` at `+0x28C`.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan_Ctor_ZeroesUnnamed58
addresses.comment:
`mov [eax+0x58], ecx` in CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, with ecx zero - and, with the `mov [eax+0x6c], ecx` at 0x4DEA34, **the only write to either field in any CUnitPlan method**. The constructor lays the object out as: vftable, 0x18D at +4, the two bytes at +8, stances 2/1/1 at +0xC/+0x10/+0x14, four CLists (+0x18, +0x28, +0x38, +0x48), **an unnamed dword at +0x58**, a fifth CList at +0x5C, **an unnamed dword at +0x6C**, the `min` vector's three pointers (+0x70, +0x74, +0x78), then +0x80..+0x8C. It never touches +0x7C at all.

What is known about the three: the destructor frees nothing at any of them, so none is a pointer the plan owns; CUnitPlan::SetActive (the reset, 0x4DEB10) clears every list, the vector and +0x80..+0x8C and leaves all three alone; the applier at 0x1D0F00 copies active, stance, ops_area, objectives, path, path2, min, our_power and their_power from one plan to another and copies none of them; and LoadKey (0x4DF720) and SaveContents (0x4DF160) never mention them, so nothing about them reaches a savegame or the network. They are runtime-only, unread by the class itself, and cannot be named from the executable alone.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::~CUnitPlan
addresses.comment:
The plan's destructor: rewrites the vftable, frees the `vector<int>` at `+0x70` and clears `+0x70`/`+0x74`/`+0x78`, destroys the list at `+0x5C` and the one at `+0x48`, and walks the singly-linked nodes of the lists at `+0x38`, `+0x28` and `+0x18` freeing each through its `+0x8` link, resetting each head/tail/count triple as it goes. `this` is in ECX and it ends in a bare `ret`, so it takes nothing on the stack.

Called once, at `0x1B5799`, with `ecx = unit + 0x1FC` - CUnit's destructor destroying the plan it holds by value.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::SetActive
addresses.comment:
Writes the plan's `active` byte at `+0x8` (`CUnit +0x204`), and **when switching it off, resets the whole plan first**: the objective, path, ops-area and fallback lists at `+0x18`, `+0x28`, `+0x38`, `+0x48`, `+0x5C` and `+0x70`/`+0x74` are emptied, `stance` (`+0xC`) goes back to 2, **`air_stance` and `naval_stance` (`+0x10`/`+0x14`) back to 1** - the same values CUnitPlan's constructor seeds them with - both power estimates (`+0x80`, `+0x84`) and `+0x88`/`+0x8C` to 0, and the byte at `+0x9` to 0. Switching it on writes nothing but the byte.

Three callers: CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit (0x1D0F16), CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute (0x1E5451) and CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute (0x1E7822). The last cannot take the reset arm, because that command's constructor hardcodes its `active` byte to 1 at 0x1E77AD - so **the reset is reachable only from the two plan-level commands, both of which the interface posts.**

The compiler gave it a register convention: the plan arrives in esi, the flag on the stack.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::SetOpsArea
addresses.comment: Replaces the plan's operations area - the province list at `+0x18`/`+0x1C`/`+0x20` - with the one it is given, freeing the old one. Both arguments are on the stack.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::CopyObjectives
addresses.comment: Replaces the plan's `objectives` list (+0x38) with the caller's. It walks the existing nodes freeing each one, zeroes the list's first, last and count, and hands the list and the argument to the list helper at 0x4E3260. `this` arrives in EAX and the source is the one stack argument (`ret 4`). Called from the plan applier at 0x1D0F00 and from the matching plan command's Execute.

addresses.comment: Replaces the plan's `ops_area` list (+0x18) with the caller's. It walks the existing nodes freeing each one, zeroes the list's first, last and count, and hands the list and the argument to the list helper at 0x49C070. `this` arrives in EAX and the source is the one stack argument (`ret 4`). It walks the existing nodes freeing each one, zeroes the list's first, last and count, and hands the list and the argument to the list helper at 0x49C070. `this` arrives in EAX and the source is the one stack argument (`ret 4`). It walks the existing nodes freeing each one, zeroes the list's first, last and count, and hands the list and the argument to the list helper at 0x49C070. `this` arrives in EAX and the source is the one stack argument (`ret 4`). addresses.name: CUnitPlan::SetMinForces
addresses.comment:
Replaces the plan's minimum force composition - the `vector<int>` at `+0x70`/`+0x74`, which is `CUnit +0x26C`, already named `plan_subunit_wanted` - with the one it is given. The `min` key of a `unit_plan` in the save, and what `CSetPlanForcesCommand` carries.

The plan arrives in eax and the source vector on the stack.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnitPlan::LoadKey(CUnitPlan* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: A battle plan as the save keeps it: objectives, path, stances, and both sides' power estimates. **The keys its switch names**, 16 of them, one case each: `active`, `air_stance`, `allow_hq_reorg`, `debark`, `embark`, `fallback_line`, `min`, `naval_stance`, `objective`, `objectives`, `ops_area`, `our_power`, `path`, `path2`, `stance`, `their_power`. Read from the switch by reversing/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::GetPowerRatio
addresses.comment: `our_power * 1000 / their_power`, in thousandths, returned through the pointer in EDI and also in EAX. Seeds `*out = 1000`; answers 1000 when their_power (+0x84) is negative, **-1 when it is exactly 0**, and falls back to a 64-bit muldiv (0x4DFEC5 onward) when our_power (+0x80) would overflow `* 1000` (the guards are 0xFFE76C8C and 0x20C49B). Bare `ret`, 5 callers. CAIUnit slot 78 turns it into a commitment factor between 0.2 and 0.7.

addresses.name: ComputePlanWantedSubUnits
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ComputePlanWantedSubUnits(void* plan, CUnit* unit, void* area, std::vector<int>* wanted, int* ownStrength, int* areaStrength, bool useArea)
addresses.comment: Builds the order of battle a plan asks for. Called only from CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (rva 0x1BD240), twice, and it is what fills CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted. In order: (1) grows `wanted` to GetNumberOfSubUnits() entries and zeroes every one of them (0x8E1DB3..0x8E1E39, the loop bound is (db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4); (2) resolves about a dozen roles to concrete subunit types by taking the database's cached role definitions at db+0x2C, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C, +0x40, +0x50, +0x58, +0x6C, +0x7C, +0x80 and +0x84 (those eleven and no others; 0x1ADF70 reaches six more of the same block, +0x44, +0x78, +0x98, +0xA0, +0xA8 and +0xAC) and keeping each only if the owner's availability byte array says so - `country->+0xDF8->+0x27C[definition->type_index] != 0` and then the second test at rva 0x1A3BC0 - falling back to db+0x34 otherwise (0x8E1E3F..0x8E2075); (3) collects the unit's own regiments through rva 0x1BD930 and accumulates, into *ownStrength, each one's strength (CRegiment +0x5C) over its maximum times its organisation over CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation, counting them by category with the 0..6 classifier at rva 0x1A8540 (0x8E20C4..0x8E22A2); (4) walks the plan's province list at [area], and for each province its 0x14-byte border records at +0xD4 ->+0x90..+0x94, skipping type 3, accumulating into *areaStrength (0x8E2387..0x8E26E0); (5) turns that frontage into counts using the plan type at plan+0xC (2, 3 and 4 each select a different global) and several defines, and finally does `wanted[definition->type_index]++` once per requested regiment for each role (0x8E2FE0, 0x8E3027, 0x8E31B6, 0x8E31E2). `useArea` switches the source of the scope: with it set the caller supplies `area` and the regiment collection is filtered by it; with it clear the unit's whole OOB is used and `area` is the plan's own province list. Returns nothing - eax is zero on every path and neither call site reads it.

addresses.name: CAIInvasion::GetTransports
addresses.comment: lea eax,[ecx+0x64]; ret. Vftable slot 61, and whoslot.py finds exactly one holder (CAIInvasion vft 0x15EBAE4), so this is not a folded stub. +0x64 is the naval list, proved by AddUnit's CUnit slot 16 (IsNaval) branch. Note slot 60 (0x791940, lea eax,[ecx+0x54], the land list) is NOT safe to name this way: it has two holders, the other being CGraphicalTableLedger slot 17.

addresses.name: GetSubUnitList
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetSubUnitList`. Builds the database if it does not exist yet, then returns &g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x1C - the array of every subunit definition, in type_index order.

addresses.name: GetNumberOfSubUnits
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetNumberOfSubUnits`. Returns (g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x20 - g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x1C) >> 2 - the number of subunit definitions, which is the size every array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index is grown to.

addresses.name: GetSubUnit
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetSubUnit`. Wraps the C string in a CString and looks it up in the database's name hash map at g_CSubUnitDataBase+0x10, returning the definition or null. This is the by-name half of the database; GetSubUnitByIndex is the by-index half.

addresses.name: GetSubUnitByIndex
addresses.comment: The Lua global `GetSubUnitByIndex`. Returns g_CSubUnitDataBase->+0x1C[index] with no bounds check. The index is CSubUnitDefinition::type_index, the same subscript every per-type array in the game uses.

addresses.name: GetThreadLuaState
addresses.comment: **A Lua state per thread, and every AI Lua call in the image goes through it.** Reads the TLS array at `fs:[0x2C]`, and on a thread's first use takes `EnterCriticalSection(0x1B15418)`, news 4 bytes, calls `luaL_newstate` (0xD2B478) and `luaL_openlibs` (0xD2B46C), and runs `script/autoexec.lua` (0x15EC700). Returns a pointer to the slot, so callers do `mov edi, [eax]` to get the lua_State. That the AI needs a per-thread state is the other half of the evidence that it runs on TBB workers. See reversing/FINDINGS-ai.md.

addresses.name: LuabindDefCEU3AIRoutePredicate
addresses.comment: luabind's `def` factory for the instantiation `memfun_registration<CEU3AI, bool (CEU3AI::*)(const CTradeRoute&), null_type>` - vftable 0x15F2E7C, type descriptor name `.?AU?$memfun_registration@VCEU3AI@@P81@AE_NABVCTradeRoute@@@Z...`. It allocates 0x14 bytes, writes that vftable, and copies **the name from [ebp+8] and the member function pointer from [ebp+0xC]** into +8 and +0xC; the enclosing scope is passed in and out in EDI. Because the name and function are *arguments* rather than baked in, this one instantiation serves every non-const `bool(const CTradeRoute&)` predicate: it has exactly three callers, 0x8EFD23, 0x8EFD2A and 0x8EFD31, which take the three (name, function) pairs ('AlreadyTradingResourceOtherWay', 0x89B310), ('AlreadyTradingDisabledResource', 0x89B3E0) and ('IsTradeingAwayNeededResource', 0x89B480) off the stack in that order. **That is why counting mangled registration signatures does not count functions** - see reversing/FINDINGS-trade2.md section 1.

addresses.name: RunDailyEventPass
addresses.comment: 0x9C0A40 to 0x9C0C76, **bare `ret` and no arguments at all** - nothing on the stack and nothing in ecx. One caller: RunDailyPass at 0x683050. For each country in the database at [0x1A855A4] (+0x168 count, +0x16C array) it skips any country with CCountry+0xCF8 <= 0 (0x9C0B3E), then reads CCountry+0x8 - **the candidate list RebuildCountryEventCandidates built** - and skips the country outright if it is null (0x9C0B57). For each candidate it re-evaluates the event's `trigger` (+0x30) slot 6 against a stack CEventScope, calls CMeanTimeToHappen::GetChance(event+0xE4 @EAX, scope @EDI) at 0x9C0B85, draws from the Mersenne Twister and fires through 0x9C0C80(event, scope) at 0x9C0C49 when chance > r, where r = (tempered draw & 0x7FFFFFFF) * 2^-31 (0x160A2B8 is exactly 2^-31). It holds no state between days. image.functionStart walks back to 0x9C08F1 on this function because 0x9C0520 abuts it. See reversing/FINDINGS-events.md.

addresses.name: FireEvent

addresses.name: CMeanTimeToHappen::GetChance
addresses.comment: 0x9C4AB0 to 0x9C4B85. **Not thiscall**: `this` arrives in EAX and the scope in EDI, and the result comes back in st0 with a bare `ret`. days = (float)this->days (+0x8); for each CMTTHModifier in the list at +0xC (node {data, ?, next at +8}), if the modifier's condition slot 6 accepts the scope, days *= modifier->factor (+0x40) / 1000.0 - the double at 0x160A300 is 1000.0, so **factor is stored in thousandths**. If days <= 0 it returns 1.0f (certainty). Otherwise it returns 1.0f - 0.5f**(1.0f/days): the double at 0x160A308 is 0.5, so **`days` is a median, not a mean**, and the result is the per-day probability that gives a 50% chance of having fired after `days` days (2.28%/day at days=30, 50% at days=1). The code computes c = exp(log(0.5)/days) and then redundantly exp(log(c)) before 1-c, storing to a float32 between every step, so the answer is quantised at four points. That 0xC0B9B0 is log and 0xC0BAFC is exp is inference from the shape of the formula. See reversing/FINDINGS-events.md.

addresses.name: CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays
addresses.comment: 0x9C4B90 to the ret 4 at 0x9C4BE3. __fastcall(CMeanTimeToHappen* this@EAX, int* out@EDI, CEventScope* scope). *out = this->+0x8 * 1000, then for each node of the modifier list at +0xC (next at +0x8) whose condition object accepts the scope through slot 6 ([[node]] + 0x18), *out = *out * node->+0x40 / 1000 - the same +0x40 factor in thousandths that GetChance uses. **This, not GetChance, is CMeanTimeToHappen's workhorse**: GetChance (0x5C4AB0) has exactly one caller (0x9C0B85, the daily event pass) and appears nowhere as data, while GetDays has 13 call sites in 5 functions - 0x45CF8F, 0x4B9B4F and 0x4B9C9F (rebel movement, with CRebelType+0x44), 0x4C0676 (the rebel type choice, with CRebelType+0x28), 0x9C0F0D and 0x9C0FFD in FireEvent, and seven in 0x9C56B0 (decisions).
