addresses.name: std::iostream_category
addresses.comment:
**Two instructions - `mov eax, 0x16F5204; ret` - and it is not half of building the exception.** It is `std::iostream_category()`: the address it answers is the static `_Iostream_error_category` singleton, whose vfptr at `+0` is `0x15A7A84` and whose RTTI type descriptor reads `.?AV_Iostream_error_category@std@@`. Its `name()` (slot 1, `0x794A66`) is `return *(const char**)(this+4)`, and `this+4` = `0x16F5204+4` holds `0x15A7A74`, the address of the literal `"iostream"`.

The three call sites are the three throw paths of `std::ios_base::clear` (`0x20B0`) and each uses the result as the `_Cat` half of an `error_code`:

    call  std::iostream_category         ; edi = the category
    mov   [esp+0xC], 0x15B4E4C           ; "ios_base::badbit set"
    lea   ecx, [esp+0x10]                ; the exception object
    call  std::exception::exception      ; 0x795991
    mov   [esp+0x20], esi                ; error_code._Val  = 1  (io_errc::stream)
    mov   [esp+0x24], edi                ; error_code._Cat  = this
    mov   [esp+0x14], 0x15A7BD8          ; vfptr <- std::ios_base::failure
    call  _CxxThrowException

So `ios_base::clear` throws `failure(msg, make_error_code(io_errc::stream))`, exactly as `<xiosbase>` documents, and the `failure` layout is {vfptr, `_Mywhat`, `_Mydofree`, `_Mycode._Val`, `_Mycode._Cat`}. `__cdecl`, no arguments, bare `ret`, pointer back in eax. The `_Generic_error_category` and `_System_error_category` singletons sit immediately after it, at `0x16F5208` and `0x16F520C`, with tables `0x15A7A5C` and `0x15A7AA8`; their accessors and virtuals are left on the frontier.

addresses.name: std::uncaught_exception
addresses.comment:
A five-byte `jmp 0x79CD77` and nothing else - `std::uncaught_exception()` tail-calling the CRT's `__uncaught_exception`. The handover's description is confirmed.

It has 16 callers and every one reads the result the same way, `test al,al` followed by a jump around a call: that is the `basic_ostream::sentry` destructor, `if (!uncaught_exception()) _Osfx();`. `std::ostream::write` (`0x664A30`) is the example the previous wave named - `0xA64B3B: call 0xB94AE9; test al,al; jne 0xA64B4B; mov ecx,edi; call 0x40A260`, and `0xA260` is already recorded as `std::ostream::_Osfx`.

No arguments, `bool` in al. Written `__cdecl` because the caller consumes nothing; the jump target's own `ret` is bare.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Callfns
std::ios_base::_Tidy
addresses.comment:
`ios_base::_Tidy()` - runs the registered callbacks with `erase_event` and then frees both of `ios_base`'s owned lists:

    _Callfns(erase_event);                 // 0x794AEE, with the literal 0
    for (p = _Arr;   p; p = next) free(p); _Arr = 0;      // +0x28
    for (p = _Calls; p; p = next) free(p); _Calls = 0;    // +0x2C

Both loops read the `_Next` pointer at offset `0` of the node before freeing it, which is the `_Iosarray` / `_Calls_t` layout. `__thiscall`, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Recorded here because it is the only callee of `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` that was not already named and it is what fixes `+0x28` and `+0x2C` as the two list heads.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Addstd
addresses.comment:
The increment side of the standard-stream reference count that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) decrements. Under `_Lockit(_LOCK_STREAM)` - the literal `2` passed to `0x79504A` - it scans the eight-entry pointer table at VA `0x174C818` from index 1 for a free slot or for itself, stores the index in `ios_base +8`, stores the pointer in the table and increments the byte at `0x174C840 + index`. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`.

Recorded here rather than left on the frontier because it is the evidence that `ios_base +8` is the standard-stream index and that the byte array at `0x174C840` is a refcount - without it the guard at the top of `0x794BAE` is unreadable.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor
addresses.comment:
**Confirmed: this is the `ios_base` destructor**, specifically the out-of-line static body that MSVC's `virtual ~ios_base()` consists of a single call to. The earlier report guessed right.

    if (_Stdstr == 0 || --_Stdstr_refs[_Stdstr] <= 0) {
        _Tidy();                                  // 0x794B15
        if (_Ploc) { _Ploc->~locale(); free(_Ploc); }
    }

The guard is the standard-stream reference count. `ios_base +8` is the slot index into an eight-entry table of standard streams at VA `0x174C818` with a parallel byte refcount array at VA `0x174C840`; this function decrements that byte and returns without tearing anything down while it is still positive, so `cout`/`cerr`/`clog` survive every `ios_base::Init` but the last. `std::ios_base::_Addstd` (`0x794B59`) is the only other code in the image that touches either table, and it increments exactly the byte this decrements.

When it does tear down: `_Tidy()` releases the `_Arr` and `_Calls` lists (`+0x28`, `+0x2C`), then `_Ploc` at `+0x30` gets `std::locale::~locale` (`0x2EE40`, `this` in `ecx`) followed by `free` (`0x795F9B`, which is what `operator delete` folded to here).

**How the 700 call sites read.** Every one of them is a derived class destroying its `ios_base` base, and each writes the `ios_base` virtual table `0x15A7B8C` into the object immediately before the call - textbook base-subobject destruction with the vfptr reset. `LogRecord::Flush` (`0x24B0`) is the example the handover named:

    lea esi, [eax+0x78]          ; the ios_base subobject inside the record
    push esi; call LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct
    push esi; mov [esi], 0x15A7B8C
    call 0x794BAE

`__cdecl`, one stack argument at `[ebp+8]`, bare `ret`, no return value. It is *not* itself virtual and sits in no class's virtual table; the virtual destructor that calls it is the scalar deleting destructor at `0x2210`, which is unnamed and left for the next wave.

addresses.name: std::_Lockit::_Lockit
std::_Lockit::Destruct
addresses.comment:
The matching `~_Lockit()`: read the kind back out of `+0` and, if it is below 4, leave the same critical section. `0xB958E8` forwards to the `LeaveCriticalSection` import. Seven instructions, no prologue at all - `this` in ecx, no stack arguments, bare `ret`, nothing returned. 47 callers, the same count as the constructor.

Spelled `Destruct` rather than `~_Lockit` for the same reason as `std::locale::Destruct` above.

addresses.name: std::exception::exception
addresses.signature: std::exception* __thiscall std::exception::exception(std::exception* this, const char** what) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**`std::exception::exception(const char* const& _What)`** - the base constructor of every standard exception in the image, not something built for `ios_base::failure`. It writes the `std::exception` vftable `0x15A7C88` at `+0`, zeroes `_Mywhat` at `+4` and `_Mydofree` at `+8`, then calls `_Copy_str` (`0x795933`) with `*what`.

**The parameter is a pointer to a `const char*`, not a `const char*`** - `mov eax,[ebp+8]; push [eax]` - which is MSVC's `exception(const char *const &)` signature verbatim, and is why every call site first parks the literal in a stack slot and passes that slot's address. Recording it as `const char*` would make every caller decompile with a bogus extra dereference.

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. 297 direct callers, of which the three in `std::ios_base::clear` are the ones the handover was looking at; the rest are every `throw std::runtime_error(...)` / `bad_alloc` / `bad_cast` in the game. The derived constructors are one instruction longer and sit right after it: `0x7959ED` (`bad_cast`, vftable `0x15A7CA8`), `0x795A16` (`bad_typeid`, `0x15A7CB4`), `0x402060` (`runtime_error`, `0x159FDA0`).

addresses.name: free
addresses.comment: A thunk to the CRT's free. Every string destructor in the executable calls it the same way - `if (capacity > 15) free(pointer)` - which is what BiceLib copies to give back a string the game allocated for it.

addresses.name: operator_new
addresses.comment:
**`operator new`, and so every allocation the game's own code makes.** Ghidra calls it `FUN_00b9602f`, and it is the function behind a `push <size>` / `call` pair - `push 0xB0` before a log record, `push 0x57C` before a country database. The size is the object's, which makes a call site worth reading: it is how big the thing about to be built is.

The standard MSVC body, a retry loop: call `malloc` (`0x796CC3`); on success return it; on failure call `_callnewh` (`0x79F4F7`) to give the new handler a chance to free something and try again; when the handler answers 0, **throw `std::bad_alloc`** - its vftable is `0x119FCE8` - through `_CxxThrowException` (`0x79894B`). So it never returns null.

The `mov edi, edi` it opens with is the two byte hot patch pad, which is why the body starts at `+2`.

addresses.name: _purecall
addresses.comment:
The CRT stub a class's own vftable holds for a method it leaves pure virtual - COrder's slot 16, the order type id, among many. It calls the installed _purecall_handler if there is one and otherwise ends the process through _amsg_exit(_RT_PUREVIRT), the R6025 "pure virtual function call" message, so reaching it is fatal. Nothing reaches it in a working game: every concrete class fills the slot. Three Lua registrations resolve here - CCommand::IsValid, CDiplomaticAction::IsValid and CDiplomaticAction::GetAIAcceptance - because those methods are pure virtual in the class that declares them; the findings used to name this address after them (Shared_GetAIAcceptance_IsValid) and no longer do.

**Read out in full**, because it is where a crash can be caught: `push [__pPurecall]` (`0x134D238`, kept encoded), `call [DecodePointer]`, `test eax,eax`, `je` past it, `call eax` with no arguments - and then `push 0x19`, **25 = `_RT_PUREVIRT`**, which is what identifies this function rather than one of the other handler wrappers in this CRT that also decode a pointer and call it.

**510 slots in the data sections hold this address and nothing calls it directly.** The game installs no handler, so reaching it is fatal as the comment above says; BiceLib installs one and saves the game before it goes - GameState/PureCall.cpp and reversing/FINDINGS-allocator.md.

addresses.name: v_sscanf_l
addresses.comment: The static helper behind sscanf, CRT source `v_sscanf_l`. Rejects a null string or a null format with errno=EINVAL (0x16) and _invalid_parameter_noinfo, then fakes a FILE on its stack over the string - _flag 0x49, _ptr=_base=string, _cnt=min(strlen(string), INT_MAX) - and tail-calls the INPUTFN it was handed. Exactly one caller, sscanf at 0x7964D4.

addresses.name: sscanf
addresses.signature: int __cdecl sscanf(const char* buffer, const char* format, ...)
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT `sscanf`, statically linked. The body is only the public wrapper: it loads the buffer into esi and calls the file-scope helper at 0x796466 with (INPUTFN=_input_l 0x7A1379, format, locale=NULL, va_list=&arg3), which builds a FILE on its own stack over the string (_flag=0x49 = _IOREAD|_IOMYBUF|_IOSTRG, _ptr=_base=buffer, _cnt=min(strlen(buffer), INT_MAX)) and runs the scan engine over it. **This is the single most-called unnamed function in the image, 168 direct call sites**, and it is how every loader turns a lexed token into a number: 152 of those sites push exactly three arguments and clean 0xc, with the middle one a literal format - `%i` 102 times, `%f` 28, `%u` 18, `%c` 8, and one each of `%x`, `%lld` and `%d.%d.%d.%d` - and the return is tested against zero, which is sscanf's count of fields assigned. The string argument is almost always `parse + 0x22C`, the lexer's current token text.

addresses.name: atol
addresses.comment: `strtol(nptr, NULL, 10)` - the body that atoi at 0x7969F1 jumps into, and separately the target of 8 direct calls of its own.

addresses.name: atoi
addresses.comment: `(int)strtol(nptr, NULL, 10)`. **291 direct call sites, the second most-called unnamed function in the image**, and the other half of how a loader reads a number: where sscanf is used for a value that must be validated, atoi is used where a bad token can silently read as 0. The body here is a four-byte alias - `mov edi,edi; push ebp; mov ebp,esp; pop ebp; jmp 0x7969DB` - because the linker folded two source functions with identical code, keeping one body and one thunk; 0x7969DB is that body.

addresses.name: malloc
addresses.comment: The CRT's `malloc`, and the only thing `operator_new` calls to get memory. Rejects a size above `_HEAP_MAXREQ` (`cmp ebx, -0x20`, so anything over `0xFFFFFFE0`), rounds a zero request up to one byte, and hands the rest to **`HeapAlloc(_crtheap, 0, size)`** - the heap handle is the global at `0x134D240`, created on first use. Answers 0 when the heap does; `operator_new` is what turns that into a throw.

addresses.name: _CxxThrowException
addresses.comment: The CRT's throw. Takes the exception object by address and a `_ThrowInfo` describing its type, and does not return - every caller has an `int3` after it. Reached from `operator_new` with a `std::bad_alloc`.

addresses.name: __alldiv
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT signed 64-bit divide (lldiv.asm). Dividend at [esp+4..0xB], divisor at [esp+0xC..0x13]; result in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). Truncates toward zero, NOT floor: it takes the absolute value of both operands, divides unsigned, and negates the quotient only if exactly one operand was negative (edi counts the negations at 0xB9998D and 0xB999A9, and 0xB99A1A negates when edi==1). 2032 direct call sites. This is the helper every 'x * 1000 / y' in the game goes through - the thousandths fixed point multiplies into a 64-bit intermediate to avoid overflow and then divides here.

addresses.name: __allrem
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT signed 64-bit remainder (llrem.asm). With the two saved registers on the stack the dividend is at [esp+0xC..0x13] and the divisor at [esp+0x14..0x1B]; remainder in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). **The remainder takes the dividend's sign alone**, which is what tells it apart from __alldiv at 0x799980: the two bodies are otherwise the same shape, but __alldiv has `inc edi` on both the dividend branch (0xB9998D) and the divisor branch (0xB999A9) and negates when exactly one operand was negative, while this one has `inc edi` on the dividend branch (0xB99A3C) and **none** on the divisor branch at 0xB99A56, so the flag counts only the dividend - and the tail tests it with `jns` rather than __alldiv's `jne`. It is signed, not __aullrem, which has no sign handling at all. 7 direct call sites.

addresses.name: __allmul
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT 64-bit multiply (llmul.asm). a at [esp+4..0xB], b at [esp+0xC..0x13]; result in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). Sign-agnostic: the low 64 bits of the product are the same for signed and unsigned operands, so MSVC emits this one body for both, and the sign lives at the CALL SITE - a 'cdq' before the push means the 32-bit operand was signed, a 'xor edx,edx' means it was not. Fast path when both high words are zero (0xB99B00, a single mul), otherwise the three partial products AHI*BLO + ALO*BHI + ALO*BLO. 1144 direct call sites.

addresses.name: __allshl
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT 64-bit left shift (llshl.asm). Value in edx:eax, count in cl, result in edx:eax, nothing on the stack, bare ret. Three cases: count >= 64 answers zero (0xB99B4A), count >= 32 moves eax into edx and shifts it by count&31 with eax zeroed (0xB99B40), otherwise `shld edx, eax, cl` then `shl eax, cl` (0xB99B3A). Sign-agnostic - a left shift is the same body for signed and unsigned, which is why MSVC emits one body for both. 4 direct call sites.

addresses.name: strlen
addresses.comment: MSVC's hand-written strlen - byte loop to a dword boundary, then the 0x7EFEFEFF / 0x81010100 zero-byte-in-a-word trick. Called by the sscanf helper to size the fake FILE's _cnt.

addresses.name: __uncaught_exception
addresses.comment: The CRT side of the above: `return _getptd()->_ProcessingThrow != 0`. Three instructions after the call - `call 0x7A0FFE; xor ecx,ecx; cmp [eax+0x90], ecx; setne al; ret`. `0x7A0FFE` is the per-thread data getter (59 callers across the CRT), and `+0x90` into that block is the in-flight-throw counter. Recorded here because `std::uncaught_exception` (`0x794AE9`) is nothing but a jump to it and cannot be read without it. No arguments, bare `ret`, `bool` in al.

addresses.name: _callnewh
addresses.comment: Calls the installed **new handler** and says whether to try allocating again: 1 when the handler ran and returned non-zero, 0 otherwise. The handler is kept encoded at `0x134CC04` and put back with `DecodePointer`, so it cannot be read straight out of memory. The game installs none that has been found, which means the first failed allocation throws.

addresses.name: set_purecall_handler_encoded
addresses.comment:
Stores its argument into `__pPurecall` (`0x134D238`) **without encoding it**, so it is the inner half of `_set_purecall_handler` and whatever calls it has to call `EncodePointer` first. The CRT startup at `0x79845B` is its only caller in the executable, and it passes an encoded null.

Named for what it does rather than `_set_purecall_handler`, because the function of that name in the CRT is the one that does the encoding.

addresses.name: _input_l
addresses.signature: int __cdecl _input_l(FILE* stream, const char* format, _locale_t locale, va_list arglist)
addresses.comment: The CRT's scanf engine - the format walker shared by every scanf-family entry point. 0x200 bytes of stack frame, /GS cookie, and the format loop compares against '%' , '*' and the length modifiers. Referenced exactly once in the whole image, as the INPUTFN constant sscanf hands to its helper, so in this binary it is reached only through sscanf.

addresses.name: strtol
addresses.signature: long __cdecl strtol(const char* nptr, char** endptr, int base)
addresses.comment: CRT `strtol`: forwards to the shared signed/unsigned converter at 0x7A2B19 as strtoxl(locale, nptr, endptr, base, flags=0), passing the process locale (0x16F5A14) while the locale-changed flag at 0x174CBF4 is still zero. Reached from atoi/atol; the sibling wrapper at 0x7A300C passes the same shape to a different, 64-bit body (0x7A2D6F) and is the _strtoi64 of the pair.

addresses.name: Return_1
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 1; ret` - the whole body, so the linker folded it and this one address fills a virtual table slot in several classes that have nothing to do with each other. It is slot 11 of CLandCombat, where it answers the combat kind 1, and that is written on CLandCombat's own slot rather than on the address.

addresses.name: Return_2
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 2; ret` - the whole body, so the linker folded it and this one address fills a virtual table slot in several classes that have nothing to do with each other. It is slot 11 of CNavalCombat, where it answers the combat kind 2, and that is written on CNavalCombat's own slot rather than on the address.

addresses.name: floor
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT `floor`, the SSE2 body, with an x87 fallback at 0xC09778 chosen by the `__use_sse2` style flag at VA 0x1BEC898. Takes the double on the x87 stack via the caller's push and answers in st(0). This is what `floorf` (rva 0x1FD0) calls.

addresses.name: _ftol2_sse
addresses.comment: **MSVC CRT `_ftol2_sse`, the float-to-integer conversion helper** - not a floor helper. It takes its argument on the x87 stack (nothing is pushed by the caller, which is why the signature has to say `@ST0`) and answers a truncated 32-bit integer in eax, via `cvttsd2si` when the `__sse2_available` flag at VA 0x1BEC9C0 is set. When it is not, it falls through to the x87 body at 0xC088A6, which is `_ftol2` proper and produces the full 64-bit result in edx:eax; that address has 26 direct callers of its own. The second entry point at 0xC0888C (`_ftol2_sse_excpt`, unreferenced here) is the control-word-checking variant. Paired with `floorf` at the sites the previous wave was describing: `CCountry::GetConvoyBuildTime`, `GetConvoyBuildCost` and `GetCategoryBuildDiscount` all do `floorf(10.5f)` then `_ftol2_sse()` and keep the larger of that and the computed value, which is the *at least 10* clamp - so the clamp reading was right about the effect and wrong about these two functions: neither is a floor helper, one is `floor` for floats and the other is `(int)`.

addresses.name: InitFixedPoint0_100
addresses.comment: A C runtime initialiser: floors the float 100.5 at 0x160A684 (via 0x401FD0, floor, then 0xC08870, float-to-int) and stores 100 in the global at 0x1A86CF4 - the fixed-point 0.100. **Not a define.**

addresses.name: InitFixedPoint0_200
addresses.comment: The same for the float 200.5 at 0x160A64C, storing 200 in the global at 0x1A86CD0 - the fixed-point 0.200.

addresses.name: InitCombatStatusShareLow
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` initialiser that writes g_CombatStatusShareLow (rva 0x16881E4) as `(int)floor(330.5f)` = 330, off the float at rva 0x120A6E0.

addresses.name: InitCombatStatusShareHigh
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` initialiser that writes g_CombatStatusShareHigh (rva 0x168818C) as `(int)floor(660.5f)` = 660, off the float at rva 0x120A654.

addresses.name: InitIneffectiveStrength
addresses.comment: A startup initialiser: loads the float `100.5` at rva 0x120A684, truncates it through 0x1FD0 and 0x808870 and stores 100 into `g_IneffectiveStrength` (0x16886CC). One of the 7299 `(int)floor(N.5f)` statics - the shape that makes a negative `GetDefines` result worthless.

addresses.name: InitDefine50Regiment
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` static initialiser that writes **Define50_Regiment** (rva 0x16886E8) as `(int)floor(50.5f)` = 50 off the float at rva 0x120A7B4 - the same literal as Define50, a separate translation unit's copy. Its address appears exactly once in the image, at rva 0x9400E8 in the CRT initialiser table.

addresses.name: InitMinimumBuildCost
addresses.comment: The same body as 0x8C3690 over the same float at rva 0x120A684, storing 100 into `g_MinimumBuildCost` (0x1688698). Two separate statics out of one literal.

addresses.name: InitDefine10
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` static initialiser that writes **Define10** (rva 0x168873C): `movss xmm0,[float 10.5 at rva 0x120A680]`, floorf (0x1FD0), the double-to-int helper 0x808870, `mov [0x168873C], eax`. Its address appears exactly once in the image, as a dword at rva 0x940198 inside the CRT initialiser pointer table at 0x9400DC..0x9401A4. **So Define10 is not a define**: it is a compiled-in `(int)floor(10.5f)` static of exactly the kind the record already calls k_thousandths_10 (0x16881A0), g_CombatModifierFloor (0x168868C) and g_IneffectiveStrength (0x16886CC), and no defines.lua entry can move it. It is also the clamp floor CUnit::AddCombatModifier reads at 0x1C30B6 - the same global FINDINGS-combatmods.md identified from the other end. project.json's comment 'Which define it is has not been established' is answerable: none.

addresses.name: InitDefine50
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` static initialiser that writes **Define50** (rva 0x168879C) as `(int)floor(50.5f)` = 50, off the float at rva 0x120A7B4, through floorf (0x1FD0) and 0x808870. Its address appears exactly once in the image, at rva 0x9401A4 in the CRT initialiser table. **Define50 is therefore not a define either**, and neither is Define50_Regiment (0x16886E8, initialiser 0x8C3780, the same float).

addresses.name: Define10_BuildCost
addresses.comment: A define, 10 - the floor of the float 10.5, taken at startup, the same literal as Define10 but a global of its own. The build cost and build time calculations multiply their technology total by it, so each point is 1% on the cost.

addresses.name: Define50_BuildFloor
addresses.comment: A define, 50 - the floor of the float 50.5 taken at startup, the same literal as Define50 but a global of its own. GetBuildTime will not let its first factor fall below it, and the manpower half of GetTotalBuildCost uses it the same way.

addresses.comment: CAIStrategy vftable (RTTI, base CPersistent). One per country - read live, 326 of them.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_vftable
addresses.comment: CAIUnit's vftable (RTTI), 90 slots. Slots 0-72 are CAIAgent's (vftable 0x15EB674, 73 slots); slots 73-89 are CAIUnit's own. Read out of the image: CAIUnit supplies its own body in 20 of the inherited slots (0, 10, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 25, 32, 49, 52, 54, 63, 64, 65, 69, 70, 71, 72) and in 17 new ones (73-89), so 37 bodies in all. The RTTI export's `introduces` list has only 34 of them: it omits slot 65 (a folded `mov al,1; ret`), slot 74 (a folded `mov eax,[ecx+0x64]; ret`) and slot 81 (the shared empty `0xABF890`). So `introduces` is not the same question as 'which slots does this class supply'.
addresses.source: reversing/FINDINGS-aiunit.md; slot map read out of the image at 0x15EC0B4, 0x15EB674 and 0x15EBAE4

addresses.name: vftable_memfun_registration_CEU3AI_bool_CTradeRoute
addresses.comment: Two slots: {0x920100 scalar deleting destructor, 0x90B370 register}. Its RTTI complete object locator is at 0x162B344 and the type descriptor at 0x1725638 names it `memfun_registration<CEU3AI, bool (CEU3AI::*)(const CTradeRoute&), null_type>` - the **non-const** of the two signatures FINDINGS-convoys.md found mangled names for. Written at exactly one place in .text, 0x8F6611, inside the parameterised factory 0x8F65D0, which three registrations share.

addresses.name: vftable_memfun_registration_CEU3AI_bool_CTradeRoute_const
addresses.comment: Two slots: {0x920100, 0x90B510 register}. Locator 0x162B2AC, type descriptor 0x1725548: `memfun_registration<CEU3AI, bool (CEU3AI::*)(const CTradeRoute&) const, null_type>` - the **const** signature. Written at exactly one place, 0x8F670B, inside 0x8F66D0, which bakes in 'HasTradeGoneStale' and 0x89B640. One registration, one function.

addresses.name: vftable_memfun_registration_CDiplomaticAction_bool_void
addresses.comment: Type descriptor name `memfun_registration<CDiplomaticAction, bool (CDiplomaticAction::*)(), null_type>`. Its one .text reference is the parameterised factory 0x8FDB10, which is called twice from CDiplomaticAction's registration chain (0x8ED418 and 0x8ED41F) and takes ('IsValid', 0x998420) then ('IsSelectable', 0xA788D0) off the stack. Both of those are slot thunks - 0x34 and 0x38 - so this one instantiation names **slot 13 IsValid and slot 14 IsSelectable**.

addresses.name: vftable_memfun_registration_CDiplomaticAction_GetAIAcceptance
addresses.comment: Type descriptor name `memfun_registration<CDiplomaticAction, int (CDiplomaticAction::*)(), null_type>`. Its one .text reference is 0x8FDB90, which bakes in the name 'GetAIAcceptance' (0x15EEBB8) and the member function pointer 0x8A3120 = `mov eax,[ecx]; jmp [eax+0x44]`. 0x44/4 = 17, so this entry is the proof that **CDiplomaticAction slot 17 is GetAIAcceptance**, with no inference left in it.

addresses.name: TriggerIndentUnit
addresses.comment: **Three spaces, and the whole of how a requirement tree is indented.** Every indent loop in every trigger renderer pushes this and 3 and appends it once per level, which is what makes the loops findable: scanning for this address is how the six scope triggers that indent themselves were found rather than guessed at.

addresses.name: GuiObject_instantTextBoxType

Unlike the textBoxType class it keeps no copy of its own name, so everything after +0x54 is shifted down by 0x1C and +0x54 is the font name. **Name deliberately ours** - no CInstantTextBox name exists anywhere in the image's RTTI.

addresses.name: GuiObject_checkboxType

Note that checkboxType and guiButtonType share one **type** class (0x1206AD0) but have different **object** classes: two keywords, one type, two widgets. Held in the window's unindexed vector at CGuiObject+0x304. **Name deliberately ours.**

addresses.name: GuiObject_textBoxType

addresses.name: CFixedWindow

addresses.name: CFixedWindow_CGuiObject
addresses.comment: The CGuiObject subobject vftable of CFixedWindow, at complete object offset 0x18, 44 slots (0x1602108 - the name tree container vftable - begins immediately after it in .rdata, which is why a naive 51-slot dump overruns into it). **This is the pointer CGui+0x5C holds for a window**, so every window offset read through that vector is 0x18 lower than the complete-object offset. addresses.name: CWindowType
addresses.comment: The class of a `windowType` entry in a .gui file - 284 of the 1547 entries in the live gui-type tree, against 274 top-level windowType declarations in the mod (the rest come from the game's own interface folder). CWindowType is a real name in the RTTI export, from CEU3DialogGuiType's hierarchy descriptor, but it has no vftable of its own there; this is it. Its +0xA0/+0xA4 are position x,y and +0xA8/+0xAC size x,y, both checked live against country_production's declaration.

addresses.name: vftable_CBillboardType

addresses.name: GuiType_positionType

addresses.name: CommandChannel
addresses.comment: 29 slots, no RTTI. THE BASE - its ctor calls no other ctor, and it holds _purecall in slots 6, 7 and 9, the slots the four subclasses fill in. Identified from the constructor's own `mov dword ptr [reg], 0x1607418` at 0x00B33A80, with reg holding this; ctor rva 0x733A60. The subclass ctors also write 0x1607518 and 0x1607504, but through this+0x7C or this+0x9C - those are the embedded TBB queue's, not the channel's.

addresses.name: GuiObject_guiButtonType
addresses.comment: The ordinary button widget class: 686 live, every one built from a guiButtonType, allocation stride 0x168. **Name deliberately ours**: the image's RTTI contains no name for this class - a sweep of every hierarchy descriptor in hoi3_tfh.exe finds CIcon, CButton, TButton, CFixedWindow, TWindow, CGuiObject and CStandardlistboxItem but nothing for buttons built from guiButtonType - so it is named after the .gui keyword its type carries. addresses.name: GuiObject_trackButton

addresses.name: g_DaysPerYear
addresses.comment: The double 365.0, divided into the elapsed day count at 0x532D8D so that `(CCurrentGameState +0xBDC - 43800000)/24/365.0` truncated is the calendar year. The same 365-day Clausewitz year BiceLib's utils::gameTickToParts assumes.

addresses.name: f_ClimateDegreesPerIndex
addresses.comment: The float 150.5f, converted inline to 150 at 0x8C078 and used as the thousandths of a degree per climate.bmp index step. The whole scale of the climate bitmap: 0.150 C per index, with index 100 as zero. No define moves it.

addresses.name: f_WindChillPerWindspeed
addresses.comment: The float 125.5f, converted inline to 125 at 0xB24EB and multiplied by windspeed at 0xB2506 - 0.125 C of wind chill per unit of windspeed, in the climate 5 branch only. No define moves it, and unlike the four latitude thresholds it is not cached in a static.

addresses.name: g_Float800Point5
addresses.comment: The float 800.5, read once in code, at 0x52E4D3 in CSpyPresence::CatchSpies, where it goes through floorf (0x401FD0) and a float-to-int (0xC08870) to give **800**, i.e. 0.800 in thousandths. Named for what it holds rather than for its one use, the same way CLASSES.md names Define10 and Define50 - which are the same floorf(N.5f) shape. Its role there: the home counter-espionage chance is scaled by `1 - 800*(1000 - mission_share[0])/1000`, so a country with no spies on counter-espionage keeps a fifth of the detection chance.

addresses.name: g_float_20000_5
addresses.comment: The float 20000.5. RunDailyRevoltRoll floors it and truncates it to the integer 20000 at 0x4C0AA8..0x4C0ABE and uses it as the divisor scale of its risk gate, giving threshold = round(revolt_risk / 50). A plain compiled-in constant with no defines.lua entry behind it, in the same family as the 100.5 and 200.5 at 0x160A684 and 0x160A64C, so it must not be named after revolt.

addresses.name: fAiCommitmentFactor_0_6
addresses.comment: `0.6f`, the commitment factor slot 78 picks when the power ratio is above 1.5 (0x4B1F9D). A compiled-in literal.

addresses.name: fAiCommitmentFactor_0_4
addresses.comment: `0.4f`, the commitment factor for a power ratio under 0.75 (0x4B1FE2). A compiled-in literal.

addresses.name: g_FogOfWarEnabled
addresses.comment: A dword with 17 code references. ClearIntelFunctor's serial body fills every province's per-country intel array with **0 when it is set and 9 when it is clear** (0x6881C5: `cmp byte ptr [0x170AD30], cl; setne cl; dec ecx; and ecx, 9`), and RefreshProvinceIntel tests it again at 0x689282 right after the UpdateIntel fan-out. 9 is the intel level FINDINGS-mapmode.md records for a country's own provinces, so clear means everyone sees everything. **The name is inference from that behaviour**; nothing in the image names it, and the other 15 references were not read.

addresses.name: g_LeaderSkillThresholds
addresses.comment: **The experience each skill needs**, ints indexed by the leader's current skill and shifted left 15 into the 48.15 fixed point before the comparison in CLeader::AddExperience: 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 12000, 18000, 25000, 33000, 43000 and 60000 for skills 0 to 9 - the same figures BiceLib's Hooks/CLeaderHooks.cpp carries once shifted - and then 100000000 for skill 10, which is 3276800000000 shifted and unreachable. **That is what caps a leader at skill 10**, not the `skill >= 12` guard.

addresses.name: g_NullDate
addresses.comment: Holds 43800000 = 0x29C55C0, which the record already identifies as the game's hour epoch (CCurrentGameState +0xBDC counts hours from 43800000 hours before year zero, and RunHourlyTick subtracts exactly this). Used as the **'never' value for a date field**: TradeRouteSetInactive compares CTradeRoute +0x84 against it before stamping a tick (0xA4D585) and CEU3AI::HasTradeGoneStale refuses to call a route stale while +0x84 still equals it (0x89B672). **The history subsystem is the second independent confirmation**: it is the default date of every CHistoryEntry (the base constructor writes the immediate 0x29C55C0 at +8 and then this static over it, at 0x200AA9/0x200AB0 and in every inlined copy), the default date of every CHistoryContainer (0x1F45BA) and what CHistoryContainer::Reset puts back (0x1F4768); CHistoryEntry::DateIsUnset (0x1EC6E0) is `year(date) < 2`, which is true of exactly this value; and it is the fallback the leader part of RunCountryDailyPass uses when a leader's history has no `rank` entry - a date no live tick can equal, so such a leader is never activated. 234 references in .text and **not one of them writes it**, so it is a read-only constant.

addresses.name: g_MapDefaultMapPath
addresses.comment: 'map/default.map', read live. Written by CMap::CMap at 0x48872C through MapPath. The first of the seven paths the cache stamp covers. The six resolved-path globals run at stride 0x1C: 0x130C750 default.map, 0x130C76C cache/time, 0x130C788 cache/navaldist.bin, 0x130C7A4 cache/climate.bin, 0x130C7C0 cache/provincecache.bin, 0x130C7DC cache/bboxcache.bin - all six confirmed live.

addresses.name: g_MapCacheTimePath
addresses.comment: 'map/cache/time', read live. Read by IsCacheStale (0x492207, 0x49225B) and WriteCacheStamp (0x492312). The file is four bytes and holds the stamp of the seven map files the cache was built from; it resolves into the per-mod user directory, Documents\Paradox Interactive\Hearts of Iron III\<mod>\map\cache\time, while the content files resolve into the mod folder under the install.

addresses.name: g_DayLengthByMonth
addresses.comment: Twelve int32 thousandths {-6, -3, 0, +3, +6, +12, +6, +3, 0, -3, -6, -12}, read by IsNight at 0xA73E4 as monthTable[month] x CProvince +0x388 / 1000 - the seasonal swing in day length, scaled by latitude. Since +0x388 is zero across the southern hemisphere the term vanishes there, so southern provinces get twelve-hour days all year. IsNight shifts the month by six where CProvinceTemplate +0xA2 is clear, which is the southern hemisphere.

addresses.name: g_ClimateHalfYearDays
addresses.comment: 183000, i.e. 183.000 days, file-initialised .data with one reader at 0x9827F in ComputeProvinceClimate. Half of it (91 days) is the fixed width of each pair of shoulder seasons and the rest, 183 minus the latitude-scaled winter width, is the summer band. Not a define and no code writes it.

addresses.name: g_WeatherHumidityPressureBase
addresses.comment: 1000, i.e. 1.000. The `1000 - pNorm` in CWeather::Update's humidity term, where pNorm is the province's pressure normalised onto [0,1000] between PRESSUREMIN and PRESSUREMAX. It has exactly ONE reference in the image, the read at 0xB2685: CWeatherManager::InitialiseWeatherState copies the weather define block only as far as +0xC0, and nothing writes this address, so the 0x3E8 the file initialises it to is what it holds for the whole run. NOT a define - no defines.lua entry moves the strength of the pressure-to-humidity coupling. It sits immediately after g_LOWPRESSUREOFFSET in the same cluster of cached weather globals, which is why it looks like one.

addresses.name: g_MaxSpyLevel
addresses.comment: Holds **10000** in .data - ten spies in thousandths - and **no instruction in the image writes it**, so it is a hard-coded ceiling and not MAX_NUMBER_OF_SPIES. Eight code readers, all espionage: 0x4D72D4, 0x4E8AC8, 0x4F7D12, 0x51F105 (the slider's placement cap), 0x52D4B4 (CSpyPresence::SetLevel), 0x52D642, 0x52E761 (the re-cap after a spy is caught) and 0x9BE191. The Lua API exposes the value as MAX_SPY_LEVEL. FINDINGS-script.md already records the address from the modify_spies work; this names it.

addresses.name: g_IneffectiveOrganisation
addresses.comment: **1000**, i.e. 1.000 organisation - a plain initialised static in `.data` whose four bytes are `e8 03 00 00` in the file, with no writer anywhere in `.text`. Read in the same three places as `g_IneffectiveStrength` (0x1BA2B3, 0x1B600C, 0x1CD50E) and always beside it: a zero-combat-width brigade counts towards its division's stats only while `strength >= 0.1` **and** `organisation >= 1.0`.

addresses.name: g_dynamic_tokens
addresses.comment: The map RegisterDynamicToken looks a key's text up in, so that names loaded from files get save tokens of their own.

addresses.name: g_random_seed
addresses.comment: the random number generator's seed, saved as `seed`

addresses.name: g_random_index
addresses.comment: The MT19937 draw index, at g_random_seed + 0x9C0. Zero means the state needs twisting. Referenced at 148 sites in 20 functions; 19 of those functions inline the whole draw rather than calling Random, which is the exhaustive list of places the engine rolls without going through 0xAA2F80: RunDailyProvincePass (for the on_encirclement on_action, not for revolt), CreateRebelsForFaction, 0x4FC100, RunDailyUndergroundPass, 0x52FD40, fourteen combat functions in 0x56xxxx-0x57xxxx, the daily event pass 0x9C0920, and ReseedGlobalRandom.

addresses.name: MonthLengthTable
addresses.comment: Table of month lengths in days (31, 28, 31, ...) used by the date helpers.

addresses.name: fAiCommitmentFactor_0_2
addresses.comment: `0.2f`, the commitment factor for a power ratio under 0.25 (0x4B1FB4) - the lowest bar the AI ever sets, and the one that makes a losing AI throw in 20%-strength divisions. A compiled-in literal.

addresses.name: fAiPowerRatio_0_75
addresses.comment: `0.75f`, slot 78's lowest ladder threshold (0x4B1FD5) and also the strength floor its reserve-recall loop demands (0x4B2BB5). A compiled-in literal.

addresses.name: fAiPowerRatio_1_5
addresses.comment: `1.5f`, slot 78's second ladder threshold (0x4B1F94). A compiled-in literal; see 0x1318064 for the three tests that settle it.

addresses.name: fAiPowerRatio_2_0
addresses.comment: `2.0f`, the top rung of CAIUnit slot 78's commitment ladder (read at 0x4B1F81). **A compiled-in literal, not a startup-cached define**: the file holds the float bits, `scratchpad/naval/definecache.py` has no entry for it, and a cached define is stored as thousandths into a `.data` global that starts out zero. The constant pool straddles `.rdata` and `.data` in this image - 0x131DBAC holds `1.0f` the same way - so being in `.data` says nothing. Also read at 0x4B908A and 0x46716C.

addresses.name: fAiPowerRatio_0_25
addresses.comment: `0.25f`, the ladder threshold below which the commitment factor drops to 0.2 (0x4B1FA7). A compiled-in literal.

addresses.name: __pPurecall
addresses.comment:
The pure virtual call handler, kept **encoded** with `EncodePointer` - so it cannot be read out of memory as a pointer, and a decode of null is what says none is installed.

Read only by `_purecall` (`0x7961D5`). Written only by the raw setter at `0x79F96E`, which has no caller, and by the CRT startup at `0x79845B` that encodes a null into this and four other handler globals. So it is empty in the game as shipped, and BiceLib is free to take it.

addresses.name: g_crtheap
addresses.comment: The process heap `malloc` allocates from, as `HeapAlloc`'s first argument. Zero until the first allocation, which creates it.

addresses.name: g_random_draws
addresses.comment: how much has been drawn from the generator, saved as `count` right after `seed` - the pair is what makes a save replay the same way

addresses.name: g_random_object
addresses.comment: A pointer to a 4-byte object (vftable 0x15FDF60) that every user of the global generator lazily creates before drawing. It carries no state of its own - the state is g_random_seed and g_random_index - so it looks like a lock or a debug hook holder. Read and written by Random (0xAA2F80), RandomThousandths, ReseedGlobalRandom and each of the functions that inline a draw.

addresses.name: g_CombatTactics
addresses.comment: The combat-tactic database singleton, created lazily by GetCombatTactics (0x39DA0) with `new(0x1C)`. Its +0x0C/+0x10/+0x14 is a vector of CCombatTactic*, each with its name at +8, and **it is the index space of CTechStatistics +0x24**: read live with BICE loaded it has 43 entries, 0 `nullCombatTactic`, 1 `tactic_basic_attack`, 2 `tactic_basic_defend`, ... 30 `tactic_advanced_defend` ... 42 `tactic_pakfront`, and the +0x24 vector is 43 long for all 108 countries. The count is the mod's; the structure is not.

addresses.name: g_CGainableTraitDataBase
addresses.comment: The gainable-trait database, 0x30 bytes, created on first use by 0x73930. Two nested std::maps: combat save token, then leader type, to a vector of CGainableTrait*.

addresses.name: g_CMap
addresses.comment: Pointer to the single CMap instance (the map and the definitions loaded with it).

addresses.name: g_MapLogic
addresses.comment: Written by InitMapLogic (0x88200) at 0x48822B, from that function's one argument, immediately before it allocates 0x2A94 bytes. So the global is set during the map-logic stage of CEU3Application::LoadDatabases, between the two technology phases. **What it points at was not read** - the name is from the stage, and the `0x2A94` object may be a different thing from the pointer stored here.

addresses.name: g_mediterranean_region
addresses.comment: A cached pointer to the region named `mediterranean_region`, looked up by name out of CMap +0x2A50 by the string hash table at 0x52A710 and stored at 0x48B6D0, inside the function at 0x489BA0. The name is the literal at 0x15BE1C8, and map/region.txt's third entry is `mediterranean_region`. The region object carries a std::vector<int> of province ids at +0x8/+0xC and its own name as a std::string at +0x18 (that is the field 0x52A710 compares). Read by the canal/strait passage tests at 0x4A7F80 and 0x4D5190. Not read by CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince, which checks only the other two.

addresses.name: g_black_sea_region
addresses.comment: The region named `black_sea_region` (literal at 0x15BE1E0, map/region.txt's first entry), cached at 0x48B734 the same way as g_mediterranean_region. **CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince rejects any candidate whose connected sea zone (CProvinceTemplate +0xA4) appears in this region's province vector** - the std::find at 0x894336-0x89435D, where a hit jumps to the next province. So the AI never plans an amphibious invasion across the Black Sea, and a mod changes which sea zones that means by editing map/region.txt.

addresses.name: g_baltic_sea_region
addresses.comment: The region named `baltic_sea_region` (literal at 0x15BE1F4, map/region.txt's second entry), cached at 0x48B79F. The second of the two blacklists CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince applies to a candidate's connected sea zone, at 0x894363-0x894381. Together with g_black_sea_region it is the only place the landing chooser consults the region database.

addresses.name: g_ignore_partisan_spawn_limit
addresses.comment: A one-byte global read at 0x50B46E by CanMobilizePartisans: when it is set, the underground's level is not compared against SPAWN_PARTISAN_LIMIT at all and partisans can be mobilised from any level. Its twin CanSpawnUnderground has no such bypass. No writer was found, so this is almost certainly a cheat or debug switch; the name describes the one use that was read.

addresses.name: g_InstantResearch
addresses.comment: The `instantresearch` console flag, a byte. Toggled at 0x4400A2, which prints `Instant research ON` / `Instant research OFF`. CTechnologyStatus::AdvanceResearch tests it at 0x532F87 and completes a level whatever the progress.

addresses.name: g_CCountryDataBase
addresses.comment: Pointer to the CCountryDataBase; null until the first use creates it.

addresses.name: g_NullLeader
addresses.comment: The shared empty CLeader, created on first use by CLeader::null (0x17F510). Sits four bytes before g_CTraitDataBase (0x16855EC).

addresses.name: g_CTraitDataBase
addresses.comment: Pointer to the lazily made object holding every CTrait (0x1C bytes); filled once traits load.

addresses.name: g_AiYesmen
addresses.comment: **The `yesmen` console cheat.** One byte. The command handler tests it at 0x4419CA, toggles it with `sete al; mov byte [0x1A8562F], al` at 0x4419D8, and prints 'AI now always responds favorably' (0x15B8598) or the off message - the `yesmen` literal it matches on is at 0x15B8590. Eight readers in the image and that is the only writer, so it is **zero in any game nobody has cheated in**. That matters because it is the second half of the `return 100` short-circuit in GetDiploScoreFromLua and in all five of its clones (0xA0DD14, 0xA0DE94, 0xA348AF, 0xA44734, 0xA448B4, 0xA44A34, 0xA44C04): `if (actor == player && g_AiYesmen) return 100`. FINDINGS-diplomacy.md read the condition right but concluded that a script's opinion of a human offer is never consulted; with the byte identified, the short-circuit **never fires in normal play** and the mod's Lua is asked about the player's offers like anyone else's. Its neighbours in the same handler are the other cheat flags - 0x1A8554F `nopopup`, 0x1A855F4 `spy`, and 0x170AD30, which project.json already names g_FogOfWarEnabled. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

addresses.name: g_save_token_count
addresses.comment: How many tokens the table should hold, checked against its length on every lookup so the table is rebuilt if tokens were added.

addresses.name: g_log_command_execution
addresses.comment: byte. When non-zero, Session::PumpCommands writes 'Executing command ' <type id> <serial> to the log for every command it runs (tested at rva 0x689855). What sets it was not found.

addresses.name: g_PersistentIdTable_HighTypes
addresses.comment: One of the two id tables FindPersistentById (0x69DA00) is handed: this one for an id type **above** 0x1268, the one at 0x16857F4 for 0x1268 and below. A `{?, bucketCount at +4, buckets at +8}` hash; the key is `(type << 16) + serial` modulo the bucket count, each chain node holding the next at +4 and the pair at +8/+0xC, and the object is the found node's payload **minus 8** because CReferenceObject sits at CUnit +8. CAIUnit slot 83 inlines the whole lookup four times (0x4C0C1F, 0x4C0E2D for this table, 0x4C0E67, 0x4C0F6C for the other) to turn its CIDValue weight list back into CUnit pointers; RunHourlyTick's unit-removal drain picks between the same two at 0x28227D and 0x28228E. The split at 0x1268 and the pairing with FindPersistentById are read; which kinds of object land in which table is not.

addresses.name: g_PersistentIdTable_LowTypes
addresses.comment: The id table FindPersistentById (0x69DA00) is handed for an id type of 0x1268 or below; see g_PersistentIdTable_HighTypes at 0x16857F0 for the shape and the readers. CAIUnit slot 83 reaches it at 0x4C0E67 and 0x4C0F6C, and the unit-removal drain at 0x28228E.

addresses.name: g_CustomGameSettings
addresses.comment: The custom game modifier settings singleton, 0xD8 bytes, fetched through GetCustomGameSettings (rva 0x1C4E0) and filled by LoadCustomGameSettings (rva 0x1F9A0). It carries the two tech decay month counts the decay pass multiplies by.

addresses.name: g_CDefines
addresses.comment: The single CDefines, made on first use by GetDefines (0x45D90).

addresses.name: g_static_modifiers
addresses.comment: The static_modifiers.txt database, lazily built by RebuildProvinceModifierValues at 0x49F40D..0x49F43E: operator new(0xBC), the shared container constructor 0x45BD30 (a 0x1FF-bucket hash at +0x0/+0x4/+0x8, an empty vector at +0xC/+0x10/+0x14), installed through 0x45C440. Everything from +0x18 upwards is a named CStaticModifier* - +0x40 is `manpower` and +0x48 is `revolt_risk`, both pinned by what the engine scales them with; the field order does not follow the file's order, so the rest are not named. It has no RTTI and its constructor writes no vftable, which is why no struct is declared for it. 60 references in 21 functions, including CCountry::UpdateIC and CAddCountryModifierEffect::LoadKey.

addresses.name: g_GameSettings
addresses.comment: Pointer to the settings singleton that settings.txt is read into (0x18C bytes). Pointer to the settings singleton (the same global as module + 0x16863F8).

addresses.name: g_ClimateLatitudeFloor
addresses.comment: (int)floor(250.5f) = 250, from the float at rva 0x120A688, written by the CRT initialiser at 0x8B1530 and read once, at 0x9821C in ComputeProvinceClimate. CProvince +0x388 at or below it means no season at all: the function returns with climate left at its default 3. On BlackICE's 2160-pixel map that is everything south of about 19 N. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_FixedPoint0_200
addresses.comment: The constant 0.200 in thousandths (200), built at startup by the initialiser at rva 0x8B1030 from the float 200.5. A general constant: the daily province pass caps its suppression term at it (0x49EEA2), and 0x4973E0 and 0x4A39B0 use it as a threshold. **The cap on how much a garrison can bend the daily revolt-risk step is this compiled-in constant, not a define.**

addresses.name: g_FixedPoint0_100
addresses.comment: The constant 0.100 in thousandths (100), built at startup by the initialiser at rva 0x8B0FA0 from the float 100.5. **A general constant, not a revolt one** - the daily province pass uses it as the per-day revolt-risk step and as the multiplier on suppression (0x49EB5D, 0x49EE7D), and the building-level change at 0x4A39B0 uses it as a threshold (0x4A3B1A). Worth knowing for the revolt model because **the plus-or-minus 0.1 a day revolt-risk step is this compiled-in constant and no defines.lua entry can move it.**

addresses.name: g_ClimateLatitudeSpan
addresses.comment: (int)floor(750.5f) = 750, from the float at rva 0x120A614, written by the CRT initialiser at 0x8B1560 and read once, at 0x9822A. The divisor that turns CProvince +0x388 - 250 into a 0..1000 season strength, so the winter band reaches its full width exactly at the north edge of the map. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_AIRWINDSPEEDMODIFIER
addresses.comment: The `weather` define AIRWINDSPEEDMODIFIER (defines.lua weather block, CDefines+0xEC+0x60), copied into this global at startup by CacheWeatherDefines (0xB5670). Every consumer reads the global, not the block - which is why a scan for `call GetDefines` + [+0xEC] finds no readers at all. Thousandths.

addresses.name: g_WeatherCloudBurnOffPerRain
addresses.comment: 200: cloud coverage burnt off per unit of precipitation, applied only where no front is over the province (0xB27C1). With the 10x humidity drain beside it this is what makes clear-air rain self-extinguishing while front rain persists. floor(200.5f); one reader. Not a define. Its effect is observable in a savegame: the saved cloud is the post-burn-off value, which is why `precipitation = 2 x (cloud + 0.2 x precipitation - threshold)` is what fits the no-front provinces.

addresses.name: g_LANDLOWTEMPERATUREIMPACT
addresses.comment: The `weather` define LANDLOWTEMPERATUREIMPACT (defines.lua weather block, CDefines+0xEC+0x44), copied into this global at startup by CacheWeatherDefines (0xB5670). Every consumer reads the global, not the block - which is why a scan for `call GetDefines` + [+0xEC] finds no readers at all. Thousandths.

addresses.name: g_WeatherWindspeedDecay
addresses.comment: 750: windspeed is multiplied by 750/1000 every hour in CWeather::Update wherever no weather front is over the province (0xB25AE-0xB25C5), so wind dies within a few hours behind a front. floor(750.5f), written once by its CRT initialiser at 0xCB391B and read once. CORRECTION: project.json's CWeather+0x10 comment says 0.980 for this decay; the bytes are `imul dword ptr [0x1a86f3c]` and 0.980 is a different global.

addresses.name: g_WeatherFiveHundred
addresses.comment: 500, read at three unrelated places in CWeather::Update: the sea's precipitation threshold, which is halved to 250 on land and dropped to 0 on land with no front (0xB2751); the frozen ceiling for the below -10 C creep (0xB2980); and the upper clamp on the infrastructure figure in the muddyness branch (0xB28C3). floor(500.5f), three readers - so it is one shared literal rather than three tunables, and naming it after any one of its uses would overstate the code. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_WeatherCloudGainUnderFront
addresses.comment: 100: cloud coverage gained per hour where the humidity-to-temperature ratio is above the terrain's threshold AND a front is over the province (0xB272D). The front case gains LESS than the no-front case because under a front the rain does not consume the cloud. floor(100.5f); one reader. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_WeatherTwoFifty
addresses.comment: 250, read twice in CWeather::Update's frozen branch (0xB2955): the precipitation above which sub -5 C weather counts as snowfall and freezes the ground at the full HOURLYFROZENINCREASE, and the frozen ceiling for the below -2 C creep. floor(250.5f); one site loads it and both tests use it. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_SPOTTINGCLOUDMODIFIER
addresses.comment: The cached copy of the `weather` define SPOTTINGCLOUDMODIFIER (CDefines +0xEC, block offset +0xB4), written by 0xB5961 inside CacheWeatherDefinesToGlobals. Read at 0x3200D in ShouldStartNavalCombat, multiplied by CMapProvince +0x8C (cloud cover) and subtracted from 1000. Together with SPOTTINGRAINMODIFIER these are the only two weather levers on naval detection anywhere in the image.

addresses.name: g_CBuildingDataBase
addresses.no_signature: a global, not a function
addresses.comment:
The one `CBuildingDataBase`, 0x30 bytes, built lazily exactly as `g_CSubUnitDataBase` is: every user does `if (!g) g = new 0x30 bytes, init`. The init at rva `0x5BD30` is shared with 198 other databases and lays out the first 0x18 bytes - `+0x00`..`+0x0B` a name -> `CBuilding*` hash map (count at `+0x00`, `0x1FF` buckets at `+0x04`, the bucket array allocated and zeroed at `+0x08`) and `+0x0C`/`+0x10`/`+0x14` a `vector<CBuilding*>`. Everything from `+0x18` on is this class's own and the init does not touch it.

**Five of those six slots are cached `CBuilding*` for well-known roles**, filled by the loader at rva `0xB769B` (the defaults, all five pointed at the built-in 'nobuilding') and rva `0xB78AB` (the modifier ladder): `+0x1C` air_base, `+0x20` naval_base, `+0x24` anti_air, `+0x28` underground, `+0x2C` industry. The setup at `0x968B8`..`0x96A50` turns four of them into a province's building shortcuts,

    province->+0x308 = province->buildings[ db->+0x24->index ]
    province->+0x304 = province->buildings[ db->+0x1C->index ]
    province->+0x300 = province->buildings[ db->+0x20->index ]
    province->+0x30C = province->buildings[ db->+0x28->index ]

where `index` is `CBuilding +0x54` and `buildings` is `CProvince +0x310`.

**`+0x18` is the sixth slot and is dead.** It is the first dword the class adds on top of the shared 0x18-byte base, so it is a member rather than padding, but no instruction in the image writes or reads it: the init stops at `+0x14`, the loader's defaults set exactly the five role slots, and the ladder has exactly five branches. The object is `malloc`ed and never zeroed, so whatever stands at `+0x18` is heap garbage, not a building.

GetRebelTypeDatabase (0x4BFE70) is its lazy getter; ChooseRebelTypeForProvince walks +0xC..+0x10 and 0x4BEF10, handed a freshly built name string at 0x4BFFD6, is very likely the by-name lookup - that call was not read.

addresses.name: g_CSubUnitDataBase
addresses.comment: The one CSubUnitDataBase, 0xC0 bytes, built lazily: every user does `if (!g_CSubUnitDataBase) CSubUnitDataBase::SetInstance(new CSubUnitDataBase)`. Layout as the constructor at rva 0x1ADEE0 and the four Lua accessors show it - +0x00..+0x0B a three-dword container zeroed at construction; +0x10..+0x1B a name -> definition hash map (count at +0x10, 0x1FF buckets at +0x14, the bucket array allocated at +0x18), which GetSubUnit searches; +0x1C..+0x27 a CArray<CSubUnitDefinition*> (begin/end/capacity), which GetSubUnitList returns by reference and GetSubUnitByIndex indexes, so the element stride is 4 and the entry count is (+0x20 - +0x1C)/4; +0x28..+0xAC a block of cached CSubUnitDefinition* for well-known roles, left uninitialised by the constructor and filled at load time; +0xB0..+0xBB a second three-dword container. The count at (+0x20 - +0x1C)/4 is what sizes every array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index, CUnit::plan_subunit_wanted among them.

addresses.name: Define10
addresses.comment: A define, 10 - the floor of the float 10.5, taken at startup. Thousandths, so 0.010. Ten places read it and they do not agree on a purpose, so the name only says what it holds. CUnit's supply and fuel consumption (0x1BB560, 0x1BB7A0) add `CRegiment +0xCC x this` to a potency whose base is 1000, so each point of that field is 1% more consumption. Elsewhere it is a floor on a multiplier (0x1C30B6 clamps 1000 + x up to it before scaling max_strength), a threshold (0x1C638A) and an additive base (0x1CDA8C). Which define it is has not been established.

addresses.name: g_save_tokens
addresses.comment: The tokens built into the executable, which BuildTokenTable copies into g_save_tokens_first by their own ids. The punctuation is not among them - the tokenizer holds ids 1 to 21 - and the loaded mod registers about as many again on top, which are heap objects numbered in load order.

addresses.name: g_next_persistent_id
addresses.comment: **The id generator.** One ULONG counter every runtime-created persistent takes its id from, stamped with id type 0x29 (41): CUnit::AfterLoad and CSubUnit::AfterLoad when a block carried no id, CAddDivisionEffect::Execute for everything it builds, and ten other sites including CGameState and the AI. A loaded id does not use it but does push it forward, so it always sits above every id in play. In a 1936 autosave type 41 is the second commonest id type - 15751 against 4713's 19689, those being the ids that came out of files. The name is BiceLib's.

addresses.name: g_AISubscriberList_1B14E50
addresses.comment: A `{first, last, count}` triple of 0x10-byte nodes, one of eight process-wide CAISubscriber channels CAIUnit::Enable (0x4B0360) push_backs the agent onto. The others are at 0x1B14E20, 0x1B14E30, 0x1B14E40, 0x1B14E60, 0x1B14E70, 0x1B14E90 and 0x1B14F30 (virtual addresses). A byte-exact sweep for this one finds **exactly two references in the whole image** - the push_back at 0x4B03AC and the unhook in the destructor at 0x4AFC6E - so nothing ever notifies this channel. 0x1B14F30 by contrast has eight references, including three inside the espionage and foreign ministers' code, so the channels are shared with other subscribers and not all of them are dead.

addresses.name: g_AISubscriberList_1B14F30
addresses.comment: The eighth of the CAISubscriber channels CAIUnit::Enable subscribes to (push_back at 0x4B0549). Eight references in the image, three of them in the espionage and foreign ministers' code (0x49CD33, 0x49CDD1, 0x49D563) and one in 0x4A2F10, so this channel is really notified and is shared with agents other than CAIUnit. What it carries was not established.

addresses.name: g_theatre_split_threshold
addresses.comment: VA 0x1B15028, an int. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres compares it at 0x8AA09C against `spill * 1000 / home` for a province group, and makes the group its own theatre when the ratio reaches it (or when `spill` alone reaches 0x1F40 = 8 provinces x 1000). It sits in the zero-initialised part of .data - image.read returns nothing there - so its value is written at runtime and could not be read statically; the name is from its one use.

addresses.name: g_AiFrontProvinceThreshold
addresses.no_signature: A global int, not a function.
addresses.comment:
**200**, in thousandths, and already recorded from findings/FINDINGS-power.md with the same value, the same `(int)floorf(200.5f)` initialiser at rva 0x9118EB and the same conclusion that it is not a define. This is an independent convergence, not a first settlement.

What is added: **a ninth code reader**, 0x4CFB8A inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4, where it is the floor on `CMapProvince::ai_front_value (+0x5C)` for a logistical-strike target - a province one step behind the enemy's front line is only interdicted when its front value is at least 200. The record said eight places; `findValue(0x1B151E4, '.text')` returns ten references, nine of them code (0x8B4229, 0x8B8835, 0x8B9738, 0x8BADBC, 0x8BB7BF, 0x8BBCFA, 0x8CFB8C, 0x8DA60C, 0x8DAA79) and the tenth the store in the initialiser.

addresses.name: g_AiAreaWeightThreshold
addresses.comment: **300**, `(int)floorf(300.5f)` written at 0x91194B from the float at 0x120AAB4. One reader: 0x4B8BF4 in CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed, where a front province whose `CMapProvince +0x5C` is at or below it gets the reduced weight at 0x1715218 instead of 1000. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_AiAreaWeightFloor
addresses.comment: **500**, `(int)floorf(500.5f)` written at 0x911A3B from the float at 0x120A5E8 - the same literal that seeds 0x16886AC. The floor weight CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed gives a province that fails the 0x1715204 test. Three references. Not a define.

addresses.name: g_event_list
addresses.comment: **The CList of every CEvent the scenario loaded**, and the one argument RebuildCountryEventCandidates (0x5C0050) takes. RunMonthlyPass creates it if it is null (0x283C72, a zeroed 0x20 bytes) and then rebuilds every country's candidate list from it; a null value therefore means the scenario has not finished loading. BiceLib's EventCandidates module reads it and calls the rebuild once per session rather than waiting for the month to turn - see reversing/FINDINGS-events.md.

addresses.name: g_log_sink
addresses.comment: The log sink every message goes through, installed during startup from `main.cpp` at `0x658D7F`. Null until then, and `0x2410` fills it with a do-nothing sink if anything logs first.

addresses.name: g_save_tokens_first
addresses.comment: std::string* - the id to key table, 0x1C per entry, the index being the token id. Null until BuildTokenTable has run, so this is only readable in a running game.

addresses.name: g_save_tokens_end
addresses.comment: One past the last entry of g_save_tokens_first; the two together give the token count.

addresses.name: g_MissionEfficiencyModifierIds
addresses.comment: 33 dwords, one per mission index, each the modifier id of the country modifier named `<order save token>_eff` - entry 0 is a hard 0 and GetMissionEfficiency never reads it. Filled at startup by InitMissionEfficiencyModifiers (0x183810), which also creates those 32 CModifierDefinition objects, which is why the table sits past the end of the file's raw .data and reads as zero there. Eight readers; the three that matter are COrder::GetMissionEfficiency (0x187A0E) and the two sites in the order factory region (0x1839F3, 0x183A8C, which are the initialiser's own writes). A modifier's offset in a CModifier block is id * 8, per the standing trap.

addresses.name: g_loopback_channels
addresses.comment: begin pointer of a std::vector<LoopbackCommandChannel*>; end is at 0x1BEA1AC. LoopbackCommandChannel::Post walks it and pushes a deserialised copy of the command into each element's concurrent_queue. 0x73DEE0 is a linear search of it. Which function registers a channel was not read.

addresses.name: g_loopback_channels_end
addresses.comment: end pointer of the vector whose begin is g_loopback_channels at 0x1BEA1A8.

addresses.name: g_session_count
addresses.comment: inc'd by both Session constructors (rva 0x6887D6 and 0x688233). A live session counter; nothing else touches it in the code read.

addresses.name: CLeader_AddExperience_rankFactor
addresses.comment: **A function-local static inside CLeader::AddExperience**, not a global anyone else uses: five 64-bit fixed points indexed by the leader's rank, behind the one-byte construction guard at 0x17EB710. The constructor fills all five from the double 32768.5 at 0x120A548, truncated to 32768 - exactly 1.0 - so **rank does not change how fast a leader learns**. **Read live**: all five are 32768 and the guard is 1, and the whole image references the array only from the ten writes that fill it and the two reads that index it.

addresses.name: CLeader_AddExperience_rankFactorBuilt
addresses.comment: The one-byte guard MSVC puts in front of a function-local static: `test byte ptr [this], 1; jne skip` at the top, `or [this], 1` before the constructor runs. Its presence is what tells you the addresses beside it are a local static rather than a global.

addresses.name: g_WinterLatitudeLow
addresses.comment: A function-static int in CWeather::BaseTemperature, (int)floor(650.5f) = 650, guard bit 3 of rva 0x17EBC1C. CProvince +0x388 above it costs climate 5 a further 4.000 C - the largest single latitude term in the function.

addresses.name: g_WinterLatitudeHigh
addresses.comment: A function-static int in CWeather::BaseTemperature, (int)floor(950.5f) = 950 from the same float as g_SpringLatitudeHigh, guard bit 2 of rva 0x17EBC1C. CProvince +0x388 above it costs climate 5 a further 2.000 C.

addresses.name: g_SpringLatitudeLow
addresses.comment: A function-static int in CWeather::BaseTemperature, (int)floor(650.5f) = 650 from the float at rva 0x120A9E8, guard bit 1 of rva 0x17EBC1C. CProvince +0x388 above it costs climate 1 a further 1.000 C; about 49 N.

addresses.name: g_SpringLatitudeHigh
addresses.comment: A function-static int in CWeather::BaseTemperature, (int)floor(950.5f) = 950 from the float at rva 0x120A9EC, initialised once under bit 0 of the guard at rva 0x17EBC1C. CProvince +0x388 above it costs climate 1 a further 1.000 C. On BlackICE's map 0.950 is about 71 N.

addresses.name: g_BaseTemperatureStaticsGuard
addresses.comment: The MSVC once-flag for the four latitude thresholds above: bit 0 for rva 0x17EBC18, bit 1 for 0x17EBC14, bit 2 for 0x17EBC10, bit 3 for 0x17EBC0C. Tested and or-ed at 0xB236B, 0xB23B6, 0xB2447 and 0xB2493.

addresses.name: CProvince::GetSunsetHour
addresses.comment:
Bare `ret`, 0x4A7450-0x4A74C2, read end to end, receiver in ESI, no stack arguments, 13 int3 after it. Answers `12 + q`, where `q = (latitude_north (+0x388) * daylightMonthFactor[m] / 1000 + 12000) / 2000` through __alldiv/__allmul (0xB99980/0xB99AF0) and a final /1000. `m` is the global month at [0x1A85590], shifted by six months when the province template's `southern_hemisphere (+0xA2)` is **clear** - so the table is written for the southern hemisphere and the northern one is the rotated case, and `daylightMonthFactor` is the 12-entry signed table at [0x170C8B0] = {-6000,-3000,0,3000,6000,12000,6000,3000,0,-3000,-6000,-12000}.

**The arithmetic is what names it.** At latitude 0 q is 6, so sunrise 6 and sunset 18 - twelve hours of daylight at the equator. At latitude_north 1000 in the +12000 month q is 12, so sunrise 0 and sunset 24 - the midnight sun; in the -12000 month q is 0, so both answer 12 - the polar night. `|latitude_north * factor / 1000| <= 12000`, so **q is in [0, 12] always** and this function always answers the later of the two hours.

Its twin is CProvince::GetSunriseHour (0x4A74D0), byte for byte the same up to the final combine, which is `12 - q` there. Three callers of the pair: CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits' ground-attack block (0x4CF37E/0x4CF393), its naval/port-strike block (0x4D0215/0x4D022A), and CAIInvasion stage 2 (findings/FINDINGS-theatre2.md).

**This corrects findings/FINDINGS-theatre2.md**, which attributed the two the other way round - explicitly as an inference from the modulo-24 comparison rather than a reading of the bodies - and concluded that the AI loads an invasion force only in darkness with three hours of darkness left. The window runs to **sunset** and needs three hours of **daylight**.

addresses.name: CProvince::GetSunriseHour
addresses.comment:
Bare `ret`, 0x4A74D0-0x4A7547, read end to end, receiver in ESI, no stack arguments, eight int3 after it. The exact twin of CProvince::GetSunsetHour (0x4A7450) - identical instruction for instruction up to the final combine, which here is `12 - q` instead of `q + 12`. See that function for q and for the sanity checks (equator 6/18, midnight sun 0/24, polar night 12/12).

**Because the two are symmetric about hour 12 and q is in [0, 12], sunrise is never later than sunset.** That makes the guard both AI mission blocks put in front of them - `if (hour > sunset && hour < sunrise) skip` at 0x4CF3AA and 0x4D0241, and the same shape in CAIInvasion stage 2 - **unsatisfiable**: it can only fire where the two have crossed over, and they cannot. The gate that actually bites is the one after it, `sunset - hour >= 3`.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_SortWingsIntoMissionPools
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890), not a function: it is reached only by `je 0x8CEE31` falling through from the stance gate at 0x8CEE74 and it leaves through the shared epilogue at 0x8CEE4F.
addresses.comment:
Phase 4's entry. Four CLists are zeroed here - P at [ebp-0x114], Q at [ebp-0xBC], R at [ebp-0x38], S at [ebp-0xF0], each {head, tail, count, byte} - and `[ebp+0xC]`, which held the caller's `force` argument, is reused as a budget `agent->+0x1E4 * 4`.

The loop at 0x8CEEF0 walks listB (the phase-1 candidate list, head at [ebp-0xD0]) and sorts each wing into one pool by role, after repeating the gates `combats_count (+0x11C) <= 0`, CUnit_IsAtOwnBase, !UnitHasBlockingOrder and not-already-in-listA:

- any tactical_bomber, cas or cag in the group -> 0x8CF047: if the budget is positive and the wing's definition has `sea_attack (+0x168) > 0`, into **R** (naval/port strike) and the budget drops by one; otherwise 0x8CF0A2.
- any strategic_bomber, or `strategic_attack (+0x17C) > 50000` -> **Q** (logistical strike, then strategic bomb or nuke).
- else any naval_bomber -> **R**.
- else any interceptor -> **S** (air intercept).
- else dropped.
- 0x8CF0A2, the overflow from the first arm: into **Q** when the agent's ops area (+0x90/+0x94) is empty, the country is at war or in an undeclared war, `strategic_attack >= 1000` and the group holds no cag; into **P** (ground attack) otherwise.

**So P is the ground-attack pool and R the naval-strike pool, and `agent->+0x1E4 * 4` caps the naval-strike pool, not the ground-attack one.** findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md had the budget on the tactical pool and left CSubUnitDefinition +0x168 unidentified; it is `sea_attack`, already named in project.json, which is what makes the arm read correctly.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_CollectBattleProvinces
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
The ground-attack target survey, 0x8CF18A-0x8CF31F, which also lazily builds the CCurrentGameState singleton and loads `[ebp+0xC] = state->tick (+0xBDC)` - the absolute hour that every mission window in phase 4 is written from.

It walks the agent's front provinces (+0xC0/+0xC4) and keeps a province in the CList at [ebp-0x94] when: `p->intel_country_count (+0x374) > ourCountry->id (+0xCA8)`; `p->intel_by_country_ptr (+0x370)[ourId] >= 2` (we can see it); and some unit in `p->units (+0x2B8)` passes slot 15, has `combats_count (+0x11C) > 0` and `current_combat (+0x110) == 0`.

**So the ground-attack target set is the provinces on our own front where a battle is in progress** - which is what makes the block the close-air-support arm.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_IssueGroundAttack
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
0x8CF330-0x8CF63C, over pool P. Per wing: not in listA; `home_base_ptr (+0x98)` set and its slot 0 answering a province; then the daylight window - `hour = state->tick % 24`, the dead guard at 0x8CF3AA (see CProvince::GetSunriseHour), and `hoursLeft = GetSunsetHour(baseProvince) - hour >= 3`.

Two target arms, each ending in the same issue:
1. 0x8CF403-0x8CF489 over `agent->+0x1AC` (recorded as invasion_target_provinces): the province must hold at least one enemy land unit (CountEnemyLandUnitsInList), `CWeather::AirCombatEffect` on it must be at or below **[0x1B151C0] = 400**, and the wing's `range (+0x148)` must be at least 1000x CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces.
2. 0x8CF4A3-0x8CF55D over the battle provinces from 0x8CF18A: weather at or below **[0x1B15240] = 330**, at most one of the agent's own wings already on `ground_attack (0x6FB)` against that province (counted through `order->+0xC` at 0x8CF50F), and the same range test.

The order: `CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x6FB, wing, p->id, &{p->id}, &now, &now + hoursLeft, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CF5F5, then the province is removed from the battle list so two wings are not sent to the same battle in one pass. **So the mission window runs from now until local sunset at the airbase.**

addresses.name: AirPhase4_IssueAirIntercept
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
0x8CF643-0x8CF902, over pool S (interceptors). Gated on `country->at_war (+0xACC) || country->in_undeclared_war (+0xACD)`.

Per wing it scans **the whole province table** - `state->provinces_begin (+0xB8C)` to `+0xB90`, the loop index doubling as the province id - and collects every province where 0x4EFA50(province@EDI, ourCountry, 0) holds, intel is at least 2, the province is not an enemy-controlled one carrying a building (`+0x304->+0x20 > 0` and CCountry::IsEnemy on `controller (+0x334)`), and the wing's `range (+0x148)` reaches it.

The order: `CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x718 air_intercept, wing, firstCollectedId, &list, &now, &now + 0x78, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CF8BF. **0x78 = 120 hours, five days** - the longest window phase 4 writes, and the only one not tied to sunset. No weather test anywhere in this block.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_StrategicArmRequiresAirStanceTwo
addresses.no_signature: A three-instruction gate inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
`cmp dword ptr [agent->unit + 0x20C], 2; je 0x4CF9FB` - and the fall-through is the full teardown and return.

**So `plan_air_stance == 2` is a hard precondition for every one of logistical_strike, strategic_bomb, nuke_mission, naval_strike and port_strike.** At any other non-zero stance phase 4 issues `ground_attack` and `air_intercept` and nothing else; at stance 0 it does not run at all (0x4CEE6E).

**The object it reads is the agent's own unit, not the wing** - `mov edx,[ebp+8]; mov eax,[edx+0x64]` - so the stance that matters is the one on the army or theatre HQ, and the AI drives that to 2 itself. `CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances`'s second loop posts `CSetPlanAttributesCommand(agent->unit, 5, 2, 2, -1000, -1000)` for every agent in `ai->unit_agents` whose unit is not already at 2, once per ProcessAI pass (see AiDrivesAirAndNavalStanceToTwo, 0x4916AD). **The gate therefore passes for the AI in the ordinary case, and the five strategic and naval missions are live, not dead.** The 1s the live sample found are on the air formations themselves, which this instruction never reads.

What is still one instruction, and still worth knowing for a mod, is the shape of the gate: anything that puts an agent's unit at stance 1 - a player deactivating that unit's plan, which resets air_stance to 1 through CUnitPlan::SetActive - silences the strategic air war for that agent until the next ProcessAI pass restores it.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_CollectInterdictionProvinces
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
The logistical-strike target survey, 0x8CF9FB-0x8CFC1A, reached only at air stance 2 and only when pool Q is non-empty.

It opens with `CUnitPlan::GetPowerRatio(&agent->unit->plan (+0x1FC))`, and **when the ratio is at or above [0x1B15210] = 750 the whole logistical-strike arm is skipped** (0x8CFA1C jumps past it) - so the AI interdicts when it is losing, not when it is winning.

Otherwise it rebuilds the list at [ebp-0x94] from the agent's front provinces: the front province must be enemy-controlled, then for each of its template's edges (`+0xD4 -> +0x90/+0x94`, stride 0x14) that is not edge kind 3, the neighbour must have `template +0x22 is_land` and `+0x13D` set, be enemy-controlled, have `ai_front_value (+0x5C)` at least **[0x1B151E4] = 200**, and **not** pass CProvince::HasHostileLandNeighbour. That last clause is what makes it a rear-area set: a province one step behind the enemy's front line.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_IssueLogisticalStrike
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment: 0x8CFC37-0x8CFD85, over pool Q. Per wing not in listA it collects the interdiction provinces whose weather is at or below [0x1B15240] = 330 and that the wing's `range (+0x148)` reaches, and then issues `CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x6FD logistical_strike, wing, firstId, &list, &now, &now + 0x18, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CFD5A. **0x18 = 24 hours.** No sunrise or sunset test - unlike ground attack and naval strike, interdiction is flown round the clock.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_IssueStrategicBombOrNuke
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
0x8CFDA5-0x8CFFF8, over pool Q again, with its own survey first.

The survey (0x8CFDA5-0x8CFE87) walks `agent->strategic_target_provinces (+0x18C/+0x190)` and keeps each enemy-controlled province. **When `ourCountry->nukes (+0x90) >= 1000` - that is, at least one bomb - an extra filter applies**: the province's `cores (+0x344)` list must hold an entry whose `+4` equals the province's own `controller_id (+0x338)`, so a nuke is only ever aimed at territory the controller also cores, never at land it merely occupies.
