The issue (0x8CFE8D-0x8CFFF8) is per wing over Q, collecting targets by weather at or below 330 and by range, and then `CreateUnitOrder(ai, token, wing, firstId, &list, &now, &now + 0x18, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CFFD6, where the token is chosen once at 0x8CFF8E - `0x579 nuke_mission` when `nukes >= 1000`, `0x6F9 strategic_bomb` otherwise. **The choice is per country, not per target or per wing**: a country with one bomb in stock sends every strategic bomber it has on a nuke mission.

addresses.name: AirPhase4_IssueNavalOrPortStrike
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CD890).
addresses.comment:
0x8CFFFB-0x8D03E8, over pool R, gated on R's count.

The survey (0x8D0031-0x8D01CB) walks `agent->enemy_units_sighted (+0x25C)`, resolves each id pair through 0xA9D390 and backs up eight bytes to the CUnit, requires CCountry::IsEnemy on `owner (+0x124)` and weather at or below 330 over `current_province_ptr (+0x130)`, and then **splits by the target province's `template +0x22 is_land`**: a land province's id goes into list X at [ebp-0xE0], a sea zone's into list Y at [ebp-0x4C], and for a sea target that is moving (`+0x140 > 0`) the first waypoint `+0x138[0]` goes into Y as well.

The issue (0x8D01E0-0x8D03E8) repeats the sunset window - `GetSunsetHour(base) - hour >= 3`, the same dead guard at 0x8D0241 - and then tries **Y first with token `0x700 naval_strike`**; only when nothing in Y is within `range (+0x148)` does it fall to **X with `0x701 port_strike`** (the token is rewritten at 0x8D030C). `CreateUnitOrder(ai, token, wing, firstId, &list, &now, &now + hoursLeft, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8D03CE.

**So port strike is the fallback, not a separate decision**, and it works because a ship in harbour sits in the coastal land province.

addresses.name: g_AiAirMissionWeatherCap
addresses.no_signature: A global int, not a function.
addresses.comment:
**330, in thousandths.** The ceiling on `CWeather::AirCombatEffect` above which the AI will not fly: five readers in .text, all `cmp eax, [0x1B15240]` on that function's result - 0x8B126F and, inside CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits' phase 4, 0x8CF4CF (ground attack on a battle province), 0x8CFC96 (logistical strike), 0x8CFF05 (strategic bomb / nuke) and 0x8D00AF (naval / port strike).

**It is not a define and a mod cannot move it.** findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md recorded 'no writer in .text' and left it open as trap 8's second or third shape; it is the third. The writer is the static initialiser at 0xD11960, `mov [0x1B15240], (int)floorf(330.5f)` - the `(int)floor(N.5f)` .CRT$XCU shape, with the float literal at 0x160A6E0. The reason the earlier scan could not see it is that `image.findValue` over .text does find it - at 0xD1197C - but .text here runs to 0xD2B000, well past the 0x970000 the folder's notes assume, so the hit was in the list and read as a sixth reader.

addresses.name: g_AiAirInvasionTargetWeatherCap
addresses.no_signature: A global int, not a function.
addresses.comment:
**400, in thousandths**, from the static initialiser at 0xD119C0 (`(int)floorf(400.5f)`, literal at 0x160A6DC). **Exactly one reader**: 0x8CF43E, the weather test on the invasion-target arm of phase 4's ground-attack block.

So the AI will fly close air support over an amphibious objective in weather that it refuses for an ordinary battle - 400 against g_AiAirMissionWeatherCap's 330. Not a define; a mod cannot move it.

addresses.name: g_AiLogisticalStrikePowerRatioCap
addresses.no_signature: A global int, not a function.
addresses.comment:
**750, in thousandths**, from the static initialiser at 0xD11B40 (`(int)floorf(750.5f)`, literal at 0x160A614). **Exactly one reader**: 0x8CFA16, on `CUnitPlan::GetPowerRatio(&unit->plan)`. At or above it, phase 4 skips the logistical-strike target survey and the whole logistical-strike block.

GetPowerRatio is `our_power * 1000 / their_power`, so the rule is: **interdict only while we have less than 0.75 of the enemy's power on this plan.** Not a define.

addresses.name: NavalConvoyRaid_WeightedRandomTarget
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits (0x4D0880).
addresses.comment:
**The only MT19937Next draw in either air or naval AI body, and it picks the province a submarine wolfpack is sent to raid.** 0x8D2B59-0x8D2CB6.

Two preconditions: the candidate vector must be non-empty (`[esp+0xFC] > 0`) and the total weight positive (`[esp+0x38] > 0`). Then:

    r = MT19937Next(&gameState->+0x124) % totalWeight          ; 0x8D2BBF, then cdq/idiv edi
    chosen = 0
    for (c = candidates, w = weights; c < candidatesEnd && r > 0; c++, w++) {
        chosen = *c
        r -= *w
    }

which is plain roulette-wheel selection over two parallel `std::vector<int>` - province ids at [esp+0xC4]/[esp+0xC8], weights at [esp+0xE8], the running total at [esp+0x38] - built by the loop at 0x8D2526. **One quirk worth knowing: `r` can come out 0** (one draw in `totalWeight`), and then the loop exits before it reads a candidate, `chosen` stays 0, and the order is issued against province id 0 all the same - nothing tests it.

The order is `CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x6E9 convoy_raid, fleet, chosen, &emptyList, &now, &now + 0x1F8, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8D2CA5, with **0x1F8 = 504 hours, 21 days** - much the longest-lived order either body writes - and an empty province list, so the single chosen province is the whole of the mission.

addresses.name: NavalConvoyRaid_ScoreConvoyRoutes
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits (0x4D0880).
addresses.comment:
What fills the two vectors the convoy-raid draw runs on, 0x8D2526-0x8D28B3, and the reason the draw is weighted at all.

The arm is reached only for a fleet that is **a wolfpack**: `CountShipsByRole` must report the fleet all submarines when the AI runs its own units (`owner_ai->+0x2C` or `unit->+0x205`), or no transports and more than half submarines otherwise; plus `at_war || in_undeclared_war` and `plan_naval_stance (+0x210) != 0`.

It then walks `agent->+0x24C`, a CList of convoy object id pairs, resolving each through FindPersistentById against [0x1A857F0] or [0x1A857F4] by whether the id type is above 0x1268. A convoy counts when CCountry::IsEnemyTag accepts its `+0x30/+0x34` tag, or failing that when that tag is on our `undeclared_war_opponents (+0x1018)` list. For each province of the convoy's `path (CConvoy +0xB0)`, skipping the route's two endpoints (`*(+0xB0)` and `*(+0xB4)`), skipping province ids **0x2927..0x292A**, and skipping what 0x8D0520 refuses, and requiring `COrder::IsTargetInRange(fleet, id)`:

    weight = CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports(convoy) * abs(i + 1 - path_count / 2)

where `i` is the province's index along the route. **The weight is zero at the route's midpoint and largest at its ends**, so the AI's submarines are drawn to the waters near the convoy terminals rather than to mid-ocean - and a province exactly at the midpoint can never be picked.

A second pass per candidate (0x8D2830-0x8D2894) accumulates the same `GetDesiredTransports` into an ordered map keyed by each province of the agent's area (`area->+0x94`) that lies within the fleet's `range (+0x148)` of the candidate - the raidable-tonnage-per-port figure the rebase block then has available.

addresses.name: NavalRebase_ChooseHomePort
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits (0x4D0880).
addresses.comment:
The rebase half of the same per-fleet loop, 0x8D2D8B-0x8D3141. It runs when the fleet's order is not blocking, and it is skipped entirely for a fleet holding any submarine (0x8D2E3A) and for one whose current port is not overcrowded - `shipsAtBase + pendingArrivals <= port->naval_base (+0x300)->level_max (+0x20)/1000 + 2` (0x8D2EDC-0x8D2EFA).

The scoring, over `area->+0x94` (the theatre's provinces), lowest wins, starting from 1e6f:

    if (candidate->area (+0x2B4) != fleetParentProvince->area) skip
    score = DistanceBetweenProvinces(candidate, fleetParentProvince) + 10.0
    load  = shipsBasedAt(candidate->+0x58) + pendingArrivals[candidate->id]
            + (we are not already there ? fleet->regiments_count (+0x40) : 0)
    over  = load - candidate->naval_base->level_max/1000
    if (over > 0) score += over * 2000
    if (we are already there) score *= 0.75
    if (score < best && CMapProvince::CanUnitReach(candidate, fleet, 0, 0)) best = score

and then `CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder(ai, 0x6DE rebase, fleet, best->id)` at 0x8D313C, with the pending-arrivals map moved over. **So the AI's fleets spread themselves across the theatre's ports in proportion to berth capacity, pay 2000 per berth of overcrowding, get a 25% discount for staying put, and never cross out of their own COwnerArea** - and the `+ 10.0` floor means distance never scores zero.

addresses.name: AILandAttackOdds_Recurse
addresses.no_signature: an instruction entry, not a function - it names one site inside rva 0x4D93B0
addresses.comment: `call 0x4D93B0` - CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds calling itself, its own third caller. It runs once per enemy defender, for the first combat in which that defender appears in `combat->attacker->units`, and asks how that unit's own attack elsewhere is going: arg1 = `&combat->attacker->units`, the cache's list = `&combat->defender->units`, target = that combat's province (+0x18), excludeProvince = the province we are estimating, and **followCombats = 0**, which is what bounds the recursion at one level - the combat walks that reach this call are inside `if (followCombats)`. The answer is clamped to 4.0 [0x171DF34], has 0 replaced by 0.01 [0x160A378], is scaled by 0.25 [0x160A258] and replaces that defender's engagement seed of 1.0, so the factor lies in (0.0025, 1.0].

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::DetachChildren
addresses.comment: CGuiObject slot 36 as CFixedWindow overrides it. Walks the window's two ordered child lists - the CGuiObject-relative +0x4C head (every child that is not a window) and then the +0x5C head (the child windows) - and for each node calls gui->vf[27](node->value) and then node->value's own slot 36, so the walk is recursive over the whole widget subtree. Node is 0x10 bytes, {CGuiObject* value; Node* prev; Node* next; bool}, and the next pointer is at +8. THE RECEIVER IS THE CGuiObject SUBOBJECT, i.e. complete CFixedWindow + 0x18, so every displacement in the body is 0x18 below the complete-object offsets this file records for CFixedWindow (+0x4C here is +0x64 there). CGui slot 27 is the shared ret-4 stub 0x60CD50 on CEU3Gui, so what the detach does on the CGui side cannot be read from this build. Named for what it does; the game's own name is not in the image.

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::AttachChild
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CFixedWindow::AttachChild(CFixedWindow* this, Hoi3CString* name, CGuiObject* child)
addresses.comment: CFixedWindow primary vftable slot 22 (table 0x1601F88; CEU3DialogGui slot 22 of 0x15CD3C4). Appends the name to the name vector at complete +0x30C, the child to the vector at complete +0x2FC (project.json's child_windows_begin), and then a freshly allocated 0x10-byte node {child, oldTail, 0, 0} to the ordered attached-children list whose head is complete +0x74, tail +0x78 and count +0x7C. Finally calls child->vf[38](byte[this+0x60]) and child->vf[25]([this+0x484]). The receiver here is the COMPLETE CFixedWindow, unlike the CGuiObject-table slots. Named AttachChild rather than AddChildWindow because FINDINGS-guilive.md section 5 measured the +0x2FC vector live and found 46 buttons, 20 child windows and 1 icon in it across 206 windows - every declared child window reaches it through this slot, but so does anything game code attaches, so the slot is not window-specific. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.name: ResetGlobalIdCounters
addresses.comment: 0x63A330..0x63A454, bare `ret`, no arguments. Sets **four globals to 1** - [0x170AF7C] at 0x23A35A, [0x170AF78] at 0x23A360, [0x170AEB8] at 0x23A3CF and [0x170AEBC] at 0x23A441 - with two copies of the inlined get-or-create of g_CCurrentGameState between them, both dead (the global is non-null from the database stage on). It does nothing else. Two callers and no others: ResetGameStateToStartDate at 0x23A587 and the savegame loader CGameState::LoadFromSave at 0x27CEAD, i.e. exactly the two places that have just wiped or are about to overwrite the object graph. The four globals have 10, 33, 16 and 20 references; the named functions among their readers are CGameState::LoadKey (two of them), CCreateHigherCommand::Execute, CreateRebelsForFaction and CSubUnit::AfterLoad, which is what the name reads: next-free-id counters, put back to 1. `inferred` - the individual counters were not followed to the point of naming what each one counts.

addresses.name: AICombatEstimateAttackValue
addresses.signature: float __cdecl AICombatEstimateAttackValue(CUnit* unit@ECX, CMapProvince* target@stack:4, int ownBrigades@stack:8, int ownProvinceCount@stack:0xC)
addresses.comment:
**The AI's own attack-side combat-modifier total for one land division**, 0x4D8C50 to the bare `ret` at 0x4D93A6 (0x757 bytes, 61 blocks, 533 instructions), read end to end. One caller in the image, CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds at 0x4D95A1, and it is in no virtual table; its address appears nowhere as a value. The receiver is in **ECX**, the three arguments are on the stack, the caller cleans 0xC, and the answer comes back in **XMM0** (the caller reads it with `addsd xmm0, engagement` at 0x4D95BF) - an LTCG convention of its own, which is why the signature places every parameter. It carries an SEH frame only because the last block inlines GetDefines, with operator_new and CDefines::CDefines (0x452E0) on the lazy-construct path (trap 8 case 1, in a function that also calls GetDefines properly six times).

The result is a **sum** of per-modifier fractions, accumulated in a float at [ebp-0x10], each term computed in 64-bit integer thousandths through __allmul/__alldiv and then divided by 1000.0. country = unit->expeditionary_owner_id ? GetCountry(&unit->expeditionary_owner) : GetCountry(&unit->owner), the combat module's own rule.

**Cached half** (everything that depends on the unit alone), returned straight from ai_combat_estimate_attack (+0x2DC) when the dirty byte +0x2E0 is clear, otherwise recomputed and written back at 0x4D8FC2:

    v  = (base_ca_bonus + SumCombinedArmsGroupTech + trait(9 combined_arms_bonus))/1000   ; only if base_ca_bonus > 0
    v += slot22()/100 * (1000 + trait(23 experience_bonus))/1000 / 1000
    v += (leader->skill * COMBAT_LEADER_IMPACT/1000 + trait(4 offence_modifier))/1000      ; only if LeaderHasRankForCommand and skill > 0
    v -= dissent * k_thousandths_10_ai/1000 * COMBAT_DISSENT_IMPACT/1000 * (1000 + trait(20 dissent_impact))/1000 / 1000
    v -= COMBAT_SUPPLY_LACK_IMPACT * (1000 - supply_received_percentage)/1000 * (1000 + trait(10 out_of_supply_modifier))/1000 / 1000
    v += GetDifficultyCombatModifier(country)/1000

**Uncached half** (depends on the three arguments):

    n = ownBrigades - 3*ownProvinceCount
    f = 1000; for i in 1 .. min(n-1, 99): f = f * (1000 + BASE_STACKING_PENALTY)/1000
    raw = 1000 - f - country->technology_status->free_stacking_allowance
    walk up higher_oob_unit_ptr to the unit whose oob_level is 0; if found
        raw -= floorf((thatLeader->skill + 0.0005)*1000) * k_thousandths_10_ai / 1000
    if raw > 0: v -= raw/1000
    v -= CWeather::LandCombatEffect(&target->weather, &out, unit->owner)/1000
    find the ProvinceEdge from unit->current_province_ptr to target->id:
        kind 2 -> e = RIVER_CROSSING_PENALTY + def->river.attack + trait(7 river_attack);       if e < 0: v += e/1000
        kind 1 -> e = AMPHIBIOUS_LANDING_PENALTY + def->amphibious.attack + trait(25 amph_attack)
                  amph = true;                                                                  if e < 0: v -= e/1000
    v += (target->template->terrain->attack + def->terrain_adjusters[terrainId].attack)/1000
    v += (target->modifiers[amph ? 11 COASTAL_FORT_LEVEL : 10 FORT_LEVEL]/1000*1000) * BASE_FORT_PENALTY/1000 / 1000

**The amphibious arm's sign is inverted and the river arm's is not.** Both are reached only when `e < 0` (`jns` at 0x4D91D9 and 0x4D924C); the river arm then does `addsd` at 0x4D9201 (`f2 0f 58 c1`) and the amphibious arm `subsd` at 0x4D9270 (`f2 0f 5c c1`), so an amphibious landing penalty of -1.8 raises this unit's estimate by 1.8 instead of lowering it. Same if/else, same function, opposite sign.

Against CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers the formulas agree term for term where both have a term, with these differences: the AI **adds** the fractions where the combat module multiplies clamped factors into CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0; it has **no** BM_NIGHT_MODIFIER, BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY, BM_MISSION_EFFICIENCY, BM_TERRITORIAL_PRIDE or BM_SHORE_BOMBARD; its BM_LEADER_BONUS omits the terrain_attack trait (0x5D0F80 kind 29); its BM_FORT_MODIFIER omits trait(8 fort_attack), def->fort.attack and the `if v > 0: v = 0` clamp; its BM_AMPH_PENALTY omits the landing-craft interpolation, the naval-base test, the max(v,-990) floor and the REB and own-province-is-water cases; and BM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES omits the `!unit->+0x97` paradrop gate. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aihelpers.md for the table.

addresses.name: AICombatEstimateDefenceValue
addresses.signature: float __cdecl AICombatEstimateDefenceValue(CUnit* unit@EAX, int brigadesLessThreeEnemyProvinces@stack:4, int enemyProvinceCount@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
**The AI's own defence-side combat-modifier total for one land division**, 0x4D8590 to the bare `ret` at 0x4D8C49 (0x6BA bytes, 47 blocks, 499 instructions), read end to end. One caller, CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds at 0x4D9A2D, no virtual table, address taken nowhere. The receiver is in **EAX** (`mov esi,eax` at 0x4D8598), the two arguments are on the stack, the caller cleans 8, the answer comes back in **XMM0**, and there is no SEH frame - its own LTCG convention, like its twin 0x4D8C50. `brigadesLessThreeEnemyProvinces` is already `theirBrigades - 3*ourProvinceCount` when it arrives (the caller's `lea edx,[eax+eax*2]; sub esi,edx` at 0x4D9938) and is clamped to at most 100 here, at 0x4D8A93.

A **sum** of per-modifier fractions in a float at [ebp-4], each term in 64-bit integer thousandths then /1000.0. country = unit->expeditionary_owner_id ? GetCountry(&unit->expeditionary_owner) : GetCountry(&unit->owner).

**Cached half**, returned from ai_combat_estimate_defence (+0x2D4) when +0x2D8 is clear, else recomputed and stored at 0x4D8A88:

    v  = trait(24 fort_defence)/1000                                                       ; the seed, unconditional
    v += (base_ca_bonus + SumCombinedArmsGroupTech + trait(9 combined_arms_bonus))/1000     ; only if base_ca_bonus > 0
    v += slot22()/100 * (1000 + trait(23 experience_bonus))/1000 / 1000
    v += (leader->skill * COMBAT_LEADER_IMPACT/1000 + trait(3 defence_modifier))/1000       ; only if LeaderHasRankForCommand and skill > 0
    v += dig_in_level * DIG_IN_FACTOR/1000 * (1000 + trait(26 digin_bonus))/1000 / 1000
    v += (prov->template->terrain->defence + def->terrain_adjusters[terrainId].defence)/1000
    v -= dissent * k_thousandths_10_ai/1000 * COMBAT_DISSENT_IMPACT/1000 * (1000 + trait(20 dissent_impact))/1000 / 1000
    v -= COMBAT_SUPPLY_LACK_IMPACT * (1000 - supply_received_percentage)/1000 * (1000 + trait(10 out_of_supply_modifier))/1000 / 1000
    v += GetDifficultyCombatModifier(country)/1000
    if prov->area->IsValid() and ProvinceIsEncircled(prov, &unit->owner):
        e = ENCIRCLED_PENALTY * (1000 + trait(21 encirclement_bonus))/1000; if e < 0: e = 0; v -= e/1000

**Uncached half**:

    n = min(arg1, 100)
    f = 1000; repeat n-1 times: f = f * (1000 + BASE_STACKING_PENALTY)/1000
    raw = 1000 - f - country->technology_status->free_stacking_allowance
    walk up higher_oob_unit_ptr to oob_level 0; if found
        raw -= floorf((thatLeader->skill + 0.0005)*1000) * k_thousandths_10_ai / 1000
    if raw > 0: v -= raw/1000
    if enemyProvinceCount > 2 and !CProvinceTemplate::IsIsolatedLand(prov->template):
        e = (enemyProvinceCount - 2)*1000 * ENVELOPMENT_PENALTY/1000 * (1000 + trait(22 envelopment_bonus))/1000
        if e < 0: e = 0; v -= e/1000

The stacking, envelopment, encirclement, dig-in, terrain, dissent, supply, difficulty, experience and combined-arms terms are the combat module's defender formulas exactly. The differences: the AI **adds** where the combat module multiplies; its BM_FORT_MODIFIER seed is the fort_defence trait with **no fort-level gate** (the combat module's defender arm is that trait and nothing else, but only when the level is above zero, and this helper takes no province argument); its BM_LEADER_BONUS omits the terrain_defence trait (0x5D0F80 kind 30) **and** MODIFIER_LEADER_DEFENCE (country modifier 100); and it has no BM_WEATHER, BM_NIGHT_MODIFIER, BM_MULTIPLE, BM_MISSION_EFFICIENCY, BM_TERRITORIAL_PRIDE or BM_SHORE_BOMBARD - note that the attack-side twin **does** read the weather and this one does not. BM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES again omits the `!unit->+0x97` paradrop gate. The encirclement gate `prov->area->IsValid()` is redundant: ProvinceIsEncircled opens with the same virtual call.

addresses.name: ProvinceIsEncircled
addresses.comment:
**The gate on ENCIRCLED_PENALTY**, 0xA6850 to the `ret 4` at 0xA690E, 0xC1 bytes, read end to end. Two `ret 4`s, 0xA6872 and 0xA690E; the first is the shared false path that three `jmp`s and a fall-through reach, so trap 3 does not apply - the block after it is reached by a jump from inside the same frame and exits through the second. `this`-less: the province arrives in EDI and is never loaded from the frame, the tag is the single stack argument, and the answer is in AL. Two callers: CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x16ACAB, for BM_ENCIRCLEMENT_PENALTY) and AICombatEstimateDefenceValue (0x4D8A0C). project.json's BM_ENCIRCLEMENT entry said it "was not read through" and that "the province is encircled for this owner" was a reading of its use; the body supports the reading:

    if (!province->area->IsValid())                       return false   ; COwnerArea slot 0, ReturnTrue / ReturnFalse
    if (province->area->+0x2C >= 2)                       return false   ; the area holds 2 or more provinces
    if (CProvinceTemplate::IsIsolatedLand(province->path_node_ptr)) return false
    for each neighbouring area a in province->area->+0x34:
        controller = a->+0x2C ? a->provinces[0]->controller : "---"
        if (CCountry::IsFriendly(g_CCountryDataBase->+0x16C[controllerId], owner, 1)) return false
    return true

So "encircled" is: a **one-province** owner area that is not an all-water-bordered island, with no friendly neighbouring area. The `0x2C >= 2` test is the load-bearing one and it is why the penalty is rare - it needs the pocket to be its own area.

addresses.name: SumCombinedArmsGroupTech
addresses.signature: int* __fastcall SumCombinedArmsGroupTech(CCountryTag* owner@ECX, int* out@EAX, CUnit* unit@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment:
The combined-arms **technology** term, 0x1B6740 to the `ret 4` at 0x1B67A7, 0x68 bytes, read end to end. Receiver (a CCountryTag by pointer) in ECX, the out pointer in EAX and returned unchanged, the unit on the stack. Resolves the country as `g_CCountryDataBase->+0x16C[owner->id]`, then

    *out = 0
    for g in 0 .. (unit->subunit_group_present_end - unit->subunit_group_present_begin)/4 - 1:
        if (unit->subunit_group_present_begin[g]) *out += country->technology_status->+0x5C[g]

which is the middle term of CUnit::GetCombinedArmsBonus (0x1B6240) - that function inlines the same loop rather than calling this one, so the two are duplicates. **Exactly two callers**, AICombatEstimateAttackValue (0x4D8CC7) and AICombatEstimateDefenceValue (0x4D865A): this is the AI pair's private copy.

addresses.name: k_thousandths_10_ai
addresses.comment: **An `(int)floorf(10.5f)` static holding 10**, and the AI combat-estimate pair's private copy of it. Four readers, all in those two functions - 0x4D8893, 0x4D8B58, 0x4D8E5D and 0x4D9088 - where it scales dissent (`dissent * 10 / 1000`) and the theatre leader's skill (`skill * 10 / 1000`) exactly as the combat module's own 10s do. Written once, by Init_k_thousandths_10_ai (rva 0x911780), off the **same** float literal 10.5 at rva 0x120A680 that InitDefine10 uses - so it is the fifth of these statics after k_thousandths_10 (0x16881A0), g_CombatModifierFloor (0x168868C), g_IneffectiveStrength (0x16886CC) and Define10 (0x168873C), and like them **no defines.lua entry can move it**.

addresses.name: Init_k_thousandths_10_ai
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` static initialiser that writes k_thousandths_10_ai (rva 0x17151FC): floorf of the float 10.5 at rva 0x120A680 through _ftol2_sse, stored and `ret`. 0x21 bytes, properly padded both sides; its address appears exactly once in the image, as a dword at rva 0x9BBC0C in the CRT initialiser pointer table. Twin of InitDefine10 (rva 0x8C3EB0), which reads the same literal into a different global.

addresses.name: AiDrivesAirAndNavalStanceToTwo
addresses.no_signature: A block inside CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4912D0), not a function: it is the body of that function's second loop over ai->unit_agents and leaves through the loop's own back edge at 0x491B99.
addresses.comment:
**This is the answer to 'does the AI ever set plan_air_stance to 2'. It does, unconditionally, for every one of its unit agents, on every ProcessAI pass.**

CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances runs two loops over `ai->unit_agents (+0x40)`. The second one starts at 0x49161E (head reloaded at 0x491621) and its body is:

    unit = agent->slot74()                       ; ReturnDwordAt0x64, = agent->unit (+0x64)
    if (!unit) continue                                                   0x491655
    if (unit->plan_air_stance (+0x20C) == 2 &&
        unit->plan_naval_stance (+0x210) == 2) continue                   0x491660-0x49166E
    cmd = new CSetPlanAttributesCommand(unit, 5, 2, 2, &-1000, &-1000)    0x4916AD
    post cmd                                                              0x491751

The stance argument 5 and the two -1000s are that command's "leave alone" sentinels; **air_stance 2 and naval_stance 2 are real writes**, landing at CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute's 0x1E7907 and 0x1E7950. The `== 2 && == 2` test is an idempotence check, not a condition: the arm exists only to avoid re-posting a command that would change nothing, so the steady state of every agent unit is air_stance 2.

The two pushes of 2 are read off the stack arithmetic, not guessed: `push ecx` at 0x49168B reserves a slot, `mov [ecx],0xFFFFFC18` at 0x491697 and 0x4916A7 fill the two power slots with -1000, and the ctor (0x1E7710, `ret 0x1C`) stores `[ebp+0x10]`->+0x68 stance, `[ebp+0x14]`->+0x6C air_stance, `[ebp+0x18]`->+0x70 naval_stance. It also sets `+0x64 active = 1` from `ebx` at 0x1E77AD, so Execute's SetActive call cannot take the reset arm.

**Consequence: AirPhase4_StrategicArmRequiresAirStanceTwo's gate passes for the AI, and logistical_strike, strategic_bomb, nuke_mission, naval_strike and port_strike are live.** CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances has exactly one caller, ProcessAI at 0x489B8F, so this is AI worker-thread code and nothing a player does is needed.

addresses.name: AiSlot76PostsAirStanceZero
addresses.no_signature: A block inside CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan (0x4DABD0), not a function.
addresses.comment:
`CSetPlanAttributesCommand(agent->unit (+0x64), 1, 0, 0, &-1000, &-1000)` - the plan builder posts **stance 1, air_stance 0, naval_stance 0**. The two zeroes come from `esi`, zeroed at 0x4DAD44; the two -1000s are written into their stack slots at 0x4DAD5D and 0x4DAD67.

air_stance 0 is the value at which CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4 does not run at all (0x4CEE6E). So the AI's own two writers pull in opposite directions: slot 76 zeroes the stances when it builds a plan, and CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances drives them back to 2 on the next pass (0x4916AD). Slot 76 is reached from CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits, which ProcessAI runs only while `ai->unit_agents_count (+0x48)` is zero, and from CObjectivesEntry slot 22 - so the zero is the rare event and the 2 is the steady state.

addresses.name: CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute
addresses.comment:
Virtual slot 6 - the command's own Execute, the same shape as CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute next door. It resolves its unit reference (`this->+0x40`/`+0x44` through FindPersistentById against [0x1A857F0] or [0x1A857F4] by whether the type half exceeds 0x1268, then `-8` to reach the CUnit), takes the byte at `this->+0x64` and calls `CUnitPlan::SetActive(&unit->plan (+0x1FC), active)` at 0x1E5451, then goes on to the rest of the command.

**It matters to plan_air_stance because SetActive(plan, 0) resets the whole plan**, air_stance included: deactivating a plan from the interface puts air_stance back to 1. This is one of only three callers of SetActive, the other two being CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit (0x1D0F16) and CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute (0x1E7822), and the last of those always passes 1 because its constructor hardcodes `+0x64 = 1`.

The failure arm is the same as its sibling's: a lookup that fails falls through to `xor eax,eax` and the plan pointer becomes 0x1FC, which survives only because an invalid command is rejected before slot 6 is reached.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists
addresses.comment:
**The writer of all four `air_target_provinces_*` lists** (`CAIUnit +0x1FC`, `+0x20C`, `+0x21C`, `+0x22C`), which `findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md` left as its open item 3. 0x4B4740 to the `ret 4` at 0x4B4E59, with 14 `int3` before the entry and four after the exit, so both boundaries are clean. One caller: CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0A4F, under `agent->unit != 0` and `air_target_lists_built (+0x83) == 0` unless Tick's own replan flag is set - so the lists are built once per agent and rebuilt only on a replan.

**Step 1, the candidate set.** `CAIUnit::GetArea(agent)` (0x4BBAE0); if it answers nothing, the agent's `unit->current_province_ptr (+0x130)`'s theatre id (`CMapProvince +0x380`/`+0x384`) is resolved through FindPersistentById instead. All four lists are then emptied through CListOfOwned_ClearByPointer (four calls, 0x4B47C2-0x4B47EF). It walks `CCountry +0xD70` - a CList whose payloads are CMapProvince - for our own country, then for our faction leader (`+0xF3C` through the country database at [0x1A855A4]+0x16C), then for every country in `+0xF78`, keeping a province when its `+0x54 home_base_ptr`'s virtual slot 1 answers false and its own `+0x380`/`+0x384` matches the area object's id pair at `+8`/`+0xC`. Separately it builds a `std::vector<CMapProvince*>` of the same `+0xD70` provinces of every country in `enemies (+0x1008)` whose `+0x44` byte is set and whose area (`+0x2B4`) equals that country's own CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation's area.

**Step 2, four scores per candidate, one appended to each list.** Each is a 0x10-byte CPersistent record - vftable 0x15EB644, save id 0x18D at `+4`, the province id (`CMapProvince +0xD0`) at `+8` and the float at `+0xC` - inserted by CList_InsertByAscendingScore (0x4DD590). This **confirms the payload layout** FINDINGS-airnaval4 deduced from the reader alone.

| list | appended at | scored against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x1FC` default | 0x4B4C68 | `ops_area (+0x90)` when `manage_reserve (+0x364)` is set, else the enemy-home-base vector; blended `0.75 * s(invasion_target_provinces +0x1AC) + 0.25 * s(that)` when `+0x1AC` is non-empty (0x4B4BE3) |
| `+0x20C` strategic | 0x4B4CC1 | `strategic_target_provinces (+0x18C)` |
| `+0x21C` naval | 0x4B4D1A | `enemy_sighting_provinces (+0x19C)` |
| `+0x22C` transport | 0x4B4E00 | `invasion_target_provinces (+0x1AC)`, and only under the gate at 0x4B4D1F |

It finishes by setting `agent->+0x83 = 1` (0x4B4E18) and freeing both temporaries.

**Why no earlier pass found it:** it reaches every list through a plain `lea reg, [agent + 0x1FC]`, exactly the shape FINDINGS-airnaval4 said no displacement scan could follow. The scan that missed it was limited to recorded function entries, and this function was not one; `scripts/fieldchain.py --field 0x1FC` lists 0x4B47BB and 0x4B4C61 in this body on the first command.

addresses.name: AirTargetTransportListGate
addresses.no_signature: A block label inside CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists (0x4B4740), not a function.
addresses.comment:
The gate on the fourth list, and **it is the opposite of the gate the reader uses.**

Here (0x4B4D1F-0x4B4DAC): `n = (agent->+0x170 - agent->+0x16C) / 4`; if `n <= 0` nothing is appended to `air_target_provinces_transport (+0x22C)` at all. Otherwise, for each CUnit in that vector, the unit's `current_province_ptr (+0x130)`'s area (`+0x2B4`) must answer true to its own virtual slot 0, and then the candidate is accepted if that area **is** the candidate's area or appears in the area's `+0x34` list. One acceptance is enough; the record is then built and appended at 0x4B4E00.

In CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 2 the same vector is tested at 0x4CE28E-0x4CE29F and the sense is reversed: for a wing carrying a transport plane, `(+0x170 - +0x16C) & ~3 > 0` makes the body **jump out** (`jg 0x4CE63B`) and skip the wing entirely, and `+0x22C` is selected only when the vector is empty.

**So the transport list is filled only when the vector is non-empty and read only when it is empty.** Within one pass the two can never both hold, so anything read out of `+0x22C` was built on an earlier pass: the lists are built once and then only on a replan (`+0x83`), while `+0x16C` is erased and refilled by slot 78 every pass (0x4B1E14). Reported as read, not explained - it looks like a sense error in one of the two places, but nothing in the code says which.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::MeanDistanceToProvinceList
addresses.signature: float __stdcall CAIUnit::MeanDistanceToProvinceList(void* provinces@EAX, CAIUnit* agent@stack:4, CMapProvince* province@stack:8) @XMM0
addresses.comment:
The scorer CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists puts on every candidate air base, and its only caller - five call sites, all inside 0x4B4740. 0x4B4E60 to three `ret 8` exits at 0x4B4F02, 0x4B4F79 and 0x4B4F8A (three int3 after the last).

`provinces` arrives in EAX and is a `std::vector<CMapProvince*>`, read as `begin` at `+0` and `end` at `+4`.

    n = (end - begin) / 4
    if (n > 0):
        total = sum over p in [begin, end) of
                CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces(province->id, p->id, g_CMap [0x1A8557C])
        if (province is itself one of them) total *= 2.0            ; [0x160A360]
        return total / n
    ; the vector is empty - fall back on the plan's objectives
    n = agent->unit->plan_objectives_count (+0x23C)
    if (n <= 0) return 10000.0f                                    ; [0x160A59C]
    total = sum over the CObjective list at unit->plan_objectives (+0x234), linked
            through +0x1C, of DistanceBetweenProvinces(province->id, objective->+8)
    return total / n

So the figure is a **mean map distance**, in CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces's units (four times the straight-line distance), doubled when the candidate base is itself one of the provinces being measured against, and 10000 when there is nothing at all to measure against. Since CList_InsertByAscendingScore keeps the lists lowest-first, **low is good**: the AI prefers an air base close to the set the list is for, and the doubling pushes a base that is itself a target towards the back.

It also confirms **`CObjective +8` is a province id**: it is the second argument to DistanceBetweenProvinces, whose own record types both as ids.

One thing about the signature: the float comes back in **XMM0**, which every call site reads directly (`movaps xmm2, xmm0` at 0x4B4BDA), not in ST(0) where Ghidra models a `float` return on a 32-bit `__stdcall`. That is why the recorded signature places the return explicitly as `@XMM0` and all three parameters with it - custom storage is all-or-nothing in Ghidra.

addresses.name: CList_InsertByAscendingScore
addresses.comment:
`ret 8`, four callers - the four list appends in CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists and nothing else. **The ascending twin of CList_InsertByDescendingScore (0x4DD4B0)**, and the two differ in exactly two ways: this one compares the float at `payload->+0xC` rather than `payload->+0x8`, and its `comisd` takes the operands the other way round.

    0x4DD4B0:  comisd xmm2, xmm1   ; new vs node  -> skips nodes smaller than new -> DESCENDING
    0x4DD590:  comisd xmm1, xmm2   ; node vs new  -> skips nodes larger  than new -> ASCENDING

Otherwise identical in shape: walk back from the tail (`[list+4]`, prev at node `+4`), insert after the first node that does not have to be passed, bump the count at `[list+8]`, and fall through to 0x5F5E0 to push at the head when every existing node loses the comparison.

**So the four `air_target_provinces_*` lists are kept lowest-score-first**, which is what makes the mean distance CAIUnit::MeanDistanceToProvinceList computes a cost rather than a merit.

addresses.name: SubWindowMap_Contains
addresses.comment:
Whether a CFixedWindow's subwindow map holds an entry under this name. The map is the three-pointer vector at complete CFixedWindow +0x414 ({begin, end, capacity_end}) whose elements are 0x20 bytes, {Hoi3CString name at +0; CFixedWindow* window at +0x1C} - so this is a linear scan from [map] to [map+4] at a 0x20 stride, comparing the key against each element's own string. The compare is 0x415F70 (memcmp with the pointers in ECX and EDX and the length pushed), guarded by the usual MSVC std::string length test, and the SSO branch (`if capacity >= 0x10 then the buffer is at +0 else the object is the buffer`) appears on both sides.

Two stack arguments and `ret 8` on both exits, nothing in ecx, so __stdcall. Returns `al`: 1 on a match at 0xAC45F7, 0 at 0xAC4604 when the walk runs off the end.

It is a template body and takes its container as an argument, so the name is from its only use, not from the body: **all four of its call sites pass CFixedWindow +0x414** (0xAC1004 in the constructor's resolve loop, 0xAC2BCD in CFixedWindow::FindChild, 0xAC2C51 in CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow, 0xAC3FC7 in the CGuiObject slot 37 descendant test), and 'subwindow' is the engine's own word for what that container holds - 0xAC2C20 logs 'Warning: Atempt to access nonexistant subwindow ' from fixedwindow.cpp line 1042 when this returns 0. Every site pairs it immediately with SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd (0x6C4640), which inserts on a miss, which is why the guard exists at all.

addresses.name: SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd
addresses.comment:
The subwindow map's `operator[]`: the same linear scan as SubWindowMap_Contains over CFixedWindow +0x414, but it returns a **pointer to the entry's value slot** - `lea eax, [edi + 0x1C]` at 0xAC46D0 - and on a miss it **appends a default entry under that name and returns the new slot** rather than failing. The miss path builds an empty Hoi3CString (0x401BD0), hands the 0x20-byte pair to the vector insert 0x542FC0 (which takes the vector in EDI, so `mov edi, esi` at 0xAC4716 first), and then computes the result as `begin + ((end - begin) & ~0x1F) - 4`, i.e. the last element's +0x1C.

Because it inserts, it is never safe on its own, and four of its five callers guard it with SubWindowMap_Contains first and dereference `[eax]` only when that said yes. The fifth, 0x7FC3FC, calls it unguarded on `[this+0xA8] + 0x414` with a name made by converting an integer to a decimal string (0xB9A0C4, radix 10) - numbered subwindows - and then dereferences `[eax]` and calls slot 20 on it, so that site relies on the entry existing.

Two stack arguments, `ret 8` on both exits, nothing in ecx, so __stdcall, with its own SEH frame (handler 0xC14BD8) around the temporary string. The name is from the container, as for 0x6C4580: all five call sites pass CFixedWindow +0x414.

addresses.name: SubWindowMap_Add
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SubWindowMap_Add(Hoi3CString* name, CFixedWindow** window, void* map@EDI)
addresses.comment:
Appends one {name, window} entry to a CFixedWindow's subwindow map. Builds the 0x20-byte pair on its own stack - an Hoi3CString assigned from `name` (0x401BD0) at +0, then the dword at `*window` written into +0x1C - and hands it to the vector insert 0x542FC0, which takes the vector in **EDI**, so the container reaches this function in EDI too and never touches the stack. `ret 8`, two stack arguments, own SEH frame.

Its only caller is the CFixedWindow constructor's subwindow build loop at 0xAC0C86, with `lea edi, [this + 0x414]` set up three instructions earlier - which is what makes the register argument readable at all.

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow
addresses.comment:
Looks one **subwindow** up by name and returns it, or 0 after logging. CFixedWindow primary vftable slot 27. The only container it touches is the map at complete +0x414: SubWindowMap_Contains, then SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd, then `mov eax, [eax]` and return - so the value really is the complete CFixedWindow pointer, with no CGuiObject adjustment (unlike slot 12, which adds 0x18).

**This function is where the engine names the container.** On a miss it builds 'fixedwindow.cpp' (0x1601DB0) with line 0x412 = 1042, logs 'Warning: Atempt to access nonexistant subwindow ' (0x1601DF4, the engine's own spelling, misspelling included) followed by the name and ' in window 2 ' (0x1601DE4) and the window's own name from `[this+0x3C]->vf[6]`, raises it through 0xA64A30 at severity 0x30, and returns 0 at 0xAC2D6A. That log line is the evidence for calling +0x414 the subwindow map rather than naming it after what it happens to hold.

`ret 4`, receiver in ecx as the **complete** object (every displacement in the body is a complete-object offset).

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::FindChild
addresses.comment:
Finds any child of the window by name, over every container it has, and returns it as a CGuiObject* - the general lookup of which GetSubWindow (slot 27) is the subwindow-only special case. CFixedWindow primary vftable slot 12. Searches in this fixed order and stops at the first hit:

    1  vector pair +0x25C / +0x26C   (guiButtonType children)        0xAC47C0
    2  vector pair +0x27C / +0x28C   (multiSpriteButtonType)         0xAC47C0
    3  registry +0x360               (3dButtonType)                  slot 1
    4  registry +0x33C               (textBoxType)                   slot 1
    5  registry +0x384               (editBoxType)                   slot 1
    6  map +0x414                    (subwindows)        result [eax] + 0x18
    7  vector pair +0x2FC / +0x30C   (attached through slot 22)      0xAC47C0

The `+ 0x18` on step 6 and nowhere else is the whole point: a subwindow is stored as a **complete** CFixedWindow pointer and has to be converted to its CGuiObject subobject, while every other container already holds CGuiObject pointers. A null value in the map is returned as 0 rather than as 0x18.

`ret 4`, receiver in ecx as the complete object. Three early `ret 4`s inside the body (0xAC2B67, 0xAC2B95, 0xAC2BC3) are the registry hits, not abutting functions - trap 2 checked.

addresses.name: CWindowType::CreateWindow
addresses.signature: CFixedWindow* __thiscall CWindowType::CreateWindow(CWindowType* this, Hoi3CString name, void* param2, void* param3)

addresses.name: CWindowType::CWindowType
addresses.signature: CWindowType* __stdcall CWindowType::CWindowType(CWindowType* this, void* inherited@ECX, CGui* gui@EDX)
addresses.comment:
The CWindowType constructor. Writes vftable 0x1602178 at +0 and 0x16021A4 at +0x64, sets the type id at +4 to 0x18D, stores its two register arguments at +0x148 and +0x14C, plants the embedded gui-type name tree at +0x150 (vftable 0x1602108, root +0x154, mode byte +0x158), and then zeroes the whole child-type area: the pointer vector at +0x174, the thirteen per-kind declared-name lists at +0x184 through +0x244 ({head, tail, count, byte} at a 0x10 stride), the two bytes at +0x254/+0x255, the orientation pointer at +0x258, the shared declaration-order list at +0x25C and the two sound strings at +0x26C and +0x288.

**CWindowType is 0x2A4 bytes** and the class is recursive: LoadKey's `windowType` case allocates 0x2A4 and calls this, so a window type's child window types are CWindowTypes in turn.

`this` arrives on the **stack** at [ebp+8], not in ecx, and the function returns it in eax - hence __stdcall with an explicit `this` parameter rather than __thiscall. ecx and edx are untouched between entry and the stores at 0xAC49BC/0xAC49C2, so both really are incoming register arguments; edx is the CGui (CWindowType::CreateWindow calls slots 16 and 18 on +0x14C), and what +0x148 is has not been settled. Three callers: 0xAC623A (LoadKey's `windowType` case), 0x6436D6 and 0xA7D8E1.

addresses.name: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand
addresses.comment: Slot 6, and the base's own body in all 24 tables of the family - the step that turns an action into something postable. Lazily creates g_CCurrentGameState, stamps `this->last_command_date` (+0x20) with its tick (+0xBDC) at 0xA0E92D, asks `operator new` for 0x40 bytes (sizeof CDiplomaticActionCommand), clones itself through slot 16 (0xA0E94F) and hands the clone to CDiplomaticActionCommand's two-argument constructor (0xA0E090 at 0xA0E953), returning the command. It does not post it: its one caller inside the engine, the hourly AI pass at 0x682BC2, takes the result and pushes it onto the session's command channel (country->+0xF1C slot 18 -> session +0x38 slot 6). Bare `ret`, no stack arguments, receiver in ECX.

addresses.name: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: Slot 6 of CDiplomaticActionCommand, which is CCommand's Execute slot, and the whole of what happens when a diplomatic offer or reply lands. With `a = this->+0x3C` (the action): (1) `a->IsValid()` (slot 13) at 0xA0E135 - false and nothing at all happens, which is how the null action makes an empty command a no-op; (2) if `a->type == 0` (PROPOSE) and `a->GetToken()` (slot 15) is not 0x309 `callaction`, set the actor/recipient CDiplomacyStatus's +0x50 to `a->date + 0xA8` (168 hours = 7 days) through 0xA4A550; (3) `a->slot 7` at 0xA0E19E - the per-class effect, the only slot every concrete class overrides with real work; (4) clone the action (slot 16) and enqueue the clone on a country through CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction - the **recipient** when type is PROPOSE, the **actor** otherwise; (5) for a reply (type != PROPOSE) also CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0x4E21E0) and 0x4E39C0 on **both** countries. Bare `ret`, receiver in ECX, no stack arguments.

addresses.name: CDiplomaticActionCommand::~CDiplomaticActionCommand
addresses.comment: Slot 0, the scalar deleting destructor. Writes its own vftable, then **deletes the held action unless it is the null-action singleton**: `if (action != 0x1B15C60 && action != 0) action->slot0(1)` at 0xA0E02F. That explicit comparison against the static object is the clearest single piece of evidence that 0x1B15C60 is a shared singleton the engine must never free. Then destroys the CCommand base (its vftable 0x15B4F74, the Hoi3CString at +0x8 with its capacity at +0x1C) and frees `this` when the low bit of the flag argument is set.

addresses.name: CNullDiplomaticAction::CNullDiplomaticAction
addresses.comment: The only constructor of the null action, and the cheapest complete statement of CDiplomaticAction's layout, because it writes every base field in order: +0x4 = 0x18D, +0x8 = 0x2D2D2D (the tag "---"), +0xC = 0 (actor id), +0x10 = 0x2D2D2D ("---"), +0x14 = 0 (recipient id), +0x18 = 0 (type PROPOSE), +0x1C and +0x20 = [0x170C2B8] (the 43,800,000-hour epoch used as a null date), +0x24 = 1 (value true), then its own vftable 0x15FB274 and a Hoi3CString of its own at +0x28. Three call sites: the CRT static initialiser at 0xD1B3A0 that builds the singleton at 0x1B15C60, CNullDiplomaticAction::Clone (0xA0DC42) and CDiplomaticActionCommand::Clone (0xA0E39A).

addresses.name: CNullDiplomaticAction::Clone
addresses.comment: Slot 16, Clone, for the null action: 0x44 bytes from `operator new` and the constructor, ignoring `this` entirely, because every null action is identical. Slot 16 is Clone for the whole family and each class's body allocates its own size - 0x28 for CNapAction (0xA2E360), 0xB0 for CTradeAction, 0x44 here - which is how the family's object sizes were read.

addresses.name: CDiplomaticAction::Create
addresses.comment: The family's factory: one switch case per action kind, keyed on the kind's **save token**, each case allocating the class and running its constructor. `switchmap.py 0x4E5800` reads 19 cases - add_war_goal, allianceaction, debtaction_action, declarewar, embargo_action, faction_action, guaranteeaction, influence_leaders, join_with_war_goal, licence_technology, milaccess, nap, offer_lendlease, offermilaccess, peace_action, request_lendlease, send_expedition, share_technology and trade_action - and returns the null-action singleton 0x1B15C60 for an unknown token (0x4E6002). 35 callers, of which the two interesting ones are CCountry::LoadKey (0x4CD398) and CDiplomaticActionCommand::LoadKey (0xA0E2B9), both of which pass the key they have just been given.

addresses.name: CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction
addresses.comment: Appends an action to the country's pending-action list (+0xF24 head, +0xF28 tail, +0xF2C count), stamping `action->last_command_date` (+0x20) with g_CCurrentGameState's tick first. Two gates before it does anything: if the country has no CEU3AI (+0x1D8 == 0) it is only accepted when the country **is** the player (`gameState->player` +0xC34 == `country->id` +0xCA8), and otherwise the action is dropped on the floor - leaked, since nothing frees it. The node is 0x10 bytes: +0x0 the action, +0x4 the previous node, +0x8 the next, +0xC a byte. Receiver in EDI, one stack argument, `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CCountry::HasPendingTradeProposal
addresses.comment: Walks the pending-action list at +0xF24 and returns true for the first entry whose slot 15 token is 0x6DA `trade_action` and whose `type` (+0x18) is 0 PROPOSE. The clearest proof available that the +0xF24 list is **not** the declare-war list the record named it after: this reader only cares about trade offers in it. Bare `ret`, receiver in ECX, no arguments.

addresses.name: CCountry::ClearPendingDiplomaticActions
addresses.comment: Deletes every action in the +0xF24 list through its slot 0 with the free flag, frees every node, and zeroes +0xF24, +0xF28 and +0xF2C. Its one interesting caller is the hourly AI pass at 0x682BE5, which runs it on every AI country after looking at that country's offers - so an offer not acted on in the hour it arrives is discarded rather than carried over. Receiver in EDI, no stack arguments, bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed
addresses.comment: Stores its argument in the status's +0x50. **Likely a diplomatic cooldown, and the name is inference from the one caller, not from the body.** The body is `status->+0x50 = when` on both arms of a comparison against `g_CCurrentGameState->tick + 0xA8`, so the comparison is dead and only the single caller gives the field meaning: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute passes `action->date + 0xA8` - the proposal's date plus 168 hours, exactly seven days - on the PROPOSE path for every kind but `callaction`. The dead comparison is consistent with a cooldown that was reduced to an unconditional store at some point. One caller in the image. Receiver in EDI, one stack argument, `ret 4`.

addresses.name: g_CNullDiplomaticAction
addresses.comment: The null-action singleton, 0x44 bytes of static storage, constructed by the CRT initialiser at 0xD1B3A0 and destroyed by the atexit handler at 0xD278A0. It is what a default-constructed CDiplomaticActionCommand holds at +0x3C (0xA0DFE6), what CDiplomaticAction::Create returns for an unrecognised token (0x4E6002), and the one pointer CDiplomaticActionCommand's destructor refuses to delete (0xA0E02F). Its IsValid (slot 13) and IsSelectable (slot 14) are both ReturnFalse at 0x592360, so `IsValid()` on the family is literally "this is not the null object" - the same shape as CNullOwnerArea, and CDiplomaticActionCommand::LoadKey uses it exactly that way.

addresses.name: CAllianceAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for an alliance offer, and the first of a run of eleven identical ones at 0x4E83F0, 0x4E8510, 0x4E8630, 0x4E8770, 0x4E8890, 0x4E89B0, 0x4E8AD0, 0x4E8BF0, 0x4E8D10, 0x4E8E30 and 0x4E8F50. Each allocates its class's size, copies the two tags by value into +0x8 and +0x10, sets `type` = 0 PROPOSE, `value` = 1 and both dates to g_CCurrentGameState's tick, and writes its own vftable. Nothing in the engine calls it: the Lua name is **`Create`**, from the registration at 0x9058B5 whose name string is 0x15EEBD8 'Create', so this is `CAllianceAction.Create(actor, recipient)` as a mod sees it.

addresses.name: CGuaranteeAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for a guarantee offer - see CAllianceAction::Create for the shared shape and the 'Create' Lua name.

addresses.name: CInfluenceNation::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for an influence action - see CAllianceAction::Create. This one also writes a field at +0x28 of its own, which CInfluenceNation adds over the base.

addresses.name: CMilitaryAccessAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for a demand for military access - see CAllianceAction::Create.

addresses.name: COfferMilitaryAccessAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for an offer of military access - see CAllianceAction::Create.

addresses.name: CCallAllyAction::Create
addresses.signature: CCallAllyAction* __cdecl CCallAllyAction::Create(CCountryTag actor, CCountryTag recipient, CCountryTag ally)
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for calling an ally into a war, and the only one of the eleven that takes a **third** tag, written to +0x28/+0x2C - the ally or the enemy the call is about. See CAllianceAction::Create for the rest of the shape.

addresses.name: CNapAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for a non-aggression pact offer - see CAllianceAction::Create.

addresses.name: CInfluenceAllianceLeader::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for influencing an alliance leader - see CAllianceAction::Create.

addresses.name: CEmbargoAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for an embargo - see CAllianceAction::Create.

addresses.name: CFactionAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for a faction invitation - see CAllianceAction::Create.

addresses.name: CTradeAction::Create
addresses.comment: The Lua-side constructor for a trade offer - see CAllianceAction::Create. The object it builds is 0xB0 bytes, the largest in the family, because of the two goods vectors CTradeRoute carries.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::CHistoryContainer
addresses.comment: **The whole of a history container's layout, in eight stores.** The receiver is in EAX, nothing is on the stack and it ends in a bare `ret`. It writes the CPersistent meta `0x18D` at +4, its own vftable (VA 0x15C88F4) at +0, the date at +8 - `0x29C55C0` as an immediate and then the same value again out of **g_NullDate** (rva 0x130C2B8), which is the default member initialiser followed by the copy from the static CDate - then zeroes the `CList` at +0xC (head +0xC, tail +0x10, count +0x14, flag byte +0x18) and the dword at +0x1C. **So CHistoryContainer is 0x20 bytes** and the derived class's own fields start at +0x20. Called from exactly two places, both tiny derived constructors: CProvinceHistory::CProvinceHistory (0x1FCBE0) and CCountryHistory's at 0x1ECA3A; CLeaderHistory's copy is inlined into CLeader::CLeader at 0x17F618..0x17F665.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::Clear
addresses.comment: Empties the entry list and frees the entries. Two passes over the list at +0xC: the first calls each entry's **virtual slot 0** with 1 (CHistoryEntry::Release, which deletes it), the second frees the 0x10-byte nodes, and then head/tail/count (+0xC/+0x10/+0x14) go to zero. It does **not** reset the date at +8 - CHistoryContainer::Reset (0x1F4730) is the variant that does. Wrapped in SEH, `ret 4`, the container on the stack. Called from eight places, among them CHistoryContainer::Release (0x200220) and CCountryHistory's and CProvinceHistory's own release at 0x1ECA60.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::AddEntry
addresses.comment: **Slot 6, introduced by CHistoryContainer and inherited unchanged by all five of its subclasses** - the one way an entry gets into a history. Allocates a 0x10-byte node with `operator new`, fills it {data = entry, prev = old tail, next = 0, flag = 0}, hangs it off the old tail's `next` (+8) or, on an empty list, writes it to the head at +0xC, and increments the count at +0x14. **It keeps the list in date order**: before appending it compares the current tail entry's date (entry+8) against the new entry's, and when the tail is later it hands both to the sorted insert at 0x1FAEE0 instead. `ret 4`. No direct caller - every one of the 21 call sites is the virtual, reached as `mov edx,[owner+<history offset>]; lea ecx,[owner+<history offset>]; call [edx+0x18]`, which is how CCountry::ChangeNeutrality logs a neutrality change and how CLeaderHistory::LoadEntry files a parsed entry.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::Reset
addresses.comment: Clear plus the date: frees every node of the list at +0xC (without calling the entries' Release, so this leaks the entries unless the caller has freed them), zeroes head/tail/count, and then puts **g_NullDate** (rva 0x130C2B8) back into the date at +8. The container is in EDI, nothing is on the stack and it ends in a bare `ret`. Three callers: 0xD46EA inside the unnamed leader/country reset at 0xD2B60, 0x1F4A8C, and 0x27DD14.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::SetDate
addresses.comment: Sets the container's own date at +8 from the dword ESI points at, and - **only when virtual slot 8 answers false** - first walks the entry list and stamps the same date into every entry's +8. **That branch is dead in every container that exists**: slot 8 is ReturnTrue (0x692590) in CLeaderHistory, CDiplomaticHistory and CWarHistory and a framed `mov al,1; ret` at 0x1EC720 in CCountryHistory and CProvinceHistory; only the abstract base's own slot holds ReturnFalse (0x192360). Container in EDI, date pointer in ESI, nothing on the stack, three bare `ret`s. Five callers, all inside the unnamed function at 0x1F1F40.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::ApplyRange
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CHistoryContainer::ApplyRange(CHistoryContainer* history@EAX, int* from@EDI, int* to@stack:4)
addresses.comment: **Replays one history container across a date range, forwards or backwards** - the mechanism the whole subsystem exists for. When `*to > *from` it walks the list head-to-tail and calls each entry's **virtual slot 7 with 1** for every entry whose date is in `(*from, *to]`; when the range runs backwards it walks tail-to-head and calls slot 7 with **0**, undoing each entry whose date is in `(*to, *from]`. The container is in EAX, the from-date in EDI and the to-date is the one stack argument, so `ret 4`. Nine call sites, all of them inside ExecuteHistory (0x1F4C20).

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::ApplyAll
addresses.comment: **Slot 7 of CHistoryContainer and of all five subclasses**, the undated form of ApplyRange: with the flag set it walks head-to-tail calling every entry's own slot 7 with the same flag, and with it clear it walks tail-to-head calling each with 0. No date test at all, so it applies or undoes the whole history. `ret 4`. Reached only through the vftable - a rel32 scan of .text finds zero direct calls.

addresses.name: CHistoryContainer::Release
addresses.comment: Slot 0 of CHistoryContainer, CLeaderHistory, CDiplomaticHistory and CWarHistory - the scalar-deleting destructor. Calls CHistoryContainer::Clear (0x1F45E0), then frees the object itself when the low bit of the flag is set, and returns the receiver in eax. `ret 4`. CCountryHistory and CProvinceHistory override it at 0x1ECA60, which does the same thing through a different clear (0x946F0).

addresses.name: CLeaderHistory::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CLeaderHistory, CDiplomaticHistory and CWarHistory - the same body in all three, which is why it is recorded on one of them and the slot recorded on the other two. Walks the list at +0xC and, for each entry, asks **CHistoryEntry::DateIsUnset (0x1EC6E0)**: an unset date goes straight to the entry's own slot 2, and a real one is first formatted through 0x44C710 and opened as a `<date> = { ... }` block. So a leader's `history` block is written back out whole on every save. `ret 4`. CCountryHistory and CProvinceHistory use a different and much larger writer at 0x1FCDA0.

addresses.name: CHistoryEntry::DateIsUnset
addresses.comment: `return GetYear(&this->date) < 2`, where the year comes from **0x2EF40**: `(*date - 0x29C55C0) / 24 / 365.0` truncated, with 365.0 read out of 0x120A550 (VA 0x160A550) and the epoch being the same 43800000 the record already holds for CCurrentGameState's tick. So an entry whose date is still **g_NullDate** - the epoch, year zero - counts as undated, and the save writer omits its date header. Bare `ret`, receiver in ecx, in no virtual table. The name is read off the arithmetic rather than from a string.

addresses.name: ExecuteHistory
addresses.signature: void __fastcall ExecuteHistory(int* from@ECX, void* containers@EDX, int* to@stack:4, void* alsoContainers@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **The engine's `history execute` stage, and the only bulk reader of the history.** Logs `Executing History from <from> to <to>` on `history.cpp:11`, then for every CHistoryContainer* in the vector at [EDX]..[EDX+4] calls CHistoryContainer::ApplyRange (0x1F47C0) with the same two dates, and does the same for a second collection held at +0x10/+0x14 of the fourth argument when that is non-null. The direction is decided once, by `setl` on `*from < *to` at rva 0x1F4C62. Extent 0x1F4C20..0x1F5298, one `ret 8`, from-date in ECX and the container vector in EDX. Four call sites, all in ExecuteHistoryToDate (0x1F52A0). **Not on the tick**: that caller runs from CEU3Application::LoadEverything, from ResetGameStateToStartDate (0x23A460), from CSetHistoryDate slot 6 (0x2D60C0) and from six lobby/scenario-setup handlers (0x2F4250, 0x2F48A0, 0x2F4EA0, 0x2F5500, 0x307BF0, 0x31D4B0).

addresses.name: ExecuteHistoryToDate
addresses.signature: void __stdcall ExecuteHistoryToDate(void* context@stack:4, int** to@stack:8, int* from@EDX)
addresses.comment: Drives ExecuteHistory (0x1F4C20) up to four times to move the world from one date to another, lazily rebuilding the game state at [0x1689790] through CGameState::CGameState (0x27D070) when there is none and clearing `loaded_from_save`, `tutorial_id` and `in_game` on the new one. Extent 0x1F52A0..0x1F57B0, two exits, both `ret 8`. **This is the function that makes the history matter**: eleven call sites, the significant ones being 0x232882 and 0x2328EF inside CEU3Application::LoadEverything (the `history execute` stage), 0x23A75E and 0x23A825 inside ResetGameStateToStartDate, 0x2D619C inside CSetHistoryDate slot 6, and the lobby date handlers at 0x2F4361, 0x2F49B1, 0x2F4FB1, 0x2F5611, 0x307E18 and 0x31D9AC. `inferred` for the argument list only: the two stack slots and the incoming EDX are pinned by the `ret 8` and by EDX being read at 0x5F52C3 before anything writes it, but which of the two stack arguments is the context and which the date was not settled.

addresses.name: CLeaderHistory::LoadEntry
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLeaderHistory::LoadEntry(CLeaderHistory* this, void* date, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **Slot 9, and the whole grammar of a leader's `history` block** - five keys, one `new` apiece, and the only producer of a CRankChange in the image. `rank` (0x10A) builds a CRankChange (vftable VA 0x15C9EB0, 0x18 bytes, value through atoi); `skill` (0x28F) a CSkillChange (VA 0x15C9EF8, 0x18); `loyalty` (0x43C) a CLoyaltyChange (VA 0x15C9ED4, 0x18); `add_trait` (0x488) a CAddTraitEntry (VA 0x15C9F40, 0x14) and `remove_trait` (0x489) a CRemoveTraitEntry (VA 0x15C9F1C, 0x14), the last two resolving the trait by name. Each entry gets the CHistoryEntry base inline (meta 0x18D at +4, date defaulted to g_NullDate at +8), **the owning CLeader\* from `this->+0x20` at +0xC**, its value at +0x10, zero at +0x14, then the real date from the first argument, and is filed through slot 6 (AddEntry). `ret 0xC`. Anything else falls to 0x1FC7DB.

addresses.name: CRankChange::GetSaveToken
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 0x10A; ret` - five bytes. **Slot 6 of a history entry is the save token naming the key it carries**, pure virtual on CHistoryEntry (both slot 6 and slot 7 of table VA 0x15C9E8C are _purecall (rva 0x7961D5)), so every entry class supplies one. 0x10A is `rank`. This is the function RunCountryDailyPass calls through at 0xDAA80..0xDAAFE when it looks through a leader's history for the day he becomes active.

addresses.name: CLoyaltyChange::GetSaveToken
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 0x43C; ret`. 0x43C is `loyalty`. Slot 6 of CLoyaltyChange.

addresses.name: CSkillChange::GetSaveToken
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 0x28F; ret`. 0x28F is `skill`. Slot 6 of CSkillChange. **And CSkillChange is the one leader history entry that does nothing**: its slot 7 is the 1420-holder empty stub at 0x20CD50, where its four siblings all have a real body. So `skill = N` inside a leader's `history` block is parsed, stored, written back out on save - and never applied. There are no live CSkillChange in the 2026-09-20 census, and the mod's 124 leader files use the key nowhere inside a history block.

addresses.name: CAddTraitEntry::GetSaveToken
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 0x488; ret`. 0x488 is `add_trait`. Slot 6 of CAddTraitEntry, whose slot 7 the record already holds as CAddTraitEntry::Apply (0x1FC9C0).

addresses.name: CRemoveTraitEntry::GetSaveToken
addresses.comment: `mov eax, 0x489; ret`. 0x489 is `remove_trait`. Slot 6 of CRemoveTraitEntry.

addresses.name: CRankChange::Apply
addresses.comment: **Slot 7 of CRankChange, and what a rank change is**: with the flag set it saves the leader's current rank into `this->+0x14` and writes `this->+0x10` into `leader->rank` (+0x6C); with it clear it puts `this->+0x14` back. The leader is `this->+0xC`. Then, for a **land** leader only (`leader->type` +0x68 == 0) that has a unit at +0x40, it calls the unit's leader setter at rva 0x1BFC10 - FINDINGS-leaders.md's CUnit::SetLeader, still unrecorded - with the null leader from CLeader::null (rva 0x17F510) - so applying or undoing a rank change takes a land leader off his unit. `ret 4`. The same {+0xC leader, +0x10 new value, +0x14 saved old value} shape is CLoyaltyChange's at 0x1FC8A0, against `loyalty` (+0x80) instead of rank.

addresses.name: CLoyaltyChange::Apply
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of CLoyaltyChange, CRankChange::Apply's twin without the unit half: set saves `leader->loyalty` (+0x80) into `this->+0x14` and writes `this->+0x10` over it, clear puts +0x14 back. The leader is `this->+0xC`. `ret 4`, two exits.

addresses.name: CRankChange::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CRankChange: writes one `rank = <this->+0x10>` line - the token 0x10A into ecx for 0xA7A1B0, then the value formatted into a stack Hoi3CString and handed to 0xA797A0. **It does not write +0x14**, which is why the saved old rank is runtime scratch for the undo path and not state a save carries.

addresses.name: CHistoryEntry::Release
addresses.comment: Slot 0 of CHistoryEntry and of the seventeen of its subclasses that add nothing needing cleanup - CRankChange, CSkillChange, CLoyaltyChange, CAddTraitEntry and CRemoveTraitEntry among them. Puts the base vftable (VA 0x15C9E8C) back and frees the object when the low bit of the flag is set, returning the receiver. `ret 4`. This is the slot CHistoryContainer::Clear calls with 1 on every entry.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetOriginalCapital
addresses.comment: **A runtime reader of a country's history, and the shortest one in the image.** Walks the list at `country->history + 0xC` (country +0xCD8), asks each entry's slot 6 for its save token, and returns `entry->+0x10` for the first entry whose token is **0x1F9 = `capital`**; with no such entry it falls back to the live `capital_province_id` (+0xE20). `ret 4`, one stack argument. Four callers - 0xBF8BD, 0xC1680, 0xE0C6A and 0x14BED6 - and the same loop is inlined twice more, at 0xBF973 and 0xC1632, so the country history is consulted for the original capital in at least six places. The name is read off the token and the fallback.

addresses.name: CMapPoint::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **CMapPoint slot 2, and the half of the class that settles its layout.** Writes exactly two keys and nothing else: key token `0x1F` = `x` from `this+0x8` (rva 0x5D1E3 reads it, rva 0x5D1E9 loads ECX with 0x1F for SaveWriteKey), then key token `0x20` = `y` from `this+0xC` (rva 0x5D239 / rva 0x5D244). Each value goes through the float formatter at rva 0x79625D with the `'%f'` literal at VA 0x15FD134 into a stack Hoi3CString, then SaveWriteValue (rva 0x6797A0), then SaveWriteToken with token 0x10 in ECX (rva 0x61360) to close the line. So a CMapPoint is **16 bytes**: CPersistent's vftable at +0x0 and its `token` word at +0x4 (set to `none`, 0x18D, by every inlined constructor), `float x` at +0x8, `float y` at +0xC - and nothing else, because this writes the whole object and CMapPoint::LoadKey reads back the same two offsets. Extent rva 0x5D1D0..0x5D294, one `ret 4`; three int3 then LoadKey's prologue at rva 0x5D2A0, so no trap 3 tail.

addresses.name: CMapPointFillDefaultN
addresses.signature: void __cdecl CMapPointFillDefaultN(CMapPoint* first@EAX, int count@ECX, void* allocator@stack:4)
addresses.comment: `std::_Uninitialized_default_fill_n<CMapPoint>`, instantiated for this class only - it plants CMapPoint's own vftable (VA 0x15BC65C) inline, so it is not a folded stub. Per element: `[p+4] = 0x18D` (CPersistent's `token`, `none`), `[p+0] = 0x15BC65C`, `[p+8] = 0.0f`, `[p+0xC] = 0.0f`, then **`add eax, 0x10`** at rva 0xACEBA - which is the cleanest single statement of CMapPoint's size in the image. Bare `ret`, 14 int3 after; `first` arrives in EAX, `count` in ECX, and the one stack dword is never read (the caller at rva 0x91A85 pushes whatever happened to be in EDX), which is MSVC's unused allocator reference. One caller, rva 0x91A8F inside CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry, which is the `vector<CMapPoint>::resize` that gives every province its building-position array.

addresses.name: CMapPointCopyConstructRange
addresses.signature: void __cdecl CMapPointCopyConstructRange(CMapPoint* first@stack:4, CMapPoint* last@EDX, CMapPoint* dest@EAX, void* allocator@stack:8)
addresses.comment: `std::_Uninitialized_copy<CMapPoint>` - the reallocation half of `vector<CMapPoint>`. Per element it writes a **fresh** vftable and token into the destination (`[dest+4] = 0x18D`, `[dest] = 0x15BC65C` at rva 0xACF24) and copies only the two floats (`fld [src+8]; fstp [dest+8]`, same for +0xC), then `add ecx, 0x10` / `add eax, 0x10` at rva 0xACF3C - a second, independent 0x10 stride for the class. Bare `ret`; the second stack dword is the unused allocator. One caller, rva 0xAC88F inside the vector's grow path (rva 0xAC830). **Trap 2: it abuts rva 0xACED0, which ends a bare `ret` at rva 0xACF0F with no padding at all, so image.functionStart(rva 0xACF2D) answers 0xACED0 and attributes this body to a copy loop whose stride is 0x14 and which has nothing to do with CMapPoint.**

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::CProvinceTemplate
addresses.signature: CProvinceTemplate* __stdcall CProvinceTemplate::CProvinceTemplate(CProvinceTemplate* this@stack:4, void* source@ECX, int provinceId@EDX) @EAX
addresses.comment:
The constructor the record already names in prose. `this` arrives on the **stack** at [ebp+8] and comes back in EAX (rva 0xA96D0), the CMap +0x2198 entry for this id arrives in ECX and is stored at +0x28 (rva 0xA92E7), the province id arrives in EDX and is stored at +0x7C (rva 0xA933B); `ret 4` at rva 0xA96DF, with an EH funclet after it in the same frame (trap 3). Allocated 0x27C bytes at a time at rva 0x8A153.

**What is new here is where the map point population comes from.** The constructor plants **two CMapPoints by value**: one at +0x34 (vftable at rva 0xA930A, token at rva 0xA9302, x/y zeroed at rva 0xA92F8/0xA92FD) whose x/y are the already-named `text_position_x`/`text_position_y` at +0x3C/+0x40, and one at +0x44 (rva 0xA931A / 0xA9317 / 0xA930D / 0xA9312) whose x/y are `city_x`/`city_y` at +0x4C/+0x50. Then at rva 0xA9524 it reads `g_CBuildingDataBase` (VA 0x1A870D4), takes `([db+0x10] - [db+0xC]) >> 2` - the length of the database's `vector<CBuilding*>`, i.e. **the number of building types** - reserves that many in the `vector<CMapPoint>` at +0x258 (rva 0xA953C) and that many floats in the vector at +0x268 (rva 0xA9548), then push_backs a default `{vftable, 0x18D, 0.0f, 0.0f}` and a `0.0f` that many times; the inlined push_back advances `_Mylast` by **0x10** at rva 0xA9618. Because the reserve is exact and the pushes exactly fill it, the capacity has no slack.

**Not read:** everything between rva 0xA934A and rva 0xA9524 (the rest of the field initialisation) and the tail after rva 0xA9670. The vector construction and the two embedded points were read end to end.

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: CProvinceTemplate slot 0, 32 bytes: calls the real destructor at rva 0xA9770 with `this` pushed, then `free(this)` (rva 0x795F9B) when the low bit of the flag is set, and returns `this`. **It has no reference anywhere in .text** - image.findValue finds none, because it lives only in the virtual table at VA 0x15C064C - so the only way a CProvinceTemplate is destroyed is a virtual slot-0 call, and the only such call in the image is the loop in CMap's destructor at rva 0x88BE3.

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::~CProvinceTemplate
addresses.comment:
The real destructor, `this` on the stack at [ebp+8], `ret 4` at rva 0xA9927, SEH-framed. **This is where the map point population would be freed.** It frees the `vector<float>` at +0x268 first (rva 0xA97ED, then the three pointers zeroed at rva 0xA97F5/0xA97FB/0xA9801), then walks the `vector<CMapPoint>` at +0x258 calling each element's **slot 0 with the delete flag clear** (rva 0xA9820..0xA982F, `add esi, 0x10` per step - a fourth independent statement of the 0x10 stride) and frees the one block (rva 0xA9838), zeroing +0x258/+0x25C/+0x260. One caller, the slot-0 thunk at rva 0xA9737.

**Not read:** the five-slot loop over +0x108 before it and everything from rva 0xA9854 on (the strings and lists at +0x12C and beyond).

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::GetNavalBasePosition
addresses.comment: `&this->building_positions[g_CBuildingDataBase->naval_base->index]`, in one line: lazily builds the database if it is absent, then `eax = [db+0x20]` (rva 0xA9DC2, the cached naval_base `CBuilding*`), `eax = [eax+0x54]` (its index), `shl eax, 4` (rva 0xA9DCE - the third independent 0x10), `add eax, [this+0x258]` (rva 0xA9DD1). `ret 4` at rva 0xA9DE1. 8 callers. **Trap 2: it abuts rva 0xA9D40, a name getter that ends `ret 4` at rva 0xA9D6D with no padding, so image.functionStart(rva 0xA9DD1) answers 0xA9D40 and findRefs --callers 0x4A9D40 returns twelve callers that have nothing to do with building positions.**

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::GetAirBasePosition
addresses.comment: The same body as rva 0xA9D70 one role along: `eax = [db+0x1C]` (rva 0xA9E42, the cached air_base `CBuilding*`), index at +0x54, `shl eax, 4`, `add eax, [this+0x258]` (rva 0xA9E51). `ret 4` at rva 0xA9E61, properly padded. **One caller**, rva 0x1D2E4C.

addresses.name: CProvinceTemplate::Save
addresses.comment:
CProvinceTemplate **slot 1**, i.e. it overrides `Save` itself rather than `SaveContents` - slot 2 on this class is the generic `ret 4` stub at rva 0x20CD50 - so this body writes the braces and the whole key list of one positions.txt province block. `this` in ECX (rva 0xAA324), writer at [ebp+8], `ret 4` at rva 0xAB2D1 with a bare `ret` at rva 0xAB308 after it (trap 3 territory, not resolved here).

**What was established:** it is the only thing besides the loaders that walks the two per-building vectors whole. It takes the element count as `([this+0x25C] - [this+0x258])` at rva 0xAAA03 and indexes +0x258 at four more places, and it does the same for +0x268/+0x26C at rva 0xAAC4B - immediately before the one reference in the image to the `'building_nudge'` literal at VA 0x15C0638 (rva 0xAAC9B). That pins +0x268 as the `building_nudge` block's vector from the writing side as well as the reading side.

**Not read:** everything else, which is most of 0xFD0 bytes. This entry exists to keep the class's table current now that slot 0 is named, and to record the `building_nudge` reference; it is not a full account of the function.

addresses.name: CMap::LoadBuildingPositions
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CMap::LoadBuildingPositions(CMap* this, CProvinceTemplate* province, CParseContext* parse)
addresses.comment:
positions.txt's `building_position` block, reached from CMap::LoadPositionsFile's switch at rva 0x902B1 on save token **0x6CC**. Per key: copy the parse state (0x41 dwords) to the stack, stop on token 4 or 0x13, build a Hoi3CString from the key text at `parse+0x24`, look the name up in `g_CBuildingDataBase` (rva 0xB8B60) to get a `CBuilding*`, construct a **stack** CMapPoint `{0x15BC65C, 0x18D, 0.0f, 0.0f}` and call its slot 3 (CPersistent::Load) to parse the `{ x= y= }` body, then store the two floats into `province->building_positions[building->index]`:

    mov  eax, [esi+0x54]        ; CBuilding::index
    shl  eax, 4                 ; * 0x10, rva 0x90541
    add  eax, [ecx+0x258]       ; province->building_positions, rva 0x90544
    movss [eax+8], xmm0         ; x
    movss [eax+0xc], xmm0       ; y

After the store it compares the building against `g_CBuildingDataBase +0x20` (naval_base) at rva 0x90559 and **only for the naval base** goes on to check the raster at `CMap +0x20E0` that the pixel belongs to this province; every other building type loops straight back. `ret 0xc` at rva 0x9074D. **Trap 2: rva 0x90750 begins at the very next byte with no padding** (`c2 0c 00 | 55 8b ec`), so a displacement scan attributes the `building_nudge` loader's work to this function.

addresses.name: LoadBuildingNudges
addresses.comment:
positions.txt's `building_nudge` block, reached from CMap::LoadPositionsFile at rva 0x902BD on save token **0x6CB**. Same shape as its sibling but one float wide: look the key name up in `g_CBuildingDataBase`, `sscanf(parse+0x22C, "%f", &value)` (rva 0x908D4), then

    mov  eax, [edi+0x54]        ; CBuilding::index, rva 0x908E8
    mov  edx, [ecx+0x268]       ; province->building_nudges, rva 0x908EB
    movss [edx+eax*4], xmm0     ; rva 0x908F6

`ret 8` at rva 0x9091D. It takes no CMap, which is why the name carries no class. **In the mod's own map/positions.txt every one of the 14,168 `building_nudge` blocks is empty**, so all 851,400 floats this would write stay 0.0f.

addresses.name: CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry
addresses.comment:
