The per-province derived-geometry pass, called once at rva 0x8A739 inside CMap::LoadMapFiles - **immediately before CMap::LoadPositionsFile at rva 0x8A73F**, which is why the vectors exist by the time positions.txt is parsed. It loops `i` over `[this+0x21FC]` provinces, takes `[this+0x2A60][i]` and, per province, writes the bounding-box centre into +0x2C/+0x30, copies it into the label pair at +0x5C/+0x60 and the float pairs at +0x3C/+0x40 and +0x4C/+0x50, derives the four-way size class at +0x24, rebases the edge list at +0x6C/+0x70, and sets the hemisphere byte +0xA2 against half of `CMap +0x2A78`. `ret 4` at rva 0x91CC3.

**For the map point question it is the allocation site.** At rva 0x919E5 it reads the `vector<CMapPoint>` triple at +0x258 and its current length as `(_Mylast - _Myfirst) >> 4` (rva 0x919FC - the 0x10 element size again), compares it with the building-type count taken from `g_CBuildingDataBase`'s `vector<CBuilding*>`, and resizes: shrink through rva 0xACBD0, grow through rva 0xAC830 then CMapPointFillDefaultN at rva 0x91A8F. The same block follows for the `vector<float>` at +0x268, with `>> 2` and rva 0xC0700. Because the constructor already sized both to the same count, **both branches are no-ops in practice** - the `jbe`/`jae` pair falls straight through on equality.

**Not read:** rva 0x91B80 onward.

addresses.name: CAndTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**AND over the child list, and nothing else.** 0x5D06E0 to two `ret 4` exits at 0x5D070A (all children passed) and 0x5D0712 (one did not); `je 0x5D070D` from inside jumps past the first, so it is one function, not two (trap 3). It walks `children_first (+0x8)` - payload at node+0, next at node+8 - and calls each child's **slot 6** through `[vftable+0x18]`, stopping at the first `al == 0`. An empty child list returns **true**. It reads no field but `+0x8` and allocates nothing.

**It holds no cached answer**: there is no memo field, no dirty flag and no early exit other than the first failing child, so every call re-walks the whole subtree. With 100,464 live CAndTriggers that is the whole cost model of the trigger forest.

**Extent, trap 2:** `image.functionStart(0x9D06E0)` answers 0x9D06C0, because CTrigger::CountEvaluation ends `ret 0xC` at 0x5D06DD with **no padding at all** before this prologue. The upper boundary is clean (11 `int3`, then CAndTrigger::GetBlockText at 0x5D0720); the lower one is an abutment, and the vftable is what settles it - CAndTrigger's table (VA 0x15B589C) holds 0x9D06E0 at slot 6.

**Two holders**, CAndTrigger and CMTTHModifier slot 6 - and CMTTHModifier derives from CAndTrigger, so that is inheritance and not a linker fold (trap 4). It means a mean-time-to-happen modifier's conditions are an AND-tree re-evaluated the same way.

addresses.name: COrTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**OR over the child list.** 0x5D0D00 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D0D2A (nothing matched) and 0x5D0D32 (something did). Instruction for instruction CAndTrigger::Evaluate with the test and the two return values swapped: it stops at the first child whose slot 6 answers `al == 1` and returns true, and an **empty child list returns false**. Reads only `children_first (+0x8)`; no cache, no allocation.

Note the asymmetry in the bytes: the AND tests `test al,al / je`, the OR tests `cmp al,1 / je`. For a bool that is the same question, but it is what is written.

**Extent, trap 2:** functionStart(0x9D0D00) answers 0x9D0CD0 - CAndTrigger::CountEvaluation ends `ret 0xC` at 0x5D0CFD with no padding. Settled by COrTrigger's table (VA 0x15F7C4C) slot 6. Upper boundary clean: 11 `int3`, then COrTrigger::GetBlockText at 0x5D0D40.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**NOR over the child list, not a one-child negation.** 0x5D12C0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D12EA (true) and 0x5D12F2 (false). The same loop again: it calls each child's slot 6 and returns **false** as soon as one answers 1; if none does - including when there are no children at all - it returns **true**. So `NOT = { a b }` is `!(a || b)`, and with the single child the scripts actually write it is plain negation. Reads only `children_first (+0x8)`; no cache.

12 `int3` before the entry and 11 after the exit, so both boundaries are clean here.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The scope switch: an AND whose children see a different CEventScope.** 0x5D1530 to two `ret 4` at 0x5D155A (false) and 0x5D1583 (true).

    sub esp, 0x4c                    ; a 0x48-byte CEventScope at esp+8, which is exactly the frame
    CEventScope::MakeScope(scope, this + 0x40, &local)
    if (local.resolved (+0x3C) == 0) return false
    for each child: if (!child->Evaluate(&local)) return false
    return true

`this + 0x40` is CContextTrigger's own data - CTrigger is 0x40 bytes - and is the 0x110-byte scope specification its constructor copies in. `[esp+0x44]` is the local scope's `+0x3C`, the `resolved` flag CEventScope's constructor sets to 1 and MakeScope clears when the context names nothing.

**So an unresolvable context is false, not an error**: `owner = { ... }` on a province nobody owns, or `ally = { ... }` for a country with no entry in the list MakeScope draws from, makes the whole block fail quietly.

**And the new scope is a stack temporary built per evaluation.** Nothing is memoised: each call copies the parent scope (18 dword moves, CEventScope::CopyConstruct) and re-runs the whole resolver, which for the `ally` and `local_enemy` contexts means an `operator new` and a `free` for a std::vector of candidate tags **every time the trigger is evaluated**. With 10,974 live CContextTriggers that is the one place in the trigger forest where evaluation touches the heap.

9 `int3` before the entry, 10 after the exit; CContextTrigger::GetBlockText follows at 0x5D1590.

addresses.name: CTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrigger::WalkChildren(CTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10, the base body: forward the whole argument list to every child and do nothing else.** 0x5D0680 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D06B1. 143 of the 164 trigger classes inherit it, so on a leaf trigger with no children it is a no-op.

**The argument list, corrected.** `project.json` recorded this slot as `(this, CEventScope* scope, int* unknown, int* passed, int* total)`. The count is right - `ret 0x10`, four stack arguments - and the order is not. The scope is the **second**: CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D2470) rebinds `[ebp+0xC]` and passes the new scope in that position while passing `[ebp+8]` through untouched, and CExistsTrigger's own slot 10 (0x5DABA0) calls `this->Evaluate([ebp+0xC])`. The last two are not counters either: COrTrigger's override divides `[ebp+0x14]` by `children_count (+0x10)`, clamps it to at least 1 and passes that down - an int split among the branches, i.e. a **weight** - and CNotTrigger's override replaces `[ebp+0x10]` with `(byte == 0)`, i.e. a **polarity bool** it inverts.

**What it is for.** A leaf's override reports itself: CExistsTrigger's is `if (polarity && this->Evaluate(scope)) collect(collector, weight, this->+0x44, this->+0x48)` through rva 0x4A5270, which inserts into a map owned by a **CAIStrategy** (its destructor is rva 0x4A3880). So slot 10 is the AI's weighted attribution walk over a trigger tree - which country or province this condition argues for, and how strongly - and not an evaluation helper. The name describes this body rather than the overrides; it is kept because that is what `project.json` already calls the slot.

**Extent, trap 2:** functionStart(0x9D0680) answers 0x9D0663, which is in the middle of an instruction - the previous function ends `ret 0x10` at 0x9D067D..0x9D067F and this prologue is the very next byte, so the backward walk never saw a boundary. retsBefore(0x9D0680, 0x9D06C0) returns exactly one `ret`, and CTrigger's RTTI `introduces` list gives slot 10 as 0x9D0680.

addresses.name: CTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrigger::CountEvaluation(CTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)

addresses.name: CAndTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAndTrigger::CountEvaluation(CAndTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 11 over the children: how many of this AND's conditions are met.** 0x5D0CD0 to the single `ret 0xC` at 0x5D0CFD. It walks `children_first (+0x8)` and calls each child's **slot 11** - `[eax+0x2c]`, 0x2C/4 = 11 - forwarding all three arguments unchanged, so the counters accumulate over the whole subtree. It never calls slot 6 itself; the leaves do.

That is the `n of m conditions met` figure the trigger tooltip shows, and it costs a **second** full evaluation of every leaf under the block.

7 `int3` before the entry; it abuts COrTrigger::Evaluate at 0x5D0D00 with none after (trap 2 for that function, not for this one).

**Eight holders**, all slot 11: CAndTrigger, CAnyCoreTrigger, CAnyNeighborCountryTrigger, CAnyNeighborProvinceTrigger, CAnyOwnedProvinceTrigger, CEnemyScopeTrigger, CMTTHModifier and CRegionScopeTrigger. All eight derive from CAndTrigger, so this is inheritance and not a linker fold (trap 4).

addresses.name: COrTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall COrTrigger::CountEvaluation(COrTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)

addresses.name: COrTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall COrTrigger::WalkChildren(COrTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10 for an OR: split the weight between the branches.** 0x5D1270 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D12B1.

    share = weight / this->children_count (+0x10)      ; signed idiv
    if (share < 1) share = 1
    for each child: child->WalkChildren(collector, scope, polarity, share)

This is what identifies the fourth argument of slot 10 as a weight rather than the depth the slot-9 signature of the same shape carries: nothing else would be divided by the number of children.

**It divides by `children_count` without testing it for zero** - an `or = { }` with no children would raise a divide-by-zero here. The loader never builds one, so this is a note about the body and not a reachable fault. 6 `int3` before the entry, 12 after.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNotTrigger::WalkChildren(CNotTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10 for a NOT: flip the polarity and hand the same weight down.** 0x5D1340 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D1375.

    flipped = (polarity == 0)                 ; cmp byte [ebp+0x10], 0 ; sete bl
    for each child: child->WalkChildren(collector, scope, flipped, weight)

This is what identifies the third argument of slot 10 as a bool: it is read as a byte, compared with zero and passed on as the result of that comparison. A leaf's override uses it as `report only if set` - see CExistsTrigger at 0x5DABA0 - so under an odd number of NOTs a satisfied condition is **not** reported to the collector. 15 `int3` before the entry, 8 after.

addresses.name: CNotTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNotTrigger::CountEvaluation(CNotTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::WalkChildren
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CContextTrigger::WalkChildren(CContextTrigger* this, void* collector, CEventScope* scope, bool polarity, int weight)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 10 for a context: rebind the scope, then run the base body with it.** 0x5D2470 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x5D24B0. The same 0x48-byte stack scope and the same `resolved (+0x3C)` gate as CContextTrigger::Evaluate, and then a **direct** call to CTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D0680) with the new scope substituted for argument 2 and the other three passed through.

This is the body that fixes slot 10's argument order: `ecx` for MakeScope comes from `[ebp+0xC]`, and `[ebp+8]` is pushed on unchanged. 9 `int3` before the entry, 13 after.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation(CContextTrigger* this, CEventScope* scope, int* passed, int* total)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 11 for a context.** 0x5D24C0 to the single `ret 0xC` at 0x5D250D. It builds the rebound 0x48-byte stack scope exactly as Evaluate does and then walks the children calling their **slot 11** with it, forwarding `passed` and `total`.

**It does not test `resolved (+0x3C)`**, which CContextTrigger::Evaluate and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren both do - so when the context names nothing the tooltip counts the children against a scope the evaluator would have refused. That is a difference between the displayed tally and the answer, and it is in the bytes rather than inferred. CContextTrigger::GetBlockText does not test it either, so the split is between the two simulation-side slots and the two display-side ones. 13 `int3` before the entry; it abuts the next function at 0x5D2510.

addresses.name: CEventScope::MakeScope
addresses.signature: CEventScope* __thiscall CEventScope::MakeScope(CEventScope* this, CEventScopeSpec* spec, CEventScope* out)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of scope rebinding - what `owner = { ... }`, `FROM = { ... }` or a bare country tag actually does.** 0x5C1C10 to four `ret 8` at 0x5C1C85, 0x5C1E03, 0x5C1F6A and 0x5C1FD4; all four restore the same SEH slot `[esp+0x84]` and the body has one prologue, so it is one function (trap 3). 14 `int3` before the entry, 9 after the last exit. Eight callers: CContextTrigger slots 6, 9, 10 and 11, CTrigger::LoadKey (0x5CAE96), and three in the effect loader at 0x59E2C8/0x59E337/0x59E635.

`spec` is the 0x110-byte scope specification a CContextTrigger keeps at `this + 0x40`: a SaveToken at +0, the key's text as 0x100 bytes at +4, a literal province id at +0x104 and a literal CCountryTag at +0x108/+0x10C. It is left as `void*` because `project.json` has no struct for it yet; EventScopeSpec_Construct (0x5C1B30) is what fills it.

It **copies the receiver into `out` first** (CEventScope::CopyConstruct), so the new scope inherits the random state, the seed, `rebel_faction`, both `from_*` fields and - crucially - `this_scope (+0x38)` unchanged, and the cases below then overwrite only `country` and `province`. That is the rebinding mechanism in one sentence.

Then, in order:

- `spec->+0x10C != 0`, i.e. the key was a country tag the database knows: `out->country = spec->+0x108/+0x10C`, `out->province = 0`. This is the `GER = { ... }` form, and it is tested **before** the token switch.
- otherwise a switch on `spec->token`:

| token | id | what it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (number) | 0xC | `province = spec->+0x104`, `country = "---"` - a bare province id |
| `owner` | 0x1EC | `country` = `g_CMap (0x1A8557C) ->+0x2200 [province] ->owner (+0x32C)`, `province = 0` |
| `controller` | 0x1ED | the same province's `controller (+0x334)`, `province = 0` |
| `from` | 0x34F | `country = from_country (+0x18)`, `province = from_province (+0x30)` |
| `ally` | 0x359 | a **random** entry of the CList at `CCountry +0xF88` of `country_id`'s country |
| `this` | 0x377 | `country` and `province` of `this_scope (+0x38)`, then returns at once |
| `capital_scope` | 0x3B4 | `province` = that country's `acting_capital_province_id (+0xE24)`, `country = "---"` |
| `sea_zone` | 0x3E8 | `province` = `province->path_node_ptr (+0xD4) ->+0xA4`, `country = "---"` |
| `local_enemy` | 0x621 | a **random** owner tag among the units in the province (`CMapProvince::units +0x2B8`) whose `combats_count (+0x11C) > 0` and whose `owner_id (+0x128)` is not the province's owner |
| `overlord` | 0x631 | that country's `faction_leader_tag (+0xF38)`, `province = 0` |
| anything else | - | sets `out->unknown_context (+0x3D) = 1` and falls into the empty-candidate arm |

The two random cases build a `std::vector<CCountryTag>` on the stack with an `operator new`, pick an element with `(rand(&this->random_state) % count)` through the LCG at rva 0x6A2E90, and free it - **per call**, so those two context keywords are the only ones in the language that touch the heap to be evaluated. When the vector comes up empty, 0x5C1F34 clears `out->resolved (+0x3C)`, which is the flag every caller but CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation then refuses on.

Two tokens, 0xC and 0xF, are **not in the compiled token table** at all; so are the other low lexer ids 7, 10, 13, 14, 15 and 19. 0xF is the one EventScopeSpec_Construct tests before trying the text as a country tag and 0xC is the one this switch answers with the literal province id, so they are the identifier and number classes of the lexer rather than save keys. That part is inference.

addresses.name: CEventScope::CEventScope
addresses.signature: CEventScope* __stdcall CEventScope::CEventScope(CEventScope* this@EAX, int seed@EDX, int unknown@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**The CEventScope constructor, and the authority on the object's size.** 0x5C1610 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C167F, 7 `int3` before and 14 after; CEventScope::SaveContents follows at 0x5C1690. It is called out of line at 40 sites and inlined at many more - the daily event pass (0x5C0A40) has a copy at 0x5C0A80-0x5C0ABC.

A register convention: `this` arrives in **EAX** and is used before it is written, the seed in **EDX**, one value on the stack, and EAX comes back unchanged so callers use it as the return - CTrigger::LoadKey does `mov ecx, eax` straight after. Hence the explicit storage on every parameter.

It writes, in this order: `+0 = vftable (VA 0x15B8AEC)`, `+4 = 0x18D` (the CPersistent `none` token), `+8 = 1` (dead - overwritten at the end), `+0x10 = 0x2D2D2D` (`"---"`), `+0x18 = 0x2D2D2D`, `+0x40 = [ebp+8]`, then zeroes `+0x24`, `+0x14`, `+0x1C`, `+0x34`, `+0x44`, `+0x28`, `+0x30`, `+0x20`, sets `word +0x3C = 1` (so `resolved = 1`, `unknown_context = 0`), `+0x2C = seed`, **`+0x38 = this`**, and finally `+8 = seed` and `+0xC = seed`.

The highest field it touches is `+0x44`, which with CEventScope::CopyConstruct's +4..+0x44 makes the object **0x48 bytes** - `project.json`'s `size` of `0x38` is wrong, and the comment on `+0x34` in the same record already says 0x48.

`+0x38 = this` is the one to keep: it means the `this` context always resolves, and since the copy constructor copies the pointer verbatim, a rebound scope still points at the scope the event was raised with.

The stack argument lands in `+0x40` and is 0 at 28 of the 29 call sites inspected; `0x474501` is the exception and passes its own `[ebp+0xc]`. Left unnamed.

addresses.name: CEventScope::CopyConstruct
addresses.comment:
**Copy one CEventScope over another, field by field, and the second witness that the object is 0x48 bytes.** 0x3C850 to the bare `ret` at 0x3C8C4, 5 `int3` after; 51 sites in the image reference the vftable constant it writes and this is the out-of-line copy they share.

It writes the vftable (VA 0x15B8AEC) and then copies **+4 through +0x44** - sixteen dwords and the two bytes at +0x3C and +0x3D, read with `movzx` one at a time, which is how we know `resolved` and `unknown_context` are two separate bools rather than the word the constructor writes them as. Nothing past +0x44 is touched, and nothing before +4.

Both arguments are in registers and there is no stack to clean, hence the bare `ret` and the explicit storage. It copies `this_scope (+0x38)` **verbatim**, which is what makes a rebound scope still resolve `this` to the original.

addresses.name: CEventScope::SaveContents
addresses.comment:
**Slot 2, and the key-by-key authority on CEventScope's layout.** 0x5C1690 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C1889, 4 `int3` before CEventScope::LoadKey at 0x5C1890. Every field is written only when it is non-zero, in this order:

| guard | key | written from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+0x14 != 0` | `country` (0x24D) | the string at `+0x10` |
| `+0x28 != 0` | `province` (0x1EE) | `+0x28` as a number |
| `+0x1C != 0` | `from_country` (0x61B) | the string at `+0x18` |
| `+0x30 != 0` | `from_province` (0x61C) | `+0x30` as a number |
| `+0x20 != 0 \|\| +0x24 != 0` | `rebel_faction` (0x644) | the object-id pair at `+0x20`, through rva 0x6789F0 |
| always | `seed` (0x356) | `+0x2C` as a number |

So six of CEventScope's fourteen dwords are persisted and the other eight - the random state at +8/+0xC, `days_in_month`, `this_scope`, the two flags, +0x40 and +0x44 - are runtime only. That is the matching half of CEventScope::LoadKey (0x5C1890), which switches on the same six tokens and writes the same six offsets.

addresses.name: EventScope_GetCountryTag
addresses.comment:
**"Which country is this scope about", resolved through `this_scope`.** 0x5C1A40 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C1B1F, 3 `int3` before and 14 after.

    s = scope->this_scope (+0x38)
    if (s->country_id (+0x14) != 0 || s->province (+0x28) == 0)
        *out = s->country (+0x10)
    else
        *out = g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) ->+0xB8C [s->province] ->owner (+0x32C)
    return out

So a scope that names only a province still answers with a country - the province's owner - and a scope that names neither answers `"---"` with id 0. It reaches the scope **only** through `+0x38`, which is the clearest single piece of evidence for what that field is: the constructor sets it to `this`, so for an unrebound scope this reads the scope itself.

Class-free on purpose (trap 11): the scope is a stack argument, `ecx` is never read, and the out pointer arrives in **EDI**, so no ordinary `__thiscall` describes it.

addresses.name: EventScopeSpec_Construct
addresses.comment:
**Build the 0x110-byte scope specification a CContextTrigger carries, from the parsed key.** 0x5C1B30 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5C1BFF, 14 `int3` on both sides.

    memcpy(out, source, 0x104)                   ; rep movsd, 0x41 dwords
    out->+0x104 = 0; out->+0x108 = "---"; out->+0x10C = 0
    if (atoi(out + 4) != 0)   out->+0x104 = atoi(out + 4)
    else if (out->+0 == 0xF)  CCountryDataBase::GetTag(db, &out->+0x108, out + 4)

So the 0x104-byte head it copies is `{ SaveToken token; char text[0x100]; }` - the parse context's current token, taken from `CParseContext + 0x20` by CTrigger::LoadKey - and this function derives the two literal forms from the text: a province id when the text is a number, a country tag when the text is a word (token 0xF) the country database knows. The country database is get-or-created here, 0x57C bytes through CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase (rva 0x24D0) on the singleton at 0x1A855A4.

`source` arrives in EDX and `out` on the stack, so the convention is explicit. Also called as the copy constructor of the member, from CContextTrigger::CContextTrigger at 0x5D150E.

**The struct wants a name in `project.json`.** There is no RTTI class for it and `mergeFindings` will not create a struct, so `void*` here and in CEventScope::MakeScope is a placeholder.

addresses.name: CContextTrigger::CContextTrigger
addresses.no_signature: `ret 0x108` - the 0x104-byte scope specification is passed **by value** on the stack, which no C declaration Ghidra accepts can express alongside the 4-byte pointer argument beside it. `this` is in ESI, and ESI comes back as the return.
addresses.comment:
**The only constructor of CContextTrigger, and where the 0x150-byte object comes from.** 0x5D14A0 to the single `ret 0x108` at 0x5D1524. One caller, CTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5CAED7, which `operator new`s 0x150 bytes and pushes the 0x104-byte spec by value immediately before.

It inlines CTrigger's own constructor - `+4 = 0x18D`, the CTrigger vftable (VA 0x15C34DC), the child list cleared at `+8`/`+0xC`/`+0x10`, a byte at `+0x14`, a word at `+0x18`, **two 0x10-byte members built at `+0x1C` and `+0x2C`** through MSVC's `__ehvec_ctor` (rva 0x796170) with element constructor rva 0x9DB0 and destructor rva 0xC480, and a byte at `+0x3C` - then overwrites slot 0 with CContextTrigger's own table (VA 0x15F7CB4) and copies the spec into `+0x40` with EventScopeSpec_Construct.

0x40 + 0x110 = 0x150, so the spec is the whole of CContextTrigger's own data and the class has no other field.

The two members at `+0x1C` and `+0x2C` are each zeroed over three dwords and destroyed by a body that frees a linked list, so they are containers; **none of the four Evaluate bodies reads either**, so they are not an evaluation cache. What does read them was not found.

addresses.name: EventScopeUnknownKey
addresses.comment: The default arm of CEventScope::MakeScope's token switch, and the **only** writer of `CEventScope::unknown_context (+0x3D)`: `mov byte ptr [esp+0x75], cl` with `cl == 1`. It then falls into the empty-candidate arm at 0x5C1F34, which also clears `resolved (+0x3C)`. Reached for every key the switch does not recognise and the spec could not turn into a literal country tag.

addresses.name: EventScopeNoCandidate
addresses.comment: `mov byte ptr [esp+0x74], 0` - the **only** writer that clears `CEventScope::resolved (+0x3C)`, reached when the candidate vector CEventScope::MakeScope built is empty. That happens for `ally` on a country with an empty list, for `local_enemy` in a province with no qualifying unit, and for every unrecognised key, which arrives here through the default arm at 0x5C1F01. It is the byte CContextTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D154D) and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D248D) test before doing anything, and that two of the three effect-side callers of MakeScope test as well (0x59E2CD, 0x59E33C). CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation, CContextTrigger::GetBlockText and the caller at 0x59E635 do not.

addresses.name: TriggerLoadKeyScopeTest
addresses.comment:
**The seam between the grammar and the evaluator**, inside CTrigger::LoadKey's default arm: `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x3d], 0; sete al`. A key that is none of the 152 trigger keywords is turned into a scope specification (EventScopeSpec_Construct at 0x5CAE72), tried against a throwaway CEventScope built at 0x5CAE82, and **only if `unknown_context (+0x3D)` is still zero** does the loader `operator new(0x150)` a CContextTrigger for it (0x5CAEA6) rather than reporting a parse error through `trigger.cpp` at 0x5CAEEE.

This is why `CContextTrigger` has 10,974 live instances while `findings/FINDINGS-script.md` could place only 2 of its 153 keys: its keys are not in CTrigger::LoadKey's table at all - they are whatever CEventScope::MakeScope recognises, which is ten tokens plus any country tag plus any number. It is also the only reader of `+0x3D` in the image.

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's id pair; always 42

fields.name: id
fields.comment: convoy id

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: the owner

fields.name: daily
fields.comment: what it carried at its last sailing (save key daily)

fields.name: goods_mask_begin
fields.comment: begin of a seven-int vector, 1 per good carried (save key ship)

fields.name: goods_mask_end
fields.comment: end of the goods mask vector

fields.name: loading_production
fields.comment: what the loading end's network produces in a day; not saved

fields.name: transports_wanted
fields.comment: transports wanted; not saved

fields.name: escorts_wanted
fields.comment: possibly escorts wanted; not established

fields.name: transports
fields.comment: transports assigned (save key convoys)

fields.name: escorts
fields.comment: escorts (save key escorts)

fields.name: is_trade
fields.comment: bool, save key trade

fields.name: is_lend_lease
fields.comment: bool, save key lend_lease

fields.name: lend_lease_efficiency
fields.comment: **The lend-lease convoy efficiency, thousandths, capped at 1000** - FINDINGS-supply listed it as an unidentified factor. Three sites, and they match the mod's own comment on the defines exactly. CConvoy::GetEfficiency (0xC6B80) multiplies the whole result by it / 1000 when is_lend_lease (+0xA1) is set. CConvoy::LoseShips (0xC5940) subtracts `LL_CONVOY_EFF_IMPACT (economy +0x4C) * transportsLost / transports`, floored at 0. RunCountryDailyPass (0xDA530, at 0x4DABA8..0x4DABCE) adds `LL_CONVOY_EFF_REGAIN (economy +0x50)` a day while it is below 1000. BlackICE sets those to 0.5 and 0.02, so a route that loses half its transports drops to 75% and takes 12 days to recover. Not saved.

fields.name: path
fields.comment: the route, save key path; nodes hold province ids

fields.name: path_last
fields.comment: The tail of the `path` list whose head is +0xB0; zeroed with the head and the count by CConvoy::ClearPath (0xC6930) at 0x4C69D4.

fields.name: path_count
fields.comment: **How many provinces the route runs through**, the count of the `path` list at +0xB0, and the single most load-bearing number on a convoy. Every delivery site requires it to be at least 2. CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports (0xC7320) multiplies it by CONVOY_PATH_LENGTH_MULT, so a long route needs more transports. CConvoy::GetDefence (0xC7C10) **divides** by it, so the same escorts defend a long route far worse. ResolveConvoyRaid scales the ships it exposes per raid by max(path_count * 0.2, 1.0). Zeroed by CConvoy::ClearPath at 0x4C69DA. Not saved - the loader rebuilds it from the `path` keys.

fields.name: start_province_id
fields.comment: loading port province id (save key start)

fields.name: end_province_id
fields.comment: unloading port province id (save key end)

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: tick the convoy started

fields.name: last_attack
fields.comment: tick of the last attack

fields.name: nukes
fields.comment:
The country's stock of nuclear bombs, x1000. The `nukes` key, save token 0x577, per findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md's map of CCountry::LoadKey - **that is where it was settled; this is corroboration from the consumer side, not a first reading.**

CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4 reads it twice, both `>= 1000` i.e. 'at least one bomb': at 0x4CFE07 it adds a filter to the strategic-target survey so that only a province its own controller cores is kept, and at 0x4CFF8E it swaps the order token from `strategic_bomb (0x6F9)` to `nuke_mission (0x579)`. The second is per country and per pass, so one bomb in stock turns the whole strategic bomber force onto nuke missions.

fields.name: daily_event_candidates_first
fields.comment: Head of the CList of CEvent* this country is a candidate for. Nodes are 0x10 bytes, {data, prev, next, byte}. **Written only by RebuildCountryEventCandidates (0x9C0050), which the tick reaches only on a month change**, and read by RunDailyEventPass (0x9C0A40) at 0x9C0B52, which skips the country entirely when it is null. It is not in CCountry's save grammar (fieldmap over CCountry::LoadKey 0x4CCDA0 has no key landing at +0x8, +0xC or +0x10) and CCountry::AfterLoad (0x4D2500-0x4D273D) never writes it, so after a load it is empty. That is the reported no-events-until-the-1st bug.

fields.name: daily_event_candidates_last
fields.comment: Tail of the candidate event CList at +0x8. Appended to at 0x9C03DE.

fields.name: daily_event_candidates_count
fields.comment: Count of the candidate event CList at +0x8. **The single cheapest live test of the loaded-save event bug**: zero right after a load, non-zero after the next month change. Incremented at 0x9C03E1 and zeroed at 0x9C017C.

fields.name: historical_models
fields.comment: **this country's models, one set per unit type**, indexed by `CSubUnitDefinition::type_index` - 1643 slots. Read by CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel's callers and, **read live**, the holder of every CHistoricalModel in the process

fields.name: oob_file
fields.comment: **the order of battle to read**, relative to `history/units`. CLoadOOBEffect::Execute writes the effect's own string here through CCountry::SetOobFile and then calls CCountry::LoadOobFile, which reads it back. Nothing else uses it, so it is an argument passed on the object rather than a property of the country

fields.name: ignored_keys
fields.comment: the first of a vector of save keys this country will not handle: CCountry::LoadKey walks it before anything else and hands the value to ParseSkipValue when the key is in it. Ends at +0x78

fields.name: ignored_keys_end
fields.comment: one past the last of ignored_keys

fields.name: mobilised
fields.comment: Set by CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies at 0x4E6D49, immediately after it adds the static modifier `initial_mobilization` to the country, and only on the transition from clear to `at_war` set. Cleared at 0x4E6EBD on the reverse transition, but only for a country the played-countries array (`CGameState +0xBCC`) says is not played - the second demobilisation path at 0x4E6DCB removes the modifier without clearing the byte, which was not explained. The third reader agrees with the name: CSubUnit slot 12 skips the RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE penalty when the owner's `+0x94` is set, which is what mobilisation would do. `inferred` would understate it and `confirmed` would overstate it; the demobilisation asymmetry is the reason.

fields.name: government_in_exile
fields.comment: set when the country is a government in exile. Renamed from `use_own_pool`, which was a consequence read off GetPool: 0x50AFF5 tests this byte and, when it is clear, emits the reason string WE_NOT_GOVERNMENT_IN_EXILE - so the flag's meaning is the exile status, and answering the country's own pool at +0x9F8 rather than the capital's is what follows from it

fields.name: duration
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `duration`, which the writer loads straight out of here and the loader parses back into it

fields.name: convoys_changed
fields.comment: set to 1 every time the `convoy` key appends to the Convoys list at +0xA0. What clears it, or reads it, has not been established

fields.name: convoys
fields.comment: the country's convoys

fields.name: convoys_count
fields.comment: How many convoys are on the list at +0xA0, the third dword of that CList. ResolveConvoyRaid reads it to divide STRAT_CONVOY_DAMAGE by it when a raid is beaten off (0x1D1534..0x1D1579), so **the strategic-warfare damage a failed raid records is per-convoy, not absolute**.

fields.name: officers
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `officers`

fields.name: subunit_total
fields.comment: The total number of regiments, ships and wings the country commands, x1000. CCountry::RecountUnitTotals (0x1004F0) zeroes it and adds `unit->regiments_count (CUnit +0x40) * 1000` per unit across its three passes - the country's own units, units on loan from faction members (CUnit +0x290 == our id), and finished deployments (+0x688). Hourly, on a TBB worker. This closes one of the four offsets FINDINGS-schedule.md left open on that function.

fields.name: army_combat_value
fields.comment: **The country's total brigade combat value, thousandths** - the sum of GetSubUnitDefinitionCombatValue (0x1A8690) over every brigade, ship and wing it commands, including units on loan from faction members and finished-but-unplaced deployments. The one writer is CCountry::RecountUnitTotals (0x1004F0, at 0x1005A3 / 0x1006CD / 0x10078A), hourly, on a **TBB worker**, so a hook must not assume the main thread. CCountry::LoadKey never writes it and CCountry::SaveContents never emits it, which is why the savegame is not an oracle for it. Three readers across both country-access idioms: CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces averages it over the hostile countries across one ops-area province's borders and compares mean/ours against 0.150, scaling that province's priority down to between 5% and 100% when the neighbours are that feeble (0x4BD78F, 0x4BD7D2); and CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances sums `+0xCC / 1000` over a side's members at 0x4918C3 and 0x491994, which is the arithmetic that function's own entry records as unread.

fields.name: officers_required
fields.comment: The officers the country's brigades require: the sum of each commanded brigade's definition `officers` (CSubUnitDefinition +0x118), written by CCountry::RecountUnitTotals at 0x1005B6 / 0x1006B9 beside +0xCC and +0xC8. It sits beside the officers pool at +0xC4, which CCountry::LoadKey reads from the save key `officers`, so the pair is have/need. The name is from the summand; nothing was watched running.

fields.name: faction
fields.comment: The country's faction, and **never null**: a country in no faction points at a shared singleton at 0x1A855A8, built with the CFaction constructor and then given the vftable 0x15C248C instead of CFaction's 0x15C2430. Every alignment term compares this against that singleton and returns zero when they differ, which is why only unaligned countries drift. Its slot 7 is the boolean the alignment and surrender code use to ask whether the faction is real.

fields.name: alignment
fields.comment: An embedded CAlignment - the country's position on the political compass. This is where CCountry::LoadKey's `alignment` key reads, and every call in the alignment code passes `country + 0xDC`. Its own +0x8/+0xC are therefore CCountry +0xE4/+0xE8, which is how CAlignment::UpdateDaily copies a faction leader's position.

fields.name: alignment_x
fields.comment: The x of the embedded CAlignment's position, thousandths - the same field as alignment+0x8. Named separately because CAlignment::UpdateDaily reads the faction leader's copy by this offset when it snaps a member onto the leader.

fields.name: alignment_y
fields.comment: The y of the embedded CAlignment's position, thousandths - the same field as alignment+0xC.

fields.name: next_alignment_update
fields.comment: A tick. The daily pass runs CAlignment::UpdateDaily only when the clock has passed this, then sets it to today + ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL x 24 - the tick is hours, so the define is in days. BlackICE sets ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL to 24, so an unaligned country's political position moves once every 24 days, and every alignment weight is a move per interval rather than per day.

fields.name: starting_manpower
fields.comment: LoadKey copies Manpower into this the moment it has read the `manpower` key, so it is the country's manpower as its history file set it. Nothing else about it has been established

fields.name: is_major
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `major`: the loader sets it from whether the value is `yes`

fields.name: flags
fields.comment: the country's flags

fields.name: variables
fields.comment: the country's variables

fields.name: ai
fields.comment: the country's CEU3AI, on two independent lines of evidence: GetDiploScoreFromLua (0x60DC70) reads it and hands it to Lua, where every DiploScore_* function's first parameter is `voAI`; and 0x26196F passes the same field to the AI agent update loop at 0x4894E0. No luabind accessor exposes it, so the name is ours

fields.name: ai_hard_strategy
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `ai_hard_strategy`, which it loads by calling slot 3 on the object here

fields.name: tag
fields.comment: the country's tag and id, as BiceLib reads them

fields.name: ai_event_strategy
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `ai_event_strategy`, loaded the same way as ai_hard_strategy

fields.name: strategy
fields.comment: **The country's merged, live AI strategy, held by value** - the third of three CAIStrategy on a CCountry, beside ai_hard_strategy (+0x1DC) and ai_event_strategy (+0x334). The game's own name: the luabind accessor CCountry::GetStrategy (0x417BE0) is `lea eax,[ecx+0x48C]; ret` and the table gives its type as CAIStrategy. Built by CCountry's constructor at 0x4C8CF6 and destroyed at 0x4CB1D6. CCountry::LoadKey hands a block to its slot 3 at 0x4CE0D1-0x4CE0E4. `CAIStrategy::Rebuild` (project.json's AIStrategyCache::Rebuild, 0x4A5C90) merges the other two into it; all eleven of its callers pass `&country[+0x48C]`. This is the object FINDINGS-aiunit.md left anonymous, and `+0xE4` on it is the theatre list FindTheatreForUnit walks.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: fixed_ai_strategy
fields.comment: **Written by the `fixed_ai_strategy` effect and read by nothing.** CFixedAIStrategyEffect::Execute (0x5B0E90) stores `value == yes` here, and a byte-level sweep of .text finds no other access to the offset at all - so the effect is inert. A byte.

fields.name: ai_objective_bonus_list_first
fields.comment: A list whose nodes carry a province id at payload +0x8 and a value at payload +0xC. CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives (0x4980E0) searches it by province id at 0x498470-0x49847C and **adds the matched entry's +0xC to the objective's priority** (0x4984A0, 0x498480). What fills it was not traced; naming it would complete the priority formula. read (the use), unnamed (the list)

fields.name: oob_theatres_first
fields.comment: Head of the order of battle's theatre CList (last at +0x574, count at +0x578; nodes 0x10 bytes {data, prev, next, byte}). **Only two writers in the image**: CCreateHigherCommand::Execute (0x5DFE20) and CAddTheatreCommand::Execute (0x550600); CRemoveTheatreCommand::Execute unlinks. **Neither saved nor loaded** - neither CCountry::SaveContents (0x4CFF20) nor CCountry::LoadKey (0x4CCDA0) is among the 32 sites that touch +0x570 - so it is rebuilt by commands during play. This is a *different set* from CAIStrategy +0xE4: no code writes both. The AI reads it in CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForTheatres (0x88AAAC) and in ProcessAI's readiness gate (0x8897F7); the interface reads it from the CInGameIdler family (0x64D850) and the map-mode band (0x66A3D0).
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: oob_theatres_last
fields.comment: Tail of the order of battle's theatre CList at +0x570.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: oob_theatres_count
fields.comment: Count of the order of battle's theatre CList at +0x570. Expected to be zero immediately after loading a save, since nothing loads the list - the cheapest live falsification of that claim.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: theatres_dirty
fields.comment: The flag that asks for a full theatre rebuild. RunCountryHourlyPass tests it at 0x4D9079: set, it calls CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres(&country->strategy, 0) at 0x4D9093; clear, it calls the cheaper CAIStrategy::MaintainTheatres with `hour == country->id % 24` at 0x4D90C6. Set at 0x4A3517, 0x4B8268, 0x4E3E63 and 0x4E7152; cleared at 0x661952; also read by ProcessAI at 0x88951C. **Inferred from its one consumer**; what each setter is reacting to was not traced.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: unknown_590
fields.comment: Thousandths. **Exactly one reader in the whole image**, 0x4B6141 in 0x4B60F0, where it becomes a shortage factor: `f = 1.0` and, when `+0x590 / 1000 < 0.2`, `f = 1.0 + (0.2 - value) * 2.5`, so f runs from 1.0 down at 0.2 to 1.5 at 0. That factor multiplies the brigade demand twice (0x4B6230, 0x4B6477). A complete byte scan of `.text` for the displacement finds no writer at all - the only `[reg+0x590]` write in the image, 0x249C6C, is on a CInGameIdler. The control for that scan is the same scan on `CUnit +0x2C8`, which does find writers. So this field is **probably never written and therefore always 0**, making the factor a constant 1.5 - but "probably" is the right word, because a writer holding a pointer to a sub-object of CCountry would use a different displacement and the scan cannot see it.

fields.name: unknown_594
fields.comment: Thousandths. **One reader and no writer anywhere**: read at 0x4B61A7 into a float and multiplied into the brigade demand at 0x4B645D. Same scan and same control as +0x590. If it really is always 0 then that one term of 0x4B60F0's demand is always 0; the demand has other terms, so this is not by itself proof the function is inert.

fields.name: LeadershipDistribution
fields.comment: the four leadership sliders, a vector: this is its first element, +0x5E8 the end and +0x5EC the capacity. Typed as a structure of the four in their live order so a read is a name; the game's GetLeadershipDistributionAt(i) is [this+0x5E4][i]

fields.name: LeadershipDistributionEnd
fields.comment: one past the last of the four

fields.name: LeadershipDistributionCapacity
fields.comment: the vector's capacity

fields.name: ProductionDistribution
fields.comment: the six production sliders, a vector: this is its first element, +0x5F8 the end and +0x5FC the capacity. Typed as a structure of the six in ProductionCategory order so a read is a name rather than an index

fields.name: ProductionDistributionEnd
fields.comment: one past the last of the six

fields.name: ProductionDistributionCapacity
fields.comment: the vector's capacity

fields.name: base_ic
fields.comment: base IC written by the daily IC calculation

fields.name: lend_lease_ic
fields.comment: **IC that costs no domestic resources**, in whole IC. CCountry::UpdateIC writes it and +0x604 from the same register at 0xF14C1/0xF14D0 - `add [country+0x604], esi` then `mov [country+0x608], esi` - so it is exactly the amount added on top of the total after that total has been capped at what the stockpiles support (0xF14A6). The value comes from the goods pool at +0x6D8, lend lease (`lea edi, [ebx+0x6d8]` on the next instruction), which is why it needs no metal, energy or rares: another country already paid for it. Read in exactly five places, one per IC distributor - consumer goods 0x118D67, production 0x119D5E, supply 0x11AB4A, reinforcement 0x11BB96, upgrade 0x11CEE9 - and by nothing else; the lend-lease distributor does not read it. Each takes its slider's share of this as a free budget, spent before anything has to pass CCountry::GetResourceLimitedIC. Two readings of this field were merged here: it was proposed both as `lend_lease_ic` (from the writer) and as `resource_free_ic` (from the five readers), and they are the same field seen from its two ends.

fields.name: max_ic
fields.comment: **GetMaxIC: the day's IC before the resource cap.** CCountry::UpdateIC sets this and the total at +0x604 to the same summed figure at 0xF0FA3 and never touches this one again; only +0x604 is then capped at what resources support (0xF14A6) and topped up with the resource-free IC at +0x608. It is the province base summed with the country scaling, so it is larger than +0x604 whenever resources are short and smaller whenever lend lease is flowing.

fields.name: core_home_area_ic
fields.comment: in thousandths. CCountry::UpdateIC adds a province's contribution here when all three hold: the province's owner id (+0x330) is this country, its COwnerArea (+0x2B4) is the acting capital's, and this country is in its `core` list (+0x344). Read at 0xF1C9E and 0x11AC33, neither named. **The game's own name is not established** - this one describes the three tests.

fields.name: ic_lost_to_shortage
fields.comment: in thousandths and **negative**: (resource-limited IC - total IC) x 1000, written by CCountry::UpdateIC at 0xF14A0 only when the metal and energy stockpiles cannot support +0x604. Written in exactly two places in the image, here and the CCountry constructor (0xC8D25), and **read nowhere in .text** - it is not cleared on a day with no shortage either. Name inferred from the arithmetic.

fields.name: ministers
fields.comment: One CMinister* per cabinet post, indexed by the CGovernmentPosition's own index at +0x4C. CChangeMinisterCommand::Execute (0x54E2D0) writes it that way, and CCountry::LoadKey's loop over it calls slot 8 on each element - CMinister's vftable has exactly nine slots, so slot 8 is its last.

fields.name: ministers_end
fields.comment: End of the `ministers` vector at +0x618 (capacity at +0x620). The array is resized at 0x4CA0A0-0x4CA0AA to the number of entries in the government-position database's vector (`[0x1A87990] +0x10 - +0xC` over 4) and every slot is then filled with the `CNullMinister` singleton at 0x1A855C8, so its length is exactly the number of cabinet posts and an unfilled post is the null minister rather than a null pointer. CCountry::SaveContents walks it at 0x4D0F96-0x4D109B, calls slot 8 on each element - CMinister's last of nine - and on true writes `position->+0x2C` as the key and the minister's `id` (+0xC) through `%d` as the value.

fields.name: ministers_capacity
fields.comment: Allocation end of the `ministers` vector at +0x618. All three are zeroed together in the constructor at 0x4C8D2B and freed together at 0x4CB179-0x4CB198.

fields.name: laws
fields.comment: **The laws, not the ministers** - correcting CLASSES.md. One CLaw* per law group, indexed by the CLawGroup's own index at +0x50. Three readings agree: CChangeLawCommand::Execute (0x54EF60) stores the value its loader reads from the key `law` (+0x44) at the index of the object from the key `position` (+0x48); CCountry::LoadKey's loop over this array calls slot 16 on each element and CLaw's vftable has exactly seventeen slots; and the parallel +0x618 loop calls slot 8, CMinister's last. The three accessors are 0xF0510, 0xF0530 and 0xF0550.

fields.name: laws_end
fields.comment: End of the `laws` vector at +0x628 (capacity at +0x630), and the independent proof that +0x628 is the laws: the array is resized at 0x4CA1D0-0x4CA1E0 to the number of **law groups** (`GetLawDataBase() +0x2C - +0x28` over 4) and filled with the `CNullLaw` singleton at 0x1A855B8, exactly as +0x618 is sized to the government positions and filled with `CNullMinister`. CCountry::SaveContents walks it at 0x4D10C1-0x4D11BE, calls slot 16 on each element - CLaw's last of seventeen - and on true writes the law group's own token (`CLawGroup +0x54`) as the key and the law's own token (`CLaw +0x2C`) as the value.

fields.name: laws_capacity
fields.comment: Allocation end of the `laws` vector at +0x628; zeroed in the constructor at 0x4C8D3D-0x4C8D49 and freed at 0x4CB154-0x4CB173.

fields.name: active_modifiers
fields.comment: the modifiers on the country, a list

fields.name: deployments
fields.comment: the head of what the country has finished and not yet placed: CUnitDeployment, and CBuildingDeployment for a capital building built without a province. Tail at +0x68C, count at +0x690. **Read live**: the USA had 50, all units

fields.name: deployments_last
fields.comment: the tail of the deployment queue

fields.name: deployments_count
fields.comment: how many are in the deployment queue

fields.name: category_levels
fields.comment: the country's level in each technology category, thousandths, indexed by the category's +0x5C - the theories and practicals

fields.name: category_shared_from
fields.comment: a country tag per technology category; where one is set the build cost discount takes the higher of that country's level and this one's. Every tag was empty in the game looked at

fields.name: lendlease_distributions
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `lendlease_distributions`, which shares its storage with `lendlease_effectiveness`. The first of a vector, ending at +0x6BC

fields.name: lendlease_distributions_end
fields.comment: one past the last of lendlease_distributions

fields.name: lend_lease_from_values
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `lend_lease_from_values`. The first of a vector, ending at +0x6CC

fields.name: lend_lease_from_values_end
fields.comment: one past the last of lend_lease_from_values

fields.name: lend_lease_from_yesterday_values
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `lend_lease_from_yesterday_values`. The first of a vector, ending at +0x6DC

fields.name: lend_lease_from_yesterday_values_end
fields.comment: one past the last of lend_lease_from_yesterday_values

fields.name: total_produced
fields.comment: a day's resource income arriving in the capital's pool; first of 23 pools up to +0xA64

fields.name: home_produced
fields.comment: The second of the 23 embedded CGoodsPool and the first term of CCountry::GetDailyIncome (pool base +0x778). Already named implicitly by the record: CDistributeConsumerGoods::Distribute adds the day's money income to 'HomeProduced's money (CCountry +0x780)', and +0x780 is this pool's `money` member. Not the same thing as +0x74C total_produced, which GetDailyIncome does not read at all.

fields.name: convoyed_in
fields.comment: The third of the 23 pools, base +0x79C. The one term CCountry::GetDailyIncome skips for goods categories 0 and 1 (supplies and fuel), at 0xF184A/0xF1851 - which is the skip the record already describes as 'for anything but supplies and fuel, convoyed_in'. Named from that description rather than from a writer.

fields.name: convoyed_out
fields.comment:
The pool the ledger labels **RES_CONVOYED_OUT**, loaded at 0x4F43FE. Named by `BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip` (0x4F3000), which pushes the localisation key within four instructions of loading this pool's supplies member and comparing it to zero. Positive control: the same pattern in the same function names the already-known home_produced (+0x778) and convoyed_in (+0x79C). The asymmetry the expense side could not offer is on the display side instead: the tooltip labels each pool by name. **Credit where it is due, corrected 2026-10-02:** this name was *not* first established here. `BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp` has carried it all along, named from the game's own accessors, while this record said `unknown`/`unused` - the two halves of the fact base had drifted and this half was the stale one. What the goods-ledger tooltip adds is an **independent derivation from a different source**, the display side rather than the accessors, agreeing name for name. It also corroborates two header details nothing else had: the tooltip's displacement list skips 0x808 and 0x898, which are the header's `traded_away_sans_allied_supply` and `traded_for_sans_allied_supply`, and it suppresses `convoyed_in` for goods 0 and 1, which is the header's note that convoyed_in counts only for goods other than supplies and fuel.

Previously recorded as `unknown_pool_7b8`: One of CCountry::GetDailyExpense's and GetDailyNeed's seven pools (base +0x7C0). The record's account of GetDailyExpense names its added terms 'traded_away, convoyed_out and the three pools at +0x8D8, +0x98C and +0x9B0', so this and +0x7DC are those two - **which is which was not established**, because the expense side skips nothing and so offers no asymmetry to fit on. A writer in CConvoy::RunDelivery or CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes would settle it.

fields.name: traded_away
fields.comment:

Both were previously named-but-unordered terms of CCountry::GetDailyExpense.

fields.name: repaid_away
fields.comment:
The pool the ledger labels **RES_REPAID_AWAY**, loaded at 0x4F42AF. Named by `BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip` (0x4F3000), which pushes the localisation key within four instructions of loading this pool's supplies member and comparing it to zero. Positive control: the same pattern in the same function names the already-known home_produced (+0x778) and convoyed_in (+0x79C). **Named but not filled.** The previous comment stands: nothing writes this pool, and GetDailyNeed and GetDailyExpense always read zero out of it. The tooltip gates its line on `> 0`, so the line never renders. So the debt-repayment term exists in the field layout and in the interface and is dead in this build.

Previously recorded as `unused_pool_824`: a CGoodsPool nothing fills; GetDailyNeed and GetDailyExpense read it and always get zero

**Live check 2026-10-02: still zero, with the controls passing.** Read across **108 live CCountry objects** at the scenario start. This pool and its partner were non-zero in **0 of 108**. The controls, read through the identical path in the same objects: `home_produced` non-zero in 106, `usage` in 106, and four sibling trade pools populated too (`convoyed_in` 16, `convoyed_out` 17, `traded_away` 9, `traded_for` 8). So the reader is looking in the right place and the zero means something.

**It still only shows 'not yet', never 'never'.** One session at the scenario start cannot rule out a pool that only fills once a loan exists, and a lending mechanic is exactly the kind of thing that would. What it does establish is that the field is not written during ordinary peacetime economy, which is what the static reading said. To close it properly: play on until a country is in debt, or grep a late-game savegame for the keys.

**Still zero six years in - live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save.** Non-zero in **0 of 108** countries in a May 1942 save with a world war running, while the controls on the same read are `home_produced` 106/108 and `usage` 105/108, and the sibling trade pools are `traded_away` **72/108** and `traded_for` **61/108** - so heavy trading is happening and these two still never fill. The scenario-start reading could only say 'not during peacetime economy'; this says 'not in six years of a live game including heavy trade'. Short of reading a writer that does not exist, this is about as close to settled as a live test gets.

**CORRECTION 2026-10-02: the zero is explained, and my previous conclusion was wrong.**
I wrote above that 0 of 108 in a May 1942 war save was 'about as close to settled as a live test gets'. It is not, and the reason is a mechanic the maintainer remembered: HoI3 has an **allow-debts arrangement for trade**, and the engine implements it as a *diplomatic action* - `CDebtAction`, with the localisation keys DEBTALLOWACCEPT / DEBTALLOWDECLINE / DEBTREVOKE (0x11FB014, 0x11FB024, 0x11FB008), the save token `debtaction_action` (0x11E54D8) and the define `ALLOW_DEBT_INFLUENCE_COST` (0x11BAA10, read at 0x49FAD). Debt is therefore **not** automatic in war: one country has to ask another and be accepted.

**And in this save `hoi3.instances(pm, "CDebtAction")` finds zero live objects.** So no debt arrangement is in force anywhere, which *predicts* both pools reading zero. The observation was never evidence about whether the fields work - it was evidence that nobody is using the feature. the maintainer's own note is that the repayment side is moot in a WW2-length game anyway, because repayment happens after a war the game ends with.

**What still holds**, re-checked by hand on 2026-10-02: a scan of every memory *write* whose displacement falls inside either pool finds 19, and they are one contiguous run at 0xC900E..0xC9074 writing both pools' seven goods slots from the same register - a constructor, not a producer. (A twentieth, 0x2EDC0C, is in the CFrontEnd region and is another class - trap 12.) So 'no writer outside construction and the daily reset' stands; what is retired is the inference from the live zero.

**The test that would actually settle it**: a save in which a `CDebtAction` is in force between two trading countries, then re-read these pools. Until then the honest status is **not established**, not 'inert'.

fields.name: traded_for
fields.comment:
The pool the ledger labels **RES_TRADED_FOR**, loaded at 0x4F3750. Named by `BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip` (0x4F3000), which pushes the localisation key within four instructions of loading this pool's supplies member and comparing it to zero. Positive control: the same pattern in the same function names the already-known home_produced (+0x778) and convoyed_in (+0x79C). Consistent with the record's existing note that CCountry::GetDailyIncome adds this pool unconditionally at 0xF1869: goods received by trade are income.

Previously recorded as `unknown_pool_86c`: The ninth of the 23 pools (base +0x874), added unconditionally by CCountry::GetDailyIncome at 0xF1869 and so one of the ones the record lists as unnamed. Read here only as its fuel member +0x878, inside the force planner's inlined GetDailyIncome.

**Credit where it is due, corrected 2026-10-02:** this name was *not* first established here. `BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp` has carried it all along, named from the game's own accessors, while this record said `unknown`/`unused` - the two halves of the fact base had drifted and this half was the stale one.
