fields.name: conversion_made
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool: what converting goods produced - fuel from crude oil, and oil from energy where a country makes synthetic. GetDailyIncome counts it

fields.name: conversion_used
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool: what converting goods consumed, the input side of conversion_made. GetDailyExpense counts it

fields.name: tribute_received
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool: what this country's subjects hand it, the receiving side of the puppet tribute. GetDailyIncome counts it

fields.name: tribute_sent
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool: what this country hands its overlord, held as a negative. The overlord is the tag at +0xF38. GetDailyNeed adds it and GetDailyExpense subtracts it

fields.name: ic_resources_reserved
fields.comment: One of the thirteen unnamed goods pools. CLASSES.md records it as never used in this build; it is **read** - CCountry::GetResourceLimitedIC (0xF15C0) subtracts its metal (+0x95C), energy (+0x960) and rare materials (+0x964) from the national stockpile before working out how much more IC the resources will support. Nothing writes it outside the constructor and the daily resets, which is consistent with it reading zero in all 108 countries of two games, so the reservation is real machinery that this build never uses. The name is ours.

fields.name: usage
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "usage"; GetDailyExpense counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4

fields.name: sent_to
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "to"; GetDailyExpense counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4

fields.name: sent_back
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "back"; GetDailyIncome counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4

fields.name: pool_in_exile
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - the stockpile a government in exile holds itself. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4

fields.name: unknown_a1c
fields.comment: an embedded CGoodsPool of which only supplies (+0xA24) and fuel (+0xA28) are ever touched - a daily accumulator, added to by CSupply::DailySupplyPass at 0x287671 and 0x287993 with the part of a province's need met by its own current_producing, and by 0x1BBFBA in the unit consumption code; reset along with +0x994..+0x9AC by 0x4F28B0. Deliberately left unnamed: the pass writes production met locally into it and the unit code adds to it as well, and which of the two the field is for was not settled.

fields.name: unit_demand
fields.comment: What the units drawing on this country asked for today, before any shortfall - supplies accumulate at +0xA48 and fuel at +0xA4C on every path through CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel, including the one where the pool cannot pay. Distinct from CCountry::usage (+0x98C), which only gets what was actually handed over.

fields.name: unused_pool_A64
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool GetDailyIncome reads; it has writes but is empty in practice

fields.name: diplo_influence
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `diplo_influence`. Neutrality sits at +0xA8C and EffectiveNeutrality at +0xA90, both of which the Lua API had already named the same way

fields.name: effective_neutrality
fields.comment: Neutrality minus the threat the country feels from one single country, floored at zero and capped at 100000. Written in exactly two places with identical code - the daily pass at 0x4DA623 and CCountry::ChangeNeutrality at 0x4FC0A8 - both as clamp(+0xA8C - this->+0xE28[this->+0x11DC]->+0x5C, 0, 100000). Read by the alignment AlignTowards term for both the country and its prospective faction leader.

fields.name: reinforcement_cost
fields.comment: what reinforcement currently costs; the spare IC calculation subtracts it from what the reinforcement slider allocates

fields.name: reinforcement_manpower_needed
fields.comment: manpower to bring every subunit back to strength, rebuilt daily by CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute; the tooltip's $NEED$

fields.name: reinforcement_manpower_used
fields.comment: manpower spent reinforcing today, rebuilt daily beside the one above; the tooltip's $USED$

fields.name: upgrade_cost
fields.comment: what upgrading currently costs; the spare IC calculation subtracts it from what the upgrade slider allocates

fields.name: last_election_at_start
fields.comment: CCountry::LoadKey copies last_election here, but only while CCurrentGameState +0xD9C is clear, which is what tells a history file from a save. Nothing that reads it has been traced, and it is not saved

fields.name: last_election
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `last_election`; a date, written through the same formatter as the other three

fields.name: last_rebel_acceptance
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `last_rebel_acceptance`; a date

fields.name: remove_fow
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `remove_fow`. The head of a linked list, with the tail at +0xABC and the count at +0xAC0; the loader appends a node per entry

fields.name: remove_fow_end
fields.comment: the tail of the remove_fow list

fields.name: remove_fow_count
fields.comment: how many are in the remove_fow list

fields.name: last_surrender
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `last_surrender`; a date. isAtWar is the byte at +0xACC

fields.name: at_war
fields.comment: **Whether the country is at war with anybody.** Its only writer is CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies (0x4E6A70): cleared at 0x4E6A91, then set to 1 at 0x4E6BCC for the first country in the whole country database whose shared `CDiplomacyStatus +0x20` (war) is non-null. Every reader in the image tests it as a byte against zero. This agrees with the name `isAtWar` the BiceLib header already carried in a comment on `last_surrender` (+0xAC8) - two readings converging, trap 14 - and it is what makes `+0xAC8 last_surrender` / `+0xAD0 war_exhaustion` sit either side of it. Among the consequences already in the record: a convoy wants no escorts while it is clear, consumer-goods demand switches between MODIFIER_WAR_ and MODIFIER_PEACE_CONSUMER_GOODS_DEMAND on it, reserve brigades take the RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE when it is clear, and `CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces` abandons its whole pass at 0x89773C unless the AI's own country has it set.

fields.name: in_undeclared_war
fields.comment: **Whether the country is in an undeclared war with anybody** - the exact twin of +0xACC at_war, and the sibling it is tested beside at five places across CAIUnit slot 73 and both AI bodies. Its only two writers are CCountry::UpdateUndeclaredWars (0xE6EE0): cleared at 0xE6EFC, then set to 1 at 0xE7025 for the first country in the database whose CDiplomacyStatus::undeclared_war (+0x24) against this one is set. Thirteen readers, all `cmp ... , 0`: four in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits, six in CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits, two in slot 73 and one at 0x4CF0C4. The scan that found this has a positive control - the same displacement scan over .text finds 101 operands for +0xACC, including UpdateAtWarAndEnemies's own two writes. Live at the 1936 scenario start it is 0 on all 108 countries while +0xACC is 1 on 5, which is what a start with declared wars and no undeclared ones should look like.

fields.name: war_exhaustion
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `war_exhaustion`

fields.name: units
fields.comment: the country's units at every level

fields.name: color
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `color`, which it loads by calling slot 3 on the object here and then copies to +0xC50

fields.name: has_color
fields.comment: set the moment the `color` key has been read

fields.name: tag
fields.comment: The country's own tag held by value: three letters plus a NUL, written a byte at a time by CCountry::CCountry at 0x4C95D3 from its second argument (`al`, `ah`, `cl`, `0`). This is what the AI reads - CGameState::StartAI passes it to CEU3AI::CEU3AI at 0x6832D2, and CAIForeignMinister slot 41 passes `&country[+0xCA4]` to Lua. Distinct from the `+0x334` `ai_event_strategy` pointer next door in the loader's key list.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: **The country's index into the country database, and the number the whole engine keys off.** Written by CCountry::CCountry at 0x4C95EC from its third argument; 0 for the `---` placeholder built at 0x515D91. `CCurrentGameState+0xBCC` (`played_countries_array`) is indexed by it at 0x6561AC, `g_CCountryDataBase[+0x16C]` at 0x8895DB and 0x6EC106, and `CCountry+0xF58` (`neighbours`) at 0x89D784. CGameState::StartAI copies it into `CEU3AI+0x24`, which every minister constructor copies into `CAIAgent+0x38`, which is what staggers each minister's daily hour.

fields.name: history
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `history`, loaded by calling slot 3 on the object here

fields.name: province_ids
fields.comment: the head of a list of `{ province id, ?, next }` nodes - CCountry::UpdateIC walks it and looks each id up in CCurrentGameState +0xB8C to sum the country's IC. **Whether it is the owned or the controlled provinces is not established**; the +0x610 test then filters on ownership, which only makes sense as a narrowing, so controlled is the likelier - an inference, not a reading.

fields.name: claims
fields.comment: The head of a linked list of province ids the country claims, each node's next at +0x8. The alignment revanchism term walks it and counts the provinces whose current owner belongs to the faction being scored. Named from that use; no loader key was checked.

fields.name: areas_first
fields.comment: Head of the country's COwnerArea list, nodes with data at +0x0 and next at +0x8. It is the outer loop of CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres (0x8A9CAD) - one pass per area, which is what produces one or more CTheatre per area - and the middle loop of CAIInvasion::PickEmbarkationPort (0x89FD88, 0x8A00EB). Which areas it holds (owned, controlled or merely present-in) was not traced.

fields.name: global_modifier
fields.comment: the country's modifier totals

fields.name: can_trade_free_resources
fields.comment: A byte with three readers, all of which require it on **both** countries of a trade and all of which make it mean 'these two can move goods without money': CEU3AI::CanTradeFreeResources (0x89B730) is nothing but that pair of tests; CTradeRoute::IsValid (0xA4CEE0) returns true unconditionally when both have it; and CTradeAction::SetTrading (0xA38DF0) passes its negation to TradeRouteSetTradedOf as the flag that decides whether the money column (goods index 2) is recomputed at all. The name is taken from the registered predicate's own word, hence `inferred`. **No writer of 1 exists in .text at a disp32 encoding** - the only write is `mov byte [ebx+0xdec], 0` at 0x4D3E29 in CCountry's reset 0x4D2B60, alongside three sibling bytes at +0xDD4, +0xDDC and +0xDE4 cleared in the same four instructions. The positive control passes (the same scan finds `mov byte [edi+0xf34], 1` at 0x4EDE10 and four `mov byte [reg+0x580], 1`), so the negative is real for that encoding - but a store through a base pointing inside the object would be a disp8 and invisible. The cheapest check is live: dump CCountry +0xDD0..+0xDF0 for a faction leader and a faction member and see whether any of the four bytes is ever 1.

fields.name: technology_status
fields.comment: 0x29C bytes, allocated and built in the CCountry constructor at 0xC9C64/0xC9C8B with 0x1311B0, which writes vftable 0x15C35BC - `CTechnologyStatus` by the RTTI export (bases CTechStatistics, PAVCTechnology::__CArray). The constructor nulls it first at 0xC9745. Its +0x90 is the technology IC bonus in thousandths (added to the GLOBAL_IC multiplier by CCountry::UpdateIC) and +0x98 the energy-to-crude-oil conversion bonus; SupplyCapacity reads +0x10 off the same pointer at 0x9DE44.

fields.name: active_leaders
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `active_leaders`. The first of a vector, ending at +0xE04 with room to +0xE08

fields.name: active_leaders_end
fields.comment: one past the last of active_leaders

fields.name: active_leaders_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the room active_leaders has

fields.name: leaders
fields.comment: the country's leaders

fields.name: capital_province_id
fields.comment: the capital, as a province id - index it into the game state's province vector. CCountry::GetCapitalLocation (0x17AF0) reads it and is otherwise identical to GetActingCapitalLocation, which reads +0xE24

fields.name: acting_capital_province_id
fields.comment: where the government sits now, as a province id; the game's GetActingCapital, registered to Lua under the name GetCapital

fields.name: diplomacy_status_array
fields.comment: One CDiplomacyStatus* per country, indexed by the other country's id (CCountry +0xCA8). ResolveConvoyRaid uses it for the at-war test before raiding a convoy (0x1D1427) and CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes (0xFEE70) to reach each pair's trade routes (0x4FEF57). project.json already describes CDiplomacyStatus's fields but never said where the array lives.

fields.name: active_mission
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `active_mission`, loaded by calling slot 3 on the object here

fields.name: graphical_culture
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `graphical_culture`. CCountry::AfterLoad (0xD2500) puts the Generic one here when a country was loaded without it

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions
fields.comment: Head of the country's list of **pending CDiplomaticActions** - offers made to it and replies made to its own offers, of every kind. Node is 0x10 bytes: +0x0 the action, +0x4 the previous node, +0x8 the next, +0xC a byte. Tail at +0xF28, count at +0xF2C. Appended by CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction (rva 0xE61C0) and by CCountry::LoadKey, whose nineteen action-token cases reach three entry points (0x4CD393 for declarewar, 0x4CD5FB for sixteen more, 0x4CDAE1 for influence and request_lendlease) that all call CDiplomaticAction::Create (rva 0xE5800) with the token, run CPersistent::Load and append to this one list. Read by CCountry::HasPendingTradeProposal (rva 0xE6360), by CAIForeignMinister::DoWork (0x89E05A) and by the hourly AI pass (0x682B83), and emptied wholesale by CCountry::ClearPendingDiplomaticActions (rva 0xE63A0). In a save it appears as one `<action_token>={...}` key per entry inside the country's block, not under a `declarewar` wrapper.

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions_end
fields.comment: the tail of the pending_diplomatic_actions list

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions_count
fields.comment: how many are in the pending_diplomatic_actions list

fields.name: has_faction
fields.comment: Tested by CCountry::IsSameSide (0xEF940) at 0xEF9BE before it will compare two countries' +0xF3C against each other - so it is 'this country belongs to a faction / has an overlord at +0xF38'. read

fields.name: faction_leader_tag
fields.comment: A CCountryTag by value: letters here, id at +0xF3C. CCountry::IsSameSide (0xEF940) and CCountry::IsFriendly (0xEF7C0) treat two countries as the same side when either one's +0xF3C names the other, or when both carry the same +0xF3C - which is what makes it the faction leader or overlord. The letters half is loaded and stored to a scratch local at several points without being compared, so only the id half is load-bearing. read

fields.name: faction_leader_id
fields.comment: Id half of the tag at +0xF38; the field both friendliness tests actually compare. read

fields.name: neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the Neighbours list at +0xFD8: a byte per country, indexed by its id. RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0) walks the provinces this country **owns** and marks the owner of each adjacent province whose owner and controller are the same - so not one somebody is occupying - and which is neither unowned nor this country. CCountry::IsNeighbour is this indexed by the tag's id

fields.name: neighbours_end
fields.comment: one past the last of neighbours

fields.name: neighbours_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the room neighbours has

fields.name: controller_neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the ControllerNeighbours list at +0xFE8, the same shape as neighbours. RebuildNeighbours walks the provinces this country **controls** and marks the controller of each adjacent province that is owned by somebody and neither owned nor controlled by this country. So occupation moves a country from one set to the other: Sweden has Denmark in neither, and Germany here, because Germany holds Denmark. CCountry::IsNonExileNeighbour reads this and then checks the other country is not a government in exile, which this list does not do for itself

fields.name: controller_neighbours_end
fields.comment: one past the last of controller_neighbours

fields.name: controller_neighbours_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the room controller_neighbours has

fields.name: non_hostile_countries_first
fields.comment: Head of a CCountryList (tail +0xF9C, count +0xFA0, nodes 0x14 bytes {chars, id, prev@+8, next@+0xC, byte}) rebuilt by CCountry::RebuildNeighbours. Membership, read off 0x4E32E9-0x4E338E: the pair's CDiplomacyStatus +0x58 byte must be non-zero, and then **the owner itself is added unconditionally** (0x4E32F7 compares the other id against our own +0xCA8 and jumps straight to the append), while anybody else is rejected if CDiplomacyStatus +0x20 (`war`) is set or either side is REB. Seven readers, all in the AI layer: 0x88D14F (in 0x88C140), 0x895A62 (in 0x895530), 0x897826 (in 0x8976E0), 0x89FD52 (in 0x89FBC0), 0x8AC3A9 (in 0x8AC390), 0x8CC823 (in 0x8CC690), 0x8D9F76 (in 0x8D9E30); plus the clear in 0x4D2B60. **It is not `enemies`** - the one reader this work followed, CAIInvasion's 0x89FBC0, iterates it to find a friendly port to load troops in, which is exactly why countries we are at war with are excluded and why we are always in it ourselves. The name is from the membership rule rather than from that single use (trap 14); +0x58 is still unidentified, though it is NOT military_access, which fieldmap.py places at CDiplomacyStatus +0x4C.

fields.name: non_hostile_countries_last
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +0xF98; read at 0x4E3341 before each append.

fields.name: non_hostile_countries_count
fields.comment: Count of the list at +0xF98; incremented at 0x4E337F.

fields.name: enemies
fields.comment: Head of the CCountryList of countries this one is at war with - nodes 0x14 bytes `{tagChars, tagId, prev@+8, next@+0xC, byte}`, tail at +0x100C, count at +0x1010. Rebuilt from nothing by CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies (0x4E6A70), which frees it at 0x4E6A97-0x4E6AC0 and appends one node per country whose `CDiplomacyStatus +0x20` is non-null, in the same loop that sets `at_war` at +0xACC. project.json already notes that the inferred `CCountry::IsWarTarget` (rva 0xA9390) "consults ourCountry->+0x1008"; this is what it is consulting.

fields.name: enemies_last
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +0x1008; read at 0x4E6BD3 before each append.

fields.name: enemies_count
fields.comment: Count of the list at +0x1008; incremented at 0x4E6C02-0x4E6C11.

fields.name: undeclared_war_opponents
fields.comment: Head of the CCountryList of countries this one is in an **undeclared** war with - the twin of the `enemies` list at +0x1008, with the same 0x14-byte node layout {tagChars, tagId, prev@+8, next@+0xC, byte}. Rebuilt from nothing by CCountry::UpdateUndeclaredWars (0xE6EE0): the list is freed and zeroed at 0xE6F03-0xE6F2E and one node appended per country whose CDiplomacyStatus::undeclared_war (+0x24) is set (0xE7032-0xE7078). Live at the scenario start the count is 0 for all 108 countries.

fields.name: undeclared_war_opponents_last
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +0x1018; read at 0xE702C before each append and written at 0xE7063.

fields.name: undeclared_war_opponents_count
fields.comment: Count of the list at +0x1018; read at 0xE705A and incremented at 0xE7060-0xE7069. Zeroed with the head and tail at 0xE6F2E.

fields.name: land_brigades_in_service
fields.comment: Counted by CCountry::RecountUnitTotals once per subunit of a unit the land predicate (unit slot 15, `[vftable+0x3C]`) accepts, and only when the country is mobilised (CCountry +0x94) or the subunit is not a reserve (CSubUnit +0xA4). So: land brigades in service, with reserves counted only once mobilisation has happened. The fourth of the four offsets FINDINGS-schedule.md left open on that function.

fields.name: dissent
fields.comment: Forced to zero every day for the rebel country: the daily pass compares +0xCA4/+0xCA5/+0xCA6 against 'R','E','B' at 0x4DB676 and writes 0 here at 0x4DB691, immediately after the influence upkeep. That it is dissent is the reported identification, not established here.

fields.name: election
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `election`, which writes whether this byte is zero

fields.name: espionage
fields.comment: the first of an array of 0xF8 byte entries, one per country, ending at +0x1164. **Entry +0 is what the save writes as `spy_allocation`** - CCountry::LoadKey's case for that key (0xCE3C1) walks the array 0xF8 at a time writing entry+0 - and entry+4 is `spy_priority` (0xCE34B writes `[edx + esi + 4]`), entry+0xF4 `covert_ops_points`; `spy_mission` walks nine values an entry. The country's `spies` key is **not** in here: it is a single field elsewhere on the country. Entry+0 is thousandths - an accessor at 0x49F3B0 answers `< 1000`, i.e. under one spy, and everything that writes it clamps to the 10000 at rva 0x130D164. CModifySpiesEffect::Execute adds to entry+0, which is what that effect is for: the spies this country has on mission in the target. The country's `spies` field at +0x1170 is a separate figure. The assigner at 0xD59D0, reached from CInGameIdler::Enter, recomputes entry+0 from relations and faction when a game is entered, so a value written mid-game does not survive a reload.

fields.name: espionage_end
fields.comment: one past the last of espionage

fields.name: espionage_capacity
fields.comment: The capacity pointer of the `std::vector<CSpyPresence>` whose begin is `espionage` (+0x1160) and end `espionage_end` (+0x1164). Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4C9ACB and again by the teardown at 0x4CA9A8. The vector is sized once per game, from the country count (`countryDatabase[+0x168]`), by 0x50EB70 at 0x4D4FC9, and then filled with one record per country - which is why the index into it is the country id.

fields.name: spy_pool
fields.comment: Spies the espionage leadership slider has bought and not yet placed, x1000; the save key is `spies` (token 0x272). CDistributeEspionage::Distribute adds `basePercentage * factor * available * 1000 * LEADERSHIP_TO_SPIES / 1000` to it at 0x51EDC6 and takes whole spies off it at 0x51F112 as it hands them to presences, highest priority band first.

fields.name: tech_decay_modifier
fields.comment: **not the tech ability array** - that is +0x698. Ints in thousandths indexed by CTechnologyCategory +0x5C, and the image's one use is at 0x420652, where the decay step is `BASE_TECH_DECAY x (this[cat] + 1000) / 1000`. So this is a per-category multiplier on the decay, and BiceLib's fixMinisterTechDecay (rva 0xDE3ED, a `mov` turned into an `add`) is a decay patch, not an ability one

fields.name: tech_decay_modifier_end
fields.comment: one past the last, read at 0x4DE3B6 to size the fold loop

fields.name: convoy_damage_statistics
fields.comment: A time series the strategic-warfare screen draws (the `linechart_their_convoy_ic` family). ResolveConvoyRaid appends to it through 0x130600 when a raid is beaten off, with the value `-(STRAT_CONVOY_DAMAGE / victim->convoys_count) / 10` and the current tick as the x value. The class of the series was not read, and whether a successful raid writes a different series was not followed.

fields.name: spiescaught
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `spiescaught`. HighestThreat, which the Lua API names, is the next field at +0x11D8

fields.name: highest_threat_tag
fields.comment: The tag of the country this one feels the most threat from, as a packed three-character tag; initialised to '---' (0x2D2D2D). Written together with +0x11DC by 0x4E21E0, which scans the diplomacy statuses for the largest +0x5C. That function has 65 callers and is not one of the daily pass's, so the pass reads a cache someone else maintains.

fields.name: highest_threat_id
fields.comment: The country id matching +0x11D8. **This is the single index EffectiveNeutrality is derived from**: +0xA90 = clamp(Neutrality - this->+0xE28[this->+0x11DC]->+0x5C, 0, 100000).

fields.comment: tick the modifier expires

fields.name: tag_18
fields.comment: a tag field. **Read live on 2026-10-02 as the player's own tag** (`IRE`, id 20, byte for byte identical to +0xC30 player) in a single-player game, and recorded in an earlier session as the null tag `---`. **What distinguishes the two is not established** - CGameState::LoadKey handles a `controller` key (token 0x1ED) that CGameState::SaveContents never writes, and its handler at 0x67FDDC is a loop over a vector rather than a store, so it could not be placed. One data point each way, so this is `inferred` and deliberately not given a name. Note +0x90 does hold `---`, so do not confuse the two. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 9.

fields.name: sunk_ships
fields.comment: the head of the ships that have been sunk, saved as `sunk_ships`, with the tail at +0x24 and the count at +0x28. **Read live**: 1295 CShip in a 1942 game

fields.name: sunk_ships_last
fields.comment: the tail of the sunk_ships list

fields.name: sunk_ships_count
fields.comment: how many ships have been sunk

fields.name: supply_network_dirty
fields.comment: set to 1 whenever CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot changes a province's supply depot label, and cleared by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork; the two rebuild sites are both `cmp byte [state+0x50], 0; je` around the call, one in the tick's hourly pass (0x282630, at 0x2826E8) and one in its daily pass (RunDailyPass 0x282C20, at 0x282CEF)

fields.name: provinces_by_supply_order
fields.comment: every province sorted by supply depot distance, farthest first. Storage is one new[] of provinceCount*4 bytes at 0x27E52A; CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder (0x289AD0) refills it in province-id order and the qsort at 0x282D18 reorders it with CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending. The length is never stored here - every walker recomputes it from provinces_end - provinces_begin.

fields.name: max_supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: the largest supply_depot_distance on the map, taken from element 0 of provinces_by_supply_order right after the sort and clamped to 500. It is not the end pointer of the +0x54 vector - +0x54's storage is a plain new[] at 0x27E52A and its length is recomputed from the province vector everywhere it is walked. Where the raw value exceeded 500 the game also re-runs CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province, which is how a province cut off at 100000 gets a fresh depot label.

A get-or-create at 0x683629 also searches it, matching an entry's `+0x20` and `+0x24` against a tag and a country id.

fields.name: tick
fields.comment: current tick: **hours**, counted from an epoch 43800000 hours earlier. RunHourlyTick subtracts 0x29C55C0 from it and divides by 24 to get days, then uses MonthLengthTable and the 365.0 at 0x160A550 for month and year. 43800000 is 5000 x 365 x 24, so the epoch is 5000 years of 365 days before year zero (the factorisation is the evidence; that the designers thought of it as 5000 BC is inference). The image advances it in exactly one place, `inc dword [edi+0xBDC]` at 0x28155F inside RunHourlyTick.

fields.name: frame_time_accumulator
fields.comment: real time waiting to be turned into game hours: CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock adds each frame's delta to it and zeroes it when it posts a CHourlyTickCommand. The add happens before the in-flight test at +0xBF0, so time that passes during a long tick is caught up afterwards rather than lost

fields.name: in_game_screen
fields.comment:
the in game idler

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation.
fields.source: live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process; BiceLib/GameClasses/CCurrentGameState.hpp:47

fields.name: game_speed
fields.comment: the speed setting, used as an index into five float thresholds that CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock loads onto the stack from 0x160A2EC, 0x1718064, 0x171DBAC, 0x15AB304 and 0x160A740 - so speed is a table lookup, not arithmetic on one constant. Which index is pause, and the five values, have not been read

fields.name: tick_in_flight
fields.comment: set to 1 by RunHourlyTick in its third instruction (0x281425) and tested by CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock at 0x28114F, which posts nothing while it is set. It is the interlock that stops a second hour being queued inside the first

fields.name: pending_unit_removals
fields.comment: A `tbb::strict_ppl::concurrent_queue` of `{id_type, id}` pairs - units a TBB worker has decided should die. `CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval` pushes with a `lock xadd`; `RunHourlyTick` drains it at `0x682230`-`0x6822B7` and calls `CGameState::RemoveUnit` per entry, **on the tick thread**. The queue object is two dwords: the representation pointer is `+0xBF8`, and the counters live in the representation - head at `rep+0`, tail at `rep+0x80`, eight micro-queues from `rep+0x180`. `CheckTransportOverload`'s comment already called this "the game state's message ring at +0xBF8"; it is a work queue, not a message ring.

fields.name: pending_unit_removals_rep
fields.comment: The representation of the queue at `+0xBF4`. `RunHourlyTick`'s emptiness test reads it directly at `0x682230`: the queue is empty when `rep[0x80] == rep[0]` and `rep[0] == rep[0] + rep[0x108]`, which is the TBB base's `empty()`.

fields.name: fired_once_events
fields.comment: The already-fired registry that the `fire_only_once` check consults. RebuildCountryEventCandidates looks an event up in it with 0x68DC10(&state->0xC38 @ECX, &event->id @EDI) at 0x9C033F, keyed by the event id pair at CEvent+0x8/+0xC; a result equal to the event means the event is dropped from every candidate list, a null result means it is still eligible. The container's class was not identified.

fields.name: random_snapshot
fields.comment: a vector that SnapshotRandomState (0x282440) clears and refills every hour with g_random_draws and the dword at 0x174DA94. A pointer to this field is the second argument to CHourlyTickCommand::Construct, so the hourly tick command carries it

fields.name: ai_pass_done
fields.comment: **The latch that makes the AI hourly.** CGameState::RunAIPass (0x283080) returns at once while this is set and sets it after launching the ProcessAI parallel_for (0x68309F, 0x683116); **RunHourlyPass clears it at its very end** (0x682B1D, guarded by `+0xD9D == 0`). A byte-exact sweep of .text finds only seven instructions touching this offset - those four plus two zeroing writes in the CGameState constructor region and nothing else - so the AI runs exactly once per game hour.

fields.name: year_change_count
fields.comment: Incremented once per year change, by RunYearlyPass at 0x283E67 as its last act, and zeroed in CGameState::CGameState at 0x27D487 immediately after the +0xC68 zero. A displacement-exact sweep of .text for `[reg + 0xC78]` finds those two sites and no other on the game state: **nothing reads it and nothing saves it**. So it counts year changes since this game-state object was built, which - because a load constructs a fresh one - is not the number of years since 1936. See reversing/FINDINGS-aisched.md.

fields.name: difficulty
fields.comment: The campaign's difficulty, 0..4 (`VERY_EASY`, `EASY`, `NORMAL`, `HARD`, `VERY_HARD` in the localisation). Element 0 of the save's `setgameplayoptions` vector, written only by `CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute` (0x2D5D20) and so fixed for the game. CCurrentGameState's constructor defaults it to 2, Normal, and every save read here carries `setgameplayoptions = { 2 0 }`.

fields.name: arcade_mode
fields.comment:
The lobby's **Game Mode**: 0 Normal, 1 Arcade. Element 1 of the save's `setgameplayoptions` vector, written only by `CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute` (0x2D5D20), so it is set once when the game is started or loaded. CCurrentGameState's constructor defaults it to 0.

**This is the switch between the two supply models.** `CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel` tests it at 0x1BBA3A: above zero the unit draws straight from the owner's capital pool (`CProvince +0x15C`), at or below zero it walks the supply network. Twenty-odd other sites read it the same way. Measured live it reads 0, and every save in `BlackICE GitHub/save games` writes `{ 2 0 }`, so the network path is the one that runs in an ordinary campaign.

fields.name: selection_groups
fields.comment: saved as `selectionGroups` by CGameState::SaveContents, and the loader puts it back here

fields.name: skip_automation_keys
fields.comment: while set, CGameState::LoadKey ignores `automate_sliders`, `automate_tech_sliders`, `automate_trade` and `ai` - each of those four is applied only when this is clear. What sets it has not been established

fields.name: intel_refresh_requests_first
fields.comment: Head of a `CList` of 0x10-byte nodes each holding an int, in the `{first, last, count}` shape this codebase uses elsewhere. `RunHourlyTick` runs both intel fan-outs at the end of an hour when the count is at least 1 and this head node's value is `-1` (`RunIntelRefreshIfRequested`). `CSetCountryControllerCommand` slot 6 pushes a node holding `-1` at `0x6D3887`, so a controller change asks for the refresh. Nothing found drains the list.

fields.name: intel_refresh_requests_last
fields.comment: Tail of the list at `+0xCF8`. The position is inference from the `{first, last, count}` shape plus `+0xD00` being read as the count; this dword was not read directly.

fields.name: intel_refresh_requests_count
fields.comment: Count of the list at `+0xCF8`. `RunIntelRefreshIfRequested` tests it with `cmp dword [eax+8], 1; jl` at `0x689319` and returns without doing anything when it is zero.

fields.comment:
**Nonzero when this session was loaded from a savegame rather than started from history** - the new-game/load switch, and the field CInGameIdler::Enter uses to tell the two apart.

One instruction in the image writes it a one: 0x27CEB9, inside CGameState::LoadFromSave (0x27CE30), set after the session reset has cleared it and immediately before CPersistent::Load parses the save, so it stays set for the life of the session. The three clears are the session reset 0x27BB26 (which the loader calls first), the startup reset 0x27B599, and 0x23A60E in the unread 0x23A460; every construction of the game state zeroes it as part of the word store that clears tutorial_active +0xD9D with it.

**23 readers, and thirteen of them are inside CInGameIdler::Enter** (0x25A89B, 0x25ACA2, 0x25B06B, 0x25B26D, 0x25B37F, 0x25B4D4, 0x25B8B7, 0x25BF47, 0x25C7F0, 0x25D22D, 0x25D4C9, 0x261935, 0x261A85) - i.e. thirteen places where entering a game does something different for a load than for a new game. The rest: CCountry::LoadKey (0x4CE6B1), CUnit::LoadKey (0x1B70C7), SupplyNeed (0x9E0D7), ProcessAI twice (0x4896B3, 0x4897CB), two inside CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler (0x248CD2, 0x248EFD), 0x24C317, and four in gamesetup.cpp (0x30E744, 0x31545A, 0x315D31, 0x3160F9).

Read live as 0 in a freshly started 1936 campaign - one session, so that is one data point, but with this writer list a zero reading is what says the session was not loaded. The record previously treated this byte as nothing but the other half of tutorial_active's word store. `likely` for the name, `confirmed` for the writers and the reader count. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 7.

**Confirmed live live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save: reads 1 in a loaded save.** The scenario-start reading was 0 in a freshly started campaign, so both arms of the flag are now observed and the name is no longer resting on the writer list alone.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation.
fields.source: live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process; reversing/FINDINGS-session.md

fields.name: tutorial_active
fields.comment: set while a tutorial is running. **Renamed from `autosave_blocked`**, which was named after one reader - the autosave gate at 0x661DC9 - out of twelve. The only two writers in the image are CTutorialScreen button handlers: 0x71D6BA sets it when one of tutorial_button_1..6 is pressed, 0x71D365 clears it on back_button, and every constructed game state zeroes it through the word store that clears +0xD9C with it. Three readers say what it is for: while it is set RunHourlyPass never clears the AI latch +0xC68 (0x682B14), RunDailyPass skips the daily event pass (0x682F7B) and RunMonthlyPass skips the event-candidate rebuild (0x683C69) - so a tutorial runs with the event system off and the parallel AI pass latched off, declaring war through the command queue instead. It is zero in every ordinary game including a loaded one, so it cannot be the cause of an AI-stopped report. See reversing/FINDINGS-schedule.md.

fields.name: tutorial_id
fields.comment:
The dword between +0xD9C and in_game, zeroed by every construction of the game state and by the startup reset (0x27B599's neighbour at 0x27B59F), by CFrontEnd::Enter (0x2EFEF5) and by CTutorialScreen (0x31D3E2).

**Set to 1..6 by CTutorialScreen::OnTutorialButtonPressed at 0x31D73C**, one arm per tutorial button, 0x82 bytes after the same function sets tutorial_active (+0xD9D) = 1 - and **read in exactly one place in the whole image**, 0x24FE97, which hands it to CInGameIdler slot 90 as the tutorial runner's value.

Method: of 2441 instructions in .text whose own displacement is 0xDA0, 2434 are copies of the inlined get-or-create accessor, identified by the CCurrentGameState vftable constant 0x15CF674 within the preceding 0x18 bytes - the same discriminator FINDINGS-session.md section 1 used for +0xDA4. Of the remaining seven, one (0x4CACC5) is a different class, five are the construction zeroes above and the tutorial-screen write, and one is the single read. Trap 14 checked both halves: neither project.json nor BiceLib/GameClasses/CCurrentGameState.hpp names this offset. `likely` rather than `confirmed` only because the name reads the one writer and the one reader rather than any string. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 5.

fields.name: in_game
fields.comment:
Nonzero while the in-game screen is the live one: set to 1 at `0x25D126`, the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter`'s session build, and cleared by `CInGameIdler::Leave` (`0x262337`), by `CFrontEnd`'s enter (`0x2EFE58`) and at `0x2ED9AF`. Zeroed by every construction of the game state.

**This is the attrition gate.** `CUnit::UpdateDaily` tests it at `DailyTickEndGate` (`0x1BB3E8`) and skips both `ApplyAttrition` and `CheckTransportOverload` when it is zero - so it is not a development-era "enable attrition" switch, and attrition does run. About twenty other places test it before touching live game data (`0x255AB7` reaches `strategic_warfare`, `0x4349B2` reaches the player tag), which is the sense the name is taken from: a game is running.

One byte. The last field of the class: the object is allocated `0xDA8` bytes and the constructor tail writes a word at `+0xD9C`, a dword at `+0xDA0` and this byte, so `+0xDA5..+0xDA7` are padding.

Not saved: no access to it lives in the save or load code, and no key in a `.hoi3` save corresponds to it.

**Confirmed in a running game**, not only traced: sampled every frame it read 0 at the main menu with the pointer already live, 1 once a campaign was up - while the clock was still not reporting in play, which is the write landing before the in-game GUI is built - and 0 again on returning to the menu. See `Reversing/Watch.hpp`.

**The writer census completed 2026-10-02, and re-derived by a second method before anything was changed on its strength** (reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 1). Of 2,822 occurrences of the displacement 0xDA4 in .text, 2,820 are instructions whose own displacement it is, 2,778 of those are writes on a register other than esp/ebp, and **2,772 of those are one inlined get-or-create accessor**, identified by the CCurrentGameState vftable constant 0x15CF674 within 0x18 bytes before the write. That leaves **exactly six real writes**, and **only one of them writes a one**: 0x25D126 in CInGameIdler::Enter. The clears are 0x262337 (CInGameIdler::Leave), 0x2ED9AF (CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd), 0x2EFE58 (CFrontEnd::Enter) and two that were **not previously in this list**: 0x27B146, the out-of-line constructor CCurrentGameState::CCurrentGameState, and 0x27B599, the startup reset 0x27B240.

**It is NOT set during a load.** The savegame loader 0x27CE30 and its caller 0x27CAE0 contain none of the six, and 0x27CAE0's only three callers are the pre-game lobby (twice) and CTutorialScreen - screens that are not the in-game screen. So in_game is 0 for the whole of a load. What GameClock::movedInPlay() actually excludes is a different window: the write at 0x25D126 sits 0x4A92 bytes from the end of CInGameIdler::Enter, and everything after it builds the in-game interface, so there is a stretch in which in_game is 1 and the in-game GUI does not exist yet.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation.

fields.name: map_mode_table
fields.comment: table with an entry per map mode; the colouring dispatch only runs a mode's routine where its entry is 1

fields.name: gui
fields.comment: The CEU3Gui, returned by virtual slot 14 (rva 0x24D7E0) and the handle for finding a gui type by name - slot 18 of what comes back is CEU3Gui::GetGuiType (rva 0x67DBC0), which is TGui's slot 18 on vftable 0x15CD754. CFrontEnd holds the same slot-14 body, so the field belongs to CEU3Idler. `likely`: no writer was located and whether it is the same object as `CEU3Application +0x120` was not established.

fields.name: multiplayer
fields.comment: zero in single player; the autosave decision branches on it, apparently multiplayer (untested)

fields.name: autosave_requested
fields.comment: an autosave is wanted

fields.name: autosave_delayed
fields.comment: the writer has spent its one frame of delay

fields.name: current_map_mode
fields.comment: map mode on screen, game numbering

fields.name: selection
fields.comment: the selected things

fields.name: graphics
fields.comment: The CEU3Graphics. Constructor argument 2, = CFrontEnd +0x20C = CBackEndIdler +0xB4. Returned by virtual slot 17. Statically: LoadEverything passes **CEU3Application +0x11C**, which project.json already names `graphics`, as CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd's arg2 at 0x2329D4/0x2329DC; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg2 at +0x20C; CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler copies [frontEnd+0x20C] to +0x178C at 0x248412. MakeBackEndIdler writes the same object to CBackEndIdler +0xB4 beside +0xB8 = the application, and ProcessSessionEndRequests hands (+0x178C, +0x60, +0x1790) back to CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd as (graphics, gui, app).

fields.name: application
fields.comment: The CEU3Application. Constructor argument 4, written at 0x248418 - the **only** write to this displacement in the image (a per-displacement scan over .text finds 32 accesses to +0x1790, 31 reads and that one write). The chain, every link in the bytes: CEU3Application::LoadEverything constructs the first CFrontEnd at 0x2329DE with `mov ecx,[edi+0x120]; mov edx,[edi+0x11c]; push edi; push ecx; push edx; push eax; call 0x6ed660`, where edi is the application - its +0x11C and +0x120 are the already-named `graphics` and `gui` - so **arg4 is the application's own `this`**; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg4 at CFrontEnd +0x210 (already recorded); CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler is called once, from CFrontEnd::LaunchGame at 0x2F1144, with [frontEnd+0x20C], [frontEnd+0x60], [frontEnd+0x210] as args 1-3 after `this`, and copies the third to +0x1790. Live RTTI on the object agrees (2026-10-02), as does the DLL: BiceLib/Gui/WidgetStats.cpp already spells this offset `IDLER_APPLICATION`. Its +0x12C is the session, which virtual slot 18 (CInGameIdler::GetSession, 0x24D800) returns and which every CCommand is posted to - that field is where the name `session_manager` came from.

fields.name: map_camera
fields.comment: held by value, not by pointer: GetMapCamera is `lea eax, [ecx + 0x1938]`. Everything that moves the map goes through it

fields.name: quit_requested
fields.comment: One byte, set to 1 by virtual slot 73 (rva 0x24C000) and never cleared; zeroed as part of a dword at 0x24846D in the constructor. Its one reader is ProcessSessionEndRequests at 0x2547D2, which on seeing it replaces the session, sets the global byte [0x1A857EF] and calls PostQuitMessage(0) through the IAT at 0xD2B2BC. A deferred request, so that a button handler never destroys the screen it is running under. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

fields.name: game_over_requested
fields.comment:
One byte with two writers: virtual slot 74 (rva 0x24C010) and ProcessSessionEndRequests itself at 0x25432E, which sets it when the played tag's CCountry has NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) below 1 and the tag is not "REB" - the elimination detector, evaluated every frame. Its one reader is 0x254335, which builds a CBackEndIdler through SessionManager::MakeBackEndIdler and makes it the pending screen.

**It does not reset the game state and it does not clear in_game** - but MakeBackEndIdler calls CGameState::SetInGameScreen, so for the remainder of that frame state->in_game_screen is a CBackEndIdler while in_game is still 1. in_game is cleared by CInGameIdler::Leave at 0x2913BC, four instructions after Update's slot-1 call returns. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 7.

fields.name: exit_to_menu_requested
fields.comment:
One byte, zeroed in the constructor at 0x248473 and set to 1 at exactly one instruction in the image, 0x24FF10 in UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows, when the tutorial runner at +0x1D54 reports itself finished. Its one reader is ProcessSessionEndRequests at 0x254573.

**This is the only route from CInGameIdler::Update to the full game-state reset**: the branch calls ResetGameStateToStartDate(1) at 0x25472C and then, 0x49 bytes later, constructs a CFrontEnd at 0x254775, which clears in_game at 0x2ED9AF. The one branch in between (0x254760, the operator-new failure arm) skips that clear, but CInGameIdler::Leave still clears the byte at 0x262337 from the run loop's swap at 0x2913BC, which runs four instructions after Update's slot returns and before the swap reads the incoming pointer. So there is no frame in which in_game is 1 over a reset game state - which is what FINDINGS-session.md section 11 item 1 asked. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.

fields.name: tutorial_runner
fields.comment:
A 0x40-byte object, created and destroyed only through virtual slot 90 (rva 0x274FE0) and tested by slot 91 (rva 0x275080). Three accessors in the image and no other reader. **It exists only during a tutorial**: the one `create` call, at 0x24FEAA, is gated on state->tutorial_active (+0xD9D) and is handed state->tutorial_id (+0xDA0) as its value. Its +0x3C byte means finished - when it is set, UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows destroys the object and sets exit_to_menu_requested, which resets the game state and returns to the main menu.

The class is unidentified (its constructor is 0x8E7370; 0x8E7950, 0x833F40 and 0x8E72B0 are consulted on it and were not read), so the name rests on the creation gate rather than on the object. See reversing/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 5.

fields.name: unitlist_start_packed
fields.comment: The `unitlist_start` positionType's declared position, packed as `(short)x | (short)y << 16`, cached by CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x65A43A after looking the type up by name. `interface/unitpanel.gui` declares `position = { x = 0 y = 144 }`, and the high word (+0x1DF2) is read back at 0x65A494 as the y.

fields.name: unitlist_offset_packed
fields.comment: The `unitlist_offset` positionType's declared position, packed the same way, cached at 0x65A45E. `interface/unitpanel.gui` declares `position = { x = 16 y = 40 }`. The high word at +0x1DF6 is the row pitch, and 0x65A464 forces it to 1 when it is 0 - a divide-by-zero guard against a mod that writes `y = 0`.

fields.name: unitlist_rows
fields.comment: **How many unit rows fit on screen**, computed once in CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x65A4AC as `(CEU3Graphics->screen_height - unitlist_start.y) / unitlist_offset.y - 1`. The worked example of reading a layout number the UI has already derived from a `.gui` file: every term is accounted for by `interface/unitpanel.gui`'s two positionTypes.

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's `id` pair

fields.name: id
fields.comment: leader id

fields.name: traits
fields.comment: the leader's traits

fields.name: unit_ptr
fields.comment: the unit the leader commands

fields.name: country
fields.comment: the leader's country (mem)

fields.name: name
fields.comment: leader name, Windows-1252

fields.name: type
fields.comment: leader type (disabled in source, unverified); compared in the rank change code

fields.name: rank
fields.comment: rank

fields.name: skill
fields.comment: current skill

fields.name: max_skill
fields.comment: maximum skill

fields.name: current_experience
fields.comment: **one 64-bit value, not two words**: the loader reads `current_experience` with `%lld` into these eight bytes and CLeader::AddExperience adds to them with `add`/`adc` and compares them against the threshold as a pair. The game's 48.15 fixed point, and a career total rather than a per-level count. **The high half can be reached**: the skill-10 threshold is unreachable by design, so a leader parked there keeps accruing, passing 2^31 after another 5536 experience points. **Read live**: zero high halves on 8000 leaders and a largest total of 809977445, 38% of the way to 2^31

fields.name: loyalty
fields.comment: saved as `loyalty`, x1000. **Read live**: 1000 on 5107 of 8000 leaders and 0 on 2825, so it carries a real value rather than being unused

fields.name: history
fields.comment: The leader's CLeaderHistory, held **by value** - 0x24 bytes, so it ends at +0xA8 where `picture` begins. Its entry list is at +0x90/+0x94/+0x98 (container +0xC/+0x10/+0x14) and **RunCountryDailyPass walks it every game day** looking for the `rank` token. CLeader.hpp already called it "a CLeaderHistory held by value"; the record said `CLeaderHistoryOffset`/`undefined4` with the comment "disabled in source, unverified". See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-history.md.

fields.name: picture
fields.comment: the leader's portrait, saved as `picture`. **Read live**: `L54027`, and `empty_position` on the null leader

fields.name: trait_gain_tracker
fields.comment: The leader's CTraitGainTracker. These are the same four bytes as CLeaderHistory +0x40 (0x84 + 0x40 == 0xC4), but the engine reaches them directly as [leader + 0xC4] - at 0x165336, 0x165CEA, 0x1648EB, 0x17FF83 and 0x1BFCCF. Zeroed by the constructor (0x17F68C) and created by CLeader::PostLoad (0x17FF60) when a save has none.

fields.name: starting_skill
fields.comment: **the skill the mod's files define**: the `skill` handler writes it here too but only while it is still negative, so it keeps the first value, and CLeader::ResetToStarting puts it back into `skill`. **Read live**: matching 7296 leaders to history/leaders/*.txt on country and id, it is the file's `skill` on every one of them - 6179 still at it, 1117 risen above it through experience, **none below it**. Nothing in the image decrements +0x70, and the only path that lowers it is ResetToStarting, which resets to the definition rather than below it

fields.name: starting_experience
fields.comment: the experience the leader was defined with, in whole points, saved as `experience`. CLeader::ResetToStarting scales it by 32768/1000 into `current_experience`. **Read live**: zero on all 8000 leaders

fields.name: leader
fields.comment: The resolved leader. LoadKey reads the `leader` key (token 0x268) into it, and both Execute (0x1D7CC9) and IsValid (0x1D80A1) overwrite it from the id pair at +0x40/+0x44.

fields.name: leader_ref_type
fields.comment: First half of the leader's object-id pair, and the half compared against 0x1268 to choose between the id pools at 0x16857F0 and 0x16857F4 (0x1D7CA9, 0x1D8081). Taken for the type half by analogy with CLeader's own id_type/id pair at +0x8/+0xC - that correspondence is inference.

fields.name: leader_ref_id
fields.comment: Second half of the leader's object-id pair, passed with +0x40 to the id resolver at 0xA9DA00.

fields.name: direction
fields.comment: 0 = promote to higher rank, 1 = demote

fields.name: rank_delta
fields.comment: How many ranks to move, added when the direction byte at +0x64 is 0 and subtracted otherwise (0x1D7CD4/0x1D7CD9, and the same in IsValid at 0x1D80C6/0x1D80D6). The default constructor sets it to 1 (0x1D7BA3); the parameterised one at 0x1D7BC0 takes it from its argument (0x1D7C53).

fields.name: persistent_meta
fields.comment: 0x18D, carried by every CPersistent - so CMap is one, which is what makes its LoadKey slot 4 and its SaveContents slot 2.

fields.name: definition_file
fields.comment: `default.map` - the name of the map definition file, the first thing the constructor puts in the +8 sub-object. The full path built from it goes to the global Hoi3CString at VA 0x170C750.

fields.name: cache_stale
fields.comment: The one gate on every map cache. Written once, at 0x489C49, from IsCacheStale(this); non-zero means every cache must be rebuilt. Six readers, all byte-sized: three in CMap::LoadMapFiles (0x48A6A0 the adjacency cache, 0x48A777 the CALC_PATHS block, 0x48AE73 whether to write adjacencies.bin back) plus 0x48B808 provincecache.bin, 0x48BE3C climate.bin and 0x48DA46 navaldist.bin. Read 0 live, which the session's own time.log corroborates: 'It takes <0> seconds to calculate paths'. Because one flag covers all of them and the stamp behind it ignores climate.bmp, a climate edit alone can never invalidate cache/climate.bin.

fields.name: cache_stamp
fields.comment: The sum of ChecksumFile over seven map files - default.map, positions.txt, terrain.txt, provinces.bmp, terrain.bmp, definition.csv, adjacencies.csv - computed by 0x492100 and stored at 0x489C3B. Compared against the four bytes of map/cache/time to decide staleness, and written back there by 0x4922D0. Read 0x856CAC69 live, which equals both the recomputed sum over the mod's own map folder and the contents of the mod's cache/time file.

fields.name: lists
fields.comment: **512 CLists, 0x2000 bytes, from +0x50 to +0x2050** - the largest single thing the map holds and the one nothing has identified. The constructor runs the CRT vector-constructor iterator over them; the element destructor (rva 0x4A30D0) walks the chain from `first` freeing each node through node+8, so they are used, not vestigial. What indexes them - 512 of what - is **not settled here**; nothing in the constructor says.

fields.name: border_cutoff
fields.comment: The map's `border_cutoff`, a float, defaulted from a constant by the constructor and overwritten by default.map's key of the same name.

fields.name: adjacencies_file
fields.comment: default.map's `adjacencies` - the first of twelve file-name strings running from +0x2054 to +0x219C, each 0x1C apart. Named `_file` throughout because the bare key `provinces` is already the province vector at +0x2200.

fields.name: positions_file
fields.comment: default.map's `positions`.

fields.name: provinces_file
fields.comment: default.map's `provinces` - the province bitmap's file name, **not** the province array, which is at +0x2200.

fields.name: terrain_file
fields.comment: default.map's `terrain`.

fields.name: rivers_file
fields.comment: default.map's `rivers`.

fields.name: province_raster
fields.comment: The province-id raster: a 16-bit image whose pixel is a province id. Read live, the object holds width 5616 at +0x04, height 2160 at +0x08, bytes per pixel 2 at +0x0C, bits per pixel 16 at +0x10, stride 11232 at +0x18 and +0x1C, and the pixel data at +0x20. The engine addresses it as base + x*bpp + y*stride and takes p[0] | p[1]<<8 (0x48FE7A and 0x4900BC). Row index is the engine's y directly, so the raster is already flipped relative to the BMP on disk. Looking 2000 provinces up at their own (+0x64,+0x68) returns the province itself 1984 times, with the same 16 misses and the same wrong ids that reading provinces.bmp gives - so this and the bitmap are the same function. Closes one of the three dwords project.json records as unidentified here.

fields.name: climate_file
fields.comment: default.map's `climate`. Three dwords at +0x20E0, +0x20E4 and +0x20E8 sit between this and the string before it, zeroed by the constructor and unidentified.

fields.name: unknown_210c
fields.comment: An Hoi3CString the constructor empties along with the other eleven file names, and **the one of the twelve that the loader side could not place**. `definitions` (default.map's definition.csv) is the obvious candidate - it is among the CMap keys FINDINGS-fieldmap.md lists as going somewhere it could not see - but nothing here proves it, so it is left unnamed rather than guessed.

fields.name: terrain_definition_file
fields.comment: default.map's `terrain_definition`.

fields.name: continent_file
fields.comment: default.map's `continent`.

fields.name: region_file
fields.comment: default.map's `region`.

fields.name: coastlines_file
fields.comment: default.map's `coastlines`. A dword at +0x2198 sits between this string and the next, zeroed by the constructor and unidentified.

fields.name: tree_definition_file
fields.comment: default.map's `tree_definition` - the last of the twelve.

fields.name: high_pressure_zones
fields.comment: default.map's `high_pressure_zones` - a list of province ids, each node {id, ?, next +0x8}. CWeatherManager::Tick walks it once an hour and propagates pressure out of each one (0xB5A90). The fieldmap left this key unplaced

fields.name: province_count
fields.comment: 14190, the map's max_provinces; presumably the length of provinces

fields.name: provinces
fields.comment: every province by id, the same pointers as the game state's vector

fields.name: provinces_end
fields.comment: One past the last province - the `provinces` vector at +0x2200 is a std::vector, and this is its second word. The province count is (this - provinces) / 4.

fields.name: provinces_capacity
fields.comment: End of the province vector's storage. The constructor reserves **14500** entries here before anything is loaded, against the 14190 max_provinces the recorded +0x21FC holds - so the vector never grows during a game and the province pointers never move.

fields.name: terrains_begin
fields.comment: vector of every terrain, begin

fields.name: terrains_end
fields.comment: vector of every terrain, end

fields.name: terrains_capacity
fields.comment: End of the terrain vector's storage - the third word of the vector whose begin and end at +0x2210 and +0x2214 are already recorded.

fields.name: unknown_2220
fields.comment: A 0x400-byte table the constructor zeroes in one memset. Paired with the 0x400 bytes at +0x2620, which it fills with 0xFF instead - a value/validity pair, on the usual reading, but **what they are indexed by is not established here** and 256 dwords fits neither the provinces nor the countries.

fields.name: unknown_2620
fields.comment: A 0x400-byte table the constructor fills with 0xFF - the 'nothing here yet' fill, beside the zero-filled one at +0x2220. It ends at +0x2A20, where the next run of zeroed words begins. Unidentified.

fields.name: by_name
fields.comment: The engine's own string hash table, `{int count; unsigned bucketCount; void** buckets;}` at +0x2A50/+0x2A54/+0x2A58 - the same shape StringHashFind (rva 0x5C7D60) walks. The constructor sets 0x1FF buckets and allocates and zeroes them; **what it indexes is not established here**, but every other instance of this table in the image is a by-name index for a loader, and CMap loads the terrains, continents and regions.

fields.name: province_templates
fields.comment: An array of CProvinceTemplate* indexed by province id, with the count beside it at +0x2A64. Already described in CProvinceTemplate +0x7C's comment but not carried as a field. Indexed at 0x48E0C5 (ReadAdjacencyCache), 0x48FEAC and 0x4900C5 (the positions.txt loader), 0x48AD30 and 0x48ADAA (LoadMapFiles) and 0x4913E4.

fields.name: unknown_2a64
fields.comment: also holds 14190; purpose not known

fields.name: map_width
fields.comment: 5616 live. Already cited in CProvinceTemplate +0x2C's comment as the value MapDistance (0x492030) wraps dx by, but not carried as a field. Equals provinces.bmp's and climate.bmp's pixel width, which is how the pixel formula in FINDINGS-mapbuild.md checks out.

fields.name: map_height
fields.comment: 2160 live. Read through the CMap global at 0x48FEC7 and 0x4900A3, where half of it is compared against CProvinceTemplate +0x68 to set the hemisphere byte +0xA2. Engine y runs 0..2159 with 0 in the far south, and a bitmap row is (height - 1 - y).

fields.name: unknown_2a80
fields.comment: An int the constructor defaults to **400**. FINDINGS-fieldmap.md puts default.map's `tree` key here, which would make it a list rather than an int, so the two do not agree and the field is left unnamed rather than named off the weaker of them.

fields.name: player
fields.comment: The player, defaulted by the constructor to the tag `---` with id 0 - the engine's no-country tag.

fields.name: naval_base_station
fields.comment:
The province's **naval** base object - the naval sibling of `+0x54 home_base_ptr`, which is the object an air unit's `CUnit +0x98` holds.

CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits' rebase block hands `candidate->+0x58 + 4` to the same ship counter (0x5D5CC0) that it hands `fleet->home_base_ptr (+0x98) + 4` eight instructions earlier (0x4D2EC2 against 0x4D2FB4), so the two are the same kind of object and `+0x58` is where a province keeps the one a fleet bases at. `+4` is the CList of units stationed there, exactly as `+0x54 + 4` is for an airfield.

**Inferred, not confirmed**: what makes it the *naval* one is that only fleets reach it and only wings reach +0x54, which is a reading of the two callers rather than of the object.

fields.name: weather_pressure_distance
fields.comment: scratch for CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure (0xB6050): the cost-so-far of the breadth-first walk out from a high pressure zone. Set to 99999 on every province at the start of each propagation and lowered as the walk reaches the province. Nothing outside that function reads it

fields.name: weather_front
fields.comment: the CWeatherFront currently over this province, or 0. CWeatherManager::Tick clears it on every province each hour (0xB5C7C) and then every live front re-stamps itself onto the provinces on its own list (CWeatherFront::Tick, 0xB4657). CWeather::Update reads it and caches it in CWeather+0x28

fields.name: strategic_resource
fields.comment: saved as `strategic_resource`, and the loader writes the value straight back here

fields.name: last_convoy_attack
fields.comment: a date, saved as `last_convoy_attack` once it is set

fields.name: out_of_supply_days
fields.comment: saved as `out_of_supply_days`, and only above zero

fields.name: nationalism
fields.comment: saved as `nationalism`, and only when it is not null

fields.name: suppression
fields.comment: How much suppression stands in and around this province, thousandths. Recomputed every day by the daily province pass (0x49EE04) from SuppressionNearProvince (rva 0x9F360): over this province and every adjacent land province under the same controller, the sum of each friendly unit's strength/max_strength times its definition's suppression, then divided by 10 - so a brigade with suppression = 2.0 at full strength contributes 200. Two readers: the daily revolt-risk step subtracts min(this * 0.1, 0.2) from its plus-or-minus 0.1, and GetProvinceEffectiveRevoltRisk subtracts this outright.

fields.name: is_night
fields.comment: a byte: whether it is night here, written once an hour by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B204) from IsNight (0xA7390). Read by CWeather::BaseTemperature for a night temperature drop and by CNavalCombat::Tick (0x17BA27) for the break-off chance. NOTE: CLASSES.md's account of the command-reach maths calls CProvince +0x2C and +0x30 a pair of province coordinates; a byte store into +0x2C and a 1..5 climate id in +0x30 cannot both be true of that, and 0xA7390 takes its x position from CProvinceTemplate+0x64 instead. **It is also the largest single term in the naval disengage chance**: CNavalCombat::Tick uses a base constant of 11000 where this byte is set against 1000 where it is clear, so a naval battle is around eleven times more likely to break off at night. The naval survey found that lever and could not identify the byte; this is it.

fields.name: climate
fields.comment: a climate zone in 1..5, filled lazily by ComputeProvinceClimate (0xA81A0) the first time CWeather::BaseTemperature finds it 0, and switched on there to pick the province's base temperature offset. The name is inferred from `climate` being one of default.map's keys and from the field being a small enumeration

fields.name: victory_points
fields.comment: victory points

fields.name: convoys_begin
fields.comment: begin of a vector of the convoy routes touching this province; the daily supply pass walks it at a depot to work out how much surplus can be shipped home, counting only entries whose end_province_id is this province and whose start_province_id lies in the acting capital's area

fields.name: convoys_end
fields.comment: end of the convoy vector at +0x38

fields.name: supply_depot_id
fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts.

fields.name: supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1, 2 or 3, worst where infrastructure is lowest: 1 above half infrastructure, 2 over a quarter, 3 at a quarter and under - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. The cost belongs to the province entered and not to the edge, so a route's distance is the sum of its provinces' entry costs, and a neighbour u on the same network is a predecessor of v on a least-cost route exactly when d(u) == d(v) - cost(v). Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50.

fields.name: supply_depot_hops
fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one by each relaxation in CSupply::SpreadFromDepot.

fields.name: home_base_ptr
fields.comment: The province's base object - the same object a unit's home-base pointer CUnit +0x98 holds. CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits compares the two for identity at 0x4CE47D (`if (wing->+0x98 != prov->+0x54) ...`), and walks prov->+0x54 -> +4 as a CList of the units stationed there, summing their regiments_count into the airfield occupancy figure at 0x4CE449-0x4CE49C. So +0x54 carries a unit list at its own +4. Read only by the air body of the two; it has **not** been shown that a naval base is a different field, so the name deliberately says 'home base' rather than 'air base'.

fields.name: infrastructure
fields.comment:
An int in thousandths that the unit AI uses as "is this province worth holding a front over". `CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed` requires a neighbour's value to be at least 200 before the province counts as a front (0x4B8830), and gives the province itself the floor weight 500 instead of 1000 when its own value is at or below 300 (0x4B8BF4). Eight more readers across the unit AI and the map code. **Written in exactly one place**: `CProvince::LoadKey`'s default arm, which treats an unknown key as a building name and, when the loaded building's definition `+0x24` is 12, sets `province->+0x5C = building->level(+0x20) * definition->+0x8 / 1000` (0x96132-0x96152). Which building type index 12 is was **not** established - the mod reorders `common/buildings.txt`, so it is not safe to count. The cheapest live check is `dumpStruct.py` on a province and a comparison against the province panel.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02, and renamed from `ai_front_value`.** Read on every province with an `infra` key in `history/provinces/`, and compared: **10,642 of 10,642 agree** with `infra * 100`, where `infra` is the file's 0-10 value. (A first pass scored 98.43% against the *first* `infra` key in each file; all 167 misses were files that repeat the key, and the engine is **last-wins** - the residual was the test, not the field.) This does not contradict 'an int in thousandths': `infra * 100` and a fraction in thousandths are the same number, since the file's 0-10 is 0-100%. Paris (2613) reads 1000 = infra 10.0 = 100%.

**The old name named a use, not the field.** The unit AI reads infrastructure when deciding whether a province is worth holding a front over, which is why it looked like an AI value. The gain from the rename is that the thresholds become readable in the units a modder sees: the 200 at 0x4B8830 is **infrastructure 2.0** and the 300 at 0x4B8BF4 is **3.0**. A province under 2.0 does not count as a front; under 3.0 it gets the floor weight 500 instead of 1000.

`+0x24 == 12` is untouched by this and is still not a building index - `infra` is building no.21 in the mod's `common/buildings.txt`, so 12 is an id of something else, as the record already says.

fields.name: rebel_type_ptr
fields.comment: The CRebelType the province revolts as, or null. Read by SpawnFullRevoltInProvince (rva 0xA6C30), which bails when it is null and otherwise hands it to FindRebelFactionForProvince as the type to match. **Not saved**, and the only writers found (0x496AB1, 0x40DE92) zero it, so what sets it at runtime is not established.

fields.name: rebel_brigades_per_manpower
fields.comment: How many rebel brigades one point of the province's manpower is worth: SpawnFullRevoltInProvince (rva 0xA6C30) spawns this times max(1, manpower(+0x320)/1000) of them. Not saved, and zeroed by the same two writers as +0x60.

fields.name: weather
fields.comment: embedded CWeather (save key weather)

fields.name: weather_wind_speed
fields.comment: Wind speed, thousandths - inside the CWeather the province holds by value at +0x68, so CWeather +0x10. Named from what it is multiplied by: NAVALWINDSPEEDMODIFIER at 0x17BA3D (CNavalCombat::Tick) and 0x166B63.

fields.name: weather_rain
fields.comment: Rain, thousandths - CWeather +0x18. Named from being multiplied by NAVALRAINMODIFIER at 0x17BA56 (CNavalCombat::Tick) and by SPOTTINGRAINMODIFIER at 0x32023 (ShouldStartNavalCombat).

fields.name: weather_cloud_cover
fields.comment: Cloud cover, thousandths - CWeather +0x24. Named from being multiplied by SPOTTINGCLOUDMODIFIER at 0x32007 in ShouldStartNavalCombat.

fields.name: weather_graphic
fields.comment: the std::string CWeather::GraphicName (0xB4400) last answered for this province, kept so UpdateProvinceWeatherRange can tell when the picture has to change

fields.name: weather_graphic_changed
fields.comment: set by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B21D) when the weather graphic name has changed since the last hour - the renderer's dirty flag

fields.name: flags
fields.comment: the province's flags, saved as `flags` by calling slot 1 on the object here

fields.name: id
fields.comment: province id

fields.name: path_node_ptr
fields.comment: the province's template: edges to neighbours and terrain

fields.name: history
fields.comment: the province's history, saved as `history` by calling slot 1 on the object here, and only when +0xEC is above zero

fields.name: history_count
fields.comment: how much history there is; the writer skips the `history` key when this is zero

fields.name: modifier
fields.comment: the province's local modifiers

fields.name: modifiers
fields.comment: **The province's CModifierValues array, indexed by `modifier id * 8`** (the value in the low dword, a CModifierDefinition* in the high). Four reads whose meaning is independently known fix it: +0x50 is id 10 FORT_LEVEL and +0x58 id 11 COASTAL_FORT_LEVEL in CLandCombatant::AddAssaultModifiers' fort block (0x169A8B, 0x169AB4), and +0x180 is id 48 MODIFIER_RADAR_LEVEL in the air and bomber radar blocks (0x16C7DC, 0x1617C7).

fields.name: modifiers
fields.comment: the head of the province's active modifier list, with the tail at +0x140 and the count at +0x144. The writer emits one `modifier` key per node. Not the CProvinceModifier held by value at +0xFC

fields.name: modifiers_last
fields.comment: the tail of the modifiers list

fields.name: modifiers_count
fields.comment: how many are in the modifiers list

fields.name: pool
fields.comment: goods in the province; the national stockpile in a capital (save key pool)

fields.name: last_pool
fields.comment: pool as the last daily supply pass left it; not saved

fields.name: last_drawn_ptr
fields.comment: points at one of the drawn buffers (save key last_drawn)

fields.name: drawn_ptr
fields.comment: points at today's drawn buffer (save key drawn)

fields.name: drawn_buffer_a
fields.comment: drawn double buffer A

fields.name: drawn_buffer_b
fields.comment: drawn double buffer B

fields.name: last_throughput_ptr
fields.comment: points at one of the throughput buffers (save key last_throughput)

fields.name: throughput_ptr
fields.comment: points at today's throughput buffer (save key throughput)

fields.name: throughput_buffer_a
fields.comment: throughput double buffer A

fields.name: throughput_buffer_b
fields.comment: throughput double buffer B

fields.name: need
fields.comment: supplies and fuel the units there need today; name inferred

fields.name: current_producing
fields.comment: resources it yields now (save key current_producing)

fields.name: max_producing
fields.comment: resources it could yield (save key max_producing)

fields.name: capital
fields.comment: the province is a capital - the game saves it as `capital` and the loader sets it from a `yes`. BiceLib had it as unlimited_supply_capacity, named for its one known effect: while it is set the province's supply capacity is unlimited

fields.name: area
fields.comment: the area the province is in: **read live**, the object's own RTTI says COwnerArea, or CNullOwnerArea where nothing owns it, and 4999 provinces share 50 of them in blocks of neighbouring ids. CCountry::NeedConvoyToTradeWith wants both acting capitals to have one, and asks AreaIsConnectedTo about the two when the capitals are on different continents

fields.name: units
fields.comment: the units in the province, what CProvince::GetUnits answers

fields.name: units_count
fields.comment: **The count of the `units` CUnitList at +0x2B8** (a CList is head/tail/count throughout, so +0x2BC is its tail). CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits reads it at 0x4D6FB3, adds it to the number of units CollectUnitsMovingIntoProvince reports heading there, and tests the sum `< 1` as 'nothing holds this province and nothing is coming to it' - a reading that only works if this is a count.

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: Every ordinary combat going on in this province - first at +0x2EC, last at +0x2F0, count at +0x2F4, 0x10-byte nodes. CMapProvince::AddCombat appends to it and CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind walks it. Bombings do not go here: CCombatManager::CreateCombat puts a combat on this list only when the combat's slot 8 is false, and in the same `else` writes +0x2FC when it is true, so +0x2FC is the province's *bombing* slot and this is the list of the rest.

fields.name: combat
fields.comment: the combat being fought here, or null. CCombat::AfterLoad puts the combat here when the province has none yet; **read live**, 4 of 4999 provinces had one and every one of them was a CCombat subclass by its own RTTI

fields.name: naval_base
fields.comment: the province's naval base; NavalBaseCapacity (0xA75D0) multiplies its level_current by a supply define and by the NAVAL_BASE_EFFICIENCY modifier

fields.name: ai_param_building
fields.comment: A pointer to one of the province's buildings. Slot 78 reads `provinces[army->ai_param_b]->+0x304->+0x20 / 1000` at 0x4B245F-0x4B2482 and, when that is below 1, clears `CArmy +0x2E4` and posts `CSetAIParamCommand`. +0x20 on a building is its level, so the test is "the building this AI parameter was set for is gone". Which building it points at was not established.

fields.name: CProvinceBuilding_array_ptr
fields.comment: one CProvinceBuilding* per defined building, index 0 nobuilding

fields.name: manpower
fields.comment: manpower

fields.name: leadership
fields.comment: leadership

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: the owner. Eight bytes: the tag at +0x32C and **the id at +0x330**, which is what code asking whether a province is owned at all compares against zero - `---` with id 0 is what CCountryDataBase::GetTag hands back where there is none. Two such tests are the sea-hop gate at rva 0x1CEEA4 and the naval-base check at rva 0xA7EE3.

fields.name: controller
fields.comment: the controller

fields.name: controller_id
