fields.comment: The id half of the `controller` CCountryTag at +0x334 (letters at +0x334, id here). Slot 76 compares it directly in the inlined IsEnemy tests at 0x4DB3EA and 0x4DB46F and uses it to index CCountry +0xE28. read

fields.name: cores
fields.comment: the head of the list of countries holding a core here; the writer emits one `core` key per node, out of the tag at the node itself

fields.name: intel_by_country_ptr
fields.comment: one intel byte per country index (0 unseen, 3 partial, 9 own)

fields.name: intel_country_count
fields.comment: number of entries in the intel array

fields.name: theatre_id_type
fields.comment: The province's theatre, held as an object id pair in the same form as CAIUnit +0x68/+0x6C: type half here, serial half at +0x384. CAIUnit slot 76 compares the pair against a CTheatre's own id (+0x8 type, +0xC serial) at 0x4DB5B8-0x4DB5C2 to give a front in the unit's own theatre a tenfold scoring bonus. read

fields.name: theatre_id
fields.comment: Serial half of the theatre object id whose type half is at +0x380; compared against CTheatre +0xC. read

fields.name: latitude_north
fields.comment: Same field as CProvince +0x388 - CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset. Normalised distance north of the equator in thousandths of half the map height, written by ComputeProvinceLatitude (0x963F0) and zero across the whole southern hemisphere.

fields.name: underground_owner
fields.comment: who owns the underground here, saved as `underground_owner`: four characters and the id at +0x390, the shape of a CCountryTag

fields.name: building_nudges_capacity
fields.comment: `std::vector<float>` _Myend for the array at +0x268, the last dword of CProvinceTemplate's 0x27C bytes that this class uses for geometry. Zeroed at rva 0xA9479, set by the reserve at rva 0xA9548, and zeroed again by the destructor at rva 0xA9801.

fields.name: building_nudges_end
fields.comment: `std::vector<float>` _Mylast for the array at +0x268. `(+0x26C - +0x268) >> 2` is the element count, taken that way at rva 0x91AC8 and rva 0xAAC4B.

fields.name: building_nudges_begin
fields.comment: `std::vector<float>` _Myfirst - **one float per building type**, the same count and the same `CBuilding +0x54` index as the CMapPoint vector at +0x258, holding positions.txt's `building_nudge` block. Written by LoadBuildingNudges (rva 0x908F6), read back and rewritten by the position-editor bodies in the rva 0x29Exxx-0x29Fxxx range, and walked by CProvinceTemplate::Save at rva 0xAAC4B immediately before the only `'building_nudge'` string reference in the image. 14,190 x 60 x 4 bytes = 3,405,600 bytes, and in this mod's data every value is 0.0f because every `building_nudge` block in positions.txt is empty.

fields.name: building_positions_capacity
fields.comment: `std::vector<CMapPoint>` _Myend for the array at +0x258. Because the constructor reserves exactly the building-type count and then pushes exactly that many, it ends equal to +0x25C and the vector never grows: the push_back's `cmp eax, [edi+0x260]` grow arm (rva 0xA9596 / 0xA95DC, calling rva 0xACC40) is taken only on the last push, and CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry's resize finds the length already correct.

fields.name: building_positions_end
fields.comment: `std::vector<CMapPoint>` _Mylast for the array at +0x258. The inlined push_back in the constructor advances it by 0x10 (rva 0xA9618); `(+0x25C - +0x258) >> 4` is the element count, taken that way at rva 0x919FC and rva 0xAAA03.

fields.name: building_positions_begin
fields.comment:
`std::vector<CMapPoint>` _Myfirst - **one 16-byte CMapPoint per building type**, indexed by `CBuilding +0x54`, holding positions.txt's `building_position` block. The constructor reserves and fills exactly `([g_CBuildingDataBase+0x10] - [g_CBuildingDataBase+0xC]) >> 2` elements, which is the number of building types the database holds (59 from the mod's common/buildings.txt plus the built-in `nobuilding` the loader registers at rva 0xB7696, so 60 here). It is a **flat vector, not a list**: the element stride is 0x10 at every one of its six access sites, there is no per-element node, and the exact reserve means no capacity slack. 14,190 templates x 60 elements = 851,400 of the 879,780 live CMapPoints; the other 28,380 are the two embedded at +0x34 and +0x44.

Written by CMap::LoadBuildingPositions (rva 0x90390). Read by CProvinceTemplate::GetNavalBasePosition (rva 0xA9D70, 8 callers), CProvinceTemplate::GetAirBasePosition (rva 0xA9DF0, 1 caller), the land/sea neighbour distance pass at rva 0xA9E70, the building-graphics placement at rva 0x23FB06, rva 0x242230, and three bodies in the rva 0x29Exxx-0x29Fxxx range that also write the nudge float. Freed only in CProvinceTemplate::~CProvinceTemplate (rva 0xA9838).

fields.name: city_token
fields.comment: CPersistent's `token` word of the CMapPoint embedded at +0x44, set to `none` (0x18D) at rva 0xA9317. Nothing reads it.

fields.name: city_vftable
fields.comment: The second **CMapPoint held by value**, occupying +0x44..+0x53: vftable word here (written at rva 0xA931A), token at +0x48, and its `x`/`y` are the already-named `city_x`/`city_y` at +0x4C/+0x50.

fields.name: text_position_token
fields.comment: CPersistent's `token` word of the CMapPoint embedded at +0x34, set to `none` (0x18D) at rva 0xA9302 like all 714 inlined CPersistent constructors. Nothing reads it; see BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp on why every instance in the image carries the same value.

fields.name: text_position_vftable
fields.comment: A **CMapPoint held by value** occupies +0x34..+0x43, and this is its vftable word (VA 0x15BC65C, written at rva 0xA930A); `text_position_token` at +0x38 is CPersistent's token, and the object's own `x` and `y` are the already-named `text_position_x`/`text_position_y` at +0x3C/+0x40. Recorded because the two words before those floats otherwise read as a hole, and because these two embedded points plus the 60-element vector at +0x258 are the whole of the 879,780 live CMapPoints in a running game: 14,190 templates x (60 + 2).

fields.name: base_temperature
fields.comment: The province's base temperature in thousandths of a degree, and the single largest term in CWeather::BaseTemperature. Zeroed by CProvinceTemplate::CProvinceTemplate (0xA92E4) and written in exactly one place, LoadProvinceClimate at 0x8C0DD: (map/climate.bmp byte at the province's position - 100) x 150 + terrain->temperature (CTerrain +0x58). Exactly one reader in the image, 0xB22F6. In BlackICE the bitmap's 84 distinct indices run 26..255, so the bitmap contributes -11.100 to +23.250 C and terrain.txt's temperature another -22.000 to +12.000.

fields.name: terrain
fields.comment: the province's terrain

fields.name: unknown_flag_14
fields.comment: A byte MapProvinceIsLandlockedWater (0x4A9B70) tests at 0x4A9B81, on a template whose is_land (+0x22) is already known to be clear: when it is set the function answers true without walking the edge vector, and when it is clear the walk has to find that every neighbour is land. So it behaves as a precomputed `this water province is a lake` flag with the adjacency walk as the fallback, but nothing here reads its writer and the inference rests on that one use. Note that CMapProvince +0x14 is weather_front and is a different field on a different class.

fields.name: is_land
fields.comment: Non-zero on a land province, zero on a sea zone. 245 places in the image read it through a province's `path_node_ptr` (+0xD4), which is why it looked fundamental and unnameable; three of them fix which way round it is. `CPathFind::MayStep` refuses a **naval** step between two provinces that both have it set, and where exactly one has it, that template's `sea_province_id` (+0xA4) must name the other province. `CProvince::IsFrontProvince` (0xA56B0) skips any neighbour that does not have it. `CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost` only looks for hostile buildings around the destination when the destination does **not** have it - i.e. only when a fleet is entering open sea. `CheckTransportOverload` puts a carried unit ashore only where it is set.

fields.name: unknown_24
fields.comment: a per-province traversal cost. CSupply::SpreadFromDepot multiplies it by an infrastructure-derived factor of 1, 2 or 3 to get the step it adds to supply_depot_distance, and 0xB615E does the same thing without the factor - edi = neighbour->template->+0x24 + accumulated, compared against CProvince +0x10 - so it is a distance charged for entering a province, not an edge length (ProvinceEdge already carries its own distance at +0xC). Its actual value was not sampled from a running game, so whether it is normally 1 is open.

fields.name: source_object
fields.comment: Whatever CMap +0x2198 held for this province id, stored by the constructor at 0xA92E7; the id itself goes to +0x7C at 0xA933B. Named from the constructor only - what the object is was not established.

fields.name: centre_x
fields.comment: The province's bounding-box centre x in map pixels, written at 0x917FB as bbox_x (+0x80) + bbox_width (+0x88)/2. This is the pair MapDistance (0x92030) uses, wrapping dx by the map width at CMap +0x2A74.

fields.name: centre_y
fields.comment: The province's bounding-box centre y in map pixels, written at 0x91815 as bbox_y (+0x84) + bbox_height (+0x8C)/2. y grows northward: province 1, Porsangerhalvoya at 71 N, sits at y 2106 of a 2160-pixel map.

fields.name: text_position_x
fields.comment: positions.txt's `text_position` x, as a float, written at 0x48FE70. Paris reads 2786.300048828125 against the file's x=2786.300049. On a sea zone the same handler also truncates this pair into +0x64/+0x68; on a land province it does not.

fields.name: text_position_y
fields.comment: The y beside +0x3C, written at 0x48FE75. Paris reads 1657.5 against the file's y=1657.500000.

fields.name: city_x
fields.comment: positions.txt's `city` x, as a float, written at 0x490070 (save token 0x2A2). Where the province declares no `city` it holds the bounding-box centre as a float: Paris, which has no `city` key, reads 2786.0 against its centre_x of 2786.

fields.name: city_y
fields.comment: The y beside +0x4C, written at 0x49007B. Province 14000 reads 1214.0 / 984.0 for the pair, which is its bounding-box centre, not its `unit` position - so this pair keeps the centre where +0x64/+0x68 has moved.

fields.name: label_x
fields.comment: A second copy of the centre, x half, initialised at 0x91822 from +0x2C in the same pass. The code after it in 0x917A0 goes on to refine this pair, so treat it as the province's display/representative point rather than a plain duplicate; whatever it ends up as, it stays a map pixel coordinate.

fields.name: label_y
fields.comment: The y half of the pair at +0x5C, initialised at 0x91827 from +0x30. **This is the y ComputeProvinceLatitude (0x963F0) reads** to build CProvince +0x388, so it is what decides a province's season. Only reader in the map/weather code is 0x96407.

fields.name: position_x
fields.comment: A map-pixel x written by the map loader at 0x8FEC4 and 0x900A0. Read by IsNight (0xA7399) as the longitude that offsets local time, and by LoadProvinceClimate (0x8BF79) as the x at which climate.bmp is sampled.

fields.name: position_y
fields.comment: The y beside +0x64, written at 0x8FEBB and 0x9009D. Compared against half the map height at 0x8FED2 to set the hemisphere byte at +0xA2, and used by LoadProvinceClimate (0x8BF72) as the row at which climate.bmp is sampled. y grows northward, so the comparison at 0x8FED2 is true in the **northern** hemisphere.

fields.name: province_id
fields.comment: The province id, passed to CProvinceTemplate::CProvinceTemplate in EDX and stored at 0xA933B. The templates live one per id in CMap +0x2A60, 0x27C bytes each, allocated at 0x8A153.

fields.name: bbox_x
fields.comment: Left edge of the province's pixel bounding box; 0x917F2 adds half of +0x88 to it to make centre_x at +0x2C.

fields.name: bbox_y
fields.comment: Bottom edge of the province's pixel bounding box; 0x91809 adds half of +0x8C to it to make centre_y at +0x30.

fields.name: bbox_width
fields.comment: Width of the province's pixel bounding box, halved into centre_x at 0x917E7.

fields.name: bbox_height
fields.comment: Height of the province's pixel bounding box, halved into centre_y at 0x917FE.

fields.name: edges_begin
fields.comment: vector of edges to neighbours, begin

fields.name: edges_end
fields.comment: vector of edges to neighbours, end

fields.name: coastal
fields.comment: Set to 1 at 0x48AD67 on a LAND province that has at least one neighbour of the other kind - the branch at 0x48AD4E compares the two templates' is_land (+0x22) and 0x48AD58 picks the field by this province's own. Checked live against the edge lists: +0xA0 is non-zero on exactly the land provinces that have a sea neighbour, 10642 of 10642.

fields.name: touches_land
fields.comment: The sea-side counterpart of +0xA0, set to 1 at 0x48AD5E on a SEA province that has a land neighbour. Checked live: non-zero on exactly the sea provinces with a land neighbour, 3547 of 3547. The pair is written in one pass of CMap::LoadMapFiles over every province's edges, so it is available from the end of the map build onward.

fields.name: southern_hemisphere
fields.comment: Set where the province's y coordinate (+0x68) is at or past half the map height (CMap+0x2A78), written at 0x8FED8 as a `setge` with the x and y stores two instructions earlier. Two consumers: ComputeProvinceClimate (0xA81A0) uses it to choose between the season tables {1,2,3,4,4,5} and {4,4,5,1,2,3} - the same list rotated by three, i.e. half a year - and CWeatherManager::CreateFront (0xB5EF4) uses it to negate a new weather front's `rotation`, so fronts curve the other way in the other hemisphere. Also written at 0x4900B6 and 0x4918DF. The identification of +0x68 as y and CMap+0x2A78 as the height is from their position beside the known x at +0x64 and the known width at CMap+0x2A74, and is corroborated by the half-year rotation.

fields.name: sea_province_id
fields.comment:
On a land province (`is_land` set), the id of the one sea province it connects to, as an index into `CMap::provinces` (`+0x2200`); 0 where there is none. Meaningless where `is_land` is clear, and nothing reads it there.

It is the single gate on a fleet crossing the coast. `CPathFind::MayStep` (0x1A2700) and `CPlannedPathFind::MayStep` (0x1A2D30) let a naval unit step out of a land province only to the province this names, and into a land province only from it; a step between two land provinces is refused outright. The helper at `0xA7D70` uses it the other way, replacing a land province by `map->provinces[sea_province_id]` until both ends of a pair are sea, which is also what fixes the target as a sea province: the loop terminates only when the province it lands on has `is_land` clear.

fields.name: unknown_flag_13d
fields.comment: tested by the supply pass, the Simplified Terrain loop and the supply network builder; 1 in every province seen; not a land/sea flag. In CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork a province with it clear has its supply_depot_distance forced to 0 rather than to the 100000 'not reached yet' value, and in CSupply::SpreadFromDepot such a neighbour is skipped outright - so a province with it clear is never relaxed and never takes part in supply. Still unidentified.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment: What sort of edge this is. Only two values are tested here: CPathFind::MayStep and CPlannedPathFind::MayStep refuse an edge whose kind is 3 outright, and the helper at rva 0x1A2600 acts only on kind 1, which is a crossing through the province named at +8. The full set of values is not known.

fields.name: to_province
fields.comment: neighbour province id, index into CMap::provinces; edge is 20 bytes

fields.name: crossed_province
fields.comment: The province a kind-1 edge crosses, as an index into CMap::provinces. The helper at rva 0x1A2600 refuses the step when that province's controller is hostile to the unit's owner, or when a foreign unit that is not retreating is standing in it - a strait or crossing that can be blocked.

fields.name: distance
fields.comment: distance in thousandths

fields.name: bearing
fields.comment: The compass bearing from this province to the neighbour, in thousandths of a full turn (0..999) - the last unnamed field of the 20-byte edge record. Its only reader in the image is CWeatherFront::Tick (0xB48AD), which hands it to IsAngleWithinArc (0xB4490) together with the front's heading and its spread arc; that routine takes both modulo 1000, and the heading it is compared against is seeded Random()%1000 and stepped by 1000000/MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE, which is what fixes the units. WHAT WRITES IT WAS NOT FOUND: there is no fpatan anywhere in the map loader and the edge builder was not located, so the name is inferred from the one consumer.

fields.name: target_province
fields.comment: target province id

fields.name: mode_68
fields.comment: picks between two ways of routing; set by every player move

fields.name: safe
fields.comment: route with CSafePathFind

fields.name: very_safe
fields.comment: route with CVerySafePathFind

fields.name: unit
fields.comment: the unit being redeployed

fields.name: target_province
fields.comment: the province it is going to

fields.name: effect
fields.comment: effect

fields.name: definition_ptr
fields.comment: building definition

fields.name: province_ptr
fields.comment: back to the province

fields.name: level_max
fields.comment: maximum level x1000

fields.name: level_current
fields.comment: current level x1000

fields.name: effect_size
fields.comment: what the building does per level, x1000, and it is only ever one thing: whichever modifier key the definition carries. ic = 1 on industry is 1000, fort_level = 0.4 on land_fort is 400, and a building with no such key is zero. The modifier it belongs to is the definition at +0xC

fields.name: effect
fields.comment: the modifier definition effect_size belongs to; its name is the std::string at +4 - FORT_LEVEL, MODIFIER_IC, MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA, or NONE where the building has no modifier key at all

fields.name: name
fields.comment: building key, e.g. air_base

fields.name: displayName
fields.comment: localised name shown by the game

fields.name: index
fields.comment: index into a province's building array

fields.name: cost
fields.comment: buildings.txt `cost`, x1000: the mod's `cost = 4.5` reads 4500

fields.name: time
fields.comment: buildings.txt `time`, in days, and not scaled

fields.name: capital
fields.comment: buildings.txt's `capital = yes`. Two things read it: the production screen only looks for a build button named after a building that has it, and a construction that finishes with no province only does anything for a flagged building - it makes a CBuildingDeployment and puts it in the country's deployment queue, instead of raising the level in a province. **Read live**: set on 47 of 60 buildings, the exceptions being the forts, infra and BlackICE's request_* entries

fields.name: port
fields.comment: buildings.txt `port`

fields.name: max_allowed_level
fields.comment: maximum allowed level, whole levels

fields.name: on_completion
fields.comment: buildings.txt `on_completion`, a std::string: the practical or theory finishing one feeds

fields.name: technology_category_ptr
fields.comment: the category whose level discounts this building's cost

fields.name: completion_size
fields.comment: buildings.txt `completion_size`, x1000

fields.name: damage_factor
fields.comment: buildings.txt `damage_factor`, x1000

fields.name: onmap
fields.comment: buildings.txt `onmap`

fields.name: visibility
fields.comment: buildings.txt `visibility`

fields.name: show_for_province
fields.comment: buildings.txt `show_for_province`; true unless the file says otherwise

fields.name: prerequisites
fields.comment: buildings.txt `prerequisites`: a `{ ... }` block whose every word becomes a std::string on a list (tail at +0xb0, count at +0xb4). **Nothing reads it** - inside CBuilding's own code the only references are the branch that fills it and the two that empty it, and none of the 44 places that fetch the building database goes on to read it. Neither buildings.txt uses the key, and read live all 61 buildings have it empty

fields.name: prerequisites_last
fields.comment: the tail of the prerequisites list, which nothing reads

fields.name: prerequisites_count
fields.comment: how many prerequisites there are; always zero in practice

fields.name: not_if_x_exists
fields.comment: buildings.txt `not_if_x_exists`: a `{ ... }` block whose every word becomes a std::string on a list (tail at +0xd0, count at +0xd4). **Nothing reads it** - inside CBuilding's own code the only references are the branch that fills it and the two that empty it, and none of the 44 places that fetch the building database goes on to read it. Neither buildings.txt uses the key, and read live all 61 buildings have it empty

fields.name: not_if_x_exists_last
fields.comment: the tail of the not_if_x_exists list, which nothing reads

fields.name: not_if_x_exists_count
fields.comment: how many are in the not_if_x_exists list; always zero

fields.name: confirm
fields.comment: buildings.txt `confirm`

fields.name: orientation
fields.comment: buildings.txt `orientation`

fields.name: repair
fields.comment: buildings.txt `repair`; true unless the file says otherwise

fields.name: building
fields.comment: building being placed

structs.name: CTrigger

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null.

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list.

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape.

structs.comment:
**One condition in the event script language, and the base of all 163 of them.** Its virtual table is the thing worth having: slot 6 is Evaluate.

The size is read from its heirs rather than from an allocation: of the 163 triggers, **129 read `this+0x40`** inside their own Evaluate, and the ones that do are reading their own value there - CAlwaysTrigger's whole Evaluate is `mov al, [ecx+0x40]; ret 4`, and CTagTrigger takes a tag pair from 0x40 and 0x44. So a derived trigger's own data starts at 0x40 and CTrigger is that big.

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's `id` pair, written after the id. **Read live**: 41 on what a scenario started with, 4713 on what the game has built since

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the regiment's id, the first half of the save's `id` pair

fields.name: strength_ceiling
fields.comment: set to the regiment's strength when it is built and afterwards only raised to it, never lowered; CUnit slot 24 totals it. Not what the regiment has left - that is +0x5C. saved as `highest`

fields.name: builder
fields.comment: who built it, saved as `builder`, and only where the id half of the tag is set

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `experience`

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment: **The combat modifiers acting on this one ship, wing or brigade** - first here, last at +0x44, count at +0x48, each node holding a 12-byte {id, attack, defence} record exactly like CUnit+0xDC's. Appended to by CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1AC300) from the naval, air, bomber and target slot 19s - 48 call sites - and freed, with all three fields zeroed, by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) at the top of every tick. **This, not CUnit+0xDC, is where air and naval combat modifiers live**, which is why a live watch on a ship's parent CUnit never saw the list fill.

fields.name: combat_modifiers_last
fields.comment: The last node of the CList at +0x40. Written on every push; the head at +0x40 is written only when the count was zero.

fields.name: combat_modifiers_count
fields.comment: How many modifiers are on the list at +0x40. The field to watch for a push, for the same reason as CUnit+0xE4.

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every combat modifier's attack side on this ship, wing or brigade**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier multiplies in `max(attack + 1000, 10)` as a 64-bit product divided by 1000; CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers seeds it back to 1000 each tick. **It multiplies the shot count**: CNavalCombatant::Attack computes `shots = sea_attack (or convoy_attack / sub_attack) * this / 1000` at 0x167B3A, the exact counterpart of CUnit+0xEC x +0xF4 on land.

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment:
The defence-side counterpart of +0x50, written by the same adder and reset to 1000 by the same slot 19. **Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else**, in CCombatant slot 11's per-sub-unit loop, where it is multiplied by +0x50 and divided by 1000. That read sits past a `ret 4` at 0x566452 and is reached only by `je 0x566455` from inside the loop, which is why it was recorded here as having **no reader** until 2026-10-01 (trap 3). The branch is taken when the sub-unit's slot 9 answers false; the true arm uses the division's CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0/+0xF4/+0xF8 instead, so on a ship or wing the two products are used together.

**What it feeds, corrected 2026-10-01 (second correction, see reversing/FINDINGS-combat3.md §3).** This entry twice said the product is a 'loss factor' that carries naval, air and bombing modifiers 'into losses'. It does not. That wording was inherited from a wrong owner: the block was first attributed to CCombatant::ApplyLosses (trap 2 - ApplyLosses ends at 0x5662ED and slot 11 begins at 0x5662F0 with no padding), and when the owner was corrected the meaning was not re-asked. **Slot 11 sums strength.** Its only two invocations in the image are 0x57B083 and 0x57B091 inside CCombat slot 17 (0x17B050), which returns the attacker's share of the two sides' total strength in thousandths; that number's only consumer is 0x17BD70, the `combat_status` window's per-tick refresh, called once from the end of CCombat::Tick and only for a combat the player's own country is in, where it picks an icon state at the 66.0%/33.0% thresholds and formats a percentage.

**So the two sides are not symmetrical.** +0x50 multiplies the shot count in CNavalCombatant::Attack and therefore changes the simulation; +0x54's single reader changes a number on screen. On this reading a defence-side naval, air or bombing combat modifier - including the two defence-only ids - is **cosmetic in this build**. The bound: 'slot 11 has exactly two invocations' is confirmed of the entry-set decode, and 6.7% of non-padding .text lies outside that decode, so it is `likely` as a statement about the whole image. One battle in a running game settles it - see FINDINGS-combat3.md's live checks.

**And the one reader only runs for the player's own battles** (2026-10-02): CCombat::Tick gates the combat_status refresh on CountryIdListContains over the attacker's or defender's CCombatant::countries with the player's id from gameState +0xC34. So in an AI-vs-AI combat this field is never read at all. Player-only, not merely display-only.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02.** A hook on the one reader (CCombatant slot 11) in a 1942 war save recorded 39,414 calls with **zero unexplained return addresses**: 39,222 via CLandCombatant's own forwarder and 96 + 96 from CCombat slot 17's two legs. So nothing outside slot 17 reaches this field in practice, the vcall-thunk route the static sweep could not close never fired, and the demotion stands: for naval, air and bombing the defence side of the combat modifier census is cosmetic in this build. Land is unaffected - CUnit +0xF0 has the AI reader.

fields.name: sub_unit_definition_ptr
fields.comment: this regiment's definition, with its country's tech applied. saved as `type`, by writing the definition's own name

fields.name: strength
fields.comment: what the regiment has left, in the scale of its definition's max_strength; the supply consumption scales by it, CUnit slot 21 averages it. saved as `strength`

fields.name: organisation
fields.comment: organisation x1000, saved as `organisation`

fields.name: home
fields.comment: where it was raised; the save writes that province's id under `home`, and the loader turns the id back into this pointer. **Read live**: a CMapProvince by its own RTTI, and null on a regiment that was never given one

fields.name: name
fields.comment: historical regiment name, saved as `name`

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: **the technology levels this regiment was raised with**, one node per entry of its definition's `technologies`, built by CSubUnit::SetType. The save writes a line per node keyed by the technology's own name - `infantry_activation={5 0.000}` - and the loader looks the key up in the technology database, which is what says these are technologies. **Read live**: every node's first word is a CTechnology; none on a CWing, 9 to 52 on a regiment

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: A CCountryTag on the sub unit itself - the three-character tag here, the id at +0x98 - distinct from `builder` at +0x34. CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers resolves a country out of it for the wing's BM_RADAR_STATION technology scaling (0x16D0A6/0x16D0B0) and passes it to CWeather::AirCombatEffect for BM_WEATHER (0x16D109/0x16D100), in both cases in preference to the parent unit's owner. **Read out of the code only**; whether it is the owner or the controller was not established.

fields.name: sunk_by_type
fields.comment: type half of the `sunk_by` object id

fields.name: sunk_by_id
fields.comment: what sank this ship, saved as `sunk_by`, and only where the pair is not the game's "no object" one. **Read live**: set on 1123 of 3736 ships

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: saved as `is_reserve`; CRegiment::GetMaxStrength scales the definition's max_strength by RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE where it is set. **Read live**: 1184 of 4000 regiments

fields.name: pride
fields.comment: the pride of the fleet, saved as `pride`. **Read live**: 31 of 3736 ships

fields.name: pending_strength_damage
fields.comment: **Strength damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths. CUnit::TakeDamage adds to it per landed shot, CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight reads it to tell whether the unit is already finished, and CSubUnit::SettleDamage subtracts it from `strength` and clears it. **Not clamped** - unlike the organisation half.

fields.name: pending_organisation_damage
fields.comment:
**Organisation damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths, spread evenly over the subunits by CUnit::TakeDamage rather than by size.

**It is damage attempted, not damage dealt.** CSubUnit::SettleDamage clamps it to the organisation the subunit actually has (`cmovg` at 0x1ABAE1) before subtracting, so in a one-sided fight most of a tick's total is thrown away. Anything reporting organisation damage has to count the clamped amount at 0x1ABAE7, not this field.

fields.name: unit_ptr
fields.comment: the CUnit this regiment belongs to; how the per regiment supply and fuel functions reach the unit's order. **Read live**: a CArmy on every regiment

fields.name: current_distance
fields.comment: how far the regiment is from the enemy in its battle, x1000, saved as `current_distance` - and only where the unit's `combats` list has something in it. **Read live**: zero on all 4000 regiments

fields.name: extra_consumption
fields.comment: every point is another 1% of supply and fuel: the consumption functions add it x10 to a potency whose base is 1000. A cached total - the levels in `technologies` added up, which CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies recomputes. **Read live**: it is that sum on all 10254 sub units in a running game

fields.name: historical_model
fields.comment: which historical model it was raised as, saved as `historical_model`; -1 where it is none. **Read live**: -1 on 3940 of 4000

fields.name: contributes_to_unit
fields.comment: **A cached `strength >= 0.100 && organisation >= 1.000`**, recomputed by `CUnit::UpdateHourly` (written at 0x1BA2C6) for the zero-combat-width brigades of a land unit only, and left alone on everything else. When it flips, the unit's definition is rebuilt. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` does not read it - it recomputes the same predicate from +0x5C and +0x60 - and 0x1CD500 asks whether any brigade of a unit satisfies it.

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: The regiment's experience, in thousandths, capped at 0x186A0 (100000 == 100%). GrantCombatExperience (0x1C4200) adds EXP_GAIN_DIV's share to it at 0x1C4671 and clamps at 0x1C467E.

fields.name: technology
fields.comment: which technology this is the regiment's level of

fields.name: level
fields.comment: the level the regiment has of it; the save's first number, and what CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies adds into extra_consumption

fields.name: progress
fields.comment: x1000, the save's second number. **Read live**: zero on land regiments and set on some ships

fields.name: key
fields.comment: unit type key as in the mod files

fields.name: type_index
fields.comment: sub unit type index, used to index per-type combat vectors

fields.name: is_air
fields.comment: an aircraft type; GetBuildTime gives it AIR_BUILD_SPEED (87)

fields.name: is_land
fields.comment: The byte `GetSubUnitDefinitionCombatValue` tests first (0x1A8695): set, the type is scored from soft_attack/hard_attack/piercing_attack/defensiveness/toughness/armor/softness; clear, it falls through to the `is_air` (+0x2C) test and then to the ship arm. It sits between `is_air` (+0x2C) and `is_ship` (+0x2E), which is where a land flag belongs. Named from that one consumer, so **inferred**.

fields.name: is_ship
fields.comment: unknown

fields.name: is_capital
fields.comment: bool, capital ship

fields.name: is_transport
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: is_sub
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: is_cag
fields.comment: The one gap in the bool run +0x2C is_air, +0x2D is_land, +0x2E is_ship, +0x2F is_capital, +0x30 is_transport, +0x31 is_sub, +0x32, +0x33 is_rocket, +0x34 is_tank. 0x1D1220 answers true only when every subunit of a unit has it set, and in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits (0x4CDF89) that predicate is the gate on issuing the carrier_protection order - so the flag marks a carrier air group. Inferred from the position in the run plus that one use, not read out of the loader; CSubUnitDataBase +0x60 is the definition cached under the `cag` key and would be the cheap cross-check, by testing +0x32 on it.

fields.name: is_rocket
fields.comment: a rocket type; GetBuildTime gives it ROCKET_BUILD_SPEED (89), and tests this before is_air, which a rocket also has

fields.name: is_tank
fields.comment: an armour type; GetBuildTime gives it TANK_BUILD_SPEED (90)

fields.name: is_buildable
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: can_be_pride
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: technology_category_ptr
fields.comment: the category whose ability discounts this type's build cost - infantry_brigade points at infantry_practical, carrier at carrier_practical

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: the technologies bearing on this type; end at +0x48. 45 to 56 of them on a loaded definition

fields.name: technologies_end
fields.comment: one past the last technology

fields.name: terrain_adjusters
fields.comment: the terrain modifiers, a vector of CUnitAdjuster **indexed by terrain id**, ending at +0x58. **Read live**: 45 entries on every definition, 28 of them non-zero on an engineer_brigade, and they are the unit file's terrain blocks exactly - 16 is `urban`, 17 `plains`, 18 `woods`, 32 `mountain`

fields.name: terrain_adjusters_end
fields.comment: one past the last terrain adjuster

fields.name: night
fields.comment: the `night` block of the unit file, held by value. **Read live**: 0.7 attack on a commando_brigade, 0.5 on a paratrooper_brigade, -2.0 movement on a naval_corps_hq_brigade, each exactly what that file says

fields.name: fort
fields.comment: the `fort` block. **Read live**: `{0.55, 0.55}` on an armor_brigade, `{0.9, 0.15}` on an engineer_brigade

fields.name: river
fields.comment: the `river` block. **Read live**: `{-0.5, 0.35, -0.75}` on an armor_brigade, `{1.35, 0.1, 0.35}` on an engineer_brigade

fields.name: amphibious
fields.comment: the `amphibious` block. **Read live**: `{-1.1, -1.1}` on an armor_brigade, `{-0.3, -0.5}` on an engineer_brigade

fields.name: other_adjusters
fields.comment: a second vector of CUnitAdjuster, ending at +0xC8 and walked by the same code as the terrain one. **Read live**: empty on every definition in this mod

fields.name: other_adjusters_end
fields.comment: one past the last of them

fields.name: usable_by
fields.comment: A std::vector<Hoi3CString> of country tags, begin here and end at +0xD8, filled from the `usable_by` key (save token 0x826) by CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey. 28 bytes an entry, which is also what fixes Hoi3CString's size: SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy divides the byte length by 28 at 0x1A3BEB. **An empty vector means no restriction** - the test answers true immediately - so only a type that declares `usable_by` is restricted at all.

fields.name: usable_by_end
fields.comment: One past the last entry of the `usable_by` vector at +0xD4.

fields.name: completion_size
fields.comment: the `completion_size` key. **Not aggregated** - `CSubUnitDefinition::Add` skips it, so it is zero on a unit's own definition.

fields.name: repair_cost_multiplier
fields.comment: the `repair_cost_multiplier` key, x1000. **The only field of the 0xE8..0x194 stat block `CSubUnitDefinition::Add` does not touch**, so it is zero on a unit's own definition and a technology effect cannot change it on a sub unit's either. No reader of it off `CUnit +0xC8` was found.

fields.name: supply_consumption
fields.comment: base figure for one sub unit

fields.name: fuel_consumption
fields.comment: base figure for one sub unit

fields.name: radio_strength
fields.comment: **Renamed 2026-10-01 from `sub_unit_amount`**, which was a guess with nothing behind it. Two independent records give `radio_strength`: the key is in `CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey`'s switch (`FINDINGS-definitions.md`), and `FINDINGS-fieldmap.md` places token `0x6D5` `radio_strength` at exactly this offset. It is a plain sum in `CSubUnitDefinition::Add`.

fields.name: amphibious_invasion_speed
fields.comment: the `amphibious_invasion_speed` key. Summed by `Add`, but `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` then **overwrites it with the mean over the brigades that declare a non-zero one** (0x1B6183..0x1B61D6). `CUnit::MovementSpeedModifier` reads it at 0x1C91C4 and adds a define (`CDefines + 0xAC` then +0x278) to it, so a mean is the right shape there.

fields.name: amphibious_invasion_defence
fields.comment: the `amphibious_invasion_defence` key. **A plain sum**, unlike its `_speed` neighbour, so it scales with the number of brigades. Read off a unit's own definition at 0x16991F and at 0x169CB5 (`CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers`).

fields.name: carrier_size
fields.comment: how many carrier air groups the ship carries, x1000 like the rest of the definition. IsCarrier (0x94650) is this being above zero, so a ship with none is not a carrier to the game

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: the `priority` key. Summed by `Add` at 0x1A8230, which is what makes the max test at 0x1A837A - and the `sprite` copy it guards - unreachable.

fields.name: sprite
fields.comment:
unit picture

**Retyped 2026-10-01 from `int`.** It is assigned by `std::string::assign` at `0x1A8399`, and the next recorded field is `+0x1B4` - exactly `0x1C` later, which is the size of the string. The sprite is a name, not an index, so `CSubUnitDefinition`'s sum arithmetic steps over it rather than through it.

fields.name: unit_group
fields.comment: which combined arms group the type is in: a one based index into common/combined_arms.txt's own order, 0 for none

fields.name: minimum_of_type
fields.comment: The `minimum_of_type` key (save token 0x82B), placed here by fieldmap.py from CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey's own store. Named from the key only; no consumer was read, and neither force planner touches it.

fields.name: max_percentage_of_type
fields.comment: The `max_percentage_of_type` key (save token 0x82C), placed here by fieldmap.py. Named from the key only; no consumer was read. Worth chasing, because a per-type cap is exactly the kind of lever the force planners do not themselves provide.

fields.name: available_trigger
fields.comment: The `available_trigger` key (save token 0x82D), whose handler hands this address to a reader rather than storing a value - fieldmap.py reports it as 'read into'. A CTrigger, by the key's name and by the shape of every other `*_trigger` key in the definition files. Not read by either force planner, which gates on `technology_status->unit_available` and `usable_by` instead.

fields.name: extra_amphibious_defence
fields.comment: The `extra_amphibious_defence` key (save token 0x83B), handed to a reader as an address by CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey. Named from the key only.

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like. See CPersistent.hpp

fields.name: attack
fields.comment: saved as `attack`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey

fields.name: defence
fields.comment: saved as `defence`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey

fields.name: movement
fields.comment: saved as `movement`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey

fields.name: attrition
fields.comment: saved as `attrition`, x1000, by the game's own CUnitAdjuster::LoadKey. **Read live**: `urban` on an engineer_brigade is `{0.46, 0.4, -0.35, 1}`, which is that unit file's urban block to the digit

fields.name: id
fields.comment: terrain id

fields.name: name
fields.comment: terrain name; length at +0x38

fields.name: movement_cost
fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `movement_cost` - mountain 1.6, plains 2.0, ocean 1.0, urban 1.25, woods 1.45, all matching `map/terrain.txt`. **Parsed and then never used**: the game does not take it into account, so a unit's speed in a terrain is its own per-terrain modifier on max_speed and nothing else

fields.name: is_water
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: inland_sea
fields.comment: map/terrain.txt's `inland_sea`. Its CTerrain::LoadKey case (save token 0x3C6) hands `this + 0x54` to the bool reader 0x67B410 at 0xADBB2; fieldmap.py reports the key as unplaced because the destination arrives as a register argument. The `is_water` case two cases up does the same thing to +0x48, which is already recorded.

fields.name: temperature
fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `temperature`. **Read live**: -10000 on mountain, which declares `-10`, and zero on the four terrains compared that declare none - one positive sample

fields.name: humidity
fields.comment: terrain.txt's `humidity`, thousandths - the gap the fieldmap already records at +0x60 between `attrition` (+0x5C) and `precipitation` (+0x64). CWeather::Update pulls a province's humidity towards it, and **a positive value is what makes the country's MODIFIER_JUNGLE_EFFECTS apply** to the high-temperature attrition (0xB3F4D) and the high-temperature combat penalty (0xB40E0). In BlackICE the terrains with a positive humidity are jungle (0.8), hills_jungle (1), mountain_jungle (0.9), equator_sea (0.5) and highlands_woods (5); the deserts set -50

fields.name: precipitation
fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `precipitation`. **Read live**: 10000 on mountain, which declares `10`, and zero on the four that declare none

fields.name: is_plains
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD8E9 when the terrain's **name** is the literal string `plains` (0x15C06B4). Not a key in map/terrain.txt - that loader has twelve cases and none of them is this. **The AI's armour and mechanised demand is built on it**: the played-country force planner counts the agent's provinces whose terrain has this byte set and asks for armour and mechanised brigades in that proportion (0x4B62E0..0x4B6344, spent at 0x4B63F0).

fields.name: is_mountain
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD92B when the terrain's name is the literal string `mountain` (0x15C06BC). **The AI's bergsjaeger demand is built on it**: half of brigadeDemand times the share of the agent's provinces whose terrain carries this byte (0x4B63FB..0x4B6445, spent at 0x4B684D).

fields.name: is_urban
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD96A when the terrain's name is the literal string `urban` (0x15C06C8). Nothing in either force planner reads it.

fields.name: is_desert
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD981 when the terrain's name is the literal string `desert` (0x15C06D0), through the string compare 0xC3C0 rather than the inline loop the first three use. Nothing in either force planner reads it.

fields.name: is_arctic
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD998 when the terrain's name is the literal string `arctic` (0x15C06D8). Nothing in either force planner reads it.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: trait name

fields.name: effect_values
fields.comment: what each effect is worth, in thousandths

fields.name: effect_kinds
fields.comment: which of the 31 effects each one is - CTrait::Effect in the header, numbered as CTrait::LoadKey's jump table numbers them

fields.name: effect_types
fields.comment: the terrain each terrain_* effect names, empty for the rest. The stride is 0x1C against a string's 0x18, and **read live** the four spare bytes hold fragments of the parser's buffer - they are padding nothing writes

fields.name: effect_count
fields.comment: how many of the sixteen are used

fields.name: allowed_land
fields.comment: from `allowed_leader`; all three are set outright when the key is absent

fields.name: allowed_sea
fields.comment: from `allowed_leader`

fields.name: allowed_air
fields.comment: from `allowed_leader`

fields.name: count
fields.comment: number of entries

fields.name: traits_begin
fields.comment: trait vector begin; index 0 is a CNullTrait

fields.name: traits_end
fields.comment: trait vector end

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_attack_dirty
fields.comment: The dirty byte for +0x2DC, in the same shape as +0x2D8: `cmp byte ptr [esi+0x2E0], 0` gates the recompute at 0x4D8C92, the helper clears it at 0x4D8FBB, and CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat sets it at 0x1BA31A.

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_attack
fields.comment: The cached half of AICombatEstimateAttackValue (rva 0x4D8C50), written at 0x4D8FC2 with the dirty byte +0x2E0 cleared at 0x4D8FBB and returned unchanged when that byte is zero. A **sum of combat-modifier fractions** - 1.0 means +100% - over the modifiers that depend on the unit alone: combined arms, experience, the leader bonus, dissent, lack of supplies and the difficulty modifier. The stacking penalty, the weather, the river or amphibious crossing penalty, the terrain attack adjuster and the fort penalty are **not** in it, because they depend on the target province and the two counts, and are recomputed on every call. 'Attack' is now from the body. Set dirty with +0x2D8 at the top of CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (rva 0x1BA31A), still the only invalidation found.

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence_dirty
fields.comment: The dirty byte for +0x2D4. Non-zero means the AI's defensive combat-value helper (rva 0x4D8590) recomputes; the helper writes zero here at 0x4D8A81 as it stores the new value. Set to 1, together with +0x2E0, at the top of CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (rva 0x1BA313).

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence
fields.comment: The cached half of AICombatEstimateDefenceValue (rva 0x4D8590), written at 0x4D8A88 with the dirty byte +0x2D8 cleared one instruction earlier and returned unchanged when that byte is zero. It holds a **sum of combat-modifier fractions** - 1.0 means +100% - covering the modifiers that depend on the unit alone: the fort_defence trait, combined arms, experience, the leader bonus, dig-in, the terrain defence adjuster, dissent, lack of supplies, the difficulty modifier and the encirclement penalty. The stacking and envelopment penalties are **not** in it, because they depend on the attackers; the helper subtracts those on every call. 'Defence' is now from the body, not just from which side uses it. CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (slot 31, rva 0x1BA2F0) sets this byte and the attack pair's at 0x1BA313/0x1BA31A and is still the only invalidation found, so how often the value is refreshed is how often slot 31 runs - which that entry records as not established.

fields.name: is_selected
fields.comment: the unit is selected - one byte; +0x5 to +0x7 are other fields

fields.name: type
fields.comment: type

fields.name: id
fields.comment: unit id

fields.name: regiments
fields.comment: the unit's own regiments; a CList<CSubUnit*> base in RTTI

fields.name: regiments_last
fields.comment: the `last` of the `regiments` CList at +0x38.

fields.name: regiments_count
fields.comment: how many brigades, ships or wings the unit holds - the `count` of the CList at +0x38, zeroed with it by CUnit's constructor at 0x1B503C. **`CUnit::RebuildDefinition` divides the synthesised definition's organisation, morale, softness and every adjuster by this number**, so it is what turns those sums into averages. Also the guard on reading the first brigade in `AddRegimentToUnit` and `RemoveRegimentFromUnit`.

fields.name: plan_subunit_difference
fields.comment: Per CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: what the plan wants of that type minus what the unit's OOB actually has. Signed - a negative entry is a surplus. Written wholesale by CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (0x1BD240) and cleared by CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds for an HQ that has no plan.

fields.name: plan_subunit_group_difference
fields.comment: The same differences summed onto one representative subunit type per group (0x1ADF70 does the folding: carrier air, capital ship, transport/submarine, and so on). Zeroed at the top of each pass and accumulated at 0x1BD544.

fields.name: plan_subunit_needed
fields.comment: Per subunit type, the part of the deficit that the group as a whole is still short of - min(difference[i], whatever is left of that group's net difference), taken in index order. This is the list the plan machinery asks for.

fields.name: unknown_flag_95
fields.comment: A byte on the **target** of a naval spotting roll: when set, ShouldStartNavalCombat doubles the computed detection value (0x31ED6). CUnit's constructor zeroes it as part of a merged dword store at 0x1B50D6 and **no writer was found anywhere in the image**, so its meaning is not established. Not to be confused with CCountry +0x95, a different class's field at the same offset, which the supply code reads at 0x1BEDAC to choose between the national pool at CCountry +0x9F8 and the capital province's.

fields.name: home_base_ptr
fields.comment: The object that knows the unit's base province - for an air unit, its airbase: its **slot 0 returns a `CMapProvince*`**, which `COrder::OrderReturnToBase` and `CAirInterceptOrder`'s slots 13 and 14 all compare against `CUnit + 0x130`. `CAir::UpdateDaily` (rva 0x1D0B60) opens by reading it, and every air order treats a null here as 'no mission possible' - `CAirInterceptOrder` slot 14 returns 'order finished' outright. `COrder::IsTargetInRange` also skips the range test when it is null. Its class has not been identified.

fields.name: upgrade_prio
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: upgrade_active
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: reinforcements_active
fields.comment: bool

fields.name: disengage
fields.comment: saved as `disengage`. **Read live**: zero on 696 of 750 units and a small number on the rest

fields.name: order_ptr
fields.comment: the unit's current order

fields.name: CSubUnitDefinitionPtr
fields.comment: sub unit definition

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: a date, saved as `end_date`. **Read live**: the epoch value on most units, so unset

fields.name: combat_cooldown
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `attack_delay`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment: **The combat modifiers acting on this unit, on land only**, a CList: first here, last at +0xE0, count at +0xE4, all three cleared together by CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers (0x1C2FE0). One node per modifier; the node's record holds the id at +0 and the attack and defend values at +4 and +8, which the tooltip prints as `x%/y%` when they differ. 0x164060 turns the id into its BM_* key.

fields.name: combat_modifiers_last
fields.comment: The list's last node - the `last` of the CList at +0xDC.

fields.name: combat_modifiers_count
fields.comment: How many modifiers are on the list. **The one to watch** when looking for what adds to it: the head at +0xDC is only written by a push onto an empty list, while every addition has to touch this.

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's attack side**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1C3040) multiplies each one in as it is added - `product = product * (delta + 1000) / 1000` - and CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds it with 1000, an empty product. The battle tooltip prints `+0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000` as its Attack Modifier (0x32AE39).

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's defend side**, the same shape as +0xEC and filled by the same function. The tooltip prints `+0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000` as its Defend Modifier (0x32AE8A).

fields.name: combat_attack_modifier_b
fields.comment: **The other attack multiplier**, thousandths, written by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (slot 19) once a tick. The game compares it against 0x3E8 and skips the block when equal (0x32ABC6), which is only worth doing for a factor of one.

fields.name: combat_defend_modifier_b
fields.comment: **The other defend multiplier**, thousandths, written by slot 19 beside +0xF4 and compared against 0x3E8 the same way (0x32ACF6).

fields.name: supply_received_percentage
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `supplies`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: fuel_received_percentage
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `fuel`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: current_combat
fields.comment: The combat the unit is in right now, distinct from the combats list at +0x114. Tested by GrantCombatExperience (0x1C433A, and at the call site 0x1BA54B) and cleared by CCombatant::DetachAllUnits when the combat ends (0x165D11).

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: the combats this unit is in. The sub unit writer only writes `current_distance` where this has something in it. **Read live**: 168 of 2000 armies, and what the nodes hold is a CLandCombat

fields.name: combats_count
fields.comment: The count of the CList whose head is the already-recorded +0x114 `combats`; CList is head/tail/count, so +0x118 is the tail. Both AI bodies test it as 'this unit is fighting, leave it alone' - 0x4CE062 and 0x4CE6B7 and 0x4CEEF5 in the air body, 0x4D1A1A in the naval one - and CUnit_IsAtOwnBase tests it on a second object at 0x1CDC74.

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: the owner

fields.name: owner_id
fields.comment: The id half of the `owner` CCountryTag whose letters the record already has at +0x124. Compared directly against CCountry +0xCA8 at 0x4B7629 and used to index CCountry::diplomacy_status_array at 0x4B763B, which is the CCountryTag id-half pattern exactly.

fields.name: leader_ptr
fields.comment: commanding leader

fields.name: current_province_ptr
fields.comment: province the unit is in

fields.name: supplied_from_province_ptr
fields.comment: **CUnit::LoadKey reads it under the key `previous`**, putting a province here, which fits a previous province better than a supply source - and +0x138 and +0x13C are the movement pointers. The BiceLib name is left as it is; which is right has not been settled

fields.name: movement_progress
fields.comment: saved as `movement_progress`, x1000. **Read live**: zero or a part of the way

fields.name: retreat
fields.comment: saved as `retreat`. **Read live**: 11 of 750 units retreating

fields.name: defences_used
fields.comment: **How many shots this unit has already defended against this tick.** CUnit::RollToHit compares it against the slots its defence value bought and increments it on each one spent; past that the unit falls back to CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF. Reset per tick somewhere not yet found.

fields.name: in_game_idler_ptr
fields.comment: the in game idler

fields.name: name
fields.comment: the unit's name

fields.name: arrow_state
fields.comment: saved as `arrow_state`. **Read live**: zero on every unit

fields.name: ai_agent
fields.comment:
**The CAIUnit that commands this unit**, or null. Written by CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63, at 0x4B9F04) and only when both of the agent's flags +0x3D and +0x3E are clear; CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits skips any unit that already has one, and SetUnit calls the previous agent's slot 64 to detach it. CAIUnit::Tick and slots 76, 78, 83, 84 and 86 all read it.

**Retyped 2026-10-01 from `CAIUnit*`, and this one matters.** `CAIInvasion::AddUnit` (slot 63, at `0x8A16D7`) writes a **`CAIInvasion*`** here under the same two-flag guard, so the field holds either of two `CAIAgent` subclasses. Anything that reads it and assumes a `CAIUnit` can get a `CAIInvasion` and then read `+0x64` - the unit pointer on a `CAIUnit` - out of the middle of the invasion's transport list. Check the vftable, or slot 65/66 (`CAIUnit` has `mov al,1` at 65 and `xor al,al` at 66; `CAIInvasion` is the mirror), before treating it as a `CAIUnit`. See `FINDINGS-aitheatre.md`.

fields.name: dig_in_level
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `dig_in`, which agrees with this name

fields.name: subunit_group_present_begin
fields.comment: begin of a vector of one int per entry of `g_CSubUnitDataBase`'s definition vector, ending at +0x1D4. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` zeroes it (0x1B5F80) and then writes 1 at each brigade definition's `unit_group` (+0x1B4) index (0x1B6123); afterwards it walks the vector from index 1 and totals the +0x28 of each marked definition into `base_ca_bonus` (+0x1CC). So this is **which combined arms groups the unit's composition covers**.

fields.name: subunit_group_present_end
fields.comment: one past the last of them.

fields.name: higher_oob_unit_ptr
fields.comment: parent unit in the order of battle

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the units directly below this one

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: The count of the `children` CList at +0x1E4. Read as `> 0` meaning 'this unit has subordinates' by CAIUnit slot 76 (0x4DC026, 0x4DC5E2), slot 84 (0x4C17FE) and others, which is how those passes tell a leaf unit from an HQ. read

fields.name: oob_level
fields.comment: 0 theatre .. 4 division, 5 navy

fields.name: plan
fields.comment: The unit's battle plan, **held by value, not by pointer** - CUnit's constructor builds a CUnitPlan in place here at 0x1B5232 and its destructor destroys it in place at 0x1B5799. 0x90 bytes, so it runs to +0x28B and expeditionary_owner at +0x28C is the next field. Every plan field already recorded on CUnit is this object's offset plus 0x1FC: +0x204 plan_active = plan +0x8, +0x208 plan_stance = +0xC, +0x20C plan_air_stance = +0x10, +0x210 plan_naval_stance = +0x14, +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted = +0x70, +0x27C plan_our_power = +0x80, +0x280 plan_their_power = +0x84. The save writes it under `plan` by calling slot 1 on it, which works because +0x1FC is the embedded object's own vftable pointer.

fields.name: plan_active
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x8. Whether the unit's battle plan is switched on; CUnitPlan::SetActive (0x4DEB10) resets the whole plan when it goes to zero.

fields.name: plan_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel.

fields.name: plan_air_stance
fields.comment:
CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

**Every writer in the image, and who reaches it:**

| writer | value | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute, store at 0x1E7907 | the command's `+0x6C`, skipped when it is 3 | the only store by this displacement; everything below goes through it |
| CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, 0x4DE9EF | 1 | construction, so 1 is every unit's starting value |
| CUnitPlan::SetActive(plan, 0), 0x4DEB78 | 1 | deactivating a plan resets it; reached from CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute and CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit, both interface commands |
| CUnitPlan::LoadKey, 0x4DF93B | whatever the save holds | load |

And the seven places that post that command, by what they pass for air_stance: **2 from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4916AD), for every unit agent, every ProcessAI pass**; 0 from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan (0x4DAD74) when it builds a plan; 3 (leave alone) from CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (0x4C375E) and from the two power-estimate sites 0x4B5152 and 0x4B7E87; and the interface's own control at 0x35244E, which passes the value the player chose (0x351C8E is its naval twin and passes 3 here).

**So the AI drives this field to 2 by itself and the strategic air war is not player-only.** The sentinel-3 AI sites mean the ground-stance machinery never disturbs it.

**Live distribution (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save)**, unchanged and still worth reading with the above: 1 on 1,125 of 1,126 `CAir` formations and on 737 of 738 `CNavy`, and **2 on all 101 of the armies attached to a CAIUnit agent**. The air formations are not the objects phase 4's gate reads; the 101 armies are. And `+0x20C` and `+0x210` holding the identical value on all 4,864 objects read is explained: the AI's one writer sets both to 2 in the same command, and CUnitPlan's constructor and reset set both to 1.

fields.name: plan_naval_stance
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x14, the `naval_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

fields.name: plan_ops_area_count
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x18 is the plan's operations-area province CList; this is its count (first at CUnit +0x214, last +0x218). CAIUnit slot 76 tests it twice on its fallback path, at 0x4DBCDA and 0x4DBEB4, to decide whether a CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand is worth posting. read

fields.name: plan_objectives
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x38 projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC), so this is the `objectives` block of the unit's battle plan: a list of CObjective, each 0x24 bytes, linked through its own +0x18/+0x1C. CAIUnit::Tick copies it into CArmy +0x2EC once a week through CopyObjectiveList (0x4DD350).

fields.name: plan_objectives_count
fields.comment: Count of the plan's objective CList whose head is `plan_objectives` at +0x234 (CUnitPlan +0x38/+0x3C/+0x40). CAIUnit slot 84 compares it against the objective list it has just computed, and against how many of the two lists' provinces match, to decide whether a CSetPlanObjectivesCommand is needed (0x4C1B08-0x4C1B61). CTogglePlanObjectiveCommand::Execute increments it at 0x1E7036. read

fields.name: plan_path_first
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x48 - the plan's `path`, a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8. **This is the list CAIUnit slot 76 walks first**: it follows the drawn path and stops at the last province whose successor the agent may not enter (CCountry::CanOperateIn), which is how the AI turns a drawn arrow into a frontier province to build a front around (0x4DAE8B-0x4DB0C3). read

fields.name: plan_path2_first
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x5C projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC, and 0x1FC + 0x5C = 0x258), so this is the `path2` block of the battle plan: a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8, exactly like plan_path_first at +0x244. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits walks both at 0x4D5DCA and 0x4D5E9A and adds 90.0 to a front province's attack priority for being on either path and 45.0 for merely touching it.

fields.name: plan_subunit_wanted

fields.name: plan_subunit_wanted_end
fields.comment: End of the std::vector<int> whose begin the record already has at +0x26C. 0x4B7D1C/0x4B7D25 takes (+0x270 - +0x26C) and compares it against the subunit database's own count before comparing the vectors element by element; CUnitPlan::SetMinForces replaces the pair.

fields.name: plan_our_power
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x80, the `our_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the owner's strength for it. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel.

fields.name: plan_their_power
fields.comment: CUnitPlan +0x84, the `their_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the opposition's strength. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel.

fields.name: expeditionary_owner
fields.comment: who the unit is on loan from, saved as `expeditionary_owner`. **Read live**: `---` on 740 of 750, and ITA, HUN, SLO and POL on the rest

fields.name: expeditionary_owner_id
fields.comment: The id half of the `expeditionary_owner` CCountryTag whose letters are at +0x28C. CAIUnit slot 79 splits on it at 0x4B335D (non-zero means the unit is on loan and may be returned) and CSendExpeditionCommand::Execute both clears it (0x1E96FC, when it already matches the command's target) and sets it.

fields.name: ai_attack_fitness
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D714A) and read only by its own insertion sort (0x4D716F).** The fitness of this unit as a contributor to an attack on one particular target province: `enemyNeighboursOfItsOwnProvince * 10 - agent->slot89(target, unit, 1) * 10`, plus 100.0 when agent->slot88(unit) exceeds 95.0f, then divided by 10 when the unit answers to another agent and by 5 when UnitHasBlockingOrder accepts it. It is recomputed for every target province of every pass, so a value read out of a live game is only meaningful during that pass.

fields.name: ai_uncovered_enemy_neighbours
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D715A).** The count, as a float, of enemy provinces adjacent to this unit's own province that are garrisoned (or whose owner is reinforcing them) and that nothing of ours is already ordered against. It is the single input to the stay-or-go decision: a unit with a non-zero value, sitting in a province with a supply depot and with no stand-in garrison available, is given a `support_attack` order instead of being marched into the target (0x4D7651, 0x4D7876).

fields.name: ai_held_back
fields.comment: **The AI's hysteresis bit on a division.** Slot 78 sets it (0x4B298B) when the division is pushed onto the held-back vector at CAIUnit +0x15C, and clears it (0x4B2CAC) when the division is recalled from it, at 0x4B2714/0x4B2746/0x4B2798 when the division is disqualified for other reasons, and sets it again at 0x4B3243 when a division is taken back out of the committed vector. While set, the strength bar the division has to clear to be committed rises from the commitment factor to halfway between it and 1.0, and the organisation bar from 0.300 to 0.650 (0x4B2835-0x4B2876); it is also worth +0.2 in the detachment score (0x4B30D4).

fields.name: unknown_2c9
fields.comment: One reader found, CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D6CE0: a non-zero value disqualifies a land unit from being considered as an attacker for the rest of the pass. No writer was looked for. It sits one byte before the recorded +0x2CA ai_pass_scratch, which slot 78 zeroes at the top of every unit iteration and never reads - worth checking whether the two are the same field and the earlier attribution was off by one. Named unknown deliberately.

fields.name: ai_pass_scratch
fields.comment: Zeroed by slot 78 at the top of every unit iteration (0x4B2104) and not read anywhere in slot 78, 79, 0x4B60F0 or 0x4B82F0. Either a flag a later slot consumes or dead.

structs.name: Hoi3CString
structs.comment:
**MSVC's std::basic_string<char>**, under the name BiceLib gives it in HoiDataStructures.hpp. `stringData` is the small-string union - the characters themselves up to fifteen, a pointer to them past that - `length` is `_Mysize`, and `maxLength` is `_Myres`, which starts at 0xF for exactly that reason. Its methods are named as what they are: std::string::assign, appendChars, appendString, fromCString, concat, clear, operator= and operatorPlus.

The name stays `Hoi3CString` rather than becoming `std::string`: it is a real type in BiceLib's own headers, used by ten game classes and read by the DLL at runtime, so the findings and the code that consumes them have to agree. Ghidra also does not take `::` in a structure's name the way it does in a function's, where it means a class namespace.

**0x18 - the three fields, and nothing after them.** This read 0x1C for a while, reasoning from the gap between string fields in about twenty classes. That gap is real, but it is a *stride* rather than a size: those classes leave four bytes after each string, which is what CTrait.hpp means by indexing its Hoi3CString[16] with an explicit 0x1C instead of a sizeof.

What settles it is a string passed **by value**, which measures the size directly. CKillLeaderEffect::GetText and CLoadOOBEffect::GetText both `ret 40` where the sibling shape without the string is 16 - a difference of exactly 24. CBuilding::CBuilding cannot tell the two apart, because 4+24+4+4 and 4+28+4 both reach its ret 36.

fields.name: unused_tail
fields.comment: The fourth dword inside `sizeof`. The size is 0x1C, not the 0x18 of the three fields above, which is why every by-value string argument was four bytes short. **What these four bytes are is not established**: an allocator member of MSVC's _String_val would explain them, but BiceLib/GameClasses/CTrait.hpp read them live across its Hoi3CString[16] and found fragments of the parser's own buffer with nothing writing them, which fits trailing padding at least as well. Do not read it; it is recorded so the size is right.

fields.name: combat_status_billboard
fields.comment:
**CORRECTION - this field is not a GUI window.** It is a live **billboard** object (the 0xB48-byte class with vftable 0x16010D0, constructor rva 0x6B68F0), built from the `combat_status` **billboardType** declared in `interface/mapitems.gfx` inside an `objectTypes = { }` block. CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow (rva 0x17BD70) finds the type in the object-type registry at `CGraphics +0x6BCF0` (rva 0x17BE56) and calls its slot 18, CBillboardType::CreateInstance (rva 0x707340), caching the result here at 0x17BE7F. Slot 24 is `C3dVisibleObject::SetFrame` (rva 0x660460), a `short` at `+0x4E`, and it takes 0, 1 or 2 because the .gfx entry says `noOfFrames = 3`. The percentage text goes into the billboard's own caption `std::string` at `+0xB2C`. **Freed with the combat**, by CCombat::DestroyInterface (rva 0x16DF80), which zeroes this field - so it must be re-read, never cached across a combat ending. See reversing/FINDINGS-gui.md; the old wording called this a GUI window with an unidentified class.

**Renamed from `combat_status_window` 2026-10-02.** The old name was left in place when the comment above was corrected, which is the same mistake that once kept the word 'loss' in CSubUnit +0x54 after the owning function had been corrected - the comment said one thing and the name went on saying another.

fields.name: combat_status_close_billboard
fields.comment:
**CORRECTION - this field is not a GUI element, and its slot 24 does take an argument.** It is a second live billboard of the same class as `+0x2C`, built from the `combat_status_close` billboardType in `interface/mapitems.gfx` (`scale = 1.7` against the other's 2.6, also three frames), cached at 0x17BF02. It gets the **same** frame index as `+0x2C`: slot 24 is `ret 4`, and the `push` that feeds the call at 0x57C29E was hoisted above the call at 0x57C292 by the compiler - the four arms at 0x57C208, 0x57C262, 0x57C26A, 0x57C278 and 0x57C290 each push the value twice. It gets the same SetPosition, UpdateTransform, SetRotation and caption treatment too. Freed beside `+0x2C` in CCombat::DestroyInterface (rva 0x16DF80). See reversing/FINDINGS-gui.md.

**Renamed from `combat_status_close_button` 2026-10-02.** The old name was left in place when the comment above was corrected, which is the same mistake that once kept the word 'loss' in CSubUnit +0x54 after the owning function had been corrected - the comment said one thing and the name went on saying another.

fields.name: modifier_used
fields.comment: **One bool per combat modifier id, at 8 + id** - +0x08 BM_DISSENT (0) through +0x25 BM_SURPRISE_BONUS (0x1D). CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) zeroes exactly these 30 bytes at the top of every tick (three movq, a dword and a word, the same run CCombatant::CCombatant zeroes and which FINDINGS-combat.md records as 'all unnamed'), and every one of the 69 AddCombatModifier call sites writes `this->[8 + id] = 1` immediately after its call. Checked on all 24 distinct ids that have a site, with no exception; the two ids with no site, BM_ARMOR_ADVANTAGE (+0x1B) and BM_SURPRISE_PENALTY (+0x24), are never written. So this is the per-side 'which modifiers were in play this tick' set, and it is almost certainly what the battle UI reads to choose which rows to print.

fields.name: tag_GER
fields.comment: First of 45 CCountryTag slots cached by name, chars here and id at +0x4; the constructor 0x4024D0 zeroes the 45 id halves at +0x4, +0xC, ... +0x164 and nothing else in that range. The names and their order are the .rdata array at 0x15C1DE4 ('GER','ENG','SOV','USA',...), which ends immediately before the string 'countrydatabase.cpp'; CCountryDataBase::AddCountry's 'GER' arm stores here at 0x51622F. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres reads the id half at 0x8A9C65 and uses it to gate two hardcoded theatres (Paris and Warszawa).

fields.name: id
fields.comment: The modifier's own id - its index in the definition vector at 0x1686194 - which is what a CModifier block indexes at id * 8. InitMissionEfficiencyModifiers writes it at 0x583994 from the vector's length taken immediately before the push_back, which is what makes the engine's 32 `*_eff` modifier ids consecutive and dependent on how many modifiers were registered before startup reached that function.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: Which modifier this is. The constructor at rva 0x56D50 takes it in edx and writes it here, and it is what everything that asks about a modifier compares - CBuildingDataBase's role ladder at rva 0xB78AB is five of these in a row, deciding which building is the naval base, the air base, the anti-air, the underground and the industry. Typed as the ModifierId enum so those read as names; the enum is built by reversing/modifierIds.py out of the global initialiser, which is the only place the 107 names exist.

fields.name: persistent_meta
fields.comment: 0x18D

fields.name: values
fields.comment: the values, one entry per ModifierType and indexed by it; CModifier::GetValue reads [this+0x18][type*8]. Typed as a structure of named entries so a read is a field rather than an index. **The index is the definition's registration order, which is CModifier::id only up to 101.** The global initialiser builds 108 definitions in array order but stamps ids that are not in that order at the end: entries 102..107 are LAND_INTEL_BOOST (id 103), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST (id 104), LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (id 102), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST a second time (id 104 again), STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_EFFICIENCY (id 105) and LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED (id 106). So an index below 102 can be read straight off reversing/modifierIds.py, and one at or above 102 has to be read off this structure instead - while a comparison against CModifier +0x24 `id` is the other way round.

fields.name: status
fields.comment: thousandths, saved as `status`: **the share of a full day's work the item received the last time the queue advanced it** - 1000 for a fully funded day, less when the item was only part funded, 0 when it got nothing. Written only by CConstruction::AddProgress (0x837D0) and defaulted to 1000 by each construction class's constructor. **Read live**: 1.0 on most items, 0 on the rest, a handful in between, which is what funding looks like. **Nothing reads it** - two sweeps found no reader outside the loader and the save writer - so a `status` written in an OOB file lasts until the item is next advanced and changes nothing. A CConvoyConstruction does not use this; it keeps its own `status` byte at +0x58.

fields.name: naval_positioning_bonus
fields.comment: Scales a ship's positioning score in CNavalCombatant::PickTarget (0x16764F): `p = p * (1000 + this) / 1000`, where p is the ship definition's `positioning` plus the combatant's accumulated +0x10B4. Thousandths. The name is ours, off the one use.

fields.name: escort_efficiency
fields.comment: The technology effect CConvoy::GetDefence (0xC7C10) applies as (1000 + this) / 1000. Named by elimination from the technology effect keys the image carries - `escort_efficiency` is the only one that could scale escorts - and the function is its only reader found. Inference, not read off a loader.

fields.name: ic_bonus
fields.comment: thousandths. CCountry::UpdateIC adds it to `1000 + countryValues[MODIFIER_GLOBAL_IC]` to get the multiplier on the province base. Read at 0xF0E3B (cached in a local) and applied at 0xF0FBB. The name is inferred from that one use; nothing else about the 0x29C bytes has been read.

fields.name: build_discount_extra

fields.name: oil_conversion_bonus
fields.comment: thousandths. `CCountry::GetOilConversionRate` (0xF17F0) returns a cached global constant plus this, and CCountry::UpdateIC inlines the same read at 0xF11AC to get `1 + 2 x rate` for the energy-to-crude-oil conversion. Name inferred from those two uses.

fields.name: combat_radio_bonus

Thousandths. The name is ours, off the modifier it feeds.

fields.name: research_efficiency
fields.comment: the `research_efficiency` technology effect, thousandths; added to 1000 and the country's MODIFIER_RESEARCH_EFFICIENCY in the research gain (0x532DF0). Named by fieldmap.py 0x537DB0, which places that effect key at +0xA8

fields.name: radar_combat_bonus

fields.name: mission_efficiency
fields.comment:
**The first half of BM_MISSION_EFFICIENCY (0x07)**: indexed by the dense index OrderTypeToMissionIndex (0x184410) makes out of the unit's order's save token, read at 0x16A506 (land), 0x166913 (naval) and 0x16CD3E (air). The second half is the country modifier whose id the runtime-filled table at rva 0x134DA00 gives for the same index. Thousandths.

Read independently by the convoy survey, which adds the indices that matter there: +0xE0 + 9*4 is `convoy_escort` and +0xE0 + 10*4 `convoy_raid`, as MissionIndexToOrderToken (0x184640) numbers them. The two surveys agree on the field and on the name.
