fields.comment: **the country's researched level of each technology**, ints indexed by a technology's index (`CTechnology +0x244`). `CHistoricalModelSet::MakeSubUnit` copies straight out of it into a new regiment's `CSubUnitTechnology::level` (`mov [ecx+4], esi` at `0x183183`), and **read live** it equals the level 6859 of 7445 regiment entries carry, counting only non-zero ones - the rest being regiments raised before the country researched further. `0x63D40` sums it over a unit type's own technologies and hands the total to GetBuildCostIC, which is what it used to be named for

fields.name: progress_by_technology
fields.comment: **how far each technology has got**, indexed by a technology's index (CTechnology +0x244) and **eight bytes an entry, 1.0 = 0x8000 for one level** - the add at 0x532F5B is an add/adc pair. A level is taken when it reaches 1.0

Stored rather than looked up, so an item keeps the factor it was given. **It is saved as `factor`**, which settles that the number travels with the item through a save rather than being recomputed on load. **Read live**: 1000 on 788 items, 800 on 27 and 900 on 8, so the penalty is negative and differs by country

fields.name: practical_factor
fields.comment: Thousandths, and **neither saved nor loaded** - the loader places no key here and the writer writes none. The constructor sets it to 1000 (0x483ED2), slot 14 overwrites it (0x4858A5) with UNIT_UPGRADE_PRACTICAL_MOD scaled by the upgrade's share of the item's cost, and both instant-build paths zero it (0x546192 in CConstructUnitCommand::Execute, 0x547208 in CConstructSingleUnitCommand::Execute). Slot 9 reads it once, at 0x484EBC, to scale the technology-category ability a finished item awards through 0xE02F0 - so **an instantly built unit earns no practical** and an upgrade earns only the define's share of it.

fields.name: type
fields.comment: the token's kind, itself a token id: 1 `=`, 3 `{`, 4 `}`, 0x10 a newline, 0x11 a tab, 0x12 a space, 0x13 the end of input, and on the write side 0xC tok_int, 0xD tok_fixed (`%d.%03d`, a thousandths value), 0xE tok_bool (`yes`/`no`), 0xF tok_word (a name, and a quoted string), 0x14 tok_uint, 0x18F long_float. In a binary save this is what gets written, as two bytes, and tok_newline, tok_tab and 0x12 are dropped instead.

fields.name: text
fields.comment: the token as text, which is what a text save carries

fields.name: depth
fields.comment: how deep in braces the writer is, starting at -1 so the outermost object writes none. CPersistent::Save raises it and lowers it again.

fields.name: stream
fields.comment: the stream written to; its vftable holds write-text at +0x14 and write-bytes at +0x20

fields.name: binary
fields.comment: set for a binary save: token ids go out as two bytes each, and the indenting and newlines are skipped

fields.name: messages_count
fields.comment: How many messages are in the list; cleared when it is freed. Nothing reads it on the way out, which is why a file full of unknown keys is silent.

fields.name: messages_last
fields.comment: Last node of the parse messages list; cleared with the other two when the list is freed.

fields.name: messages_first
fields.comment: First node of the parse messages list; a node is two Hoi3CStrings at +0 and +0x20 with the next pointer at +0x40. CParseContext::FreeMessages is handed this field's address - the destructor passes `this+4` - and frees the chain.

fields.name: error_handler
fields.comment: Null in the ordinary constructor (0x67A460); set from the caller's EDI by the second one (0x67A520), whose six call sites are all in the 0xB3xxxx network module. `ReportParseError` (0x67A960) sets the byte at its `+4`, calls its slot 0 with the parse context and, where that returns true, sets `+5` as well and queues no message. `ParseObjectReference` (0x1EC150) reads the same three and stores nothing when all three are set, so once the handler has taken an error the block is still consumed but its value is dropped. project.json already describes `+4` in ReportParseError's comment; this names the field it hangs off.

fields.name: session_name
fields.comment: The name the context was made with - the third argument of `CParseContext::CParseContext` (0x67A460), which takes it in EDX and assigns it here; the destructor (0x67A630) frees it with the usual `capacity >= 0x10` test, size at `+0x33C` and capacity at `+0x340`. Two constructor call sites pass the literal `UNNAMED_SESSION` (0x1002AF, 0x231700), which is where the name comes from. Exactly two places read it: `CCommand::LoadKey` (0x67BCD0) copies it into the command's own string at `+8` when that is still empty, and `ParseObjectReference` (0x1EC150) copies it into every object reference it fills. Nothing writes it after construction and neither copy is ever saved, so it is a runtime label for which stream a command or a reference came out of. **The `session` reading is inferred** from the default literal; what is checked is that it is a string and who its five users are.

fields.name: tokenizer
fields.comment: the tokenizer; its current CToken is at +0xC and a flag saying one is ready at +0x110

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the key just read. Its type is the token id CPersistent::Load hands slot 4, which is what a class switches on.

fields.name: separator
fields.comment: the `=` between the key and the value

fields.name: value
fields.comment: the value just read, which slot 4 converts out of its text

fields.name: weather_pressure_distance
fields.comment: scratch for CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure (0xB6050): the cost-so-far of the breadth-first walk out from a high pressure zone. Set to 99999 on every province at the start of each propagation and lowered as the walk reaches the province. Nothing outside that function reads it

fields.name: weather_front
fields.comment: the CWeatherFront currently over this province, or 0. CWeatherManager::Tick clears it on every province each hour (0xB5C7C) and then every live front re-stamps itself onto the provinces on its own list (CWeatherFront::Tick, 0xB4657). CWeather::Update reads it and caches it in CWeather+0x28

fields.name: strategic_resource
fields.comment: The strategic resource here, as a **pointer to the entry in the strategic-resource CNameDataBase**, not a number. Null when the province has none. The entry carries its key as an Hoi3CString at +0x30 and answers a bool from virtual slot 14, which is what decides whether the key is written at all.

fields.name: last_convoy_attack
fields.comment: a date, saved as `last_convoy_attack` once it is set

fields.name: out_of_supply_days
fields.comment: saved as `out_of_supply_days`, and only above zero

fields.name: nationalism
fields.comment: saved as `nationalism`, and only when it is not null

fields.name: is_night
fields.comment: a byte: whether it is night here, written once an hour by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B204) from IsNight (0xA7390). Read by CWeather::BaseTemperature for a night temperature drop and by CNavalCombat::Tick (0x17BA27) for the break-off chance. NOTE: CLASSES.md's account of the command-reach maths calls CProvince +0x2C and +0x30 a pair of province coordinates; a byte store into +0x2C and a 1..5 climate id in +0x30 cannot both be true of that, and 0xA7390 takes its x position from CProvinceTemplate+0x64 instead

fields.name: climate
fields.comment: a climate zone in 1..5, filled lazily by ComputeProvinceClimate (0xA81A0) the first time CWeather::BaseTemperature finds it 0, and switched on there to pick the province's base temperature offset. The name is inferred from `climate` being one of default.map's keys and from the field being a small enumeration

fields.name: victory_points
fields.comment: victory points. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: supply_depot_id
fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0), from the province's area or, failing that, from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot on the controller - which answers the supplying country's acting capital. A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1, 2 or 3, worst where infrastructure is lowest: 1 above half infrastructure, 2 over a quarter, 3 at a quarter and under - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. The cost belongs to the province entered and not to the edge, so a route's distance is the sum of its provinces' entry costs, and a neighbour u on the same network is a predecessor of v on a least-cost route exactly when d(u) == d(v) - cost(v). Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: supply_depot_hops
fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed for every province by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one each time CSupply::SpreadFromDepot relaxes a neighbour. CSupply::DailySupplyPass never reads it; the only other reader found is 0xDB3CC.

fields.name: infrastructure
fields.comment:
The same field project.json records on CMapProvince; both structures carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two. It is written by CProvince's own code - zeroed in CProvince::CProvince at 0x494767 and in the province building reset at 0x496680, computed in CProvince::LoadKey at 0x496152, in SetProvinceBuildingLevel at 0x4A3B0A and in CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged at 0x4B8024 - and the full account is on the CMapProvince entry.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02** against 10,642 provinces' `infra` keys in `history/provinces/` - 100.00% agree with `infra * 100`. `CMapProvince +0x5C`'s entry, which used to carry the name `ai_front_value`, is now named `infrastructure` to match this one. See reversing/FINDINGS-infrastructure.md.

fields.name: weather_graphic_changed

Added here because project.json carries the offset on CMapProvince only.

fields.comment: the area the province is in: **read live**, the object's own RTTI says COwnerArea, or CNullOwnerArea where nothing owns it, and 4999 provinces share 50 of them in blocks of neighbouring ids. CCountry::NeedConvoyToTradeWith wants both acting capitals to have one, and asks AreaIsConnectedTo about the two when the capitals are on different continents

fields.comment: The same field as CMapProvince +0x2EC; project.json carries both structures with the same offsets because Ghidra has no inheritance between them.

fields.comment: the combat being fought here, or null. CCombat::AfterLoad puts the combat here when the province has none yet; **read live**, 4 of 4999 provinces had one and every one of them was a CCombat subclass by its own RTTI

fields.comment: buildings[naval_base.index]: the province's naval base, cached at rva 0x969D7 out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x20. Never null once the province has been reset - the array holds one CProvinceBuilding per defined building - so readers test its level at +0x20, not the pointer.

fields.comment: Revolt risk, thousandths, saved as `revolt_risk` and only when positive. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the same in both.

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: the owner. Eight bytes: the tag at +0x32C and **the id at +0x330**, which is what code asking whether a province is owned at all compares against zero - `---` with id 0 is what CCountryDataBase::GetTag hands back where there is none. Two such tests are the sea-hop gate at rva 0x1CEEA4 and the naval-base check at rva 0xA7EE3. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.comment: the controller. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: cores
fields.comment: the head of the list of countries holding a core here; the writer emits one `core` key per node, out of the tag at the node itself

fields.name: port
fields.comment: the province's map port - the link to the sea province beside it - or null where it has none. Built at map load from the land/sea adjacency, not from buildings.txt; the naval base building is the separate thing at +0x300, and the sea hop tests both.

fields.name: regions_first
fields.comment:
Head of the list of regions the province belongs to, nodes with the region at +0 and next at +0x8; count at +0x360. UndeclaredWarCoversProvince (0x4763A0) walks it against an undeclared war's region vector, and the canal tests at 0x4A7EE0/0x4A7F80 compare `count ? *head : 0` against the cached g_mediterranean_region / g_black_sea_region / g_baltic_sea_region pointers - which is also what identifies the member type, since those three are looked up by the names of map/region.txt's first three entries.

**The element class is `CRegion`, named live 2026-10-02.** Reached as `*(*(province + 0x358))`; `classNameForVftable` answers `CRegion` on 8 of 8 provinces tried, so +0x358 is the begin pointer of a `vector<CRegion*>` rather than an inline list. This settles `FINDINGS-opsarea.md`'s open item 1 - `ScoreOpsAreaProvinces` adds +100 per region whose byte at `CRegion +0x6D` is set, and the owning class of that byte was open. `CAreaBorder` had already been eliminated statically and that elimination was right.

fields.name: regions_count
fields.comment: How many regions the province is in; the count of the list at +0x358. Tested for zero at 0x4A7F21, 0x4A7F86, 0x4A7FA1 and 0x4A8013 before the head is dereferenced, which is the usual CList shape here.

fields.name: intel_by_country_ptr
fields.comment: one intel byte per country index (0 unseen, 3 partial, 9 own). CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: intel_country_count
fields.comment: number of entries in the intel array. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: radar_level_applied
fields.comment: The last value of provinceValues[MODIFIER_RADAR_LEVEL] (modifier id 0x30, so +0x180 in the 8-byte-per-entry values array) that RebuildProvinceModifierValues acted on. At 0x4A03EB..0x4A047F it compares the new value against this one and, on a crossing of 1000 (1.0) in either direction, calls 0x4DD250 or 0x4DD370 on the controller country with province->id (+0xD0), then stores the new value here. Nothing else in the image reads it. The name is from the modifier id, which is certain; what 0x4DD250 and 0x4DD370 do was not read.

fields.name: latitude_north
fields.comment: The province's distance north of the equator, normalised to thousandths of half the map height, written once per game entry by ComputeProvinceLatitude (0x963F0) as clamp(template->centre_y - height/2, 0) x 1000 / (height/2). **Zero everywhere south of the equator**, because of the clamp at 0x96412; the abs() at 0x9646D is dead. Two readers: ComputeProvinceClimate (0x9821C, which leaves climate at 3 when it is 250 or less) and CWeather::BaseTemperature (0xB23A1, 0xB23ED, 0xB247E, 0xB24CA, the four latitude thresholds 950/650 on climates 1 and 5). IsNight (0xA73DE) reads it as well, scaling the per-month day-length table at rva 0x130C8B0. Not saved; CProvince::CProvince zeroes it at 0x94B44.

fields.name: underground_owner
fields.comment: who owns the underground here, saved as `underground_owner`: four characters and the id at +0x390, the shape of a CCountryTag

fields.name: underground_action
fields.comment: The underground action here, saved as `underground_action`; **2 is the default and is not written**, which is the only field of the province with a non-zero skip value. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the same in both.

fields.name: tag_18
fields.comment: a tag field. **Read live on 2026-10-02 as the player's own tag** (`IRE`, id 20, byte for byte identical to +0xC30 player) in a single-player game, and recorded in an earlier session as the null tag `---`. **What distinguishes the two is not established** - CGameState::LoadKey handles a `controller` key (token 0x1ED) that CGameState::SaveContents never writes, and its handler at 0x67FDDC is a loop over a vector rather than a store, so it could not be placed. One data point each way, so this is `inferred` and deliberately not given a name. Note +0x90 does hold `---`, so do not confuse the two. See reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 9. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: sunk_ships
fields.comment: the head of the ships that have been sunk, saved as `sunk_ships`, with the tail at +0x24 and the count at +0x28. **Read live**: 1295 CShip in a 1942 game

fields.name: sunk_ships_last
fields.comment: the tail of the sunk_ships list

fields.name: sunk_ships_count
fields.comment: how many ships have been sunk

fields.name: provinces_by_supply_order
fields.comment: every province sorted by supply depot distance, farthest first. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: tag_90
fields.comment: a tag field holding the null tag ---. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.comment: saved as `automate_sliders` by CGameState::SaveContents, and the loader puts it back here

fields.comment: the loader sets it to zero when it has read `ai_seed` and seeded the generator, so it counts what has been drawn since

fields.name: unknown_b3c

fields.name: combat_manager
fields.comment: embedded CCombatManager. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: provinces_begin
fields.comment: province vector begin, indexed by id; id 0 is a placeholder. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.comment: province vector end. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.comment: province vector allocation end. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CGameState's own save and load read it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures

fields.name: allied_objectives
fields.comment: **The allied objectives, indexed by the country the objective is set for**, and the half that is saved. A `std::vector` of 0x10-byte elements (end +0xBA0, capacity +0xBA4) resized to the country count by 0x67E320; element `i` is itself a vector (begin +0, end +4, capacity +8) of 0x14-byte records `{ province id, int* requesters_begin, int* requesters_end, int* requesters_capacity, ? }`. So country `i` has a set of provinces, and each province carries the set of countries that asked `i` to take it. Written only by CGameState_AddAlliedObjective / CGameState_RemoveAlliedObjective / CGameState_ClearAlliedObjectivesForCountry. `CGameState::SaveContents` flattens it at 0x67F97E-0x67FA73 into one int list under the key `allied_objectives` (token 0x758), three ints per (record, requester) pair in the order **province, requester, country**, and the key is skipped when the list is empty - which is why no savegame in this repository carries it.

fields.name: allied_objectives_end
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0xB9C; the element size is 0x10, so the country count is (this - +0xB9C) / 0x10.

fields.name: allied_objectives_capacity
fields.comment: Allocation end of the vector at +0xB9C.

fields.name: allied_objectives_by_requester
fields.comment: **The same allied objectives, inverted: indexed by the country that asked.** Identical shape to +0xB9C - a vector of 0x10-byte per-country elements (end +0xBB0, capacity +0xBB4), each a vector of 0x14-byte `{ province id, vector<int> countries }` records - but here the int vector holds the countries the objective was set *for*. Not saved; CGameState::LoadKey rebuilds it by feeding every saved triple through CGameState_AddAlliedObjective, which writes both halves. **This is the field `CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces` (0x8976E0) walks**: for each candidate ally `Y` it takes `state->allied_objectives_by_requester[Y]` and appends `record->province` to `CEU3AI +0x118` for every record whose int vector contains our own country id, which is worth a flat +100 on that province's AI objective priority.

fields.name: allied_objectives_by_requester_end
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0xBAC; 0x10 bytes an element, one per country id.

fields.name: allied_objectives_by_requester_capacity
fields.comment: Allocation end of the vector at +0xBAC.

Nonzero when this session was loaded from a savegame rather than started from history. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures. Set to 1 only at 0x27CEB9 in CGameState::LoadFromSave, cleared by the two resets and by every construction. See the CCurrentGameState row and reversing/FINDINGS-session.md section 7.

**Confirmed live live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save: reads 1 in a loaded save.** The scenario-start reading was 0 in a freshly started campaign, so both arms of the flag are now observed and the name is no longer resting on the writer list alone.

structs.name: CAIStrategy

fields.name: type_id
fields.comment: The constant 0x18D, written by the constructor at 0x4A33CD. Not read by anything this work looked at.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: tag
fields.comment: **Whose strategy this is** - four tag characters here, the country id at +0xC. The constructor seeds it with 0x2D2D2D, `"---"`, at 0x4A33DA, which is what identifies it. Three independent readers: ApplyCountryAIStrategies does `GetCountry(&acc[+8])`; CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres reads [+8]/[+0xC] and tests the three bytes against 'R','E','B' at 0x8A9B43-0x8A9B56; and the `area_theatre` case passes both halves to CTheatre's constructor, which is how a loaded theatre gets its `country`. FINDINGS-fieldmap.md's "area_theatre ... +0x8 read into" is this, not a store.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: initialized
fields.comment: saved as `initialized`

fields.name: is_static
fields.comment: saved as `static`, which is not a name C++ will take

fields.name: consolidate
fields.comment: saved as `consolidate`

fields.name: conquer_prov
fields.comment: the provinces the AI means to take: a list of sixteen bytes - first, last, count and a spare - with one `conquer_prov` key written per entry

fields.name: defend_prov
fields.comment: the provinces it means to hold: a list of sixteen bytes - first, last, count and a spare - with one `defend_prov` key written per entry

fields.name: threat
fields.comment: who it counts as a threat: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had two

fields.name: threat_bucket_count
fields.comment: The bucket count of the hash the `threat` list at `+0x3C` is indexed by - 0x1FF, which the existing comment on `+0x3C` already describes as part of its twenty-eight bytes. CAIUnit::SetArea uses it as a map: `value = enemyStrategy.threat[ourCountryId]` through `id % this->+0x50` into the bucket array at `+0x54`, matching on the node payload's `+0xC` and taking its `+0x10` (0x4BB70E-0x4BB72A). Those payloads are CCountryValue-shaped records.

fields.name: threat_buckets
fields.comment: The bucket array for the `threat` hash; see `+0x50`.

fields.name: antagonize
fields.comment: who it will antagonise: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had seven

fields.name: antagonize_bucket_count
fields.comment: The bucket count of the hash over the `antagonize` list at `+0x58`, read the same way as `+0x50` at 0x4BB75D-0x4BB775. CAIUnit::SetArea's fallback adds `ourStrategy.antagonize[enemyId]` to `enemyStrategy.threat[ourId]` and takes the whole of a theatre's front when the sum exceeds **100**.

fields.name: antagonize_buckets
fields.comment: The bucket array for the `antagonize` hash; see `+0x6C`.

fields.name: befriend
fields.comment: who it will court: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had seven

fields.name: protect
fields.comment: who it will protect: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had three

fields.name: vassal
fields.comment: who it wants as a subject: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had none

fields.name: military_access
fields.comment: who it wants access through: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had three

fields.name: area_theatres_first
fields.comment: **Head of the `area_theatre` CList of CTheatre\*** (last at +0xE8, count at +0xEC; nodes 0x10 bytes {data, prev, next, byte}). Written by CAIStrategy::LoadKey's `area_theatre` case (token 0x6EF, append at 0x8A46CD-0x8A4725) and by the AI's own builder at 0x8AB8E0/0x8AB8F5/0x8AB9AA and maintenance pass at 0x8ACCA1; read back out under the same key by CAIStrategy::SaveContents (0x8A4D43, key id 0x6EF at 0x8A4D56). **This is the half of the theatre layer a savegame round-trips**, and the list FindTheatreForUnit (0x8ACD00) walks through its `manager[+0xE4]` argument.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: area_theatres_last
fields.comment: Tail of the `area_theatre` CList at +0xE4.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: area_theatres_count
fields.comment: Count of the `area_theatre` CList at +0xE4. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres tests it at 0x8A9BEE to decide whether to build theatres from scratch or only refresh the ones it has.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: max_subunits
fields.comment: how many brigades the AI is aiming for, x1000. **Read live**: 1250 for Germany

fields.name: land_perc
fields.comment: the share of production going to land, x1000; land, air and naval add to one. **Read live**: 837 for Germany

fields.name: air_perc
fields.comment: the share going to air, x1000. **Read live**: 50 for Germany

fields.name: naval_perc
fields.comment: the share going to navy, x1000. **Read live**: 113 for Germany

fields.name: armor_bias
fields.comment: how much of the land share goes to armour, x1000. **Read live**: 330 for Germany

fields.name: building_prov
fields.comment: the provinces it means to build in: a list of sixteen bytes - first, last, count and a spare - with one `building_prov` key written per entry

fields.name: rival
fields.comment: who it treats as a rival: twenty-eight bytes, a list of sixteen and then a count, 0x1FF and a pointer. **Read live**: Germany in a 1942 game had two

structs.comment: **Three per country, measured live (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save): 324 instances against 108 countries, exactly 3.0 each.** What the three are was not established - worth knowing before anything is read into a single instance. A scan of the first 0x1200 of each for a container of live CTheatre or CAIUnit pointers found none, so the theatre/agent association is not held here either; it is by country tag (see CTheatre +0x7C).

fields.name: air
fields.comment: the carrier's air wings, saved as `air` by calling each wing's own Save; the one key CShip adds to CSubUnit's. **Read live**: 79 of 3736 ships have one, and what it holds is a CAir

fields.name: ai_param_b
fields.comment: One of two AI parameters a CSetAIParamCommand replicates: its Execute (0x1E9160) writes this field from the command's +0x68. CAIUnit slot 78 zeroes it directly at 0x4B2498 and then posts the command with 0 in that slot, so the change reaches a multiplayer peer as well as this machine. What it means was not established. read

fields.name: ai_param_a
fields.comment: The other AI parameter: CSetAIParamCommand::Execute (0x1E9160) writes it from the command's +0x64. CAIUnit slot 78 reads it and passes it straight back, so that pass preserves it while clearing +0x2E4. read

fields.name: ai_objectives
fields.comment: A second list of CObjective, `{first, last, count}` at +0x2EC/+0x2F0/+0x2F4. CAIUnit::Tick clears it (0x486A70) and refills it with a deep copy of the unit's plan objectives (CUnit +0x234) through CopyObjectiveList (0x4DD350), and it does so **only for a land unit** - the copy is behind `unit->slot9()`, which is `mov eax,ecx; ret` on CArmy and the shared null stub on CUnit, CNavy and CAir. It is past the end of a CAir (0x2F4 bytes) and of a CNavy (0x2FC), which is the second reason it belongs to CArmy (0x308) rather than to CUnit. The name is from what the copy does; no reader of the list was traced.

fields.name: ai_objectives_last
fields.comment: Tail of the AI's objective list at +0x2EC. Written by CopyObjectiveList, by CAIUnit slot 84's hand-rolled copies (0x4C19C7, 0x4C1AE9) and by slot 76's two reset sites (0x4DBE0E, 0x4DC85E). read

fields.name: ai_objectives_count
fields.comment: Count of the AI's objective list at +0x2EC. CAIUnit slot 84 uses it twice: as a load-balancing penalty (`+ 20.0 * count` when choosing which subordinate gets an objective, 0x4C193B) and as the 'has this subordinate been given anything yet' test. The whole triple is **scratch, not state**: slot 73, slot 76 and slot 84 all refill it from CUnit +0x234 and slot 84 frees it again in the same pass. read

fields.name: army_role
fields.comment: A small enum the AI branches on: slot 78 tests `== 8` three times (0x4B231E, 0x4B2BC2, 0x4B30B9) and `== 3` / `== 4` in its detachment score (0x4B30FA, 0x4B310D, 0x4B315D, 0x4B3170). Value 8 marks an army that is put on the vector at CAIUnit +0x16C, is given +0.9 in the detachment score, and whose owning agent skips it when +0x3F is set; 3 and 4 shift the score by 2 and 1.5 in opposite directions depending on whether the plan stance is 3 or more. What the numbers mean was not established.

fields.name: at_sea
fields.comment: The `at_sea` key (save token 0x3FC), the only field CNavy::LoadKey (0x1CF6A0) places; the handler at 0x1CF6ED writes it through 0x8969F1. Zeroed by CNavy::CNavy at 0x1CEE4B.

fields.name: unknown_2f4
fields.comment: A float, zeroed by CNavy::CNavy with a `movss` at 0x1CEE57. Not saved and not loaded. Meaning not established.

fields.name: combat_cooldown
fields.comment: **A fleet's post-combat cooldown, in slot-31 ticks.** ShouldStartNavalCombat refuses to start a combat while it is above zero (0x31889, via AsNavy()). Set to `8 + (rand() % 8)` at 0x1C80E7 inside 0x1C7E10, whose three callers (0x100F22, 0x165D99, 0x17B01B) put it on the combat-exit path. Decremented by CNavy::CheckOrderAndCombat (slot 31, 0x1CFDD0). Cleared at 0x1BF2C3 inside CUnit::EnterProvince, so entering a new sea zone cancels it. Zeroed by CNavy::CNavy; never saved or loaded. Those four sites are every reference to the offset in the image.

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the technology's key as the files spell it - `art_barrel_ammo`. A sub unit's save keys are technology keys, and its loader looks them up by this

fields.name: name
fields.comment: its name for the player - `Artillery Barrel and Ammunition`

fields.name: allow
fields.comment: the `allow` block: a trigger held by value, which loads itself

fields.name: change
fields.comment: `change`; 388 of 388 agree

fields.name: on_completion
fields.comment: `on_completion`, save token 0x445 - **the practical or theory this technology feeds**. The ability rebuild at 0x41FEFC calls slot 2 on it and reads its +0x60, so it is a category, not a command

fields.name: effects
fields.comment: **what this technology does to each unit type**: a list whose nodes hold the effect at +0 and the next node at +8. Each effect is a whole CSubUnitDefinition holding only the changes, and its `Key` is the unit type it is for. **Read live**: 16044 effects across 1175 technologies in this mod

fields.name: research_bonus_from
fields.comment: `research_bonus_from`, a linked list: [0] the CTechnologyCategory, [4] the weight in thousandths, [0xC] the next node. Walked at 0x533448..0x53348B, each category's ability term times its weight summed into the research bonus

fields.name: start_year
fields.comment: `start_year`; 1173 of 1174 agree across 31 values

fields.name: first_offset
fields.comment: `first_offset`; 801 of 802 agree across 32 values

fields.name: stealable
fields.comment: `stealable`; 569 of 569 agree

fields.name: additional_offset
fields.comment: `additional_offset`; 795 of 795 agree

fields.name: max_level
fields.comment: `max_level`, and **the loader turns 0 into 1** rather than leaving it; 877 of 877 agree

fields.name: difficulty
fields.comment: `difficulty`, save token 0x35F, **a plain integer and not thousandths** - the loader at 0x534B19 uses the same helper `start_year` does. The research cost is `(difficulty x 0.1 + 1) x 125` leadership-days per level before the practical bonus. BlackICE writes 1..14, and three technologies write 0.5, which that helper truncates to 0

fields.name: is_nuclear
fields.comment: `is_nuclear`; 14 declare it and agree, but all 14 say yes, so this rests on the loader

fields.name: build_cost_ic_modifier
fields.comment: read by 0x45140 into sixteen bytes; what they hold has not been read

fields.name: build_cost_mp_modifier
fields.comment: the same, for manpower

fields.name: build_time_modifier
fields.comment: the same, for time

fields.name: activate_unit
fields.comment: `activate_unit`, the vector CTechnology.hpp says has no field of its own: begin here, end at +0x304. ApplyTechnologyEffects walks it at 0x532AEE..0x532B1C and marks each definition's index available in CTechnologyStatus +0x27C

fields.name: activate_unit_end
fields.comment: one past the last of the activate_unit vector

fields.name: activate_building
fields.comment: the building this technology unlocks; the loader also writes this technology onto that building at its +0x10

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like

fields.name: by_unit_type
fields.comment: ints indexed by `CSubUnitDefinition::Index`. **CAirOrder's loader looks an unknown key up as a unit type** and stores the value here at that type's index, so an air order's block can carry a line per unit type. **Read live**: null on 356 of 357 air orders

fields.name: provinces_first
fields.comment: the provinces the mission covers, one `provinces=` line each; nodes of 16 bytes - the CMapProvince, the previous node, the next and a spare

fields.name: provinces_last
fields.comment: the last node of that list

fields.name: provinces_count
fields.comment: how many. **Read live**: zero on 356 of 357 air orders

fields.name: strike_province_ptr
fields.comment: The province the mission is currently striking. `COrder::ShouldBombProvince` (rva 0x18BEF0), the slot-17 body the six bombing missions share, is nothing but `return province == this->+0x68`, so a bombing combat starts in this province and no other. `CAirInterceptOrder` slot 14 sets it to 0 when the target falls out of range, which is what places the field on CAirOrder rather than on COrder.

fields.name: return_to_base
fields.comment: **CNavalOrder's own, not COrder's +0x18**: its loader takes the `return_to_base` key before COrder sees it and stores it here

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: **CNavalOrder's own, not COrder's +0x1C**, for the same reason

fields.name: capital
fields.comment: saved as `capital`

fields.name: sub_unit
fields.comment: saved as `sub_unit`

fields.name: other
fields.comment: saved as `other`

fields.name: combat
fields.comment: saved as `combat`. **Read live**: set on all three CSupportAttackOrder in a running game

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the `id` pair, written after the id. **Read live**: 39

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the faction's id, handed out from the game state's `rebel_id` counter

fields.name: type
fields.comment: what kind of rebels these are, saved as `type` by its key. **Read live**: a CRebelType by its own RTTI; the mod defines six

fields.name: province
fields.comment: where they are; saved as `province` by writing that province's id. **Read live**: a CMapProvince

fields.name: country
fields.comment: **whose country they are rising in**, saved as `country`

fields.name: government
fields.comment: the government they would install, saved as `government`. **Read live**: a CGovernment by its own RTTI; the mod defines eighteen

fields.name: independence
fields.comment: **who they want the province to end up as**, saved as `independence` - `CHI` for the Chinese Nationalists inside Japan

fields.name: name
fields.comment: saved as `name`

fields.name: targets_first
fields.comment: **who they are fighting**, a CCountryTag per entry and one `target=` line each; nodes of 20 bytes - the tag's four characters, its id, the previous node, the next and a spare

fields.name: targets_last
fields.comment: the last of them

fields.name: targets_count
fields.comment: how many. **Read live**: one, `JAP`

fields.name: armies_first
fields.comment: **the armies they have in the field**, an object id per entry and one `army=` block each, nodes of the same 20-byte shape

fields.name: armies_last
fields.comment: the last of them

fields.name: armies_count
fields.comment: how many. **Read live**: none on the faction in the running game, one in the save it came from

fields.name: wants_removal
fields.comment: **Set by the faction's own daily pass (rva 0xB9D60) to ask to be deleted.** RunDailyPass tests it at 0x682E7D and, unless CCurrentGameState +0xC88 is set, unlinks the faction from +0xC7C/+0xC80, frees it and decrements +0xC84. Not saved

fields.name: provinces_head
fields.comment: head of the intrusive list of provinces they claim, saved as one `provinces={ ... }` block of ids. **Not a vector**, though the begin/end shape of +0x94/+0x98 reads like one and this entry used to call it that: the daily faction pass 0x4B9D60 walks it as a linked list - `next = node[+8]`, ending on null (0x4B9E0A) - and its removal path patches both +0x94 and +0x98 as head and tail fixups (0x4B9F5C, 0x4B9F6A). The payload is at node +0x0

fields.name: provinces_tail
fields.comment: tail of that list, not one-past-the-end. See +0x94

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the rebel type's key. **Read live**: six in this mod - disgruntled_rabble, fascist_rebels, nationalist_rebels, organized_partisans, partisans, patriot_rebels

fields.name: spawn_chance
fields.comment: `spawn_chance`, an embedded CMeanTimeToHappen (0x1C bytes, vftable 0x15F5CB8) that the constructor builds in place at 0x4BEF6B and CRebelType::LoadKey fills through its slot 3 at 0x4BFCA8. **It is read**, at 0x4C0670 - `lea eax, [esi+0x28]; call 0x9C4B90` - by ChooseRebelTypeForProvince (0x4C0430) through CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays. This comment previously said nothing was found that reads it; what the earlier scan missed is that the workhorse evaluator is GetDays (13 call sites) and not GetChance (one caller, the daily event pass). **The rebel type whose spawn_chance evaluates largest is the one that spawns**, which is what the mod's own comment in common/rebel_types.txt says. Because the accumulator is multiplicative and the comparison starts at 0 with a strict `>`, a modifier with factor 0.0 whose condition holds vetoes the type outright. See reversing/FINDINGS-revolt.md.

fields.name: movement_evaluation
fields.comment: the `movement_evaluation` factor block, read into this sub-object (token 0x63F)

fields.name: siege_won_trigger
fields.comment: the `siege_won_trigger` block, read into this sub-object (token 0x640)

fields.name: siege_won_effect

fields.name: demands_enforced_effect
fields.comment: the `demands_enforced_effect` block, read into this sub-object (token 0x643)

fields.name: area
fields.comment: the `area` key (token 0x648) - how far the rebels roam. The daily faction pass treats 0 as the value that lets a faction die when its country holds nothing, so 0 is probably `nation`: inference from that one reader

fields.name: ideology
fields.comment: the `ideology` key (token 0x438)

fields.name: unit
fields.comment: the `unit` key (token 0x256) - the CSubUnitDefinition the rebel brigades are built from

fields.name: defection
fields.comment: the `defection` key (token 0x64F)

fields.name: independence
fields.comment: the `independence` key (token 0x651). Non-zero makes FindRebelFactionForProvince (rva 0x286CF0) require the faction's own area to match the province, so there is one faction per area rather than one per nation

fields.name: defect_delay
fields.comment: the `defect_delay` key (token 0x652)

fields.name: resilient
fields.comment: the `resilient` key (token 0x650). Read through CRebelFaction +0x30 by CUnit::RetreatFromCombat, which is a second, independent confirmation of this offset

fields.name: reinforcing
fields.comment: the `reinforcing` key (token 0x688)

fields.name: smart
fields.comment: the `smart` key (token 0x68B)

fields.name: auto_convert
fields.comment: the `auto_convert` key (token 0x59D)

fields.name: is_triggered_only
fields.comment: The `is_triggered_only` key of rebel_types.txt (token 0x61D), which fieldmap.py could not place. Read out of the loader: CRebelType::LoadKey's jump table (0x4BFD9C, byte index table 0x4BFDD8, base `eax - 0x61D` at 0x4BFB72) sends token 0x61D to 0x4BFD7A, which is `add edi, 0x19C; push edi; call 0xA7B410` - the same bool parser the other byte keys use. Its only runtime reader is ChooseRebelTypeForProvince at 0x4C063B, which skips such a type unless its caller asked for triggered-only types; the only caller that does is SpawnPartisansFromUnderground (0x50B920). So a triggered-only rebel type can be drawn by an underground mobilisation and by nothing else.

structs.name: CGovernment

fields.name: duration
fields.comment: `duration`, token 108 - atoi of the value text, unscaled. **Read live**: 18 of 18, and 0 on the ten governments that do not declare it

fields.name: ideologies
fields.comment: **the ideologies this government is acceptable to**, appended by LoadKey a node at a time where the value is `yes`. **Read live**: the names in it are exactly the file's, 18 of 18

fields.name: token
fields.comment: **the government's own key as a save token**, registered at construction by RegisterDynamicToken. **Read live** against the running game's table: 2451 is `nogovernment` and 2452 to 2469 are the eighteen in file order

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the government's key. **Read live**: eighteen in this mod, from absolute_monarchy to socialist_republic

fields.name: index
fields.comment: **which government this is**, the constructor's third argument. **Read live**: 1 to 18 in file order, because index 0 belongs to CNullGovernment

fields.name: valid_for_new_country
fields.comment: `valid_for_new_country`, token 1715. **The constructor defaults it to 1** and BlackICE never sets it, so it is 1 on all eighteen

fields.name: elected_positions
fields.comment: **which government positions an election changes**, a bitset numbered by each CGovernmentPosition's own index - so bit 0 is the null position and is never set. These three are its block vector; twelve bits fit the single 4 byte block. **Read live**: the bits are the file's, 18 of 18

fields.name: elected_position_count
fields.comment: how many bits the set has - **read live** 12 on every government, the size of the position database including its null

fields.name: election
fields.comment: `election`, token 1736, through the shared yes/no parser. **Read live**: 18 of 18, and the constructor defaults it to 0

structs.comment: One form of government from `common/governments.txt`, a CModifier. **Read live**: eighteen in this mod, and all four loaded fields agree with the file on every one.

fields.name: revolutionary_war
fields.comment: saved as `revolutionary_war`, read straight off whether the value token is `yes`

fields.name: action
fields.comment: a game tick, saved as `action` and written as a date. **Read live**: 60815253, which is 1942-05-19, on most of the wars in a 1942 game

fields.name: name
fields.comment: saved as `name`. **Read live**: `War of Italian Aggression`, `2nd War of German Aggression`, `Chinese Civil War`

fields.name: attackers
fields.comment: **one side of the war**, a vector of CCountryTag with one `attacker=` line per entry. **Read live**: `ITA` alone against 28 countries in the War of Italian Aggression

fields.name: attackers_end
fields.comment: one past the last attacker. **Read the end here, not the capacity at +0x34** - the two differ on some wars and reading the capacity hands back stale tags past the end

fields.name: attackers_capacity
