fields.name: defenders
fields.comment: the other side, the same shape, one `defender=` line per entry

fields.name: defenders_end
fields.comment: one past the last defender

fields.name: defenders_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the allocation

fields.name: history
fields.comment: a CWarHistory held by value, saved as `history` by calling its own Load and Save. **Read live**: a CWarHistory by its own RTTI, carrying CPersistent's vftable and token like any other

fields.name: is_limited
fields.comment: saved as `limited`. **Read live**: set on all 19 wars

fields.name: target
fields.comment: saved as `target`. **Read live**: the no-country tag `---` on every war in the game

fields.name: original_attacker
fields.comment: saved as `original_attacker`. **Read live**: `---` on every war

fields.name: original_defender
fields.comment: saved as `original_defender`. **Read live**: `---` on every war

fields.name: casus_belli
fields.comment: **what the goal is**, saved as `casus_belli` by its key; the loader looks the name up and falls back to indexing the list by number. **Read live**: a CCasusBelliType on 259 of 262 goals, a CNullCasusBelliType on one

fields.name: attackers
fields.comment: one side, a vector of CCountryTag. **Read live**: `USA` in the one undeclared war in the game

fields.name: attackers_end
fields.comment: one past the last

fields.name: defenders
fields.comment: the other side. **Read live**: `GER`

fields.name: defenders_end
fields.comment: one past the last

fields.name: regions_begin
fields.comment: Begin of the war's region vector, the third vector on the class beside attackers (+0x8/+0xC) and defenders (+0x18/+0x1C). UndeclaredWarCoversProvince (0x4763A0) takes its length as (+0x2C - +0x28)/4 and looks each member up in a province's +0x358 region list. CUndeclaredWar::LoadKey's `region` key (token 0x414) is where it comes from; fieldmap.py reports that key as unplaced, so this is the placement.

fields.name: regions_end
fields.comment: One past the last region of the vector beginning at +0x28.

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the casus belli's key. **Read live**: `oder_neisse_line`, `china_war_goal`, `occupation_japan`

fields.name: building
fields.comment: which building, saved as `building` by its index into the building database. **Read live**: a CBuilding by its own RTTI on all 89

fields.name: count
fields.comment: saved as `count`. **Read live**: zero on all 89

fields.name: status
fields.comment: **its own `status` key rather than CConstruction's at +0x3C**: the loader takes the key before the base sees it and sets this byte only where the value is `yes`, anything else falling through to the base and being parsed as a number. It decides where the finished convoys go - set, and CConvoyConstruction::Deliver (0x86770) adds them to CCountry +0xB4, `escorts`; clear, and they go to +0xB0, the transports. So `status = yes` in a convoy_construction block means escorts. **Read live**: set on 20 of 68.

fields.name: country
fields.comment:
The country this brigade definition belongs to. SetName writes +0x8 and +0xC as two separate dwords from two separate arguments and hands +0x8 to the tag lookup at 0x402610, which is a CCountryTag - four tag characters then an id, filling exactly the eight bytes to id_type at +0x10.

This read `display_name`, an Hoi3CString, until the wave of 2026-09-24. A string here is 0x1C bytes and would have swallowed +0xC, +0x10, +0x14 and the name at +0x18 - and measuring the gap after every Hoi3CString field in this file gives 0x1C in around twenty places across unrelated classes, with this the only one that gave 0x8. Both the code and the layout said the same thing; nothing had asked either.

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the `id` pair

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the brigade's id, saved as `id`

fields.name: name
fields.comment: saved as `name`. **Read live**: `IV/SG 136`, `IV./StG 410`, `II/KG 42 (leicht)`

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `experience`

fields.name: model
fields.comment: the model numbers, saved as `model={ 6 2 1 1 ... }`; a vector of ints ending at +0x48

fields.name: persistent_meta
fields.comment: 0x18D, the value every CPersistent in this image carries at +0x4 - so CTheatre is one. Read live, identical on all three theatres sampled.

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the `id` pair. **Read live**: 45 on every theatre

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the theatre's id, handed out from the game state's `theatre_id` counter

fields.name: provinces_first
fields.comment: **the provinces in the theatre**, a CList of CMapProvince*, saved as one `provinces={ ... }` block of ids. **Read live**: the ids come back in the save's own order, and the count matches the walk - 20 provinces on the smallest theatre, 569 on the largest

fields.name: provinces_last
fields.comment: the last node of that list

fields.name: provinces_count
fields.comment: how many provinces

fields.name: key_provinces_first
fields.comment: a second CList of CMapProvince*, filled by a key the token table calls `key` through an adder of its own (`0xAFCE0`). **It cannot survive a save**: CTheatre::SaveContents walks this list and the one at +0x30 into a single sorted, deduped `provinces={ ... }` block, which is why no save carries a `key=` line. **Read live**: 3 of 100 theatres hold exactly one province here and it looks like the theatre's seat - Paris on the theatre whose HQ unit is `Paris HQ`, San Francisco on `Pacific High Command`, Washington D.C. on `Eastern Defense Command`. It is not where the HQ unit stands: two of the three differ

fields.name: key_provinces_last
fields.comment: the last node of that list

fields.name: key_provinces_count
fields.comment: how many

fields.name: fronts_first
fields.comment: **the fronts**, a CList of CAreaBorder, one `front=` block each - a province list, a `local_enemy` tag and the `front` and `sea` flags. **Read live**: the nodes hold a CAreaBorder by its own RTTI

fields.name: fronts_last
fields.comment: the last front

fields.name: fronts_count
fields.comment: how many fronts. **Read live**: one to six per theatre, and it matches the walk

fields.name: added_provinces_first
fields.comment: A third province CList (tail +0x64, count +0x68) that CTheatre::AddProvince (0xAF950) appends to alongside the saved list at +0x30. 0x4AFD30 walks it and re-stamps province->+0x380/+0x384 for every member whose controller matches its argument. Whether CTheatre::SaveContents also writes it was not checked, so no claim is made that it is live-only.

fields.name: added_provinces_last
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +0x60; read at 0x4AF995.

fields.name: added_provinces_count
fields.comment: Count of the list at +0x60; incremented at 0x4AF9C1.

fields.name: hot
fields.comment: saved as `hot`. **Read live**: set on 19 of the 100

fields.name: unit_type
fields.comment: type half of the theatre's `unit` id. **Read live**: 41

fields.name: unit_id
fields.comment: the theatre's own unit, saved as `unit`

fields.name: country
fields.comment: whose theatre it is, saved as `country`. **Read live**: ENG has 11, JAP and VIC 6 each

fields.name: owner_id
fields.comment: The id half of the `owner` CCountryTag whose letters are at +0x7C. Read live as **3** on Germany's theatres, matching CCountry's own id for GER, and **0** on the null-tag theatre.

fields.name: areas_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList of COwnerArea* - the regions the theatre spans. `CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed` walks it node by node through `+8` at 0x4B9656 and is the whole of its own body. Distinct from `fronts_first` (+0x50, CAreaBorder) and `provinces_first` (+0x30).

fields.name: areas_last
fields.comment: Tail of the COwnerArea CList whose head the record already has at +0x84, by the first/last/count idiom this class uses at +0x30/+0x34/+0x38, +0x40/+0x44/+0x48, +0x50/+0x54/+0x58 and +0x60/+0x64/+0x68. Not read directly by anything in this file.

fields.name: areas_count
fields.comment: Count of the COwnerArea list at +0x84, by the same idiom. **It is the one number the garrison and marine wants are built on**: the played-country force planner takes min(round(this * shortageFactor * 3), brigadeDemand) as the garrison want (0x4B6489..0x4B64C5) and uses it as a floor on the marine want (0x4B6B35), so a theatre asks for about three garrison brigades per region it spans.

fields.name: type
fields.comment: which mission, looked up by name and saved as `type` by its key. **Read live**: a CNullMission on all 108 in the game, key `no_mission`

fields.name: scope
fields.comment: a CEventScope held by value, saved as `scope` through its own Load and Save. **Read live**: a CEventScope by its own RTTI

fields.name: parent_scope_ptr
fields.comment: set to `this + 0x54` when `parent_scope` is read

fields.name: parent_scope
fields.comment: a second CEventScope held by value, saved as `parent_scope`

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: a game tick, saved as `start_date` and written as a date

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: whose mission it is, saved as `owner`. **Read live**: `---` on all 108, which goes with every one of them being the null mission

fields.name: ideology_group
fields.comment: The CIdeologyGroup that owns this faction. The CFaction constructor (0x5224B0) stores its second argument here, and its only caller is CIdeologyGroup::LoadKey's `faction` case, which passes the group. The two FACTION_*_DIST predicates take a CFaction and dereference this to get the position they measure to.

fields.name: tag
fields.comment: the faction's tag, saved as `tag`. **Read live**: the game holds exactly three - `axis`, `alli` and `comi`

fields.name: icon
fields.comment: saved as `icon`. **Read live**: nothing readable as a string on any of the three, so what it holds has not been settled

fields.name: rule
fields.comment: an object of its own, loaded through its vtable, saved as `rule`

fields.name: modifier
fields.comment: an object of its own, loaded through its vtable, saved as `modifier`

fields.name: neutrality
fields.comment: saved as `neutrality`, x1000. **Read live**: 25.0 for the axis and zero for the other two

fields.name: suseptibility_modifier_index
fields.comment: The index, in a country's modifier-values array, of the modifier named `suseptibility_<this faction's tag>`. CIdeologyGroup::LoadKey builds that string from the literal 'suseptibility_' at 0x15C2690 plus the faction's tag, takes the current length of the global modifier-definition vector (([0x1A86198] - [0x1A86194]) / 4), writes it here at 0x527032 and then registers the modifier - so the index is this faction's entry by construction. CModifier.hpp's entries 140/141/142 are the same three. Five of the seven alignment terms scale themselves by (1 + country.modifier[this]).

fields.name: influence
fields.comment: saved as `influence`. **Read live**: `align_towards_axis`, `align_towards_allies`, `align_towards_comintern` - the decision each faction pulls countries with

structs.name: CMinister

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: the type half of the object id pair - **read live** 38 on all 6257

fields.name: id
fields.comment: **the minister's id**, the number that opens his block and what a country's `head_of_state = 54001` points at. **Read live**: 6257 of 6257, none shared

fields.name: unused_string
fields.comment: **empty on all 6257** - nothing in LoadKey writes it

fields.name: name
fields.comment: read from `name`. **Read live**: `Alfred Rosenberg`, `Thomas Mann`

fields.name: current_type
fields.comment: **the CNullMinisterType on all 6257** in a running 1942 game, so what fills this and its neighbour has not been seen. Not the postings; those are the list at 0x5C

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: a game tick, read from `start_date` - when the minister becomes available

fields.name: death_date
fields.comment: a game tick, read from `death_date`

fields.name: postings
fields.comment: **the posts he can hold and the type he is in each**, appended a pair at a time by LoadKey. **Read live**: exactly the file's on 5746 of 5747

fields.name: ideology
fields.comment: `ideology`, out of the ideology database. **Read live**: 5747 of 5747, ten distinct

fields.name: loyalty
fields.comment: read from `loyalty`, x1000. **Read live**: 1000 or 750

fields.name: picture
fields.comment: his portrait, read from `picture`. **Read live**: `M54001`, `M57` - and it **defaults to `empty_position`**, which is what the five blocks that declare no picture end up with

structs.comment: One person who can hold a government post, declared in `common/countries/<Country>.txt` - **not** in `minister_types.txt`, which declares CMinisterType. **Read live**: 6257 blocks in the mod and 6257 objects.

fields.name: entry
fields.comment: the localisation entry the key found, or the empty one made for a key that was not there

fields.name: replacements_first
fields.comment: a vector of the $VARIABLE$ replacements to apply when this is rendered: **0x20 byte records**, each the variable's name as a string at +0 and the replacement object at +0x1C. ReleaseTextReplacements destroys the objects and DestroyStringsInRange empties the names

fields.name: replacements_last
fields.comment: end of the replacements

fields.name: replacements_end
fields.comment: end of the replacements' storage

fields.name: value0
fields.comment: sixteen bytes from settings + 0x6C, passed to RenderText by value; BiceLib copies them verbatim and what they mean is not established

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8

fields.name: text
fields.comment: **the one string the effect was written with**, which is what the class is for. Both descendants read it and mean different things by it: for CLoadOOBEffect it is the order of battle's path under history/units, for CRemoveBrigadeEffect the brigade to take away, which it puts into REMOVE_BRIGADE

structs.name: CEventScopeSpec
structs.comment: The scope specification a `CContextTrigger` carries - what the script wrote on the left of `= { ... }`, before it is resolved against a scope. Built by `EventScopeSpec_Construct` (rva 0x5C1B30) and embedded at `CContextTrigger +0x40`; 0x40 + 0x110 = 0x150, which is the allocation size, so the spec is the whole of that class's own data. `CEventScope::MakeScope` (rva 0x5C1C10) switches on `token` to decide what the context rebinds. Added by hand because `mergeFindings.py` refuses `struct_fields` for a struct the record does not already hold, which left two signatures taking it as `void*`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md section 3.

fields.name: token
fields.comment: the keyword, as a save token. The ten MakeScope switches on - `owner` 0x1EC, `controller` 0x1ED, `from` 0x34F, `ally` 0x359, `this` 0x377, `capital_scope` 0x3B4, `sea_zone` 0x3E8, `local_enemy` 0x621, `overlord` 0x631 - plus 0xC for a bare number and 0xF for an identifier, neither of which is in the compiled token table because both are the lexer's own classes

fields.name: text
fields.comment: the keyword's text, copied verbatim; the 0x104 bytes from +0 are copied as one block

fields.name: literal_province
fields.comment: `atoi(text)` when the text is a number - the `1234 = { ... }` form, which MakeScope answers with the province directly

fields.name: literal_country_tag
fields.comment: `CCountryDataBase::GetTag(text)`, set only when `token` is 0xF - the `GER = { ... }` form

fields.name: literal_country_id
fields.comment: the id half of the tag at +0x108. **MakeScope tests this against zero before its switch**, so a literal country tag wins over any keyword reading

fields.name: unknown_context
fields.comment: **Was the key not a scope keyword at all.** 0 at construction, set to 1 only by the default arm of CEventScope::MakeScope's token switch (0x5C1F01), and read in exactly one place in the image: CTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5CAE9B, which makes a CContextTrigger for an otherwise unknown trigger key only while this is still 0. So the flag is the whole of how the grammar decides whether something like `owner`, `GER` or `64` is a scope rather than a parse error - and the ten tokens CEventScope::MakeScope knows, plus any country tag and any number, are the complete list of CContextTrigger's keys.

fields.name: resolved
fields.comment: **Did this scope resolve to anything.** 1 at construction (`mov word ptr [eax+0x3c], 1`, which sets this byte and clears +0x3D) and cleared in exactly one place, 0x5C1F34 in CEventScope::MakeScope, when the candidate list for an `ally` or `local_enemy` context came up empty or the key was not a context at all. CContextTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D154D) and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D248D) test it and do nothing when it is 0 - so **an unresolvable scope makes the block false rather than raising anything** - and so do two of the three effect-side callers of MakeScope, at 0x59E2CD and 0x59E33C. CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation and CContextTrigger::GetBlockText do **not** test it, which is a real asymmetry between the tooltip's tally and the answer.

fields.name: this_scope
fields.comment: **The scope the event was raised with - what `this = { ... }` means.** The constructor sets it to `this`, so it is never null and for an unrebound scope points at the scope itself; CEventScope::CopyConstruct copies the pointer verbatim, so every scope a context rebinds **still points at the original**. Two readers: CEventScope::MakeScope's `this` arm (token 0x377) takes the country and province off it, and EventScope_GetCountryTag (rva 0x5C1A40) resolves "which country is this scope about" through it rather than off the scope directly. Not saved.

fields.name: from_province
fields.comment: The **FROM** province, saved and loaded under the key `from_province` (token 0x61C). CEventScope::MakeScope's `from` arm copies it into the new scope's `province`, beside the `from_country` pair.

fields.name: seed
fields.comment: The random seed the scope was built with, saved under the key `seed` (token 0x356) - the only one of the six keys SaveContents writes **unconditionally**. The constructor puts its EDX argument here and in the live state at +8 and +0xC, and at two of the call sites inspected that argument comes straight out of the generator at rva 0x6A2F80. So this is the seed as recorded and +8 is the state as it stands.

fields.name: province
fields.comment: **The province the scope is about**, saved and loaded under the key `province` (token 0x1EE). Everything that resolves a scope indexes a province array with it: CEventScope::MakeScope uses `g_CMap (0x1A8557C) + 0x2200` for the `owner`, `controller`, `sea_zone` and `local_enemy` contexts, and EventScope_GetCountryTag uses `g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) + 0xB8C` to fall back on the province's owner when the scope names no country. Zero means the scope is not about a province; the constructor leaves it so, and every context that sets a country clears it.

fields.name: rebel_faction_id
fields.comment: Second half of the object reference at +0x20 - the id ParseObjectId writes into `pair[1]`.

fields.name: rebel_faction_type
fields.comment: First half of the `{ type = N id = N }` object reference saved under the key `rebel_faction` (token 0x644). CEventScope::LoadKey reads it with **ParseObjectId** (rva 0x67B250) given `scope + 0x20`, which is the same call CReferenceObject::LoadKey makes with `this + 8` and the reason CMinister keeps `id_type` at 0x8 and `id` at 0xC; SaveContents writes the pair back through rva 0x6789F0. So a scope can be about a rebel faction as well as a country and a province, and nothing in the evaluation half read here ever looks at it.

fields.name: from_country_id
fields.comment: Id half of the tag at +0x18, and the field SaveContents guards the `from_country` key on - a zero here means FROM has no country and the key is not written at all.

fields.name: from_country_tag
fields.comment: The letters of the **FROM** country, saved and loaded under the key `from_country` (token 0x61B); the id half is at +0x1C. The constructor sets it to `"---"`. CEventScope::MakeScope's `from` arm (token 0x34F) copies this pair into the new scope's `country`, which is what `FROM = { ... }` resolves to.

fields.name: country_tag
fields.comment: The three letters and a NUL of the `country` CCountryTag whose id half the record already has at +0x14. CEventScope::SaveContents (rva 0x5C1690) writes it as the `country` key by taking `strlen` of this address and making a string of it; CEventScope::LoadKey writes it and +0x14 together from CCountryDataBase::GetTag. The constructor sets it to `0x2D2D2D`, `"---"`.

fields.name: random_state
fields.comment: **The scope's own random number state**, advanced in place. CEventScope's constructor (rva 0x5C1610) sets it from its EDX argument - the same value it puts in `seed` at +0x2C - and CEventScope::MakeScope passes `&scope->+8` to the LCG at rva 0x6A2E90, which reads the state, runs two steps of the MSVC `rand` recurrence (0x343FD / 0x269EC3) and writes the new state back before returning a 30-bit value. That is what picks the country for an `ally = { ... }` or `local_enemy = { ... }` context, so **those two contexts are deterministic given the scope's seed and advance it as a side effect**. The copy constructor copies it, so a rebound scope starts from wherever the parent had got to and advances its own copy.

fields.name: country_id
fields.comment: **the country the scope is about**, and what every effect indexes the country database with. The Lua API declares `_Country` at +0x10 as a `CCountryTag&` - that is its getter's return type, not the layout: the tag sits there **by value**, three letters at +0x10 and this id at +0x14, which is why CCountryTag::GetCountry is passed `scope + 0x10`

fields.name: days_in_month
fields.comment: The one field the two CEventScope builders disagree about. RebuildCountryEventCandidates sets it to the current month's length, recomputed at 0x9C0273-0x9C02E4 from state+0xBDC with the same 0x29C55C0 epoch and 365.0 constant (0x160A550) RunHourlyTick uses and then indexed into MonthLengthTable (0x1713294); RunDailyEventPass leaves it zero (0x9C0AAD). CMeanTimeToHappen::GetChance never reads the scope, only forwards it, so this can only matter to a trigger. **The name is inference from how the value is derived, not from a use.** CEventScope is 0x48 bytes, vftable 0x15B8AEC, base CPersistent; +0x10 and +0x18 are two CCountryTags, both 0x2D2D2D ("---") at construction and only +0x10 ever filled in with the country being scoped.

fields.name: combat
fields.comment: which kind of combat earns it, as the token itself

fields.name: hours_required
fields.comment: hours of such combat a leader needs

fields.name: trait
fields.comment: what is earned, resolved as the file is read

fields.name: trigger
fields.comment: held by value; it loads itself from the `trigger` block

fields.name: has_trigger
fields.comment: set when a `trigger` block was read at all

fields.name: hours_by_trait
fields.comment: a std::map of trait to hours - a red-black tree, the value at each node's +0x10

fields.name: leader
fields.comment: The leader who owns this tracker, and the only back-pointer it has. Set once by CTraitGainTracker::Init (0x1741D2, which refuses to run twice on the strength of it) and read by Update to get the leader's type, trait list and the AddTrait target (0x174464, 0x1745D1).

fields.name: duration
fields.comment: saved as `duration`

fields.name: current
fields.comment: saved as `current`

structs.name: CLeaderHistory

fields.name: leader
fields.comment: **The owning leader, and CLeaderHistory's only field of its own.** CLeader::CLeader writes `[leader + 0xA4] = leader` at 0x17F665 - 0x84 + 0x20 - and CLeaderHistory::LoadEntry reads it out of `this->+0x20` to put on every entry it builds. CProvinceHistory and CCountryHistory keep their owner at the same +0x20 (CProvinceHistory::CProvinceHistory, 0x1FCBFE, stores its one argument there) and read it back through the non-virtual getter at 0x1EC730.

fields.name: unknown_1c
fields.comment: **CHistoryContainer's last dword, and nothing reads it.** Written zero by CHistoryContainer::CHistoryContainer (0x1F45D1) and by CLeader::CLeader's inlined copy (leader+0xA0, 0x17F655), and that is every reference found. It is what makes the container 0x20 bytes, so it matters even unread.

fields.name: date
fields.comment: **CHistoryContainer's, at +0x8 on all five subclasses.** The container's own current date - what ExecuteHistory has advanced it to - in the engine's hours. Defaulted to g_NullDate (rva 0x130C2B8) by CHistoryContainer::CHistoryContainer (0x1F45BA), put back there by Reset (0x1F4768), and the only thing SetDate (0x1F4780) changes in practice. Reached as [leader + 0x8C], [province + 0xE0] and [country + 0xCD4].

fields.name: entries
fields.comment: The leader's dated history entries. Each node's data answers a save token from vslot 6 and carries its date at +8. RunCountryDailyPass walks this list looking for the token 0x10A (rank) to decide the day the leader becomes active (0xDAA80..0xDAAFE). Read as [leader + 0x90].

structs.comment: A CHistoryContainer subobject held by value at CLeader +0x84; 0x24 bytes, its own data being just the owning CLeader* at +0x20. The container's layout is in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-history.md section 1. **A field was removed from this struct on 2026-10-03**: `+0x40 trait_gain` was a misattribution - those four bytes are CLeader +0xC4, which the record already holds as `trait_gain_tracker`, and the size settles it because CLeader::CLeader builds `picture` at CLeader +0xA8 = CLeaderHistory +0x24.

fields.name: country
fields.comment: held by value, and **the null tag `---` on all 20000 sampled** - a model does not know its country. The real tag is on the CHistoricalModelSet that holds it

fields.name: definition
fields.comment: the unit type this is a model of

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: **what this model was built with**: a vector of the same 12 byte {technology, level, progress} entries a regiment carries, which is why PickBestModel can compare the two directly. **Read live**: non-empty on 1677 of 4000 models, always a whole number of entries, and in this mod every entry's level is the model's own index

fields.name: index
fields.comment: which model this is, and what `historical_model = N` in an order of battle picks by

structs.name: CHistoricalModelSet

fields.name: models
fields.comment: a vector of the type's models, in index order

fields.name: unknown_c
fields.comment: zero on 878 of 1296 sets and unrelated bytes on the rest, so nothing appears to read it

fields.name: definition
fields.comment: the unit type, and the same pointer every model in the vector carries at its own `definition`. **Read live**: 25 of 25, and its `type_index` is the slot this set sits in

fields.name: country
fields.comment: held by value; **read live** the id half is the owning country's index on 1296 of 1296, and the letters are the country's - GER, SWE. This is the tag the model's own field never has

structs.comment: **One unit type's models for one country** - the object a CCountry's `historical_models` array holds, and what CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel takes in ecx. **Read live**: 108 countries x 1643 unit types, each with exactly `HISTORICAL_MODEL_MAX` models, which accounts for every CHistoricalModel in the process. The name is BiceLib's.

structs.name: CNameDataBase

fields.name: count
fields.comment: how many entries - **read live** 11 ideologies and 12 positions

fields.name: by_name
fields.comment: what GetByName searches; its shape has not been read

fields.name: first
fields.comment: the entries in index order, entry 0 being the null object

structs.comment: **A database of named, file-loaded objects, kept in index order with a null at 0.** No vftable - the first word is the count - and one shared by-name lookup. The ideologies and the government positions are both one of these; the pattern is worth recognising, because an index from one of them is 1-based as far as the mod's files are concerned. The name is BiceLib's.

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the key, the first field after the CModifier base - **read live** `head_of_state` and `national_socialist` among them

fields.name: index
fields.comment: **its index in its database**, and the bit number CGovernment's `elected_positions` uses. **Read live**: 0 to 11 and 0 to 10, 0 being the null object

fields.name: key_token
fields.comment: The cabinet post's own name as a save token - the key CCountry::SaveContents writes each minister under, loaded at 0x4D1052-0x4D1056. It is the token form of the `key` string already recorded at +0x30 (`head_of_state` and the rest).

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the key, the first field after the CModifier base - **read live** `head_of_state` and `national_socialist` among them

fields.name: index
fields.comment: **its index in its database**, and the bit number CGovernment's `elected_positions` uses. **Read live**: 0 to 11 and 0 to 10, 0 being the null object

structs.name: CMinisterPosting

fields.name: position
fields.comment: which post - the key of the line in the file

fields.name: type
fields.comment: what kind of minister he is in it - the value

structs.comment: **One post a minister can hold**: the position and the type he is in it, side by side. LoadKey builds these straight into the list nodes, so a node is 8 bytes of posting and then its links. The name is BiceLib's.

structs.name: CMinisterType
structs.comment: One of the 106 kinds of minister in `common/minister_types.txt`, a CModifier - and its key and index sit where every CModifier-derived named type keeps them.

structs.name: CReferenceObject
structs.comment: A CPersistent that other objects hold pointers to - CMinister and CRebelFaction are two. **Its own fields have not been read**; it is here so that the classes deriving from it lay out, and what CMinister keeps at 0x8 and 0xC is recorded on CMinister until something says the base owns it.

structs.name: LogRecord

fields.name: vbptr
fields.comment: The virtual base pointer, 0x15FCE98, whose vbtable reads {0, 0x78} - which is what puts the basic_ios base at +0x78 rather than the +0x50 a plain ostringstream keeps it at.

fields.name: sink
fields.comment: The LogSink this line goes to; FlushAndDestruct calls slot 1 of its vftable, which is the recorded LogSink::Write. Typed void* because LogSink has no layout here yet.

fields.name: file
fields.comment: The source file the line was logged from. An Hoi3CString, not a `const char*`: the constructor assignStrings into it, and every call site runs its literal through std::string::fromCString first.

fields.name: line
fields.comment: The source line, read at [ios-8] for the sink call.

fields.name: channel
fields.comment: Which log channel the line belongs to, read at [ios-4].

structs.comment:
The temporary every log line in the game is built into: `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl`. It is a std::basic_ostringstream<char> with four fields of its own added, which is why its basic_ios virtual base sits at +0x78 instead of +0x50.

**Two gaps, deliberately.** +0x04..+0x4F is the std::basic_stringbuf (0x4C bytes, vftable 0x15F2B34, with _Seekhigh at +0x40 and _Mystate at +0x44), and +0x78 is the std::basic_ios virtual base (0x44 bytes, vftable 0x15FCE94). Neither type is modelled here, and a byte blob would claim a layout nobody has read, so they are left undefined and described instead.

The size of 0xBC is **inferred**: basic_ios' last written member is _Fillch at +0x40, giving at least 0x41 and 0x44 by alignment. Every LogRecord in the image is a stack local, so no allocation size settles it.

structs.name: CUnitPlan
structs.comment:
A unit's battle plan, held **by value** at CUnit +0x1FC - CUnit's constructor calls this class's constructor on `this + 0x1FC` and its destructor mirrors it, and 0x90 is exactly the gap to expeditionary_owner at +0x28C.

The layout was read three ways that agree: the constructor field by field, CUnitPlan::LoadKey's sixteen cases, and CUnitPlan::SaveContents writing the same token for the same offset. Three offsets are left out because nothing identified them - +0x58, +0x6C, and +0x7C, which is the one field the constructor never initialises.

fields.name: active
fields.comment: whether the plan is switched on.

fields.name: allow_hq_reorg
fields.comment: whether the plan may reorganise the headquarters under it.

fields.name: stance
fields.comment: the land stance, 0..4.

fields.name: air_stance
fields.comment:
The air stance, 0..2, and the same field as `CUnit +0x20C plan_air_stance` (the plan is embedded at CUnit +0x1FC).

**1 is both the constructed and the reset value**: the constructor writes 1 at 0x4DE9EF and CUnitPlan::SetActive's deactivate arm writes 1 again at 0x4DEB78. 0 comes only from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan's command (0x4DAD74) and switches the air body's phase 4 off entirely; 2 comes from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances's command (0x4916AD) and from the interface, and is what phase 4's strategic and naval arm requires. 3 is not a value of this field at all - it is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "leave this one alone" sentinel, tested at 0x1E78C4.

fields.name: naval_stance
fields.comment: the naval stance, 0..2.

fields.name: ops_area
fields.comment: the provinces the plan operates over.

fields.name: fallback_line
fields.comment: the provinces of the fallback line.

fields.name: objectives
fields.comment: the plan's objective provinces.

fields.name: path
fields.comment: the planned route.

fields.name: path2
fields.comment: a second planned route.

fields.name: min
fields.comment: how many regiments of each subunit type the plan wants, indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index and sized to the subunit database. The same vector CUnit reaches as plan_subunit_wanted at +0x26C. **It is twelve bytes, +0x70..+0x7B** - _Myfirst, _Mylast, _Myend, with no stored allocator - so **+0x7C is a separate dword**, and it is the one field CUnitPlan's constructor never initialises.

fields.name: our_power
fields.comment: the plan's estimate of our strength.

fields.name: their_power
fields.comment: its estimate of theirs.

fields.name: embark
fields.comment: the province to embark at.

fields.name: debark
fields.comment: the province to debark at.

+0x2C..+0xAC holds 33 cached role definitions the constructor does not initialise, and which nothing has identified; they are left out rather than guessed at.

fields.name: all
fields.comment: a list of everything the database holds.

fields.name: by_name
fields.comment: a 0x1FF-bucket hash map from a definition's key to the definition.

fields.name: definitions_begin
fields.comment: the start of the definition array; GetSubUnitByIndex indexes it.

fields.name: definitions_end
fields.comment: one past the end. The count is (this - definitions_begin) / 4, which is what GetNumberOfSubUnits answers and what sizes every array indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index.

fields.name: unused_list
fields.comment: a second list, zeroed by the constructor and not seen in use.

structs.name: CEU3BitmapFontKerning
structs.comment: One kerning pair of a glyph: how much the pen moves by when this glyph is followed by `second`. Nearly always -1 in the fonts shipped; garamond_16 has 199 of them across all glyphs.

fields.name: second
fields.comment: the character code that has to follow for this pair to apply

fields.name: amount
fields.comment: pixels added to the advance, almost always negative

structs.name: CEU3BitmapFontGlyph
structs.comment: One character of a bitmap font, as CEU3BitmapFont::LoadGlyphs builds it from a `char` line of the .fnt. The first seven fields are that line's numbers in file order. Fixed size whether or not the glyph has any kerning: (0x81C - 0x1C) / 8 is 256, so the pair array is sized for every possible partner.

fields.name: x
fields.comment: left edge in the font texture

fields.name: y
fields.comment: top edge in the font texture

fields.name: width
fields.comment: how wide the glyph is in the texture, which is not what the pen moves by

fields.name: height
fields.comment: how tall it is; forced to 0 for the space (id 0x20) at 0x6FA3BD whatever the file says, and GetStringWidth reads a zero height as a glyph that draws no ink

fields.name: xoffset
fields.comment: where the glyph is drawn relative to the pen

fields.name: yoffset
fields.comment: the same vertically

fields.name: xadvance
fields.comment: **what the pen moves by** - the number that decides how wide text draws. The .fnt's value reaches here unchanged, since the parse is positional and nothing scales it

fields.name: kerning
fields.comment: pairs in the order the .fnt listed them, only the first kerning_count of them meaning anything

fields.name: kerning_count
fields.comment: how many of the pairs are filled; zeroed as the glyph is made and incremented by each kerning line naming this glyph first

structs.name: CEU3BitmapFont
structs.comment: A bitmap font, one per `bitmapfont` block in interface/core.gfx. Only the two fields the text measuring needed are known.

fields.name: font_name
fields.comment: the `fontName` key, which is the stem of both gfx/fonts/<name>.tga and the .fnt beside it. CEU3BitmapFont::LoadKey takes the key straight onto this+0x78 and both loaders read it from there; 0x78 + 0x18 leaves it ending at 0x90, four bytes short of the glyph table

fields.name: glyphs
fields.comment: one pointer per character code, null where the font has no such glyph. Indexed by the raw byte in GetStringWidth, so 256 entries exactly - and 0x94 + 256 * 4 is 0x494, which is the next field LoadGlyphs writes (0x6FA26D), so the length is measured rather than assumed

structs.name: MapCamera
structs.comment:
Where the map is looked at from, held by value inside CInGameIdler at +0x1938 and reached through CInGameIdler::GetMapCamera. Named for what it holds: it has no vftable, so there is nothing in the RTTI export to name it after.

Only the fields the scrolling touches are known; the zoom and rotation it also carries have not been worked out.

fields.name: edge_left
fields.comment: the screen x the map starts at. The mouse being within six pixels of it scrolls the map west

fields.name: edge_top
fields.comment: the screen y the map starts at; within six pixels scrolls north

fields.name: edge_right
fields.comment: the screen x the map ends at; within six pixels scrolls east

fields.name: edge_bottom
fields.comment: the screen y the map ends at; within six pixels scrolls south

fields.name: x
fields.comment: where the camera is looking, in map coordinates. This is what every kind of scrolling adds to and what the clamp bounds

fields.name: y
fields.comment: the same, north to south

fields.name: x_settled
fields.comment: a second copy of `x`. CentreOnProvince and the camera's own setup both write the position and then copy it into this pair, which is what makes those moves immediate - so this is the value the camera has rather than the one it is heading for. Which of the two the renderer reads has not been checked

fields.name: y_settled
fields.comment: the same, north to south

structs.name: CMessageVariable
structs.comment:
**One `$KEY$` a message's text can use**, and the node of the list that holds them. The game builds these inline at every message it raises rather than through a function, so BiceLib reproduces the steps: take 0x44 bytes from the game's allocator, make both strings empty, assign them, then link.

The list is the usual `{first, last, count}`. The gaps at +0x18 and +0x34 are what the compiler left and are zeroed rather than guessed at.

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the name without its dollars - `UNIT` fills `$UNIT$`

fields.name: value
fields.comment: what it is replaced with

fields.name: previous
fields.comment: the node before this one

fields.name: next
fields.comment: the node after it, null at the end

fields.name: factor
fields.comment: **Stored in thousandths.** CMeanTimeToHappen::GetChance divides it by the double 1000.0 at 0x160A300 (0x9C4AF1) before multiplying it into the days figure, so `factor = 0.5` in script is 500 in memory. The modifier is applied only when the modifier's condition object slot 6 accepts the scope (0x9C4AD4).

fields.name: index
fields.comment: The group's index into CAlignment's per-group weight vector at +0x18 - CAlignment::GetValueForGroup is literally `values[group->+0x50]`, and the constructor sizes that vector to the number of groups.

fields.name: faction
fields.comment: Read from the key `faction`: CIdeologyGroup::LoadKey allocates 0xD8 bytes, runs the CFaction constructor with this group as the second argument, loads the block through the faction's slot 3, and stores the result here. CIdeologyGroup::GetFaction (0x527140) returns it, or the null-faction singleton when it is null.

fields.name: position_x
fields.comment: The group's x on the political compass, thousandths. CIdeologyGroup::LoadKey's `position` key (token 0x4B) is ParsePoint(this + 0x58) at 0x5270E4. Every alignment distance in the game is measured to this pair.

fields.name: position_y
fields.comment: The group's y on the political compass, thousandths; the second half of the `position` key.

fields.name: position_x
fields.comment: The country's x on the political compass, thousandths. CAlignment::LoadKey reads the `position` key here through ParsePoint; the constructor zeroes it and then calls ClampMove with a zero delta, which places it inside the ideology groups' bounding box.

fields.name: position_y
fields.comment: The country's y on the political compass, thousandths.

fields.name: group_weights
fields.comment: The first of a vector of ints, ending at +0x1C with capacity at +0x20 - **one weight per ideology group**, indexed by CIdeologyGroup+0x50. The constructor sizes it to the group count and the destructor frees it. ComputeDrift fills every entry with the seven-term sum and then uses the entries as the magnitudes of unit vectors toward each group.

fields.name: bounds
fields.comment: The first of eight dwords (+0x28..+0x44) holding the bounding box of all ideology-group positions: minimum x and y at +0x28/+0x2C, extents at +0x30/+0x34, and two derived ratios at +0x38..+0x44. Zeroed by the constructor, rebuilt by 0x4C46C0 from the group manager's vector, and read by ClampMove to keep a drift inside the compass.

fields.name: next_offer_allowed
fields.comment: A tick (hours), set to the proposal's `date + 0xA8` - **exactly seven days** - by CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed (0xA4A550), whose one caller is CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute on the PROPOSE path, for every kind of action except `callaction` (0x309). **Likely a per-pair cooldown on diplomatic offers, but no reader was found**, and the setter's own comparison against `tick + 0xA8` is dead - both arms store the same value - so the feature may be partly gutted. The name is read off the one writer's arithmetic, not off a consumer.

fields.name: occupation_policy
fields.comment: The COccupationPolicy the array's owner applies to provinces it has taken from the other country, or null. Named from the loader: CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey (rva 0x648190) stores the key occupation_policy, token 0x57C, here. RTTI says **COccupationPolicy derives from CModifier**, and RebuildProvinceModifierValues (rva 0x9F3E0, at 0x49FBE2) adds its whole values array (+0x18) into the occupied province's modifier values - which is the entire occupation penalty to IC, resources, manpower, leadership, partisan support and revolt risk. Skipped when owner and controller agree and when the controller is REB.

fields.name: war
fields.comment: Non-null while the pair are at war. **Inferred, not proven**: CCountry::IsEnemy (rva 0x2F1B0) answers true on nothing but this being non-null plus the two unconditional REB cases, and the daily province pass inlines the same three tests at 0x49EE35 to decide whether revolt risk accumulates. No writer of the field was found.

fields.name: undeclared_war
fields.comment: The pair's undeclared war, or null - the field that sits between +0x20 `war` and +0x28 `nap`. Read in exactly one shape: CCountry::IsEnemy (0x42F25D) and the dozen places that inline it take it, give up when it is null, and otherwise hand it to UndeclaredWarCoversProvince (0x4763A0) together with the province, which walks its +0x28/+0x2C region vector against the province's own region list. CUndeclaredWar::LoadKey (0x475A60) has a `region` key (token 0x414), which is what makes the vector the war's regions. Likely rather than confirmed because nothing seen here writes the field.

fields.name: nap
fields.comment: The non-aggression pact for the pair, or null. A CRelation subclass: +0x10/+0x14 the `second` party, +0x18 `start_date`, plus +0x24, the border force balance stored as first:second. CCountry::CanBreakNap reads all of those.

fields.name: influence_running
fields.comment: Non-zero while a diplomatic influence is running between the pair. Two agreeing readers: CCountry::PayDailyInfluenceUpkeep charges INFLUENCE_UPKEEP once a day for each country whose status toward the payer has it set, and CCountry::GetInfluencedCountryCount counts the same thing. What the two directions mean is not settled - both readers index other->+0xE28[us].

fields.name: relation
fields.comment: The pair's relation, thousandths. Inferred, not proven: the alignment relation term averages this field over a faction's members and scales it by RELATION_WEIGHT, which leaves little else it could be, but no loader key and no second reader were checked.

fields.name: war_seen_tick
fields.comment: CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies writes the current tick (`CGameState +0xBDC`) here at 0x4E6C32 for every pair whose `+0x20` (war) is non-null, and only for those. Because the function runs on every diplomatic action and once an hour, the value is refreshed for as long as the war lasts rather than stamped at its start, so it is the last tick at which the pair were seen to be at war and **not** a war-start date. No other writer or reader was looked for, which is why this is `inferred`.

fields.name: co_belligerent
fields.comment:
Set to 1 between two countries when either joins the side of a war the other is already on, and cleared when either leaves. The writers are SetWarSideCoBelligerentFlags (0xA51CB0) and ClearWarSideCoBelligerentFlags (0xA51C40), each of which writes **both** directions of the pair; their four callers are CWar::AddAttacker (0x64F220, already named), CWar::AddDefender (0x6506B0, already named) and the two Remove siblings 0x650440/0x651710, passing `war->attackers` (+0x2C) or `war->defenders` (+0x3C). Found by scanning every function that mentions the disp32 0xE28 for a byte store to [reg+0x58] - 177 candidates, of which only these two write both halves of a pair. Not a save key (FINDINGS-theatre2.md) and not military_access (+0x4C). This is the byte CCountry::RebuildNeighbours tests at 0x4E32E9 to decide membership of CCountry +0xF98, so that list is **us plus our co-belligerents, minus anyone we are also at war with** - the rule the record had to name from the walk alone.

**Two readers in the AI confirm the sense from the other side**, found independently (reversing/FINDINGS-subdivide.md): AreaMayWidenFrontSearch (0x495140, at 0x4951DD) and CAIUnit::RebuildAreaNeighbourProvinces (0x4BC860) both require this byte on exactly the branch where CCountry::IsSameSide has already answered no - i.e. "not on our side, but co-belligerent, so this area may widen the front search". That survey proposed the name `military_access` for it from that role alone; the writers settle it the other way, and military_access is +0x4C.

fields.name: threat
fields.comment: How much threat the array's owner feels from the other country, thousandths. Two independent readers agree: the alignment threat term takes the maximum of this over a faction's members, and 0x4E21E0 scans it to cache the worst offender in CCountry +0x11D8/+0x11DC - which is the one value EffectiveNeutrality is derived from.

fields.name: trade_routes
fields.comment: The pair's trade routes - head at +0x60, count at +0x68. It is what the game's own Lua `CDiplomacyStatus:GetTradeRoutes()` hands out (the luabind registration is for `const CList<CTradeRoute*>&`). CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes (0xFEE70) skips a pair whose count is zero and otherwise walks this list.

fields.name: trade_routes_count
fields.comment: How many trade routes the pair has; the count of the list at +0x60, tested at 0x4FEF66 before the list is touched.

fields.name: needed
fields.comment: An fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>: the total daily IC the production queue wants, the sum of every construction's cost divided by 1000. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4C9DB1, rebuilt by 0x11A290 at the end of every Distribute, and returned verbatim by slot 3 GetNeeded (0x11A2E0).

fields.name: spent_beyond_free
fields.comment: An fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>, zeroed at the start of every Distribute (0x519D23). It accumulates the IC the pass asked for **beyond the resource-free part** - the two adds, 0x51A03B and 0x51A137, both happen before the resource check, so it counts what was wanted rather than what was got. Nothing in the ten distributors reads it back; only the constructor, the two adds and the reset touch it. The name is ours.

structs.name: Session
structs.comment: The multiplayer/singleplayer session, `session.cpp`. **No RTTI**, so this struct's anchor is the vftable write in its constructor (rva 0x6887A0, write at 0x00A887E0) rather than a type descriptor. CInGameIdler reaches it as `[this+0x1790]->[0x12C]`. See FINDINGS-commands.md.

fields.name: state
fields.comment: The value Session::PumpCommands switches on. BindChannel writes 4; the pump branches on 0, 2, 3, 4, 7, 0xA, 0xB and 0xC. That 4 is the in-game value is inferred.

fields.name: may_post_commands
fields.comment: THE GATE. Set to 1 by BindChannel for channel modes 1 and 2, cleared for modes 0 and 3. CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock tests it at rva 0x2811E5 before allocating a CHourlyTickCommand, and CInGameIdler::AutosaveCheck tests it too. Not 'a channel exists' - modes 0 and 3 have one.

fields.name: channel
fields.comment: The one command channel. Slot 6 posts a command, slot 7 pumps it, slot 8 returns the pending list. Written by BindChannel, which also writes the session back into channel+0x1C.

fields.name: pending_commands
fields.comment: begin of a std::vector the pump moves the channel's pending list into before executing, so the list can grow while commands run.

fields.name: turn
fields.comment: Incremented once per channel pump (rva 0x73C08C). A post stamps word command+0x34 with it, capped below 0x7FFF.

fields.name: address
fields.comment: The remote address the constructor is given; 'NoAdress' for the startup session. Only the mode 0 and mode 1 channels are handed it.

fields.name: executed_serials
fields.comment: head of a linked list of the serials of commands already executed; tail at +0x224, count at +0x228, capped at +0x230. Appended to right after Execute. This is what 'Command double! Skipping.' is checked against.

fields.name: executed_serials_cap
fields.comment: How many executed serials to remember. BindChannel writes 0x64 (100).

fields.name: command_executing
fields.comment: Set to 1 immediately before CCommand::Execute and cleared immediately after (rva 0x68985C and 0x689942). The pump returns early if it is already set, so command execution never nests.

structs.name: CommandChannel
structs.comment: The base of the four command-channel classes, `this` as the first stack argument. **No RTTI**; anchored on the vftable write at 0x00B33A80 in its constructor (rva 0x733A60), which happens before any field write and calls no other constructor, which is what makes it the root. 29 slots; the base leaves slots 6, 7 and 9 `_purecall`, so post and pump are declared here and filled in by each subclass. See FINDINGS-commands.md.

fields.name: session
fields.comment: The back pointer BindChannel writes. Both posts read [this+0x1C]->[0x54] for the turn stamp, and the loopback pump increments it.

fields.name: pending_commands
fields.comment: A {head, tail, count} list of cloned commands waiting to execute. Virtual slot 8 returns it; the loopback pump appends to it and Session::PumpCommands drains it.

structs.name: ServerCommandChannel
structs.comment: Mode 1, the host's channel (`server.cpp`). **No RTTI**; anchored on the vftable write at 0x00B34584 (ctor rva 0x734550). Its `+0x9C` ring is its own, not the base's. See FINDINGS-commands.md.

fields.name: queue
fields.comment: The TBB concurrent_queue this class uses, at a different offset from the loopback channel's. The post pushes the command pointer itself into it, without serialising.

fields.name: next_serial
fields.comment: lock xadd'd by the post to stamp command+0x38.

structs.name: LoopbackCommandChannel
structs.comment: Mode 2, the loopback channel a single-player game posts through. **No RTTI**; anchored on the vftable write at 0x00B3BE32 (ctor rva 0x73BE00). Its `+0x7C` is an embedded TBB concurrent_queue, which is why it is filed here and not on the base - the same offset is a second ring in ServerCommandChannel. See FINDINGS-commands.md.

fields.name: queue
fields.comment: An Intel TBB concurrent_queue - 0x220-byte rep from the TBB import at 0xD2B564, items_per_page 0x20 at rep+0x100, item_size 4 at rep+0x104, tail counter at rep+0x80, micro-queue array at rep+0x180. The post pushes deserialised command pointers into it and the pump try_pop's them.

fields.name: next_serial
fields.comment: lock xadd'd by the post to stamp command+0x38.

fields.name: class_id
fields.comment: 0x18D for CHourlyTickCommand. Distinct from the type id at +0x2C/+0x30.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: Empty at construction in CHourlyTickCommand.

fields.name: type_id
fields.comment: The value virtual slot 7 returns; CHourlyTickCommand's constructor writes 0x28D here and at +0x30.

fields.name: type_id_2
fields.comment: Written with the same value as +0x2C by the constructor. Why there are two has not been established.

fields.name: issued_turn
fields.comment: WORD, not a byte. 0xFFFF until posted; the post writes the session's turn counter (session+0x54, zeroed if above 0x7FFF) here. Session::PumpCommands reads it at rva 0x689CD7 and can reject the command with 'Atempted to execute invalid order with stamp '.

fields.name: targeted_async
fields.comment: WORD, 0 for an ordinary command. When non-zero the post skips the serial and takes the 'Sending targeted asynchronous command: ' path instead of the queue.

fields.name: serial
fields.comment: A per-channel monotonic serial, taken with lock xadd on channel+0x88 (loopback) or channel+0xA8 (server) at post time, carried across the pump's clone by hand, and appended after Execute to the 100-entry history at session+0x220 that 'Command double! Skipping.' is decided against.

fields.name: random_snapshot
fields.comment: begin of a std::vector<int> copied from CCurrentGameState+0xC58 by the constructor (rva 0x2DA351), end at +0x40, capacity at +0x44, free()d by the destructor. Serialised by virtual slot 2 through 0x6DB4A0, so it travels with the command wherever the command goes.

fields.name: random_snapshot_end
fields.comment: end of the vector at +0x3C.

fields.name: random_snapshot_capacity
fields.comment: capacity end of the vector at +0x3C.

structs.name: CSpyPresence
structs.comment: One country's spy presence in one other country, 0xF8 bytes. **No vftable and so no RTTI**, but the name is the game's own: luabind registers CSpyPresence (.?AVCSpyPresence@@ at 0x1747B64) with GetLevel, GetPriority, GetLastMissionChangeDate, GetMission and GetSpyPresence. The layout is anchored on CCountry::GetSpyPresence (rva 0x44920), six instructions that return `(char*)this->espionage[+0x1160] + tag->id * 0xF8` - which fixes both the stride and the indexing - and on the constructor at rva 0x12D380, which writes every field. CCountry +0x1160/+0x1164/+0x1168 is a std::vector of these, one per country, sized once from the country count. See reversing/FINDINGS-espionage.md.

fields.name: level
fields.comment: Spies present, **x1000** - one spy is 1000, and the ceiling is g_MaxSpyLevel (10000, ten spies). The save key is `spy_allocation`, written through the thousandths vector writer 0x4C8050, and the Lua accessor is GetLevel. Set only through CSpyPresence::SetLevel (0x52D4A0), the slider's placement (0x51F0F2) and the -1000 a caught spy costs (0x52E74F).

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: 0..3, a plain integer - the save key `spy_priority` goes through the `%d` vector writer 0x4608D0. CChangeSpyPriority::Execute (0x5589A0) is the only writer outside the loader. **Band 0 never receives a spy**: CDistributeEspionage::Distribute's outer loop is `while (band > 0)`, so 0 means 'none here'. A presence already at 70% of MAX_NUMBER_OF_SPIES is treated as one band lower.

fields.name: missions
fields.comment: One entry per `SpyMission`, in the order the nine localisation keys sit in .rdata from 0x15EC590 and the order CSpyPresence::RunDailyMissions tests them: 0 counter_espionage, 1 military, 2 tech, 3 boost_ruling_party, 4 boost_our_party, 5 lower_national_unity, 6 increase_threat, 7 raise_national_unity, 8 covert_ops. Plain integers - how many spies are put on each. The save writes nine `spy_mission` values per country; the mapping is confirmed by each handler reading exactly the define its name predicts.

fields.name: mission_share
fields.comment: **Derived, x1000**: `missions[k] * 1000 / sum(missions)`, rewritten wholesale by CSpyPresence::SetMissionAllocation (0x52D4D0) every time any allocation changes, and zeroed when the total is zero. Never saved - CCountry::LoadKey goes through the same setter, so a load recomputes it. Every mission effect is scaled by its own entry.

fields.name: last_mission_change
fields.comment: A game tick; the save key is `spy_date` and the Lua accessor GetLastMissionChangeDate. The constructor sets it from the global 0x170C2B8 (43800000, the epoch) and CChangeSpyMission::Execute writes the current tick (0x558F87). **Nothing reads it** but the save writer: SPY_MISSION_CHANGE_DAYS, the define that would give it meaning, has no reader in the image, so there is no cooldown on changing a spy mission.

fields.name: lower_unity_modifier
fields.comment: A `CStaticModifier` held **by value**, 0x48 bytes (the constructor writes vftable 0x15BC568 here at 0x52D3D6, and 0x54 + 0x48 = 0x9C where the next one starts). CSpyPresence::ApplyUnityModifiers fills it from the `spy_lower_national_unity` template for mission 5, with the presence's level and mission_share[5] as its values. Its own values array pointer is at +0x18 (so +0x6C here) and a std::string at +0x2C (so +0x80).

fields.name: raise_unity_modifier
fields.comment: The second embedded CStaticModifier, vftable written at 0x52D3F8. Filled from the `spy_raise_national_unity` template for mission 7, with the level and mission_share[7].

fields.name: target_tag
fields.comment: The three characters and NUL of the country this record is **about** - the place the spies are. From the constructor's second argument; the construction site 0x4D5017 passes the country being iterated. CSpyPresence::IsHostileMission resolves it to a country through 0x402610.

fields.name: target_id
fields.comment: The id half of target_tag, and the index of this record in the owner's vector.

fields.name: owner_tag
fields.comment: The three characters and NUL of the country whose vector this record lives in - the spies' owner. From the constructor's third argument, which the construction site fills from the country being set up (`[ebp+8] + 0xCA4`).

fields.name: owner_id
fields.comment: The id half of owner_tag.

fields.name: covert_ops_points
fields.comment: x1000, the save key `covert_ops_points`. Mission 8 adds `level * SPY_COVERT_OPS_GAIN / 1000 * mission_share[8] / 1000` at 0x530307 and then clamps it down to SPY_COVERT_OPS_MAX at 0x530326 - a hard store, not a refusal. 0x444C60 reads it out of `actor->espionage[province->controller]` for the covert-ops check. The record is 0xF8 bytes, so this is its last field.

structs.name: CAIUnit

fields.name: air_target_lists_built
fields.comment:
Set to 1 by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists as its last act (0x4B4E18) and tested by CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0A45 immediately before calling it: `if (agent->unit (+0x64) == 0) skip; if (Tick's own replan flag) call; if (+0x83) skip; call`. So the four `air_target_provinces_*` lists are built once per agent and rebuilt only when Tick decides to replan. Nothing clears it in either body.

It sits between the already-recorded `+0x80 stance_set` and `+0x85 replan_naval`, i.e. in the same run of agent flags.

fields.name: known_enemy_convoys
fields.comment:
Head of a CList of **convoy object id pairs** - each node holds the id type at +0, the serial at +4 and the next node at +0xC, the same shape as the +0x25C enemy_units_sighted list.

CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits' convoy-raid block is the only reader found: at 0x4D2526 it walks the list, resolves each pair through FindPersistentById against the persistent database at [0x1A857F0] (id type above 0x1268) or [0x1A857F4] (at or below), and scores the resolved object's `path` for a submarine raid target. That the resolved object is a CConvoy is not an inference - `CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports` is called on it twice (0x4D27F9, 0x4D288B) and `CConvoy +0xB0 path` / `+0xB8 path_count` are read as the record describes them.

Nothing writes it in either body, and what fills it was not looked for.

fields.name: command_level_state
fields.comment: **Not zero for the life of the object.** The constructor zeroes it and FINDINGS-aiunit.md notes that the luabind getter GetOwnerAI (0x4E90A0, `mov eax,[ecx+0x54]`) therefore answers null on a CAIUnit - but slot 82 (0x4C0600) *writes* it, at 0x4C0775, from 0x4DA340(this, unit->oob_level), gated on `this->+0x54 == 0` or its own bool argument being false plus 0xA56B0(unit->current_province, 0). So GetOwnerAI called on a CAIUnit answers null only until slot 82 has run once, and after that it hands back whatever 0x4DA340 returned. What that is was not established.

fields.name: owner_ai
fields.comment: The country's CEU3AI. Written by CAIUnit::CAIUnit (0x4AF530) from its first stack argument at 0x4AF578, and all four call sites pass the CEU3AI. **Not +0x54**, which CAIUnit's constructor zeroes even though that is where CAIAgent keeps the owner for the five ministers and where the luabind getter GetOwnerAI (0x4E90A0) reads.

fields.name: unit
fields.comment: The unit this agent commands. Zero at construction; written only by CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63, 0x4B9EB0), which refuses to overwrite it. Slot 54 reads `unit[+0x204]` (plan_active) through it, slot 82 asks it the `isLand` predicate, and slot 74 (0x4AF4D0) is a plain getter for it.

fields.name: area_id_type
fields.comment: Type half of the object id of the agent's **area**, which in every path that fills it is a CTheatre. Written from the theatre's own `+0x8` in CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForTheatres (0x48AC4D) and CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea, and from FindTheatreForUnit's result in the two unit paths. GetArea (0x4BBAE0) resolves the pair through the game's id registry; a type above 0x1268 goes to the registry at 0x1A857F0 and anything lower to 0x1A857F4.

fields.name: area_id
fields.comment: Serial half of the area's object id; see area_id_type.

fields.name: stance_set
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (slot 77, 0x4C36F0) at 0x4C3714, before anything else. The constructor seeds it 0. Slot 73 runs 0x4C3330 when the hour matches the country's stagger **or** this byte is clear, so it reads as 'a stance has been chosen at least once'. read

fields.name: replan_naval
fields.comment: The naval sibling of +0x86 replan_subordinates. Slot 73 reads it at 0x4B0C9F as the second of the two things that make it pass `force` to CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits, and that body clears it at 0x4D08E8 as its first act when force is set. Seeded 1 by the constructor's `+0x84 = 0x10101`, so one naval pass runs at the start of a game. No other writer found in the bodies read.

fields.name: replan_subordinates
fields.comment: Tested by slot 73 at 0x4B09F5 as one of the three things that make it call slot 78, and **cleared by slot 78 as its last act** (0x4B328C). So it is a request flag: whatever sets it asks for one subordinate-assignment pass. Nothing in slot 78 or 79 sets it.

fields.name: area_dirty
fields.comment: Zero at construction (the constructor writes `+0x84 = 0x10101`, which leaves +0x84/+0x85/+0x86 at 1 and this byte at 0). CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea sets it to 1 on a freshly made agent; CAIUnit::Tick treats it as 'do the area work now' in place of waiting for the weekly slot, and CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BA5A0) clears it as its first act.

fields.name: regroup_air_pending
fields.comment: 'This agent's air groups want regrouping.' Read, cleared and set by CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits only: it gates the split/merge phase at 0x4CE64F (`if (!this->+0x88 && !force) skip`), is cleared at 0x4CE67B before the phase runs, and is set back to 1 at 0x4CEA1D/0x4CEA30 whenever a wing was detached or merged. When it is still set after the phase the function returns 1 at 0x4CEE12 and assigns no missions at all that pass, so a pending regroup suppresses the whole mission half of the body.

fields.name: ops_area_first
fields.comment: The agent's own copy of the operations area it last computed - a `std::vector<CMapProvince*>`, begin here, end at +0x94, capacity end at +0x98. Slot 76 erases it (std::vector_erase at 0x4DBEAC), fills it with the front provinces it has claimed (std::vector_pushBackByAddress at 0x4DC71F and the inlined push_back at 0x4DC2AB), tests whether it is non-empty to decide whether to post a command, and CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree (0x4DCA70) passes its address to three callees that read it as begin/end of 4-byte elements and dereference them as provinces. read

fields.name: ops_area_last
fields.comment: End of the ops-area vector at +0x90. read

fields.name: ops_area_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the ops-area vector at +0x90; read by the inlined push_back growth check at 0x4DC2F6. read

fields.name: area_neighbours_first
fields.comment: Begin of a `vector<CMapProvince*>` (end at `+0xA4`, capacity end at `+0xA8`) that 0x4BC860 clears and refills on every replan from the provinces **adjacent to the operations area but not in it** that the country may enter - same side, or military access and not an enemy. The push_back is at 0x4BCD12.

fields.name: area_neighbours_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at `+0xA0`; 0x4BC860 resets it to begin at 0x4BC8AC.

fields.name: order
fields.comment: 0x4AF4E0 asks it for its kind through slot 16 and compares against the save tokens 0x4E5 and 0x56C, which is the order-kind idiom the record already knows from CStrategicRedeploymentOrder's 0x5A4. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF5D5.

fields.name: front_provinces_first
fields.comment: A second vector (end +0xC4, capacity end +0xC8) that 0x4BBB50 clears and rebuilds from the ops area at +0x90, as the first step of CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree. What it holds was not established - only that 0x4BBB50 empties it before walking the ops area's provinces. read (the clearing), inference (the contents)

fields.name: front_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the front-province vector whose begin the record already has at +0xC0. 0x4B630E..0x4B6316 takes (+0xC4 - +0xC0) / 4 as its element count and 0x4B634E does the same.

fields.name: amphibious_transport_tonnage
fields.comment: A tonnage floor on the transport-ship want: 0x4B7479 takes max(4 * enemy units counted in the objective areas * infantry transport_weight, this value) before dividing by a transport's capacity. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF604 and written in exactly one other place, 0x4C67CC, at the end of a loop in the unidentified CAIUnit helper 0x4C4370, from a tonnage accumulated on that function's frame. The use is read; the producer is not.

fields.name: submarine_want
fields.comment: Added straight onto the want vector's submarine entry - `want[nuclear_submarine or submarine] += this->+0xD8` at 0x4B7182, with no scaling at all. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF60A and accumulated by the unidentified CEU3AI helper 0x48C140 (`+= [esp+0x48]` at 0x48C750, and again at 0x48D52A).

fields.name: naval_units_first
fields.comment: Begin of a `std::vector<CNavy*>` (end +0xE0, capacity end +0xE4) that slot 78 erases at 0x4B1EDC and refills at 0x4B25A2-0x4B2614 with `unit->vf[11]()` for every **naval** unit in the agent's subtree. One of ten per-pass containers, not the seven the earlier survey counted.

fields.name: naval_units_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0xDC.

fields.name: naval_units_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the vector at +0xDC.

fields.name: naval_transports_first
fields.comment: Begin of a second `std::vector<CNavy*>` (end +0xF0, capacity +0xF4) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1F12. Filled at 0x4B2687 with the naval units whose aggregate definition has `transport_capacity` (`CUnit +0xC8 -> +0x144`) above zero **and** which either hold no objectives or fail 0x4B16F0 - the fleets available to lift troops.

fields.name: naval_transports_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0xEC.

fields.name: naval_transports_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the vector at +0xEC.

fields.name: air_units_first
fields.comment: **Head of the CList of CAir* that slot 78 rebuilds**, with the tail at +0x100 and the count at +0x104. Slot 78 walks and frees the chain from here at 0x4B1E76-0x4B1E92 and then zeroes all three words (0x4B1E94, 0x4B1E9A, 0x4B1EA0); it refills through 0x4DD3D0 at 0x4B26A8 with `unit->vf[13]()` for every **air** unit in the subtree. The record's existing `CAIUnit +0x100 subordinate_list_first` has the head one word too high.

fields.name: subordinate_list_first
fields.comment: A list (tail +0x104) that slot 78 frees node by node and re-heads at 0x4B1E86-0x4B1EA0, one of the seven subordinate-assignment containers it rebuilds every pass. read

fields.name: air_units_count
fields.comment: Count of the CList headed at +0xFC. **0x4CD890's entry test**: `if (agent->+0x104 < 1) return false` at 0x4CD8BA, which is why that body only runs for an agent commanding aircraft.

fields.name: subordinate_vector_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x110) that slot 78 erases at 0x4B1EA6-0x4B1ED6. **Its emptiness is slot 78's entry test**: at 0x4B1D48 the function records `(+0x110 - +0x10C) > 0` into a local before clearing anything, so the pass knows whether it had subordinates assigned last time. read

fields.name: subordinate_vector2_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x120) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1E45. One of its seven per-pass containers; what it holds was not established. read

fields.name: subordinate_vector3_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x130) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1D81. read

fields.name: subordinate_vector4_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x140) slot 78 erases first of all, at 0x4B1D42-0x4B1D7B. read

fields.name: subordinate_vector5_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x150) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1DB2. read

fields.name: subordinate_vector6_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x160) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1DE3. read

fields.name: subordinate_vector7_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x170) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1E14. read

fields.name: strategic_target_provinces_first
fields.comment: A std::vector<CMapProvince*> (end at +0x190) that both force planners walk to size the strategic-bomber want: they sum `province->modifiers[MODIFIER_LOCAL_IC] / 1000 + province->current_producing.crude_oil (+0x27C) / 1000` over it and divide by 300 (0x4B6E00..0x4B7014 in one arm, 0x4B5770 in the other). Only ever cleared through a plain displacement - by the constructor at 0x4AF6E2 and the destructor at 0x4B00C1 - so whatever fills it does so through `lea reg, [agent+0x18C]` and a vector helper, which a displacement scan cannot attribute.

fields.name: strategic_target_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x18C; the count is (+0x190 - +0x18C) / 4.

fields.name: enemy_sighting_provinces_first
fields.comment: A std::vector (end at +0x1A0) that 0x4B77CE..0x4B78A0 push_backs `unit->current_province_ptr (+0x130)` into, once per enemy unit taken off the sighting list at +0x25C. Named from that one producer; nothing was found that reads it.

fields.name: enemy_sighting_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x19C.

fields.name: invasion_target_provinces_first
fields.comment:
Begin of a `std::vector<CMapProvince*>` (end +0x1B0, capacity end +0x1B4) that slot 78 erases at 0x4B2000-0x4B2025.

**Retyped from `int*`.** CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4 walks it at 0x4CF403-0x4CF489 and uses each element as a province object, not an id: `lea eax,[elem + 0x2B8]` into CountEnemyLandUnitsInList (the units list), `lea edi,[elem + 0x68]` into CWeather::AirCombatEffect (the embedded weather), and `[elem + 0xD0]` into CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces (the id). An int could not be used any of those three ways.

The first phase-4 arm of the ground-attack block scores exactly these provinces, so whatever the vector is for, the AI bombs enemy stacks standing in it in preference to the battles on its own front.

fields.name: invasion_target_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x1AC.

fields.name: invasion_target_provinces_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the vector at +0x1AC.

fields.name: hostile_route_provinces_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList (last +0x1C0, count +0x1C4, nodes {data, prev, next, byte} with next at +8) holding **the provinces we do not control that lie on the routes from the operations area to the agent's selected target areas** - at war with us, rebel-held, ours-while-we-are-rebels, or covered by the pair's undeclared war. Cleared and refilled by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches (clear 0x4BBFFB, fill 0x4BC72F-0x4BC791), the routes coming from CCountryTag::FindProvinceRoute out of the three ops-area provinces nearest each target area. CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces doubles a province's priority once per member of this list the province is adjacent to, but only when the plan stance is 3 or more (0x4BD9C8-0x4BDA3C). Four further readers: 0x4C9D25, 0x4C9E81, 0x4CA0F3 (all in 0x4C956B's body), 0x4CAA00 and 0x4D5FB3.

fields.name: hostile_route_provinces_last
fields.comment: Tail of the CList at +0x1BC.

fields.name: hostile_route_provinces_count
fields.comment: Count of the CList at +0x1BC.

fields.name: target_area_provinces_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList (last +0x1D0, count +0x1D4) holding **every province of every owner area the agent has selected as a target**. Cleared and refilled by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BC02B-0x4BC053 and 0x4BC3E5-0x4BC44A: an area qualifies when it is on `ourCountry->areas_first (+0xD30)` with its byte +0x68 set, is not our acting capital's area, passes 0x7FD90, and is reachable from one of our own ops-area owner areas in at most two hops under OwnerAreaCost_Accessible but not at all under OwnerAreaCost_NoEnemy. Three readers: 0x4C9D03, 0x4D5C73 and 0x4D6D4B / 0x4D6E63 / 0x4D7826.

fields.name: target_area_provinces_last
fields.comment: Tail of the CList at +0x1CC.

fields.name: target_area_provinces_count
fields.comment: Count of the CList at +0x1CC.

fields.name: air_target_provinces_default
fields.comment:
Head of a CList (tail +0x200, count +0x204; nodes {payload, prev, next, byte} with the link at +8), kept **lowest-score-first** by CList_InsertByAscendingScore (0x4DD590). The payload is a 0x10-byte CPersistent record - vftable 0x15EB644, save id 0x18D at +4, a province id at +8 and a float at +0xC - built at 0x4B4C1B-0x4B4C45. It is *not* the 0x1C scored-province record used by +0x2C0.

**Writer: CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists (0x4B4740)**, called once per agent from CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0A4F and gated by `air_target_lists_built (+0x83)`. It clears this list at 0x4B47C2 and appends one record per candidate air-base province at 0x4B4C68.

**Reader: CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 2**, which picks one of the four by the wing's air role at 0x4CE253-0x4CE27B and scores it for a `rebase_air` destination. So these are **candidate air bases, ranked by proximity to the set each list is for** - this one's float is the mean distance to the agent's `ops_area (+0x90)` (or, when `manage_reserve (+0x364)` is clear, to the enemy's home air bases), blended 1:3 with the mean distance to `invasion_target_provinces (+0x1AC)` when that vector is non-empty.

fields.name: air_target_provinces_strategic
fields.comment:
The +0x1FC list used for a wing carrying a strategic bomber, or whose definition's `strategic_attack (+0x17C)` exceeds 50000; selected at 0x4CE259-0x4CE26E. Same node and payload shape as +0x1FC.

**Written by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists**: cleared at 0x4B47D1, appended at 0x4B4CC1, with the float being the mean map distance from the candidate base to `strategic_target_provinces (+0x18C)` (0x4B4C84). Lowest first. So a strategic bomber is rebased towards the provinces the force planner has already marked as strategic-bombing targets.

fields.name: air_target_provinces_naval
fields.comment:
The +0x1FC list used for a wing carrying a naval bomber; selected at 0x4CE270-0x4CE27B. Same node and payload shape as +0x1FC.

**Written by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists**: cleared at 0x4B47E0, appended at 0x4B4D1A, with the float being the mean map distance from the candidate base to `enemy_sighting_provinces (+0x19C)` (0x4B4CDD) - the provinces enemy units have been sighted in. Lowest first. So the naval-bomber list is 'bases near where we last saw the enemy', which is what makes it the naval one in practice rather than by any test on water.

fields.name: air_target_provinces_transport
fields.comment:
The +0x1FC list used for a wing carrying a transport plane, and only when the vector at +0x16C/+0x170 is empty; selected at 0x4CE29F-0x4CE2A5. Same node and payload shape as +0x1FC.

**Written by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists**: cleared at 0x4B47EF, appended at 0x4B4E00, with the float being the mean map distance from the candidate base to `invasion_target_provinces (+0x1AC)` (0x4B4DC9).

**But the writer's gate is the reader's gate inverted** (see AirTargetTransportListGate, 0x4B4D1F): nothing is appended here unless `(+0x170 - +0x16C)/4 > 0` and some unit in that vector sits in the candidate's area or an adjacent one, while phase 2 skips the wing outright when that vector is non-empty. Within one pass the two conditions are mutually exclusive, so whatever phase 2 reads out of this list was built on an earlier pass - the lists are rebuilt only on a replan, the vector every pass.

fields.name: enemy_units_sighted_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList of unit object id pairs - each node holds the id type at +0, the serial at +4 and the next node at +0xC - which both force planners resolve through the id registry (0x1A857F0 / 0x1A857F4) at 0x4B7550 and 0x4B5A00 and then count brigade by brigade to size the anti-ship wants. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF802, filled by the unidentified CEU3AI helper 0x48C140 (0x48CB21). The pair to +0x26C, which is walked the same way and **decrements** the same wants.

fields.name: enemy_units_lost_first
fields.comment: Head of a second CList of unit id pairs in the same form as +0x25C, walked by 0x4B78B3..0x4B7A0A.
