Every arithmetic step there is the mirror image of the +0x25C loop's: `dec want[...]` instead of `inc`, and the naval threat score has 0.07 / 0.15 / 0.02 subtracted instead of added. So the two lists are sightings gained and sightings lost. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF81A, filled by 0x48C140 (0x48D4E6).

fields.name: front_province_scores
fields.comment:
One of the AI's circular-sentinel ordered maps (comparator byte here, sentinel node at +0x298, size at +0x29C; nodes {next, prev, key, value}), keyed by a front province from +0xC0 and holding **a 0..100 nearness score, 100 on the front province closest to the unit's own plan objectives**. CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches builds it in two passes: the mean CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces from each plan objective in the same owner area (0x4BBF98, through AIOrderedMap_SubscriptFloat), then an in-place rescale to `(max - v) * 100 / (max - min)` at 0x4BC120-0x4BC1E8, skipped when every mean is equal. Nothing in 0x4AF000-0x4E0000 reads it besides the constructor, the destructor and that function; its subscript 0x4DCE40 has only two callers in the whole image, so **0x4D57F0 is the only possible consumer** and that function is unread.

**The name is doubtful - live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save.** Read live: **0xB6** on a freshly created agent and **0xB5** on the tick-0 agents, but **0x6F697412** on a live attached one and 0x532025CA on a detached one. No map size plausibly takes those values, so this is either not a size or not one field. What it *is* good for is a **state signature**: small means a fresh agent, large means one that has been attached, which is how the two kinds of unattached agent above were told apart. Treat the name as `inferred` and do not build on it.

fields.name: front_province_scores_sentinel
fields.comment: The sentinel node of the ordered map at +0x294. CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches tears the map down by writing `[sentinel] = sentinel` and `[sentinel+4] = sentinel` at 0x4BBD66/0x4BBD6B, which is the family's circular-list reset, and uses it as `end()` when it walks the map at 0x4BC1DC.

fields.name: front_province_scores_count
fields.comment: Size of the ordered map at +0x294; zeroed at 0x4BBD6E and incremented at 0x4BC1A2.

fields.name: unknown_2a4
fields.comment: Begin of a vector (end at +0x2A8) that CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches clears at 0x4BBD9E-0x4BBDBE with the usual zero-length-memmove-then-`end = begin` idiom and then never fills; its begin is handed to 0x10F4A0 at 0x4BBDCD with ecx = 0x10 and the map's sentinel as the second argument. What it holds is not established, and the windowed scan that found no other toucher covered only 0x4AF000-0x4E0000.

fields.name: unknown_2a8
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x2A4; see that field.

fields.name: unknown_2b4
fields.comment: Written to the constant **7** by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BBDD8 (as `[edi+0x20]` with edi = agent + 0x294) and by nothing else this pass found. Meaning not established. Beware when scanning for it: `[reg+0x2B4]` across the AI module is overwhelmingly CMapProvince::area, which is trap 12.

fields.name: unknown_2b8
fields.comment: Written to the constant **8** by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BBDDF, immediately after +0x2B4 gets 7. Meaning not established. The `movss [eax+0x2B8]` sites in CAIUnit::ClearUnit are CUnit +0x2B8, a different object.

fields.name: scored_provinces_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList (last +0x2C4, count +0x2C8) of the 0x1C scored-province records, kept in **descending score order** by CList_InsertByDescendingScore (0x4DD4B0) on the float at `record->+8`. CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces empties it through CListOfOwned_Clear at 0x4BD30A and appends one record per ops-area province. Its consumers pair it with the map at +0x2D0, or with (+0x2FC, +0x30C) instead when `unit->plan_stance` (CUnit +0x208) is 0 - which is the pair CAIUnit::RebuildOpsAreaProvinceRecords builds, and that function is called only at stance 0. Both switch sites: 0x4CC4B9-0x4CC4E9 and 0x4DCB20-0x4DCB2E, reached from CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0BC2 and 0x4B09F0. Record layout: +0 the province, +8 the score, +0xC the amount apportioned to it by 0x4C93B6, +0x18 a per-province cap.

fields.name: scored_provinces_last
fields.comment: Tail of the CList at +0x2C0; the insert walks backwards from here.

fields.name: scored_provinces_count
fields.comment: Count of the CList at +0x2C0, bumped by CList_InsertByDescendingScore at 0x4DD531 and tested for zero by 0x4DCB34 before the list is walked. **The `byte [reg+0x2C8]` reads and writes in CAIUnit slot 78, CAIUnit::ClearUnit and CAIUnit::SetPlanStance are CUnit +0x2C8, not this** - ClearUnit compares its base against `agent->unit` two instructions earlier and slot 78 reads `oob_level` off the same register. Trap 12.

fields.name: scored_province_map
fields.comment: An AI circular-sentinel ordered map, CMapProvince* -> the 0x1C scored-province record, with the same layout as +0x294 (comparator here, sentinel +0x2D4, size +0x2D8). CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces empties it through AIOrderedMap_Clear at 0x4BD305 and fills it through AIOrderedMap_Subscript at 0x4BDC6A, one entry per ops-area province, beside the list at +0x2C0. Read by 0x4CC450, which pairs the two and swaps both for (+0x2FC, +0x30C) at plan stance 0.

fields.name: focus_owner_areas_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList of `COwnerArea*` (0x10-byte nodes, payload at `+0`, next at `+8`), with the tail at `+0x33C` and the count at `+0x340`. **Rebuilt by CAIUnit::RebuildFocusOwnerAreas (0x4B0D20)**, which SetArea calls at 0x4BA679 before reading it: the entries come from the agent's theatre's `+0x84` list through 0x4B0F20. CAIUnit::SetArea then walks it at 0x4BA843-0x4BAA92 and, for each owner area 0x495140 approves, pulls in every front of every theatre of the country controlling that area - so this list is what lets a theatre agent claim ground on a front that is not its own theatre's.

fields.name: unknown348
fields.comment: Zeroed at the top of slot 78 (0x4B1F59), with the seven containers it rebuilds. Nothing else in the slot bodies read here touches it. read

fields.name: apportion_a
fields.comment: One of two floats 0x4BD270 zeroes at the top of every replan (0x4BD2F5); `+0x350` is the other. Nothing read in this pass writes them again, because 0x4BD270's middle was not read.

fields.name: apportion_b
fields.comment: The second of the two floats 0x4BD270 zeroes at 0x4BD2FD. See `+0x34C`.

fields.name: divisions_needed
fields.comment: What CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed last returned - the number of divisions the agent's theatre wants. Written only by CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower at 0x4B50AD.

fields.name: divisions_counted
fields.comment: What CAIUnit_SumOurPower last returned - how many `oob_level == 4` units it added up. Written only by CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower at 0x4B509C.

fields.name: our_power
fields.comment: The agent's own copy of the figure it pushes into `CUnitPlan::our_power`. Zeroed and refilled by CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower at 0x4B5088/0x4B508E, compared against the plan's value a thousandth at a time, and sent on through CSetPlanAttributesCommand's sixth argument.

fields.name: their_power
fields.comment: The agent's own copy of `CUnitPlan::their_power`; the out parameter CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed fills at 0x4B50A2/0x4B50A8, and the command's seventh argument.

fields.name: manage_reserve
fields.comment: Read into a local at the top of slot 78 (0x4B1FFC) and tested once, at 0x4B279F and again at 0x4B2A19: clear, every division is pushed straight onto the held-back vector at +0x15C and the whole reserve calculation is skipped with a surplus of -2. So this byte is what switches the commitment and reserve logic on. No writer was found in slot 78, 79 or 0x4B60F0.

fields.name: frontier_war_candidate
fields.comment: Set by CAIUnit::ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier (0x4BDF30) at 0x4BE14A when CAIStrategy::IsWarCandidate (0x4A9A30) accepts a neighbour of the operations area, and also implied by `+0x364`'s word write. So `+0x364` is "shooting war on my frontier" and `+0x365` is the weaker "war I might start".

fields.name: frontier_controlled
fields.comment: Seeded 1 by the constructor; zeroed and recomputed by CAIUnit::ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier (0x4BDF30). Set to 1 for an operations area province unless all three of: `gamestate +0xD0C` is zero, the province's controller is not this agent's country, and the owner AI's `+0x2C` is set. Since `+0x2C` is set exactly for an AI-run country, the byte can only stay zero for a province an AI country does not control.

fields.name: invasion_transport_need
fields.comment: Extra transport ships an amphibious plan needs. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion zeroes it at 0x492489 and adds `tonnageShort / transportCapacity + 1` at 0x4935DE; the force planner adds it straight onto the transport-ship want at 0x4B74F0. One writer and one reader, which is what makes the name safe.

fields.name: invasion_brigade_need
fields.comment: Extra brigades an amphibious plan needs. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion zeroes it at 0x492483 and adds a brigade shortfall at 0x493756. **It is the additive term in both force planners' brigade demand** - `+0x370 + round(need * shortage * 3)` at 0x4B626D and `+0x370 + need * 3` at 0x4B528B - so an invasion the AI is planning raises the land demand of the whole theatre.

structs.comment:
A unit-AI agent. **There is one per AI-controlled theatre, not one per country** - which is what explains the census shape rather than any missing object: a live Ireland campaign showed 112 agents across 78 tags with **none for IRE**, the played country, because HoI3 keeps theatre AI control as a per-theatre toggle and the player's own theatre has no agent. (the maintainer, 2026-10-02; it is his knowledge of the game rather than anything read out of the bytes, and it retires what looked like an anomaly.)

**Two consequences for reading a live game.** The agent count is a function of how many theatres are under AI control, so it moves when the player takes a theatre over or hands one back - it is not a fixed property of the scenario. And a player who leaves their theatres on AI keeps agents for their own country, so loading a save as a formerly AI-controlled nation should show populated agents for it.

**Keep this separate from the tick-0 finding, which is a different fact.** At tick 0 all 112 agents were freshly constructed shells - `unit`, `ops area`, `front`, the hostile route and the target areas all null on 112/112 - because the AI had not run yet, not because of who controlled what. Both are true at once and conflating them would make a negative look structural. See reversing/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md.

**A count that looked like confirmation and was not - corrected 2026-10-02.** I wrote here that 103 `CTheatre` against 102 `CAIUnit` meant one agent per theatre with the single missing one being the player's. **That does not survive its own arithmetic**: the played country had three theatres, so three agents would have to be missing, not one. the maintainer caught it.

What the same save actually shows, counting agents by their unit's owner (`CUnit +0x124`): **GER, the played country, has 3 agents** - so a player's theatres can stay AI-attached, which is what happens when a formerly AI-controlled nation is loaded and its theatre AI is left on. 66 countries have at least one agent; ENG has 14, JAP 8, SOV 4, IRE 1. The 103-vs-102 shortfall is therefore **one theatre somewhere else without an agent**, not the player's, and separately **one agent that exists with no unit at all** (`+0x64` null, and `+0x90`, `+0xC0`, `+0x1BC`, `+0x1CC` and all four list heads null with it, though 36 of its first 0x300 dwords are non-zero, so it is initialised rather than raw). the maintainer's reading is that a tick will finish setting it up; that is a prediction and has not been watched.

**The lesson is the one trap 12 keeps teaching in a different costume**: two counts that differ by one invite a story, and the story has to be checked against something other than the difference.

**How the pool actually behaves, watched over a game day (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save) - and it retires three wrong stories, two of them mine.** The agent count is **never exactly the theatre count**, because the pool holds transients in both directions:

- **On the way in.** A theatre was created during the run and an agent appeared with it in the same step (theatres 103 -> 104, agents 104 -> 105), with no unit yet. Its signature is `+0x294` small - 0xB6, matching the 0xB5 seen on freshly constructed agents at tick 0 - and 75 non-zero dwords in its first 0x300.
- **On the way out.** A second unattached agent sat unchanged across 13 ticks with 79 non-zero dwords and `+0x294` **large** (0x532025CA), which is the attached signature rather than the fresh one. So it had been attached and lost its unit: a dissolved theatre's agent, not yet freed.

Counts seen in one session: 102 agents (first process), then 104, then 105, against 103 and 104 theatres. **So neither 'one per theatre' nor 'the missing one is the player's' is right**, and a count difference of one invites a story that has to be checked against something else - here, the per-owner tally (GER has 3 agents, its three theatres all attached) and the `+0x294` signature.

A theory of mine that the data refuted, recorded so it is not tried again: the stale agent is **not** freed memory matching the vftable by accident. It sits in the middle of a regular 0x388 stride run with the same vftable as its neighbours; nothing in it changes over 1.5s while the game runs; and an attached agent's `+0x294` is just as large, so a large value there is normal.

fields.name: country_tag
fields.comment: The agent's own country, held by value: four characters here and the id at +0x38. Both of the replan callees read it as `lea ecx,[agent+0x34]; call CCountryTag::GetCountry` (0x4BBB77, 0x4BD31C, 0x4BD7C8) and the owner-area cost functors are built by copying both halves into a stack functor (0x4BC2C5/0x4BC2D1). AreaMayWidenFrontSearch's caller reads the id half directly as the agent's country id.

fields.name: country_id
fields.comment: The id half of the CCountryTag at +0x34. CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches compares it against a province's `controller_id` (CMapProvince +0x338) at 0x4BC0A2 to decide whether an ops-area province is ours.

fields.name: parent
fields.comment: **The parent in the agent tree.** Written by CAIAgent::SetParent (slot 48, 0x49C690) and by nothing else read here; CAIUnit::GetArea (0x4BBAE0) and CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForTheatres (0x48AA80) both climb it to the root of the tree, and slot 82 refuses to act on an agent that has one. Zeroed by CAIAgent::CAIAgent at 0x49C770.

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the children list - nodes of `{agent, prev, next, byte}`. CAIAgent::Update (slot 9, 0x49CA90) walks it through `+8` calling each child's slot 9, and CAIAgent::DisableAndDisband (slot 49, 0x49C8A0) empties it. Together with +0x40 being the parent, this is what makes the AI's unit agents a **tree**, and 0x48AA80 relies on it to find a tree's root.

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the children list.

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. The constructor zeroes +0x40 through +0x4C and the byte at +0x50, which is exactly a parent pointer followed by a CList.

structs.name: CEU3AI

fields.name: country_tag
fields.comment: The AI's own country tag, eight bytes with the id at +0x24. Two independent readers in the trade predicates: CEU3AI::IsTradeingAwayNeededResource does `lea ecx, [this+0x20]` at 0x89B4B2 and 0x89B4FC followed by CCountryTag::GetCountry (0x402610), and CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingResourceOtherWay does `lea edi, [this+0x20]` at 0x89B322, reads the id half as [edi+4] at 0x89B329 and calls GetCountry on edi at 0x89B343 - both comparing it against a CTradeRoute's from_id and to_id to work out which side of a route the AI is on. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

fields.name: country_id
fields.comment: The country id half of the tag at +0x20. Compared against CTradeRoute +0x28 (from_id) at 0x89B4A2 and 0x89B32E, and against +0x30 (to_id) at 0x89B4EC. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

fields.name: runs_units
fields.comment: **1 for an AI-run country, 0 for the human's own country.** The constructor (0x488020, vftable 0x11EB660) seeds it 1 at 0x4880BA, and ProcessAI (0x4894E0) clears it at 0x4895BA the first time it runs for the country whose id equals `gamestate->player` (`+0xC34`) - once only, because the write is guarded on the byte still being set. Four consumers in the unit AI, and they are the whole of what the flag does: CAIUnit::UpdatePlanAxis (0x4C3330) returns at once unless it is set, so the AI never redraws a human's attack arrows; slot 82 posts CSetCommandLevel only when it is set; CAIUnit::SetArea *skips* its objective-owner-area pass when it is set, so objectives constrain the human's delegated AI and not the AI's own; and ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier reads it in the `+0x366` test. The same split appears a second way in slot 73, which chooses 0x4B5210 or 0x4B60F0 on `gamestate->played_countries_array[countryId]`.

fields.name: unit_agents_first
fields.comment: **The country's CAIUnit agents**, a CList of `{agent, prev, next, byte}` nodes. All four creation paths push_back onto it, and ProcessAI walks it at 0x48986D calling each agent's slot 9 once per game hour. Distinct from the minister list at +0x74 and the invasion list at +0x50.

fields.name: unit_agents_last
fields.comment: Last node of the unit-agent list.

fields.name: unit_agents_count
fields.comment: How many unit agents. ProcessAI tests it at 0x4897C6 and only runs CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits when it is zero, so that path builds the player's agents once.

fields.name: invasion_agents_first
fields.comment: **The country's CAIInvasion agents**, the same node shape. Filled at 0x493B34-0x493B5D right after CAIInvasion's constructor (0x49F920), and walked by ProcessAI at 0x489887 immediately after the unit agents.

fields.name: invasion_agents_last
fields.comment: Last node of the invasion-agent list.

fields.name: invasion_agents_count
fields.comment: How many invasion agents.

fields.name: flag_a5
fields.comment: A second ProcessAI gate beside +0xA6: set at 0x889B94, read at 0x88961B, 0x889A82 and 0x899CF2. What it means was not established - recorded only so the next reader does not mistake it for +0xA6.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: theatres_changed
fields.comment: Set to 1 by the AI's theatre layer whenever it makes or re-points a theatre - 0x8ABAA4 and 0x8ABB77 in CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres, 0x8ABF22 in CAIStrategy::RefreshTheatreProvinces, each as `mov byte [GetCountry(tag)->+0x1D8 + 0xA6], 1`. Cleared only by ProcessAI, at 0x8896BC and 0x889852, and only once every theatre in CCountry +0x570 has a resolvable HQ unit; until then ProcessAI leaves it set and retries next hour. Written on the **tick** thread and cleared on a **worker** - an unsynchronised byte either way.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: update_stances_pending
fields.comment: CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4912D0) returns immediately when its `force` argument is false and this byte is clear (0x4912F3-0x491301). ProcessAI's one call site is at 0x489B8F. read (the gate), inference (the name)

fields.name: priority_province_list_first
fields.comment: A list of province ids. CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives (0x4980E0) adds **100 flat** to a candidate objective's priority when the province is in it (0x49848F-0x4984A8). What fills it was not traced. read (the use)

fields.name: priority_province_list_last
fields.comment: Tail of the province-id CList whose head project.json already records at +0x118. Zeroed with the head at 0x49772B and written on every append at 0x4979D5 by CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces.

fields.name: priority_province_list_count
fields.comment: Count of the province-id CList at +0x118. Zeroed at 0x497731 and incremented at 0x4979DB. The list is freed and rebuilt in full once per AI pass, so this is never persistent state.

structs.comment: **One per country, measured live (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save): 108 instances against 108 CCountry.** So this is the per-country AI object rather than a global.

fields.name: persistent_token
fields.comment: CPersistent's own field, written as 0x18D by every body that builds a CObjective (0x1E700B, 0x498641) and copied by CopyObjectiveList. read

fields.name: province
fields.comment: The objective province. `CObjective::LoadKey` (0x4E33D0) reads the key `province` (token 0x1EE) into it through the province reader 0xA7B470.

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: `CObjective::LoadKey` reads the key `priority` (token 0x8A) into it with `%i` (format at 0x15FD14C).

fields.name: invasion
fields.comment: `CObjective::LoadKey` reads the key `invasion` (token 0x3A5) into it with `%i`, through the same reader as `priority` - so it is a number, not a flag.

fields.name: hold
fields.comment: `CObjective::LoadKey` reads the key `hold` (token 0x715) into it through the bool reader 0xA7B410.

fields.name: prev
fields.comment: An objective **is** its own list node: CopyObjectiveList (0x4DD350) allocates 0x24 bytes per objective and links them through +0x18 (prev) and +0x1C (next), with a byte at +0x20, exactly the standalone-node shape the record calls `{data, prev, next}` with the data inlined.

fields.name: next
fields.comment: The next objective in the plan's list; see prev.

fields.name: list_flag
fields.comment: The fourth member of the embedded list node (prev +0x18, next +0x1C, this byte), cleared by every creator. read

fields.name: band1_cursor
fields.comment: CDistributeEspionage has RTTI (`.?AVCDistributeEspionage@@` at 0x17149E0) and derives from CDistributionSetting, so +0x8, +0x10 and +0x18 are the base's. Its spending loop starts a cursor pointer at `this + 0x34` and drops it by 4 per priority band, so +0x34, +0x30 and +0x2C are round-robin cursors for bands 3, 2 and 1: the loop resumes at the country the previous pass stopped at and wraps to 1 when it runs out. That is why the slider does not always favour the first country in the list.

fields.name: band2_cursor
fields.comment: The round-robin cursor for priority band 2. See band1_cursor.

fields.name: band3_cursor
fields.comment: The round-robin cursor for priority band 3, the first band spent. The class is therefore at least 0x38 bytes, against CDistributeProduction's 0x30. +0x28 would be band 0's cursor and the loop never reaches it (`while (band > 0)` at 0x51F15E), so whether +0x28 is that or something else is open.

fields.name: positioning
fields.comment: Naval positioning, thousandths, save key `positioning` (0x39B). Rolled once at combat start by CNavalCombat slot 13 (0x17B910) and then written by CNavalCombatant::UpdatePositioning (0x166E70) as `clamp0(+0x10B8 + 400 + leaderSkill*100 - stackPenalty)`; CNavalCombatant::Attack (slot 15) adds 20 a tick while it is below `max(100, 400 + leaderSkill*100 - stackPenalty)`. leaderSkill is CLeader.skill (+0x70) of the highest-ranked real leader on the side; stackPenalty is NavalStackingPositionPenalty (0x1D5B80). **The base 400, the per-tick 20 and the skill weight 100 are all hardcoded literals, not defines** - only the three NAVAL_STACK_POS_* defines are mod-facing. Because the die can be up to 190, a side can start above its own cap and then never move. What positioning is multiplied into is not established.

fields.name: positioning_roll
fields.comment: The positioning die: `(rand() % 20) * 10`, i.e. 0..190 thousandths, rolled once per side by CNavalCombat slot 13 (0x17B978 for the attacker, 0x17B9D8 for the defender) and added straight into +0x10B4 by UpdatePositioning. Never re-rolled. FINDINGS-combat.md records it as zeroed beside +0x10B4 with nothing known about it.

fields.name: humidity
fields.comment: save key `humidity`, thousandths; CWeather::Update pulls it towards the terrain's own humidity (CTerrain+0x60) and CWeather::Clamp holds it between MINHUMIDITY and MAXHUMIDITY

fields.name: pressure
fields.comment: save key `pressure`; a new province starts at PRESSUREDEFAULT (CProvince::CProvince at 0x9479E) and the high pressure zones push it up by PRESSUREPROPAGATION a step in CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure

fields.name: windspeed
fields.comment: save key `windspeed`; read by the air, bomb and naval weather terms and by WINDATTRITIONTHRESHOLD, and decayed by a compiled-in 0.750 an hour where no front is over the province **Corrected 2026-10-01: the factor is 0.750, not 0.980.** `CWeather::Update` reads `[0x1A86F3C]` = floor(750.5) = 750, which has exactly two references in the image - that read and its CRT initialiser. 0.980 is `[0x1A8703C]`, a different global: the humidity and pressure transfer factor in SpreadWeather.

fields.name: temperature
fields.comment: save key `temperature`, thousandths of a degree; the threshold tested by every LAND/AIR/BOMB temperature define, by the two attrition thresholds, and by the cold movement penalty

fields.name: precipitation
fields.comment: save key `precipitation`; drives the land rain penalty, the air and bomb rain terms, the naval rain term, naval spotting, firing range and whether the ground freezes

fields.name: muddyness
fields.comment: save key `muddyness`, 0..1000; the only thing that slows land movement (MUDDYNESSMOVEMENTMODIFIER) and the only weather term in supply losses (MUDDYNESSSUPPLYTAXMODIFIER). It rises while it rains, dries by max(the province's infrastructure effect, 2) an hour, and is zeroed below -5C - where `frozen` takes over

fields.name: frozen
fields.comment: save key `frozen`, 0..1000; non-zero suppresses the mud movement penalty and the mud supply tax entirely. Rises by HOURLYFROZENINCREASE in the cold, falls by HOURLYTHAW above 0C

fields.name: cloud_coverage
fields.comment: save key `cloud_coverage`; the air and bomb cloud terms, naval spotting, and - at or above ALLOWEDTOFLYTHRESHOLD - the flat refusal in CAir::CanMoveTo

fields.name: front
fields.comment: the weather front over this province, copied from CProvince+0x14 at the top of CWeather::Update (0xB25D1) and zeroed there when there is none. Not saved

fields.name: province
fields.comment: back pointer to the owning province. CProvince::CProvince writes it at 0x94795 (`mov [esi+0x94], esi`), and every CWeather method reaches the terrain, the climate and the night flag through it - the same convention as CProvinceModifier+0x2C

fields.name: fronts
fields.comment: the live weather fronts: head +0x08, tail +0x0C, count +0x10. CWeatherManager::Tick walks it, frees the fronts whose Tick answers false, and tops it up towards (low pressure zones) x MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE/1000

fields.name: freeze_fronts
fields.comment: while set, CWeatherManager::Tick (0xB5CD7) marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed. What sets it was not established

fields.name: zone_cooldowns_begin
fields.comment: a vector of countdowns, one per low pressure zone (end at +0x1C). Every entry is decremented once an hour at 0xB5A65, filled by 0xB54F0 when empty, and tested by CreateFront (0xB5D40) before a zone may spawn another front

fields.name: zone_cooldowns_end
fields.comment: end of the per-zone cooldown vector at +0x18; +0x20 is its capacity. CWeatherManager::InitialiseWeatherState clears this vector and then pushes one zero per low pressure zone, and CWeatherManager::Tick calls that function whenever the vector is empty.

fields.name: zone_cooldowns_capacity
fields.comment: capacity of the per-zone cooldown vector at +0x18

fields.name: zone_headings_begin
fields.comment: A SECOND per-zone vector, filled in step with the cooldowns at +0x18 by CWeatherManager::InitialiseWeatherState (0xB54F0) - one int per low pressure zone (end +0x2C, capacity +0x30). It is the zone's last front heading, in thousandths of a full turn: CreateFront reads it, and either takes a fresh Random()%1000 where it is zero or advances it by 1000000/MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE and wraps it at 1000, stores it back, and hands it to the new front as its `direction`. So this is what makes a zone's fronts fan out evenly around the compass - confirmed in autosave.hoi3, where zone 13833's eight live fronts sit on a 0.125 lattice. 0xB59C0 resets every entry to zero. Note InitialiseWeatherState clears only the +0x18 vector before refilling both, so a second call would grow this one; it cannot happen, because Tick only calls it while +0x18 is empty.

fields.name: zone_headings_end
fields.comment: end of the per-zone heading vector at +0x28

fields.name: zone_headings_capacity
fields.comment: capacity of the per-zone heading vector at +0x28

fields.name: direction
fields.comment: save key `direction`: the front's heading, in thousandths of a full turn. CWeatherFront::Tick adds `rotation` to it on every move and passes it to IsAngleWithinArc (0xB4490) against each candidate neighbour's bearing, which is what decides where the front goes next. Seeded from the home zone's heading cache (CWeatherManager+0x28), which starts at a Random()%1000 and then steps by 1000000/MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE per spawn so a zone's fronts fan out evenly. It is NOT wrapped back into 0..999 after `+= rotation`, but the rotation sum is bounded by about 50 so it stays near the range. Confirmed against autosave.hoi3.

fields.name: provinces
fields.comment: save key `provinces`: every province the front currently covers. Head +0x0C, tail +0x10, count +0x14, trailing byte +0x18. The constructor puts the home province in it; every move empties it completely and refills it with the neighbours recruited that step, so a front abandons its whole footprint each time it advances. A front whose count reaches zero is deleted by CWeatherManager::Tick. Live fronts in a 1942 savegame hold 1 to 59 provinces.

fields.name: provinces_tail
fields.comment: tail of the `provinces` CList at +0x0C

fields.name: provinces_count
fields.comment: count of the `provinces` CList at +0x0C, and the front's liveness test: CWeatherFront::Tick answers `count > 0` and CWeatherManager::Tick deletes the front when it answers false. It is also the front's size class - under 3 provinces widens the spread arc by 0.150, over 30 halves it, over 100 halves it again AND limits each province to recruiting one neighbour, and under 4 provinces lets the front die once it is more than 1000 map pixels from home.

fields.name: provinces_flag
fields.comment: the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class

fields.name: home
fields.comment: the front's home province - the loader's `home` key. CWeatherManager::Tick matches its id (province+0xD0) against the low pressure zone ids on CMap+0x21D8 at 0xB5D38

fields.name: rotation
fields.comment: save key `rotation`: how much the front's `direction` turns per move, in thousandths of a turn. Set to +/-10 at birth ([0x1686FC8], negated where the home province is in the southern half of the map, CProvinceTemplate+0xA2) and multiplied by 800/1000 after every move, so the whole curvature of a front's path is bounded by about 0.050 of a turn (18 degrees) and integer truncation kills it after roughly eleven moves. Confirmed in autosave.hoi3: 38 of 45 fronts read 0.000 and the rest 0.001..0.008 with both signs present.

fields.name: move_countdown
fields.comment: the loader's `speed` key, used as a countdown: CWeatherFront::Tick decrements it every hour and only moves the front when it reaches zero, then resets it to WEATHERMOVEMENTDELAY/1000

fields.name: flag_3d
fields.comment: Zero at construction. AddUnit (slot 63) refuses to claim a unit's CUnit +0x198 while either this or +0x3E is set (0x8A16CB-0x8A16D7); also read at 0x8A177D. Meaning not established.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: finished
fields.comment: **Once set, the agent never acts again**: slot 10 returns immediately on it. Set from IsInvasionOver's answer at 0x89FB1F, by slot 73 when no landing province qualifies (0x89FBAD), and at 0x8A116F. Tested by AddUnit before claiming a unit.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: land_force_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList (last +0x58, count +0x5C, trailing byte +0x60) zeroed by the constructor. **The land force**: PickLandingSite sums `SumTransportWeight` over it as the load to be carried (0x89FD0A) and refuses to add more when its count exceeds 5 (0x89FCEE); IsInvasionOver declares the invasion over when its count drops below 1. Appended to at 0x8A17BA/0x8A17D0, in a small function between slots 63 and 64 that was not read - **the land/transport split between +0x54 and +0x64 is inferred from the two SumTransportWeight calls and from IsInvasionOver asking +0x64's first member for a CNavalInvasionOrder, not proved.**
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: land_force_last
fields.comment: Tail of the land-force CList whose head is +0x54; count +0x5C, trailing byte +0x60. Appended to at 0x8A17BA/0x8A17D0, which is inside AddUnit (slot 63, 0x8A1680-0x8A1853 with no padding before 0x8A1856), not in a separate function. The branch is taken when CUnit slot 15 answers true, and project.json already records CUnit slot 15 as IsLand - so the land/transport split is read, not inferred.

fields.name: land_force_count
fields.comment: Count of the land-force CList at +0x54. Capped at 5 by PickLandingSite's `canTakeMore` test (0x89FCEE); when it falls below 1 IsInvasionOver answers true.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: land_force_flag
fields.comment: The trailing byte of the land-force CList at +0x54; zeroed by the constructor at 0x89F943 and by every node append. Same shape as the other two lists' +0x70 and +0x80.

fields.name: transports_first
fields.comment: Head of a second CList (last +0x68, count +0x6C, trailing byte +0x70). **The transports**: PickLandingSite requires `SumTransportWeight(&+0x64) >= SumTransportWeight(&+0x54)` (0x89FD00 against 0x89FD0A) before it will consider the force able to take more, and IsInvasionOver asks `[+0x64]->data->+0xB0` (a COrder*) for save token 0x3A5, `invasion`. Appended to at 0x8A182B/0x8A1841.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: transports_last
fields.comment: Tail of the naval CList whose head is +0x64; count +0x6C, trailing byte +0x70. Appended to at 0x8A182B/0x8A1841, inside AddUnit, on the branch taken when CUnit slot 16 (IsNaval, per project.json) answers true.

fields.name: transports_count
fields.comment: Count of the transport CList at +0x64. IsInvasionOver answers true below 1, and takes its CNavalInvasionOrder branch at exactly 1.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: transports_flag
fields.comment: Trailing byte of the naval CList at +0x64.

fields.name: units_first
fields.comment: Head of the CList of every unit committed to the invasion (last +0x78, count +0x7C, trailing byte +0x80). This is the list slot 63 (AddUnit) appends to and slot 62 returns `lea eax,[ecx+0x74]`.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: air_units_last
fields.comment: Tail of the CList whose head is +0x74 and count +0x7C. **+0x74 is the AIR list, not 'every unit committed'**: AddUnit reaches it only on the branch where CUnit slot 17 answers true, and project.json records CUnit slot 17 as IsAir. The three lists are a disjoint partition of the committed units by domain - air to +0x74, land to +0x54, naval to +0x64 - and AddUnit returns false for a unit that is none of the three. project.json's existing name `units_first` on +0x74 and `CAIInvasion::GetUnits` on 0x49F910 (slot 62) are therefore too wide; reported, not changed.

fields.name: air_units_count
fields.comment: Count of the air CList at +0x74; incremented at 0x8A170B.

fields.name: air_units_flag
fields.comment: Trailing byte of the air CList at +0x74.

fields.name: staging_province
fields.comment: Where the invasion sails from, handed to the constructor by the invasion planner. A CProvince on two readings: PickLandingSite compares `[+0x84] + 0x2B4` against a COwnerArea* (CProvince +0x2B4 is `area`) at 0x89FDBD, and passes `[+0x84] + 0xD0` (CProvince::id) as a distance argument.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: landing_province
fields.comment: **Where it lands.** Null at construction; written only by PickLandingSite at 0x8A0176, the winner of its minimising search. Slot 73 re-runs that search whenever `0x4EF7C0(country, &this->+0x88->controller, 1)` stops holding, and sets `finished` when nothing qualifies. A CProvince because `+0x88 + 0x334` is handed to a function that takes a CCountryTag* and CProvince +0x334 is `controller`.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: owner_ai
fields.comment: The owning CEU3AI, the constructor's third argument. Note that CAIAgent keeps the owner at +0x54 for the ministers and CAIUnit at +0x60; CAIInvasion is a third place, so the luabind getter GetOwnerAI (0x8E90A0, `mov eax,[ecx+0x54]`) answers null on one of these too. Slot 70 passes it to 0x897B40.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: landing_province_id
fields.comment: The landing province's id, written beside +0x88 from `province->+0xD0` at 0x8A0186. Also compared and rewritten at 0x8A04F1/0x8A04FF/0x8A05B1 and 0x8A1017/0x8A1040 inside the three unread stage functions.
fields.source: agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion

fields.name: first_id
fields.comment: Id half of the CRelation base's `first` CCountryTag at +0x8 - the save block's `first="HON"`. FindMatchingTradeRoute (0xA4A750) compares +0xC and +0x14 between two routes before it will compare their goods, which is the pair identity; and the same 8-byte-apart tag/id shape is already recorded at +0x24/+0x28 and +0x2C/+0x30 for `from` and `to`. Placed by shape and by that use, not by a store, hence `likely`.

fields.name: second_id
fields.comment: Id half of the CRelation base's `second` CCountryTag at +0x10 - the save block's `second="POL"`. Same evidence as +0xC.

fields.name: from
fields.comment: The selling side, save key `from` (token 0x34F). Eight bytes: the three letters at +0x24 and the id at +0x28, both initialised to "---"/0 by the constructor at 0x64C400. CTradeRoute is anchored by RTTI - vftable 0x15FBD48, 12 slots, base CRelation - with its loader at 0x64CBA0 and its constructor writing the vftable at 0x64C3FA (also 0x64C56C and 0x64C6D8). fieldmap places this key here directly.

fields.name: from_id
fields.comment: The country id half of `from`.

fields.name: to
fields.comment: The buying side, save key `to` (token 0x350); id at +0x30. Placed by fieldmap out of CTradeRoute::LoadKey (0x64CBA0), whose whole grammar is five keys: `from`, `to`, `convoy`, `trade_from`, `trade_to`. The base CRelation adds `first`, `second` and `start_date`, all of which a real savegame's `trade={...}` block carries beside these.

fields.name: to_id
fields.comment: The country id half of `to`.

fields.name: trade_from
fields.comment:
**Inferred, not proven.** A three-dword block the constructor zeroes at 0x64C40C, in the slot where the save's `trade_from` - seven fixed-point values, what the `from` side hands over each day - must live. The loader's handler for the key passes its destination in a register so fieldmap records nothing, and the writer was not read. Treat the name as a placement and the type as unknown: three dwords is the shape of a vector header, not of seven values, so either this is a `std::vector<CFixedPoint>` of seven or the values sit elsewhere.

**Two readings disagree about the direction, and both are inference.** This name came from the order of the keys in `CTradeRoute::LoadKey`. On 2026-10-01 the survivors survey read it the other way round - i.e. this field is what 0x44 is called here - from two places: `CEU3AI::IsTradeingAwayNeededResource` takes the goods the `from` side gives away out of +0x44 (at 0x89B4A9, on the branch where `route->+0x28 == ai->+0x24`), and `CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance` hands Lua +0x44 as `voTradedFrom` and +0x34 as `voTradedTo`. **Not swapped here, because replacing one inference with another is not progress.** The decisive check is live and cheap: a savegame's `trade={...}` block names `trade_from` and `trade_to` in plain text, so one dumpStruct.py against a live CTradeRoute whose save entry is known settles it.

**The shape is settled**, though: this is a vector header whose first dword points at exactly seven four-byte values, one per goods category, in thousandths - which answers the "three dwords is the wrong shape" doubt in FINDINGS-convoys.md.

fields.name: trade_to
fields.comment:
**Inferred, not proven**, on the same evidence as +0x34: the second of two identical three-dword blocks the constructor zeroes (0x64C414), matching the save's second goods block `trade_to`. The constructor also leaves +0x40 and +0x50 unaccounted for, which is the reason not to trust the shape.

**Two readings disagree about the direction, and both are inference.** This name came from the order of the keys in `CTradeRoute::LoadKey`. On 2026-10-01 the survivors survey read it the other way round - i.e. this field is what 0x34 is called here - from two places: `CEU3AI::IsTradeingAwayNeededResource` takes the goods the `from` side gives away out of +0x44 (at 0x89B4A9, on the branch where `route->+0x28 == ai->+0x24`), and `CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance` hands Lua +0x44 as `voTradedFrom` and +0x34 as `voTradedTo`. **Not swapped here, because replacing one inference with another is not progress.** The decisive check is live and cheap: a savegame's `trade={...}` block names `trade_from` and `trade_to` in plain text, so one dumpStruct.py against a live CTradeRoute whose save entry is known settles it.

**The shape is settled**, though: this is a vector header whose first dword points at exactly seven four-byte values, one per goods category, in thousandths - which answers the "three dwords is the wrong shape" doubt in FINDINGS-convoys.md.

fields.name: disabled
fields.comment: A byte flag, and **the only field that decides whether a route counts for CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource**: that function walks the pair's routes at CDiplomacyStatus +0x60 and skips every one whose +0x54 is zero (`cmp byte [edx+0x54], 0; je` at 0x89B425), so the routes it compares against are the ones with the flag set. The name is the registered function's own word for them and is therefore `likely`, not read from a writer - no writer was looked for. FINDINGS-convoys.md lists +0x50 as unaccounted for by the constructor, which is the neighbourhood this sits in. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

fields.name: convoy_responsible
fields.comment: A CCountryTag by value, letters here and the id at +0x5C. CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes writes it at all three points where it marks the route inactive - 0x4FEFF3/0x4FF006, 0x4FF8C1 and 0x4FFAD1 - and the value it writes is exactly the expression CTradeRoute::GetConvoyResponsible (0xA4D6A0) computes: the `to` tag when the `to` block's money entry is non-zero, otherwise the `from` tag. So it records which side owed the convoy at the moment the route failed. `likely` because no reader was identified; a +0x58 read is a disp8 and the scan used here cannot see one.

fields.name: convoy_responsible_id
fields.comment: Id half of the CCountryTag at +0x58; written in the same instruction pair at each of the three sites (e.g. `mov [ebx+0x5c], ecx; mov [ebx+0x58], eax` at 0x4FEFF3/0x4FF006).

fields.name: last_inactive
fields.comment: A CEU3Date in ticks (hours). CTradeRoute::GetLastInactive (0x887F80) is nothing but `*out = this->+0x84`, and that accessor's luabind name is the game's. TradeRouteSetInactive (0xA4D550) is its only writer: it stamps gameState->tick (+0xBDC) when the route goes inactive, but only if the field is still g_NullDate or more than 0x228 = 552 hours = 23 days have passed, so the stamp is deliberately sticky. CEU3AI::HasTradeGoneStale calls a route stale once `last_inactive + 0x150` (336 hours = 14 days) is past.

fields.name: provinces_first
fields.comment: Head of the area's province list, next at +0x8 on each node. Walked by CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres at 0x8A9CFA to seed the per-area leftover list, by CountEnemyUnitsInArea, and by CAIInvasion stage 3 at 0x8A10A0. The first node's data is also used as the area's representative province, whose controller stands for the area's: PickEmbarkationPort reads area->+0x24->data->+0x334/+0x338 at 0x89FF5C.

fields.name: provinces_count
fields.comment: How many provinces the area holds. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres tests it for zero before doing any work on an area (0x8A9CD3) and compares it against the leftover count at 0x8AAAD9 to decide whether anything has claimed part of the area yet; stage 3 of CAIInvasion uses it as `provinces x 10` at 0x8A1086.

fields.name: neighbour_areas_first
fields.comment: Head of the list of adjacent areas, nodes 0x10 bytes with next at +0x8. CAIInvasion stage 1 walks it at 0x8A0407 looking for a friendly neighbour with a port, and UnitCanReachObjectiveOverland walks it at 0x8A126A looking for an enemy-controlled neighbour.

fields.name: unknown_3c
fields.comment: Tested for zero by `CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed` at 0x4B9042: non-zero skips the two clamps that otherwise cut the region's division need to 1 when it holds fewer than 3 provinces and to 2 when it holds fewer than 15.

fields.name: ports_first
fields.comment: Head of the list of the area's provinces that have a naval base; count at +0x50. CAIInvasion stage 1 walks it at 0x8A0377 to find the nearest reachable port for a land unit, and CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion walks it at 0x892C87 to pick the invasion's objective port, reading NavalBaseCapacity off a member at 0x8930AD.

fields.name: ports_count
fields.comment: Count of the port list at +0x48. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion tests it for zero at 0x892C67 and falls back to CEU3AI::PickInvasionLandingProvince when the area has no port.

fields.name: region_group
fields.comment: A pointer to a group object several COwnerArea share. `CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed` reads it at 0x4B90B4, hands it to 0x803F0 in eax and gives up unless that answers more than 1; it then walks `CAIUnit +0x338` and recurses only into a region whose own +0x6C **equals** this one's (0x4B90E7 against 0x4B90F1). So the group is what bounds the recursion.

fields.name: fronts_first
fields.comment: Head of the area's CAreaBorder list; CollectAreaFrontsForCountry (0x47DA40) walks it at 0x47DA8A and reads node->data->+0xC. This is where CTheatre's own fronts list (+0x50) ultimately comes from.

fields.name: trade_route
fields.comment: **The CTradeRoute the action proposes, embedded rather than pointed at.** CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance passes `this + 0x28` as the `const CTradeRoute&` argument of CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource (0xA38B60-0xA38B64), and reads the route's two goods blocks through the action instead, at this+0x5C and this+0x6C - which are exactly 0x28 + 0x34 and 0x28 + 0x44, the route's two blocks. That double fit is the evidence; it also means CTradeAction's luabind `const CTradeRoute& GetTradeRoute() const` hands out an interior reference. See reversing/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

fields.name: provinces_begin
fields.comment: Begin of the front's std::vector<CMapProvince*>, end at +0xC. CAreaBorder::LoadKey (0x47C630) hands &this[+8] to the province-list reader for save token 0x1DC `provinces` at 0x47C6D6, which is why fieldmap.py reports that key as unplaced. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres sizes it as ([+0xC]-[+0x8])>>2 at 0x8A9DB8 and walks it.

fields.name: provinces_end
fields.comment: End of the province vector at +0x8.

fields.name: local_enemy
fields.comment: The front's enemy, chars here and id at +0x20; save token 0x621 `local_enemy`, stored by CAreaBorder::LoadKey at 0x47C824/0x47C82A. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres tests it against REB at 0x8A9D5A, passes it to 0x8A9390, and uses the id half as the controller a neighbouring province must have for the front's land-mass measurement to count it.

fields.name: front
fields.comment: Save token 0x396 `front`: CAreaBorder::LoadKey calls ParseBool(&this[+0x28]) at 0x47C67C-0x47C680. CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres copies it straight into the new theatre's CTheatre +0x70 (`hot`) at 0x8AA209-0x8AA20C, so **a theatre is `hot` exactly when the front it was built from declared `front = yes`** - and the four hardcoded-province theatres set +0x70 = 0 explicitly (0x8AA4D5, 0x8AA6C1, 0x8AA899, 0x8AAA7B).

fields.name: active
fields.comment: The command's `active` key, which FINDINGS-fieldmap.md lists as the one of its four keys it could not place. Read at 0x553C4D in Execute: set adds the objective, clear removes it. The other three are already placed - `country` at +0x3C/+0x40, `requester` at +0x44/+0x48 and `province` at +0x4C.

fields.name: index
fields.comment: The group's own index in the law database's law-group vector (`GetLawDataBase() +0x28`), and the subscript into `CCountry +0x628 laws`. Read as that subscript in three places: CChangeLawCommand::Execute at 0x54EF8B, CCountry::LoadKey's default arm at 0x4CF39E, and the law accessor at rva 0xF0510. The parallel field on CGovernmentPosition is +0x4C, which project.json already records - the two commands use the same save key `position` for two different classes, which is what made `+0x618` and `+0x628` look interchangeable.

fields.name: key_token
fields.comment: The group's own name as a save token. CCountry::SaveContents loads it at 0x4D1185 and passes it straight to the key writer at 0x4D118C, so a country's laws are saved as `<law group name> = <law name>` - which is exactly the shape a history file uses, and it is why CCountry::LoadKey has no `law` key: the default arm resolves the key text as a law group through the database's name map at 0x4CF344.

fields.name: name_token
fields.comment: The law's own name as a save token: CCountry::SaveContents loads it at 0x4D1188 and writes it as the value of the law-group key through 0x461360. CLaw derives from CModifier and has 17 vftable slots; slot 16 is the one the save loop asks before writing anything, and CNullLaw overrides the same 17, so an unset law group writes nothing.

fields.name: last_command_date
fields.comment: When the action was last put on the wire, in hours on the tick scale - the save's own key name (token 0x3EC), loaded through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E806. **Two independent writers, both setting it to the current tick**: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand stamps it just before wrapping the action in a command (0xA0E92D) and CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction stamps it again as the action is enqueued (0x4E62EB). That is what makes it later than `date` for an offer that has travelled: in the save corpus it differs from `date` in 34 of 56 blocks and is never earlier.

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the offer was made, in **hours** on the same scale as g_CCurrentGameState's tick (+0xBDC), counted from the 43,800,000-hour epoch. Loaded from the save key `date` (token 0x1F8) through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E70A, written by every Lua `Create` factory from the current tick, and set to the epoch itself - the engine's null date, [0x170C2B8] - by the null action's constructor. CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's only use of it is `date + 0xA8`, seven days, handed to CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed.

fields.name: recipient
fields.comment: The country being offered to, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the tag at +0x10 and the id at +0x14. Loaded from the save key `recipient` (token 0x2EA) at 0xA0E86A/0xA0E874. The base's slot 14, `IsSelectable` (0xA0EAE0), is three instructions: `return actor_id != recipient_id` - so the family's default selectability test is just "these are two different countries".

fields.name: actor
fields.comment: The country making the offer, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x8 and the country id at +0xC. Loaded from the save key `actor` (token 0x2E9) at 0xA0E7B5/0xA0E7BB, where CCountryDataBase::GetTag's result is copied as two dwords. CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor fills it with "---" and id 0. Every reader that wants the CCountry indexes `g_CCountryDataBase::countries_first` with +0xC: CTradeAction::IsValid, CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute and the base's slot 14 all do.

fields.name: persistent_id
fields.comment: Always 0x18D. Written by CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor (0xA0EB30), by each of the eleven Lua `Create` factories (e.g. 0x8E84A9) and copied by every slot-16 clone, so every action in the family carries it. **It is not a per-class discriminator**: CCommand +0x4 is recorded as "a class id" and holds the same 0x18D, and the kind of action is carried by slot 15's save token instead. What reads it was not traced; token 0x18D resolves to `none`.

fields.name: type
fields.comment: The action's `CDiplomaticAction::EType`, and the **stage** an offer is at rather than what kind of offer it is: the kind is the C++ subclass, and its name is slot 15's save token. `CDiplomaticAction::GetType` is registered to Lua and resolves to a two-instruction `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret` at 0x416000. The enum has **three** values, all registered in one luabind chain ending at 0x8ED397: ('PROPOSE', ebx) at 0x8ED38D with ebx zeroed at 0x8EAE68 and never rewritten, ('DECLINE', 1) at 0x8ED37F, and **('ACCEPT', 2) at 0x8ED3BB**, appended to the same value vector at 0x8ED3C9 and registered by the loop at 0x8ED3CE. So 0 = PROPOSE, 1 = DECLINE, 2 = ACCEPT. What acts on it: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute enqueues a PROPOSE on the recipient and anything else on the actor; the hourly AI pass at 0x682BA8 only touches entries still at PROPOSE and writes 2 into the field at 0x682BB3 to accept them. The body at 0x416000 has two references and so is **not** recorded under a class name (trap 4); the field is.

fields.name: value
fields.comment: A bool, exposed to Lua as GetValue/SetValue: CDiplomaticAction::SetValue (0xA0E980, one reference, no vftable) is `this->+0x24 = [ebp+8]` and the getter is the folded `mov al,[ecx+0x24]` at 0xA0E990. **CTradeAction::IsValid (slot 13, 0xA38770) branches on it at 0xA387DA**: set, and it validates a fresh trade offer; clear, and it instead requires that an identical route already exist on the pair. So `value` is the proposal/cancellation polarity a script controls. **Units: none - it is a bool, not thousandths.** In the save it is written `value=yes` / `value=no`, 39 yes and 6 no over the 45 saves on this machine, which is also how the `value` loader case reads it: ParseBool (rva 0x67B410) at 0xA0E6E6, not a number. Seven of the family also use it as their slot-18 answer, through the folded `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x24], 0; setne al; ret` at 0xA0FE10 and the recorded ReturnByteAt24 at 0xA0E990.

structs.name: GuiTooltipText
structs.comment: The interface's shared tooltip-result record, 0x59 bytes used of 0x5C allocated: three Hoi3CStrings at +0, +0x1C and +0x38, an int at +0x54 and a byte at +0x58. Its three compiler-generated members are at rva 0xC500 (destructor), 0xC560 (copy constructor) and 0x128B0 (assignment), and the copy constructor names every field exactly once, which is what established the layout. **The name is ours, not the game's** - the type has no vftable and no Lua registration, so there is nothing to read a real name off, and agent A's GUI-framework work may yet supply one. A builder constructs the record itself, so a caller supplies raw stack space and calls the destructor afterwards; BiceLib has to follow that discipline or it leaks or double-frees. 114 callers of the destructor is what shows this is the interface's standard tooltip return rather than one panel's local struct. See reversing/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md.

fields.name: text
fields.comment: The line or lines the tooltip shows. **The only slot the builders read here ever fill**; CAlignment::BuildDriftTooltip appends its whole finished text into it at 0x4FBB6E and leaves the other two empty.

fields.name: second
fields.comment: A second string, emptied by every constructor and filled by none of the builders read for FINDINGS-uinumbers.md. The localisation table's XXX / XXX_DELAYED pairs (DIP_HIGHEST_THREAT_TOOLTIP, ESP_NUM_SPIES) make 'the delayed text' a plausible reading, but it is a guess, not a finding.

fields.name: third
fields.comment: A third string, same status as +0x1C. The three are 0x1C apart, which is Hoi3CString's size, and all three are named once each by the copy constructor at 0xC560.

fields.name: number
fields.comment: Initialised to 0 by every producer (`xor eax,eax; mov [out+0x54],eax` at 0x4FA0FE in CAlignment::BuildDriftTooltip, and the equivalent at 0x40D47D and 0x78529F). Copied by both the copy constructor and operator=. Its meaning is not established.

fields.name: flag
fields.comment: Initialised to **1** by every producer, which is what makes `mov byte ptr [reg+0x58], 1` the signature instruction for this type - 86 sites in .text, and they land in exactly the functions the localisation-key sweep ranked highest. Its meaning is not established; 'show this tooltip' is the obvious guess and is only a guess. The struct is 0x59 bytes used and 0x5C allocated.

fields.name: fonts_by_name
fields.comment: The `fonts` registry: a 511-bucket chained hash keyed by the element's own `std::string` at +8, read by StringHashFind (rva 0x5C7D60) and filled by CEU3Graphics::LoadKey's `fonts` case (token 28) at 0xA70F30, which hands it `this+0x84` where `this` is the CPersistent subobject at CGraphics+4. One of five sibling registries initialised together in the CGraphics constructor (rva 0x66DAB0) and torn down together at 0xA6F5E0.

fields.name: bitmapfonts_by_name
fields.comment: The `bitmapfonts` registry, filled by CEU3Graphics::LoadKey's token 335 case at 0xA71160 (`this+0x90`, this being CGraphics+4). `interface/*.gfx` declares 61 `bitmapfont = { }` entries. Same 511-bucket shape as the other four.

fields.name: sprite_types_by_name
fields.comment: **The `spriteTypes` registry** - the big one, 6,881 entries in the mod's `interface/*.gfx` - filled by CEU3Graphics::LoadKey's token 52 case at 0xA70F05 (`this+0x9C`, this being CGraphics+4). StringHashFind's busiest consumer at 70 of its 206 call sites, and scratchpad/gui/names.py recovers only `GFX_*` literals at them (`GFX_topbar_bg`, `GFX_terrainimg_plains`, `GFX_no_ship_selected`, `GFX_empty_position`, `GFX_counter_`, ...), which is exactly what `spriteType = { name = "GFX_..." }` declares. Elements are CSpriteType / C2dObjectType subclasses, keyed by `name` at +8.

fields.name: light_types_by_name
fields.comment: The `lightTypes` registry, filled by CEU3Graphics::LoadKey's token 82 case at 0xA7118B (`this+0xA8`, this being CGraphics+4). Only one `lightTypes = { }` block exists across the mod's `.gfx` files.

fields.name: screen_width
fields.comment: The screen width in pixels. **Confirmed live: reads 1920 beside +0x6B9C0's 1080**, which also independently confirms the existing screen_height name on its neighbour. FINDINGS-gui.md section 9 item 4 carried this as inference from a neighbour with no reader located; it is now a reading. Written by the CGraphics constructor at 0xA6DD33 / 0xA6DD3C. `fullScreen = yes` on a windowType makes the loader overwrite the CWindowType's declared size with this pair - topbar declares 2048x100 and its live type reads 1920x1080.

fields.name: screen_height
fields.comment: The screen height in pixels. `CInGameIdler::Enter` reads it at 0x65A48E and computes `(height - unitlist_start.y) / unitlist_offset.y - 1` into `CInGameIdler +0x1DF8` - how many unit rows fit on screen - and `interface/unitpanel.gui` declares those two positionTypes with y = 144 and y = 40, which is what makes it a height rather than a width. `likely`: no writer was located, so this rests on the arithmetic.

fields.name: object_types_by_name
fields.comment: **The `objectTypes` registry: every named map/3D object type, and the table the combat_status lookup runs against.** `{int count; unsigned bucketCount = 511; Node** buckets;}` at +0/+4/+8, initialised at 0xA6DE9F..0xA6DED1 in the CGraphics constructor. Read by StringHashFind (rva 0x5C7D60) at 51 sites and written by StringHashInsert (rva 0x142D80) from CEU3Graphics::LoadKey's `objectTypes` case (token 54) at 0xA70FB2 - which passes `(CGraphics+4) + 0x6BCEC`, i.e. this address, and reading that 0x6BCEC as the base would put every field here four bytes out. Elements are CObjectType subclasses (CBillboardType, CCounterType, CFlagType, CProjectionType, CProvinceType, CSpriteType, ...) keyed by `name` at +8; an element whose own slot 15 answers false never reaches the table and logs `Failed to load 3d object type = <name>` from graphics.cpp:1258. scratchpad/gui/names.py recovers the literals looked up here and every one that resolves is declared inside an `objectTypes = { }` block in `interface/mapitems.gfx`, `arrows.gfx`, `battlearrow.gfx` or `core.gfx` - `combat_status`, `combat_status_close`, `counter_arrow`, `unit_counter`, `capital`, `allied_objective`, `moveArrow`, `MessageMapText` and the rest.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: The type's name, and **the key the `objectTypes` registry at `CGraphics +0x6BCF0` is hashed on**: both StringHashFind (rva 0x5C7D60) and StringHashInsert (rva 0x142D80) read the stored object's string at `value+8` rather than copying anything into the table. `CObjectType : CPersistent`, so +0 is the vftable. Its sibling hierarchy puts the same thing at the same offset - `CGuiType +8` is written by CGuiType::LoadKey's `name` case at 0xAC8776.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: The gui element's name, as declared by `name = "..."` inside any `guiTypes` entry in an `interface/*.gui` file. Written by CGuiType::LoadKey (rva 0x6C8710) key 26: `add edi, 8; call ParseString`. It is also the key the ternary search tree at `CGui +0x38` is built on, though the tree holds the characters itself so a lookup never reads this field.

fields.name: down_sound
fields.comment: `downsound = "..."` from the .gui file - the sound played when the window is lowered or closed. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 321 case at 0xAC6A17 through ParseString. Exactly 0x1C above up_sound, so the two strings are adjacent and +0x288 + 0x1C = +0x2A4, which is the whole size of the class.

fields.name: up_sound
fields.comment: `upsound = "..."` from the .gui file - the sound played when the window is raised. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 320 case at 0xAC64F8 through ParseString; that case is reached by the `je` on `cmp eax, 0x140` in the dispatch head, not through either byte table.

fields.name: declared_children_head
fields.comment:
Head of the list of **every** declared child's name, across all thirteen kinds, in the order the .gui file declares them - the fourteenth container, and the one FINDINGS-guistatic.md was reaching for when it counted fourteen at a 0x10 stride from +0x174. Tail at +0x260, count at +0x264.

Every per-kind case of CWindowType::LoadKey appends to its own list and then jumps to one shared tail at 0xAC58B5, which appends the same name here. The window factory passes `&this+0x25C` as the CFixedWindow constructor's 6th-from-last argument, and the constructor's ordered resolve loop at 0xAC0DF0..0xAC10A3 walks *this* list - which is why the loop can put the window's children into its two intrusive lists in declaration order across kinds.

fields.name: orientation
fields.comment: `orientation = "..."` from the .gui file, stored not as a string but as whatever 0xB29CC0 makes of one - CWindowType::LoadKey's token 191 case parses the keyword into a temporary string, hands it to 0xB29CC0 and stores the returned pointer here. The window factory passes it to the CFixedWindow constructor's 8th argument, which the constructor stores and later compares against 1 and 3 while adjusting the window's position.

fields.name: click_to_front
fields.comment: `click_to_front = yes/no` from the .gui file - whether clicking the window raises it. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 420 case at 0xAC6539 through ParseBool. The window factory reads it with `movzx ecx, byte ptr [esi+0x255]` and hands it to the CFixedWindow constructor as its 26th and last stack argument, which the constructor tests at 0xAC01EC.

fields.name: full_screen
fields.comment: `fullScreen = yes/no` from the .gui file. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 47 case at 0xAC6487 through ParseBool. Sits immediately after the last per-kind container's byte at +0x250 and immediately before click_to_front, and the CWindowType constructor zeroes the two as one word (`mov word ptr [esi+0x254], bx`).

fields.name: overlapping_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `OverlappingElementsBoxType` children - the thirteenth and last of the per-kind lists, so the 0x10 stride ends here, with the tail at +0x248, the count at +0x24C and the byte at +0x250. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x2DC / +0x2EC, project.json's `child_overlapping_boxes_begin`.

fields.name: three_d_gui_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `threeDguiType` children. Twelfth of the thirteen.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's second `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the window's +0x474 name list, which project.json already calls `three_d_gui_names`, and that list feeds the registry at window +0x3F0 - project.json's `registry_unused_2`. So registry 5 is the `threeDguiType` index, read off the keyword rather than inferred from its being the only non-button of the three unused kinds.

Its LoadKey case is the odd one of the thirteen: it appends to this list **and** writes the window type's own +0x84/+0x88/+0x90/+0x94 before joining the shared tail, which the other twelve do not.

fields.name: list_box_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `listBoxType` children. Eleventh of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x454 name list, whose registry is window +0x3A8.

**The token table spells the keyword `listBoxType`, with a capital B.** The data mostly does not: a case-sensitive grep finds `listboxType` in 36 of the game's .gui files and 55 of the mod's against `listBoxType` in 3 and 5, and live windows do hold list boxes, so the .gui key lookup cannot be case-sensitive. The engine's own spelling is the one in the table.

fields.name: child_window_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's **`windowType`** children - the tenth of the thirteen, and the one that answers FINDINGS-guistatic.md's open item 5.

Its children are themselves CWindowTypes: LoadKey's `windowType` case does `operator new(0x2A4)` and calls CWindowType::CWindowType, so the type tree is recursive. The CFixedWindow constructor is handed `&this+0x214` as its 11th stack argument and walks it at 0xAC0C33..0xAC0C90, building a full CFixedWindow per name through CWindowType::CreateWindow and adding each one to the window's **subwindow map at +0x414**.

So the chain `windowType` keyword -> CWindowType +0x214 -> CFixedWindow +0x414 is complete, and **CFixedWindow +0x2FC is not on it**. +0x2FC is written only by CFixedWindow::AttachChild (slot 22) and erased only by slot 23, so it holds what game code attaches at run time, which is why a live snapshot found buttons and icons in it.

fields.name: checkbox_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `checkboxType` children. Ninth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x31C / +0x32C, project.json's `child_checkboxes_begin`.

Its child type is built with the same 0xB2DA90 constructor as `guiButtonType` and `multiSpriteButtonType` - a checkbox type *is* a button type - which is why FINDINGS-guistatic.md could get as far as 'the third user of the button type class' and no further.

fields.name: icon_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `iconType` children. Eighth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x29C / +0x2AC, project.json's `child_icons_begin`.

fields.name: edit_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `editBoxType` children. Seventh of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x444 name list, whose registry is window +0x384.

fields.name: scrollbar_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `scrollbarType` children. Sixth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x464 name list, whose registry is window +0x3CC.

fields.name: instant_text_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `instantTextBoxType` children. Fifth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x2BC / +0x2CC.

fields.name: text_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `textBoxType` children. Fourth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x424 name list, whose registry is window +0x33C.

fields.name: three_d_button_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `3dButtonType` children. Third of the thirteen.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's first `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the window's name list at +0x434, which project.json already calls `three_d_button_names`, and that list is the source for the registry at window +0x360 - project.json's `registry_unused`. So registry 1 is the `3dButtonType` index, read off the keyword rather than inferred from the widget's base class and its CGraphics objectTypes lookup.

fields.name: multi_sprite_button_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `multiSpriteButtonType` children. Second of the thirteen; same {head, tail, count, byte} shape as +0x184.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's third `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the vector pair at window +0x27C / +0x28C, which project.json currently calls `child_vector_unused` - so that vector is the `multiSpriteButtonType` children's, and it is empty on every live window because the keyword occurs in no .gui file the game or the mod ships, not because its purpose was unknown.

fields.name: gui_button_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `guiButtonType` children - the first of **thirteen** per-kind lists at a 0x10 stride from +0x184 to +0x244, each {head, tail, count, byte} with the tail at +4 and the count at +8.

The nodes are 0x28 bytes: the child's name as an Hoi3CString at +0, prev at +0x1C, next at +0x20, a byte at +0x24. **The list holds names, not objects** - each child type built by LoadKey is inserted into the one gui-type tree at CWindowType +0x150 and only its name is listed here, which is why CFixedWindow::CreateWindow and the six per-kind factories all look a name up in that tree.

The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list, node by node through 0x409D00, into the window's own +0x25C/+0x26C vector pair: so **CFixedWindow +0x25C holds exactly the window's `guiButtonType` children**, which settles what project.json's `child_buttons_begin` is a vector of.

*FINDINGS-guistatic.md said fourteen containers running from +0x174; that is wrong twice. There are thirteen and they start at +0x184. +0x174 is a separate three-pointer std::vector walked at a 4-byte stride, and the fourteenth participant is the all-kinds declaration-order list at +0x25C.*

fields.name: moveable
fields.comment: `moveable = N` from the .gui file - whether the player can drag the window. An **int**, not a bool: LoadKey's token 154 case uses ParseInt (0x67B470, already recorded), not ParseBool. The window factory reads only its low word, `movzx edx, word ptr [esi+0x128]` at 0xAC508A, and hands that to the CFixedWindow constructor's 16th argument - so what +0x12A/+0x12B carry, if anything, is not read there.

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: `priority = N` from the .gui file - the window's draw and hit-test order. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 138 case at 0xAC5676, through 0x67B640, which is a parse helper not yet recorded (it is not ParseInt; it goes through 0xB964D4 with the format string at 0x15FD134).

fields.name: vertical_border
fields.comment: `verticalBorder = "..."` - the sprite used along the window's vertical edges. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 164 case at 0xAC5766 through ParseString.

fields.name: horizontal_border
fields.comment: `horizontalBorder = "..."` - the sprite used along the window's horizontal edges. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 163 case at 0xAC5742 through ParseString.

fields.name: horizontal_scrollbar
fields.comment: `horizontalScrollbar = "..."` - the name of the scrollbar child that scrolls this window horizontally. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 159 case at 0xAC56DC through ParseString.

fields.name: vertical_scrollbar
fields.comment: `verticalScrollbar = "..."` - the name of the scrollbar child that scrolls this window vertically. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 158 case at 0xAC56B8 through ParseString.

fields.name: background
fields.comment: `background = "..."` from the .gui file - the sprite name for the window's backdrop. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 153 case at 0xAC5631 through ParseString. The window factory 0xAC4FE0 passes `&type+0x84` to the CFixedWindow constructor as its 23rd argument.

fields.name: parent
fields.comment: `parent = "..."` from the .gui file - the name of the type this one inherits from. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 132 case at 0xAC5721 through ParseString. CWindowType::CreateWindow passes it to the CGui's slot 18 when a child window's own type is not in the tree at +0x150, so it is the fallback type as well as a declared field.

fields.name: position
fields.comment: `position = { x = N y = N }` as declared in the `.gui` file, two ints. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey (rva 0x6C55E0) at 0xAC5658: `lea edi, [ebx+0xA0]; call 0xA7B670`, the `{ x = y = }` reader, with ebx the CWindowType itself (LoadKey's `this` is the CPersistent subobject, which sits at offset 0 of a CGuiType). **This offset is per-subclass, not shared by all gui types**: a `positionType`'s coordinates are read at `+0x64`/`+0x68` in CInGameIdler::Enter, and `+0x64` on a CWindowType is its CFactory base's vftable, the RTTI export giving that base at offset 100.

fields.name: size
fields.comment: `size = { x = N y = N }` from the `.gui` file, two ints, written by CWindowType::LoadKey at 0xAC5703 through the same `{ x = y = }` reader as `position`.

structs.name: CGui

fields.name: graphics
fields.comment: The CGraphics, and the same object as CInGameIdler+0x178C. Confirmed live by pointer equality with the process's only CEU3Graphics instance; the five name registries on CGraphics (+0x88 fonts, +0x94 bitmapfonts, +0xA0 spriteTypes, +0xAC lightTypes, +0x6BCF0 objectTypes) are reached through this field from the GUI side.

fields.name: gui_types
fields.comment: **The GUI type registry, and it is not a StringHashFind table.** An embedded object whose vftable 0x1602108 the CGui constructor writes at 0xA7C4E2; slot 1 is the by-name find (rva 0x6ACE70) and slot 2 the `const char*` form (rva 0x67DEE0), which walks a **case-insensitive ternary search tree** rooted at +0x38. CGui::LoadKey (rva 0x67D700) hands `this+0x30` - this being the CPersistent subobject at CGui+4, so this address - to the `guiTypes` block reader together with the CFactory base at CGui+0xC. CEU3Gui::GetGuiType (rva 0x67DBC0) is the public way in.

fields.name: gui_types_root
fields.comment: The root of the ternary search tree of gui types, zeroed by the CGui constructor at 0xA7C4E9 and tested by the registry's slot 2 (rva 0x67DEE0, `cmp [ecx+4],0` with ecx = CGui+0x34). A node is `{void* value; char key; Node* low; Node* high; Node* equal;}` at +0/+4/+8/+0xC/+0x10 and the value is the CGuiType.

fields.name: gui_types_mode
fields.comment: The mode byte of the embedded name tree at +0x34, tested by NameTree_Insert (rva 0x4D8A0): 0 selects the ternary search tree (TernarySearchTreeInsert, rva 0x4DA70), 1 selects the string-keyed node list (rva 0x4D8E0). Reads **0** live, so the gui-type registry is the ternary tree, as the lookup side already said. Container slot 3 (0xAC47B0) is the only thing that writes it a 1 and nothing in the GUI path calls it.

fields.name: gui_types_count
fields.comment: **An insert count, not an entry count.** TernarySearchTreeInsert increments it on an existing key as well as a new one, so it over-reports by the number of duplicate gui type names. Reads 1550 live while the tree holds 1547 distinct names - three duplicates in the loaded set.

fields.name: gui_objects_begin
fields.comment:
**Begin of the vector of every live gui object in the process** - the answer to FINDINGS-gui.md's open item 1. 2305 objects in a paused 1936 game, across 13 classes. Thirteen TGui slots push into it (slots 16 and 23 are the bare push_back 0xA7DC60; the other eleven look a name up in the +0x34 tree, build a widget from the type and then push); slots 19 and 30 iterate it. **It holds CGuiObject subobject pointers, not complete objects** - complete+0x18 for a CFixedWindow, complete+4 for a list box, complete+0 for an icon or button. No code that removes an element was found, and front-end widgets are still in it after CFrontEnd has been destroyed, so a held pointer should be revalidated rather than trusted.

**Open item 1 of FINDINGS-guilive.md is closed, live (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save): yes, elements are removed, and by erase-and-compact with no holes.** Measured by snapshotting the vector either side of opening and closing the production window in a running game.

Opening it took the vector from **2,415 to 4,124** entries while `widget_nulls` stayed at **0**, and **six names disappeared entirely** - `info_text`, `outliner_standard`, `outliner_combat_entry`, `outliner_unit_entry_bg`, `movment`, `outliner_top_unit_entry` (the outliner, which a full-screen window hides). `widget_end` moved by exactly 0x1AB4, i.e. 1,709 entries, matching the count delta, and `widget_begin` never moved - so the backing buffer did not reallocate but elements inside it shift when one is erased.

**The rule for the DLL, and it is a hard one: never cache a widget pointer or an index across anything that can open or close a panel.** A cached pointer to a removed widget dangles; a cached *index* is worse, because after a compaction it addresses some other live widget and returns plausible garbage instead of crashing.

**Removal is not symmetric.** Closing the window did not undo the opening: all 47 names it added were still present afterwards and the count rose again to 4,279. So some panels are torn down on hide and others are built once and kept, and the vector grows monotonically as a session visits panels - which is what the 64,000-slot preallocation is budgeted for (4,339 in use after three cycles).
fields.source: reversing/FINDINGS-guilive.md; live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save; reversing/FINDINGS-guilive.md

fields.name: gui_objects_end
