fields.comment: End of the live gui object vector at +0x5C. (end - begin) / 4 is the object count.

fields.name: gui_objects_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the live gui object vector at +0x5C.

structs.comment:
**A reproducible widget leak, measured %s.** Every open-and-close of a full-screen window (tested with production) leaves **30 widgets behind permanently**: ten each of `outliner_header`, `outliner_header_entry` and `entry_text`. Counts across a baseline and three cycles: 10 -> 10 -> 20 -> 40 for the two header names, 39 -> 10 -> 49 -> 69 for `entry_text`, and the vector total 2,415 -> 4,124 -> 4,279 -> 4,339, whose +60 over the last two cycles is exactly 3 x 10 x 2. Additive, not a one-off transition.

**The mechanism is specific**: the six outliner names that *are* removed on open come back and return to their exact original counts, so those are properly destroyed and rebuilt. The outliner's **header** widgets are not destroyed on hide, and a fresh set is created on each rebuild on top of the surviving one. So this is a partial teardown, not a missing one.

**Consequences.** It is not a practical crash risk in one session - at 30 per cycle the 64,000 slots take about 2,000 cycles to exhaust - but it degrades the very path BiceLib now depends on: a name lookup over this vector gets slower, and **a name's instances multiply, so 'the widget called X' becomes ambiguous and the wrong copy may be the stale one**. If the vector ever did exceed capacity it would reallocate and move `widget_begin`, invalidating a pointer to the array itself and not merely to an element. This is engine GUI code rather than anything BlackICE does.

**And the leak is specific to that path, not systemic - second test, live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save.** Message popups were watched over the same three-snapshot method and they tear down **cleanly**. Two messages on screen added 32 widgets across 16 names; dismissing both removed **14 of those names entirely** (`DefaultPopup`, `default_popup_banner`, `AgreeButton`, `DeclineButton`, `CenterOK`, `Header`, `Line1`..`Line6`, `LeftShield`, `RightShield`, each at 2 instances while up), `Background` went 3 -> 5 -> 3, and **no pre-existing name failed to return to its original count**.

The residual was +2 (4,339 -> 4,371 -> 4,341) and it is **not a leak**: `messagelogbutton` and `logtext`, each at **one** instance rather than one per message, so they are the message-log indicator created once on first need and retained. The arithmetic closes exactly - 14x2 plus Background's 2 destroyed, those 2 kept, 32 in total.

So the widget system's create/destroy is sound, and the 30-per-cycle growth recorded above is confined to the outliner's header rebuild. **This is also a second, independent demonstration that elements really are removed from the vector** - 14 names here, 6 on the production-window test - which is what the no-caching rule rests on.

A by-product worth keeping: popups are built from a **`DefaultPopup`** window definition and cost about 16 widgets each, so that name can be looked up in `interface/*.gui` as a cross-check on the GUI loader.

fields.name: visible
fields.comment: Whether the object draws. The whole of slot 13 (Show, rva 0x660440) is `mov byte [ecx+0x29], 1`, slot 14 (Hide, rva 0x660450) writes 0, and slot 15 (rva 0x10A0) reads it.

fields.name: frame
fields.comment: **The frame index into the type's texture strip** - what the combat-status icon state really is. Written by slot 24 (SetFrame, rva 0x660460) and read by slot 25 (rva 0x660470). CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow drives it with 0, 1 or 2 from the attacker's strength share against 66% and 33%, and `interface/mapitems.gfx` gives both combat_status billboardTypes `noOfFrames = 3`.

fields.name: position
fields.comment: The object's world position as a homogeneous vector: slot 90 (SetPosition, rva 0x44AB80) copies three floats into +0x84/+0x88/+0x8C and writes 1.0f into +0x90. CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow sets it to the negated midpoint of the attacker's and defender's first units each tick.

fields.name: scene
fields.comment: Whatever owns and draws the object: slot 16 (rva 0x10B0) sets it, slot 17 (rva 0x10C0) reads it, and CCombat's destructor path hands slot 17's result to CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject (rva 0x66FBC0). The owner's class was not identified, so the name is inference from the use.

fields.name: type
fields.comment: The CObjectType the object was created from, written by the constructor (rva 0x11B0) from its second argument - which is the type, because slot 18 of a CObjectType is `new <size>` followed by this constructor with `this` as the argument.

structs.name: CBillboardObject
structs.comment: A billboard instance as produced by CBillboardType's slot-18 factory (0xB07340): 0xB48 bytes, vftable 0x16010D0, derived from C3dVisibleObject. **The name is ours** - the instance class has no RTTI entry, unlike the CBillboardType that makes it. See reversing/FINDINGS-gui.md.

fields.name: type
fields.comment: The CBillboardType, written by the constructor (rva 0x6B68F0) at 0xAB6934 - a second copy of what the C3dVisibleObject base already stored at +0xF8.

fields.name: rotation
fields.comment: The billboard's facing angle in radians, and the only thing CBillboardObject::SetRotation (slot 37, rva 0x6B6F50) does: `[this+0xB24] = -(argument + pi/2)`.

fields.name: caption
fields.comment: **The text drawn on the billboard - and for `combat_status`, the number the combat UI has already computed.** CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow builds it at 0x57C2CB with FormatFixedPoint(share * 100000 / 1000) and assigns it here through std::string::assignString at 0x57C2E4 (`mov ecx,[esi+0x2C]; add ecx,0xB2C`), where `share` is CCombat slot 17's attacker strength share in thousandths - so a share of 660 reads "66.000". Initialised by the constructor at 0xAB698F and the only `std::string` at this displacement on any of the 23 C3dVisibleObject subclasses, which is what identifies the class: 0xB2C + 0x1C is exactly the 0xB48 the factory allocates. The billboardTypes carry `font = "Arial_17_black"` and `font_size = 7` for it.

fields.name: province
fields.comment: **The province this unit base sits in, and what CUnitBase virtual slot 0 returns** - which answers the question FINDINGS-airnaval.md has been asking since 2026-09 about CUnit +0x98's class. Read live: of 542 units whose home_base_ptr (CUnit +0x98) is non-null, 542 point at a CUnitBaseProvince or a CUnitBaseCarrier by their own vftables, and on 400 of 400 sampled CUnitBaseProvince objects this field points at a CMapProvince; on 540 of those 542 units it equals the unit's own current_province (+0x130), the two exceptions being units in transit. Slot 0 is the folded getter 0x4944C0 (`mov eax,[ecx+0x20]; ret`), which the record currently names COrder::GetStance because 36 of its 37 vftable slots are COrder slot 19 - the name does not belong to this class's slot. Note CUnitBaseProvince also carries a CSelectable subobject whose vftable pointer is at +0x18.

fields.name: ship
fields.comment: **The carrier this air group is based on.** Read live: all 1851 CUnitBaseCarrier objects point at a CShip here, and that ship's +0xB0 is a CNavy on all 1851. This settles the unidentified third clause of CUnit_IsAtOwnBase (0x5CDC30), which under `if (unit->+0x98->slot1())` reads `base->+0x18->+0xB0` and rejects the unit when that object's CUnit +0x11C combats_count is positive or its +0x110 current_combat is set: the clause means **the fleet carrying this air group is not in combat**. CUnitBase slot 1 is ReturnFalse on CUnitBaseProvince and ReturnTrue on CUnitBaseCarrier, so slot 1 is IsCarrier() rather than the validity test FINDINGS-reorganise.md took it for.

fields.name: has_focus
fields.comment: **Likely the keyboard-focus flag** - recorded as inferred because the merge takes only confirmed/inferred and the real strength is 'likely'. FINDINGS-guilive.md section 4 left this open: a byte with its own getter (CGuiObject vftable slot 2, 0xA800B0, mov al,[ecx+0x44]) and setter (slot 33, 0xA800A0), reading 0 on 2,304 of 2,305 live widgets - exactly one set. The static half: CFixedWindow slot 35 (0xAC4140) writes 0 here on itself and then calls slot 33 with 0 on every child in both ordered child lists, i.e. clear-the-whole-subtree; CFixedWindow slot 34 (0xAC4080) walks the child-window list comparing each child's name (its slot 17) against a string argument, calls slot 33 with 1 on the match, recurses with slot 34 otherwise, and returns a bool. Clear-all plus set-one-by-name over a widget tree is what focus is. Not visibility - that is +0x43, one byte away (trap 12).

fields.name: type
fields.comment: **The widget's CGuiType, and the only route from a live object back to its name** - the name is the Hoi3CString at CGuiType+8. Non-null and pointing at a named type on all 2305 live gui objects, across all 13 widget classes, so it is a CGuiObject field and not a per-class one. Note that a nested child's type is nested inside its parent's windowType and so is **not** in the CGui+0x34 tree: only 286 of the 2305 objects point at a top-level type.

fields.name: gui
fields.comment: The owning CGui. Equals the process's only CEU3Gui on all 2305 live gui objects. CFixedWindow's child walk (slot 36, 0xAC1220) calls gui->vf[27](child) through it before destroying a child, and slot 27 on CEU3Gui's TGui vftable is the shared empty `ret 4` stub 0x60CD50 - which is the reason to suspect nothing is ever removed from CGui+0x5C.

fields.name: is_open
fields.comment: **Whether the widget is on screen.** CFixedWindow::Show (rva 0x6C2690) writes 1 at 0xAC26CC and CFixedWindow::Hide (rva 0x6C2270) writes 0 at 0xAC22A3. Live: 1 on 129 of 2305 objects, and the 12 windows with it set in a paused 1936 game are exactly what is drawn - topbar, menubar, outliner and three of its row windows, four alerticon_window, diplomessageicons_window, actions_list_current. **A window object existing says nothing about visibility; 194 of the 206 live windows are built and closed.** Not to be confused with +0x44, which also has a getter (slot 2) and setter (slot 33) and reads 0 on 2304 of 2305.

fields.name: subwindows_capacity_end
fields.comment:
Capacity end of the subwindow map at +0x414 - the third pointer of the vector. Read only by the insert helper 0x542FC0, which compares the end against it to decide whether to grow.

**Do not confuse it with the CGuiObject-relative +0x41C**, which is complete +0x434, `three_d_button_names`. CFixedWindow::Show and CFixedWindow::Hide both read `[esi+0x41C]` with esi as the CGuiObject subobject and that is the name list, not this field.

fields.name: subwindows_end
fields.comment: End of the subwindow map at +0x414. Every walk of the map compares its cursor against this. (end - begin) / 0x20 is the subwindow count.

fields.name: subwindows_begin
fields.comment:
**Begin of the window's subwindow map - the container that really holds the child windows the .gui file declares, and not +0x2FC.** A std::vector of 0x20-byte entries, {Hoi3CString name at +0; CFixedWindow* window at +0x1C}, used as a name-keyed map: SubWindowMap_Contains (0x6C4580) tests a key, SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd (0x6C4640) returns the value slot, SubWindowMap_Add (0x6C44F0) appends. Complete-object offset; the pointer CGui +0x5C hands you is complete+0x18, so this is +0x3FC from it.

Filled only by the CFixedWindow constructor's build loop at 0xAC0C33..0xAC0C90, which walks the name list the constructor was handed in its 11th argument - that argument is `&CWindowType +0x214`, the `windowType` keyword's declared-name list - and for each name calls CWindowType::CreateWindow (0x6C76D0) on the window's own type at +0x88 and adds the result here under that name.

The value is a **complete** CFixedWindow pointer: CFixedWindow::FindChild adds 0x18 to it to get a CGuiObject, the show and hide walks read `[entry+0x1C]` and then call CGuiObject slot 13 with `this = value + 0x18`, and CGuiObject slot 37's recursion does the same. 'Subwindow' is the engine's own word, from the warning CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow logs at fixedwindow.cpp line 1042.

+0x418 is the end and +0x41C the capacity end.

fields.name: three_d_gui_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-child-name list whose widgets the registry at +0x3F0 indexes - the sixth and last pair. The kind is threeDguiType: unlike the other five this one is not built by a 0xAC6xxx/0xAC7xxx factory at all. For each name the constructor looks the name up in the gui-type tree embedded at CWindowType +0x150, hands the result to the EXTERNAL factory 0xB45670, and inserts what comes back. **Empty on all 206 live windows because the keyword appears 0 times in both interface/ folders.**

fields.name: scrollbar_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-child-name list for the scrollbars the registry at +0x3CC indexes. Fifth of six pairs.

fields.name: list_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-child-name list for the list boxes the registry at +0x3A8 indexes. Fourth of six pairs.

fields.name: edit_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-child-name list for the edit boxes the registry at +0x384 indexes. Third of six pairs.

fields.name: three_d_button_names
fields.comment: Head of the linked list of declared child names whose widgets the registry at +0x360 indexes - the second of six (name list, registry) pairs at 0x10 and 0x24 strides respectively. Nodes are the same 0x24-byte shape as +0x424's, with the next pointer at +0x20. The kind is 3dButtonType: the constructor iterates THIS list, calls the factory 0xAC6C80 for each name and inserts the result into the registry at +0x360. **Empty on all 206 live windows because neither the mod's nor the game's own interface/ folder uses the keyword at all** - 0 occurrences of 3dButtonType against 996/392 for positionType in the same grep.

fields.name: attached_children_count
fields.comment: Number of child windows in the list at +0x74.

fields.name: attached_children_tail
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +0x74.

fields.name: attached_children_head
fields.comment: Head of the ordered list of the window's children attached through slot 22, same node shape as +0x64. Complete-object offset; +0x5C from the CGuiObject pointer CGui+0x5C hands you. Two independent writers: CFixedWindow::AddChildWindow (rva 0x6C2F90), which also pushes into the child-window vector at +0x2FC, and the constructor's resolve loop at 0xAC0F4A..0xAC0FBE, which reaches this list only on the branch that found the name in that same +0x2FC vector. NAMED FOR THE DISCRIMINATOR, NOT FOR 'window': the resolve loop reaches this list only on the branch that found the name in the vector at complete +0x2FC, and that vector is filled by nothing except slot 22 - the constructor has no build block for it at all, so a declared child window gets here because CGui's window factory calls the parent's slot 22. FINDINGS-guilive.md section 5 measured that vector live and found 46 buttons, 20 child windows and 1 icon, i.e. game code attaches non-windows through the same slot, which is why project.json's child_windows_begin on +0x2FC is a slight misnomer and why this list is not called child_windows either.

fields.name: child_elements_count
fields.comment: Number of nodes in the list at +0x64. The push tests it for zero to decide whether to write the head or the old tail's next.

fields.name: child_elements_tail
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +0x64. The push reads it to link the new node, so insertion is at the end and the list is in declaration order.

fields.name: child_elements_head
fields.comment: Head of the ordered list of every child widget EXCEPT the ones attached through slot 22 (see +0x74) - in the order the .gui file declares them, across all kinds. Complete-object offset; the pointer CGui+0x5C hands you is complete+0x18, so this is +0x4C from it, which is how FINDINGS-guilive.md refers to it. Node is 0x10 bytes, {CGuiObject* value; Node* prev; Node* next; bool}. Filled by the CFixedWindow constructor's ordered resolve loop at 0xAC0DF0..0xAC10A3, which for each declared child name searches the window's fourteen per-kind containers in a fixed order and pushes whatever it finds here - unless the name resolves in the vector at +0x2FC, which goes to +0x74 instead.

fields.name: child_buttons_begin
fields.comment: Offset from the **complete** CFixedWindow; the pointer in CGui+0x5C is complete+0x18, so this is +0x244 from there. Begin of a vector of the window's guiButtonType children (class 0x1207698) - 455 across the 206 live windows. **Not indexed by name**, unlike the four registries below: a button cannot be found by name on its parent window. End at +0x260.

fields.name: child_multi_sprite_buttons_begin
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x264 from the CGuiObject pointer. The second of seven child vectors and empty on all 206 live windows, so what it holds is not established. CFixedWindow::Hide iterates it like the others.

fields.name: child_icons_begin
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x284 from the CGuiObject pointer. Begin of a vector of the window's iconType children (CIcon, vftable 0x11FFC68) - 398 across the 206 live windows. Not name indexed.

fields.name: child_instant_text_boxes_begin
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x2A4 from the CGuiObject pointer. Begin of a vector of the window's instantTextBoxType children (class 0x11FDB70) - 473 across the 206 live windows, the biggest child collection in the game. **Not name indexed**, which matters: the instant text boxes are where a lot of panel text lives and the only way to one is a scan.

fields.name: child_overlapping_boxes_begin
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x2C4 from the CGuiObject pointer. Begin of a vector of the window's OverlappingElementsBoxType children (class 0x12013D8) - 11 across the 206 live windows.

fields.name: attached_children_begin
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x2E4 from the CGuiObject pointer. Begin of the vector that holds the window's **child windows** - 67 elements across the 206 live windows, of which 20 are windows (class 0x1202058), 46 are buttons and 1 an icon. **This is the parent-child link between windows**, not +0x4C: only 20 of the 206 live windows are children of another, the rest are top level.

fields.name: child_checkboxes_begin
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x304 from the CGuiObject pointer. Begin of a vector of the window's checkboxType children (class 0x11FDFC8) - 54 across the 206 live windows.

fields.name: text_boxes_by_name
fields.comment: **An embedded name tree keyed by child name, holding the window's textBoxType children** - the same container as CGui+0x34 (vftable 0x1202108, stride 0x24: {vftable, root, modeByte, count, ...}). Complete-object offset; **+0x324 from the CGuiObject pointer the CGui vector hands you**. 101 entries across the 206 live windows, against 102 live text box objects. **This is the one BiceLib wants**: on the topbar window it holds ic_number, manpower_number, money_number, supplies_number, fuel_number, energy_number, metal_number, raremat_number, oil_number, leadership_number, dissent_number, national_unity_number, diplomacy_number, espionage_number, datetext and countryname, and the rendered text of each is the Hoi3CString at object+0xD8. Look up with slot 1 of the container's vftable (a std::string) or slot 2, GuiTypeTree_Find (rva 0x67DEE0), with a plain const char*; the walk lowercases the query so any case works. Paired with the name list at complete+0x424.

fields.name: three_d_buttons_by_name
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x348 from the CGuiObject pointer. The second of six embedded name trees, and empty on all 206 live windows - as is its name list at complete+0x434 - so what kind it indexes is not established. CFixedWindow::Hide consults it like the others.

fields.name: edit_boxes_by_name
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x36C from the CGuiObject pointer. The embedded name tree holding the window's editBoxType children (class 0x11FED90) - all 7 live edit boxes are in it. Paired with the name list at complete+0x444.

fields.name: list_boxes_by_name
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x390 from the CGuiObject pointer. The embedded name tree holding the window's listboxType children - 78 entries across the 206 live windows against 79 live list boxes. **It stores the list box's complete-object pointer, which is its CGuiObject pointer minus 4** - established live on 78 of the 78. Paired with the name list at complete+0x454.

fields.name: scrollbars_by_name
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x3B4 from the CGuiObject pointer. The embedded name tree holding the window's scrollbarType children (class 0x11FF7A0) - 19 entries across the 206 live windows. Paired with the name list at complete+0x464. This is the registry whose arm in CFixedWindow::Hide (0xAC22E0) is the clearest worked example of the lookup.

fields.name: three_d_guis_by_name
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x3D8 from the CGuiObject pointer. The sixth embedded name tree, empty on all 206 live windows, as is its name list at complete+0x474.

fields.name: text_box_names
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x40C from the CGuiObject pointer. Head of a linked list of 0x24-byte nodes, each holding a child's name as a std::string at +0 with the next at +0x20. CFixedWindow::Show and ::Hide walk it and look each name up in the text-box registry at complete+0x33C, which is what pairs the six lists (stride 0x10 from here) with the six registries (stride 0x24 from +0x33C). 101 nodes across the 206 live windows, matching the registry exactly.

structs.name: GuiType_positionType
structs.comment: The loaded definition of a `positionType` entry in `interface/*.gui` - a named anchor point. **The name is ours**, taken from the .gui keyword: the engine creates these through CGuiType's factory and the RTTI export has no class for them. See reversing/FINDINGS-guilive.md.

fields.name: position_x
fields.comment: **Struct name deliberately ours**: the class of a `positionType` gui entry (vftable rva 0x1206B04) has no RTTI and no name anywhere in hoi3_tfh.exe, and CGuiType / CWindowType are the real names of its bases. Its declared `position` is at +0x64/+0x68 and **not** at CWindowType's +0xA0, which is the collision FINDINGS-gui.md section 4 warned about. Live: unitlist_start reads (0,144) and unitlist_offset (16,40), exactly as interface/unitpanel.gui declares, and CInGameIdler+0x1DF8 reads 22 = (1080-144)/40-1.

fields.name: position_y
fields.comment: The y of a positionType's declared position. **Struct name deliberately ours** - see +0x64.

structs.name: GuiObject_textBoxType
structs.comment: A live `textBoxType` widget - the shape that holds displayed text, and so the one the DLL reads a computed number out of. **The name is ours**, from the .gui keyword; no RTTI class exists for it. Its own name is at +0x54, its font at +0x70 and **its displayed text at +0xD8**; verified live by reading topbar's children, where ic_number, manpower_number, money_number, leadership_number, oil_number and supplies_number all gave the figures on screen. Note the text is Windows-1252 and carries the game's colour escapes, so it must go through Text::toUtf8. See reversing/FINDINGS-guilive.md.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: The widget's own copy of its name, **in the case the .gui file declared** - 'CountryName', 'DateText' - while the key in the parent window's registry is lowercased, 'countryname', 'datetext'. That is the case-insensitivity of the tree visible from both ends in one object. The offset is class specific: on the instantTextBoxType class (0x11FDB70) +0x54 is the font name, because that class keeps no name copy and everything below shifts by 0x1C. Struct name deliberately ours - see +0xD8.

structs.name: CRegion
structs.comment: A map region - the grouping `ScoreOpsAreaProvinces` scores an ops-area province by. **0x78 bytes**, measured live from the stride of 400+ instances (a uniform 0x78 gap, which is also the trap-15 check that these are real objects and not a table of vftable pointers). Reached from a province as `*(*(CProvince + 0x358))`. Named live 2026-10-02; the RTTI export carries the class. See reversing/FINDINGS-opsarea.md open item 1.

fields.name: ai_front_relevant
fields.comment:
The byte `CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces` tests to add **+100** to an ops-area province's priority, once per region of that province whose byte is set (0x4BD78F region of the body). **The name is a guess from that single reader and is marked `inferred` accordingly** - what sets it is not established. Read live 2026-10-02 as **0 on all 400+ regions** at the scenario start with the game paused at tick 0, so the +100 never fires there; whether that is because the AI has not started (no CAIUnit has a unit pointer at tick 0) or because the byte is set by war is the open question, and running the game on would answer it.

**It does get set - live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save.** Read 1 on **30 of 2,000+** live regions in a May 1942 war save, against **0 of 400** at the scenario start. So ScoreOpsAreaProvinces's +100-per-region really does fire, and the byte is something a war turns on. That is support for the `inferred` name rather than proof of it: what *sets* it is still unread. (Note the region count: an earlier reading of '400 regions' was the scan limit, not the population.)
fields.source: live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save; reversing/FINDINGS-opsarea.md; live 2026-10-02

fields.name: session
fields.comment: The CSession. CEU3Application::CEU3Application (0x22F080) builds the startup session with mode 2 at 0x22F30F and stores it here; CInGameIdler::GetSession (virtual slot 18, 0x24D800) is three instructions returning [this+0x1790]->[0x12C], and CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock tests +0x34 on the result and posts through +0x38. The class is `CSession` from the session.cpp strings its constructor 0x6887A0 carries ('NoAdress', 'InitialSession'); the field's own type is left void* because nothing here read the object's layout.

fields.name: graphics
fields.comment: The one live CEU3Graphics, named by RTTI on the live object. Sits immediately before `gui`, which is consistent with FINDINGS-gui.md having found `CGui +0x30` pointing at the same object from the other side.
fields.source: live 2026-10-02, verified against the process's only CEU3Gui

fields.name: gui
fields.comment:
The one live CEU3Gui. **The route the DLL uses to reach the GUI, verified live 2026-10-02**: `CCurrentGameState +0xBE8` (in_game_screen) -> `CInGameIdler` -> `+0x1790` -> `CEU3Application` -> `+0x120` -> the one live `CEU3Gui`, compared for pointer equality against the process's only instance. Three reads, and RTTI names every step.

**There is no global holding the gui pointer** - a scan of the whole 16 MB exe image for the live address found **zero** hits - so an owner walk is the only cheap way in. It needs a session, because at the main menu `+0xBE8` holds a `CFrontEnd` instead of the idler; BiceLib's WidgetStats falls back to a cached vftable scan there.

Written by the construction at 0x231C41, which sets CEU3Gui's three vftables (0x11CD754 TGui, 0x11CD7D8 CPersistent, 0x11CD7F4 CFactory) and then installs the object here at 0x231C5D with the usual release-the-old-one guard.
fields.source: live 2026-10-02, verified against the process's only CEU3Gui

structs.name: CMapPoint
structs.comment: A map coordinate as a CPersistent: four bytes of vftable, four of the unread `token` word, then two floats. **0x10 bytes**, from six independent strides (shl 4, sar 4, the inlined push_back's `add [edi+0x25c],0x10`, and three loop increments). There are **879,780 live**, which is 14,190 CProvinceTemplate x (60 building types + 2 embedded) exactly - about 13.5 MiB, half of it the vftable and the dead word. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md.

fields.name: x
fields.comment: The point's x in map pixels. Save key `x`, token 0x1F: CMapPoint::SaveContents writes it from here (rva 0x5D1E3) and CMapPoint::LoadKey sscanfs into here (rva 0x5D2D6).

fields.name: y
fields.comment: The point's y in map pixels. Save key `y`, token 0x20: written from here at rva 0x5D239, parsed into here at rva 0x5D2C1. Last four bytes of a 0x10-byte object.

vftable_slots._about: Slot names BiceLib has established but that cannot be read off the slot's body - the linker folds identical bodies together, so the three unit predicates are one `mov al,1; ret` and one `xor al,al; ret` between them. Keyed by class, then slot. A record on a base class names that slot in every table below it, which is how CPersistent's six virtuals reach all 754 classes that derive from it; a name read off the slot's own body wins over one inherited this way.
